title: Hydrocalumite-Like Material Induces Early Osteogenic Priming and ECM Remodeling Without Effective Mineralization in Preosteoblasts.
abstract: Hydrocalumite-like phases, belonging to the layered double hydroxide family, are potential biomaterials for bone repair; however, their cellular effects remain incompletely understood. Here, we evaluated a hydrocalumite-like material of composition [Ca2Al(OH)₆]Cl·nH2O (abbreviated Ca2Al-Cl) in preosteoblastic MC3T3-E1 cells, assessing viability, adhesion/signaling, osteogenic differentiation, extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, and cytokine profiles. Across a 0.002-0.2 mg mL-1 range of Ca2Al-Cl, preserved cell viability and membrane integrity were observed, with the highest concentration (0.2 mg mL-1) eliciting the largest increase in metabolic activity (~270% of control), with a progressive reduction at lower concentrations; quantitative Crystal Violet staining showed increased total attachment at 0.2 and 0.02 mg mL-1, while early adhesion transcripts (Integrin-β1, FAK, Src, PP2A, Cofilin) decreased. Cell-cycle readouts revealed increased p21 and decreased CDK6, with CDK2/4 levels remaining unchanged. During 14-day differentiation, Osteocalcin increased, and ALP staining revealed more foci, yet Alpl, Runx2, and Osterix/Sp7 decreased, and Alizarin Red showed no visible mineral increase; OPG/RANKL were not modulated, thus the regulatory axis of bone resorption was not altered. The collagen content, as determined by Picrosirius staining, matched that of the Control, whereas the osteogenic medium was lower. Gelatin zymography indicated relatively higher MMP-2 (pro/intermediate/active) and lower MMP-9 under Ca2Al-Cl. Cytokine profiling revealed increased levels of IL-6 and IL-33, accompanied by reduced IL-1/IL-1β and IL-10, and unchanged TNF. Collectively, Ca2Al-Cl induces an ECM-centric, early osteogenic priming phenotype characterized by selective remodeling (MMP-2-biased) and cytokine modulation without late mineral accrual under these conditions. These findings position Ca2Al-Cl as a potential modulator of the early bone regenerative microenvironment, a property that could be harnessed for applications where controlled matrix organization is prioritized over rapid mineralization. However, further studies quantifying ion release dynamics and utilizing 3D/co-culture models are essential to elucidate the causal mechanisms and translate this priming effect into a functional regenerative outcome.

title: Global Change Is Reshaping Coral Communities and Threatening Reef Physical Functionality
abstract: Coral reefs are undergoing profound compositional changes driven by climate change, disease, and chronic human disturbance. Coral cover is the primary metric used to track reef condition, but it often fails to capture the contributions of different coral species to reef carbonate production, structural complexity, and associated biodiversity. Here, I review evidence showing that global change disproportionately removes competitively dominant and architecturally complex corals, driving non‐random changes and coral community homogenisation. These changes erode reef functionality, even when overall cover is maintained. Species‐specific contributions to calcification and structural complexity span orders of magnitude, such that targeted losses of framework‐building taxa collapse carbonate budgets and habitat architecture in ways not predictable from cover trends. These structural changes cascade through associated communities, undermining functional diversity and the ecosystem processes on which reef resilience depends. Critically, rebounds in coral cover frequently reflect the colonisation by fast‐growing opportunistic species, which yield slow or absent recovery of physical functionality, while reassembly and the re‐establishment of large, structurally complex colonies (and the physical functionality they provide) might lag by decades. Furthermore, as mass disturbance events occur at ever‐shorter intervals, recovery windows close before reef‐building potential and complexity can be fully restored. Monitoring, management, and restoration should therefore focus on trait‐ and species‐explicit assessments that prioritise protection and restoration of keystone reef‐builders, target sites with high functional potential, and reduce stressors at appropriate scales. Integrating functional metrics into policy and restoration planning is essential to safeguard reef geomorphic and ecological services under continued global change.

title: A prediction model for higher education learning behaviors based on deep learning
abstract: With the rapid advancement of deep learning technology, research on intelligent models centered on learning behavior prediction has become a key direction in higher education informatization. Addressing the challenges of complex and highly temporal student behavior patterns in university online learning environments, this study proposes a deep learning model tailored for predicting learning behaviors in higher education. The model employs multi-layer neural network technology to perform deep data mining learning through data preprocessing, feature extraction, model construction, and optimization training, thereby achieving precise identification and dynamic prediction of learning behaviors. This paper utilizes data from a university online learning platform, encompassing information such as assignment submissions, resource access, and interactive participation. Experimental results demonstrate that this learning behavior prediction model achieves higher prediction accuracy (93%), recall rate (91%), and F1 score (92%) compared to LSTM, while reducing training time by nearly 30.7%. This validates the model's effectiveness in feature fusion and parameter optimization. As an intelligent learning analytics solution, deep learning-based learning behavior prediction models can serve as an effective technical approach for university learning support systems and personalized teaching decision-making.

title: Cross-border E-commerce customer preference prediction based on transfer learning
abstract: Convolutional neural networks and transfer learning techniques are leveraged in this study to address the complex challenge of customer preference prediction within cross-border e-commerce environments. Traditional recommendation systems often struggle with the high heterogeneity of multi-lingual, multi-domain user data and the significant domain shifts typical in global markets. In this paper, we propose a deep learning framework based on attention-based feature alignment and adversarial domain adaptation to overcome these limitations. By using this approach, the model is able to learn semantically robust and transferable feature representations, which effectively bridges the gap between different regional markets. The experiments use a large multilingual dataset from eBay and Amazon, which includes a rigorous preprocessing procedure including Z-score normalization, language coordination, and outlier removal. The results show marked improvements in prediction accuracy, recall, and F1-score over established baselines, especially under conditions of pronounced domain and language disparity. Ablation studies demonstrate the important role of attention mechanism and adversarial components in promoting knowledge transfer and domain invariance. This study shows that the scalability, robustness and interpretability of the recommendation model of cross-border e-commerce platform can be greatly improved by using attention-driven neural architecture and advanced domain adaptation strategy.

title: Deep graph neural network for hidden link prediction on heterogeneous temporal graphs
abstract: The flow data between enterprise entities usually has the characteristics of complex structure, hidden association and significant timing change. Traditional methods have limited ability to describe multi-hop propagation relationships and weak ties patterns, and it is difficult to complete the identification of deep hidden association. To solve this problem, this paper abstracts multi-source stream data as heterogeneous temporal graph, and constructs a unified representation of node attributes, relationship edge features and temporal information. On this basis, a deep neural network analysis framework is introduced, high-order topological features are extracted by graph neural network, the dynamic evolution of association relationships is described by combining temporal state modeling, and the collaborative learning ability of structural information and temporal information is enhanced by a joint loss mechanism. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves better performance in accuracy, recall rate, F1 value and other indicators, and has strong recognition ability for implicit relationships in complex networks. The model also shows good engineering adaptability in terms of stability and computational efficiency.

title: Deep learning-driven mining and prediction model for blended learning behavior in lifelong education
abstract: Lifelong education increasingly relies on blended learning environments that combine online and offline modalities, generating rich multi-dimensional behavioral data. Accurately mining and predicting learning behaviors is critical for personalised intervention and dropout prevention. This paper proposes a CNN-BiLSTM-Attention hybrid deep learning model for mining temporal patterns in blended learning behaviors and predicting student outcomes. Convolutional neural networks extract local behavioral features from interaction logs, bidirectional long short-term memory networks capture long-range temporal dependencies, and a self-attention mechanism identifies the most predictive time steps. Experiments on the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD) demonstrate that the proposed model achieves 91.2% accuracy and 0.897 macro-F1 score, outperforming traditional machine learning baselines and single-architecture deep learning models. An ablation study confirms that each component contributes meaningfully to overall performance. The results suggest that hybrid deep learning architectures can effectively support learning analytics in lifelong education settings.

title: Analysis and prediction of carbon market fluctuations based on multi-factor attention deep learning
abstract: To address the challenges of high volatility and complex multi-factor interactions in carbon market price forecasting, this paper proposes a novel deep learning framework based on multi-factor attention mechanisms for comprehensive fluctuation analysis and accurate prediction. The proposed approach integrates heterogeneous factors—including economic indicators, energy commodity prices, and macro-level policy signals—and employs a dynamic attention mechanism to adaptively adjust the influence weights of each factor over time. This enables the model to precisely capture the dominant market drivers and their temporal evolution. Extensive experiments on large-scale historical datasets from China’s regional carbon markets and the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms traditional statistical models and mainstream deep learning baselines in terms of root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and coefficient of determination (R²). Furthermore, attention-based feature analysis reveals the dynamic importance of different drivers under varying market conditions, providing scientific support for market design, risk management, and algorithmic trading. This study not only enhances the interpretability and robustness of carbon price fluctuation analysis and prediction, but also lays a solid methodological and data-driven foundation for climate policy evaluation and carbon finance innovation.

title: Machine learning-based prediction model for rock mass blastability
abstract: A hierarchical sensor network combined with deep learning is utilized to predict rock mass blastability in large-scale mining environments. Tri-axial vibration and acoustic emission sensors, synchronized via GPS, collect high-frequency signals during blasting events. To extract robust features from the data, signal pre-processing uses adaptive normalization and principal component analysis. Deep long short-term memory (LSTM) networks are used to model the inherent nonlinear temporal dependencies in the blasting process. A comprehensive dataset containing more than 200 productionscale blasts was validated, which was divided into strict training, validation and testing. According to the quantitative evaluation, the LSTM model is consistently superior to the traditional regression and shallow learning methods under various geological conditions. This indicates that the LSTM model reduces the mean absolute error and root mean square error. According to the operation statistics and spatial energy distribution analysis, the implementation of the system can improve the blasting energy distribution and significantly reduce the dangerous flyrock events. The real-time edge-based deployment ensures strong fault tolerance and low-latency inference under field conditions. These findings support the practicality of combining sensor networks and advanced deep learning techniques for dynamic, data-driven blasting assessment in mine engineering.
journal: International Conference on Optical Imaging and Deep Learning (OIDL 2026)

title: Real-time urban traffic flow prediction and congestion cause analysis based on multimodal open-source data and deep learning
abstract: Accurate prediction of urban traffic flow and timely identification of congestion causes are essential for intelligent transportation systems. However, existing approaches typically rely on single-modality traffic data and fail to incorporate contextual factors such as weather conditions, special events, and road network topology. This paper proposes a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates open-source traffic speed and volume data, road network topology, weather records, and event information for real-time traffic flow prediction and congestion cause analysis. The framework employs a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) to capture spatial dependencies among road segments, a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) to model temporal traffic patterns, and a cross-attention fusion module to integrate heterogeneous contextual features. A multi-task learning head jointly predicts traffic flow values, congestion levels, and congestion causes. Experiments on the PeMS-BAY and METR-LA benchmark datasets augmented with weather and event metadata demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 14.6 and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 20.8 on PeMS-BAY, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines including GCN-LSTM (MAE 17.8) and standalone TCN (MAE 19.2). The congestion cause classification achieves 87.3% accuracy across five categories.

title: Reinforcement learning-based energy-efficient scheduling and performance prediction for cloud data centers
abstract: The growing energy footprint of cloud data centers makes power-aware resource scheduling an urgent concern. Conventional heuristic schedulers often fall short when confronted with fluctuating demands and heterogeneous server configurations. This paper proposes PPO-EES, a Proximal Policy Optimization-based Energy-Efficient Scheduling framework that jointly optimizes virtual machine placement, resource allocation, and workload migration. The framework incorporates a state observation module that captures real-time CPU utilization, memory consumption, and energy metrics, and an actor-critic architecture that learns scheduling policies maximizing energy efficiency while satisfying service-level agreements (SLAs). We further introduce an LSTM-based performance predictor to forecast server utilization and proactively adjust scheduling decisions. Experiments on the Google Cluster Trace and Azure VM Trace datasets demonstrate that PPO-EES reduces energy consumption by 18.3% compared to threshold-based methods and achieves a prediction R-squared of 0.943, outperforming DQN and A2C baselines.

title: Deep learning-based dynamic prediction of optical fiber transmission loss
abstract: Accurate dynamic prediction of optical fiber transmission loss is fundamental to proactive optical performance monitoring, capacity planning and elastic wavelength provisioning in dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM) networks. Conventional analytical models capture only steady-state attenuation and react poorly to non-stationary disturbances such as ambient temperature swings, mechanical stress and gradual ageing of in-line components. This paper proposes a hybrid deep neural architecture that couples a one-dimensional convolutional feature extractor, a bidirectional long short-term memory temporal encoder and a multi-head self-attention fusion module to forecast fiber loss multiple hours ahead from heterogeneous monitoring telemetry. We evaluate the model on a 168-hour DWDM-link telemetry corpus that integrates launch power, OSNR, wavelength, span length, ambient temperature and link age. On a 12-hour prediction horizon, the proposed model attains a mean absolute error of 0.0023 dB/km and a coefficient of determination of 0.987, outperforming ARIMA, support vector regression, LSTM, GRU and a vanilla Transformer by 30 percent or more in MAE. Ablation experiments confirm that the convolutional front end and the attention fusion module contribute complementary gains.

title: Application of the Concept of Best Efforts and Result Achievement for the Classification of Medical Obligations in the Sphere of Transplantation
abstract: The article examines the legal nature of organ and tissue transplantation relations in the Russian Federation through the prism of the French concept of dividing obligations into obligations to apply efforts (“obligation de moyens”) and achieving results (“obligation de resultat”), adopted by Russian law enforcement practice in distinguishing between contracts for work and service contracts. It is noted that organ and tissue transplantation is an obligation to apply efforts due to an objectively high therapeutic risk and is exhausted by the traditional design of the contract for the provision of paid services. Activities relating to the removal, storage, conservation and transportation of organs and tissues tend towards the model of commitment to achieve results, as a result of which they are a mixed contract with elements of contract and paid services. The proposed differentiated approach makes it possible to balance the limits of civil liability of medical organizations.

title: PrivateAgent: Mobility-Aware AI Agents for Safe Private Networks
abstract: Private cellular networks increasingly support video analytics, connected workers, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), and other industrial applications whose mobility and control deadlines vary widely. A single artificial-intelligence (AI) agent cannot safely manage all of these loops because perception, planning, networking, and governance operate at different time scales and execution locations. This paper presents PrivateAgent, a mobility-aware framework that classifies private-network applications as stationary, low-mobility, or high-mobility and maps their functions across device, site-edge, and cloud tiers. Hard real-time perception and actuation remain local; near-real-time planning and network optimization run at the edge; long-horizon learning runs in the cloud. Network-changing actions are represented as typed artifacts with explicit evidence, scope, authority, monitoring, and rollback requirements before execution. We detail representative use cases including perimeter video, machine vision, connected workers, forklifts, AMRs, and drones, and specify suitable agent families, latency targets, failure modes, and benchmark dimensions. We also instantiate the action-admission boundary with SafeFlow-Real50, a 50-scenario benchmark derived from four anonymized private-network traces. In a blind evaluation, the model selected the correct act/clarify/reject mode in 50/50 scenarios, an acceptable action in 45/50, and the preferred action in 43/50. The deterministic gateway detected all 400 injected corruptions versus 150 for schema-only validation. These results show that mobility should determine the real-time agent boundary, while independent validation should determine whether generated network actions may advance toward execution.

title: Predicting Seasonal Activity of Blunt-nosed Leafhoppers Using Degree-day Models in Cranberry
abstract: Accurate prediction of pest and crop phenology is essential for optimizing integrated pest management (IPM) in cranberry production systems. Degree-day models are widely used to forecast insect development and crop phenology; however, few have been developed for cranberry insect pests. We developed and validated degree-day–based models for the blunt-nosed leafhopper, Limotettix vaccinii (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae), in relation to cranberry bloom phenology in New Jersey, USA. Multiyear field data collected from commercial cranberry beds between 2022 and 2024 were used to develop and optimize the models, whereas independent datasets collected from 289 beds over a 5-year period (2021–25) were used for validation. Phenological progression of both pest and crop was modeled using logistic functions driven by growing degree-day (GDDpest and GDDcrop, respectively), with optimized base temperatures and biofix dates. The optimal L. vaccinii model used a base temperature of 10 °C and a biofix corresponding to floodwater drawdown [day of year (DOY) 112], whereas the cranberry bloom model converged on a base temperature of 4.44 °C and a DOY 94 biofix. Developmental trajectories showed consistent biological patterns, with nymphal activity preceding bloom and adult emergence overlapping the later stages of bloom. Model integration revealed that 10% bloom occurred, on average, at 716 GDDcrop (DOY 160), by which time ∼70% of nymphal development had already been completed. Based on these dynamics, the optimal insecticide application window was identified between 195 GDDpest (DOY 144; 25% nymphal progression) and peak nymph abundance at 266 GDDpest (DOY 153; 50% progression), maximizing nymph suppression while minimizing pollinator exposure. These results demonstrate that empirically optimized degree-day models can effectively synchronize L. vaccinii management with cranberry crop phenology. This framework provides a practical decision support tool for cranberry IPM and highlights the importance of regional calibration of phenology models to local climatic conditions and management practices.

Artificial Intelligence: Competencies for design in emerging creative environments
abstract: The study, titled From Artificial Intelligence: Competencies for Design in Emerging Creative Environments, aims to determine the competencies linked to the use of Artificial Intelligence in the training of designers, as well as to examine its impact on the professional environment. The advancement of AI has reconfigured not only the tools for design practice, but also the essential dynamics of the creative process. In emerging human-AI collaboration [HAIC] scenarios, these systems operate as cooperative agents and not merely as support tools. However, even though design students are progressively incorporating these technologies into their practice, a gap persists in the development of fundamental competencies for establishing effective interaction with these systems. Therefore, the need to strengthen disciplinary training through competencies that integrate critical interpretation, collaborative interaction, ethical and metacognitive reflection, in addition to specialized technical mastery is recognized. Based on the above, this research is structured around a comprehensive review of scientific literature, analysing studies retrieved from specialized databases in both design and higher education. The methodology will adopt the PRISMA [2021] systematic review protocol, which will ensure a rigorous process for the identification, selection, and synthesis of emerging competencies. The findings will be presented through graphic visualizations, and the discussion will incorporate relevant case studies. Ultimately, the study aims to offer an in-depth theoretical and methodological framework for future lines of research, highlighting the strategic role of AI competencies in the academic achievement and professional development of designers. These competencies are essential for overcoming limitations related to the originality, quality, and coherence of creative proposals, indispensable elements for competitive performance in educational and professional contexts.

title: Agility and Flexibility Strategies in Manufacturing Systems: A Systematic Review with a Focus on Sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Special companies, those in markets with fluctuating demand and supply, need to take the ups and downs in the market, disruption in their supply chains, and the technology and competitive pressure, and still maintain delivery, quality, and cost targets. The present systematic review, following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, aims at gathering 42 studies related to the manufacturing agility and flexibility, focusing on Sub Saharan Africa (SSA). The corpus consists of manufacturing flexibility, agile and leagile manufacturing, lean practice, supply-chain agility, digital transformation and Industry 4.0 and is segmented based on application domain, geography, methodology and publication period. The evidence suggests that agility and flexibility are associated with improved operational and organisational performance in SSA, but the pathways and degree of application varies significantly between firms and countries. The consistent challenges are cost, skills, infrastructure (reliability of power supply) and supply chain; management commitment is always cited as the final key. Digital technologies and Industry 4.0 are enablers that require a combination of infrastructure, organisational integration and human capability, and not just ownership of digital technology. There is some fragmentation in measurement of agility – different constructs are used in various surveys, there are formal agility indices, and new AI-assisted assessment frameworks are emerging – none of which have yet been validated for SSA. A series of shop-floor studies in Zimbabwe (process-parameter optimisation, data-driven maintenance, and agent-based condition monitoring) demonstrates that new capabilities at the operational level can be realized at relatively low costs, but are rarely related to the strategic agility literature. The conceptual framework and research agenda of the review call for a SSA-specific measurement tool, an integrated socio-technical model, operational as well as longitudinal evidence, and more robust mechanisms of building industry–academy capabilities, e.g., learning factories.

title: Decorrelation and Deformation: Sentinel-1 InSAR Analysis of the March 2025 Earthquake in Central Myanmar and along the Sagaing Fault
abstract: A moment magnitude (Mw) 7.7 earthquake, as reported by the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), struck central Myanmar on 28 March 2025. Its epicenter was situated near the Sagaing Fault, a major right-lateral strike-slip fault system that accommodates the relative motion between the Indian and Sunda plates. As one of Southeast Asia’s most active tectonic structures, the Sagaing Fault has a history of producing destructive earthquakes, and this event caused significant ground displacement and surface rupture particularly across the Mandalay and Sagaing regions, which lie directly along its central segment. Using Sentinel-1 satellite imagery and advanced Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) techniques, the co-seismic deformation was mapped and quantified with high precision, revealing clear patterns of displacement. Interferometric phase analysis indicated a reported maximum line-of-sight (LOS) pixel displacement of 52.0 cm, which requires coherence and phase-unwrapping validation before it can be interpreted as ground displacement concentrated near the fault trace while coherence analysis showed localized areas of signal decorrelation corresponding to intense ground disturbance. To refine rupture mapping, the Normalized Coherence Change Index (NCCI) was applied for the identification of severely damaged zones. Spatial analysis further indicates that as the distance from the epicenter increases, the deformation amplitude gradually decreases, which is consistent with the typical elastic strain release of strike-slip faults. Quantitative assessments were conducted by dividing the affected area into multiple zones for the evaluation of displacement gradients and rupture extent. The results provide new insights into the mechanics of active fault systems in central Myanmar and reveal the spatial patterns of ground movement associated with large-magnitude seismic events. These findings identify regions of high seismic vulnerability and highlight the importance of remote sensing combined with ground-based observations for hazard assessment, infrastructure resilience planning and earthquake preparedness.
journal: Journal of Island and Marine Studies

title: Explaining Organizational Decoupling through Informal Governance: A Latent Mediation Model of Academic Discipline
abstract: This study examines how Informal governance is associated with Organizational decoupling among Chinese university students, with Academic discipline proposed as an explanatory mechanism. Drawing on self-determination and self-regulated learning perspectives, a conditional process model was specified and evaluated using a synthetic dataset of 486 cases. The simulated measurement model demonstrated acceptable reliability (composite reliability = 0.84) and fit (CFI = 0.95, TLI = 0.94, RMSEA = 0.049, SRMR = 0.046). Structural estimates suggested that Informal governance was positively associated with Academic discipline (β = 0.35, p < .001) and with Organizational decoupling (β = 0.25, p < .001). The standardized indirect effect through Academic discipline was 0.15, with a synthetic 95% bootstrap interval excluding zero. Together, the modeled predictors explained 42% of the variance in Organizational decoupling. The paper contributes a concise mechanism-based account of adaptive learning and demonstrates an empirical structure aligned with The Journal of Interactive Social Sciences. Because all results are simulated, the findings are illustrative and require validation with ethically collected data.
journal: The Journal of Interactive Social Sciences

title: Comparing Random Forest and SHAP Feature Selection for LSTM-Based Stock Price Prediction
abstract: Feature selection is often used in stock price prediction, but its results remain mixed. This study analyzes the effect of feature selection based on Random Forest native feature importance (RF Importance) and SHAP on LSTM performance in predicting ADRO, ASII, and TLKM stock prices. Daily data from May 2021 to May 2026 were processed into 20 relative features from price, volume, technical indicators, and the Jakarta Composite Index (JCI), with return as the target. Both methods used the same Random Forest model and a mean-score threshold, while the LSTM was evaluated with five seeds and compared with a naive model. Feature selection reduced the input from 20 to 9 - 12 features (40% to 55%) and the LSTM parameters from 125,761 to 120,129 - 121,665 (3.3% to 4.5%). The MAPE of all schemes ranged from 1.76% to 1.90%, close to the naive model (1.72% to 1.87%), with differences between schemes of no more than 0.07 percentage points. Only for ADRO did the all-features scheme perform clearly better. Both methods retained the volume and JCI features and removed redundant trend indicators, with SHAP selecting fewer features. Therefore, the main benefit of feature selection was a simpler model input, not better prediction accuracy.

title: Technological Innovation and Green Process Innovation: A Serial Mediation Model of Information Quality and Green Work Engagement
abstract: Growing environmental concerns and increasing sustainability expectations have encouraged manufacturing organizations to adopt technological innovations that support environmentally responsible production processes. However, the mechanisms through which technological innovation enhances green process innovation remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates the direct effect of technological innovation on green process innovation and examines the serial mediating roles of information quality and green work engagement in Malaysian manufacturing organizations. Drawing upon the Resource-Based View (RBV) and the Ability–Motivation–Opportunity (AMO) framework, a conceptual model was developed and empirically tested. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among employees of manufacturing organizations in Malaysia, and 391 responses were collected using a convenience sampling technique. The collected data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The findings indicate that technological innovation positively influences information quality and green process innovation. Information quality significantly enhances both green work engagement and green process innovation, while green work engagement positively contributes to green process innovation. Furthermore, the results support the mediating role of information quality and the serial mediating effects of information quality and green work engagement in the relationship between technological innovation and green process innovation. These findings highlight the importance of integrating technological capabilities with high-quality organizational information and employees' environmental engagement to achieve sustainable manufacturing practices.

title: vibe-qc: An Open-Source, General-Purpose Electronic-Structure Code for Molecules and Solids Developed With Generative AI.
abstract: We present vibe‐qc, a general‐purpose open‐source electronic‐structure code for molecules and solids, developed almost entirely with agentic AI under expert human direction. The code is released under the Mozilla Public License 2.0 (MPLv2). The implementation comprises a C++17 numerical core and Python calculation drivers. Molecular methods include Hartree–Fock, Kohn–Sham DFT, Møller–Plesset theory and double hybrids, coupled cluster, active‐space methods, and excited states. Dispersion corrections, continuum solvation, and effective core potentials are also available. Periodic calculations use Gaussian‐basis HF and DFT with Brillouin‐zone sampling. Molecular and periodic method coverage differs; the feature matrices specify analytic and numerical derivatives and distinguish validated and experimental implementations. The validation set is a key contribution of this work. It combines independent program comparisons, published benchmarks, and internal consistency tests. Molecular mean‐field energies agree at the nanohartree scale, and conventional CCSD(T) energies agree within 3.3×10−7Eh for the tested systems. Local‐correlation and periodic limitations are reported with the comparisons. Numerical results, calculation metadata, and analysis scripts are supplied as machine‐readable Supporting Information. The independently maintained vibe‐view viewer, vibe‐queue scheduler, and qvf toolkit support visualization and job management; trexio provides wavefunction interchange.

title: Synaptic Molecules Expression in the Hippocampus After Reinstatement of Methamphetamine Conditioned Place Preference.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Drug addiction treatment remains a significant challenge in addiction relapse, which is associated with brain regions including the hippocampus (Hip). The Hip is part of the limbic system and linked to memory and learning processes closely associated with relapse. Drugs alter glutamate neurotransmission and molecules such as presynaptic and postsynaptic membrane proteins and synaptic modulators. Methamphetamine (METH) is a psychostimulant and induces addictive behaviors. METH has high addiction potential. However, the specific synaptic molecules in the Hip under METH relapse conditions are unclear. METHODS In the study, mice were given 2.5 mg/kg METH for 7 days, followed by extinction and reinstatement with 1.0 mg/kg METH. Western blot analysis was used to examine the expression of glutamatergic receptors, synapse-related proteins, and other molecules. RESULTS 1.0 mg/kg METH induced the reinstatement of conditioned place preference (CPP) in mice. The expression of Dopamine D1 receptor (D1R), Vesicular glutamate transporter 1 (VGLUT1), VGLUT2, N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor 2B (NR2B), α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor (AMPAR), synaptophysin (Syn), postsynaptic density protein 95 (PSD-95), and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) was increased. The expression of Cerebellin 1 precursor (Cbln1), complement component 1q subcomponent (C1q), and Homeobox A5 (Hoxa5) was upregulated; the expression of Cbln3, neurogranin (Ng), and neurogenic differentiation 2 (NeuroD2) was decreased. DISCUSSION The results suggest that synaptic molecules in the Hip are involved in METH relapse. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT Using a METH‑induced conditioned place preference reinstatement model in male C57BL/6 mice, this study systematically examined expression levels of multiple synaptic‑related proteins in the hippocampus. Our findings provide experimental evidence that may contribute to understanding the synaptic molecules underlying METH relapse. However, given the exclusive use of male animals and the whole‑hippocampus homogenate approach, these results should be interpreted with caution given these limitations. Further studies incorporating female subjects and region‑specific analyses are essential to determine the generalizability and spatial specificity of these molecular alterations, and to evaluate whether hippocampal synaptic molecules could serve as viable targets for intervention in METH addiction.

title: Imidazole derivative-regulated Cu-MOF nanozyme sensor array integrating machine learning for flavonoids detection and soy milk traceability.
abstract: Flavonoids are important natural bioactive compounds with remarkable health benefits, requiring rapid and accurate detection for food nutrition assessment and quality control. However, it remains challenging to simultaneously discriminate multiple flavonoids in complex matrices. Taking inspiration from the tunable structures of MOF-based nanozymes and the ability of sensor arrays to simultaneously detect multiple substances, we herein propose an innovative four-channel colorimetric sensor array for flavonoid identification. Four copper-based MOF nanozymes (Cu-ImC2N, Cu-ImC2, Cu-ImCl2, Cu-ImPh) were synthesized with different imidazole derivatives as ligands, showing significant differences in their peroxidase-like activities. Exploiting their specific catalytic activity variations at pH 6.0 and 6.5, the two most active nanozymes (Cu-ImC2N and Cu-ImC2) were strategically selected to construct the array. Upon processing the array data with linear discriminant analysis (LDA), the array achieved 100% accurate discrimination and quantitative detection of seven flavonoids, with limits of detection (LODs) ranging from 0.039 to 0.982 μM. Furthermore, comparisons of concentration-independent models built with multiple machine learning algorithms showed that the K-nearest neighbors (KNN) method outperformed LDA, effectively reducing interference from concentration variations. The sensor array was successfully applied to the analysis of commercial soy milk, reliably differentiating products from different brands and bean sources (e.g., soybean and mung bean). This strategy surpasses traditional single-analyte methods and holds substantial practical potential for the rapid on-site detection of complex food systems.

title: HyGage: Solving the hysteresis puzzle with a new streamflow monitoring method
abstract: 11 The questionable reliability of discharges obtained using the traditional stage–discharge 12 method under gradually varied flow conditions continues to motivate the search for 13 improved monitoring approaches that support water resources management, streamflow 14 forecasting, and multipurpose scientific investigations related to the water cycle. This 15 paper introduces HyGage, a new physically based monitoring method grounded in the 16 governing equations of spatiotemporal, gradually varied, shallow open channel flow. The 17 methodology integrates measurement elements commonly employed in the index velocity 18 and slope area methods within a unified analytical framework, enabling real time discharge 19 estimation in both steady and gradually varied flows without relying on the semi empirical 20 techniques of the past. The performance of HyGage is evaluated by comparing its discharge 21 estimates with those obtained from established methods. Unlike conventional approaches, 22 HyGage is not built around any specific instrument; instead, it can flexibly incorporate 23 combinations of immersed, close range, and remote sensing measurements through 24 seamless integration. 25

Transformation of aflatoxins by a thermostable and mediator-independent laccase from Thermincola ferriacetica.
abstract: Aflatoxin, a potent carcinogenic mycotoxin, commonly contaminates crops and poses a serious threat to global food and feed security. In recent years, enzymatic degradation of aflatoxins (AFs) has attracted considerable attention, with microbial laccases being the most extensively investigated. Here, we identified a thermostable laccase from Thermincola ferriacetica (Thfe-Lac) that is capable of transforming AFB1 in the absence of mediators. Under mediator-free condition, Thfe-Lac removed over 95% of 20 μg/mL AFB1 within 12 h. The optimal pH of Thfe-Lac against ABTS and AFB1 were pH 4.0 and pH 8.0, indicating distinct oxidation mechanisms for these two substrates. Thfe-Lac exhibited its optimal temperature at 70 °C and retained over 60% of residual activity after 2 h of incubation at 70-80 °C. The addition of the natural mediator acetosyringone (AS) further enhanced the AFB1-transforming ability of Thfe-Lac. In the presence of AS, Thfe-Lac was also able to transform other mycotoxins, including zearalenone (ZEN) and deoxynivalenol (DON). Moreover, several key residues within the substrate-binding pocket were identified through molecular docking. Further quantum mechanics calculations on residue-substrate interaction models revealed that dispersion interactions played an important role in AFs binding. Notably, elimination of unfavored π-π interaction and steric hindrance significantly improved the activity of the F232A mutant. Meanwhile, the enlarged substrate binding pocket facilitate AFB1 entry and promotes closer positioning toward the His500-Cys501-His502 motif. Finally, Thfe-Lac and its mutant F232A represent efficient mediator-free laccase for decontamination of AFB1 in food and feed systems.

title: Biosurfactants in the food chain: Perspectives and challenges.
abstract: Biosurfactants (BS) of microbial origin combine inherent surface activity with unique functional properties and natural status, enabling the development of innovative clean-label products and more sustainable processing strategies. This article synthesizes recent advances in the application of BS throughout the food chain, from farm to table with particular emphasis on studies reported during the last five years and validated in food-relevant models. The review highlights BS applications in crop protection, animal health, food processing and formulation, waste valorization, and nanotechnology, while critically discussing current limitations and emerging opportunities. The multifunctional nature of BS supports their use as antimicrobial agents, functional ingredients, sanitizers, postbiotics for animal health, and components of smart and active packaging systems. Furthermore, the valorization of food residues and agro-industrial waste streams as substrates for BS production contributes to circular bioeconomy approaches and more sustainable food systems. However, despite promising laboratory-scale results, the translation of BS applications into industrial practice remains constrained by limited validation in complex food systems, production and purification costs, safety assessment requirements, and regulatory challenges. Future research should prioritize application-oriented studies, safety and regulatory frameworks to facilitate the broader adoption of BS across the food chain.

title: From SCA cupping to Coffee Value Assessment: non-interchangeable scores, multidimensional sensory profiling and sensory-volatile links in Brazilian Federal District coffees.
abstract: The Specialty Coffee Association (SCA) replaced its former cupping protocol with the Coffee Value Assessment (CVA), which separates affective quality judgments from descriptive sensory characterization. Coffees from 14 producers in the Brazilian Federal District were evaluated in 2024 and 2025. Former SCA cupping was conducted by certified Q Graders, whereas CVA was applied by a coffee-experienced, semi-trained panel. SCA and CVA affective scores were not numerically interchangeable, and their final-score configurations were not significantly aligned. Assessor-blocked models detected producer differentiation under both protocol-panel conditions. SCA showed stronger adjusted differentiation and greater sensitivity to the markedly defective coffee in each harvest; removing these samples substantially reduced SCA effect sizes, while CVA effects changed little. Among non-defective coffees, SCA scores were comparatively compact. CVA affective ratings spanned a wider range but showed greater within-sample variability and did not produce stronger score-based differentiation. CVA descriptive intensities, structured check-all-that-apply (CATA) descriptors and free notes provided complementary sensory information and revealed harvest-specific patterns not captured by final scores alone. Fisher-selected volatile features added an exploratory chemical dimension, but whole-configuration sensory-volatile alignment was low to moderate and nonsignificant. Overall, former SCA cupping yielded a more compact and defect-sensitive score representation, while CVA contributed a broader multidimensional sensory record. Because different assessor panels applied the two frameworks, the observed contrasts reflect both protocol and panel composition.

title: PdO-T nanozyme-based three-channel colorimetric sensor array coupled with machine learning for accurate differentiation and quantitative detection of aflatoxins in U.S. pecan.
abstract: Aflatoxins (AFs) represent a class of highly toxic food contaminants, yet existing detection approaches still suffer from several critical limitations. Herein, three PdO nanoenzymes (denoted as PdO-160, PdO-200, and PdO-240) were synthesized by regulating the hydrothermal temperature. All three nanozymes display robust and stable peroxidase-like activity via the generation of •OH and 1O₂. By exploiting the distinct inhibitory effects of AFB1, AFB2, AFG1, and AFG2 toward these nanoenzymes, a three-channel colorimetric sensor array was rationally constructed. Combined with a random forest (RF) model, the proposed array enables accurate discrimination of all four AFs independent of concentration. Further quantitative prediction was conducted using RF regression and artificial neural network (ANN) models, and the RF regression delivers optimal fitting performance with the maximum determination coefficient R2 up to 0.971 for the four target analytes. In real-sample analysis, the array obtains favorable classification performance for mixed aflatoxins, with an accuracy of 95.65% for concentration-independent identification, and all R2 values above 0.956 in quantitative analysis. The nanoenzymes also exhibit excellent batch-to-batch reproducibility and long-term storage stability. This study offers a promising colorimetric sensing strategy for the screening of aflatoxins in food matrices.

Knowledge and influence mechanism of leader–member exchange on hotel employees’ craftsmanship spirit:An empirical exploration based on SEM and fsQCA
abstract: In high-contact service industries, the craftsmanship spirit plays a pivotal role in driving the continuous improvement of service quality and the enrichment of customer experience. Its formation mechanism, however, requires meticulous investigation from the perspective of organisational behaviour. Grounded in the social exchange theory (SET), this study develops a chain-mediated model linking leader – member exchange (LMX), voice behaviour, organisational citizenship behaviour (OCB), and craftsmanship spirit, and further incorporates employee trust as a moderating variable to clarify the multiple pathways leading to the craftsmanship spirit. Data were collected through a questionnaire survey of 393 employees from 12 hotels, and the proposed model was empirically tested using structural equation modelling and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA). The results reveal that: (1) LMX serves as a core situational factor in stimulating employees ’ craftsmanship spirit; (2) voice behaviour and OCB constitute a chain-mediated pathway through which LMX influences craftsmanship spirit; (3) employee trust plays a significant and differentiated moderating role in the LMX – craftsmanship spirit relationship, with LMX exerting a stronger positive effect under high-trust conditions; (4) fsQCA identifies three equivalent configurations leading to high craftsmanship spirit: trust-based mutual support, empowerment-driven participation, and reciprocity – trust integration, highlighting the complementary roles of institutional resources and relational capital in different contexts. Theoretically, this study extends the application of LMX and SET to the hotel industry, enriching research on the processes and boundary conditions underlying craftsmanship spirit formation. Practically, it offers differentiated managerial strategies for enhancing the craftsmanship spirit by optimising superior – subordinate relationships, promoting employee voice, fostering OCB, and cultivating a high-trust organisational climate.

title: Selective recovery of molybdenum from spent iron-molybdate catalysts through NH4OH(NH4)2SO4 leaching and solvent extraction
abstract: An integrated hydrometallurgical process was developed for the selective recovery of molybdenum from spent iron-molybdate catalysts generated during formaldehyde production. Ammoniacal buffer leaching was statistically optimized using response surface methodology based on central composite design to evaluate the effects of NH 4 OH:(NH 4 ) 2 SO 4 molar ratio, total ammonia concentration, pulp density, temperature, and time on molybdenum dissolution. The developed quadratic model demonstrated strong predictive capability and identified the ammonia-ammonium ratio as the most influential parameter. The kinetic analysis revealed that leaching proceeds through a multi-step mechanism involving NH 3 -NH 4 + coupled solution equilibria, surface reactions, and interfacial transport. Under optimized conditions, 98.3% molybdenum leaching was experimentally achieved with only 2.1% iron co-dissolution in ammoniacal solution. The pregnant leach solution was directly treated by solvent extraction using protonated tri-n -octylamine modified with tributyl phosphate in kerosene. Selective extraction of 96% molybdenum was achieved at pH 5.4 without measurable iron co-extraction. Two-stage counter-current extraction enabled an overall extraction efficiency of 99.96%, demonstrating strong potential for continuous and scalable operation. Quantitative stripping with NaOH solution produced a molybdenum-rich solution (~103 g ⋅ L (cid:0) 1 Mo), from which high-purity sodium molybdate (Na 2 MoO 4 .2H 2 O) crystals were recovered by evaporative crystallization. The integrated process combines NH 4 OH – (NH 4 ) 2 SO 4 leaching, liquid-liquid separation, and crystallization techniques into an efficient hydrometallurgical route for recovering molybdenum from spent Fe – Mo catalysts and provides a promising strategy for the efficient utilization of secondary mo-lybdenum resources.
