title: Image-Based Soil Nutrient Prediction Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models
abstract: Recent advances in precision agriculture have enabled the use of machine learning and image processing for rapid soil nutrient assessment. This study presents a non-destructive approach for estimating soil nutrient content from digital soil images captured using a camera and analyzed through specialized software. A dataset of 1,500 soil images was processed using color correction, noise reduction, and feature extraction techniques to improve data quality. Five machine learning models, Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), and a Stacking Regressor, were evaluated for predicting nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium levels. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based deep learning model was served as a benchmark. No single model was best for every nutrient and metric. For nitrogen, GBM achieved the lowest test MAE (0.1652), whereas the Stacking Regressor achieved the highest test R² (0.9886). For potassium, Random Forest achieved the lowest test MAE (0.0051), whereas XGBoost achieved the highest test R² (0.9999). For phosphorus, XGBoost achieved both the lowest test MAE (0.1558) and the highest test R² (0.9929). Thus, the best-performing model depends on the nutrient and evaluation metric. Further validation using independent field datasets is required to establish robustness under diverse environmental conditions.

title: Model Terpadu Pemberdayaan Desa Berbasis Green Economy melalui Hilirisasi Nilam dan Perlebahan di Desa Lambadeuk, Aceh Besar
abstract: Lambadeuk Village, Aceh Besar Regency, possesses patchouli and linot (stingless bee) honey potential that remains underutilized for economic value addition. Partner groups face challenges such as limited processing technology, absent SOPs, low capacity, weak business governance, and restricted market access. This community initiative aims to establish a green economy-based empowerment model through appropriate technology, capacity building, and product downstreaming. Carried out with the Benteng Makmur Farmer Group and KTH Lestari Alam, activities employed a participatory method spanning problem identification to evaluation. Benteng Makmur was facilitated with a stainless-steel steam distillation unit and patchouli processing SOPs, while KTH Lestari Alam received additional linot bee colonies and harvesting SOPs. The initiative improved community capacity, production self-reliance, and value-added opportunities. The added colonies are targeted to increase honey production by up to 50%, while the distillation unit underpins high-value patchouli oil development. Integrating appropriate technology, standardization, and green economy principles effectively supports sustainable village-level enterprises.

title: Frequency-Domain Evaluation and Estimation of Semi-Markov Disease Natural History Models
A Lightweight Deep Learning Framework for Real-Time Cyberattack Detection in Internet of Things Networks
abstract: The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) networks introduces significant cybersecurity challenges because connected sensors, gateways, and embedded controllers operate with limited memory, processing capacity, and energy. Conventional intrusion detection solutions may impose computational costs that exceed the capabilities of these devices, while cloud-only analysis adds latency and creates privacy concerns. This narrative review develops a conceptual lightweight deep learning framework for real-time cyberattack detection at the IoT edge. The proposed architecture combines flow-based feature extraction, selective preprocessing, a compact one-dimensional convolutional network, calibrated risk scoring, and adaptive response at the gateway. It discusses feature selection, class imbalance, model compression, data drift, adversarial resilience, and deployment constraints. An illustrative design chart compares qualitative trade-offs between model classes; it does not represent measured experimental findings. The article outlines an evaluation protocol using reproducible train-test separation, device-aware latency measurement, and cross-dataset validation. The central conclusion is that practical reliability requires jointly optimizing detection quality, false-alarm burden, inference time, memory use, and operational maintainability rather than accuracy alone.

title: Evaluating Software Quality Through Automated Testing and Predictive Defect Detection Using Machine Learning
abstract: Software quality assurance increasingly depends on the ability to combine automated testing with data-driven estimates of defect risk. Conventional test suites reveal failures in executed scenarios but do not necessarily identify which untested changes are most likely to introduce faults. Machine learning models can prioritize code review and testing by learning associations between historical defect outcomes, code structure, change activity, and process characteristics. This narrative review synthesizes established research on software defect prediction and proposes a transparent evaluation framework integrating data preparation, temporal validation, calibrated prediction, risk-based test selection, and continuous monitoring. It distinguishes test effectiveness from model discrimination and emphasizes precision–recall analysis, operational cost, data leakage prevention, and human oversight. A conceptual graph illustrates how testing effort might be redistributed according to predicted risk; it does not represent measured experimental outcomes. The paper argues that machine learning should supplement rather than replace automated tests, and that deployment claims require prospective, project-specific evidence. Limitations include incomplete defect labels, shifting development practices, class imbalance, and uncertain cross-project transferability

title: MGP_HNSC32: A H&E Morphology-Derived 32-Gene Prognostic Signature in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSC) exhibits substantial molecular and morphological heterogeneity, yet current morphology-based prognostic models often lack biological interpretability. We developed a transformer-based computational framework (CTransPath) to virtually predict gene expression directly from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) whole-slide images. Morphology-associated genes were identified from the TCGA-HNSC cohort, and a 32-gene morphology-guided prognostic signature (MGP_HNSC32) based on H&E-derived predicted gene expression was developed using Random Survival Forest and multivariable Cox regression modeling. In TCGA-HNSC, the MGP_HNSC32 risk score significantly stratified patients by progression-free interval (PFI; HR = 4.13, 95% CI: 2.84-6.02), overall survival (OS; HR = 2.42, 95% CI: 1.78-3.29), and disease-specific survival (DSS; HR = 4.88, 95% CI: 2.95-8.06; all p < 0.001), and remained independently associated with prognosis after multivariable adjustment. High-risk tumors were enriched for cell cycle, E2F, MYC, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition pathways and displayed poorly differentiated histology with nuclear atypia and stromal desmoplasia. In contrast, low-risk tumors showed keratinizing morphology and immune-rich stroma, corresponding to differentiation- and metabolism-related transcriptional programs. In the independent HANCOCK cohort (n = 701), risk scores calculated entirely from H&E-derived predicted gene expression using the TCGA-derived coefficients and prespecified cutoff were associated with progression-free survival (HR = 1.40, 95% CI: 1.03-1.90, p = 0.034). However, the continuous risk score was not significantly associated with progression-free survival (HR = 1.001, 95% CI: 0.999-1.003, p = 0.328). MGP_HNSC32 links histomorphology to transcriptional programs and demonstrates preliminary prognostic associations using routine H&E images. The H&E-based gene-expression prediction component should be considered proof-of-concept, and further independent and prospective validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Drought‐induced leaf senescence and regreening upon rewatering associated with chlorophyll metabolism in Kentucky bluegrass
abstract: Drought stress is a major factor limiting the quality and persistence of cool‐season turfgrass species by accelerating leaf senescence and reducing overall vigor. This study was conducted to examine physiological responses associated with drought‐induced leaf senescence and post‐drought regreening in Kentucky bluegrass ( Poa pratensis L.), with particular emphasis on chlorophyll metabolism. Plants of two cultivars, Baron and Bewitched, were grown under controlled environmental conditions and subjected to well‐watered control and drought stress treatments, with post‐drought rewatering. Physiological parameters such as turf quality, relative water content, chlorophyll fluorescence, and chlorophyll content were evaluated throughout drought and recovery. In addition, the activities of a chlorophyll degradation enzyme, pheophytinase (PPH), and a chlorophyll synthesis enzyme, porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD), were measured in response to drought and rewatering to observe the effect of drought on chlorophyll metabolism and to determine which pathway plays a more important role. Drought stress caused leaf dehydration, chlorophyll loss, reduced photochemical efficiency, and lower turf quality in both cultivars, although these parameters recovered following rewatering. PPH activity increased significantly during prolonged drought stress, whereas PBGD activity did not change significantly under drought. During post‐drought recovery, PBGD activity increased, while PPH activity declined to non‐stress levels. The decline in chlorophyll during drought‐induced leaf senescence may be associated with enhanced chlorophyll degradation enzyme activity, whereas the regreening observed during rewatering is likely related to the resumption of chlorophyll synthesis. These findings provide insight into the physiological mechanisms controlling drought‐induced senescence and post‐stress recovery in turfgrass and may be useful for the development of drought‐tolerant cultivars.

title: Quantifying genetic and nongenetic improvement for grain yield in faba bean breeding
abstract: Faba Bean ( Vicia faba ) is a cool season legume crop, often grow as a rotation crop to improve sustainability of the farming systems. The Australian faba bean breeding program is publicly funded, with improving grain yield as a key breeding objective to increase grower profitability. In this study, we aimed to quantify the genetic and nongenetic improvement for grain yield using historical multi‐environment trial data collected from 2018 to 2024, comprising 1985 breeding lines evaluated in 158 field trials across 25 locations in southern Australia. Genetic gain estimates varied with the method used. Best linear unbiased estimates–based analyses showed negative gain with different breeding stages populations, whereas best linear unbiased prediction–based estimates indicated small but significant gains ranging from −1.6 to 7.8 kg/ha per cycle. With a subset data from 2020 to 2024 and pedigree information, genetic gain calculated via estimated breeding values–based method showed consistent positive gain across all populations, ranged from 7.6 to 15.3 kg/ha per cycle. Nongenetic trends estimated from check varieties (9 kg/ha/year) or using the single check PBA Samira (30 kg/ha/year) were positive but statistically insignificant. Environmental covariates analysis further suggested that water availability was the key driver of grain yield variation among breeding trials in faba bean. Despite the short timeframe, this study provided an evidence‐based evaluation of grain yield gain for the current breeding program and laid the foundation for future breeding program optimization.

title: UAV-based multispectral imaging and machine learning for characterizing herbicide injury and desiccant responses in field crops
abstract: Purpose Herbicides and desiccants are critical for weed control and harvest management; however, their efficacy varies across crop species, environments, and growing seasons. This study evaluated unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based multispectral imaging combined with machine-learning (ML) as a non-destructive approach for quantifying herbicide injury and desiccation responses across Canadian Prairie agroecosystems. Methods Field trials were conducted from 2022 to 2024 at three sites in Alberta and Saskatchewanusing tame oat, oriental mustard, and lentil. Tame oat and oriental mustard were used as pseudo-weed models for wild oat and wild mustard, respectively. UAV multispectral imagery and concurrent ground-based visual ratings were collected from 0 to 21 days aftertreatment to characterize temporal crop responses. Six ML models were evaluated using UAV-derived vegetation indices. Results Ensemble models, including Gradient Boosting, Extreme Gradient Boosting, and Random Forest, consistently demonstrated strong predictive performance, with site-specific coefficients of determination (R) of 66–90% in oat, 60–75% in mustard, and 43–96% in lentil. Multi-site models achieved R values of 65–83%; however, leave-one-site-out (LOSO) and leave-one-year-out (LOYO) validation for oat and mustard showed reduced predictive performance in independent environments, highlighting limitations in model transferability. Vegetation indices captured temporal herbicide injury and stress dynamics across crops, while area under the desiccation progress curve (AUDPC) analysis quantified lentil dry-down and differentiated desiccant performance. Pearson correlation analysis identified NDVI and NDGI indices strongly associated with visual injury ratings across crops and environments. NDVI showed the most consistent relationships in oat and mustard, whereas NDVI, NDGI, and VARI exhibited comparable relationships with lentil desiccation responses. Conclusion Overall, integrating UAV-based multispectral imaging, vegetation indices, ML, and AUDPC provides a scalable, objective, and non-destructive framework for evaluating herbicide injury and desiccant efficacy under variable field conditions.

A trait-based perspective on nitrogen limitation from leaves to crop canopies
abstract: Nitrogen limitation can strongly reduce crop productivity; however, changes in leaf-level photosynthetic performance do not always parallel reductions in growth and yield, highlighting the need to consider how nitrogen-dependent responses scale from individual leaves to whole canopies. Here, I develop a trait-based perspective for interpreting the coordination of leaf-level function, leaf-area deployment, canopy resource capture, and crop performance under nitrogen limitation. Rather than proposing an alternative to existing crop physiological or modeling frameworks, this Perspective uses functional traits as a cross-scale lens to examine conditions in which comparatively maintained leaf-level function may not translate into maintained canopy performance. A nitrogen-limited potato system is used as an empirically grounded illustrative case. Leaf-level observations show comparatively weak relationships between specific leaf area and area-based photosynthesis, whereas stronger associations emerge for mass-based photosynthesis and photosynthetic nitrogen-use efficiency. At the crop level, nitrogen nutrition status is associated with total and tuber biomass, while biomass accumulation is closely related to intercepted photosynthetically active radiation across crop development. Together, these observations support a condition termed leaf-canopy decoupling, in which leaf-level physiological function is maintained while leaf-area deployment and canopy resource capture are constrained. This interpretation does not imply that canopy limitation universally dominates crop responses to nitrogen, but it generates a testable cross-scale hypothesis whose magnitude and consequences may vary by developmental stage, environment, and crop source–sink strategy. By linking functional traits to canopy development and resource capture, this Perspective offers a complementary basis for investigating nitrogen responses across crop functional types and identifying trait and management combinations that may improve nitrogen-use efficiency.

Blockchain and the transparency paradox: Fear of exposure, information asymmetry, and traceability resistance in Saudi manufacturing supply chains.
abstract: Blockchain can strengthen supply-chain transparency and traceability, but implementation does not necessarily imply full acceptance of the visibility it creates. This study examines how psychological transparency risk, economic transparency risk, and traceability resistance relate to blockchain traceability implementation in Saudi manufacturing firms. Drawing on Transparency Paradox Theory, Information Asymmetry Theory, and Technology Threat Avoidance Theory, the model distinguishes risk appraisals from organisational resistance behaviour. Three-wave survey data from 703 firms were analyzed using PLS-SEM, supported by confirmatory factor analysis, predictive assessment, unit-weighted comparison, and Gaussian Copula analysis. The model explained 67.3% of the variance in implementation and 66.7% in resistance. Contrary to expectations, psychological and economic transparency risks were positively associated with implementation and negatively associated with resistance. Traceability resistance was negatively associated with implementation and was the only direct relationship supported in the hypothesized direction. The indirect effects through resistance were positive, while relational trust and digital capability produced asymmetric moderating effects. The findings show that recognising exposure, control, and commercial vulnerability should not be equated with resistance. Firms may acknowledge these risks while continuing to implement blockchain, whereas delayed integration, restricted access, selective disclosure, and symbolic compliance remain important barriers. The study contributes by separating transparency-risk appraisal, resistance behaviour, and operational implementation, while offering practical guidance on differentiated access controls, disclosure governance, and monitoring of observable resistance.

Spatio-temporal monitoring of agricultural drought in China based on downscaled soil moisture data
abstract: : Agricultural drought threatens China’s food and ecological security, and accurate spatio-13 temporal monitoring is key for disaster mitigation. Soil moisture is critical for drought assessment, 14 but the accuracy of existing remote sensing-based SM products in China remains to be improved. 15 This study develops a framework that synergistically integrates a spatiotemporally adaptive gap-16 filling algorithm with a machine learning-based downscaling approach, generating a seamless 0.05 ∘ 17 monthly SM dataset for China from 2003 to 2023. The methodology harnesses the complementary 18 strengths of random forest modeling and spatiotemporal reconstruction techniques to effectively 19 fuse multi-source satellite observations, achieving dual improvements in SM data accuracy and 20 spatial coverage. Using this dataset, the standardized soil moisture index was applied to characterize 21 the spatio-temporal evolution of agricultural drought. Results demonstrate that (1) The downscaled 22 SM dataset achieves significant improvements in both spatial resolution and accuracy, showing a 23 2.3–34.4% reduction in ubRMSE and 1.2–52.7% improvement in correlation coefficients compared 24 to benchmark datasets. (2) Drought characterization based on the downscaled SM dataset and SSI 25 accurately identified the extent of agricultural drought, showing a significant spatiotemporal 26 consistency with agricultural disaster area. (3) Agricultural drought intensified significantly across 27 China during the study period, characterized by northward migration of drought center and spatially 28 heterogeneous aridification patterns — decreasing severity from northwest to southeast while 29 increasing from northeast to southwest. High-frequency drought zones were predominantly 30 clustered in ecologically vulnerable regions, particularly the agro-pastoral ecotone of northern 31 China. (4) Distinct intra-annual drought dynamics emerged, with a southwest-to-northeast 32 expansion dominating from January to June, followed by bidirectional propagation from the Yellow 33 River-Huaihe River Basin (YRB-HRB) to northwestern and southeastern regions from June to 34 December. This study provides high-accuracy data support for agricultural drought monitoring and 35 offers scientific insights for developing regional differentiated drought mitigation strategies, which 36 are of great significance for ensuring national food security. 37

Posttraumatic growth in nursing home workers: differential associations of gratitude, meaning in life, and distress four years after the pandemic.
abstract: PURPOSE/AIMS To examine associations between posttraumatic growth, gratitude, meaning in life, and psychological distress among nursing home workers several years after the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS A cross-sectional study was conducted with 251 nursing home workers in Madrid, Spain, who had worked during the COVID-19 pandemic. Participants completed the Posttraumatic Growth Inventory-Short Form, the Purpose in Life Test-10, the Gratitude Questionnaire-6, and the Patient Health Questionnaire-4. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, and multiple linear regression models were performed. RESULTS Posttraumatic growth was present across the sample several years after the pandemic, although spiritual change showed lower scores than other growth dimensions. Gratitude and meaning in life were both positively associated with posttraumatic growth at the bivariate level. In adjusted models, gratitude remained significantly associated with all posttraumatic growth dimensions, whereas meaning in life did not retain independent associations. Psychological distress was also positively associated with posttraumatic growth, indicating that growth-related appraisals and distress coexisted in this sample. No significant differences in posttraumatic growth were observed across professional roles. CONCLUSION/IMPLICATIONS This study contributes to the limited literature on nursing home workers by showing that posttraumatic growth remained present several years after the COVID-19 pandemic and was more closely associated with gratitude than with meaning in life in adjusted models. For research, the findings support a more differentiated view of positive post-adversity processes and their coexistence with distress. For geriatric nursing and long-term care, they underscore the value of considering not only emotional burden but also positive psychological appraisals when addressing staff well-being after major collective adversity.

Hybrid architectures of CNN-ViT and SE-CNN with grad-CAM for monkeypox disease detection
abstract: In the aftermath of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, the monkeypox virus (MPV) emerged as a significant global health concern, leading the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare it a public health emergency. Accurate detection of monkeypox (Mpox) is challenging due to its similarity to other pox viruses such as measles and chickenpox. Conventional diagnostic methods often struggle to distinguish between these diseases, necessitating the development of more advanced diagnostic tools. This paper presents a novel approach to detect Mpox using two efficient deep learning (DL) models: the first one is a hybrid architecture of a Convolutional Neural Network—Vision Transformer (CNN–ViT), and the second model is a Squeeze-and-Excitation Convolutional Neural Network (SE-CNN). These models are employed for the classification of medical images into two categories: Monkeypox and Others. The proposed models are applied to a dataset of 1140 images, and utilize fine-tuning for the models’ hyperparameters. Data augmentation techniques are implemented for training images to maximize the models’ performance. Additionally, a gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) visualization technique is applied to explain the decision of the models and aid doctors in clinical decision-making. Experimentally, the accuracy, error matrix, area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, Recall, F1-score, and Precision are used to measure the performance of the proposed models. The CNN–ViT and SE-CNN achieve a testing accuracy of 97.80% and 96.05%, respectively, while the micro-average area under the ROC curve is 97% for CNN–ViT and 99% for SE-CNN. The weighted F1-score, Precision, and Recall for CNN–ViT are all 97.26%, 97.33%, and 97.27%, respectively, while for SE-CNN are 96.04%, 96.13%, and 96.05%, respectively. The proposed models provide a rapid and accurate method to differentiate Mpox from other cases, offering a valuable tool for healthcare professionals in the screening and diagnosis of Mpox.

title: An element-resolved coupled cluster atomization energy data set ranging across the periodic table.
abstract: We introduce the total atomization energy periodic table compass (TAE-PTComp), a collection of 67 atomization energy data sets, each specifically designed to probe various chemical environments of one particular element of the periodic table. In total, this set comprises 2097 carefully curated closed-shell, single-reference molecules containing up to 50 atoms, with an average of 31 structures per element-specific subset. The chemical space covered ranges from conventional covalent and coordination compounds to noncovalently bound clusters, extracted fragments of periodic crystalline structures, and artificial "mindless" molecules. Additionally, we include a balanced amount of charged species with charges of ±1. For each molecule, as well as its constituent atoms (and ions), we provide high-level coupled cluster reference energies. We therefore envision this benchmark as a resource for parameter fitting, validation, and testing of approximate density functional theory methods, semi-empirical models, and machine-learning interatomic potentials. An initial assessment of TAE-PTComp for a representative set of density functional approximations, together with the semi-empirical g-xTB method and the machine-learned Universal Model for Atoms (UMA), shows that this benchmark can efficiently differentiate between broadly robust methods, such as the range-separated hybrid ωB97M-V, and approaches that exhibit localized, element-specific failures, such as the hybrid M06-2X functional.

title: Study on the Dynamic Response Characteristics and the Damage Constitutive Model of Magnetite Based on the Energy Dissipation Method
abstract: In underground metal mining operations, pillars are often subjected to dynamic loads induced by blasting. To investigate the response characteristics of pillar rock mass under dynamic loading conditions and to propose a damage constitutive model based on energy dissipation to describe the mechanical behavior of magnetite, dynamic triaxial tests were first conducted on magnetite, and its energy evolution characteristics were analyzed. Subsequently, a damage variable based on energy dissipation was introduced, and a modification factor was proposed based on energy evolution parameters, thereby developing a new damage constitutive model. Finally, the fitting results of the proposed model were compared with those of the conventional damage constitutive model based on the Weibull distribution and with the experimental data. The results indicate that the energy evolution characteristics of magnetite during the loading process are closely related to the loading method, the loading process, and the development of damage. Energy evolution indicators, such as the proportion of elastic energy, can be used to quantitatively characterize and distinguish the elastoplastic evolution process of rock during loading. It is feasible to employ energy evolution indicators as modification factors for the damage constitutive model, and they possess clear physical significance, thus outperforming modification factors derived from statistical approaches. The proposed damage constitutive model accurately describes the response characteristics of rock under dynamic loading conditions and it performs particularly well in capturing the yielding and residual characteristics of the rock.

title: Modeling and Simulation Techniques for Ultrahigh-Performance Concrete Materials and Structures
abstract: This paper presents a focused review of modeling and simulation strategies for ultrahigh-performance concrete (UHPC), emphasizing predictive capabilities, calibration demands, and multiscale consistency. Continuum damage plasticity and cap-based formulations are shown to effectively reproduce nonlinear behavior and strain-rate sensitivity at the structural scale, while cohesive zone and bond-slip models provide a mechanistic representation of fiber pullout and interface behavior. Emerging approaches, including molecular dynamics and peridynamics, offer improved insight into fracture processes but remain computationally intensive and difficult to integrate into routine design workflows. Across modeling scales, a central challenge is the robustness and transferability of parameters because most current approaches rely on case-specific calibration rather than unified physical principles. Key research needs include the development of standardized calibration protocols, hybrid numerical strategies for localized damage, and multiphysics coupling for long-term performance prediction. Advancing these areas is essential to transition UHPC modeling from research-driven simulations toward reliable, design-oriented predictive tools.

title: A Conflict Warning Approach Based on Roadside Perception-Driven Trajectory Prediction
abstract: Highway traffic crashes primarily originate from delayed responses to dynamic traffic conflicts. Implementing real-time proactive conflict prediction mechanisms is crucial for collision warning systems and safety applications. While vehicle-centric sensing is constrained by limited fields of view and occlusion vulnerabilities, and approaches based on unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) trajectories face operational reliability challenges in severe weather and lighting conditions. Roadside multisensor fusion systems overcome these limitations through persistent spatiotemporal observation. To this end, this paper proposes a conflict warning approach based on roadside perception-driven trajectory prediction. First, we propose a novel trajectory prediction architecture that processes variable-length roadside perception trajectories while jointly encoding road topology constraints and multiagent interaction dynamics. Subsequently, we introduce an adaptive conflict detection framework leveraging vehicle proximity distribution to model probability of near-collision event occurrence, learning context-dependent proximity thresholds from trajectory data. These contributions are then integrated into a conflict warning system that demonstrates robustness across diverse highway interaction scenarios, validated against unified trajectory dataset and co-simulated environments. Our warning method achieved a true positive rate of 95.52% and a false alarm rate of 3.03%, and demonstrates early-warning temporal stability.
journal: Journal of Transportation Engineering, Part A: Systems

title: Impact of Subway Passenger Flow–Built Environment Interaction on Road Congestion around Subway Stations Using Machine-Learning Models
abstract: To alleviate urban traffic congestion, metro systems have become critical urban transportation infrastructure. While effectively relieving pressure on long-distance commutes, the areas surrounding metro stations often emerge as congestion-sensitive zones due to the transient aggregation of feeder traffic and the high-density land use patterns concentrated there. This study focuses on road networks within a 500 m radius of stations along six metro lines in Kunming, China. It integrates four categories of multisource heterogeneous data: metro smart card transactions; point of interest (POI) data; meteorological data; and the Amap Road Congestion Index. Employing an innovative integrated modeling framework combining light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM) and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) interpretability analysis, this research dissects the complex interactive relationships underlying traffic congestion around metro stations. The research results indicate that the LightGBM model can effectively identify road traffic congestion conditions around metro stations, and SHAP can effectively analyze the nonlinear relationship of the interaction between metro passenger outflow and POI facility density on road traffic congestion around metro stations. The study found that, when the density of pedestrian facilities exceeds 60 / km 2 , as the density of pedestrian facilities increases, its impact on road traffic congestion becomes positive, with an effect value above 0. When the density of government institutions exceeds 120 / km 2 and passenger outflow is greater than 120 people/10 min, the interaction between the two further exacerbates road traffic congestion. When company density is around 50 / km 2 , the SHAP value spikes sharply, reaching a maximum exceeding 0.6, indicating that, in areas with moderate company density but extremely high passenger flow, the interaction between the two generates a substantial positive predictive driving force for traffic congestion. When the density of business residential areas is low, it exerts an inhibitory effect on road traffic congestion; however, as its value increases, this inhibitory effect weakens and gradually transitions to a positive contribution. Further, regarding whether it is a peak period, the influence of off-peak periods on road traffic is compactly clustered around zero; however, once entering a peak period, the feature contribution exhibits a stepwise increase. These findings enhance the understanding of the causes of traffic congestion near urban metro stations, providing a robust empirical basis for optimizing functional zoning around stations, implementing differentiated facility allocation, and enabling precise traffic control strategies.
journal: Journal of Transportation Engineering, Part A: Systems

title: Mapping Coastal Resource–Environment Carrying Capacity in an Intensively Developed Coastal Area: Evidence from Rui’an, China
abstract: Coastal zones are dynamic land–sea interfaces where development pressures often approach ecological and environmental limits. Here, we operationalize a pressure–condition–response (P–C–R) framework to deliver a customized, high-resolution ( 30 × 30 m ) assessment of coastal resource–environment carrying capacity (RECC) for Rui’an (Zhejiang, China) using 2017 multisource geospatial, environmental, socioeconomic, and planning data sets. GIS-based spatial overlay and index modeling produce a composite coastal carrying capacity index (CAI) that ranges from 0.5 to 2.1, revealing strong spatial heterogeneity and a persistent “higher pressure north of the Feiyun River–lower pressure south of the river” pattern. Overload hotspots occupy ∼ 10 % of the coastal zone and cluster along the northern urban shoreline belt, whereas near-saturation dominates ( ∼ 78 % ), indicating widespread proximity to threshold conditions where incremental disturbances could shift local areas into overload. The cooccurrence of high pressure and constrained condition aligns with carrying risk concentrated where intensive human use coincides with limited buffering capacity; intensive land reclamation and shoreline artificialization are prominent contributors associated with this pattern. These outputs provide zoning-ready evidence to support differentiated governance pathways, including constraining additional development intensity and reducing loads in overloaded areas, institutionalizing capacity assessment index (CAI)-based early warning and adaptive controls across near-saturation belts, and maintaining ecological bottom lines in undercapacity areas.
journal: Journal of Water Resources Planning and Management

title: Research Hotspots and Evolutionary Trends ofEarthquake-Induced Landslides: A BibliometricAnalysis Based on Web of Science
abstract: Earthquake-induced landslides are a major natural hazard and have attracted extensive global attention. Using 9,160 articles retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, we screened 6,956 publications highly relevant to earthquake-induced landslides through Python-based processing and manual verification. We combined VOSviewer with a latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) topic model to quantify publication output, map keyword networks, delineate thematic structure, and trace research hotspot evolution. Publication trends exhibit three stages: an initial stage (1972–1999), a steady-growth stage (2000–2008), and a rapid-growth stage (2009–2024). The global research landscape has shifted from early dominance by Europe and North America to a multipolar pattern, with China emerging as a leading contributor while the United States, Italy, and Japan remain consistently productive. Research hotspots evolved from fundamental geological issues and slope-stability mechanisms to the widespread use of GIS and remote sensing for landslide inventory construction, spatial mapping, and hazard monitoring, followed by rapid growth in numerical modeling and machine learning. The LDA results cluster the literature into six research directions, and topic similarity analysis suggests that “mechanism studies” are most tightly coupled with “dynamic modeling,” whereas “cascading hazard impact assessment” is relatively independent. Overall, future research in this field is likely to emphasize (1) developing high-quality landslide inventories; (2) improving model transferability across events and regions; and (3) promoting application-oriented translation and decision support for risk governance.

title: Limbal Stromal Cell-Derived Exosomes Promote Corneal Epithelial-like Differentiation of Bone Marrow Mesenchymal Stem Cells Through miR-146a-5p-Associated Activation of the PI3K-Akt Pathway.
Physics-guided deep residual learning for sound absorption prediction of micro-perforated panels
abstract: To address the limited accuracy of analytical models, the high computational cost of finite element method (FEM) simulations, and the sample dependence of purely data-driven approaches for micro-perforated panel (MPP) sound absorption prediction, this study proposes a physics-guided deep residual network (PGDRN). A paired analytical-FEM dataset is constructed under identical structural parameters and frequency sampling points. Instead of directly fitting the complete FEM absorption curve, the FEM response is decomposed into an analytical baseline and an analytical-FEM residual correction. The network is trained to learn this residual discrepancy, while the analytical absorption coefficient and resonance mismatch are introduced as physics-guided features to enhance the representation of resonance-related frequency regions. Experiments on 1000 paired analytical-FEM samples show that PGDRN achieves an MAE of 0.0012, an RMSE of 0.0021, an R²of 0.9999, and a peak absorption coefficient error of 0.0022 on the test set. Compared with Mambular, the strongest data-driven baseline, PGDRN reduces MAE, RMSE, and peak error by 94.76%, 95.14%, and 95.53%, respectively. Ablation and limited-sample analyses confirm the contributions of residual learning and physics-guided features to prediction accuracy, peak-region stability, and sample efficiency. FEM sound-field visualization further supports the physical consistency of the predicted absorption behavior. The proposed method provides an accurate and interpretable surrogate model for rapid MPP sound absorption prediction under limited FEM samples.
