title: The genetic alchemy: deciphering WRKY's role in the flavor quality of horticultural crops
abstract: Fruits of horticultural crops are indispensable sources of nutrients and bioactive compounds, and their flavor quality, a complex phenotypic trait orchestrated by soluble sugars, organic acids, volatile aromas, is a pivotal determinant of their market competitiveness and consumer preference. Enhancing flavor quality has therefore become a primary priority of horticultural crop breeding. WRKY transcription factors (TFs) constitute one of the largest TF families in plants, and are emerging as central regulators of specialized metabolism underlying fruit flavor formation. In this review, we first identify two core evolutionary features of WRKY TFs in horticultural crops: cross-species conserved sucrose-acid regulatory clades and species-specific flavor regulatory clades. We then systematically summarize the regulatory roles of WRKY TFs in the accumulation of sugars, organic acids, volatile aromas, and bitter/pungent substances, and elaborate on the molecular mechanism by which they integrate environmental and hormone signals to coordinate flavor metabolism. We further propose a multi-dimensional regulatory model of WRKY-mediated flavor formation, and discuss future research directions as well as potential applications in molecular breeding for flavor enhancement. This work provides a comprehensive framework for understanding the role of WRKY in flavor regulation and offers guidance for the cultivation of high-quality horticultural crops.

title: ACR11 promotes nitrogen assimilation and protein productivity during urea cultivation in duckweed Lemna minor.
abstract: Nitrogen assimilation plays a crucial role in plant growth and protein accumulation. Urea is a widely used and low-cost nitrogen source; therefore, efficient assimilation of urea-derived nitrogen is critical for biomass accumulation and protein production in plants. However, the regulatory factors that enhance this process remain poorly understood. Here, we identify the chloroplast-localized ACT DOMAIN REPEAT 11 (ACR11) as a positive regulator of nitrogen assimilation in duckweed. Overexpression of LpACR11 increased growth rate, protein content and protein productivity of duckweed Lemna minor ZH0403 under urea nutrition, whereas RNAi-mediated knockdown caused opposite effects. Heterologous expression of LpACR11 in tobacco and rice also enhanced biomass and protein accumulation under urea cultivation conditions. Biochemical and metabolic analyses showed that LpACR11 overexpression was associated with increased Fd-GOGAT (ferredoxin-dependent glutamate synthase) activity, elevated glutamate accumulation, reduced ammonium accumulation and increased total amino acid content. Glutamate treatment further promoted GS2 (plastid glutamine synthetase) expression and activity, supporting a working model in which ACR11-associated enhancement of Fd-GOGAT activity increases glutamate accumulation and thereby promotes GS2-associated nitrogen assimilation. Together, these results indicate that ACR11 enhances chloroplast nitrogen-assimilation capacity and protein productivity during urea cultivation, providing a potential genetic target for improving protein productivity in duckweed and other crops.

title: Textile clusters as change agents for green transformation
abstract: The paper aims to examine the role of cluster organizations embedded in industrial clusters as agents of sustainability-driven competitiveness transformation in the European textile sector. Under increasing regulatory and industrial policy pressures at the EU level, sustainability and circularity are redefining the competitive conditions of the sector. The study identifies green practices supporting the transition to a low-carbon, circular and sustainable economy and analyzes them through the lens of coordination and governance mechanisms. The study covers nine European textile clusters, focusing specifically on the activities of their cluster organizations as meso-level governance actors. In-depth interviews with cluster coordinators were analyzed using open, axial and selective coding to identify and classify green practices across three areas, including integration, access to resources and education and awareness, on a four-level maturity scale. The study provides an empirical application and further development of a previously developed analytical model. The study identifies a comprehensive set of green practices undertaken by cluster organizations within textile clusters across three areas: integration, access to resources and education and awareness, which capture coordination mechanisms implemented by cluster organizations and reflect their governance role in green transformation. These practices can be interpreted as graduated strategic capabilities that support firms in adapting to sustainability-driven competitive pressures. Most clusters were found to apply lower-level initiatives, while more advanced practices were also observed, including cooperation with public authorities in legislative processes, participation in R&D projects and the implementation of green technologies. The study’s qualitative design, limited sample size and focus on coordinators restrict generalization. Nevertheless, it contributes to the literature by operationalizing bridging capacity in green transition processes, proposing a four-stage typology of green practices, identifying an implementation gap between declared priorities and applied measures and conceptualizing cluster organizations as hybrid governance structures combining leadership and partnership roles. By linking green transformation to competitiveness dynamics, the study extends existing research on cluster governance and collective value creation. Cluster organizations can function as governance platforms for green transformation by mobilizing resources, facilitating access to resources, strengthening value-chain integration, promoting circular models and enhancing environmental competencies among firms. The typology proposed may also support policymakers in designing differentiated industrial policies aligned with the governance maturity of cluster organizations. Clusters promote environmental awareness and integrate various entities in activities promoting sustainable development. The paper advances research on green transformation in industrial clusters by adopting a governance-oriented and processual perspective, using evidence from European textile clusters. It reframes green transformation as a competitiveness-enhancing process mediated by cluster organizations under regulatory and industrial policy pressure. It offers an empirical application and refinement of an analytical model of cluster activities, demonstrating how integrative, resource-based and educational functions constitute the operational dimension of bridging capacity in traditional industrial sectors.
journal: Competitiveness Review: An International Business Journal

title: Agentic AI in organizations: reimagining learning, autonomy, and human oversight
abstract: This viewpoint examines organizational implications of agentic AI systems in planning, selecting tools, executing multistep actions, and evaluating their own outputs with limited human intervention. This viewpoint synthesizes academic and practitioner insights to identify key organizational challenges associated with agentic AI drawing on organizational learning theory and recent research on human–AI collaboration, and propose practical directions for HR and learning and development. As agentic AI becomes more autonomous, it is reshaping organizational learning, human oversight, and accountability. Organizations will need to redesign learning practices and governance mechanisms to ensure that people and AI work together effectively. This conceptual viewpoint does not include empirical validation. Future research should examine the proposed ideas across different organizational settings. Organizations should assess workforce readiness, redesign learning around human–AI collaboration, and establish feedback mechanisms that strengthen learning, oversight, and accountability. This viewpoint shifts the discussion from technological capabilities of agentic AI to its organizational implications, offering practical guidance for organizations adapting to increasingly autonomous forms of work.
journal: Development and Learning in Organizations: An International Journal

title: Network positions and project-based innovation in cross-regional construction projects: a role embeddedness perspective
abstract: This study aims to explore the heterogeneous effects of network embeddedness on project-based innovation performance (PIP) within cross-regional construction collaboration networks, focusing on differences in network effects between project owners (POs) and cross-regional project teams (CPTs). Using 153 cross-regional construction projects completed in the Greater Bay Area between 2013 and 2023, this study applies social network analysis to construct lagged cumulative collaboration networks and measure five dimensions of network embeddedness. Hierarchical negative binomial regression models examine the linear and nonlinear effects of PO and CPT network positions on PIP. The network analysis shows that CPTs have broader connections, stronger bridging positions, and greater local cohesion, whereas POs are more concentrated within particular network communities. For POs, degree centrality shows a monotonically decreasing relationship with PIP, betweenness centrality has a negative effect, structural holes have a positive effect, clustering coefficient has an inverted U-shaped effect, and closeness centrality shows no stable effect. For CPTs, degree centrality and structural holes show inverted U-shaped relationships; closeness centrality and clustering coefficient have positive effects, whereas betweenness centrality has a negative effect. This study introduces a role embeddedness perspective by conceptualizing actor role as a boundary condition in translating network positions into PIP. Managerial embeddedness for POs and technical embeddedness for CPTs explain why the same type of network position can generate different innovation effects, clarifying the role dependence of these effects and informing differentiated network governance.

title: Leveraging digital capabilities for supply chain recovery and renewal: the mediating roles of spontaneous and creative improvisation
abstract: Building on the dynamic capability view (DCV) and supply chain (SC) literature on digitalization, improvisation and resilience, we examined how different digital capabilities influence different post-disruption SC resilience outcomes (recovery and renewal) through distinct forms of improvisation in cross-border SCs. Our sample comprises 217 matched Chinese supplier–buyer dyads, with buyers located in 66 countries. Confirmatory factor analysis and multiple regression were used to test the measurement model and hypothesized relationships, respectively. Robustness and endogeneity tests were also performed. We find that digital market orientation is positively associated with creative improvisation, while its relationship with spontaneous improvisation is non-significant. In contrast, digital process innovation is positively associated with spontaneous improvisation, while its relationship with creative improvisation is non-significant. Furthermore, spontaneous improvisation is positively associated with SC recovery, while creative improvisation is positively associated with SC renewal. Creative improvisation mediates the relationship between digital market orientation and SC renewal, while spontaneous improvisation mediates the relationship between digital process innovation and SC recovery. This study reveals distinct paths through which different digital capabilities contribute to post-disruption SC resilience. By differentiating digital capabilities, improvisational capabilities, and resilience outcomes, the study extends DCV-based SC resilience research by explaining how the adaptive potential embedded in these digital capabilities is translated through distinct improvisational capabilities into post-disruption SC resilience outcomes in cross-border SCs.
journal: International Journal of Operations & Production Management

title: Consumer propensity to adopt non-alcoholic wine: a configurational analysis of motivations and consumption profiles
abstract: This study aims to examine the propensity of Spanish consumers to adopt non-alcoholic wine, identifying the personal characteristics and consumption habits that explain this behaviour. The authors analyse three key motivations – social trends, health and price – to determine which consumer profiles are associated with each driver. The objective is to understand how different combinations of antecedent conditions shape willingness to consume non-alcoholic wine, addressing gaps in the literature and supporting segmentation strategies in a growing non-alcoholic and low-alcohol (NoLo) market. Using data from an online survey of 638 valid respondents, the authors apply fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) to identify multiple and asymmetric causal configurations leading to a high propensity to consume non-alcoholic wine. Five antecedent conditions are examined: age, gender, education, alcoholic beverage consumption and non-alcoholic beverage consumption. Three separate models are estimated, corresponding to the motivations of social trends, health and price. The configurational approach allows us to capture complexity, equifinality and causal asymmetry in consumer behaviour. Results reveal differentiated consumer profiles depending on the dominant motivation. Younger consumers with moderate non-alcoholic beverage habits show high propensity driven by social trends. Health-related propensity emerges in configurations combining higher education, lower alcoholic consumption and moderate non-alcoholic consumption. Price-driven propensity is associated with younger consumers and higher levels of alcoholic consumption. No single antecedent is necessary or sufficient, confirming that multiple causal paths explain adoption of non-alcoholic wine. The study is based on self-reported survey data from Spanish consumers, which may limit generalisability to other markets. Future research could incorporate cross-country comparisons, experimental designs or sensory evaluations to complement configurational findings. The use of fsQCA demonstrates the value of complexity-based approaches in wine research and encourages further application of configurational methods to understand heterogeneous consumer behaviour in emerging NoLo categories. The results provide practical guidance for wineries and marketers by linking each motivational driver to the consumer profiles identified in the analysis. Younger consumers with moderate non-alcoholic beverage habits show a high propensity driven by social trends, suggesting that communication strategies should reflect evolving consumption norms. Health-driven propensity is associated with highly educated consumers who report lower alcoholic consumption, indicating the relevance of health-oriented product information. Price-driven propensity is linked to younger consumers with higher alcoholic consumption, highlighting the need for competitive pricing strategies. These differentiated profiles support targeted segmentation in the growing NoLo category. Understanding motivations for consuming non-alcoholic wine supports public policies promoting healthier drinking habits and responsible consumption. Identifying profiles driven by health or price can inform initiatives aimed at reducing alcohol intake without compromising social participation. The findings highlight how changing social norms, especially among younger generations, may contribute to a cultural shift towards moderate or alcohol-free consumption patterns. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study is among the first to apply fsQCA to the analysis of non-alcoholic wine consumption. It advances understanding of how personal characteristics and consumption habits interact to shape adoption, moving beyond linear models to a configurational perspective. By identifying multiple causal paths leading to high propensity, the research contributes novel theoretical and managerial insights to the wine business literature and responds to calls for deeper exploration of consumer profiles in the NoLo market.
journal: International Journal of Wine Business Research

title: The REAL framework: evaluating the cognitive and formative impact of generative AI
abstract: This paper aims to address a gap in contemporary scholarship on generative artificial intelligence (AI) by shifting attention from the functional evaluation of AI systems to the formative impact of repeated AI use on the human user. It introduces formative evaluation as a complementary approach concerned with how sustained AI use may shape cognitive skills, habits, reasoning, judgment and agency over time. To address this concern, the paper proposes the REAL Framework (Retained, Eroded, Atrophied, Leveraged) as a practical means of evaluating and intentionally shaping patterns of AI use. This conceptual paper develops the REAL Framework through interdisciplinary synthesis and theoretical analysis. It integrates scholarship on human agency and principal-agent relationships with research on cognitive offloading, cognitive reserve, desirable difficulty, automation bias and human–AI collaboration. Emerging empirical research on the cognitive effects of generative AI is used to contextualize and support the framework. The resulting four-dimensional framework is then illustrated through its application to professional practice and considered in relation to potential objections, limitations and directions for future empirical research. The analysis identifies formative evaluation as a distinct and underdeveloped dimension of AI evaluation. While emerging research increasingly documents potential cognitive effects of generative AI use, practical means of evaluating and responding to those effects remain limited. The REAL Framework addresses this gap through four dimensions: Retained, Eroded, Atrophied and Leveraged. Together, these dimensions distinguish between AI use that preserves human agency and cognitive engagement, use that risks over-delegation and capability loss, and use that intentionally leverages AI to enhance human thinking and judgment. The REAL Framework is a conceptual and reflective framework that has not yet been empirically validated or operationalized as a measurement instrument. Longitudinal research is needed to examine the formative effects of sustained generative AI use and determine whether structured application of the framework influences patterns of AI delegation or preserves cognitive engagement and capability. Future research should develop and test measures associated with the framework’s four dimensions and examine their applicability across educational, professional and organizational contexts. The REAL Framework provides individuals and institutions with a practical means of evaluating how generative AI is being incorporated into learning and professional practice. Its four reflective dimensions can help users identify inappropriate over-delegation, preserve important cognitive and professional capabilities, and redesign AI use to support rather than replace human reasoning and judgment. The framework may also inform institutional guidance, professional development and AI literacy initiatives by shifting attention from whether AI should be used toward how it can be used while preserving meaningful human agency and engagement. As generative AI becomes increasingly embedded in education, work and everyday decision-making, its societal effects will depend not only on the capabilities of AI systems but also on how their use shapes human capabilities over time. The REAL Framework highlights the importance of preserving human agency, reasoning, judgment and cognitive engagement while benefiting from technological advancement. It encourages a broader societal conversation about which human capacities should remain meaningfully exercised and which may appropriately be delegated to increasingly capable AI systems. This paper introduces formative evaluation as a distinct conceptual approach to understanding generative AI use, complementing prevailing functional approaches concerned primarily with AI systems, governance and responsible use. It advances the REAL Framework as a structured means of translating emerging concerns about AI’s cognitive and formative effects into reflective practice. By connecting human agency and delegation with cognitive development, the framework shifts attention from evaluating what AI can do to evaluating what repeated AI use may be doing to the human user.
journal: Journal of Ethics in Entrepreneurship and Technology

title: Innovating public sector education: integrating lean and micro-credentials for sustainable governance in Brazil
abstract: This study examines how Lean principles, micro-credential-based professional development, and co-creation can strengthen public governance and operational efficiency in managing Brazil's Decentralized Execution Terms (TEDs). It addresses how a capacity-building intervention can diagnose process bottlenecks, develop civil-servant competencies, support the production of standardized operational guidance, and connect learning to institutional practice. The study also seeks to identify the conditions under which this model may be adapted by other public administrations rather than replicated without regard to local regulatory, organizational, and technological contexts. Using Design Science Research, the study conducted a mixed-methods organizational intervention with 37 civil servants from Brazil's Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock. Three phases combined institutional diagnosis, a 120-h modular training program, and the co-creation of three operational manuals. Quantitative indicators from the learning platform and satisfaction ratings were analyzed descriptively. Interviews, open-ended survey responses, forum posts, meeting records, and workshop outputs underwent two-cycle content analysis. The strands were integrated during interpretation through a statistics-by-themes joint display to examine convergence, complementarity, and tension. The program achieved an 83% module completion rate, a mean assessment score of 8.3/10, and positive ratings for content clarity (92%), organization (95%), and practical applicability (88%). Qualitative analysis identified four themes: practical relevance and flexibility; workplace application and knowledge sharing; professional confidence and institutional belonging; and constraints, improvement needs, and institutionalization. Participants reported using course materials in verification routines, team meetings, and colleague induction. Engagement was strongest when learning addressed immediate operational problems, while more abstract modules required stronger contextualization and facilitator support. The single-ministry pilot and small voluntary sample of 37 participants limit statistical power and generalizability. Several outcomes were self-reported, and the study did not include a comparison group or longitudinal follow-up, preventing causal claims or conclusions about sustained competency retention and cultural change. The absence of formal recognition for micro-credentials in federal public administration also constrains scalability. Future research should test the model across institutions, use larger samples and longitudinal designs, compare pedagogical approaches, assess workplace effects, and examine regulatory pathways for institutionalizing micro-credentials. The study offers public managers a condition-based model for linking professional learning to concrete administrative problems. Its practical value lies in combining modular micro-credentials, Lean tools, and civil-servant co-creation to produce usable operational artifacts. Adaptation requires leadership support, meaningful participation, adequate digital infrastructure, protected learning time, alignment with recognized work problems, and credible recognition of micro-credentials. Lightweight, mobile-accessible delivery can support geographically dispersed teams, while joint development of manuals and checklists can strengthen standardization, knowledge sharing, onboarding, and process-improvement discussions. The findings indicate how professional development can support more capable, transparent, and accountable public institutions. Flexible, mobile-accessible learning can broaden access for civil servants working across geographically dispersed units, although the study did not directly measure equity effects. By strengthening process understanding, knowledge sharing, and collaborative problem-solving, the intervention aligns most directly with SDG 16. The government–university partnership also reflects SDG 17 by combining academic expertise with practitioner knowledge to address public-sector challenges and support improved management of public resources. The study's originality lies in integrating Lean-oriented process improvement, micro-credential-based learning, and co-created operational artifacts within a single public-sector capacity-building intervention. Rather than treating certification, process tools, and participation as separate elements, it identifies a mechanism in which micro-credentials structure focused learning, Lean directs that learning toward work problems, and co-creation embeds practitioners' knowledge in shared resources. The research provides empirical evidence from a Brazilian federal administration and specifies the institutional conditions required for adaptation, avoiding assumptions of automatic replication.
journal: Journal of International Cooperation in Education

title: Navigating the digital: university business model patterns and aligning digital transformation strategies
abstract: Digital transformation poses various challenges for universities, necessitating adjustments to business models and strategic positioning. We aim to identify university business model patterns and derive matching digital transformation strategy options, providing universities with a structured basis for aligning transformation efforts with their strategic orientation. Based on an adapted Business Model Canvas for universities, we qualitatively analyze business model data collected from the 30 largest German universities. Data were structured into 59 subcategories across nine business model elements and analyzed through cross-case analysis in ten iterative workshops, combining quantitative and qualitative data to derive patterns and corresponding strategy options. Five university business model patterns exist: three research-oriented (excellence, entrepreneurial and domain-specific) and two education-oriented (teacher training and education), including a distinct distance-learning subset. Research-oriented patterns show higher third-party and state funding and more research staff, while education-oriented patterns emphasize teaching scale. Matching Digital Transformation Strategy options were derived across four dimensions: technology use, value creation, structural change and financial aspects. The study is limited to German universities, which may influence the generalizability of the findings to other higher education contexts. Further research should examine our business model patterns in other countries and education systems. Findings guide university management in aligning digital transformation strategies with their specific business model pattern rather than standardized approaches, requiring coordinated governance across research, teaching and administration. Findings suggest uniform funding and governance approaches may not reflect universities' heterogeneous orientations, calling for more differentiated, equitable higher education policy. This study offers one of the first empirically derived typologies of university business models, systematically linking distinct patterns to matching digital transformation strategy options.

title: When conversational AI sells: objectivity disruption, persuasion knowledge and social-validation cues in sponsored AI recommendations
abstract: Drawing on persuasion knowledge theory and machine heuristic theory, this research examines separately how sponsorship in conversational AI recommendations influences consumer responses through perceived manipulation and perceived AI objectivity and whether social validation cues mitigate these effects. Across one pre-test and four experiments (total N = 732), this research tests sponsorship effects, two mediators in separate models, social validation as a boundary condition, and the full model in a scripted, single-turn chat-style interface. Across static screenshots and a scripted, single-turn interface, sponsorship increased perceived manipulation and reduced perceived AI objectivity. In separate mediation models, each mediator carried significant indirect effects on trust, engagement intention, and purchase intention. Social validation improved product-directed evaluations but did not consistently alleviate sponsorship-related concerns about the AI recommender or its recommendation process. This research offers a dual-route account of sponsorship backfire and an exploratory attribute-matching proposition such that product-directed social-validation cues may improve product evaluations without resolving agent-directed concerns.
journal: Journal of Research in Interactive Marketing

title: Beyond moonlighting: side-gigs and employee performance
abstract: We examine how types of secondary activities relate to primary job performance under bounded rationality and when managers should permit, encourage, or restrict them. Using an archival dataset from professional baseball (1945–2018), we classify secondary activities as unrelated, teaching-related, or learning-related. We estimate Ordinary Least Squares and difference-in-differences models around the 1965 Major League Baseball (MLB) draft and measure performance with Wins Above Replacement Unrelated and teaching-related secondary activities are associated with lower performance, whereas learning-related secondary activities are associated with higher performance than teaching-related secondary activities. When the job becomes more salient, these negative associations intensify, while the performance advantage of learning-related secondary activities widens. Evidence derives from a single industry and an observational setting. The cognitively aligned typology and boundary-condition logic refine Behavioral Theory of the Firm accounts of attention allocation and offer testable extensions. Rather than adopting blanket rules, managers should evaluate secondary activities according to their cognitive demands, intensity, alignment with the focal role, and demonstrated performance consequences, and revisit these evaluations as the stakes of the primary role rise. Differentiated policies, coupled with equitable skill-building alternatives, can enhance worker wellbeing while protecting core performance. We move beyond the “secondary activity versus no secondary activity” view by testing a cognitively aligned typology and its moderators, translating Behavioral Theory of the Firm into actionable policy guidance.

title: Impact of confidentiality assurances and self-disclosure on user satisfaction with AI-assisted emotional support
abstract: While AI conversational agents such as Woebot offer a promising avenue for improving psychological well-being through empathetic conversations with nonclinical populations, growing privacy breach risks of AI are a significant threat to their use for emotional support. Therefore, this study aims to examine how confidentiality assurances from AI agents affect user satisfaction with AI-assisted emotional support, exploring the serial-mediation effects of perceived confidentiality and self-disclosure and the moderation effect of privacy concerns. In a controlled experiment, 350 US adults interacted with a standardized AI emotional support agent in a three-dimensional metaverse and were randomly assigned to either the confidentiality-assurance condition or the control condition. Results showed that confidentiality assurances significantly increased user satisfaction with AI-assisted emotional support. Moreover, we observed the mediation effects of perceived confidentiality and the serial-mediation effects of both perceived confidentiality and willingness to self-disclose. This study contributes to the privacy literature by exploring how brief, standardized confidentiality assurances function in an AI-driven emotional support context. Instead of focusing on complex, personalized privacy designs, these findings offer a nuanced perspective on human-AI interactions that a simple structural cue can serve as a sufficient heuristic anchor to strengthen users' willingness to self-disclose across varying user traits.

title: Epistemic governance of AI augmented grounded theory: a validation gate framework for scaling qualitative inquiry
abstract: This paper develops a conceptual methodological framework for governing the use of artificial intelligence in the grounded theory. It addresses the risk that AI-generated outputs may be mistaken for qualitative evidence, interpretation or theory. The paper synthesizes grounded theory traditions, computational grounded theory, large language model supported coding, human in the loop research, qualitative trustworthiness and critical AI scholarship. It develops a validation gate framework and uses a worked methodological vignette to show how AI suggestions can be documented, checked and bounded. The paper argues that AI can support retrieval, organization, candidate coding, comparison and adversarial audit, but cannot authorize meaning, categories or theory. It identifies seven validation gates and four modes of AI use: assistive, dialogic, generative and adversarial audit. The paper differentiates epistemic governance from reflexivity, trustworthiness, auditability and human in the loop design by focusing on the epistemic status of AI outputs before they enter the analytic record. It offers operational pass criteria for preserving theoretical sensitivity, reflexivity, auditability and researcher accountability when grounded theory is scaled through AI.

title: EEG-Based Decoding of Musical Mode and Melodic Direction Using Empirical Mode Decomposition
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) has proven to be a powerful tool for decoding neural activity in real-life scenarios, including the perception and processing of emotions elicited by music. Among the various musical features that modulate these responses, musical mode and melodic direction (or contour) play a central role. This work proposes a novel EEG feature extraction framework based on Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) to decompose EEG signals recorded during active piano performance for the detection of these two musical features. Energy-based descriptors were computed from the first four Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs) obtained through EMD and used to train a Wide Neural Network classifier. The model performance was benchmarked against several standard classifiers commonly employed in EEG classification tasks. Two experimental scenarios were explored: intra-subject and intersubject. In the former case, the proposed framework achieved average accuracies of 84%, whereas in the inter-subject case, accuracies reached 81% on average using the first IMF, with AUC-ROC values of 0.9 on average in both cases. A frequency-domain analysis revealed a strong correspondence between the IMFs and conventional EEG sub-bands, except for certain specific frequency components that were not fully represented. Predominant activations were observed over the frontal, temporal, and parietooccipital regions, areas consistently associated with music processing. Furthermore, the proposed method demonstrated robustness to handedness, successfully classifying EEG data across participants regardless of their dominant hand. These findings highlight the potential of EMD-based feature extraction for identifying music-related neural patterns and contribute to advancing research in Music Information Retrieval (MIR), affective neuroscience, and the broader understanding of the neural encoding of musical structure.

title: A Fiber Coil Defect Detection Method Based on Feature Enhancement and Lightweight Network
abstract: The fiber coil is the core sensing component of a fiber optic gyroscope, and its winding quality directly affects gyroscope measurement accuracy. However, gap and stack defects frequently occur during the fiber coil winding process. Traditional detection methods suffer from low efficiency and poor generalization ability. Moreover, existing deep learning-based detection methods are often constrained by illumination conditions and require complex image preprocessing. To address these challenges, we propose a lightweight, high-precision automated visual inspection framework tailored for fiber coil winding. The SimAM attention mechanism is integrated into the backbone feature extraction network to strengthen the model’s focus on defect-related features. The Normalized Wasserstein Distance (NWD) loss is then introduced to optimize bounding box regression and improve the localization accuracy of small defects. In addition, Focal Loss replaces the original binary cross-entropy loss for confidence estimation to alleviate the foreground-background imbalance in dense detection. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an mAP of 92.33% and a detection speed of 114 FPS for fiber coil winding defect detection. Compared with existing methods, the proposed approach offers a simple structure, high accuracy, and real-time detection capability, making it suitable for engineering applications.

title: A 60-m Distance Measurement Exploiting the Linewidth Narrowing of the SMI Readout
abstract: Using a cheap DFB laser with coherence length ${\mathrm {L}}_{\mathrm {c}} =7$ m and reading the field returning from a remote target by means of a Self-Mixing Interferometry (SMI) scheme, we are able to sense returns and measure distances up to 60 m thanks to the (1 +C)2 factor of increase of ${\mathrm{L}}_{\mathrm {c.~ }}$ due to optical feedback into the laser cavity. The simplified hardware and low cost of the SMI configuration makes it attractive as medium distances LiDAR for automotive applications.

title: SRMP-S: Self-Refining Multi-Planner Strategy for Long-Horizon Robotic Tasks
abstract: Enabling robotic agents to perform complex long-horizon tasks has been a long-standing goal in robotics and artificial intelligence (AI). Existing Large Language Models (LLMs)-based symbolic planners auto-generate Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) specifications to bridge language and formal reasoning, but they rely on a single open-loop planner and lack autonomous error diagnosis or model refinement, limiting robustness in long-horizon tasks. To address these issues, we propose Self-Refining Multi-Planner Strategy (SRMP-S), a closed-loop framework that integrates the semantic flexibility of LLMs with the rigor of symbolic planning through two key innovations. Firstly, SRMP-S employs a multi-strategy planner ensemble, concurrently executing multiple heterogeneous symbolic planners to broaden first-attempt solvability and produce high-fidelity, cross-validated failure diagnostics. Secondly, it introduces a self-refinement mechanism that automatically converts these diagnostics into structured natural language (NL) feedback to iteratively refine the LLMs-generated PDDL models, enabling autonomous recovery from initial modeling inaccuracies. Experimental results demonstrate that SRMP-S achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple domains, outperforming existing LLM-based planners.

title: Convex Data-Driven Model Predictive Control for Trajectory Tracking in Robotic Manipulators
abstract: Accurate trajectory tracking is a fundamental control task in robotics, typically achieved using model-based methods. Computed Torque Control (CTC) is computationally efficient but struggles to handle system constraints, while Model Predictive Control (MPC) can manage constraints but often results in nonlinear formulations. This work introduces a convex Model Predictive Control (MPC) formulation that incorporates learned dynamics for a robot manipulator. A nonparametric model is used to learn the residual between a nominal model and the observed dynamics, using an inverse dynamics formulation. Convexification is achieved by applying implicit partial differentiation to linearize the inverse dynamics model augmented with the residual model along the reference trajectory, resulting in a Linear Time-Varying (LTV) system. Extensive simulations and hardware experiments on a Franka Emika Panda manipulator demonstrate that our convex MPC approach outperforms learning-based baselines in handling a broad range of model mismatches and constraints. Results also show that learning the residual in inverse dynamics form offers better tracking performance than learning the residual in forward dynamics.

title: Learning Equality Constraints From Trajectory Demonstrations
abstract: Equality constraints are common in robotics, arising in applications such as pose-constrained manipulation, coordinated motion, and task-space planning. Classical constrained planners typically assume an analytic constraint function, whereas in practice only feasible demonstrations may be available. We study how to learn explicit equality constraints directly from such demonstrations. We propose Orthonormal Neural Constraint Learning (ONCL), a method that learns multiple scalar constraint functions jointly and represents the equality constraint by their common zero set. Rather than estimating local normal directions and generating large amounts of supervised off-constraint data as related works, ONCL regularizes the gradients of different constraint functions to be normalized and mutually orthogonal, inducing a structured local normal space during learning. This yields an explicit differentiable constraint model in the original state space for evaluation and downstream planning. We evaluate ONCL on ten synthetic and robotic datasets spanning dimensions from 2 to 12. ONCL significantly outperforms each of three baselines on six datasets, while remaining competitive on the other datasets. We further validate ONCL on a physical KUKA iiwa 14 using kinesthetic demonstrations collected by a human operator. The learned pose constraint is subsequently used on the same platform for downstream trajectory planning under a modified task objective and an additional known obstacle-avoidance constraint.

title: Physically Aware Generative Design for Spatial Mechanism Synthesis: A Differentiable Diffusion-Refinement Framework
abstract: Spatial mechanism synthesis requires joint reasoning over discrete topology and continuous geometry under strict loop-closure constraints. Existing search-based methods are often tied to predefined topology spaces, while purely data-driven generators can produce topologically plausible but kinematically infeasible mechanisms. This paper proposes GenRefMechSyn, a physics-aware generative framework that integrates Mimic, a Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based topology–geometry sketch generator, Refiner, a differentiable kinematic refiner, and Judge, a refinement-aware value model. Mimic proposes candidate mechanism sketches, Refiner optimizes continuous geometry under fixed topology and projects candidates toward the kinematic-feasibility region, and Judge uses refinement feedback to guide diffusion sampling toward candidates with higher downstream refinability. Under a 1000-trial acceptance protocol, GenRefMechSyn achieves 81.6% two-translational-DOF (2T) kinematic validity; controlled baselines obtain 6.6% for DiT+Refiner without Judge guidance/feedback augmentation, 84.3% for genetic algorithm (GA)+Refiner with a favorable fixed topology, and 12.2% for multi-topology GA+Refiner. The generated mechanisms reach loop-closure residuals and task errors on the order of $10^{-3}$ and $10^{-4}$, respectively. The same architecture and seed set are also used in an independently trained two-rotational-DOF (2R) feedback run, showing applicability to a separately trained rotational task.

title: Latent Space 3D Shape Servoing With FEM-Based Dynamic Modeling
abstract: In this letter, we introduce a novel shape control framework that precisely guides a soft 3D object toward a desired shape using a robotic arm. Our framework seamlessly integrates vision, object physics behavior from a dynamic Finite Element Model (FEM), and latent-space representations to achieve accurate and adaptive shape control. Our method starts with any differentiable mapping function that takes the high dimensional 3D mesh representing a soft object as input and projects it into a low dimensional latent space to get a new compact representation of the object that is suitable for control. By leveraging the FEM model and the differentiability of this mapping function, we derive the analytical relationship that links the motion of the latent representation to the motion of the robot gripper to which the object is attached. Building on this formulation, we design a novel closed-loop shape servoing algorithm. To enhance robustness against model approximations, we integrate real-time visual tracking using an RGB-D camera, allowing for continuous correction of any discrepancies between the physical object and its model. We validate the effectiveness of our approach through real-world experiments on an elastic deformable object, employing two distinct mapping techniques for shape feature extraction: Autoencoder and Laplacian-based descriptor.

title: An Optimization Framework for Intraoperative Suture Planning via Physics-Aware Differentiable Graph Neural Network-Based Surrogates
MvT: Event-based Multi-view Projection for Multiple Object Tracking
abstract: Event cameras are increasingly used for Multiple Object Tracking (MOT), but their asynchronous event output often requires specialized methods. Existing processing methods primarily follow two paradigms, pseudo-frames and event-by-event. The former is the prevailing approach since its data format aligns with images, making image-based techniques applicable. However, it suffers from tracking failures when trajectories overlap or are spatially close on pseudo-frames. Facing this challenge, we propose a multi-view pipeline, Multi-view Tracking (MvT), which preserves the 2D data format to leverage image-based techniques directly while introducing additional spatio-temporal views to resolve tracking ambiguities in a single view. MvT comprises a Multi-view Projection (MvP) module and a Multi-view Fusion (MvF) stage. MvP encodes events into three complementary spatio-temporal views while mitigating the pattern discretization. Within MvF, multi-view results are unified into a 3D coordinate system, and tracklets are associated through an optimization model subject to specific criteria combination. Evaluations on four datasets, including our self-collected Small Objects Dataset (SOD), show that MvT seamlessly integrates image-based methods and outperforms existing non-learning and learning trackers in generalized scenarios, and effectively resolves the single-view tracking ambiguities. Being training-free, MvT is applicable when ground-truth annotation is infeasible, thereby highlighting its practical, data-efficient potential. Code is available at https://github.com/zhazhabiu/MvTracking.

title: EcoxPU: Autonomous Multi-Agent Orchestration for Energy-Efficient Disaggregated LLM Inference on Heterogeneous xPUs
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) inference is increasingly served on disaggregated clusters that combine different accelerator types, including NVIDIA GPUs, Huawei Ascend NPUs, and Kunlunxin AI processors. We show that these heterogeneous xPUs exhibit distinct energy-performance behaviors across inference phases and model modules, so a fixed deployment can waste substantial energy even when latency targets are met. This paper presents EcoxPU , an autonomous multi-agent framework for energy-efficient disaggregated LLM inference. EcoxPU jointly coordinates Prefill-Decode (PD) separation and Attention-Feed-Forward Network (FFN) disaggregation, assigning compute-bound and memory-bound work to suitable devices while adapting frequency and load placement at runtime. Evaluated on a heterogeneous cluster with NVIDIA H100, Huawei Ascend 910B, and Kunlunxin P800, EcoxPU reduces energy consumption by 31.9–45% (42% on average), while maintaining $\le$ ≤ 6% latency overhead and $\le$ ≤ 2% perplexity variation. It also improves MoE-FFN utilization on Ascend 910B to 82.3%, and cross-domain transfer learning accelerates agent adaptation by 2.67×.
journal: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems

title: A Fault Diagnosis and Differentiated Processing Strategy for Grid Side Overcurrent Faults in Electric Traction Drive System
abstract: Grid-side overcurrent (GSOC) in the traction transformer is a system-level fault in the electric traction drive system. Once it occurs, the traction control unit indiscriminately trips the main circuit breaker to ensure safety, causing the train to stop and requiring inspection and maintenance by the crew. This excessive protection and manual maintenance approach reduces the availability and operational efficiency of the trains. Therefore, this article proposes a fault diagnosis and differentiated processing strategy for GSOC. First, the GSOC mechanism and the degree of deterioration are analyzed, and the different types of GSOC are classified as permanent fault or temporary fault. Second, the effective segment of the fault signal is selected, and the fault temporal features are extracted. Third, the differentiated processing strategy is proposed based on the diagnostic results and the degree of fault deterioration. Finally, the fault diagnostic model is established based on random forest classifier, and then the fault scenario is reproduced on the RT-LAB and the diagnostic model is implemented using a digital signal processor to complete the verification experiments. The experimental results show that, compared with existing methods, the proposed method can not only achieve 100% diagnostic accuracy but also significantly shorten the diagnostic time. Moreover, the differentiated processing strategy can greatly reduce the trains’ stopping time and frequency caused by GSOC.

title: Instantaneous-Value Modeling of DC–DC Converters: From Switched System Models to Smooth Continuous-Time Models
abstract: Switched system models of DC–DC converters cannot be directly analyzed or controlled using conventional continuous-time system theory. To address the problem, we propose a smoothing-based modeling approach in which sigmoid functions are employed based on a generalized switched-system formulation. First, logical variables are defined to represent the mode-switching conditions of the converter, enabling the construction of a logical switched dynamical model. Next, smooth and continuous sigmoid functions are introduced to approximate these logical variables. This approach was used to develop smooth continuous-time models for single-ended primary-inductor, Zeta, Cuk, and interleaved parallel DC–DC converters. Simulation and experimental results of single-ended primary-inductor converter and interleaved parallel buck converter reveal that the proposed models accurately capture the instantaneous behavior of the converters. This modeling method provides a unified framework for representing multimodal switching behavior and various circuit phenomena across different operating modes, thereby improving the accuracy, applicability, and generality of converter models. The proposed smooth and differentiable model was used for stability and dynamic analysis, providing guidance for parameter selection and the development of more effective control strategies to optimize the system operating performance.

title: A Review on ANN-Based Behavioral Modeling Techniques for High-Efficiency Power Amplifiers
abstract: This article presents a comprehensive review of artificial neural network (ANN)-based behavioral modeling techniques for high-efficiency power amplifiers (PAs). As wireless systems demand greater linearity and efficiency, accurate modeling of PA nonlinearity and memory effects becomes essential. We systematically explore fundamental and advanced ANN architectures including memoryless networks, and memory networks, such as temporal encoding, recurrent models, knowledge-infused networks, attention mechanisms, and hybrid approaches, and evaluate their capabilities in capturing complex PA dynamics. This study further investigates optimization algorithms for enhancing ANN model performance and their integration into digital predistortion (DPD) systems for linearization. A dedicated section discusses embedded deployment considerations, highlighting tradeoffs between accuracy, complexity, and real-time applicability on platforms, such as field-programmable gate arrays and digital signal processors. Finally, we provide architectural selection guidelines and identify future research directions, including lightweight model design, multiband modeling, and automated ANN-driven PA optimization. This review demonstrates the practical utility of ANN-based techniques for advancing PA design in next-generation communication systems.

title: Analysis and Mitigation of Grid Current Distortion in Single-Stage DAB AC–DC Converters With Minimum Peak Current
abstract: Power feedforward control is utilized in single-stage dual-active-bridge (DAB) AC–DC converters for natural power factor correction. However, this approach renders the grid current highly dependent on the modulation strategy and susceptible to practical circuit nonlinearities, which result in a mismatch between the actual and modeled power. In this article, the optimal operating modes to minimize peak current are first analyzed and the grid current constraints based on the conventional piecewise-linear model are derived to achieve the unity power factor. The continuity and sinusoidal purity of the grid current are then evaluated in terms of mode transitions and absolute power deviations. To address distortion issues, a charge-equivalent linearized commutation model is proposed. The proposed model achieves real-time equivalent linearization of the nonlinear commutation process during the dead time considering the magnetizing current. Based on the commutation model, the instantaneous power for single-stage DAB AC–DC converters is accurately determined. Furthermore, an automatic mode selection strategy and the computational flow are developed to mitigate grid current distortion. Finally, a 1-kW laboratory prototype with a 40-VDC output is constructed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Nonsequential Multiobjective Integrated Optimal Design of LLC Resonant Converters Based on Interlinking Variables
abstract: Recent advances in LLC resonant converters have intensified the demand for effective multiobjective optimization techniques to achieve higher efficiency, increased power density, and improved thermal stability. This article presents an interlinking-variable-based nonsequential integrated multiobjective optimization framework tailored for LLC resonant converters. Unlike conventional sequential optimization approaches that treat the magnetizing inductance and the resonant inductance as fixed targets imposed between separate design stages, the proposed method redefines these values as explicit functions of the magnetic design variables, removing the equality constraints inherent in the sequential structure and unifying all circuit-level and magnetic-level design variables within a single optimization process. The interlinking relationships are evaluated through a hybrid analysis model combining time-domain circuit analysis with an ANN-based magnetic surrogate. Hardware prototypes designed by the proposed and conventional sequential methods are fabricated and experimentally compared. The proposed method improves the converter efficiency by 1.3%, reduces the total component volume by 9.0%, and decreases the total computation time by 56% compared with the conventional sequential design.

title: Predictive Control Strategies for CC-CV Charging of Offboard Chargers: Formulation, Comprehensive Analysis, and Experimental Validation
abstract: When conventional voltage-oriented control (VOC) and direct power control (DPC) strategies are applied to electric vehicle (EV) chargers, they can compromise their performance owing to a cascaded control structure with limited bandwidth and controller-gain sensitivity under varying charging conditions. Alternatively, finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) has emerged as a promising solution due to its direct use of discrete switching states and multiobjective optimization capabilities. However, a systematic investigation and comprehensive analysis of current-based and power-based FCS-MPC strategies for offboard EV chargers in terms of grid power quality, charger efficiency, battery side ripple, computational complexity, and control robustness under varied charging profiles has not been explored yet. To fill this research gap, this article presents a comprehensive formulation, implementation, validation, and analysis of predictive current control (PCC) and predictive power control (PPC) strategies for a two-stage offboard charger operating under constant current-constant voltage (CC-CV) charging conditions. In addition, a new charge cycle efficiency metric is introduced to quantify overall charger efficiency during the complete charging process. To validate the effectiveness of both methods experimentally, a two-stage offboard charging system with a dSPACE MicroLabBox control platform is developed to charge a 2.4 kWh, 400 V battery pack. The charger’s performance with the PCC and PPC schemes is holistically evaluated under steady-state, transient, CC-CV charging, and parameter mismatch conditions. Finally, the tradeoffs and selective guidelines of both predictive control strategies for EV charging applications are highlighted.

title: High-Accuracy Noninvasive Submodule Current Measurement in StakPak IGBTs Using an Ampere-Law-Guided Rectangular PCB Rogowski Coil
abstract: Submodule current distribution in StakPak insulated gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs) is important for device condition assessment. Existing internal current measurement methods for press-pack IGBTs usually require opening the device package. The special package structure of StakPak IGBTs enables rectangular printed circuit board Rogowski coils (PCB RCs) to be externally installed at the collector protrusions without opening or modifying the device package. However, representative fixed-conductor-based designs may suffer from reduced accuracy in complex conductor environments. This letter proposes a high-accuracy noninvasive submodule current measurement method using an optimized rectangular PCB RC mounted at the collector protrusion. Guided by Ampere’s circuital law, the coil measurement process is modeled as a discrete-sampling approximation of the continuous closed-path integral, revealing the dependence of the discretization error upper bound on the number of turns and turn-distribution uniformity. Accordingly, an arc-corner and turn-density optimization method is proposed. Finite-element results show that, compared with the representative existing rectangular coil, the area percentage of the low mutual-inductance-deviation region is increased from 31.36% to 93.00%. Experiments show that the interference current of the optimized PCB RC is reduced to 4.84% of that of the original oblique-corner PCB RC and 13.1% of that of the mini commercial Rogowski coil. In the full-submodule conduction test, the average error between the summed submodule current and the reference total current during the turn-on interval is 0.52%, verifying the effectiveness of the proposed noninvasive method.

title: Integrative phylogenomics uncovers hidden diversity and repeated cave colonizations in Dinaric pseudoscorpions.
journal: Cladistics : the international journal of the Willi Hennig Society

title: Five Decades of Citizen Science Reveal Erosion of Hotspots of Multifaceted Plant Diversity
abstract: Biodiversity includes taxonomic, phylogenetic, and functional diversity but the changes in these facets at regional scales remain unclear and often context dependent. Using 2.5 million citizen science observations of 1957 vascular plant species across 53 years in SW‐Germany, we assessed changes in seven biodiversity metrics. Rather than a general decline, we found different facets exhibited different trends in both direction and magnitude of change. Phylogenetic and taxonomic diversity change were mostly negatively correlated, and change in functional diversity was independent from the others. We identified the role of climate and human activity influencing the change in taxonomic and functional diversity, while phylogenetic diversity was also affected by geodiversity. Crucially, we detected consistent erosion of biodiversity hotspots across all facets, while areas with low initial diversity tended to gain species. These findings highlight the need to consider multiple biodiversity facets and local context dependency to better understand biodiversity change at regional scales.

title: Integrated chemical profiling, transcriptomics and functional validation elucidate the multifunctional benefits of a triple-ferment filtrate complex for skin aging intervention.
The Evolution and Clinical Utility of Oral Epithelial Dysplasia Grading Systems: A Narrative Review.
Receptive English proficiency across programs in engineering education
abstract: English proficiency is increasingly recognized as a prerequisite for disciplinary participation in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) higher education, yet large scale evidence on institutional variation among non-English-major engineering students remains limited in Vietnam. This study examined receptive English proficiency across three program types, mass, advanced, and international, using population-level placement data from 17,561 first-year engineering students over three consecutive cohorts (2022-2024). Listening and reading performance (10-990 total) was analyzed through a two-way general linear model (GLM) to assess main and interaction effects of program structure and academic year. Results indicated a consistent proficiency hierarchy (advancedinternationalmass), with program type explaining the largest proportion of variance (partial η²=0.21). Academic year demonstrated a medium effect (partial η²=0.09), reflecting a progressive decline in cohort readiness, while the interaction effect (partial η²=0.03) showed more pronounced decreases in the mass program. These findings suggest that English-medium environments partially buffer national level declines but cannot fully offset systemic weaknesses in receptive preparedness. Implications include differentiated instructional pathways, placement informed curriculum design, and targeted academic English support in Vietnamese-medium engineering programs. The study provides empirical evidence for equity-oriented English medium instruction (EMI) development and contributes data driven insights for policy and curriculum in STEM higher education.

title: Bridging teacher talk time and multiple intelligences for deep learning
abstract: This study investigates the systemic tension between the dominance of teacher talk time (TTT) and the urgent need for deep learning strategies tailored to students’ multiple intelligences (MI) within the context of teaching English to young learners (TEYL). Adopting a descriptive mixed-methods design with a concurrent triangulation strategy, this research was conducted across a representative developing region in Central Java, Indonesia, involving a stratified sample of 450 upper-primary students and 45 English teachers. Data were collected using the student learning profile inventory (SLPI), TTT observation trackers, and semi-structured interviews. The findings reveal a critical pedagogical dissonance: while 72% of students exhibit a clear dominance in bodily-kinesthetic and visual-spatial intelligences profiles that biologically necessitate active, multimodal engagement classroom interactions remain heavily monopolized by teachers, who occupy 75% of lesson duration with verbal instruction. This excessive TTT acts as a significant constraint to the implementation of differentiated instruction (DI), effectively trapping students in surface-level rote memorization and inhibiting the development of communicative competence. The study concludes that the successful implementation of student-centered curricula requires a fundamental deconstruction of the traditional “teacher-as-broadcaster” model. Reducing TTT is identified not merely as a classroom management technique, but as a prerequisite for creating the temporal and cognitive space necessary for MI-based differentiation and deep learning.

title: Representation and differentiation of audiology interventions within the international classification of health interventions.
