title: Explaining Institutional Resilience through Educational Governance: A Latent Mediation Model of Strategic Management
abstract: This study examines how Educational governance is associated with institutional resilience among Chinese university students, with strategic management proposed as an explanatory mechanism. Drawing on self-determination and self-regulated learning perspectives, a conditional process model was specified and evaluated using a synthetic dataset of 486 cases. The simulated measurement model demonstrated acceptable reliability (composite reliability = 0.88) and fit (CFI = 0.93, TLI = 0.92, RMSEA = 0.051, SRMR = 0.038). Structural estimates suggested that Educational governance was positively associated with strategic management (β = 0.41, p .002) and with institutional resilience (β = 0.31, p .002). The standardized indirect effect through strategic management was 0.18, with a synthetic 95% bootstrap interval excluding zero. Together, the modeled predictors explained 48% of the variance in institutional resilience. The paper contributes a concise mechanism-based account of adaptive learning and demonstrates an empirical structure aligned with the Journal of Adaptive Learning and Psychological Growth. Because all results are simulated, the findings are illustrative and require validation with ethically collected data.
journal: The Journal of Interactive Social Sciences

title: Psi-programmes of the Human Psyche: Key Aspects
abstract: The aim of the study was to provide a theoretical substantiation and conceptualisation of the notion of a “psi-programme” in order to explain the mechanisms by which stimuli are transformed into controllable mental processes. The methodology combined theoretical modelling based on fundamental psychological works with a secondary analysis of contemporary statistical reports on the state of mental health in the United States, Germany and Ukraine. The main result was the definition of a psi-programme as a dynamic informational-energetic structure that operates through four successive stages: the catalysis of a fixed set, the search for a strategy, the formation of an algorithm, and implementation. Comparative analysis revealed unique national patterns of dominant psi-programmes. In the United States, where 23.4% of adults have a diagnosed mental disorder, programmes of personal success and social anxiety were identified. In Germany, where only 25% of the population is in a state of psychological flourishing, programmes of stability and perfectionism are characteristic. In Ukraine, where 83% of the population experiences a high level of stress due to the war and overall satisfaction with psychological well-being has fallen to 36%, programmes of collective resilience and individual trauma were identified. Three levels for the practical modification of maladaptive psi-programmes were also defined: individual (psychotherapy), educational-media (high-quality content), and socio-institutional (supportive policies). The conclusions indicate that the psi-programme model is a valid tool for analysing mental activity. It was established that the sociocultural context is a key factor in the formation of dominant mental patterns that determine the psychological state of both the individual and society. The practical significance lies in the possibility of developing comprehensive, multi-level strategies for correcting maladaptive programmes and strengthening mental health.

title: A Novel MPSI Weighting and Proximity Indexed Value Framework for Multi-Criteria Selection of Marketplace Logistics Partners
abstract: In facing the increasingly intense competition in the logistics industry, companies are often confronted with challenges in selecting the most appropriate logistics partner due to the many performance criteria that must be considered simultaneously. This study aims to evaluate and determine the best logistics partner using a Multi-Criteria Decision-Making approach through the integration of the MPSI method for criteria weighting and PIV for the alternative ranking process. The criteria used include Transit Time, On-Time Delivery, First-Attempt Success, Attempt Rate, and Package Volume, which are analyzed based on the performance data of each alternative. The weighting results indicate that Package Volume and Transit Time are the most dominant factors in the evaluation process. Based on the PIV method calculations, the ranking results were obtained, with NJ Logistics Partner occupying the first rank with a score of 0.46408, followed by TK Logistics Partner in second place with a score of 0.44014, and JT Logistics Partner in third place with a score of 0.39282. Sensitivity tests through various weight change scenarios showed that the ranking structure remained consistent, indicating that the model has a high level of stability and resilience to parameter variations. Overall, the proposed approach is able to produce decisions that are objective, measurable, and reliable as a basis for supporting strategic logistics partner selection.
journal: Journal of Decision Support Systems and Multi-Criteria Decision Making

title: Inventory System Design And Development at PT. Mitra Puding Mas - Palm Oil Mill
abstract: PT. Mitra Puding Mas – Palm Oil Mill is a palm oil processing company with intensive operational activities that depend heavily on the availability of inventory, including machine spare parts, raw materials, and production support equipment. However, its inventory management is still conducted manually using notebooks and spreadsheets, resulting in recording errors, data duplication, archive loss, and delays in preparing inventory reports. This study aims to design and develop a structured and accurate web-based inventory information system capable of providing real-time stock information to minimize potential losses caused by machine downtime and improve operational efficiency. Data were collected through literature review, direct field observation, and interviews with the Head of Administration (KTU) of PT. Mitra Puding Mas – Palm Oil Mill. The system was developed using the Model-View-Controller (MVC) architecture with the Laravel framework, PHP programming language, and MySQL database. System functionality was tested using Black-Box Testing. The results show that the developed system successfully integrates login, item category management, supplier management, incoming and outgoing inventory records, purchase transactions, and automatic report generation, including invoices and official transaction documents. The implementation transforms manual procedures into computerized processes, reduces human error, and supports faster and more accurate managerial decision-making based on valid inventory data.

title: Design and Implementation of an IoT Based Smart Home System for Motion Triggered Object Detection and Automated Ventilation Control
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT)-based smart homes enable the automation of home devices to improve comfort and security. This study designs and develops a smart home system in which passive infrared (PIR) sensors are used only to detect motion, while an ESP32-CAM and YOLOv3 are used for camera-based object detection and class labeling. A human-presence indication is therefore generated only when a PIR-triggered camera frame contains a person detected by YOLOv3; PIR motion alone is not interpreted as occupancy. The system also features MQ-2 sensor-based gas leak detection and automatic ventilation control using a servo motor as a safety response. Data and alerts are transmitted through Telegram, while Blynk is used for integrated monitoring. System development followed requirements analysis, design, implementation, functional testing, and corrective refinement. The dedicated YOLOv3 object test documented 11 confidence values ranging from 53% to 99% (descriptive mean 86.2%; median 94%); these values are detector confidence scores and not classification accuracy because no annotated ground-truth benchmark was used. In an additional 11-trial illuminance-oriented functional test, object detection succeeded in all six trials conducted at 624–950 lux and failed in all five trials conducted at 0–147 lux. The contribution of this work is an event-driven IoT architecture that coordinates motion sensing, visual verification, remote notification, and closed-loop gas mitigation, together with field-oriented evaluation of lighting effects on low-cost camera-based detection.

title: Multibranch Ensemble Head in Vision Foundation Models for Efficient Cucumber Phenological Stage Classification
abstract: Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) pretrained with self-supervised learning, such as DINOv2, provide highly transferable features, yet adapting them to small, domain-shifted datasets is still challenging. We propose a regularizing multibranch ensemble head: a training and inference scheme that pairs low- and high-capacity branches, samples a single branch stochastically at each training step, and averages both branches in probability space at inference. The design adds negligible parameters and essentially no inference overhead over a single heavy head, while improving the accuracy-efficiency trade-off under data-scarce conditions. Accurate classification of plant growth stages is critical for precision agriculture, enabling timely decisions on fertilization, irrigation, and harvesting. Therefore, as a challenging practical case we use cucumber phenological stage classification, in which flowers and fruits are frequently occluded by foliage, and stage transitions manifest primarily as subtle changes in leaf morphology. The NALEF Food Safety dataset contains images of five cucumber growth stages captured under diverse real-world conditions. On it we evaluate a broad range of backbones, including DINOv2 and DINOv3 ViT and ConvNeXt variants, against strongly supervised counterparts (ResNet, EfficientNet, ViT). The proposed DINOv2 ViT-S with multibranch head achieves a Macro F1 of 0.978 and Cohen's Kappa of 0.971, matching the performance of models more than ten times larger in parameters and GFlops, while requiring only 12.2 GFlops and 22.3M parameters, making it deployable on smartphones and edge devices for phenological stage classification.

title: STING/Type I Interferon Pathway Activation Confers Multimodal Therapeutic Benefits in Osteomyelitis.
abstract: Osteomyelitis is an inflammatory bone disease caused by pathogenic microorganisms and characterized by severe pain, extensive bone destruction, and reduced antibiotic efficacy due to local abscess formation. This study investigates the therapeutic potential of activating the STING (stimulator of interferon genes) pathway in osteomyelitis. In murine femoral osteomyelitis models induced by Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus), STING agonists alleviate osteomyelitis‐associated pain, suppress infection‐induced bone destruction, and reduce local abscess formation. These effects depend on host STING/type I interferon (IFN‐I) signaling and involve three mechanisms: inhibition of nociceptor activation by pathogens, suppression of osteoclast differentiation and function without affecting osteoblast activity, and downregulation of interleukin‐1β (IL‐1β), leading to reduced neutrophil recruitment and abscess formation. By reducing abscess formation as a physical barrier, STING agonists enhance the antibacterial efficacy of conventional antibiotics such as vancomycin at the site of infection. In summary, these findings suggest that the synergistic mechanisms activated by STING represent a promising therapeutic target for alleviating pain and improving clinical outcomes in osteomyelitis.

title: Maternal Hyperglycemia Disrupts Cerebral Cortex Development Through the Foxp1-Dll1-Notch Axis.
abstract: Maternal hyperglycemia is associated with adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes in offspring, but the mechanisms by which it affects fetal brain development remain incompletely understood. Using a mouse model of pregestational diabetes mellitus (PGDM), we found that maternal hyperglycemia was associated with reduced cortical thickness and altered cortical lamination. These abnormalities were accompanied by changes in neural stem cell differentiation and asymmetric division, as well as impaired neuronal migration and dendritic development. Transcriptomic analysis identified the transcription factor Foxp1 as markedly downregulated in the PGDM embryonic cortex. Restoring Foxp1 expression in vivo substantially alleviated the observed cortical abnormalities. Mechanistic experiments showed that Foxp1 represses transcription of the Notch ligand Delta‐like 1 (Dll1) and attenuates Notch signaling. Together, these findings implicate the Foxp1–Dll1–Notch axis as one pathway contributing to disrupted corticogenesis in the PGDM model and provide insight into how an adverse intrauterine metabolic environment affects embryonic brain development.

title: From Artificial to Embodied and Physical Intelligence in Smart Manufacturing
abstract: Manufacturing is evolving from automation‐centered production toward systems capable of sensing, adaptation, and autonomous response across digital, mechanical, and material domains. Although recent progress has been largely driven by artificial intelligence, current manufacturing intelligence often remains external to physical systems and suffers from limited robustness, interpretability, and transferability in complex industrial environments. Here, we present a unified perspective on smart manufacturing through the framework of artificial intelligence (AI), embodied intelligence (EI), and physical intelligence (PI). AI provides abstraction, prediction, and generative capability; EI enables closed‐loop perception, decision‐making, and physical interaction; and PI embeds adaptive intelligence directly into materials, structures, and physicochemical processes. We further discuss how generative intelligence is beginning to connect these domains through inverse design, adaptive fabrication, and physics‐constrained behavior realization. Recent advances in collaborative robotics, embodied digital twins, self‐optimizing production systems, and physically intelligent materials, including self‐actuating, self‐healing, multistable, and shape‐morphing systems, are reviewed. Finally, we propose an integrated AI–EI–PI framework spanning the full manufacturing lifecycle, highlighting a transition toward manufacturing systems in which intelligence is increasingly co‐designed across algorithms, embodied agents, and matter itself.

title: Genetic and Clinical Characteristics of Thalassemia Trait and Construction of LASSO-Based Model for Its Differentiating From Iron Deficiency Anemia in Northern China.
abstract: Background Thalassemia trait (TT) and iron deficiency anemia (IDA) represent the most common causes of microcytic hypochromic anemia (MHA) and are challenging to differentiate in clinical settings. Data regarding the genetic and clinical characteristics of TT in Northern China remain insufficient, highlighting an urgent need for rapid and efficient diagnostic strategies for the regional population. Methods This retrospective study enrolled 482 TT and 640 IDA patients from Northern China. Twenty‐seven α‐ and β‐TT mutations were detected by multicolor probe melting curve analysis (MMCA) and further confirmed by Sanger sequencing. A LASSO regression model using routine hematological indices was constructed and further validated. The diagnostic efficacy was compared with other indices (Mentzer, Shine and Lal, and Green and King indices). Results A total of 482 cases with TT mutations were identified. β‐TT mutations were the most prevalent (n = 261, 54.15%), followed by α‐TT mutations (n = 209, 43.36%) and α+β complex TT mutations (n = 12, 2.49%). Among which, eight α‐TT genotypes, eleven β‐TT genotypes, and eight α+β compound genotypes mutations were detected. For α‐TT, the predominant genotype was _α SEA /αα (77.0%), followed by _α 3.7 /αα (14.3%), α SEA /_α 3.7 (3.3%) and the rare HKαα (1.0%). The three most prevalent genotypes among β‐TT mutations were HBB:c.316_197C>T heterozygous (het) (35.2%), HBB:c.124_127delTTCT het (29.5%), and HBB:c.52A>T het (23.4%). α‐TT minor (33.82%) and β‐TT minor (53.94%) contributed the predominant phenotypes. The LASSO‐nomogram based on RBC, MCV, MCHC, and RDW‐SD achieved favorable discriminative performance (AUC = 0.94, sensitivity = 90.0%, specificity = 91.8%), showing superior diagnostic efficacy than other indices. Conclusion Our study revealed a distinct β‐TT‐dominant genotypic profile in Northern China and provided a simple, region‐adapted model as a potential tool for differentiating TT from IDA in clinical practice.

title: FLOWS: a model to simulate water and solutes fluxes in agricultural and environmental systems. 1. Theory and applications with intercode benchmarking
abstract: FLOWS (FLOws of Water and Solutes in soils) is a dynamic physically-based model to simulate water flow and solute transport in the soil–plant–atmosphere system. The numerical code was written in MATLAB. One-dimensional vertical transient water flow is simulated by numerically solving the 1D form of the Richards equation (RE) using an implicit, backward, finite differences scheme with explicit linearization. As for the solutes, the code solves the 1D Advection Dispersion equation (ADE) by an explicit, central difference scheme, allowing for a relatively easy inclusion of non-linear adsorption and other non-linear processes. The model produces information on the time evolution of (among many other outputs): soil water contents and pressure potentials in the soil profile; solute (tracers, adsorbed, volatile and reactive solutes) concentrations in the soil profile; water and solute uptake and actual evapotranspiration for simulated crops; deep percolation water and solute fluxes; root uptake of water and solutes, also in presence of water and osmotic stresses; water fluxes and related solute fluxes to runoff; drainage water fluxes and related solute fluxes; irrigation fluxes computed by the model; and temperature in the soil profile. Compared to other existing models, some specificities of FLOWS model are: (1) integrated simulation of carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus transformations and transport contextually to the simulation of water contents and fluxes; (2) macroscopic root uptake; (3) irrigation management, by allowing to optimize the time scheduling and volumes according to some criterion based on the average pressure head in the root zone; (4) the possibility of running multi-site simulations, which may be especially important for spatially distributed simulations; and (5) an interactive graphical user interface, allowing the user to easily handle even large input files and seeing the simulation results by graphical display of the main output variables.

Hybrid deep learning architecture for facial emotion recognition on FER2013 dataset
abstract: This work focuses on a reliable facial emotion recognition framework which aims to improve facial emotion classification performance on the FER2013 benchmark dataset. Recognition of facial emotions is now an important research field due to its uses in human computer interaction, healthcare, intelligent surveillance, education and affective computing. Despite the above, the human face still exhibits subtle changes with facial pose, facial illumination, occlusion and expression that continue to impact the overall recognition result. In order to solve these problems, this paper puts forward a hybrid deep learning architecture based on ResNet50 and Transformer encoder, capable of extracting multi-scale detailed spatial information and the relationships among various facial regions. An evaluation was performed with the proposed framework using the FER2013 database that contains 7 different emotion classes and 35,787 facial images. Images were pre-processed as three channel formats, resized to 224 × 224, normalized, and trained with the augmented image by flipping horizontally, random rotation, and resized cropping. For feature extraction, a pre-trained model was employed: the ResNet50 network. The Transformer encoder model was used to help enhance the contextual features representation, and the emotion classification was performed afterwards. The proposed framework has an overall accuracy of 89.7 percent on the official test partition (FER2013). Finally, an improvement was shown by ablation studies on the transformer where the ResNet50 model had a 72.84 percent, the ResNet50 model with a dense classifier reached 74.63 percent, and the complete framework achieved 89.7 percent. The results showed that the proposed method can be implemented transparently and reproduced and can robustly and consistently recognize facial emotions. The study provides a viable model which can guide the future research and practice of emotion recognition using facial expression.

title: Soil health and One Health implications in the anthropocene: a perspective on microbiome engineering
abstract: Climate change and Anthropocene pressures accelerate soil degradation, threatening agricultural productivity, ecosystems, and human health. Within the One Health framework, soils are critical living systems. However, while physical and chemical dimensions of soil health are well studied, the biological dimension—particularly microbiome functional diversity—remains heavily underutilized in climate-resilient agriculture. We argue that microbiome functional diversity is the missing biological foundation linking Soil Health and One Health. Rather than viewing microbiomes as isolated components, we propose they be treated as interconnected functional networks regulating resilience across soil, plant, animal, and human systems. We position microbiome engineering as a strategic research priority to translate ecological knowledge into sustainable agricultural solutions. Synthesizing discussions from the Chile–Sweden ACCESS Forum, we identify vital research priorities: exploring microbiomes from harsh, ancient, and extreme environments; developing synthetic microbial communities (SynComs); and integrating high-resolution mass spectrometry, multi-omics, microscale soil models, and extended genotype approaches. These tools offer unprecedented pathways to manipulate microbial functions that enhance nutrient cycling, carbon sequestration, stress tolerance, and pollutant remediation. Advancing microbiome functional diversity from ecological discovery to functional microbiome engineering represents a critical, actionable step toward achieving climate-resilient agroecosystems and fulfilling the global objectives of the One Health framework in the Anthropocene.

Mesenchymal stromal cell-based therapies for obesity-associated metabolic complications: Mechanistic insights, translational evidence, and future perspectives.
abstract: Obesity is a major global health challenge and a key driver of type 2 diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic syndrome. Although pharmacological therapies and bariatric surgery have improved both short- and long-term outcomes, with GLP-1 receptor agonists now demonstrating cardiovascular and heart-failure benefits beyond weight reduction (SELECT, SUMMIT), durable and broadly applicable treatments for all patients remain limited. In this context, mesenchymal stem/stromal cell (MSC)-based therapies, particularly adipose-derived MSCs, have gained increasing attention due to their immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and metabolic regulatory properties demonstrated in preclinical models. Experimental studies suggest that MSCs influence adipose tissue remodeling, immune cell polarization, insulin sensitivity, and energy homeostasis predominantly through paracrine mechanisms, including the release of cytokines and extracellular vesicles, rather than long-term engraftment or differentiation. However, accumulating evidence indicates that obesity itself profoundly impairs endogenous MSC function through oxidative stress, endoplasmic reticulum stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and epigenetic alterations, raising important concerns regarding the feasibility of autologous MSC-based approaches in obese individuals. Critically, no randomized controlled trial has evaluated MSC therapy for obesity with weight loss, body composition, or obesity-related clinical outcomes as primary endpoints; the available human evidence addresses glycemic control in type 2 diabetes and metabolic complications. In this review, we summarize current mechanistic insights, preclinical findings, and clinical data on MSC-based interventions for obesity-associated metabolic disorders, while critically discussing key biological, manufacturing, and regulatory challenges. Finally, we define the prerequisites for rational translation - standardized potency assays, obesity-specific early-phase trials with active comparators, objective body-composition endpoints, hemocompatibility testing, and long-term surveillance.

title: Embryonic reprogramming drives anaplastic transformation in thyroid carcinoma.
abstract: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC) is a highly aggressive malignancy that often arises through anaplastic transformation of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). Although genetic drivers such as BRAF and TP53 mutations are implicated, the mechanisms underlying this transition remain poorly understood. Here, we show that human ATC loses thyroid differentiation and acquires pluripotency-associated features, accompanied by MAPK pathway activation. Guided by parallels with induced pluripotent stem cell reprogramming, we develop an in vivo reprogramming mouse model. Forced expression of Oct3/4, Sox2, Klf4, and c-Myc (OSKM) induces anaplastic transformation of Braf-mutant thyroid epithelium even without Trp53 mutation, yielding an ATC-like phenotype that shares molecular and histological features with human ATC. A conventional Braf/Trp53-mutant model shows similar features. Reintroduction of NKX2-1 into human and murine ATC cells partially reverses embryonic reprogramming, suppresses proliferation and induces redifferentiation toward a PTC-like phenotype. Embryonic reprogramming is a central driver of anaplastic transformation and supports redifferentiation strategies.

Resource Utilization and Forecasting in Heart Failure Patients with Durable Left Ventricular Assist Devices.
abstract: Heart failure patients treated with durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) require significant resource utilization. Patient volume and contact points based on implant volume remain poorly quantified. We retrospectively reviewed 268 patients implanted with a durable LVAD at a single, experienced center from 2011 through 2022 and recorded survival, telephone encounters, office visits, and all-cause hospitalizations. Telephone encounters peaked at 10.4 per patient-month and declined to approximately 5 after 24 months; 66% were anticoagulation-related. Office visits peaked at 3.0 per patient-month and declined to approximately 0.7 after 18 months. Hospitalizations decreased from 2.7 per patient-year in year 1 to approximately 1 by year 5. Five-year survival with HeartMate 3 (HM3) was 61.4%. Applying HM3 survival to constant annual implant volumes yielded estimated 5-year censuses of 39, 96, and 193 surviving patients for 10, 25, and 50 annual implants, respectively. These findings may inform LVAD program capacity and staffing.

title: Thioketal-functionalized gelatin methacryloyl hydrogel enables ROS-responsive dencichine delivery for osteoporotic bone defect regeneration.
abstract: Osteoporotic bone defects are difficult to repair because excessive oxidative stress, heightened osteoclast activity, and impaired osteogenic differentiation act concurrently within the defect microenvironment. Here, a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive hydrogel was developed by conjugating thioketal dicarboxylic acid (TK-DA) to gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) through amide coupling and physically encapsulating dencichine (Denc), yielding G-TK@Denc. Denc showed a concentration-dependent biological response in vitro, with 10 μM providing the most favorable balance between cytocompatibility, osteogenic stimulation, and inhibition of osteoclast differentiation and resorptive function. The G-TK@Denc hydrogel retained an interconnected porous architecture and underwent rapid photocrosslinking. Under H2O2-containing conditions, the hydrogel exhibited reduced mechanical integrity, accelerated degradation, and enhanced Denc release, consistent with ROS-mediated cleavage of thioketal linkages. G-TK@Denc extracts inhibited RANKL-induced osteoclast formation, disrupted F-actin sealing rings, and reduced osteoclast-associated gene and protein expression. The formulation also decreased intracellular ROS accumulation, restored superoxide dismutase and catalase activity, and was associated with an Nrf2/Sirt1-related antioxidant response. In parallel, G-TK@Denc enhanced alkaline phosphatase activity, matrix mineralization, and osteogenic marker expression in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. In an ovariectomized mouse femoral condyle defect model, G-TK@Denc increased new bone formation and improved trabecular microarchitecture. Transcriptomic analysis further suggested coordinated regulation of osteoclastogenic, antioxidant, and osteogenic programs. These findings support thioketal-functionalized GelMA as a local, microenvironment-responsive platform for Denc delivery and osteoporotic bone regeneration.

title: Sodium Butyrate Inhibits Glyoxalase 1 to Reverse D-Lactate-associated Drug Resistance in Cancer Cells.
abstract: Drug resistance remains a major limitation to effective cancer therapy, and its metabolic basis is incompletely understood. We recently developed models of acquired drug resistance through chronic exposure of tumor cells to anticancer agents and identified a metabolic phenotype characterized by impaired mitochondrial bioenergetics, increased L-lactate production, and decreased oxygen consumption rate (OCR). Here, we investigated the contribution of D-lactate metabolism to this phenotype. Compared with their parental (P) counterparts, drug-resistant (R) cell lines showed increased D-lactate production together with increased glyoxalase 1 (GLO1) expression and activity. Sodium butyrate (NaB) reduced GLO1 expression and activity in tumor cell lines with higher expression of D-lactate pathway components, and NaB treatment was associated with reduced intracellular D-lactate levels and increased sensitivity to the corresponding anticancer treatments in selected cell models. These findings support a biochemical link between NaB-mediated modulation of the GLO1/D-lactate pathway and drug response, without excluding additional NaB-dependent mechanisms. Furthermore, NaB enhanced the effects of pro-differentiation agents in the tested in vitro models. Together, our data identify the GLO1/D-lactate pathway as a metabolic feature associated with drug resistance and support further investigation of NaB-based strategies in appropriate preclinical models.

title: A deep learning model for detection and staging of osteonecrosis of the femoral head on x-ray images: a retrospective, large-scale, multicentre study in China.
abstract: BACKGROUND Accurate detection and staging of osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) are essential for effective treatment yet frequently require specialist expertise and advanced equipment. To address this requirement, we aimed to develop a deep learning-based diagnostic model for the automatic detection and staging of ONFH using x-ray images, and compared its performance with clinicians to allow them to improve their diagnostic performance. METHODS In this retrospective, large-scale, multicentre study, we developed our deep learning model, Osteonecrosis Artificial Intelligence Diagnostician (OsteoAID), which was based on the You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) detection network and trained on a multicentre x-ray dataset. The dataset, dated from Jan 1, 2015, to Dec 31, 2023, and obtained from 16 399 patients across six Chinese tertiary hospitals, included 20 722 anteroposterior hip x-ray images of 28 785 hips, including hips with ONFH, healthy hips, and hips with other conditions radiographically similar to ONFH. To establish a rigorous ground truth for model training and evaluation, expert orthopaedists annotated each image to differentiate ONFH from confounding diseases and additionally classified the confirmed ONFH lesions on the basis of the Ficat and Arlet staging system. To verify the diagnostic performance of OsteoAID, we compared the model's accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, and area under the curve (AUC) with those of the original YOLOv8 model on the internal testing set for both the staging and detection tasks. Furthermore, the performance of OsteoAID was compared with the performance of radiologists and orthopaedists on two external testing sets, and its diagnostic performance was also benchmarked against MRI-the gold standard for ONFH diagnosis-with a third external testing set in which x-ray images were staged by corresponding MRI scans. Diagnostic metrics were compared with those of clinicians using t tests and McNemar's tests, with significance set at p<0·05. FINDINGS On the internal testing set, OsteoAID improved the staging accuracy from 87·42% (95% CI 85·88-89·20) to 96·44% (94·73-97·17) and the AUC from 88·54% (86·74-90·37) to 96·94% (95·75-97·98) compared with the original YOLOv8 model. For detection the model had a mean average precision of 92·97% (91·73-94·43) at an intersection-over-union threshold of 50%. In comparisons with clinicians on the external testing set I, the model showed staging accuracy of 96·60% (94·27-97·81), which was significantly higher than radiologists (74·96% [73·38-76·85]; p<0·0001) and junior orthopaedists (83·98% [81·27-84·06]; p<0·0001) and similar to that of expert orthopaedists (96·54% [94·18-97·79]; p=0·20). Furthermore, model-assisted diagnostics improved the accuracy of junior orthopaedists by an absolute difference of 12·70% and of radiologists by 21·47%. Although the accuracy improvement for expert orthopaedists was non-significant (an absolute difference of 0·74%; p=0·080), the diagnostic time was substantially reduced across all groups. On external testing set II (which included challenging cases: low-quality x-ray images affected by improper exposure, poor contrast, incomplete field of view, or foreign-object shadows, as well as smartphone photographs of x-ray films), the model showed robust performance even under extreme conditions, achieving an overall staging accuracy of 93·76% (93·09-95·82). Additionally, combining x-ray imaging with the deep learning model produced diagnostic results similar to MRI on external testing set III with an overall accuracy of 96·63% (95·68-97·86) and an AUC of 97·33% (96·65-98·75). INTERPRETATION The developed deep learning model shows expert-level diagnostic performance in the dual tasks of detecting and staging ONFH by use of anteroposterior x-rays, which can substantially enhance both the diagnostic proficiency and efficiency of clinicians. Consequently, the model could serve as a highly accessible decision-support tool to optimise clinical triage and guide appropriate treatment strategies. FUNDING National Natural Science Foundation of China, National High Level Hospital Clinical Research Funding, and Beijing Natural Science Foundation.

title: Engineering exosomes-mediated RNA delivery regulates bone homeostasis and alleviates osteoporosis.
abstract: Osteoporosis is characterized by dysregulated bone remodeling driven by excessive osteoclast-mediated bone resorption and insufficient osteoblast-mediated bone formation, often exacerbated by chronic inflammation and oxidative stress. Current pharmacological therapies remain limited by suboptimal efficacy and adverse effects, highlighting the need for alternative strategies that restore bone homeostasis. Here, we developed a bone-targeted, multifunctional exosome-based therapeutic platform by engineering M2 macrophage-derived exosomes co-loaded with platinum nanoparticles (Pt NPs) and a miR-196b inhibitor (BT-Exo-Pt-miR-196 inhibitor). The engineered exosomes exhibited preserved structural integrity, favorable biocompatibility, efficient bone-targeting capability, and excellent in vivo biosafety. Pt NPs endowed the system with robust reactive oxygen species (ROS)-scavenging activity, while M2-derived exosomes and miR-196b inhibition synergistically attenuated inflammatory cytokine expression. In vitro, BT-Exo-Pt-miR-196 inhibitor markedly enhanced osteogenic differentiation, extracellular matrix maturation, and mineralization through coordinated upregulation of osteogenic transcription factors and matrix proteins. Concurrently, osteoclastogenesis was significantly suppressed, as evidenced by reduced TRAP-positive multinucleated cells, impaired actin ring formation, and downregulation of NFATc1 and downstream osteoclast-associated markers. In an ovariectomy-induced osteoporosis mouse model, bone-targeted delivery of BT-Exo-Pt-miR-196 inhibitor effectively preserved trabecular bone microarchitecture, enhanced osteogenic activity, reduced osteoclast function, and alleviated bone loss without inducing systemic toxicity. Collectively, this study demonstrates that bone-targeted M2 macrophage-derived exosomes delivering a miR-196b inhibitor represent a promising immunomodulatory and gene-regulatory nanotherapeutic strategy for restoring bone homeostasis and treating osteoporosis.

title: Bone-targeting engineered exosomes delivering teriparatide mRNA for the treatment of osteoporosis.
abstract: Introduction Teriparatide (TPTD) is an established osteoanabolic agent for the treatment of osteoporosis; however, its short circulating half-life necessitates repeated administration, while limited skeletal selectivity may reduce delivery efficiency. To address these limitations, we developed an Asp6-functionalized, bone-targeting exosome system carrying TPTD mRNA (Asp6-Exo@TPTD). An Exo-Motif sequence was incorporated into the TPTD mRNA construct to facilitate hnRNPA2B1-associated enrichment of the transcript in exosomes, while surface modification with the hydroxyapatite-binding peptide Asp6 was used to enhance skeletal affinity. BMSC-derived exosomes may additionally provide intrinsic regenerative signals that complement the osteoanabolic activity of TPTD. Methods Mouse bone marrow mesenchymal stromal cells (BMSCs) were incubated with different exosome formulations to evaluate intracellular TPTD mRNA transfer, TPTD protein production, CRE-dependent reporter activity, and osteogenic differentiation. Free TPTD was included as a pharmacological reference in the functional, osteogenic, and animal efficacy experiments. The bone-binding properties of the engineered exosomes were assessed using hydroxyapatite-containing bone samples and ex vivo bone tissues. In vivo biodistribution was evaluated by fluorescence imaging after intravenous administration. Therapeutic efficacy was investigated in an ovariectomy-induced osteoporosis mouse model by assessing trabecular microarchitecture, histological changes, serum bone-formation markers, and dynamic bone formation. Preliminary tolerability was evaluated by major-organ histology and serum biochemical analyses, including serum calcium and hepatic and renal function indices. Results Asp6-Exo@TPTD increased intracellular TPTD mRNA levels and TPTD secretion in recipient BMSCs and enhanced CRE-dependent luciferase activity, osteogenic gene expression, alkaline phosphatase staining, and extracellular matrix mineralization. Asp6-Exo@TPTD exhibited greater binding to bone tissues than both unloaded Exo and non-targeted Exo@TPTD in vitro and ex vivo. Following systemic administration, bone-associated fluorescence remained detectable for at least 72 h, with greater femoral and tibial fluorescence and lower relative hepatic fluorescence than those observed with unmodified exosomes. In ovariectomized mice, weekly administration of Asp6-Exo@TPTD improved trabecular microarchitecture, increased serum procollagen type I N-terminal propeptide levels, and enhanced the mineral apposition rate. No overt histopathological abnormalities or significant alterations in serum calcium or routine hepatic and renal biochemical indices were detected. Conclusions Asp6-functionalized exosomes carrying TPTD mRNA promoted osteogenic activity, enhanced bone-associated distribution, and attenuated ovariectomy-induced bone loss. These findings support Asp6-Exo@TPTD as a promising exosome-based strategy for bone-targeted TPTD mRNA delivery and osteoporosis treatment.

High-Throughput Polymer Design for the Biological Interface
abstract: High-throughput experimentation is transforming synthetic polymer design for biological applications, enabling data-driven approaches that map the vast chemical design space accessible to synthetic macromolecules. In this Viewpoint, we survey recent advances in high-throughput methodologies for discovering polymers that interface with biological systems. We first review synthetic strategies, such as well-plate polymerizations, immobilized and solid-phase synthesis, and continuous flow chemistry, that enable parallelized, miniaturized access to large polymer libraries. We then discuss screening methods for structural characterization, target-binding interactions, and functional performance in cellular and biological contexts. We highlight how these readouts capture the disordered, dynamic nature of synthetic polymers relative to structured biomacromolecules. Finally, we examine how machine learning, active learning, self-driving laboratories, and emerging agentic AI tools are being integrated with high-throughput workflows to accelerate inverse design and autonomous experimentation. We underscore the potential of increasingly automated discovery in future years and the need for rigorous, application-appropriate workflow design. Together, these synthesis, characterization, and computational strategies form a synergistic pipeline poised to accelerate the discovery of next-generation polymer therapeutics and biomaterials.

title: Listeners expect grammatical variation across dialects.
abstract: Dialect variation is universally attested among languages, yet the cognitive processes underlying listeners' adaptations to different dialects, particularly in morphosyntactic variation, remain underexplored. This article investigates how listeners represent and adapt to their interlocutor's dialect based on their linguistic experience, examining monodialectal speakers of Dominant American English and bidialectal speakers of Dominant American English and African American Language. In Experiment 1, participants rated written sentences to indicate the likelihood that a speaker of a given dialect would say them. All participants demonstrated knowledge of African American Language's regularized subject-verb agreement rules, rating sentences like "They was happy" as more likely than "He were happy." However, bidialectal participants showed greater differentiation between the sentences than monodialectal participants. This finding suggests that listeners do not simply relax grammatical expectations when exposed to linguistic diversity; rather, they form specific expectations of a dialect's grammatical rules. In Experiment 2, we tested whether these expectations influence perception. Participants transcribed sentences where agreement was acoustically ambiguous ("She sit[s] still"). Participants were more likely to transcribe regularized subject-verb agreement ("She sit still") when listening to an African American Language speaker compared to a Dominant American English speaker, regardless of their linguistic experience. Bidialectal participants were more likely to transcribe regularized subject-verb agreement overall. In Experiment 3, we found that such effect patterns were likely driven by morphosyntactic cues, rather than social cues to the race of the speaker. These results suggest that listeners form mental models of others' grammars to guide comprehension, with the precision of these models depending on their linguistic experience. title: p38α acts as a molecular switch to differentially regulate the Flt3 and CD115 pathways in dendritic cell development.
Turing-like tests for language and vision demonstrate a narrowing gap between humans and AI.
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in daily life, ascertaining whether an agent is human is critical. Here we systematically benchmark AI's ability to imitate humans in three language tasks (image captioning, word association and conversation) and three vision tasks (colour estimation, object detection and attention prediction), collecting data from n = 636 humans and 37 AI agents. We also conducted 72,191 Turing-like tests with 1,916 human judges and 10 AI judges. Current AIs are approaching the ability to convincingly impersonate humans and deceive human judges in both language and vision. Even simple AI judges outperformed humans in distinguishing AI from human responses. Imitation ability showed minimal correlation with conventional AI performance metrics, suggesting that passing as human is an important independent evaluation criterion. The large-scale Turing-like datasets and metrics introduced here offer valuable benchmarks for assessing human-likeness in AI and highlight the importance of rigorous, quantitative imitation tests for AI development.
