abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) requires an agentic system to design, train, and evaluate its own successor. Data-driven post-training is a central part of that loop, yet existing evaluations measure it on a single benchmark, where an agent selects from a static pool or distills a stronger model to push one score up in one run. Real post-training is multi-domain, and a gain in one domain has to be weighed against a regression in another. We propose ParetoRSI-Gym, in which an agent searches for data, curates it, trains, reads back per-domain results, and repeats, with everything but the data held fixed: the initial LLM, the five domains (math, code, finance, medicine, science), the toolset, and the SFT pipeline. Generalization benchmarks in each domain separate capability gains from overfitting to the scores the agent optimizes against. Across three agent systems, three base models, five rounds and multiple seeds, the strongest system, Claude Code with Opus-5, raises the generalization scores of its proxy-best checkpoint by 9.2% relative to the starting model (+2.3 absolute points), averaged with equal weight over three base models and five domains, with a single-domain relative gain of up to 63% (medicine on Ministral-3-3B). Further analysis shows that the harness matters as much as the model it drives, and that each agent keeps a unique data selection strategy. We see our work as a step towards evaluation of RSI systems in real-world machine learning engineering.

title: Path-Specific Geometric-Stochastic Channel Model for Scattering from ISAC Targets: A Unified Measurement-Based Characterization of Robots, Humans, and Automobiles at 28 GHz
abstract: This paper develops a channel model for scattering from a broad class of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) targets-robots, humans, and automobiles-based on a unified measurement campaign at 28~GHz. Nine targets are characterized from numerous transmitter--receiver configurations per target, spanning full bistatic and aspect angles and thus covering backward to forward scattering. Repeated acquisitions are collected for each configuration to capture target motion and dynamics, yielding nearly 117\,000 acquisitions in total. Measurements are collected with a 2~GHz-wide channel sounder equipped with a 256-element phased-array antenna, followed by digital beamforming and super-resolution processing for reliable extraction of multiple paths in delay and 2D angle, with average estimation errors of 0.1~ns and 0.2$^\circ$ respectively. From these measurements, we reduce a \emph{path-specific} channel representation in which the scattering is modeled as a cluster of paths whose center is defined by the bistatic specular \emph{geometry}; the cluster shape is described \emph{stochastically}. To ensure physically grounded spatio--temporal consistency, extracted paths are mapped to incident points on the target, each with an associated radar cross section (RCS) that is compatible with the 3GPP TR~38.901 ISAC channel model, and are subsequently mapped back to path properties for channel synthesis. The resulting statistical distributions are well behaved, physically interpretable, and consistent across targets, geometries, and motion. Comparison between measured and synthesized channel realizations demonstrates close agreement in pathloss trends and fluctuation behavior. Together, these results yield a high-fidelity, measurement-derived channel representation suitable for ISAC simulation, target modeling, and system design.

title: CyberDual: AI Attackers versus AI Code Reviewers in Real Software Maintenance
abstract: Open-source projects now let AI agents review incoming code, but the code under review may itself come from an AI attacker. We present CyberDual, an arena for this dual role of AI: attacker agents hide an exploitable bug in real maintenance work on widely used open-source projects, and reviewer agents try to find and repair it. Execution decides each match: we rerun the attacker's proof of concept (PoC) on the code that comes out of review. Every attack is new, and the windows can be rebuilt each quarter from the latest upstream history. Three agentic reviewers catch 85-91% of 1,088 valid attacks from six attackers. Yet when the attacker spreads the bug over real upstream commits, about one in six attack slots still ends with a working exploit after review. The strongest attacker has open weights: GLM 5.3 almost never refuses, and its attacks make up 13 of the 28 that get past all three reviewers. When they miss, Claude reviewers mostly approve the attack, while GPT-6-Sol mostly repairs the wrong code; a reviewer from a second vendor catches about two thirds of a Claude reviewer's misses. Beyond a leaderboard, CyberDual has three uses. First, PoC execution gives both sides a reward that agent reports cannot game, so its surviving attacks can train reviewers against stronger attackers. Second, it can gate a release on both scores: Claude Sonnet 5 refuses one in five attack slots, yet attacks about as well as GPT-6-Sol, so refusal alone does not remove attack capability. Third, it can warn the teams behind a deployed reviewer when a new attacker crosses a threshold: GLM 5.3 in Claude Code already gets an exploit past Sonnet 5 in 17% of its attack slots.

title: Is the arXiv Apocalypse upon us? A break in preprint growth coincident with agentic AI
abstract: As an experiment in agentic assisted analysis, we used an agentic AI model to analyse the effect of agentic AI on arXiv submissions; data acquisition, analysis and the first draft were carried out by the model under the author's direction. Monthly arXiv submissions have grown exponentially for three decades, at about $9\%$ per year. Fitting a piecewise log-linear trend with seasonal modulation to the full record, we find two post-pandemic breaks in growth rate. The first, in mid-2022, precedes ChatGPT and is carried by the expansion of AI research within computer science (CS); outside CS, growth from 2022 to 2025 remained at $8\%$ per year. The second, between December 2025 and February 2026, follows the release of models capable of extended autonomous work and is absent from the AI categories themselves. Since December 2025 submissions without a CS listing have run $17\%$ above trend, and in September 2026 total submissions reached a record $40\,363$. The excess is largest in mathematics, where submissions doubled within a year, and follows a gradient from formal and theoretical fields to experimental ones that is not ordered by surveyed rates of AI-tool adoption. In mathematics the increase is distributed across subfields and authors, two-thirds of it arising from a larger number of distinct authors rather than from a few prolific submitters. Across fields the clearest signature is a shift to single authorship: solo-authored papers rose by $70\%$ within a year in mathematics and condensed matter, and by $44\%$ in quantitative biology even as its total output fell, but not in experimental particle physics. The analysis is deliberately agnostic of LLM-detection methods: it uses only submission counts and metadata, with treatment timing fixed by calendar dates, and is therefore free of the outcome-triggered timing bias of author-level studies.

title: py-ARGOS: A Python package for automatic, statistically principled discovery of ordinary differential equations from data
abstract: Recovering the governing equations of a dynamical system from data is a central problem in data-driven science, yet the available Python tooling forces a compromise among automation, statistical rigor, and reliability. We present py-ARGOS, a Python package implementing two automatic algorithms, bootstrap ARGOS and Bayesian-ARGOS, behind a uniform interface. Both are statistically principled throughout: automated model selection reduces the candidate library, each coefficient is reported with a bootstrap confidence or Bayesian credible interval that quantifies its uncertainty, and a term is retained when this interval excludes zero. Built-in diagnostics additionally flag unreliable fits. On chaotic benchmark systems, the two algorithms improve on the SINDy family's identification performance.

title: A Multi-Domain Study on the Effectiveness of LLMs at Writing Property-Based Tests
abstract: A property-based test (PBT) checks a property of a program on many generated inputs, but writing one takes a property, a generator of valid inputs, and an oracle. LLM-based PBT writers produce all three, yet they have been evaluated only on Python libraries. We study how two of them, Proptest-AI and Agentic-PBT, generalize to ten programs in five domains: deep learning libraries, databases, system software, compilers, and LLM serving engines. Most of these programs take text in their own language, such as queries, configurations, and programs. Agentic-PBT covers more branches than Proptest-AI on seven of the ten programs with Opus 5 and on all ten with GLM-5.3-Flash. Domain-specific fuzzers cover more of the compilers and of PostgreSQL and less of PyTorch than Agentic-PBT. We filed 180 bug reports, 44 of which duplicate reports that others filed after the models' knowledge cutoffs; maintainers have confirmed 65 of the others, in all five domains, and fixed 23. We draw lessons for building and evaluating such writers: low observability hurts them, and mature fuzzers paired with LLM-written properties could check that each feature behaves as documented.

title: Multimodal Requirements Traceability Link Recovery in Industrial Settings
abstract: Requirements traceability links support activities such as change-impact analysis, coverage checking, and validation. Industrial requirements can include traceable images, which text-only approaches cannot process directly. For a fixed classifier configuration, binary decisions alone offer no direct way to adjust the balance between missed and incorrect links. We extend a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) approach for inter-requirements traceability link recovery (TLR). Our extension retrieves text and image candidates separately, classifies each retrieved pair with a vision-language model, and filters the predicted links by verbalized confidence. We evaluate our approach on three non-overlapping industrial requirement sets and six public text-only datasets. On the industrial test sets, our approach achieves an F1 score of 0.310, compared with 0.114 for our replication of the baseline approach by Hey et al. Our approach recovers links in all four modality combinations while improving text-only F1 on the industrial data and maintaining similar performance on the public datasets, but recovery remains limited by failures to retrieve related text requirements for image queries. Confidence filtering produces link sets with different precision and recall, removing false positives and some correctly recovered links from the unfiltered link set. This study provides industrial evidence on the potential and limitations of a current RAG-based TLR approach for multimodal requirements and identifies cross-modal retrieval as the component to prioritize in further optimization.

title: Acute Stroke Classification Using Asymmetric Data Standardization and Orthogonal-Focal Loss Optimized CNN-ViT Cross-Attention Fusion: A Multicenter External Validation Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Rapid differentiation of ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke subtypes is vital for acute management. Although current deep learning models achieve high single-dataset accuracy, they suffer from "shortcut learning" and domain shift in external validation. This study proposes a hierarchical computer-aided diagnostic (CAD) system mimicking emergency triage. Methods: We introduce a 3-channel Radiology-Focused Preprocessing pipeline that feeds radiological Hounsfield Unit (HU) windows into Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) backbones via asymmetric formats (.mat and .png). The architecture utilizes a novel joint cross-attention fusion network optimized by an Integrated Orthogonal-Focal Loss. Results: Our system achieved a 95.48% F1-score on the internal stroke dataset. However, multi-center external validation (AISD, BHSD, PhysioNet) using a Mask Anchor filter revealed a drop to the 58-62% range, exposing the "internal validation illusion" caused by hardware noise. Critically, models exhibited high precision (77%) but low sensitivity (57%) for ischemic stroke, proving prone to hemorrhage overdiagnosis. Multi-seed variance analysis demonstrated that the DenseNet201+ViT backbone yielded the lowest deviation (0.59) and highest stability, making it the most reliable architecture for real-world clinical integration. Conclusions: To overcome diagnostic challenges, future research must focus on multimodal architectures that combine 3D volumetric extraction with clinical data.

title: A thermodynamic correction layer for machine learning interatomic potentials
abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials enable atomistic simulations with near \textit{ab initio} accuracy over large length and time scales. Foundation models extend this capability across the periodic table but inherit the thermodynamic description of the electronic structure methods used to generate their training data. Small errors in relative phase stability can therefore produce large errors in transformation temperatures. We introduce an additive thermodynamic correction layer that shifts phase free energies towards an assessed reference without retraining or modifying the base potential. A first order thermodynamic construction converts the required phase free energy shifts directly into configuration energy targets, which are fitted using a linear atomic cluster expansion and refined iteratively from measured free energies. We apply the method to melting and solid to solid transformations across elements with different crystal structures using a foundation GRACE model. After the correction, all transformation temperatures lie within the prescribed tolerance of the assessed values, including Ca, Ti, and Zr, where a solid to solid transition and melting are corrected together. Static energy curves, bulk moduli, and liquid structure remain close to those of the base model. Vacancy formation energies, thermal expansion, and liquid density depend on the corrected phase balance and change where the correction is large. The method requires neither retraining, differentiable dynamics, nor access to the parameters of the base potential. It provides a modular route for combining transferable atomistic models with assessed phase thermodynamics.

title: A Product-Grassmann Tucker Surrogate for Parametric Field Prediction
abstract: Many-query applications such as design optimization, uncertainty quantification and digital twins call for repeated full-field predictions from expensive partial differential equation (PDE) simulations. Grassmannian reduced-order models interpolate parameter-dependent subspaces but commonly vectorize the spatial field, and the ambient dimension then grows with the product of the grid sizes. Tensor-based models preserve the multiway structure but often use shared mode-wise bases or a fixed core across parameters. We propose a Tucker-based surrogate that keeps the spatial directions and time as separate modes. The factor subspaces are interpolated on a product Grassmann manifold, Procrustes alignment places the Tucker cores in one coordinate system, and a truncated singular value decomposition models their variation. Across five PDE benchmarks in two and three spatial dimensions, including public computational fluid dynamics data, the interpolation size is reduced by factors of 13 to 482 and the stored model by factors of 13 to 464 relative to a single-subspace Grassmannian surrogate with the same local interpolation. Cached queries run 3.3 to 8.5 times faster, the mean errors over ten resampled splits differ by at most 0.22 percentage points (0.36 when every model choice is re-selected inside each split), and the prediction-error terms of the two methods differ by less than 0.1 percentage points. The remaining accuracy differences are consistent with the larger representation error of the Tucker format. In a three-dimensional grid study the interpolation-size ratio rises to 2,260 and the query speedup to 11.9 at 64^3.

title: FlockWorld: Toward Population-Scale Multi-Agent Video World Models through Artificial Life Simulation
abstract: Most action-conditioned video world models remain limited to a single player, while existing multiplayer models support only small, fixed groups of agents. We introduce FlockWorld, an artificial-life environment built on Reynolds's Boids algorithm for studying population-scale multi-agent video world models. Specifically, FlockWorld renders synchronized egocentric crops, assigns distinct colors to preserve camera-agent identity across views, exposes rule-derived accelerations as actions, and lets the number of camera agents be configured independently of the size of the surrounding population. We further introduce FlockDiT, an action-conditioned latent diffusion transformer trained with flow matching on FlockWorld data to jointly generate synchronized egocentric videos for multiple agents. Our results suggest that joint generation benefits agent detection at density-matched settings and that diffusion forcing improves rollout fidelity. Together, FlockWorld and FlockDiT provide a controlled testbed for multi-agent video generation.

title: Agentic AI Orchestration Framework for Spatial Intelligence: Supply Chain Deployment
abstract: Industrial spatial decisions are assembled across systems that share neither a reference frame nor an owner, and analysts spend substantial effort reconciling those systems rather than reasoning about space. This paper presents ANASSA, a reference architecture integrating structured reasoning, multi-agent workflow orchestration, authoritative spatial grounding, and feedback-driven execution, and reports its instantiation in an operating supply-chain deployment. The architecture places typed data contracts at agent boundaries, validates spatial claims against a certified authoritative foundation, and enforces two blocking human-in-the-loop approvals inside a six-step cognitive loop. The deployment covers multi-hazard risk assessment on an ocean-and-inland freight lane, including cold-chain excursion detection over container telemetry. Across a three-month proof of concept (POC) with three implementation iterations, three deployment outcomes are reported: 25% improvement in data quality, 50% reduction in spatial workflow runtime, and 60% lower decision latency relative to the preceding manual workflow. Absolute deployment-scale quantities and baseline counts are confidential; reported percentages are observed relative changes. These are uncontrolled deployment observations, not controlled experiments. We therefore specify instrumentation and ablation protocols for mechanism-level evaluation.

title: Software Engineering for AI-Driven Science
abstract: AI has made significant contributions to scientific discovery. Autonomous agents can now independently analyse complex problems, design experiments, write and execute code, analyse findings, and derive scientific conclusions. Nevertheless, errors in AI-generated code, experimental procedures, or evidence interpretation can lead to invalid research conclusions, undermining the reliability and reproducibility of automated scientific discovery. In this vision paper, we propose Software Engineering for AI-Driven Science (SE4AI4Sci) as an emerging research area for addressing this challenge. As an organising framework, we introduce the Scientific Assurance Chain, connecting intent, experimental design, implementation, execution, evidence, and claim. Through six documented failures in recent AI-for-science systems, we show where this chain can break, where existing assurance mechanisms fall short, and what new research challenges follow. We also outline a research agenda for adapting and extending software engineering techniques across the chain.

title: Cumulative Marginal Matching for One-Step Diffusion
abstract: The sampling procedures of diffusion and flow-matching models involve hundreds of denoising steps incurring substantial inference time, which has motivated a growing body of work on training schemes for few-step and one-step generation. Existing approaches primarily seek to align the generation trajectory of few-step and base models, yet their training objectives only involve discrepancies at a single point in the trajectory, encouraging only local \emph{point-level} alignment. While recent methods such as \emph{Shortcut-CSL} introduce cumulative objective that enforce alignment over the entire trajectory, this is suboptimal as they do not directly enforce alignment between the distributions induced by the two models throughout the generation process. We propose \emph{Cumulative Marginal Matching} (CMM), a principled objective for few-step generation: by viewing flow-matching as a sequence of intermediate marginal distributions connecting the prior and data distributions, CMM directly optimizes the cumulative discrepancy between the base and few-step marginal distributions over the entire sequence. Specifically, we formulate this discrepancy using the Wasserstein-2 distance. By exploiting the pushforward representation of flow-matching, we transform an intractable cumulative Wasserstein objective into a tractable surrogate that can be optimized using samples from the intermediate marginal, which are readily generated through the conditional interpolation process of flow-matching. Furthermore, we show that the existing \emph{Shortcut-CSL} objective arises as a first-order approximation of that of the CMM, establishing a theoretical connection between the two objectives. Experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate improvement in generation quality over \emph{Shortcut-CSL} and other state-of-the-art one- and few-step baselines under identical training budgets.

title: Large Language Models: A Plain-Language Overview for Engineers
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are neural networks trained on huge text collections to generate text by predicting what comes next. Engineers using ChatGPT and other generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools need a clear picture of what training changes and prompts add. The article starts with the Transformer, which connects words in context, and pre-training, where models learn to predict text. It then explains how fine-tuning adapts models to requests, with reinforcement learning from human feedback using human answer rankings. Next, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) supplies documents, while chain-of-thought prompting encourages intermediate steps and agents use tools. FlashAttention lowers training and running costs by reducing data movement during attention; quantized low-rank adaptation (QLoRA) saves fine-tuning memory. Readers get a life cycle figure and tables comparing methods and their limits. A short checklist for judging LLM evaluation claims flags test material in training (data contamination) and model-based grading (LLM-as-a-judge). It also covers very long inputs (long context) and hallucination, meaning false or unsupported claims. Check factual accuracy separately from whether an answer sounds helpful.

title: NovaFabric: A Black-Box Recorder for AI Agents with Sealed, Replayable, Diffable and Auditable Runs
abstract: An AI agent run is no longer a function call. It is a cascade of prompts, model calls, tool invocations, file and network effects and sub-agents. When such a run misbehaves, or an auditor asks what happened, logs and traces answer poorly: they are mutable, partial and cannot be re-executed. This technical report describes NovaFabric, an open-source (Apache-2.0) black-box recorder for AI agents that turns a run into a sealed, replayable, diffable and auditable evidence capsule. The design rests on two formats only. The Run Capsule is a directory of flat files and the source of truth; every database is a rebuildable index over capsules. The Evidence Bundle is the signed export for an auditor. Everything else follows existing standards: OpenTelemetry GenAI, OpenLineage, W3C PROV, in-toto/DSSE, RFC 3161 and CycloneDX. A single-node run is the smallest case of a distributed one; the schema supports a capsule hierarchy for Slurm arrays and Kubernetes jobs, though automatic parent finalization is library-only today. The report covers the architecture and the engines behind the verb chain capture, seal, replay, diff and audit: fail-closed mocked replay; a diff gate with a stable exit-code contract; DSSE signatures that bind their intent and a capsule root that commits to file names; a capsule treated as untrusted input; signer identity-trust levels with offline TSA and CRL checking; maker-checker promotion against an operator-held trust list; and a deny-by-default authorization table for every dashboard route. It presents no new experiments; the evaluation is in arXiv:2609.12582. Every count except the private ADR tally is generated by a probe script run on the public source at the v0.107.0 tag (150 top-level commands, 84 Python subpackages, 16,721 test functions), every capability carries an explicit maturity label, and honest-limits boxes state where the system stops.

title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Liver Lesion Segmentation and Structured Radiology Reporting
abstract: Despite advances in automated liver lesion segmentation, a gap remains between image-derived predictions and clinically interpretable radiology reports. Bridging this gap requires quantitative measurements that are both reproducible and traceable. We present an evidence-grounded agentic AI framework that connects liver and lesion segmentation with deterministic quantification and structured reporting. TotalSegmentator-based nnU-Net models delineate the liver, Couinaud segments, and lesions, while computational tools extract volumes, dimensions, counts, and anatomical locations. A large language model (LLM) organizes these measurements into a predefined reporting schema, with numerical consistency checks against source measurements. On 51 LiTS cases, the segmentation stage achieved a liver Dice score of 0.947, lesion sensitivity of 75.6%, and positive predictive value of 68.9%. Exploratory screening of 25,494 MERLIN reports identified 10,208 (40.0%) with liver-related abnormalities. By connecting quantitative imaging evidence with agentic report generation, this work takes a step toward human-centered medical AI that prioritizes traceability and clinical relevance.

title: How Much Graph Is Too Much? Graph Construction and Exposure in Spatio-Temporal Forecasting
abstract: Spatio-temporal graph neural networks combine a node's history with information from graph neighbors. The central question is whether graph neighbors provide predictive information beyond each node's own history. Forecast accuracy depends on both the choice of neighbors and the way graph messages enter the temporal model. We study these choices as graph construction and graph exposure on U.S. state unemployment, traffic speed, and electricity demand. Our diagnostic design uses two comparisons: varying exposure while holding the domain graph fixed, and varying construction while holding late gated integration fixed. A GRU using only each node's own history and randomized graph controls help assess what the graph contributes. Under a common change forecasting protocol, the same domain graph can improve or worsen error relative to the GRU across integration designs. Late integration alone is insufficient, while adding a fusion gate yields lower mean error in all three tasks. With late gated integration fixed, a graph based on residual correlations has the lowest mean error among the tested graphs, although randomized graphs perform similarly on unemployment. The findings support evaluating graph construction and integration together, with conclusions tied to the comparisons actually performed.

title: Do AI Coding Agents Write Infrastructure as Code Like Humans? An Empirical Study of GitHub Pull Requests
abstract: Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) configurations define cloud resources, networking, and access control, and AI coding agents increasingly write them. Little is known about how agent contributions differ from those of humans and automation bots, how maintainers evaluate them, and whether they introduce different sustainability concerns. We study 349,156 IaC pull requests (PRs) from 49,241 GitHub repositories, distinguishing humans, automation bots, silent agents, and disclosed agents. Bots account for 32.9% of ostensibly human PRs, and 12.3% of the remaining PRs contain agent traces, a share that grows over the study period. Agent PRs are about four times larger than human PRs and more often modify core infrastructure modules, whereas bots mainly maintain dependencies. Silent-agent PRs have higher overall merge rates than human PRs (87.4% vs. 78.9%) but are merged 4.0 percentage points less often within the same repositories. Disclosed agents create new infrastructure more often than humans (34.0% vs. 21.4%), and even for the same change type within the same repository, their PRs are 8.4 points less likely to be merged; silent-agent PRs show comparable acceptance for most change types. Finally, in 2,645 matched agent-human Terraform PR pairs, agent and human PRs introduce sustainability smells at similar rates (10.4% vs. 10.3%; paired odds ratio 1.02, 95% CI 0.83-1.25), most commonly missing remote state and monolithic configurations.

title: WHO ASSURES THE ASSURER? A POSITION ON META-ASSURANCE FOR AI-MEDIATED EVALUATION
abstract: Artificial intelligence is now used to evaluate other systems. Large language models (LLMs) generate assurance profiles, control questions and test cases, judge benchmark outputs, and support automated red teams. At the same time, the evaluated systems are often LLM-based agents themselves. In this position paper, we argue that this situation creates a new type of assurance problem. Three basic assumptions of classical evaluation are broken: (1) the evaluator and the target can fail in the same way (correlated blind spots); (2) the evaluation criteria are written by the same type of model that is evaluated (circular criteria); and (3) the target can influence the inputs of the evaluator (injectable evaluation). We connect this problem to known results in computer science and propose seven principles for what we call metaassurance. Finally, we present four testable propositions for future research.

title: Differentiating induced pluripotent stem cells into articular chondrocytes: advances, challenges, and future directions
abstract: Cartilage injury and osteoarthritis-associated degeneration remain major clinical challenges because articular cartilage is avascular, aneural, and alymphatic, leaving it with limited intrinsic capacity for repair. Current clinical strategies, including microfracture, osteochondral grafting, autologous chondrocyte implantation, and mesenchymal stem cell-based approaches, can relieve symptoms and partially restore tissue architecture. However, these approaches, particularly mesenchymal stem cell-based therapies, often produce fibrocartilage rather than durable hyaline cartilage and do not reliably reproduce the long-term mechanical competence or molecular identity of native articular cartilage. Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) have emerged as a promising alternative cell source for cartilage regeneration because they combine unlimited self-renewal with the capacity to generate patient-specific or allogeneic chondroprogenitors, articular chondrocytes, cartilage organoids, and engineered cartilage constructs. iPSC-derived chondrocytes also provide versatile platforms for modeling osteoarthritis and genetic skeletal disorders, performing genome editing, testing disease-modifying drugs, and developing personalized tissue-engineering systems. Nevertheless, clinical translation remains limited by protocol variability, incomplete lineage specification, hypertrophic differentiation, residual pluripotent cells, immune compatibility, tumorigenic risk, biomechanical immaturity, and the need for scalable Good Manufacturing Practice-compliant manufacturing. This review summarizes the developmental principles and molecular signaling networks that guide iPSC chondrogenesis, compares current differentiation and tissue-engineering strategies, and discusses therapeutic applications and key barriers that must be addressed to achieve safe, reproducible, and clinically effective iPSC-based cartilage repair.

title: Effect of curriculum relevance on the effectiveness of undergraduate physiotherapy programme in Kenyan universities
abstract: The effectiveness of undergraduate physiotherapy programmes is essential for producing competent practitioners who can respond to Kenya’s growing rehabilitation needs. This study examined the effect of curriculum relevance on the effectiveness of undergraduate physiotherapy programmes in Kenyan universities. The study was guided by the Context, Input, Process and Product (CIPP) evaluation model and adopted a mixed-methods convergent parallel design. It was conducted in three public universities offering undergraduate physiotherapy programmes: Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT), Masinde Muliro University of Science and Technology (MMUST), and Alupe University. The target population comprised 609 stakeholders, including students, graduates, faculty members, programme administrators, clinical supervisors, physiotherapists in charge, and a representative of the Physiotherapy Council of Kenya. A multistage sampling approach combining stratified, simple random, census and purposive sampling was used to obtain a sample of 286 respondents. Data were collected using structured questionnaires, semi-structured interviews and document analysis. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation and linear regression in SPSS version 27, while qualitative data were analyzed thematically and triangulated with quantitative findings. The findings showed that respondents generally perceived the undergraduate physiotherapy curriculum as relevant, with a composite mean of 3.81 (SD = 1.026). Understanding of programme goals and objectives received the highest rating (mean = 3.96, SD = 1.160), while incorporation of cultural and community health contexts received the lowest rating (mean = 3.63, SD = 0.968). Programme effectiveness was also positively rated, with a composite mean of 2.24 (SD = 1.252), reflecting generally favourable perceptions of graduate preparation and professional competencies. Simple linear regression established that curriculum relevance had a statistically significant positive effect on programme effectiveness (B = 1.013, β = .356, t = 5.811, p < .05), explaining 12.7% of the variation in programme effectiveness (R² = .127; F(1,232) = 33.769, p < .05). Consequently, the null hypothesis that curriculum relevance has no statistically significant effect on programme effectiveness was rejected. Qualitative findings supported the quantitative results, while emphasizing the need for continuous curriculum adaptation to changing healthcare needs, including community-based rehabilitation, tele-rehabilitation and technology-supported practice. However, when curriculum relevance was considered alongside instructional capacity, infrastructure and professional competence, its independent contribution became statistically non-significant (B = .202, β = .071, p = .156). The study concludes that curriculum relevance significantly enhances programme effectiveness when considered independently, but its impact depends on adequate resources, faculty capacity, infrastructure and clinical training opportunities. The study recommends regular stakeholder-inclusive curriculum reviews; greater integration of community-based rehabilitation, digital health, tele-rehabilitation, assistive technology, evidence-based practice and interprofessional education; alignment of student enrolment with available teaching and clinical resources; and continuous professional development for academic and clinical educators. These measures would strengthen the responsiveness, quality and effectiveness of undergraduate physiotherapy education in Kenyan universities.

title: ADEPTS: An auto-differentiable framework for time-dependent nonlinear thermo-chemical mantle convection inversion
abstract: Time-dependent mantle-dynamics inversion must simultaneously address the high dimensionality of the initial state, nonlinear rheology, and the complex propagation of gradients through long-term thermo-mechanical evolution. Here, we develop a geodynamic inversion framework ADEPTS based on a two-dimensional staggered-grid finite-difference discretization and automatic differentiation, with the aim of jointly constraining the initial temperature field and mantle material properties. The forward model solves the incompressible Stokes equations, the temperature advection–diffusion equation, and the compositional advection equation, while accounting for temperature- and strain-rate-dependent nonlinear viscosity and plastic yielding. For the nonlinear Stokes system arising at each time step, we implement two gradient-computation strategies: unrolled differentiation through a fixed number of Picard iterations and implicit differentiation based on the sufficiently converged discrete nonlinear residual equations. Numerical experiments show that unrolled differentiation enables stable inversion even when the nonlinear solve has not fully converged, while the accuracy of implicit differentiation depends on sufficient convergence of the nonlinear Stokes system. When the nonlinear solve is insufficiently accurate, both gradient consistency and optimization convergence deteriorate for implicit differentiation, whereas sufficiently converged nonlinear solves recover the expected gradient accuracy and yield reconstruction results comparable to those obtained with unrolled differentiation. Under idealized noise-free twin-experiment conditions, we further test the joint inversion of the initial temperature field and physical parameters. The joint inversion recovers the initial temperature field together with the density of a compositional anomaly, the reference viscosity, and the stress exponent, while simultaneously fitting observations of the final-time temperature field, surface horizontal velocity, and surface normal stress. The two differentiation strategies impose different requirements on the accuracy of the nonlinear Stokes solve, but both can be used for gradient computation and inversion within a differentiable time-dependent mantle-dynamics framework.

title: Problems of digitalization of veterinary control (supervision)
abstract: This article examines the legal challenges and prospects for the digitalization of state veterinary control (supervision) in the Russian Federation. Digitalization of veterinary control (supervision) significantly impacts the rationale for measures taken to protect citizens from substandard agricultural products, the epizootic situation in the constituent entities of the Russian Federation, and the overall effectiveness of the Federal Service for Veterinary and Phytosanitary Surveillance. The authors analyze the functions of the Federal Service for Veterinary and Phytosanitary Surveillance in organizing the work of state veterinary services in rural areas. Based on an analysis of the regulatory framework, the functioning of federal state information systems, and modern digital technologies, the authors substantiate the importance of transitioning to electronic veterinary accompanying documents, integrating information platforms, and implementing artificial intelligence tools to improve the effectiveness of control and supervision activities. Particular attention is paid to ensuring food security, product traceability, combating counterfeiting, as well as the organizational and personnel challenges associated with the digitalization of state veterinary control. The authors conclude that the development of a unified digital ecosystem in the field of veterinary supervision helps reduce administrative barriers, increase transparency and efficiency in management decision-making, and strengthen national security in the agroindustrial complex.

title: Soil Biogeochemical Cycles and Their Influence on Crop-Environment Dynamics in Changing Climates
abstract: Soil biogeochemical cycles regulate nutrient availability, soil organic matter dynamics, greenhouse-gas exchange, and crop productivity, but their functioning is increasingly modified by climate change. This review synthesizes the major processes controlling carbon (C), nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), sulfur (S), and silicon (Si) cycling in agricultural soils and examines how these interconnected cycles influence soil-crop-environment relationships under changing climatic conditions. Warming, drought, excessive soil moisture, altered precipitation, and elevated atmospheric CO2 can modify microbial activity, organic-matter turnover, nutrient mineralization and immobilization, redox conditions, nutrient losses, and greenhouse-gas emissions. Their effects are strongly context dependent and vary with soil texture, pH, organic-matter content, drainage, microbial communities, crop type, and management. The review further evaluates how plant nutrient acquisition, rhizosphere processes, and plant-soil-microbial feedbacks connect biogeochemical cycling with crop performance and environmental outcomes. Conservation agriculture, organic amendments, biochar, and microbial inoculants may improve nutrient retention and soil resilience, but their effectiveness depends on soil, climate, amendment properties, and management history and may involve agronomic or environmental trade-offs. We identify major knowledge gaps concerning interactions among elemental cycles, responses to compound climate extremes, microbial regulation of nutrient transformations, and the transferability of management practices across agroecosystems. Integrating long-term field experiments, process-based modelling, molecular approaches, and high-resolution soil monitoring will be essential for developing climate-resilient nutrient-management strategies.
journal: Journal of Soil, Plant and Environment

title: The Role of the South Korean Saemaul Foundation in Developing a Sustainable Oyster Mushroom Program in Bleberan Village, Special Region of Yogyakarta
abstract: Background: The Saemaul Undong program, developed by the South Korean Saemaul Foundation in Bleberan Village, Yogyakarta Special Region, is designed to promote community self-reliance through the development of oyster mushroom cultivation. This program is implemented in a community that still faces limitations in business diversification, low agricultural productivity, vulnerability to climate change, and limited institutional and technological capacity. Objective: This study aims to analyze the role of the Saemaul Foundation in developing sustainable oyster mushroom cultivation and to identify the impacts, enabling factors, and conditions necessary for the program’s sustainability. Methods: The study employs a convergent mixed-methods approach with a quantitatively dominant descriptive component with descriptive analysis based on questionnaires and a Likert scale to measure economic, social, and environmental impacts, as well as multi-scenario modeling using Python that includes minimum, moderate, and optimal scenarios. Results: The results indicate that the program has a positive impact on all three aspects, supported by training, intergenerational knowledge transfer, support from village-owned enterprises (BUMDes), market access, and halal certification. The modeling indicates that optimal sustainability requires substrate localization, production efficiency, circular waste utilization, and consistency in maintaining three production cycles per year. Conclusion: Consequently, the Saemaul Foundation needs to gradually shift its role from an input provider to a technical facilitator and market link to strengthen community self-reliance and local institutions.

title: Developing Adult Education Schools in Uttar Pradesh, India, in Light of the National Education Policy 2020 Using the Delphi Technique
abstract: This study aimed to develop a proposed framework for enhancing adult education schools in Uttar Pradesh, India, in light of the directives of the National Education Policy (NEP 2020) and the New India Literacy Programme (NILP 2022–2027). To achieve this objective, a descriptive-forecasting research methodology utilizing the Delphi technique was employed across three iterative rounds to achieve consensus among experts. The study sample comprised a panel of 20 experts and specialists in educational policy, adult education, and non-formal learning. The findings yielded a validated list of 24 indicators categorized into four primary dimensions, all achieving high consensus rates ranging between 90.0% and 100.0%, with an overall mean consensus of 95.0%. The framework encompasses: Institutional and Administrative Development, Curriculum and Educational Program Enhancement, Digital Empowerment, and ICT Integration (via national platforms such as DIKSHA), and Professional Development for Human Resources. Based on these findings, a comprehensive proposed framework was articulated to serve as an actionable guide for decision-makers at the State Literacy Mission Authority (SLMA) in Uttar Pradesh. The study concludes with practical recommendations and avenues for future research.
journal: International Journal of Educational Sciences and Arts

title: HelioDA-XFE: ERA5-Based Solar Radiation Estimation and PV Potential Classification over Eastern Anatolia, Türkiye
abstract: Accurate assessment of solar energy potential is a core input for renewable energy planning in high-altitude regions such as Eastern Anatolia, where ground measurement stations are sparse. This study proposes HelioDA-XFE, an explainable feature engineering framework that estimates daily surface solar radiation (SSRD) from same-day ERA5 reanalysis fields (concurrent estimation, not forecasting) and assigns relative, radiation-based photovoltaic (PV) resource classes over an analysis domain centred on the Eastern Anatolia Region of Türkiye. The framework consists of four steps: (1) feature generation based on lags, rolling means, and seasonality encoding, (2) feature selection with mutual information (MI), (3) XGBoost models for regression and for a three-class classification of relative PV resource classes defined by SSRD terciles, and (4) SHAP-based interpretability analysis. A total of 5,228,990 grid-cell days covering 2000-2025 on a rectangular 19x29 cell (551-cell) domain at 0.25° resolution were evaluated with an expanding-window cross-validation scheme that prevents temporal leakage. The model reached R² = 0.972 ± 0.002 and RMSE = 0.354 ± 0.009 kWh/m²/day in regression, and 92.8 ± 0.5% accuracy with 0.928 ± 0.005 macro-F1 in classification, outperforming linear and decision tree baselines in both tasks. SHAP analysis indicated that clear-sky radiation is the dominant driver (mean |SHAP| = 1.51 kWh/m²/day), followed by cloud cover layers as the second largest driver group, confirming the physical consistency of the model. A theoretical, temperature-corrected PV potential that excludes system losses yielded annual specific yields of 1799 kWh/kWp for the domain and 1824 kWh/kWp for Elazığ; transferring the trained model to the 0.1° ERA5-Land grid mapped the intra-provincial distribution of PV yield across 94 points within Elazığ province. Because the target is the ERA5 radiation field itself, these results describe temporal generalization within the ERA5 climatology rather than independent radiation accuracy, and the outputs are intended for relative comparison and pre-feasibility screening. Within that scope, the framework offers a computationally light, transparent, and locally trained tool for regional solar energy assessment.

title: Parametric Insurance in Arid Regions: International Experience and Prospects for Implementation in Uzbekistan
abstract: Climate change, increasing drought frequency and duration, water scarcity and high dependence of agricultural production on irrigation are fundamentally transforming agricultural risk profiles in arid and semi-arid economies. Traditional indemnity-based agricultural insurance, which requires individual loss assessment, is associated with high transaction costs, delayed claims settlement and limited accessibility for smallholder farmers. Parametric insurance provides an alternative by linking payouts to objectively measurable indices such as precipitation, temperature, soil moisture, vegetation health, river runoff or combinations thereof rather than to individually assessed losses. This study aims to systematize international experience in parametric and index-based insurance for climate risks and assess the prospects for adapting such instruments to Uzbekistan. The methodology combines a structured literature review, comparative institutional analysis of international insurance schemes, analysis of Uzbekistan's emerging agricultural insurance framework, and conceptual modelling of a drought insurance product suitable for irrigated and rain-fed agricultural systems. The findings indicate that a hybrid index combining meteorological, hydrological and satellite-derived indicators is potentially more appropriate for Uzbekistan than a simple rainfall index. The proposed model should account for precipitation deficits, dry-spell duration, temperature stress, vegetation conditions and irrigation-water availability while incorporating crop-specific phenological stages. A three-level architecture is proposed: micro-level insurance for individual producers, portfolio-level coverage for agricultural clusters and producer organizations, and sovereign or quasi-sovereign coverage against catastrophic drought events. The study demonstrates that parametric insurance should not be regarded as a substitute for climate adaptation. Its effectiveness is enhanced when combined with water-saving technologies, agricultural advisory systems, digital financial infrastructure, agricultural lending and reinsurance. Uzbekistan's recently established agricultural insurance framework creates a significant institutional opportunity for introducing parametric mechanisms as part of a broader climate-risk financing strategy.

title: Implementation Processes and Mediating Factors in Agricultural Support Programmes: Evidence from Zambia's Transition from FISP to CASP
abstract: Background: Agricultural input subsidy programmes remain central to food security policy in sub-Saharan Africa, yet persistent implementation failures undermine their effectiveness. Zambia's Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP), a major intervention reaching over one million smallholder households, has faced chronic challenges in timely delivery, equitable targeting, and digital access through its e-voucher system. As Zambia transitions from FISP to the Comprehensive Agriculture Support Programme (CASP), understanding these implementation barriers is critical for designing more effective support. This article examines the implementation processes of FISP in a remote rural context and identifies the institutional, socio-economic, and environmental factors that mediate programme effectiveness. Methods: The study employed a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design. Quantitative data were collected from 300 households (150 FISP beneficiaries and 150 non-beneficiaries) in Kawimbe ward, Mbala District, Northern Province, using structured questionnaires measuring e-voucher functionality, input timeliness, accessibility, targeting fairness, and mediating factors. Qualitative data were gathered through 15 key informant interviews with agricultural officers, agro-dealers, traditional leaders, and cooperative leaders, and 12 focus group discussions stratified by gender and beneficiary status. Data were analysed using logistic regression, hierarchical regression, mediation analysis, and thematic analysis. Results: Implementation failures were pervasive. Only 34% of beneficiaries received inputs on time, with mean delays of 3.4 weeks. E-voucher functionality challenges affected 52% of beneficiaries, and agro-dealer stock-outs affected 55%. Female-headed households comprised only 14% of beneficiaries despite constituting 22% of farming households. Geographic location (distance to agro-dealer) and female-headed household status were significant predictors of late delivery (AOR=1.15 per km, p=0.003; AOR=2.84, p=0.006, respectively). Cooperative membership was protective (AOR=0.42, p=0.014). Thematic analysis revealed five major themes: "The Digital Entitlement Gap," "The Proximity Penalty," "Gendered Exclusion," "Elite Capture and Political Interference," and "The Timeliness-Yield Connection." Conclusion: Implementation failures in FISP reflect systemic transfer entitlement failures that disproportionately affect remote and female-headed households. These findings provide critical evidence for designing CASP with decentralised logistics, multiple delivery channels, gender-sensitive targeting, mobile distribution points, and strengthened community oversight. Addressing these mediating factors is essential for ensuring that agricultural support programmes achieve their intended food security outcomes in remote rural contexts.

title: Cabbage yield estimation with multi‐view convolutional neural networks from UAV‐derived point clouds
abstract: Three‐dimensional (3D) data from remote sensing, including point clouds, provide detailed canopy structural information that can enhance both estimation accuracy and model generalization. The main objective of this study was to evaluate the accuracy of per‐plant yield estimation of cabbage ( Brassica oleracea var. capitata L.) using a multi‐view convolutional neural network approach based on 3D projection images from multiple viewpoints. In addition, the generalization ability of this approach was examined using test datasets from unseen fields. Four types of models were established in this study. Two models used multi‐view images with eight oblique views, either with or without an additional top‐down view. The other two were baseline models for comparison: a single‐image convolutional neural network using orthomosaic crops and a simple pixel‐based linear model. The models were evaluated on datasets from the same field as training and validation, as well as on two independent fields. The multi‐view models achieved Lin's concordance correlation coefficient of 0.74 ± 0.013 and 0.73 ± 0.017 on the dataset from the same field as training and validation, which exceeds the single‐image models. Although prediction errors increased in independent fields compared with random‐split test dataset, multi‐view models outperformed the baselines, demonstrating robustness under extrapolative conditions. Gradient‐weighted Class Activation Mapping results suggested that the multi‐view models focused on regions different from those highlighted by the single‐image model. These results highlight that multi‐view models not only improve yield estimation accuracy but also enhance generalization, supporting broader applications such as stress detection and growth monitoring in precision agriculture.

Soil erosion and land-use management influence bioavailable selenium in a highland agricultural landscape in Kenya
abstract: Selenium (Se) is an essential micronutrient whose availability in agricultural systems is influenced by geochemical, pedological, and anthropogenic factors. The study aimed to investigate the effects of soil erosion, land-use, and management practices on the bioavailability and redistribution of selenium within a soil–plant continuum in a highland agricultural landscape in Nandi County, Kenya. A stratified sampling approach was applied across three plots representing distinct land-use management practices and varying soil erosion rates. Selenium concentrations were measured both in soils and crops (maize, beans, and pumpkin) collected from the experimental sites. Total and bioavailable Se concentrations in soils were evaluated using a mixed acid digestion (HF, HNO3, and H2O2) and an ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) extraction, respectively, followed by ICP-MS analysis. Structural equation modelling and regression analyses revealed that soil pH (β = − 0.41, p 0.05). These findings suggest that appropriate land management and erosion mitigation may help maintain soil Se bioavailability, while targeted agronomic strategies could be considered to enhance crop Se concentrations. However, the relatively low Se concentrations observed in several crops suggest a potential concern regarding Se adequacy, and assessment of dietary intake and human biomarkers would be required to establish nutritional risk. Soil erosion and land use influence soil selenium bioavailability. Despite soil selenium concentrations, crops show poor uptake efficiency. Integrated soil management and biofortification may inform local biofortification strategies. Soil erosion and land use influence soil selenium bioavailability. title: Understanding Sexual Experiences through the EX-PLISSIT Model: A Qualitative Study of Young and Middle-Aged Chinese Women on Peritoneal Dialysis
abstract: This study aims to explore the real-life sexual experiences of young and middle-aged Chinese women undergoing peritoneal dialysis within the socio-cultural context of Confucianism, providing a basis for developing targeted interventions. A phenomenological design was employed, with semi-structured interviews conducted among 15 female peritoneal dialysis patients using an interview guide based on the EX-PLISSIT model; data were analyzed using Colaizzi’s method with MAXQDA software, yielding four main themes and eleven sub-themes: Multidimensional Sexual Health Impairment (Reduced Sexual Function, Lower Sexual Self-esteem, and Weakening of the Wife’s Role), Lack of Sexual Awareness (Sexual Knowledge Deviation and Insufficient Information Support), Intimacy Dual-path Differentiation (Negative Coping and Relational Alienation, Positive Coping and Relational Bonding), and Diverse Sexual Health Support Needs (Privacy Protection, Service Accessibility, Professional Integration, and Long-term Support). This study elucidates the multidimensional sexual distress experienced by these women and validates the EX-PLISSIT model’s utility in transforming subjective sexual experiences into actionable intervention targets. Consequently, nurses should incorporate sexual health assessments into routine peritoneal dialysis care. Guided by the EX-PLISSIT framework, they can employ “permission-giving” to navigate cultural taboos, explore contributing factors, and deliver structured, needs-based interventions that enhance intimacy and sexual quality of life.

Salinity tolerance dynamics in selected crop species at germination stage under in vitro and in situ conditions in Patuakhali, Bangladesh
abstract: Salinity is a major abiotic stress limiting crop productivity, predominantly in coastal regions. This study aimed to evaluate the salinity tolerance of selected crop species at the germination stage under both in vitro (petri dishes) and in situ (pot culture) conditions. The main research question was to identify crop species capable of tolerating different salinity levels and to assess their physiological and ionic responses for suitability in saline coastal regions of Bangladesh. Fourteen crop species from pulse, vegetable, fodder, and fibrous groups were tested under salinity levels of 0, 4.50, 8.65, and 13.07 dS m⁻¹ in petri dishes. Parameters measured included germination percentage (GP), shoot and root length, fresh and dry weight, salinity tolerance index (TI), sensitivity index (SI), and Na+: K+. The five best-performing species in petri dishes were further evaluated in pot culture using saline soil (0.73–15.42 dS m⁻¹). Statistical analyses were conducted using ANOVA and Tukey’s test to determine the significance differences among the treatments. Germination generally decreased with increasing salinity, though snake bean and millet performed better at moderate levels. Five species showed GP > 80% in vitro, while in situ results exceeded 87%. Snake bean, cucumber, and gima kalmi were salt-tolerant up to 8.65 dS m⁻¹, while mung bean, jute, and kenaf were moderately tolerant. However, low control germination of millet limits confidence in salinity tolerance classification. A balanced Na+: K+ contributed to higher tolerance. Snake bean, cucumber, and gima kalmi are promising salt-tolerant crops, while several others show moderate tolerance. These findings provide preliminary evidence for prioritizing candidate crops for further field-based evaluation and adaptation strategies in saline coastal regions of Bangladesh.

title: Reassessment of a GWAS study of submergence survival in Arabidopsis highlights new genetic hubs and pathways involved in stress tolerance
abstract: Climate change threatens global crop productivity, making it crucial to understand the genetic basis of plant stress tolerance. A decade ago, a genome-wide association study (GWAS) in Arabidopsis thaliana identified genetic loci linked to survival under submergence. Since then, genomic resources have expanded. This study reanalyzes that original phenotypic dataset using updated, high-density SNP databases and other platforms to uncover new genetic components of submergence tolerance. Our reassessment successfully recovered 15 of the 20 previously reported SNPs and identified locus-level concordance for these previously reported SNPs regions and expanded the candidate list with an additional 104 new genes. These genes participate in biological pathways coherent for submergence survival, including cell wall/cytoskeleton remodeling, reactive oxygen species management, hormone signaling (ethylene, auxin, and ABA), and energy-saving metabolic reprogramming involving nucleotide salvage, translational control, and C:N management. Notably, we identify ten overlapping genetic signals between analyses, including a histidyl-tRNA synthetase (HRS1) and an uncharacterized ethylene-responsive factor (ERF17), and signals in the long arm of Chromosome 5, suggesting putative integrative nodes. This study demonstrates that reassessing existing GWAS data with updated models, cross-platform validation, and transcriptional filtering can expand biologically relevant gene lists for future experimental validation and crop improvement.

title: Coupled carbon-nitrogen-phosphorus cycling in rice-rapeseed rotations: A redox-stoichiometric framework for climate-smart nutrient synchronization
Biochemistry of protozoan Metacaspases: Structure, processing, and inhibition.
abstract: Metacaspases are calcium-dependent cysteine proteases (clan CD, family C14) present in fungi, protozoa, and plants but absent from mammals. Although structurally related to metazoan caspases, they differ in substrate specificity (cleaving after arginine or lysine), calcium-dependent activation, and monomeric architecture. In protozoan parasites such as Trypanosoma brucei, T. cruzi, Leishmania spp., Plasmodium spp., and Toxoplasma gondii, metacaspases regulate programmed cell death, cell cycle progression, protein quality control, differentiation, and virulence. Their absence in humans and essentiality in multiple parasitic life stages make them attractive drug targets for neglected tropical diseases. This review integrates structural, biochemical, functional, and pharmacological data on protozoan metacaspases. We examine calcium-dependent activation, the role of calcium homeostasis, functional diversification across parasite lineages, and the involvement of metacaspases in apoptotic and non-apoptotic pathways. Recent advances in small-molecule inhibitor discovery are covered, including oxime-based compounds, chalcones, flavonoids, peptidomimetics, and non-peptidyl scaffolds from virtual screening and rational design. A comparative biochemical analysis highlights species-specific differences in calcium dependence, processing, and regulation. Inhibitors are systematically classified by kinetic mechanism, offering a framework for understanding their mode of action and guiding structure-based drug design. We address selectivity challenges arising from metacaspase conservation across eukaryotes, distinguish experimentally validated binding sites from computationally predicted ones, and critically evaluate current in vivo and in vitro evidence for inhibitors in disease models. Finally, we discuss isoform redundancy, species-specific regulation, and translational development challenges, along with future research directions. title: Large-scale continuous estimation of soil heavy metal content using 3DT-NET and DS-corrected hyperspectral imagery.
abstract: This study proposes a novel framework for soil heavy metal pollution monitoring and source apportionment, namely "multi-source data fusion-spectral correction-feature selection-inversion mapping-uncertainty assessment-source apportionment." In this study, GF-5A and Sentinel-2B images were fused using the 3DT-NET algorithm, and the fused imagery was subsequently corrected using the direct standardization (DS) spectral correction method. Fractional-order differentiation was then applied to enhance soil spectral features, while the Boruta algorithm was employed to select informative bands for heavy metal modeling. Machine learning models were developed to predict heavy metal concentrations, and the associated prediction uncertainty was quantitatively assessed. Finally, soil heavy metal pollution sources in specific sampling areas were identified through correlation analysis. Compared with GF-5A imagery alone, the fused and DS-corrected spectra increased the best prediction accuracy (R2) from 0.476 to 0.611 for Pb (+28.4%), from 0.448 to 0.551 for Zn (+23.0%), and from 0.654 to 0.764 for Cu (+16.8%). Relative to Sentinel-2B imagery, the improvements were even greater, with R2 increasing from 0.285 to 0.611 for Pb (+114.4%), from 0.215 to 0.551 for Zn (+156.3%), and from 0.458 to 0.764 for Cu (+66.8%). Source apportionment results further showed that Zn is jointly controlled by elevation and slope, whereas Pb and Cu are mainly affected by slope. Overall, the proposed framework provides an effective and transferable solution for overcoming the spectral-spatial trade-off in satellite remote sensing, and offers strong support for regional pollution screening, risk zoning, source tracing, and precision land management.

title: Preoperative breast cancer subtyping using multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging and explainable machine learning.
abstract: Breast cancer exhibits substantial molecular heterogeneity with distinct molecular subtypes that differ markedly in prognosis, treatment response, and clinical management. To enable imaging-based subtype differentiation, this study retrospectively analyzed suspected breast cancer patients who underwent breast MRI between September 2020 and September 2024, finally including 292 breast cancer lesion records from 283 patients with postoperative IHC-confirmed subtypes. All patients received SyMRI, DCE-MRI, and DWI. Quantitative metrics were extracted-pre- and post-contrast T1, T2, and PD values, T1-Ratio, and PD-Ratio, ADC, TIC patterns, BI-RADS categories, and morphological features. Elastic-net logistic regression was embedded within the training folds for feature selection, and five machine-learning classifiers-LR, SVM, KNN, RF, and DT-were evaluated using the historical internal test set and repeated patient-grouped nested cross-validation. After false-discovery-rate adjustment, ADC-Tumor, post-contrast T1, post-contrast T2, T1-Ratio, and Burr sign differed significantly across molecular subtypes. Repeated patient-grouped nested validation selected the random-forest model (macro-average one-vs-rest AUC, 0.946 ± 0.035), which achieved a macro-average AUC of 0.862 (95% CI, 0.789-0.927) in the historical internal test set; class-specific results and confusion matrices were reported with uncertainty intervals. TreeSHAP analysis of the selected random-forest model identified post-contrast T1 (overall mean absolute SHAP, 0.053), post-contrast T2 (0.053), and T1-Ratio (0.050) as the leading overall contributors, with distinct subtype-specific patterns. These findings support further investigation of multiparametric breast MRI as a preliminary adjunct for preoperative subtype assessment; the model cannot replace histopathological and IHC confirmation and requires independent external validation.

title: From Cell to Circuit: Altered Functional Network Topology in iPSC-derived Neuronal Circuits in Major Depressive Disorder.
abstract: The functional organization of brain networks relies on a delicate balance between segregation and integration, which supports both localized neural processing and global information exchange. While numerous whole-brain imaging studies have linked disruptions in this balanced topology to Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), it remains unclear whether such macroscale alterations are reflected in neuronal circuit dynamics at the cellular level. In this study, we investigated whether neuronal networks derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) of nine MDD patients display a distinct functional topology compared to nine matched controls. We obtained skin biopsies from all participants, cultivated fibroblasts, and reprogrammed these into hiPSCs. We then differentiated hiPSCs into neural progenitor cells (NPCs), which we later developed into neurons. We recorded spontaneous activity in the derived neuronal networks using calcium imaging, and applied graph theory analysis to quantify differences in functional topology between groups. We observed a significant decrease in the clustering coefficient and average node degree in MDD-derived neural networks. Furthermore, global efficiency showed a downward trend across varying thresholds and network sizes in patient-derived lines. Together, these findings demonstrate diminished segregation and reduced overall nodal connectivity in MDD-derived neural networks. This suggests that a predisposition for less efficient functional topology exists in depression at the microscale, highlighting the utility of hiPSC technology in modeling cellular disease mechanisms and exploring potential cellular correlates of network-level phenomena reported in depression.

Polyol Pathway Inhibition by Epalrestat Attenuates Pathological Bone Loss through Redox Homeostasis and Sorbitol-Linked Calcium Signaling.
abstract: The contribution of polyol metabolism to pathological bone remodeling remains incompletely understood. Here, we examined its role in osteoclastogenesis and evaluated the skeletal effects of epalrestat, a clinically approved aldose reductase inhibitor. Exploratory single-cell analysis of two human femoral-head specimens suggested greater macrophage-associated polyol-pathway activity in the osteoporosis specimen. In primary bone marrow-derived macrophages, silencing of Akr1b3 and Sord produced opposing effects on osteoclast differentiation. Epalrestat suppressed RANKL-induced osteoclastogenesis and attenuated bone loss in diabetic, ovariectomy-induced, and inflammatory mouse models under early-intervention regimens. Mechanistic analyses showed improved NADPH/NADP⁺ and GSH/GSSG balance, reduced oxidative stress, and attenuated cytosolic and mitochondrial Ca²⁺ signals and Ca²⁺ oscillations. Genetic and osmotic-compensation experiments further supported a model in which intracellular sorbitol contributes to the osmotic regulation of Ca²⁺ oscillations. Additional findings included reduced inflammation in osteolysis and arthritis models, altered macrophage polarization, and partial preservation of bone marrow vascular features. Together, these findings connect glucose metabolism with redox and Ca²⁺ regulation during osteoclast differentiation and provide a rationale for further evaluation of epalrestat in skeletal disease.

title: GABARAPL1 drives therapeutic differentiation of cancer cells by targeting epigenetic changes regulated by SFPQ.
abstract: Differentiation-based cancer therapy is a potentially low-toxicity approach with demonstrated clinical benefits. However, the therapeutic efficacy of differentiation therapy remains limited in tumor types other than acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL). Our previous studies reported that diptoindonesin G (Dip G), a natural compound, can induce differentiation in both acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cells and basal-like breast cancer cells. In this study, we report a crucial role of GABAA receptor-associated protein-like 1 (GABARAPL1) in driving cancer cell differentiation. By utilizing myeloid cell differentiation models and primary leukemic cells, we demonstrate that upregulation of GABARAPL1 expression was crucial for Dip G-induced differentiation and that Dip G upregulated GABARAPL1 expression by targeting nucleolin (NCL). Also, GABARAPL1 promoted differentiation independent of its autophagic function. Both pharmacological and genetic upregulation of GABARAPL1 expression effectively overcame the differentiation blockade in various tumor models, including AML cells. Mechanistically, GABARAPL1 interacted with splicing factor proline and glutamine rich (SFPQ) and recruited MDM2 to promote the degradation of SFPQ by the proteasome. Upon SFPQ depletion, the transcription of linker histone H1.2 gene was repressed, which in turn rescued the transcription of the differentiation-related pathway. Our study not only highlights the contribution of GABARAPL1 to differentiation but also provides a potential therapeutic strategy aimed at expanding the scope of application of differentiation-based cancer therapy.

title: Heterologous expression of LbbHLH36 from Lycium barbarum enhances carotenoid accumulation in tomato fruits via synergistic activation of biosynthesis and suppression of degradation.
abstract: Carotenoids are critical determinants of nutritional quality in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) fruits, and their biosynthesis is tightly regulated by the bHLH transcription factor family. In this study, we investigated the heterologous regulatory function of LbbHLH36, a gene isolated from Lycium barbarum L., in carotenoid accumulation and its responsiveness to abiotic stresses in tomato. The LbbHLH36 coding sequence was cloned into the pNULPGE700 vector and introduced into the model tomato cultivar 'Micro Tom' via Agrobacterium-mediated leaf disc transformation. Quantitative real-time PCR revealed that LbbHLH36 transcript levels peaked in mature fruits of transgenic lines and were associated with significant upregulation of key early biosynthetic genes, including SlPSY1, SlPSY2, SlPDS, and SlZDS. Enzymatic assays further demonstrated increased activities of the rate-limiting enzymes phytoene synthase (PSY) and phytoene desaturase (PDS), alongside a marked suppression of carotenoid cleavage dioxygenase 4 (CCD4) activity in transgenic plants. Metabolomic analyses confirmed that overexpression of LbbHLH36 substantially elevated total carotenoid, lycopene, and β-carotene contents in tomato fruits. Furthermore, LbbHLH36 expression was strongly induced by high temperature, low temperature, drought, and salt stress, suggesting its potential involvement in crosstalk between stress responses and primary metabolism. Collectively, our findings reveal that LbbHLH36 acts as a positive regulator of carotenoid accumulation in tomato through a dual mechanism that concurrently regulate biosynthetic flux and attenuates catabolic degradation, highlighting its value as a candidate gene for nutritional quality improvement in Lycium barbarum, tomato, and other Solanaceous crops.
