title: Crop Yield Estimation With Help of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) & Advanced Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Determining Crop Yield Potential is increasingly becoming part of Intelligent Precision Agriculture Technology used to optimise management of farms, to enhance the use of resources & to achieve sustainable food production. Traditional Yield Assessment methods carried out through manual observation and statistical assessment (in most cases) require significant time, resources, and are often not effective because they do not account for the spatial variability present within agricultural fields. Therefore, this research proposes the development of an innovative intelligent crop yield prediction framework based on UAV technology, and advanced Remote Sensing & Artificial Intelligence Techniques, as an alternative to the traditional method of measurement. The current study reports on data collected from wheat fields using UAV collected high-resolution aerial photographs captured with RGB imaging cameras. The collected aerial imagery data were then processed using photogrammetric reconstruction techniques to create orthorectified maps of fields and 3D representations of wheat crops-from this data advanced image processing was performed for the purpose of Segmentation, Canopy Extraction and analysis of the Spatial Variability in Wheat Crops. UAV imagery was used to obtain various crop features (phenotypic and spectral), including: percentage of vegetation coverage, canopy texture, plant vigor, biomass characteristics, and growth variability. RGB-based vegetation indices (GLA, VARI, RGBVI, and ExG) were derived from UAV images for analysis of crop health and physiology. The extracted features were used to develop yield prediction models based on machine learning and deep learning algorithms. To predict yield, we used various predictive models (RF, SVM, DN, and LASSO). Performance of the models was compared using statistical measures such as root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and coefficient of determination (R²). The results showed that the deep learning models outperformed the other prediction algorithms, due to their ability to learn complex spatial/non-linear relationships from UAV imagery. The suggested framework offers a quick, automated, and non-destructive method of estimating agricultural yield and for use within precision agriculture. The combination of aerial imagery from UAVs (drones), analysis through GIS, and data mining through Artificial Intelligence will permit a more efficient means for monitoring agriculture and making data-driven decisions at the farm level. The results of this research highlight the benefits that can be achieved from the development and application of UAV-enabled Smart Agriculture systems in terms of increasing productivity, decreasing resource wastage, and contributing to sustainable agricultural practices.

title: Fear-Specific Technophobia as a Mediator Between Daily Technical Support and Instrumental Versus Hedonic Technology Use in Later Life: Cross-Sectional Survey Study
abstract: Background Population aging and rapid digitalization have intensified concerns about older adults’ digital participation. Although access disparities have narrowed, older adults continue to differ from younger groups in how they use digital technologies, with their use skewed toward instrumental rather than hedonic purposes. Technophobia is a salient psychological barrier; yet, its distinct fear dimensions and their links to different forms of technology use remain insufficiently differentiated. Daily technical support (DTS) may provide an important sociotechnical context for understanding these relationships. Objective This study aimed to test how DTS promotes older adults’ instrumental and hedonic technology use by reducing multidimensional technophobia (fear of inconvenience, fear of personal failure, and human-machine ambiguity) and whether these mechanisms differ by gender. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among Chinese adults aged ≥55 years recruited via online platforms and offline communities in Nanjing (June-October 2024). A total of 212 valid responses were included (mean age 66.96, SD 6.96, range 55‐86 years; 142/212, 68.4% women). Measures assessed day-to-day technical support, 3 dimensions of technophobia, instrumental versus hedonic technology use, and demographic variables. We used partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 5000 bootstrap resamples to test direct, indirect, and moderated mediation effects, reporting 95% bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) CI. Results DTS significantly reduced fear of inconvenience (β=−0.455, 95% BCa CI −0.632 to −0.229; P<.001) but did not significantly affect fear of personal failure (P=.12) or human-machine ambiguity (P=.26). Fear of inconvenience and human-machine ambiguity negatively predicted instrumental use (IU; β=−0.215, 95% BCa CI −0.410 to −0.009; P=.05 and β=−0.211, 95% BCa CI −0.389 to −0.001; P=.04). DTS had a positive direct effect on IU (β=0.104, 95% BCa CI 0.009 to 0.203; P=.04) but not on hedonic use (HU; β=0.075; P=.11). The indirect effect of DTS on IU through fear of inconvenience was significant (β=0.097, 95% BCa CI 0.020-0.204). Gender moderated the effect of DTS on fear of inconvenience (β=0.287, 95% BCa CI 0.052-0.518; P=.02), and such conditional indirect effect was significant for men (β=0.098, 95% BCa CI 0.001-0.219) but not for women (β=0.036, 95% BCa CI −0.002 to 0.116). Conclusions DTS was associated with greater instrumental technology use among older adults through lower fear of inconvenience, with a stronger indirect association among men, whereas no comparable pathway emerged for HU. This suggests that gender may shape how older adults benefit psychologically from technical support rather than reflect general differences in support needs. Interventions should move beyond one-size-fits-all approaches by providing targeted, task-oriented support that addresses older adults’ specific technological fears and practical barriers.

title: Agentic Orchestration for Rapid Evidence Reviews: A Transferable Methodology Using General-Purpose AI Agents, With a Worked Case Study in Global Nutrition Data Policy (Preprint)
abstract: BACKGROUND Policy institutions increasingly need evidence synthesized in weeks rather than years. Rapid reviews meet that need, but the compressed timeline usually forces a trade-off against thoroughness and rigour. Large language models (LLMs) now perform well on individual review tasks such as screening and data extraction, and a few purpose-built systems have automated large parts of the systematic review workflow. Those systems, however, are custom-built software that most researchers cannot access or reproduce. OBJECTIVE This paper describes a transferable methodology for conducting rigorous rapid reviews with general-purpose AI agent tools, and reports its screening accuracy against human screening, the human oversight it required, and the effort involved when applied to a real commissioned policy review. METHODS ARROW (Agentic Rapid Review Orchestration Workflow) is a methodology in which a human reviewer directs a general-purpose coordinating agent. The coordinating agent divides a rapid review into parallel specialist agents (search, screening, extraction, appraisal, and synthesis) and separate checking agents that try to disprove each extracted claim before it is accepted. The workflow builds in human decision points at protocol, inclusion, and synthesis, keeps a complete record of every step, and is designed to meet emerging reporting standards. We applied it to a PROSPERO-registered rapid review (CRD420261362746) of methods for assessing, adjusting, and integrating administrative and low-coverage survey data for child anthropometric estimation, conducted to inform the 2027 revision of the WHO, UNICEF and World Bank Joint Child Malnutrition Estimates methodology, and checked the agents against a human-screened sample. RESULTS The workflow screened 34,757 identified records through a tiered agent pipeline, using a high-throughput first-pass agent and then three independent screening agents with different instructions under a two-of-three majority rule. Every record the agents included then went to human review. Checked against the human-screened sample (372 records, about 8% of the pool), the pipeline reached a Cohen κ of 0.884, sensitivity of 93.3%, and specificity of 96.5%, against a human-to-human κ of 0.805 on an overlapping sample. Full text was retrieved for 772 of 978 records, and agents extracted 480 studies into a structured template with human checking. Every reported count was recomputed independently, and any figure that could not be audited was labelled as an estimate. The review was completed in about 15 calendar days with an estimated 40 hours of human reviewer time. CONCLUSIONS General-purpose AI agent tools make multi-agent evidence synthesis practical for individual researchers and small teams without software engineering resources. Rigour is protected by independent checking agents and by human control at every stage. We discuss what this means for research capacity and methods training, and the conditions under which the approach is appropriate.

title: Age and tumor size interact to increase the risk of incomplete response to therapy in differentiated thyroid carcinoma.
abstract: BACKGROUND This study evaluates whether age modifies the association between tumor size and the risk of incomplete response to therapy (IRT) in patients with differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC). METHODS A retrospective cohort study that included patients with DTC who underwent thyroidectomy from 2018 to 2022. Clinical outcomes were based on the 2015 ATA response to therapy classification, with the study outcome defined as biochemical or structural IRT. The cutoffs for age and tumor size were 55 years and 2 cm, respectively. We tested the interaction between age and tumor size on the risk of IRT using logistic regression models adjusted for aggressive histological factors. RESULTS There were 232 patients included, with a mean age of 41.3 years and a median follow-up of 4.0 years. There were 39 patients (17%) who were 55 years and older, and 118 (51%) patients who had a tumor size of >2 cm. There were 54 (23%) patients with IRT. Age modified the association between tumor size and IRT (P value for interaction=0.03), such that the IRT OR (95% CI) for age ≥55 years in patients with tumor size ≤2 cm was 0.56 (0.06, 4.87). While in patients ≥55 years of age with tumor size >2 cm, it was 7.54 (2.25, 25.31). Tumor size >2 cm in patients 2cm, advanced age is associated with a higher risk of IRT.

title: VirtualLab_CC: An LLM-augmented virtual laboratory for automated computational chemistry research
abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have opened new avenues for automating scientific research workflows. Systems like the AI Scientist [1] demonstrate fully autonomous endto-end research pipelines for machine learning, but their applicability to domains requiring expensive high-performance computing (HPC) resources, specialized quantum chemistry software, and rigorous thermochemical accuracy remains unexplored. Here we present VirtualLab_CC, a hybrid LLM-augmented virtual laboratory for computational chemistry that integrates Claude (Anthropic) as an orchestration layer with a multi-agent architecture, gated lifecycle management, and bidirectional HPC cluster synchronization. Unlike fully autonomous systems, VirtualLab_CC enforces human-in-the-loop quality gates at every critical decision point while automating routine operations: conformer searches, input generation, job submission and monitoring, output parsing, failure diagnosis, and manuscript preparation. The system manages 21 specialized skills spanning literature review, cluster operations, result extraction, novelty verification, AI-assisted peer review, and citation validation. We demonstrate VirtualLab_CC on a prototype case study of 1,3-dipolar cycloadditions between stabilized Criegee intermediates and biogenic terpene dipolarophiles, involving 17 molecular species, 34 conformers, and over 100 SLURM jobs across multiple calculation stages. The system successfully identified and autocorrected cluster failures, detected a methodological anomaly (a suspiciously low dioxirane barrier requiring IRC verification), and coordinated multi-method validation across three DFT functionals. VirtualLab_CC bridges the gap between fully autonomous AI research and the rigorous quality control demands of computational chemistry, providing a practical framework for LLM-augmented scientific workflows in resource-constrained HPC environments.

title: A PRIVACY PRESERVING PERSONAL AI ASSISTANT AND THE COST OF CLOUD MODEL INFERENCE: ARCHITECTURE, CAPABILITY TRADEOFFS, AND EVALUATION PROTOCOL
abstract: Personal AI assistants need reliable research and controlled access to private data. This report specifies a local-first Windows architecture and examines the capability, privacy, and operating-cost tradeoff between local Llama 3.2 3B through Ollama and self-hosted Kimi K2.5 on rented NVIDIA GPUs. We analyzed a supplied project design summary, mapped trust boundaries and failure modes, and calculated illustrative costs from a documented eight-H200 deployment and published rental rates. The design separates public research from authenticated browser sessions, enforces permissions outside the model, and requires evidence-supported answers. At an illustrative $4.59 per GPU-hour, eight H200s cost $36.72 per running hour, $4,406.40 for four hours daily over 30 days, or $26,438.40 for continuous 30-day operation, before storage and operations. An assumed 100 W incremental local draw for four hours daily at $0.15/kWh costs $1.80 monthly on an existing PC. These are scenarios, not measured deployments. Kimi K2.5 offers multimodal and agentic capabilities that a text-only 3B baseline should not be assumed to match; no matched end-to-end test was performed. Stronger cloud inference can impose substantial dedicated GPU rental cost and transfers prompts to a cloud operator. Local inference preserves a narrower data boundary at far lower incremental cash cost but requires direct task-quality evaluation.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: Securing the Ai-first Sdlc: Identity, Access, and Data Protection for Enterprise Ai Agents
abstract: AI agents can now participate in several steps of software delivery: reading requirements, changing code, requesting tests, and preparing releases. Giving them this freedom creates a difficult security question. How can an enterprise allow useful work without giving an agent more authority than the task requires? Existing practices such as least privilege, identity management, separation of duties, and audit logging provide much of the foundation. The challenge is applying them consistently when a human delegates work to agents that use several connected systems. This paper proposes Agentic Identity and Access Governance (AIAG), a security framework for the AI-First Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC). Four connected mechanisms define the proposal: a Role Conflict Matrix that checks the combined permissions of people and their sponsored agents; an Agent Access Manifest that records permitted tools and operating limits; a governed boundary between live personal-information access and general AI-assisted work; and an MCP Gateway that enforces access policy before tool calls execute. A customer notification-preference change is used to explain how these mechanisms affect development, testing, release approval, and support. We also describe credential handling, data-egress controls, audit, and practical ways to evaluate the framework. The work is conceptual, informed by technical analysis and exploratory proof-of-concept activity. No end-to-end deployment or measured security results are claimed.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: STRATEGIC MANAGEMENT OF THE EXPORT POTENTIAL OF AGRICULTURAL ENTERPRISES IN THE CONTEXT OF EUROPEAN INTEGRATION
abstract: Research on special management of the export potential of agricultural enterprises in the context of European integration processes. The relevance of the topic is due to the transformation of the foreign trade environment, changes in the conditions of access of Ukrainian agricultural products to the European Union, ensuring the adaptation of enterprises to modern regulatory market requirements, logistical challenges and increased international competition. The purpose of the article is to analyze the current state of export of agricultural products in the context of European integration processes, to generalize modern approaches to managing their export potential and to substantiate the directions of improving export management to increase the competitiveness of agricultural enterprises in the European Union market. The methodological basis of the study was the methods of analysis, comparison, generalization, systematization, statistical analysis and a systemic approach. The paper examines the current state of Ukrainian agricultural exports, identifies the main trends in the development of foreign trade in the context of European integration, analyzes the impact of changes in the trade regime with the European Union, logistical factors and geographical diversification of exports on the realization of the export potential of agricultural enterprises. It summarizes modern approaches to export potential management, including strategic, adaptive, marketing, risk-oriented and innovative approaches. It identifies the main components of the modern export potential management system and substantiates the directions of its improvement, which include the diversification of sales markets, the development of production of products with higher added value, improving logistics, digitalization of management, the implementation of international quality standards and the development of a risk management system. The practical value of the results obtained is made possible by the possibility of using the proposed approaches and directions of improvement for the efficiency of managing the export potential of agricultural enterprises, increasing their competitive positions in the European Union market and expanding their presence in other international markets.

title: Potential distribution of the cashew tree (Anacardium occidentale) in the Caatinga under CMIP6 climate projections from EC-Earth3-Veg and MIROC6
abstract: Cashew ( Anacardium occidentale ) is one of the most economically and socially important perennial crops in the Brazilian semiarid region, supporting rural livelihoods while also representing a native species adapted to tropical drylands. Understanding how climate change may alter the environmental suitability of native species is critical for conservation planning and sustainable land use in dryland ecosystems. Here, we modeled the current and future potential distribution of Anacardium occidentale (cashew tree) across the Caatinga biome using MaxEnt (v.3.4.4) and bioclimatic predictors derived from two CMIP6 Earth System Models (EC-Earth3-Veg and MIROC6) under the SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 emission scenarios for the baseline period and future projections (2050 and 2070). Occurrence records were compiled from GBIF, SpeciesLink, and Embrapa databases and refined through ecological filtering and pedoclimatic zoning. The current model showed high predictive performance (AUC ≈ 0.88), with approximately 25% of the biome classified as highly suitable (≥ 0.5), mainly concentrated in the northern Caatinga. Suitability patterns were primarily driven by precipitation seasonality, annual rainfall, elevation (altitude), and vegetation cover, indicating strong dependence on water availability and habitat structure. Future projections revealed substantial contractions of suitable areas, particularly under SSP5-8.5, with losses ranging from 68% (EC-Earth3-Veg) to 76% (MIROC6). Both climate models consistently indicated that increasing temperatures and reduced seasonal precipitation will intensify aridification, leading to a spatial retreat of the species niche toward coastal and sub-humid zones—areas that correspond to the historical origin and current climatic refugia of the species. These results demonstrate the high vulnerability of Anacardium occidentale to ongoing climate change and highlight the importance of conserving coastal and sub-humid microrefugia, as well as implementing climate-adaptive management strategies to support rural livelihoods and extractive systems dependent on cashew production in the Brazilian semi-arid region.

authors.name: Rita de Cássia Silva von Randow

title: Advancing sustainability performance through dynamic capabilities and digital transformation: evidence from Saudi higher education institutions
abstract: Digital transformation is increasingly central to how higher education institutions improve efficiency, accessibility, stakeholder engagement, and sustainability. Yet the organizational capabilities that enable universities to convert digital initiatives into multidimensional sustainability outcomes remain insufficiently differentiated. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory and the triple-bottom-line perspective, this study examines the direct and indirect relationships of sensing, seizing, learning, and integrating capabilities with sustainability performance through digital transformation in Saudi higher education institutions. Survey data from 215 academic and administrative staff serving as key informants were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Sustainability performance was specified as a reflective-formative higher-order construct comprising economic, environmental, and social dimensions. Learning and integrating capabilities were positively associated with both digital transformation and sustainability performance, whereas sensing and seizing capabilities showed no statistically significant direct or indirect relationships. Digital transformation was positively associated with sustainability performance and partially mediated the relationships of learning and integrating capabilities with sustainability performance. The model explained 44.1% of the variance in digital transformation and 58.0% of the variance in sustainability performance, while PLSpredict indicated out-of-sample predictive relevance for the three sustainability dimensions. The findings suggest that learning and integrating capabilities were more directly associated with sustainability outcomes in the study sample than sensing and seizing capabilities. For university leaders, the results emphasize institutional learning, cross-functional integration, and the embedding of digital practices into routine academic and administrative processes.

title: Cover crop management influences soil properties and grapevine performance across three growing seasons in a subtropical vineyard
abstract: Cover crop management can modify soil conditions and grapevine performance, but these responses may depend on the vegetation-management strategy and growing season. This study evaluated the effects of different cover crop management systems on soil, physiological, yield, and fruit technological variables of Vitis vinifera L. cv. Viognier cultivated in Campo Largo, Paraná, Brazil, for three growing seasons (2023–2026; 2023/24, 2024/25, and 2025/26). The treatments were: T1, spontaneous vegetation (white clover in winter and Cynodon spp in summer) with herbicide application in the vine row; T2, spontaneous vegetation without herbicide; T3, black oat in winter and predominantly white clover + angola grass in summer; T4, common vetch in winter and mombaça grass in summer; and T5, multispecies cover crop mixtures in winter (black oat + rye + vetch + forage radish) and summer ( Cynodon ssp + buckwheat + mombaça grass). Cover crop biomass and macronutrient accumulation, soil chemical and physical properties, soil water content, and grapevine nutritional, physiological, vegetative, yield, and technological variables were evaluated. Data were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models accounting for repeated measurements across growing seasons, complemented by multivariate analyses. T4 (vetch and mombaça) and T5 (oats + rye + vetch + forage radish; and Cynodon ssp + buckwheat + mombaça) generally showed greater biomass production and accumulation of N, P, K, Ca, and Mg than systems based on spontaneous vegetation. Vegetation management also affected selected surface-soil properties, particularly available P, total organic carbon, total N, cation exchange capacity, bulk density, and soil water content, although responses varied among growing seasons. Grapevine leaf area (LA) and the Yield/LA ratio did not differ among treatments, whereas physiological responses were treatment- and season-dependent. The clearest yield response occurred in 2025/26, when T2 and T4 reached 11.06 and 11.12 Mg ha −1 , respectively, approximately 20% greater than T1 (9.21 Mg ha −1 ). Soluble solids and pH were unaffected by vegetation management, and differences in titratable acidity occurred only in 2023/24. Global multivariate profiles differed among treatments but were strongly season-dependent. Overall, sown cover crops increased biomass production, nutrient accumulation, and selected surface-soil attributes, but these responses did not consistently translate into greater grapevine yield or fruit technological maturity within the 3-year experimental period.

title: Development and internal validation of CTA-based radiomics models for differentiating symptomatic from asymptomatic unruptured spontaneous intracranial vertebrobasilar artery dissection
abstract: Spontaneous intracranial vertebrobasilar artery dissection (sIVBD) has heterogeneous clinical presentations, and conventional clinical and morphologic assessment may not fully characterize lesion heterogeneity. We aimed to develop and internally validate CTA-based radiomics models for differentiating symptomatic from asymptomatic unruptured sIVBD and to evaluate the incremental contribution of radiomics beyond conventional clinical and CTA features. This retrospective single-center study included 173 patients with unruptured sIVBD, comprising 56 symptomatic and 117 asymptomatic patients. Patients were stratified into a development cohort ( n = 138) and an independent internal validation cohort ( n = 35). Radiomic features were extracted from subtraction CTA images after three-dimensional lesion segmentation. Feature reproducibility was assessed using inter-reader intraclass correlation coefficients. Four models were developed: a conventional CTA model (M1), a clinical plus conventional CTA model (M2), a radiomics XGBoost model (M3), and a combined model integrating M2 predictors with a cross-fitted radiomics probability (M4). Primary development-cohort evaluation used five-times-repeated five-fold stratified nested cross-validation. Discrimination, calibration, Brier score, and decision-curve analysis were assessed. Of 851 radiomic features, 722 (84.8%) met the prespecified reproducibility criterion. In patient-averaged out-of-fold evaluation, AUCs were 0.630 for M1, 0.681 for M2, 0.676 for M3, and 0.723 for M4. Compared with M2, M4 increased AUC by 0.0416 (95% CI, −0.0130 to 0.0962; p = 0.136) and reduced the Brier score by 0.0101 (95% bootstrap CI, −0.0208 to 0.0006). Across 25 outer folds, M4 had the highest mean AUC (0.715) and the lowest between-fold variability. In the independent internal validation cohort, AUCs were 0.814, 0.807, 0.803, and 0.966 for M1 through M4, respectively. A combined model integrating clinical variables, conventional CTA features, and cross-fitted radiomics information showed the best overall performance for differentiating symptomatic from asymptomatic unruptured sIVBD. Radiomics may provide complementary quantitative information beyond conventional assessment.

title: Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI deep learning model combined with clinical model for noninvasive differentiation of hepatocellular carcinoma from mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
abstract: This study aims to develop a framework integrating dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI)-based multi-channel deep learning combined with clinical modeling for the non-invasive preoperative discrimination between hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (MF-ICC). The internal development cohort comprised 334 surgically confirmed patients, including 231 patients with HCC and 103 with MF-ICC, and was divided at the patient level into a training cohort ( n = 233) and an internal validation cohort ( n = 101). The independent external validation cohort included 50 patients, comprising 40 with HCC and 10 with MF-ICC. We constructed separate two-dimensional deep learning models based on arterial phase, portal venous phase, and delayed phase images and then developed fusion models (2D model). A multi-channel deep learning model was further developed by directly inputting the three-phase images stacked along the channel dimension. Moreover, a clinical model was built based on independent predictors identified through multivariate analysis, which was ultimately integrated with the best-performing deep learning model. Model performance was evaluated and compared. Deep learning model directly feeding the three-phase images as a multi-channel input achieved better discrimination (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.814 in the internal validation cohort) than all single-phase and corresponding fusion models. The comprehensive 2D + multi-channel + clinical model showed the best performance for the differentiation of HCC from MF-ICC, achieving an AUC of 0.887 (95% CI, 0.819–0.954) in the internal validation cohort, and generalized well to the external validation cohort (AUC = 0.908; 95% CI, 0.811–1.000). However, no significant differences in AUCs were found among the models after correction for multiple comparisons. The fusion model integrating clinical predictors with DCE-MRI multi-phase deep learning feature may provide a valuable tool for preoperatively differentiating HCC from MF-ICC.

title: Shoot-branching number control: insight for soybean architecture breeding
abstract: Shoot branching in plants (including tillering in graminaceous crops) is a key agronomic trait affecting plant architecture, resource allocation, and final yield. Branching is a complex developmental process modulated by genetic networks regulating axillary meristem (AM) initiation and subsequent bud activation. This review summarizes the genetic regulatory networks identified in model plants, specifically Arabidopsis thaliana (a dicot) and Oryza sativa (a monocot). Building on this cross-species theoretical framework, we focus on soybean ( Glycine max ), a major economic crop, and provide a comprehensive analysis of recent progress in the functional characterization of branch number specific regulators and quantitative trait loci (QTLs). Given the bottlenecks in soybean architecture improvement resulting from its complex and highly redundant genome, recalcitrance to genetic transformation, and high environmental sensitivity, we discuss potential strategies based on multidisciplinary approaches and emerging technologies. This review aims to provide a new insight for shaping the ideal plant architecture in soybean through molecular design breeding.

title: Water quality for agricultural reuse: integrating risk assessment, governance, and sustainable implementation for resilient food systems
abstract: Global freshwater scarcity, climate change, and rising food demand have intensified the need for sustainable agricultural water management. Wastewater reuse has emerged as a strategic solution, alleviating water stress, enhancing climate resilience, and supporting circular resource management. However, the long-term sustainability of agricultural water reuse depends critically on water quality that safeguards crop productivity, ecosystem integrity, and public health. This review provides a novel interdisciplinary synthesis by integrating conventional indicators (salinity, nutrients, microbial pathogens) with emerging contaminants (pharmaceuticals, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances [PFAS], microplastics, antibiotic resistance genes). Unlike previous reviews focused narrowly on treatment or regulation, we combine Quantitative Microbial Risk Assessment (QMRA), chemical and ecological risk evaluation, and AI-assisted multi-criteria decision analysis (AI-MCDA) into a unified framework. We systematically surveyed peer-reviewed literature (Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, 2010–2025) and international guidelines (WHO, FAO, EU, US EPA, ISO), highlighting both progress and persistent gaps in harmonizing standards. Advances in monitoring technologies IoT sensors, biosensors, remote sensing, and digital twins are critically assessed for their role in real-time surveillance and adaptive governance. Case studies from the Middle East, North Africa, Europe, Australia, the United States, China, and India illustrate diverse adoption pathways shaped by institutional capacity, economic feasibility, and public acceptance. Finally, we identify specific knowledge gaps, including limited long-term field data on contaminant accumulation, inadequate regulation of PFAS and microplastics, and insufficient integration of AI into risk governance. Future research directions emphasize harmonized monitoring protocols, interdisciplinary One Health approaches, and embedding reuse within the Water–Energy–Food Nexus. By linking water quality monitoring, risk assessment, governance, and sustainable implementation, this review advances a comprehensive framework for safe and resilient agricultural water reuse in support of global food security and climate adaptation.

title: ToxPipe: integrating AI into toxicoinformatics
abstract: ToxPipe is a modular, fully open-source software stack designed to accelerate toxicological data analysis and decision-making by integrating large language model (LLM) capabilities with workflow, monitoring, and user-interface services. ToxPipe leverages existing open-source technologies like LibreChat, LiteLLM, and Langflow to provide centralized and streamlined access to different LLMs for end users and developers and logging and auditing of LLM use for organizations. ToxPipe also allows for open-source/local model support. While the ToxPipe ecosystem also supports advanced AI functions such as MCP server integration, RAG and literature search, and agent creation, we did not observe clear benefits using these configurations relative to the GPT-5.5 baseline assertion coverage scores. ToxPipe is available as a series of Docker containers for rapid and reproducible deployment.

title: Historical mobility and settlement transitions influence livestock farmers’ climate risk perceptions and strategies against feed gaps in Central Côte d’Ivoire
abstract: To meet the increasing demand for livestock and livestock products in Côte d’Ivoire, sedentary livestock farming in peri-urban areas is promoted; however, there is limited information on how these farmers manage production amid climate uncertainties. This study examined the livestock production system and evaluated farmers’ perceptions of climate risks, livestock feed gaps, and management practices. A cross-sectional survey was conducted using a semi-structured questionnaire with 126 cattle farmers across two locations (Bouaké and Toumodi) in Central Côte d'Ivoire. The locations were selected as case studies representing two contrasting settlement histories of sedentary herding systems: Bouaké, with a non-pastoral tradition, and Toumodi, with a pastoral tradition. Overall, 98% of farmers reported using common grazing resources, with 70% practicing continuous year-round grazing. The most commonly perceived climate risks were decreased rainfall (94%) and increased temperatures (82%), which often led to frequent livestock feed gaps (88%) and negative impacts on livestock productivity (e.g., weight losses, mortality). Moreover, our logistic regression models revealed that perceptions of climate hazards and the occurrence of new diseases were location-specific ( P < 0.01), but the latter perception was attributed to increased herd movement to access water and forage. A high perception of climate risk was a greater concern across herders, regardless of the settlement history. However, the proportion perceiving low climate risk was generally higher among those with additional cropping activities, though this finding was inconclusive due to the small sample of mixed crop-livestock farms (25%). The primary management strategy to address feed gaps was increased mobility, which was more prevalent among herders in Toumodi (77%) with a pastoral tradition than among herders in Bouaké (∼50%) ( P < 0.05). Furthermore, an exploratory latent class analysis of coping and adaptation strategies revealed that a subgroup of herders in Bouaké (42%) is not aware of significant innovative practices, making them a key target for support. We conclude that future climate adaptation efforts should prioritize underrepresented regions by considering the specific production characteristics of settled herders and by strengthening connections among livestock keepers, breeders, and agroecological contexts.

title: Integrating Species Distribution Modelling and Spring Low-Temperature Exposure to Assess Climatic Suitability for Actinidia arguta in Europe
abstract: Actinidia arguta (kiwiberry) is a cold-hardy perennial fruit crop with increasing cultivation interest outside its native East Asian range. This study assessed its climatic suitability across Europe using an ensemble species distribution modeling (SDM) framework calibrated with occurrence records from East Asia. After occurrence filtering and spatial thinning, 1483 presence records were retained. Twenty-one candidate environmental predictors were screened for multicollinearity and four variables—temperature seasonality (BIO4), maximum temperature of the warmest month (BIO5), precipitation seasonality (BIO15) and precipitation of the warmest quarter (BIO18)—were retained in the final SDM. Five algorithms (GLM, RF, MAXNET, GAM, GBM) were evaluated using environmental cross-validation and models meeting a TSS ≥ 0.60 threshold were combined in a TSS-weighted ensemble. Temperature seasonality showed the highest permutation importance (0.491), followed by precipitation of the warmest quarter (0.316). The European projection identified comparatively high climatic suitability primarily in parts of Central and Southeastern Europe, with approximately 68,226 km2 exceeding a suitability value of 0.50 and 21,634 km2 exceeding 0.60. Environmental clamping affected 10.2% of the European projection domain but only 0.4% of the area with suitability ≥ 0.50 and none of the area with suitability ≥ 0.60. A complementary March-May analysis of climatological minimum temperature showed that spring low-temperature exposure was strongly seasonal. In March, 32.4% and 23.4% of the area with suitability ≥ 0.50 overlapped with Tmin ≤ −1.0 °C and ≤−1.5 °C scenarios respectively, whereas no corresponding overlap occurred in April or May. These temperature scenarios represent climatological exposure rather than frost-event frequency or damage probability. Overall, the results identify broad-scale patterns of climatic suitability while emphasizing that such projections should not be interpreted as direct estimates of agronomic or commercial cultivation potential.

title: Impacts of Future Climate Change on Comparative Advantages in Yield, Irrigation Water Productivity, and Economic Returns of Summer Soybean and Maize Under Sowing Date Optimization in the Huaibei Plain, China
abstract: In China’s Huaibei Plain, summer soybean and maize compete for land due to highly overlapping growing seasons. This study employs the DSSAT model under full irrigation to assess crop climatic adaptability and sowing date optimization across a baseline (2001–2020) and two future emission scenarios (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5, 2031–2050) under 13 sowing-date treatments, with 10 June as the conventional sowing date for both crops. Results indicate that future summer growing seasons will become warmer and wetter overall. Relative to the baseline, conventional sowing under future climates leads to shortened growth periods and synchronous yield declines, with maize suffering substantially larger yield losses than soybean. Sowing date optimization effectively mitigates these climate-induced yield losses, with recommended adjustments of advancing soybean by 10–15 days and delaying maize by 20 days. Following optimization, maize yield surpasses the baseline by 8.2% under SSP2-4.5 and recovers to near-baseline levels under SSP5-8.5, while soybean yield remains comparable to the baseline under SSP2-4.5 and slightly below it under SSP5-8.5. Maize maintains clear advantages in grain yield and net return, whereas soybean has higher irrigation water economic efficiency, defined as the irrigated–rainfed net return difference per unit irrigation water. Under these simulated full-irrigation conditions, we suggest maintaining a maize-dominant pattern with moderate soybean allocation and optimized sowing dates for both crops as a scenario-based reference for enhancing regional climate adaptability.

title: Machine Learning-Based Regional Assessment of Second-Crop Corn Yield Using Climatic and Water-Balance Variables
abstract: Second-crop corn is an important component of Brazilian grain production and is highly exposed to climatic variability because crop development occurs during the transition from the rainy to the drier season. This study assessed the performance of machine learning algorithms for estimating second-crop corn yield within the 2012–2023 historical data domain in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil. Municipal yield data from 22 municipalities and daily climatic data covering the period from 2012 to 2023 were analyzed. Yield data were obtained from Aprosoja/MS, whereas climatic variables, including solar radiation, air temperature, evapotranspiration, relative humidity, wind speed, and precipitation, were obtained from NASA/POWER. Pearson correlation analysis was used as an initial screening procedure to identify climatic variables associated with yield variability. Multiple linear regression (MLR), a multilayer perceptron (MLP), a support vector machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, and a gradient boosting regressor (GBR) were evaluated. Under the observation-level random partition adopted in this study, RF and XGBoost showed the highest performance in the randomly held-out testing subset, both reaching R2 values of approximately 0.80. However, XGBoost exhibited near-perfect calibration performance followed by a substantial decrease during testing (MAPE = 14.05%; R2 = 0.80), indicating overfitting. Random Forest achieved similar testing performance with a smaller calibration-to-testing gap. Therefore, under the specific random partition used in this study, RF was considered the preferred model. In contrast, GBR failed to provide reliable predictive performance under the present dataset and configuration, with a testing MAPE of 547.78%, and was therefore considered too unreliable for interpretation in this study. Importantly, because the partition did not preserve temporal or spatial independence, these results represent generalization within the 2012–2023 historical data domain and should not be interpreted as evidence of future-year or spatially independent predictive performance. Because the dataset was partitioned randomly at the observation level without preserving temporal independence, the reported performance represents generalization within the 2012–2023 historical data domain and should not be interpreted as future-year forecasting performance.

title: Causal-based approaches to explain and learn from self-extension - A review
abstract: The last decades have seen a revolution in autonomous robotics. Deep learning approaches and their hardware implementations have made it possible to endow robots with extraordinary perceptual capabilities. In addition, they can also benefit from advances in Automated Planning, allowing them to autonomously solve complex tasks. However, on many occasions, the robot still acts without internalising and understanding the reasons behind a perception or an action, beyond an immediate response to a current state of the context. This gap results in limitations that affect its performance, reliability and trustworthiness. Deep learning alone cannot bridge this gap, because the reasons behind behaviour, when it emanates from a model in which the world is a black-box, are not accessible. What is really needed is an underlying architecture based on deeper reasoning. Among other issues, this architecture should enable the robot to generate explanations, allowing people to know why the robot is performing, or has performed, a certain action, or the reasons that may have caused a certain plan failure or perceptual anomaly. Furthermore, when these explanations arise from a cognitive process and are shared, and thus validated, with people, the robot should be able to incorporate these explanations into its knowledge base, and thus use this understanding to improve future behaviour. Our article looks at recent advances in the development of self-aware, self-evolving robots. These robots are designed to provide the necessary explanations to their human counterparts, thereby enhancing their functional capabilities, in the quest to gain their trust.

title: Two-Dimensional Spiral to Three-Dimensional Through-Type Silicon Radiation Detectors: Structural Evolution, Optimization Mechanism and TCAD Simulation Progress
abstract: Silicon drift detectors (SDDs) and three-dimensional (3D) trench electrode silicon detectors have become core radiation-sensing devices for X-ray spectroscopy, pulsar navigation, high-energy-physics experiments and low-dose medical imaging. Conventional concentric-ring and first-order spiral SDDs suffer prominent drawbacks including distorted surface potential gradients, uneven drift electric fields, ill-defined electron drift channels and large Si/SiO2-interface leakage current. Traditional non-through 3D trench detectors have large substrate dead zones, leading to degraded charge-collection efficiency. Based on original structural designs and mathematical modeling from our research group and other researchers, this review sorts out the evolution route of silicon radiation detectors from planar two-dimensional spiral electrodes to 3D penetrating-electrode architectures. It elaborates the fundamental physics of SDDs and 3D trench electrode detectors and establishes a unified Sentaurus TCAD multi-physics simulation system with consistent substrate, thickness and bias boundary conditions. Four innovative two-dimensional spiral SDD architectures and two novel through-type 3D silicon detectors are summarized, together with their analytical models, optimization mechanisms and key performance features. Quantitative cross-comparison is implemented over multiple critical metrics to extract general structural-optimization rules. Industrial bottlenecks regarding fabrication yield, array uniformity, high-temperature stability and simulation-process matching are analyzed. Future trends of composite detectors, wafer-level manufacturing and coupled multi-physics simulation are forecasted with application-targeted design proposals. We hope this review can provide systematic theoretical reference and design guidance for developing next-generation high-performance silicon radiation detectors.

title: UAV-Based Hyperspectral Monitoring of Foliar Nitrogen in Spinach (Spinacia oleracea L.): Comparing Flight-Specific, Window-Based, and Time-Integrated Modeling Approaches
abstract: Spinach (Spinacia oleracea L.) is an economically important leafy vegetable whose nitrogen management remains comparatively understudied with remote sensing tools relative to major row crops. This study evaluated the potential of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based hyperspectral imagery to estimate foliar nitrogen content (%N) in field-grown spinach at a commercial plot across two growing seasons and four nitrogen fertilization treatments. Nine spectral indices were related to destructively measured %N at four phenological stages of the Biologische Bundesanstalt, Bundessortenamt und CHemische Industrie (BBCH) scale (BBCH 16, 30, 45, and 49) under three modeling scenarios, ranging from flight-specific regression to a continuous model incorporating days after sowing (DAS) as a proxy for crop development, with model performance assessed out-of-sample by repeated cross-validation. Foliar nitrogen content differed significantly among treatments from BBCH 30 onward and only marginally at the earliest stage, with the two highest doses converging into a statistically indistinguishable class. The Vogelmann red-edge index 3 (VOGREI3) yielded the most accurate estimates, peaking at BBCH 45 (cross-validated coefficient of determination, R2 = 0.845) before declining significantly at BBCH 49, a loss consistent with spectral saturation of the closed canopy. A single continuous model incorporating DAS covered the BBCH 45 and BBCH 49 flights with a relative error of 12.4%, against 9.6% and 14.9% for the corresponding flight-specific models, and required no stage-specific recalibration within the calibration seasons. In an unseen season, plot ranking was preserved, and a few reference samples corrected the bias. UAV hyperspectral imagery combined with development-stage-aware modeling therefore shows potential for non-destructive nitrogen monitoring in spinach once locally calibrated, although transferability across further seasons, sites and cultivars remains to be established.

title: PSeq-Net: End-to-End Sparse-Global Sequence Modeling for Bridge Detection in Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing Imagery
abstract: Robust bridge detection in ultra-high-resolution remote sensing imagery is important for transportation infrastructure mapping, geographic information system updating, and post-disaster assessment. However, local cropping can interrupt the spatial continuity of long-span bridges, leading to fragmented detections and geometrically inconsistent predictions. This paper proposes a polygon sequence network (PSeq-Net), an end-to-end sparse-global sequence modeling framework for bridge detection in very-high-resolution (VHR) remote sensing imagery. PSeq-Net generates an ordered quadrilateral vertex sequence for each bridge, unifying visual encoding and structured geometric prediction. Hierarchical sparse feature sampling preserves fine-grained evidence in bridge-relevant regions while using compact representations of background areas, enabling efficient processing of 2048 × 2048 inputs. Global context aggregation integrates long-range spatial dependencies, and geometry-aware optimization improves the structural plausibility of predicted bridge shapes. Experiments on the large-scale GLH-Bridge benchmark show that PSeq-Net achieves 37.87% average precision (AP), 73.58% AP50, and 31.38% AP75, outperforming representative oriented and large-scale bridge detectors. Further analyses highlight improved localization of elongated and boundary-crossing bridges, reduced fragmentation, and robustness across diverse scene backgrounds and image resolutions.

title: GUF-Net: Gated Uncertainty-Aware Fusion Network for Robust Building Change Detection in Remote Sensing Images
abstract: Building change detection (BCD) in high-resolution remote sensing imagery has achieved considerable accuracy with deep learning, yet most existing models still suffer from performance degradation under noise interference, partly due to inadequate uncertainty handling. To address this, we propose GUF-Net, a gated uncertainty-aware fusion network that integrates three key components: (1) a pixel-wise uncertainty modeling module that generates a pixel-level uncertainty map alongside the change probability map; (2) an adaptive gated fusion mechanism that dynamically weights multi-scale features and uncertainty information; and (3) a redesigned loss function that can directly supervise the uncertainty estimation, ensuring that it reflects prediction reliability rather than serving as an unsupervised auxiliary output. Experiments on three public benchmarks (WHU-CD, CDD, and LEVIR-CD) show that GUF-Net achieves competitive F1 scores of 93.88%, 96.55%, and 90.43%, respectively, ranking top three on CDD and WHU-CD, while its advantage is less pronounced on LEVIR-CD. Under the strongest Gaussian, salt-and-pepper, and speckle noise conditions on the WHU-CD test set, the F1 score of GUF-Net decreases by only 0.86, 3.95, and 1.29 percentage points, respectively, exhibiting the smallest degradation among the compared models. Unlike existing uncertainty-aware baselines evaluated solely on clean data, GUF-Net jointly supervises evidential pixel uncertainty and routes it through adaptive gating, enabling stable fusion under degraded imaging conditions. Ablation studies confirm that the gated fusion, uncertainty injection, and global context aggregation each contribute to the overall performance. These results suggest that explicit uncertainty modeling and adaptive fusion can improve the reliability of BCD under noisy conditions, although there remains room for further improvement in clean-set accuracy and model efficiency.

title: SWOT Assessment of Agricultural Water-Management Systems in Kazakhstan: Infrastructure, Institutional Constraints, and Strategic Development Directions
abstract: (1) Background: Kazakhstan’s agricultural sector is increasingly exposed to water scarcity, an aging irrigation infrastructure, climate change, and transboundary-water risks. (2) Methods: The study combines a cross-sectional infrastructure inventory as of 1 September 2024 with documentary evidence from 2010–2024. SWOT factors were extracted from infrastructure inventories, official water-sector documents, basin-inspectorate materials, and sector statistics and then screened for relevance and classified according to a consistent rule: strengths and weaknesses represent internal system characteristics, whereas opportunities and threats represent external conditions. Ambiguous factors were reassessed against this rule. The final factors were linked in a traceable TOWS cross-matrix to derive SO, WO, ST, and WT strategic directions. No quantitative weighting or ranking was applied; therefore, the resulting directions are interpreted as qualitative development areas rather than ranked priorities. (3) Results: The analysis identifies substantial regional differences in the scale and condition of reservoirs, hydraulic complexes, canals, pumping facilities, and drainage infrastructure. The main internal constraints are infrastructure deterioration, conveyance losses, limited metering, financing and maintenance constraints, and shortages of technical capacity. External opportunities include public investment, water-saving technologies, digital monitoring, and improved basin governance, whereas climate variability, transboundary dependence, inflationary pressure, and water-quality risks remain key threats. (4) Conclusions: Improving agricultural water security requires a shift from infrastructure expansion alone toward rehabilitation, demand-side efficiency, digital monitoring, basin-level governance, and climate and transboundary risk management.

title: Legal and Economic Ecosystem Transformation Through AI: Innovation Challenges for Human-Centric Development
abstract: The current technological shift towards the application of artificial intelligence (AI) is gradually reshaping the way in which the legal and economic ecosystem functions, particularly in the agricultural sector. This study addresses agricultural economics, policies and rural development in the European Union (EU) and in the Republic of Serbia as a candidate for EU membership. It draws on a structured review of the academic literature and of EU, international and Serbian policy documents issued over the past ten years, including the AI Act, the Digital Omnibus on AI, the Data Governance Act and the proposal for the Common Agricultural Policy after 2027. The empirical component is an exploratory cross-sectional survey of 150 respondents drawn from three professional groups—farmers, lawyers and engineers. Four research hypotheses on the perceived human-centric development potential of AI applications were tested; one was confirmed, two were partially confirmed, and one was not confirmed. Major transformation channels across six regulatory dimensions of the legal framework were mapped onto agricultural AI use cases, showing that the human-centric safeguards of EU law apply with uneven effect: farmer credit scoring, seasonal labour management, the assessment of eligibility for public benefits and AI embedded in machinery fall under high-risk obligations, whereas agronomic decision support systems are governed mainly by data protection law, the Data Act and contractual arrangements. The survey results show that the perceived human-centric benefits of AI differ across the three groups, with farmers reporting the lowest expected benefits and the highest perceived risks of exclusion and labour displacement. Trust in institutions and legal protection was the only construct significantly associated with expected benefits once professional group and other perceptions were controlled, and the differences between the groups were largely accounted for by differences in trust, AI literacy and perceived data sovereignty. Several innovation challenges were identified, the principal ones being the generational and digital divide, labour transformation, platform concentration and institutional capacity; these are particularly acute in Serbia, where the vast majority of holdings are family farms. The proposed Human-Centric Agri-Rural AI Transformation (HCAT) framework links these challenges to four governance pillars, twelve instruments and twelve monitoring indicators, which are offered as a conceptual contribution to be validated in future research, and it provides a sequenced approach for candidate countries aligning with EU policies and frameworks.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Cyber Defense: From Intelligent Threat Detection to Autonomous AI Agents
abstract: The article provides a comprehensive analysis of the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in cybersecurity, taking into account the latest technological trends of 2024–2026. The main possibilities of applying AI to protect information systems are studied: automatic detection of threats and anomalies, real-time incident response, prediction and prevention of cyberattacks, recognition of malicious code and phishing, and continuous learning and adaptation of defense systems. Particular attention is paid to the phenomenon of autonomous AI agents as a new stage in the evolution of intelligent cyber defense systems: practical cases of agentic incident triage and investigation systems (Microsoft Security Copilot), autonomous vulnerability discovery (Google Big Sleep), autonomous penetration testing (XBOW, PentestGPT), as well as the first documented case of an AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign are analyzed. The risks and challenges associated with the use of AI are considered: misuse of technologies by attackers, false positives and missed threats, vulnerabilities of machine learning models and agentic systems, and ethical and legal aspects. The necessity of a balanced approach combining automated AI systems with expert human control based on human-in-the-loop and human-on-the-loop models is substantiated.

title: A Robust Protocol for Germ Layer Differentiation of Human Pluripotent Stem Cells and Evaluation of Their Chromosome and Genomic Integrity.
abstract: Human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) can differentiate into any cell type of the human body and represent a powerful in vitro model to recapitulate early human development. However, their use in regenerative medicine and developmental studies is limited by their genomic and chromosomal instability acquired during long-term culture, often driven by the clonal advantage conferred by spontaneous gain or loss of chromosomes. Here, a detailed culture condition that robustly recapitulates early differentiation and describes methods to assess chromosomal and genomic (in)stability in hPSC cultures. First, the cell culture approaches are described that enable controlled exit from pluripotency and homogeneous differentiation into primitive streak, neuroectoderm, paraxial/lateral mesoderm, and definitive endoderm-like cells. Second, a comprehensive set of protocols is described to assess genomic and chromosomal instability during routine pluripotent stem cell culture, including the detection of single- and double-strand breaks during S-phase, mitotic abnormalities (such as ultrafine bridges, lagging chromosomes or micronuclei) and their direct consequence-the emergence of aneuploidy after cell division. In summary, this work aims to standardize protocols to model early human post-implantation lineage commitment and to provide the tools required to assess routine karyotypic stability of hPSCs during in vitro culture.

title: Spatial Variability of Soil Properties and Implications for Climate-Smart Rice Production in four Agricultural Zones in Anambra State, Nigeria
abstract: Spatial variability in soil properties strongly influences water dynamics, nutrient availability, and crop productivity in tropical agroecosystems, thereby affecting the sustainability of climate-smart rice production systems. This study evaluated the spatial variability of selected soil physical, hydraulic, and chemical properties across four agro-ecological zones (Awka, Anambra, Aguata, and Onitsha) of Anambra State, southeastern Nigeria. Surface soil samples (0–30 cm) were collected from georeferenced locations differing in elevation and landscape characteristics. Laboratory analyses were conducted to determine particle size distribution, bulk density (BD), saturated hydraulic conductivity (Ksat), soil pH, and organic matter (OM). Descriptive statistics, analysis of variance (ANOVA), correlation analysis, and principal component analysis (PCA) were employed to evaluate variability and relationships among soil properties. Results revealed considerable spatial heterogeneity across the study area. Sand content ranged from 332 to 582 g kg⁻¹, while clay content varied between 218 and 354 g kg⁻¹. Bulk density ranged from 1.346 to 1.458 g cm⁻³, whereas Ksat varied from 0.0182 to 0.0468 cm hr⁻¹. Soil pH was moderately acidic (5.3–5.7), while OM content ranged from 2.2 to 3.3%. ANOVA indicated no significant zonal differences in Ksat and BD, suggesting that micro-scale variability exerted a stronger influence than agro-ecological classification. PCA explained 96.5% of total variability, with soil texture and hydraulic properties constituting the dominant controlling factors. The findings highlight the importance of site-specific soil and water management strategies for improving rice productivity, enhancing water-use efficiency, and strengthening climate resilience in southeastern Nigeria.
journal: Scholarly Journal of Science and Technology Research and Development

title: Digital Literacy in Agriculture: Current State and Development Prospects
abstract: Digitalization of Kazakhstan’s agricultural sector is a strategic direction of state socio-economic policy. The introduction of digital technologies into the agro-industrial complex contributes to increasing the efficiency of production processes and rationalizing the use of material, financial, and natural resources. Objective – to substantiate the impact of digital literacy on the performance of digital management in the republic’s agricultural sphere, to determine vectors for the development of digital competencies of economic entities. Methods – a systems approach allowing digital management to be viewed as a complex multi-level series of interconnected elements to establish the scale of AIC computerization in the country. The quantitative principle was applied in assessing the effect of digital culture on the effective regulation of the agricultural industry. The information base of the study consisted of legal acts of the Republic of Kazakhstan, state programs in digital transformation of agro-industrial production, statistical data, materials of international organizations, and scientific works of domestic and foreign researchers. Results – it was shown that information readiness represents not only a set of individual skills and knowledge, but also a vital institutional potential necessary for the optimal functioning of the agricultural sector administration model. Conclusions – it was revealed that the presence of formal access to digital technologies and information systems does not ensure methodically structured coordination in the absence of digital erudition among specialists and managers of the agro-industrial complex. The widespread dissemination and promotion of digital literacy will reduce management costs, strengthen competitive advantages in the agri-food market, address pressing environmental problems, stimulate labor productivity growth, adapt to climate change, improve crop yield indicators, and enable timely planning of field work.
