The approach provides carrier-independent containment within fully mediated MCP execution environments. Code and data are publicly available.

title: Interpreting Physics in Video Encoders using Multi-Object Interaction Videos
abstract: Video encoder models are increasingly used as world models for physical AI, where a policy plans by rolling out the latent, so what physics the latent holds bounds what the agent can plan over. Moreover, existing interpretability work probes quantities belonging to a single object; the quantities that make physics relational, such as momentum transfer, restitution, and friction, are defined between bodies and have not been examined. We probe relational physics attributes in two frozen self-supervised video encoders (V-JEPA2 and VideoMAE) under two-body settings and test if they transfer across environments. Our early findings are mixed. Both encoders separate elastic from inelastic collisions reliably. V-JEPA2's own predictor is less likely to predict a collision that creates kinetic energy compared to one that loses it. Momentum-violation detection appears in only one of the two encoders, a kinetic-energy readout survives a change of environment for V-JEPA2 but not for VideoMAE, and neither model holds a friction coefficient that survives a change of geometry.

title: Multi-Material Topology Optimization of Phononic Crystals for Targeted Elastic Wave Bandgap
abstract: Phononic crystals are periodic elastic structures that exhibit frequency bandgaps within which elastic waves cannot propagate. The formation and width of these bandgaps depend on the spatial distribution of material properties within periodic phononic unit cells. In this work, we propose novel topology optimization formulations to achieve multi-material design of phononic crystals for bandgap optimization at targeted frequencies, where we discover the influence of spatially varying properties of base materials on the band structures that block and permit elastic wave propagation. Specifically, we model wave propagation by Floquet-Bloch theory and solve the resulting eigenvalue problem by the finite element method along the boundary of the irreducible Brillouin zone. We first propose a multivariate weight-based method via a novel interpolation scheme that maps the design variables of an arbitrary number of candidate materials into effective density and stiffness for elastic wave-propagation calculations, where bandgaps arise from the contrast in the stiffness and inertia among material constituents. We then develop two formulations for bandgap optimization. The first formulation maximizes the gap between two adjacent frequency bands using a bound-based approach, where we introduce two auxiliary scalar variables as additional design variables and incorporate them directly into the design objective, yielding a linear, differentiable design objective, with the eigenfrequencies entering the formulation through associated constraints. The second formulation places a bandgap over a user-defined target frequency range through a dynamic band-pairing strategy, where we adaptively identify the relevant pair of adjacent bands amid optimization iterations. Towards the end, we validate the bandgap performance of our designs against the transmission loss spectra computed from COMSOL Multiphysics.

title: EGGPlacer: Energy-Guided Generative Chip Placement with Diffusion Models
abstract: Chip placement strongly affects routed wirelength and thermal behavior, yet these downstream metrics are difficult to evaluate during macro placement. Learning-based macro placers commonly optimize the macro-only half-perimeter wirelength (HPWL), denoted mHPWL, which ignores standard cell connectivity and spatial demand. In contrast, analytical mixed-size placers optimize differentiable full netlist wirelength and density objectives but are typically unaware of thermal effects. We propose EGGPlacer, an energy-guided diffusion framework that incorporates analytical placement feedback and thermal feedback into macro placement generation. An analytical placer acts as an online physical response model, exposing the standard cell distribution and a full netlist wirelength proxy induced by each intermediate macro placement, while a differentiable thermal model provides temperature feedback. These signals are formulated as composable energies and injected throughout reverse diffusion without retraining the underlying generative model. Experiments on public placement benchmarks show that EGGPlacer achieves competitive mixed-size HPWL relative to strong analytical and learning-based macro placers. In the end-to-end evaluation, EGGPlacer also obtains the lowest average routed wirelength and peak temperature among the evaluated methods. Ablation studies further demonstrate that analytical and thermal guidance provide distinct and complementary benefits across wirelength proxies, routed wirelength, and thermal objectives.

title: VibeGame: Prompt-to-Game Development with AI-Native Engine and Self-Evolving Adversarial Agent Team
abstract: Large language model agents have enabled software development through natural-language interaction, but extending this paradigm to end-to-end game development remains challenging. Building a playable game requires coordinating code, scenes, assets, animations, physics, and configurations, while allowing developers to validate their integrated behavior through interactive testing. We introduce VibeGame, a framework for creating complete 2D game projects from natural-language prompts and optional reference images. Its AI-native game engine represents project state as schema-validated structured text and provides frame-synchronous runtime control, enabling agents to inspect game states, execute actions, and verify behavior at their own pace. Built upon this interface, we design an Adversarial Agent Team of eight specialized agents to separate implementation from review, so that problems are found and fixed through multi-round loops. For each conducted and accepted project, we further introduce a training-free self-evolution mechanism to distill it into reusable skeletons, modules, and collaboration contracts for future development. We evaluate prompt-assets-to-game (PA2G), where agents are given an asset library, and prompt-to-game (P2G), where agents generate their own art. On a GameCraft-Bench subset, VibeGame in P2G consistently outperforms a range of agent harnesses in either P2G or PA2G with the same underlying model, including GPT-6.1-Sol.

title: Uncertainty Quantification for Financial Foundation Models: A Survey
abstract: Financial foundation models increasingly support workflows spanning financial question answering, disclosure analysis, forecasting, and decision-making. In these settings, uncertainty may concern whether evidence is valid and available at the relevant time, whether an interpretation is justified, which outcomes remain plausible, or which action is preferred under costs and risk constraints. Because these objects arise at different points in a workflow, uncertainty cannot be reduced to confidence in a final output. We introduce a source-aware framework that distinguishes six sources of uncertainty across evidence and context, model and inference, and outcome and action, while treating agentic workflows as the execution layer through which uncertainty can propagate, change form, or be reduced. We develop a mechanism-based taxonomy grounded in how methods construct or verify uncertainty and reliability representations, and use it to assess their applicability across financial task domains. We further map finance-specific empirical studies across the taxonomy and task domains to characterize the current research landscape. Our analysis shows that most reviewed studies address uncertainty in individual parts of financial workflows, with limited work connecting evidence and reasoning reliability to downstream prediction and constrained action. By connecting where uncertainty arises, how it is represented, and how it bears on downstream decisions, this survey provides a unified foundation for studying and evaluating uncertainty in financial foundation models.

title: Localising the Seizure Onset Zone from Routine Interictal and Ictal Scalp EEG Via a Factorised Spatiotemporal Ensemble Deep Learning Framework
abstract: Background Drug-resistant focal epilepsy requires precise localisation of the epileptogenic zone (EZ) for surgical resection. Current practice depends on invasive recordings or spontaneous seizure capture, a costly and risky bottleneck. Interictal scalp EEG can exhibit localising features like spikes, but scalp EEG suffers from volume conduction (the smearing of brain signals across multiple electrodes) and low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), which obscure subtle spatial dynamics. Neurophysiologist review of long, often multi-day recordings is time-consuming and expertise-dependent, and while computational methods exist, they tend to rely heavily on human-designed features. Deep learning for EEG localisation could therefore help to improve clinical efficiency and sensitivity. Objectives To develop and validate a non-invasive deep learning approach for lobar-level localisation of the seizure onset zone (SOZ), the primary electrophysiological proxy for the epileptogenic zone (EZ), using interictal and ictal segments from routine scalp EEG. The model is trained on expert-annotated clinical labels and is intended to augment, not supplant, clinical judgement in EZ delineation. Methods We curated 262 sessions (6,000+ hours) from 100 patients with unilateral focal epilepsy, tested with an extra 28-patient internal and a 9-patient external dataset. The framework integrates: (1) an online augmentation pipeline (Gaussian noise, amplitude scaling, temporal cropping, and hemispheric channel swap) to mitigate overfitting. (2) a multi-scale temporal block for 20-200 ms discharge morphologies; (3) a factorised spatiotemporal Transformer decoupling temporal and spatial attention to counter volume conduction; and (4) a hemispheric mutual exclusivity penalty encoding unilateral priors. A five-model heterogeneous ensemble, fused via model soup, was evaluated on held-out, seizure-free, and cross-institutional cohorts. Results The ensemble achieved 88.46% session-level exact match on internal test data, outperforming EEGNet (50.00%). Performance generalised to the seizure-free holdout set (82.76%) and to cross-institutional data (84.62%). Rare occipital class (RO) recall rose from 0.500 to 1.000, with zero false positives on healthy controls (n=108). On unlabelled random segments, accuracy was 66.67% (vs. 14% chance). A full 24-hour recording was processed in 4.26 minutes, with inference under 8 seconds, highlighting localising windows for targeted expert clinical review Conclusion Clinically actionable SOZ spatial information is encoded in routine interictal scalp EEG. Our factorised ensemble provides a safe, interpretable, and efficient tool to expedite presurgical evaluation, potentially reducing reliance on prolonged monitoring and invasive implantation.

title: Wildlife damage to tropical agroforests: predicting primate-induced fruit loss using species’ energy requirements
abstract: 1. Quantitatively assessing wildlife damage to food crops in tropical agroforestry systems is notoriously problematic. At the same time, the animal species likely to destroy these crops, such as primates, are often endangered and a source of conflict. Resolving these conflicts may require the implementation of financial compensation where non-monetary solutions are unavailable. Currently, however, there is no suitable method for assessing fruit losses due to the complexities of agroforestry plots used by most small households practising polyculture-based agriculture. 2. We constructed an energy balance model to predict the quantity of cultivated fruit and other locally sourced food required by crop-dependent primates to meet their metabolic needs. The proposed method is based on the principle that, under conditions of energy balance, an animal’s daily energy intake corresponds to its total energy expenditure. The ecophysiological model incorporated the daily food and energy intake of wild primates, measured using the bite-size method and the nutritional composition of food, as well as their total energy expenditure and body composition, measured using doubly labelled water. We tested the model’s predictions on lemurs foraging in several agroforests in Mayotte, and on two frugivorous primate species in Madagascar during different seasons. Additionally, we evaluated whether more conventional dietary analysis methods (feeding-time sampling), or published energetics data could reliably inform the model, and reduce the costs and constraints of field observations. 3. The predictions were generally consistent with direct estimates of food intake (91% ± 25%, n = 14 across different seasons), though this was influenced by the lemurs’ evolutionary-driven seasonal fattening strategy. Time-derived estimates using correction factors or published measurements of total energy expenditure were also consistent, but further studies are required to confirm these findings. 4. Policy implications. The study provides proof of concept for a promising approach to quantifying wildlife-related agricultural losses in small-scale agroforestry. This innovative method provides policymakers, farmers’ associations, and non-governmental organisations with sufficiently accurate quantitative estimates to support the development of evidence-based financial compensation schemes.

title: Analysis of Crop Production Choices among Agro-Pastoral Households in Beletweyne, Somalia
abstract: Crop choice is the first and most consequential decision an agro-pastoral household makes each season, yet it is usually explained by agronomic suitability or input availability. This article applies Rogers’ Diffusion of Innovations Theory to explain why households in Beletweyne District, Somalia, adopt or reject crop options promoted through aid and extension. We operationalise the theory’s five perceived attributes of innovations (relative advantage, compatibility, complexity, trialability and observability), its five-stage innovation-decision process, communication channels and adopter categories, and combine them in a nine-step model comprising a stage funnel, binary and multinomial logit estimation, adopter-category classification and a Bass diffusion curve. The design builds on a mixed-methods survey of 96 households in three villages, supplemented by 10 key-informant interviews and four focus-group discussions. Descriptive signals from the survey show abundant financial aid (mean 4.98 of 5) but thin extension (mean 2.85), a configuration the theory predicts will stall adoption at the knowledge and persuasion stages. Analysis shows how the outputs are read. The article offers a theory-to-estimation protocol for crop-choice research in fragile settings.
journal: Journal of Sociology in East and Horn of Africa

title: Application Of The RAD Method In The Bus Ticket Management And Sales Information System at PT. RAPI
abstract: PT. RAPI is a company engaged in land transportation services that provides intercity and interprovincial bus transportation. The management and ticket sales processes at PT. RAPI were previously carried out manually using ledger books, including the recording of passenger data and ticket transactions. This condition makes data management and reporting processes less structured. This research aims to develop a web-based bus ticket booking, sales, and management information system to support the administrative and ticket transaction processes at PT. RAPI. The system development method used in this research is Rapid Application Development (RAD), which emphasizes rapid development and user involvement during the system development process. The research uses a descriptive method with a qualitative approach, while system modeling uses Unified Modeling Language (UML) and system testing uses Black Box Testing. The resulting system provides several functions, including user registration and login, ticket booking, seat selection, booking history, payment confirmation and proof of payment upload, bus and route management, departure schedule management, offline ticket transactions, payment verification, and report generation. The implementation of these functions provides PT. RAPI with a computerized system for managing bus ticket booking, sales, and administrative data in an integrated manner.

title: Mapping Agricultural Entrepreneurship Research in India: A Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: Aims: This study aims to assess the research landscape of agripreneurship in India by identifying publication trends, influential authors, major research themes, collaborative networks, and emerging research areas. Additionally, it seeks to highlight existing knowledge gaps within the field. Study Design: Bibliometric analysis employing performance analysis and science mapping techniques. Place and Duration of Study: The study analysed journal articles concerning agricultural entrepreneurship in India, published from 2000 to March 2025. Methodology: A total of 3,208 research articles were retrieved from the Lens.org database using the keywords "Agriculture," "Entrepreneur," and "India." To ensure relevance and quality, only journal articles were included. The Biblioshiny application, part of the Bibliometrix R package, was utilised to analyse annual scientific production and citation patterns. For keyword co-occurrence analysis and network visualisation, VOSviewer was employed. A minimum threshold of three keyword occurrences was set to construct the bibliometric maps. Results: The analysis shows an increasing focus on Indian agricultural entrepreneurship (agripreneurship) research, especially in the last ten years. Key areas of study have been sustainable entrepreneurship, precision farming, digital advancements, and agribusiness initiatives led by young people. Although research output has increased in research publications, gaps remain in interdisciplinary collaboration, empirical support, and policy applicability. The lack of cooperation between academic institutions, industry, and policymakers underscores the necessity for more robust institutional connections. Conclusion: In India, research on agripreneurship is advancing, with a growing focus on sustainability, technological advancements, and entrepreneurship among young people. Bridging current knowledge gaps through interdisciplinary studies, enhanced institutional partnerships, and targeted policy measures can aid in building an inclusive and sustainable agripreneurial ecosystem. Future studies should prioritise empirical evaluations, real-world case analyses, and practical models to bolster rural development and agricultural resilience.
journal: Journal of Scientific Research and Reports

title: 'All Under One Roof': Health Professional Perspectives on Integrating Musculoskeletal Pain Management in a Proximity-Based Primary Healthcare Model.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Musculoskeletal (MSK) pain is a leading contributor to disability and service demand in primary healthcare (PHC), particularly in socioeconomically disadvantaged communities. Contemporary responses increasingly emphasise people-centred, multimodal and non-pharmacological approaches. However, in practice, service integration is often limited to co-location, with insufficient clarity regarding how collaboration and integration are operationalised within private, fee-for-service PHC environments. METHODS This qualitative study explored how 22 health professionals working within a large-scale, proximity-based primary healthcare precinct in Australia defined and experienced service integration for MSK pain management. Semi-structured interviews were conducted across two timepoints (2021 and 2023) and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, informed by implementation and people-centred care principles. RESULTS Three interdependent enablers of integration were identified: (1) Relationships, enabled by physical proximity, including shared philosophy and respect for professional roles; (2) Communication, characterised by knowledge exchange, forward momentum and shared processes; and (3) Consumer-centred access, via availability of affordable and needed services. Integration was experienced as a continuum, ranging from parallel multidisciplinary practice to higher-order interdisciplinary collaboration involving shared processes and collective responsibility for consumer outcomes. CONCLUSION Within this site-specific context, physical proximity acted as a necessary but insufficient condition for effective integration. Higher levels of interdisciplinary practice emerged only when proximity was combined with shared values, effective communication and coordinated consumer flow. These findings provide a base for how proximity-based primary healthcare environments can operationalise people-centred integration and can inform scalable models of MSK care in private PHC settings.

Century-scale spatiotemporal variability and trends of rainfall erosivity and erosivity density in an ecologically sensitive tropical monsoon region of India (1901–2020)
abstract: Understanding long-term rainfall erosivity variability is essential for assessing soil erosion risk and supporting sustainable land and watershed management in tropical monsoon environments. This study presents a century-scale (1901–2020) assessment of rainfall erosivity and erosivity density across Kerala, India, using India Meteorological Department (IMD) gridded rainfall data (0.25° × 0.25° resolution) from 50 grid cells. Rainfall erosivity and erosivity density were estimated from monthly rainfall records using the Arnoldus empirical approach to examine their spatial distribution, temporal variability, elevation relationships, long-term trends, and homogeneous erosivity domains. Trend characteristics were evaluated using the modified Mann–Kendall test and Sen’s slope estimator, while agglomerative hierarchical clustering with Ward’s linkage was employed to identify regions exhibiting similar erosivity characteristics. Mean annual rainfall ranged from 824 to 4,123 mm, with mean annual rainfall erosivity and erosivity density ranging from 1,291 to 29,987 MJ mm ha⁻¹ h⁻¹ y⁻¹ and 1.34–7.38 MJ ha⁻¹ h⁻¹, respectively. The results reveal substantial spatial heterogeneity and pronounced interannual and inter-decadal variability in both rainfall erosivity and erosivity density. Despite episodic periods of elevated erosivity, trend analyses indicate that rainfall, rainfall erosivity, and erosivity density generally declined across most grid cells during the study period, with localized increasing trends restricted to a few eastern highland areas. Elevation exhibited weak inverse relationships with rainfall erosivity and erosivity density, suggesting that erosivity variability is influenced by rainfall characteristics, monsoon dynamics, and topographic setting rather than elevation alone. Hierarchical clustering identified four statistically distinct erosivity domains representing intermediate, high, very high, and extreme erosivity conditions, providing a framework for regional erosion-risk assessment and spatially differentiated soil conservation planning. The observed variability in rainfall erosivity is consistent with differences in rainfall intensity distribution, monsoon variability, and regional topographic influences, highlighting the importance of rainfall characteristics beyond annual precipitation totals. Although the monthly rainfall-based approach may not fully capture short-duration erosive storms, it provides a consistent basis for evaluating century-scale regional erosivity variability. The resulting erosivity database and domain classification offer valuable inputs for RUSLE-based soil erosion modelling, watershed prioritization, and climate-informed land management in tropical monsoon environments.

title: From hypothetical scenarios to real-world service robots: The next wave of service and marketing research on physical AI
abstract: This commentary advances that the next wave of service robot research should move toward a service-systems perspective on physical AI. Recent advances in generative and agentic AI are transforming robots from stand-alone service interfaces into embodied and networked actors that must be orchestrated with other physical AI deployments, virtual AI, employees, customers, digital platforms, and the physical infrastructure they operate in. I propose that future research should focus less narrowly on whether customers accept robots and more on where, how, and under what conditions physical AI creates value for customers, employees, firms, and society. Key research opportunities include studying robot-enabled service systems, backstage value creation, differences between special-purpose and general-purpose robots, orchestration as a core organizational capability, scalable innovation through no-code programming and fleet learning, and corporate digital responsibility (CDR), safety, and cybersecurity challenges of embodied AI. By reframing service robots as part of broader service systems, marketing and service research can develop richer theories of cost-effective service excellence (CESE), responsible deployment, and the human touch where it matters most.

title: Low-Carbon Urban Morphology as a Configuration Problem: Empirically Constrained Bayesian Optimization at the Intra-Urban Scale
abstract: Urban compactness and functional mixing are widely recognized as important carbon mitigation strategies. However, determining appropriate levels of compactness and functional mixing, and their potential carbon reductions, remains challenging due to nonlinear morphology–emission relationships and strong spatial dependence. This study develops a spatially explicit Bayesian optimization (SEBO) framework integrating spatial relationship analysis, nonlinear response-interval identification, and constrained configuration optimization. Using 4,347 grid cells in the Nanjing metropolitan region, spatial econometric models identify sector-specific morphology–emission associations and green-blue moderation effects. Tree-based machine learning then identifies responsive ranges for morphological adjustment, which constrain Bayesian optimization to explore lower-emission configurations and assess mitigation potential. Results reveal substantial sectoral differences in morphology–emission relationships and response intervals. Vertical intensity and functional mix are associated with transportation, residential, and power-related emissions, while horizontal density primarily relates to residential emissions. Optimizing vertical intensity yields average simulated reductions of 14.09%, 19.25%, and 5.75% in transportation, residential, and power-related emissions, respectively. However, mitigation potential varies with initial morphological and ecological conditions, with some scenarios yielding higher predicted emissions. These findings support spatially differentiated, context-specific urban morphology optimization rather than universal compactness targets.

title: Determinants of climate information source use among households in Ethiopia using evidence from the Ethiopian socioeconomic survey
abstract: Climate change is a significant threat to agriculture-related livelihoods. In response, climate information sources (CIS) play a critical role in strengthening farmers’ resilience to climate change and improving agricultural decision-making. However, empirical evidence on household use of CIS in Ethiopia remains limited. This study examined the determinants of households’ use of climate information sources in Ethiopia. The analysis used secondary data from the fifth wave of the Ethiopian Socioeconomic Survey, collected between September 2021 and June 2022. Descriptive statistics and a binary logistic regression model were used to examine patterns and determinants of the use of climate information sources. The findings indicated that only 39.1% of households reported using at least one source to obtain climate information, while 60.9% reported no use. Although this represents a substantial improvement over the use of CIS reported in earlier Ethiopian studies, the findings indicate that the use of climate information sources remains limited among the majority of households. Radio and television were the major communication channels for disseminating climate information, reported by 85.81% of households, indicating the continued importance of media in climate information dissemination. The results of logistic regression indicate that the sex of the household head, residence, educational level, mobile phone ownership, and regional location were significantly associated with use of CIS. Marginal effects revealed that female-headed households were 16.0% less likely to use CIS than male-headed households. Urban residence and mobile phone ownership were 23.9% and 10.7% more likely to use CIS, respectively, while each additional year of education level increased the probabilities of using CIS by 0.2%. Significant regional disparities were also found, with households in Oromia, Amhara, and Dire Dawa being 28.6, 17.2, and 18.4% points more likely to use CIS, respectively. The study suggests that relevant stakeholders and policymakers strengthen communication infrastructure, improve digital inclusion, and promote region-specific strategies for disseminating climate information, which are essential for increasing households’ use of climate information sources in Ethiopia. title: Vision-language models and visual foundation models in neurosurgery
abstract: Background Visual foundation models (VFMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) offer adaptable approaches to neurosurgical imaging, segmentation, intraoperative assistance, and clinical decision support. However, the available evidence varies substantially in model type, supervision, validation setting, and clinical task, and their readiness for routine clinical use remains uncertain. Methods We conducted a narrative review of peer-reviewed primary research reports published between January 2020 and August 2026, identified through PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar. Studies evaluating visual, vision-language, or multimodal foundation models in neurosurgical applications were included. Supervised Vision Transformer (ViT) and ViT–CNN systems were retained as contemporary transformer-based comparator studies but were not classified as foundation models. Evidence was synthesised according to model adaptation, clinical application, within-study comparative performance, validation setting, and translational limitations. Results Seven studies met the review criteria. FastGlioma provided a prospective multicentre evaluation of a visual foundation model for intraoperative detection of glioma infiltration. In lumbar-spine MRI, zero-shot SAM and MedSAM performed below supervised nnU-Net on segmentation metrics. A task-adapted SAM2-UNet system achieved a mean Dice score of 0.771 for brain-tumour segmentation, although its mean IoU was 0.569 compared with 0.571 for Mask R-CNN in the reported comparison. Supervised transformer-based systems demonstrated performance in acute traumatic brain injury triage and vertebral fracture classification, although the latter combined ViT, CNN, ensemble fusion, and GAN-based augmentation. In multimodal reasoning, GPT-4o achieved higher absolute diagnostic accuracy than CNS-Obsidian, whereas CNS-Obsidian had higher length-adjusted diagnostic accuracy. Evidence for clinical translation remained limited by heterogeneous validation settings, incomplete reporting of computational performance and safety outcomes, predominantly single-centre or preclinical evaluations, and limited assessment of patient outcomes. Conclusion Foundation-model-based systems show potential across selected neurosurgical tasks, but current evidence is insufficient to establish routine clinical readiness or patient benefit. Reported results are primarily task-specific and should not be interpreted as evidence of a general architectural advantage. Future studies should evaluate these systems prospectively under human supervision while determining whether clinicians can reliably detect and mitigate erroneous outputs. Multi-centre validation, uncertainty assessment, computational efficiency, workflow integration, and patient-centred outcomes should be prioritised.

Bidirectional regulation of the PD-1 pathway: Tumor immune exhaustion versus lupus nephritis T cells activation.
abstract: The PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint pathway serves as a core regulatory hub that maintains peripheral immune tolerance. In different disease contexts, this axis exhibits opposing outcomes. In cancer, sustained antigenic stimulation elevates PD-1 expression and locks T cells into an exhaustion phenotype-a state characterized by progressive loss of effector functions, coordinated upregulation of multiple inhibitory receptors, and a TOX-driven epigenetic landscape. Conversely, in lupus nephritis (LN)-a severe autoimmune complication of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)-PD-1+ T cells (both CD8+ and CD4+ subsets) undergo clonal expansion, display a highly activated phenotype, and produce abundant granzyme B, perforin, and IFN-γ, thereby directly inflicting renal tissue damage. Importantly, LN-associated PD-1+ T cells are not uniformly exhausted; single-cell studies suggest that activated and partially exhausted subsets can co-exist. This review systematically elucidates the molecular, cellular, and microenvironmental bases that determine the bidirectional nature of PD-1 signaling-driving T cells toward exhaustion in cancer while promoting T cell activation in LN. Key differentiating factors underlying this divergence include the intensity and persistence of antigen stimulation, activation of the TOX-dependent exhaustion epigenetic program, the cytokine milieu composition (type I interferons, IL-12, IL-6), the balance between co-stimulatory and co-inhibitory signals, and the strikingly different metabolic environments-a nutrient-deprived, hypoxic tumor microenvironment versus an inflamed, metabolically active kidney in LN. As a theoretical synthesis, we propose a conceptual "balancing window" model of PD-1 signal strength to describe this bidirectional regulatory mechanism; this model is hypothesis-generating and not clinically validated. Finally, we discuss the clinical translation implications of this framework, encompassing PD-1 agonistic strategies in autoimmune diseases (still largely preclinical/early clinical), PD-1 blockade in cancer therapy, and the iatrogenic lupus-like syndrome induced by immune checkpoint inhibitors-the latter providing biological plausibility rather than definitive proof of causality. All proposed biomarkers and algorithms are presented as investigational tools not yet ready for routine clinical practice. Moreover, LN pathogenesis involves multiple pathways beyond T cells-including immune complexes, complement, B cells, and innate immunity-and the PD-1 axis should be considered within this broader context.

Exploring pathways between childhood parental abuse and adulthood generalized anxiety disorder: The roles of neuroticism, extraversion, and conscientiousness.
abstract: BACKGROUND Childhood parental abuse is an established risk factor for adulthood generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), but the personality mechanisms explaining this pathway are underinvestigated. Based on developmental psychopathology and triple vulnerability models, this study evaluated whether neuroticism, extraversion, and conscientiousness mediated the 18-year prospective paths from maternal and paternal abuse to adulthood GAD severity. Each abuse source was tested independently. METHOD Community adults (N = 3293) (M age = 45.61 years, standard deviation [SD] = 11.41, range = 20-86; 54.95% women; 89.7% non-Hispanic White) participated in three Midlife Development in the United States (MIDUS) study waves. A parallel latent variable mediation analysis estimated all three personality traits as mediators. Covariate-adjusted analyses controlled for age, sex, race, education, and body mass index (BMI). Random-intercept cross-lagged panel models (RI-CLPMs) and residualized-change models differentiated trait-level from within-person effects. RESULTS Greater maternal, but not paternal, abuse significantly predicted higher neuroticism, which, in turn, significantly mediated the path to GAD symptoms (B = 0.051, p = .008). This effect remained significant after covariate adjustment and in unadjusted and covariate-adjusted RI-CLPMs (Bs = 0.074 and 0.060, ps < .001), though paternal abuse showed a smaller effect. Change-based mediation was attenuated (B = 0.007, p = .014). Conscientiousness and extraversion did not mediate any path. DISCUSSION Neuroticism mediated the 18-year path from childhood maternal abuse to GAD symptoms, mainly via trait-level differences, but pre-existing personality differences are still potential confounders. Neuroticism-focused prevention approaches, possibly optimized via transdiagnostic strategies, require assessment.

title: AeroReformer2: Spoken-query referring segmentation for aerial images
journal: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Spoken language offers a natural, hands-free interface for specifying an arbitrary target in dense remote-sensing imagery, yet existing referring remote-sensing image segmentation benchmarks accept only written expressions. To bridge this gap, we introduce \dataset, a spoken-query benchmark derived from RISBench that adds accent- and voice-diverse speech while preserving the original image, mask, and data splits. Its hard evaluation sets combine rotor, wind, and mixed interference with three signal-to-noise levels. We also propose \model, an efficient bilateral network that combines a boundary-preserving visual path with token-preserving speech encoding, kernel linear cross-modal attention, and a resolution refinement head. The design conditions visual features at two scales without materializing a dense speech--visual affinity matrix, then restores fine boundaries using high-resolution visual features. On the clean test split, \model with Swin-Base achieves 62.09\% mean intersection over union (mIoU) and 68.22\% overall intersection over union (oIoU), outperforming the strongest audio-adapted remote-sensing baseline by 5.38 and 2.08 percentage points, respectively. It retains the best hard-set mIoU at 54.09\%. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first benchmark and model study of full-sentence spoken-query referring segmentation for remote-sensing imagery. The code will be made publicly available.

title: Reprogramming tumor-associated macrophages via ID3 mRNA delivery for enhanced immunotherapy in pancreatic cancer.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) features a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment dominated by tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), which facilitate immune evasion and compromise immunotherapeutic efficacy. The interaction between signal regulatory protein α (SIRPα) on macrophages and cluster of differentiation 47 (CD47) on tumor cells delivers a "don't-eat-me" signal that inhibits the phagocytosis of tumor cells by macrophages. Here, we present a macrophage-directed mRNA delivery strategy to reprogram TAMs in PDAC. Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) were engineered to deliver inhibitor of DNA binding 3 (ID3) mRNA, whose expression was associated with reduced SIRPα expression and pro-inflammatory macrophage reprogramming. To promote preferential uptake by TAMs, mannose-modified LNPs (MLNPs) were developed by exploiting elevated CD206 expression on these cells. In an orthotopic PDAC model, MLNP-mediated ID3 mRNA delivery enhanced macrophage phagocytosis, promoted pro-inflammatory immune remodeling, and increased intratumoral T cell and natural killer cell (NK) infiltration, accompanied by tumor-growth suppression. Furthermore, MLNP-ID3 showed enhanced combination activity with anti-PD-1 therapy. Collectively, these findings establish a macrophage-targeted mRNA strategy for transcriptional reprogramming of TAMs and present a promising immunotherapeutic framework for PDAC.

title: Canal-mediated water redistribution and ecohydrological responses in an arid inland oasis: Evidence from stable isotopes and remote sensing
Selection and evaluation of reliable reference genes in PMA-differentiated THP-1 macrophages following LPS stimulation.
abstract: Macrophages are innate immune cells differentiated from peripheral blood monocytes and play a pivotal role in immune responses against various antigens. However, the number of primary monocytes available for functional studies is limited due to their poor proliferative property. The human monocytic cell line, THP-1 is widely used as a simplified model for studying primary human macrophages because it can be differentiated into macrophage-like THP-1 cells (THP-1/M) by phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA). In this study, expression of 12 candidate reference genes was measured by RT-qPCR in PMA-differentiated THP-1/M subjected to short-term lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation (3 h; M3) or long-term LPS stimulation (24 h; M24), the latter following a 2-day resting phase. Expression stability was assessed using four algorithms: geNorm, NormFinder, BestKeeper, and RankAggreg. We found that the RPLP0/HPRT1 and GAPDH/PPIB pairs were the most stably expressed genes under the M3 and M24 conditions, respectively. In contrast, B2M was considered as the least stable gene under both conditions. Furthermore, analysis of TNF and IL1B expression revealed that normalization using other candidate reference genes resulted in differences in relative expression levels and/or expression variations compared to normalization using the selected optimal genes under both conditions. These results indicate that, even at the same LPS concentration, the most reliable reference genes in THP-1/M cells may differ depending on the protocol, including the PMA-free resting period and LPS duration; therefore, reliable reference genes should be determined for gene expression analysis in every specific protocol for THP-1 differentiation into THP-1/M cells and their subsequent stimulation.

title: Predicting taste alteration in head and neck cancer patients using 3D transformer-based deep learning model.
abstract: PURPOSE Taste alteration is a common post-treatment side effect of head and neck cancer (HNC) radiotherapy. Accurate normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) models can support treatment planning aimed at reducing side effects that impair quality-of-life. Deep learning (DL) offers opportunities to incorporate full 3D dose, CT, and organofinterest (OOI) data. Using a large prospective cohort, this study explores whether CNN and transformerbased DL models can outperform a conventional logistic regression model for predicting taste alteration 6 months after radiotherapy. MATERIAL/METHODS Data from 972 patients was used, with the endpoint being moderatetosevere patientreported taste alteration at six months (EORTC QLQH&N35). DL models were trained using 3D dose distributions, planning CT, OOI segmentations and clinical features. A conventional NTCP model using oral cavity mean dose, parotid mean dose, and age served as reference. Attention maps were evaluated for the transformer-based DL model to quantify the model attention to specific regions of the head and neck area. In addition, two cropping approaches for the 3D data were compared. RESULTS The CNN and transformer DL models performed comparable to the reference NTCP model in the test set (Reference: AUC = 0.71; ResNet: AUC = 0.68; TransRP: AUC = 0.71), though calibration was best for the reference model. Shifting the crop improved DL performance and transformer attention focused on supraglottic and submandibular regions. CONCLUSION This study showed that the prediction of taste alteration can be achieved using DL models, particularly transformer-based models which, in contrast to CNNs, can account for global features of comprehensive 3D information of dose distribution, CT-images and organs-of-interest segmentations.

title: 30-meter land surface temperature from Landsat via progressive self-training downscaling
abstract: Land surface temperature (LST) is a critical parameter for characterizing surface energy balance and hydrothermal processes. While Landsat provides invaluable LST observations at medium spatial resolution for over 40 years, its native spatial resolution of thermal bands (e.g., 100 m) remains insufficient compared to its 30 m optical bands, failing to meet the demands of fine-scale studies. To address this issues, this study proposes a progressive self-training framework for downscaling Landsat LST to 30 m without relying on fine-scale ground truth, while maintaining minimal data dependence. The framework progressively optimizes a cross-modal fusion network to refine thermal details in a coarse-to-fine manner, characterized by one pre-training and two fine-tuning stages. Spatial validation against SDGSAT-1 30 m LST and temporal validation using in situ measurements confirm its reliability and accuracy, with both station-averaged MAE and RMSE outperforming the official cubic product by approximately 0.4 K. Further performance comparison experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently reconstructs coherent fine-scale thermal patterns while preserving spatial heterogeneity. Multi spatial resolution evaluations and ablation studies verify the effectiveness of the proposed strategy and network design. Overall, the framework provides a stable pathway for enhancing the spatial resolution of Landsat LST, providing fine-resolution data support for fine-scale surface process studies and localized environmental monitoring.

title: Integrative single-cell and computational pathology analyses reveal a C11orf24-associated stem-like epithelial population linked to tumor microenvironment remodeling and immune evasion in bladder cancer.
abstract: BACKGROUND Cancer stem-like cells drive tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, yet the epithelial stemness hierarchy in bladder cancer (BLCA) remains poorly defined. We aimed to characterize stemness-associated epithelial populations and their clinical significance. METHODS We analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing data from 92,218 cells across 13 treatment-naïve BLCA samples to characterize epithelial stemness and tumor-microenvironment interactions. Spatial transcriptomics and independent bulk cohorts were used for orthogonal and clinical validation. An HStem-associated histopathology-based prognostic model was developed by integrating quantitative image features with deep-learning representations, followed by functional validation of the candidate gene C11orf24. RESULTS We identified a highly stem-like epithelial population (HStem) at the apex of the differentiation hierarchy, exhibiting MYC activation, oxidative phosphorylation, and DNA repair enrichment, with preferential presence in advanced-stage tumors. HStem cells were inferred to serve as major communication hubs within the TME, interacting extensively with fibroblasts and endothelial cells via MIF-CD74/CXCR4 and MIF-CD74/CD44 axes. An 86-gene HStem signature enabled development of a robust image-based prognostic model. High-risk tumors showed immune exclusion, immunosuppressive enrichment, T-cell dysfunction, and predicted checkpoint blockade resistance. C11orf24 emerged as a candidate stemness-associated regulator; C11orf24-positive cells displayed enhanced stemness and stromal interactions. Functional experiments demonstrated that C11orf24 perturbation altered clonogenic growth, migration, and invasion in BLCA cells. Pharmacogenomic analyses identified predicted therapeutic vulnerabilities that warrant experimental validation. CONCLUSIONS We identify an HStem population associated with BLCA progression, microenvironmental remodeling, and immune evasion. Integrating single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with computational pathology, we establish a clinically relevant stemness framework and identify C11orf24 as a potential therapeutic target, offering opportunities for stemness-directed precision oncology.

title: Scalar Positioning in Political Discourse
abstract: This Element advances the Scalar Deictic Space approach as a cognitive–discursive framework for analysing how political discourse constructs, differentiates, and dynamically reorganises identity, agency, urgency, and legitimacy. Building on the primacy of spatial cognition, SDS conceptualises political meaning-making as a scalar configuration anchored in a deictic centre, organised across proximal, medial, and distal zones of positioning. These zones reflect graded relations of intentionality, dependency, and symbolic alignment rather than fixed group memberships. By moving beyond binary Us–Other models, SDS reveals how political discourse internally stratifies the in-group, redistributing power and responsibility through shifting spatial, temporal, and modal configurations. Drawing on variety of examples including US, Iranian, and Ukrainian political discourse, the Element demonstrates how scalar positioning enables actors to legitimise action and project future while maintaining ideological coherence. As a dynamic analytical tool for tracing diachronic change in political worldviews, SDS critically examines cognitive foundations of political persuasion.

title: Decoding the climate–potato link: six decades of teleconnection-driven European potato yield variability revealed by explainable machine learning
abstract: Understanding how large-scale climate teleconnections affect staple crop yield is essential for anticipating production risks and strengthening food security in a warming world. This study examines the influence of major teleconnection patterns on potato yield across Europe, where potatoes remain a key component of the food supply. To account for differences in cropping calendars, Europe was divided into three regions (North, Center, South) based on potato growing season timing. Nine machine learning techniques were applied to model regional yield responses using a dataset spanning 1961–2023, incorporating multiple teleconnection indices with lags of up to 36 months. Among all models, the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) performed best in every region, with the highest accuracy in the South (R 2 = 0.79) and lower but still robust skill in the North (R 2 = 0.62). Explainable artificial intelligence using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) showed that the East Atlantic (EA) and East Atlantic/West Russia (EA/WR) patterns were consistently the most influential predictors, although their importance varied regionally. Lagged EA indices emerged as particularly significant, indicating a strong climate-memory effect in potato production. Despite the highest prediction accuracy in the South, this region exhibited the lowest historical yield levels, likely reflecting combined heat and water stress. By demonstrating that regional potato yield is strongly modulated by specific teleconnection patterns, these findings highlight the value of teleconnection-aware prediction systems for climate-risk management and underscore the need to integrate climate indices into long-term agricultural and food security planning in Europe.

title: Harnessing Neuroendocrine and Circadian Clocks in Beneficial Insects for Agricultural Chrono-Management
abstract: Pollinators and natural enemies provide essential agricultural ecosystem services that are regulated by circadian clocks, hormones, and biogenic amines. This review synthesizes research on the integration between neuroendocrine systems and circadian clocks across different taxa, identifying both conserved regulatory mechanisms and lineage-specific adaptive traits. These multilayered interactions coordinate insect behavior, life-history development, and the alignment of insect activities with available resources. We propose agricultural chrono-management, a framework to improve ecosystem services by using targeted environmental cues to align beneficial insect activity with farming schedules. However, most evidence so far comes from the laboratory and controlled studies, and field validation remains limited. We further evaluated the feasibility, ecological risks, and climate resilience of photoperiodic regulation, nutritional modulation, and synthetic ecological interventions. Key future research priorities include multiomics integration, large-scale field validation, and predictive modeling of ecosystem services. This synthesis links molecular-level regulatory mechanisms to ecological outcomes and establishes a foundational framework for climate-resilient management of beneficial insects.
journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry

title: Breast carcinoma amplified sequence 2 rescues adult hippocampal neurogenesis and cognitive deficits in Alzheimer's disease via regulating BDNF/TrkB signaling.
Leveraging genomic deep learning models for the prediction of noncoding variant effects
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
abstract: Characterizing noncoding variant function remains an important challenge in human genetics. Genomic deep learning models have emerged as a promising approach to enable in silico prediction of variant effects. These models include supervised sequence-to-activity models, which predict molecular phenotypes such as genome-wide chromatin states or gene expression levels directly from DNA sequence, and self-supervised genomic language models. Here we review progress in leveraging these models for noncoding variant effect prediction. We describe practical considerations for making such predictions and categorize the types of ground-truth data used to evaluate variant effect predictions, providing insight into the settings in which current models are most useful. Our Review highlights key considerations for practitioners and opportunities for improvement in model development and evaluation.

title: Global forest typology at 10-meter resolution for forest and land-use monitoring
abstract: Distinguishing forest types—primary, naturally regenerating, planted, and plantation forests—from agricultural tree crops and other land uses is essential for carbon accounting, biodiversity assessment, conservation planning, and supply-chain regulation. However, no existing global dataset resolves this typology at high spatial resolution. We present the Forest Typology (ForTy) v1 dataset, a global 10-meter resolution baseline map for 2020 that classifies all land into six categories aligned with FAO and EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) definitions: Primary Forest, Naturally Regenerating Forest, Planted Forest, Plantation Forest, Tree Crops and Agroforestry, and Other Land. A cascaded deep learning pipeline, trained on 1.7 million globally distributed samples, generates per-class relative confidence maps from geospatial satellite embeddings by combining weakly supervised learning with active learning. Independent validation against 8,190 expert-labeled stratified random sites yields an overall accuracy of 90.2% for the six-class scheme, 94.8% for natural forest classification, and 95.5% for forest/non-forest classification.

title: RiceExtent v1.0: a global rice-specific land cover product from multi-source data integration
abstract: Accurate land cover information is fundamental for monitoring land-use dynamics, supporting sustainable agriculture, and informing environmental and climate-related decision-making; however, detailed and globally consistent crop-specific datasets, particularly for rice, remain limited. The study presents RiceExtent v1.0, a harmonized global rice-specific land cover dataset athigh (10 m) and moderate (250 m) resolution, developed by integrating verified local, national, and regional rice maps with ESA WorldCover v200 using a hierarchical multi-criteria dataset ranking and spatial merging approach that prioritizes source accuracy and spatial detail. Using an extent-based merging strategy that aggregates multi-source rice data, RiceExtent derives a maximum observed rice cultivation extent rather than annual mean estimates, thereby capturing double and triple cropping patterns, fragmented smallholder fields, and inter-annual variability often underrepresented in other products. The final product was evaluated using area-based statistical comparison metrics against Spatial Production Allocation Model (SPAM), RiceAtlas, and GloRice, along with USDA rice production statistics. Validation using independent ground-truth samples was performed using True Positive Rate (TPR). The developed dataset captures an estimated global rice area of ~ 1.67 million km² and shows broad agreement with official statistics and improving representation in Southeast Asia, South Asia, Africa and the Americas. RiceExtent v1.0, provided through an open repository (https://dataverse.tdl.org/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18738/T8/JYAEHV) with accompanying Python script, offers a robust resource for agricultural monitoring, crop and hydrological modeling, and climate impact assessments, while enabling collaborative refinement of global rice mapping.

title: Plant-based meat alternatives can support reductions in agricultural land expansion and greenhouse gas emissions but entail micronutrient trade-offs

title: Wheat in Crisis: Variability of Wheat Area in Lebanon 2017–2025
abstract: Wheat is a vital staple crop worldwide. However, its production has been increasingly challenged in Lebanon in recent years by multi-factorial crises intersecting socio-economic, political, security, and climate factors. This study provides the first national, multi-year monitoring of wheat area in Lebanon (2017–2025), linking satellite observations with crisis impacts. We conducted a multi-temporal supervised classification across the 2017–2018 to 2024–2025 seasons, using Google Earth Engine, Sentinel-2 imagery, and Random Forest classifier, achieving an 87% overall accuracy. We then estimated wheat area based on a random stratified sample. Interannual changes were related to major crises and input-price dynamics. Wheat area increased during 2019–2021 but dropped sharply in 2021–2022 as subsidies weakened and input costs surged. Indeed, during the transition toward economy dollarization, production costs in USD peaked in 2021–2022 and then eased consistently with the 2022–2023 area rebound. In 2023–2025, the crop area decreased again dramatically (−34% in 2023–2024 and −38% in 2024–2025) due to the conflict with Israel and associated widespread displacement that likely constrained field access and reduced sowing, particularly in southern Lebanon. Ultimately, our findings highlight the critical need for ground-truth data for accurate area estimation, alongside yield and socio-economic metrics to better understand interannual wheat area variability.

title: High-Efficiency Combustion Mode in Three-Strut Scramjet Combustor via Clustering Analysis
abstract: This study investigates the influence of five design parameters on the combustion characteristics of a three-strut combustion chamber through single-factor analysis, clarifying their relationship with combustion efficiency and resistance. A Halton sequence with mean squared error–based infill sampling was employed to generate a sample set, and an accurate surrogate model was developed using Gaussian process regression. The Nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) was then applied to optimize the chamber geometry with the objectives of improving combustion efficiency and reducing resistance. Through clustering analysis, two distinct high-efficiency combustion modes were identified: a multizone violent combustion mode and a blended mild combustion mode. In the former, the rapid combustion of pilot fuel creates favorable conditions for subsequent fuel combustion, increasing the combustion efficiency from 73% to 93% compared with the baseline case; however, due to excessively abrupt flow field changes, the reduction in resistance is not significant. In the latter, the flame fronts merge and develop smoothly, and although it only improves combustion efficiency to 85% compared with the baseline case, it substantially reduces resistance from − 7,762 newtons (N) to − 8303 N . This work provides enhanced design flexibility for high-performance scramjet combustors.

title: Efficient Synergistic Design Framework for Electric Aircraft Integrating Co-Flow Jet
abstract: Flow control technologies such as the Co-Flow Jet (CFJ) have demonstrated significant potential for improving aerodynamic performance. However, most existing studies treat CFJ parameters as fixed during aircraft conceptual design, limiting the ability to evaluate their system-level impact on aircraft performance. To address this limitation, this study proposes an efficient multidisciplinary design framework that integrates key CFJ design parameters into the conceptual design process of CFJ electric aircraft. The framework combines a quasi-three-dimensional aerodynamic analysis method with energy consumption and weight estimation models of the jet system, enabling rapid evaluation of aerodynamic performance, propulsion power consumption, and aircraft weight within a unified framework. Based on the proposed methodology, a multidisciplinary design optimization problem is formulated to improve aircraft cruise performance. The framework is applied to a representative aircraft configuration, and the predicted aerodynamic performance is validated against computational fluid dynamics simulations. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can efficiently capture the coupled effects of CFJ aerodynamic benefits, jet system energy consumption, and additional structural weight. Parametric studies further reveal the sensitivity of optimal CFJ configuration to cruise velocity and fan efficiency, providing useful guidance for the preliminary design of CFJ electric aircraft.

title: FRGB3D: Fast Reliability-Weighted Gaussian Background Modeling for Roadside LiDAR Traffic Monitoring
abstract: Intelligent transportation systems rely on accurate perception technologies for traffic monitoring, with light detection and ranging (LiDAR) emerging as a critical sensing modality. However, effective background–foreground separation is challenging due to the varying measurement reliability across point clouds caused by distance, reflectivity, and atmospheric conditions. This paper presents fast reliability-weighted Gaussian background modeling for 3D LiDAR traffic monitoring (FRGB3D), a novel unsupervised approach for LiDAR point cloud background modeling and foreground detection that explicitly incorporates physics-based reliability assessment with adaptive learning mechanisms. The key contributions include (1) a physics-based reliability metric that quantifies measurement quality using range and reflectivity characteristics, (2) a reliability-weighted adaptive learning approach for Gaussian background modeling that dynamically adjusts learning rates based on point reliability, and (3) an adaptive thresholding mechanism that incorporates both measurement reliability and learned model uncertainty. Through comprehensive experiments using both the Car Learning to Act (CARLA) simulator and real-world LiDAR data collected in Lowell, Massachusetts, we demonstrate that FRGB3D achieves superior foreground detection performance compared with baseline methods. FRGB3D achieved F1-scores of 0.84, 0.68, and 0.77 across base, adverse-weather, and high-density traffic scenarios, respectively, consistently outperforming simple difference, moving average, and standard Gaussian background modeling approaches. Real-world experiments demonstrated competitive object-level performance average precision (AP) (AP@0.5 = 0.48) while maintaining real-time processing capabilities with 19.1 frames per second (FPS), making it suitable for practical traffic monitoring applications.
journal: Journal of Computing in Civil Engineering

title: Comparative Analysis of Two Approaches for Improved Site Safety: Domain Approach versus General End-to-End Compliance Reasoning
abstract: Field compliance checking seeks to automate the process of extracting safety requirements, capturing site information, identifying violations, and generating documentation for different responsible parties to improve construction site safety. However, existing safety checking methods are typically limited in their ability to employ domain knowledge and multimodal data, and they often lack generalizability and scalability. There is also limited effort to automatically generate natural-language descriptions of compliance-checking results for documentation purposes. Aimed toward addressing these gaps, this paper studies and compares two approaches for automated safety checking: a domain approach and an end-to-end approach. The domain approach integrates existing domain-specific information extraction, site visual information detection, and knowledge graph–based compliance reasoning methods. The end-to-end approach relies on multimodal foundation models. The comparative analysis evaluates the information extraction and compliance reasoning capabilities of both approaches in terms of performance, errors, and limitations. The results showed that the domain approach achieved strong performance with good potential for generalizability and adaptability. In contrast, the end-to-end approach requires additional fine-tuning to achieve comparable results.
journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management

title: A Review of Human-Centric Construction Manufacturing: Current Practices and Research Opportunities
abstract: The industrialization of the construction industry has transformed traditional practices by streamlining construction processes in controlled, factory-based environments through construction manufacturing production systems, in which building components are produced in factories and assembled on-site. Beyond improvements in efficiency and environmental performance, this production paradigm establishes long-term relationships between workers and management, creating an opportunity for human-centric construction manufacturing that prioritizes workers’ well-being as a core element of production within the Industry 5.0 paradigm. Human-centric construction manufacturing offers a practical means of integrating worker well-being, safety, mental health, inclusiveness, and skill development into construction production systems. Despite growing interest in human-centric considerations, existing research remains fragmented, loosely defined, and predominantly technology-driven. To address these gaps, this paper presents a scoping review on human-centric construction manufacturing that synthesizes key research themes, enabling technologies, emerging trends, research gaps, and future research directions within construction production systems. A total of 54 articles were included in the review, spanning three research areas examined from a human-centric perspective, i.e., ergonomics, safety, and workforce planning, each further categorized into subresearch areas. Workers’ mental health, equity, diversity, inclusion, and holistic well-being in the construction manufacturing paradigm remain significant and underexplored research opportunities. Among the most prominent technologies were simulation, virtual reality, optimization, sensing technologies, and 3D modeling, while computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and digital twins were less frequently applied, despite their strong potential to support human-centric construction manufacturing. Overall, this review establishes a comprehensive foundation for understanding the current state of human-centric construction manufacturing, identifies critical research needs, and provides guidance for future efforts toward developing safer, healthier, and more productive factory environments that support resilient construction manufacturing systems.
journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management

title: Early medical student experiences in a longitudinal coaching program grounded in the Master Adaptive Learner framework.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Coaching promotes self-directed learning, reflective practice, and professional development. Previous research has focused on senior medical students or established programs, leaving a limited understanding of how students experience coaching during the initiation of a new program. We sought to explore first- and second-year medical students' experiences in a newly established longitudinal coaching program oriented around the Master Adaptive Learner model, and to identify factors that support or hinder program effectiveness. METHODS We conducted qualitative semi-structured focus group interviews with first- and second-year medical students within the coaching program. Audio recordings were de-identified, transcribed, and analyzed using thematic analysis informed by descriptive phenomenology. Three investigators independently coded transcripts, iteratively refining a codebook and achieving thematic saturation. RESULTS We held 7 focus groups with 20 participants. Three themes were identified: (1) Relational dynamics, emphasizing trust, personal connection, and the value of longitudinal interaction; (2) Role of coach in supporting education, highlighting coaches' neutrality, facilitation of self-reflection, and perceived educational benefits; and (3) Early program challenges, including prescriptive elements, communication barriers, and variability between coaches. Participants valued the relational aspects more than the structured Master Adaptive Learner-aligned reflective exercises, particularly during the pre-clerkship phase. DISCUSSION Early-stage coaching programs are most effective when they prioritize relationship-building and psychological safety: without consistently strong relational foundations, structured MAL-oriented reflection may not be feasible or salient for students. For institutions implementing new coaching programs, our findings suggest four actionable priorities: (1) invest early in relational groundwork; (2) clearly differentiate coaching from directive developmental relationships like advising or mentoring; (3) minimize overly prescriptive structures during launch phases, and (4) encourage MAL-oriented reflective work only after trust and psychological safety have been firmly established.

title: Advancing clinical integration in undergraduate dental education through AI-enabled instructional design: a qualitative thematic analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND Despite growing interest in artificial intelligence (AI) in health professions education, qualitative evidence for integarting AI-supported instructional redesign on teaching practices and students' experiences in undergraduate dental education remains limited. The aim of this study was to explore the educational impact of AI-supported instructional redesign of lessons in undergraduate dental education. METHODS We conducted this inductive qualitative thematic analysis in an undergraduate dental education setting. Existing lessons were redesigned using AI-supported recommendations to strengthen alignment between learning objectives, authentic clinical contexts, and expected clinical outcomes. Data were collected through classroom observations and students' focus group discussions. An inductive thematic analysis was performed, and findings from multiple data sources were curated, collecetd, and triangulated to enhance credibility. RESULTS AI-supported instructional redesign transformed teaching by promoting authentic clinical scenarios, clinically oriented discussions, and explicit reasoning activities. Thematic analysis identified four interconnected themes: (1) a shift from teacher-centred knowledge delivery to facilitation of clinical reasoning; (2) transformation from passive attendance to active cognitive engagement; (3) building clinical meaning through authentic clinical contexts and collaborative dialogue; and (4) creating conditions for professional learning through psychological safety. AI functioned as a pedagogical design-support tool rather than replacing the educators' instructional role. Overall, the observed educational changes appeared to arise primarily from the pedagogical redesign enabled by AI-supported planning rather than from students' direct interaction with AI. CONCLUSION This study endorses the role of AI-supported instructional redesign in enriching the existing undergraduate dental curriculum. This approach can potentially help educators align learning objectives, instructional strategies, and authentic clinical contexts. The reported educational modifications reflect primarily the implementation of learner-centred and clinically oriented pedagogical strategies, with AI functioning as a design-support mechanism rather than as a direct instructional agent.

title: Spatial Context as a Time-Invariant Confounder: A Fixed-Effects Extension of MGWR
