title: A Non-Autonomous (Time-Varying) Lotka–Volterra Competition Model for Conventional and Islamic Banking Assets in Indonesia
abstract: This study examines the joint evolution of conventional and Islamic banking assets in Indonesia using a non-autonomous Lotka–Volterra competition model. The model was calibrated to a compiled annual series for 2016–2024 with time-dependent intrinsic growth and capacity terms, constrained nonlinear least squares, and adaptive Runge–Kutta integration. The working series includes two interpolated observations (2017–2018). For these inputs, the time-dependent model achieved in-sample MAPE of 1.52% for Islamic banking and 2.22% for conventional banking, while the fitted interaction coefficients were near zero under the imposed bounds. Nevertheless, the constant-parameter model had the lowest reported AICc, and five rolling-origin tests produced mean errors of 7.69% and 5.50%, respectively. Bootstrap and enlarged-bound analyses indicated weak identification of several growth and capacity parameters. Frozen-time Jacobian calculations yielded locally stable equilibria for the autonomous systems evaluated at the observed years, without establishing stability of the full non-autonomous system. A continuation to 2028 produced a conditional Islamic-market-share median near 7.2% and a reported 90% bootstrap interval of 6.4–9.2%. These outputs describe the behavior of the retained dataset and model assumptions rather than a causal effect of the 2021 BSI merger or a validated financial forecast. The results underscore the importance of complexity penalties, identifiability analysis, and source-data provenance in aggregate financial-dynamics modeling.

title: Readiness of Rural Residents to Use Artificial Intelligence in Agrarian Business
abstract: The article is devoted to the analysis of the awareness and readiness of rural residents and agricultural com-plex workers in Russia to use products and solutions created with artificial intelligence (AI). The work is based on a secondary analysis of data from the nationwide survey conducted by the VCIOM Analytical Center (N = 1604, weighted sample). It is shown that at the nearly level of the general awareness of AI application in agri-culture, the readiness of its usage is sharply differentiated by age: it is declining more than twofold from Gen-eration Z to boomers generation. The research defines with the logistic regression that besides age, it is con-sidered that education, income, type of settlement and gender are significant predictors of readiness, while frequency of internet use loses its meaning once other factors are controlled for. Multiple correspondence analysis revealed that these characteristics form a coherent gradient of digital and innovative inclusion. Factor analysis of eighteen statements about the benefits and risks of AI identified three orthogonal dimensions of perception – techno-optimism, ethico-naturalistic risk, and techno-systemic risk, of which only the first two ef-fectively predict readiness to adopt the technology. Drawing on the latent profile analysis, four stable attitude types – from techno-enthusiasts to ethical sceptics differing not only in the degree of perception factors but also in socio-demographic composition – are highlighted. These findings are interpreted in light of diffusion-of-innovations theory and technology-acceptance models.

title: AI Powered IoT-Based System for Weed and Pest Control in Agriculture Using Deep Learning
abstract: Weeds, pest attacks, labour shortage and over-dependence on chemical pesticides are the serious challenges faced by the agricultural sector in the wake of ever growing weed infestation. Manual weed and pest control has potential negative environmental impacts, increased production costs and reduced yields. The application of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), Deep Learning, robotics, and laser technologies are a promising way of developing sustainable and autonomous agricultural systems. This study introduces an intelligent agricultural system based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) for weed identification, harmful insect identification, crop condition monitoring and automatic weed removal using a laser beam. The system will be based on Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, Computer vision modules, Convolutional neural networks (CNN), Unmanned robotic platforms, Environmental sensing systems, and Electronic Swarm Suppression (ESS) mechanisms to enhance agricultural productivity and reduce crop losses. The system uses deep learning algorithms for real time weed, crop, beneficial and harmful insect classification. High-resolution cameras and sensing devices collect environmental and crop data continuously and feed the data into an IoT system for processing in a cloud-edge computing system. High precision weed elimination with a robotic platform containing laser emitters which do not harm adjacent crops. Further, computer vision and environmental monitoring are employed to identify aerial insect swarms and to enable automatic attacks of insect swarms by means of a laser beam and ESS technology. Multiple agricultural blocks were used for experimental evaluation of the maize, wheat, soybean and vegetable crops. The results show substantial increases in the accuracy of weed detection, pest identification, crop protection and cost savings for operations over current practices. The proposed system achieved a 97.6% accuracy in the weed classification, 96.8% accuracy in the detection of the insect and a 42.3% reduction in pesticide use. In addition, the crop yield rose by 18.7% and the operational costs dropped by 28.4%. Overall, the results suggest that AI-powered IoT can significantly enhance precision agriculture and promote sustainable food production.
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Developing a digital agricultural monitoring model to strengthen national food security in Indonesia: a qualitative systems analysis
abstract: Global geopolitical dynamics, climate change, disruptions to food supply chains, commodity price volatility, and dependence on agricultural inputs constitute strategic challenges to national food self-reliance and food security. These conditions require the development of an agricultural surveillance system capable of providing rapid, accurate, integrated, real-time, and predictive information as a basis for strategic decision-making. This study aims to analyze the current state of agricultural digital surveillance, identify strategic factors influencing its implementation, and formulate an agricultural digital surveillance technology model to strengthen food security self-reliance in response to global geopolitical dynamics. The study employs a descriptive-analytical qualitative approach, with data collected through in-depth interviews, observation, documentation, and literature review. Data were analyzed using NVivo-assisted Thematic Analysis, PESTEL Analysis, SWOT Analysis, and Soft Systems Methodology (SSM). The findings indicate that the main challenges are data fragmentation, limited interoperability, disparities in human resource capacity, a surveillance system that remains sectoral, and the suboptimal utilization of technology for predictive analysis. The SWOT analysis places the strategic position in Quadrant I, indicating that the priority strategy should focus on leveraging technological strengths to capitalize on opportunities arising from agricultural digital transformation. SSM produced an integrated model that connects digital data acquisition, data integration, big data and AI analytics, risk analysis, an Early Warning System, a digital dashboard, strategic decision-making, policy response, and monitoring and evaluation. The model is expected to strengthen early detection, policy responses, food self-reliance and sovereignty, as well as national resilience in response to global geopolitical dynamics.

title: Integrating Agro-Edutainment and Fintech into an Educational Tourism Business Model for Nutritional Literacy in Bintaro, Jakarta, Indonesia
abstract: This study examines the integration of agro-edutainment and financial technology (fintech) into an educational tourism business model to support nutritional literacy in Bintaro, Indonesia. A quantitative survey approach was employed at Kebun Berseri, a community-based urban farming destination. The study population comprised visitors, local residents, and community members involved in educational tourism activities. Using purposive sampling, 80 female respondents who had participated in educational tourism activities were included. Data were collected using a questionnaire designed to assess agro-edutainment experiences, fintech utilization, nutritional literacy, healthy consumption behavior, and perceived social impact. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS, including measurement model evaluation, structural model assessment, and hypothesis testing. The findings revealed significant positive relationships between agro-edutainment and nutritional literacy (β = 0.729), agro-edutainment and social impact (β = 0.739), and fintech and social impact (β = 0.178). Conversely, fintech was negatively associated with nutritional literacy (β = -0.217), while its relationship with healthy consumption behavior was not statistically significant. These findings highlight the potential of experiential agricultural education while emphasizing the need to integrate meaningful nutrition education into digital tourism services. Keywords: agro-edutainment, educational tourism, financial technology, nutritional literacy; urban farming

title: STRUCTURAL TRANSFORMATIONS OF UKRAINIAN EXPORTS
abstract: The article examines the structural transformation of Ukraineʼs exports under the impact of the full-scale war of 2022, which triggered an unprecedented shock to the countryʼs trade system. The relevance of the study stems from the profound shifts in logistical, institutional, and production conditions that reshaped external trade flows and generated a critical dependence on the European Union market. The research is based on the hypothesis that the war caused not temporary fluctuations but a deep and irrever­sible structural reconfiguration of Ukraineʼs export model, reflected in changes in geog­raphical orientation, commodity composition, and market concentration. The methodological framework includes: comparative analysis of export dynamics in 2010–2024; calculation of the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI) to assess geographic concentration; graphical modeling of long-term trends; identification of factors influencing the war on the export of goods from Ukraine. The statistical database was compiled based on data from the State Statistics Service of Ukraine, the European Commission, UN Comtrade, analytical reports from international organizations (Oxfam, Deloitte, Pricewater­houseCoopers, Brookings Institution, Statista), and author calculations. The results substantiate the proposed hypothesis. The share of exports directed to the EU increased from 24% in 2010 to over 60–66% in 2022–2024, while exports to Asia and Africa contracted sharply due to the blockade of Black Sea ports. The commodity structure shifted from metallurgy to agriculture. Export concentration reached record levels (HHI ≈ 0.48 in 2023). The study identifies key adaptive mechanisms, including the expansion of Danube logistics routes, deepening integration with the EU, and digitalization of customs procedures. The findings confirm that Ukraineʼs export sector is undergoing a systemic and irreversible transformation that will shape the trajectory of post-war recovery and long-term integration into European and global markets.

title: INSTITUTIONAL CHALLENGES TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF LAND CAPITAL IN UKRAINE
abstract: The article explores the essence and current state of the agricultural land market in Ukraine as a strategic determinant in the transformation of the national agro-industrial complex under martial law. The study identifies key factors that have historically hindered the development of land relations: the prolonged moratorium, the shadow rental market, soil degradation, and the chronic undercapitalization of the sector. The research hypothesis posits that the current liberalized land market model, amid war and institutional weakness, leads to excessive land concentration and worsened soil degradation. This necessitates immediate adjustments to strengthen environmental controls and protect small producers, drawing on the practices of European countries. The methodological foundation of the study is a systems approach incorporating statistical analysis to evaluate land fund losses, comparative analysis to contrast Ukrainian and Polish market regulation models, and a structural-logical method to define state policy priorities. The research relies on data from the StateGeoCadastre, the Ministry of Economy of Ukraine, and analytics from international institutions. The study confirms that under the full-scale armed aggression of the Russian Federation, domestic land capital has suffered catastrophic losses. These are evident in the extensive mining of vast territories, heavy metal contamination of chernozems, and the destruction of southern irrigation systems following the breach of the Kakhovka HPP. An analysis of the land marketʼs implementation (from 2021 to early 2026) shows that despite granting market access to legal entities, market dynamics remain moderate, land prices in foreign currency equivalent are the lowest in Europe, and there is no massive influx of investment due to high security risks. A comparative analysis of Polandʼs strictly regulated (social) land market model and Ukraineʼs liberalized model confirms the hypothesis regarding the urgent need to enhance state environmental oversight and protect small farming enterprises. The research highlights that excessive land concentration by the corporate sector poses a particular threat when inspection measures are relaxed. It is demonstrated that an effective post-war transformation requires a comprehensive approach encompassing syste­matic humanitarian demining, land reclamation, preferential lending for small agribusinesses using land as collateral, and the innovative reconstruction of irrigation systems. The article emphasizes the importance of harmonizing national land legislation with EU standards, which will help restore agricultural potential and solidify Ukraineʼs position as a key guarantor of global food security.

title: INSTITUTIONAL CONSTRAINTS ON THE DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF UKRAINIAN AGRICULTURAL SECTOR
abstract: This study investigates the theoretical and methodological foundations and tools of digital transformation in Ukraineʼs agricultural sector and develops scientific and methodological approaches to establishing a system of indicators for assessing agricultural digital maturity in the context of sustainable development and European integration. The hypothesis is put forward that the effectiveness of digital transformation is deter­mined not so much by the level of implementation of individual digital technologies as by the coherence of organisational, economic, techno­logical, and institutional tools that ensure their integration into the agricultural sector manage­ment system. The hypothesis was tested through the systematisation of scientific approaches to the digitalisation of agricultural production, compa­rative and structural-functional analysis, asses­sment of the relationships between digitali­sation indicators, innovation potential, and sustainable development, and an examination of official statistical data, European Commission materials, and international indices, including the Global Innovation Index and the Digital Economy and Society Index. It was established that the digital transformation of the agricultural sector is a comprehensive process encompassing the use of precision agriculture technologies, sensor and satellite monitoring, the Internet of Things, Big Data, artificial intelligence, geographic informa­tion systems, unmanned technologies, and digital management platforms. Indicators for assessing digital transformation were systematised into technological, economic, environmental, social, and institutional blocks, enabling a compre­hensive assessment of the level of digital maturity of the agricultural sector and the effectiveness of digital solutions implementation. Technological heterogeneity of the agricultural sector was identified, manifested in a significant gap between digitally mature large enterprises and small and medium-sized producers with limited access to digital infrastructure, financial resources, and modern digital competencies. Methods and tools for digital transformation were systematised according to organisational, economic, techno­logical, and institutional criteria. The feasibility of their integrated application was substantiated to ensure the relationship between digital modernisation and increased efficiency of agri­cul­tural production. The proposed approach can be used to improve state digitalisation policy, substantiate priorities for supporting agricultural enterprises, and monitor the effectiveness of digital transformation in Ukraineʼs agricultural sector.

title: Intelligent Manufacturing Scheduling Optimization Based on Genetic Algorithm and MES
abstract: Against the backdrop of intensified global manufacturing competition and the deep advancement of Industry 4.0, production scheduling, as a core link in efficient operations within intelligent manufacturing, faces challenges that traditional methods can no longer meet, such as delayed data acquisition and insufficient dynamic response. Therefore, a scheduling model for Industry 4.0 intelligent manufacturing based on a Genetic Algorithm (GA) and a Manufacturing Execution System (MES) is proposed. During the process, the particle swarm algorithm was used to optimize the Genetic Algorithm's parameters serially, thereby reducing complexity. At the same time, the ant colony algorithm was integrated to optimize key processes, improving the model's stability and convergence and establishing a scheduling optimization model that integrates data collection, rapid processing, and reasonable allocation. The experimental results show that the inventory turnover rate of the intelligent manufacturing scheduling model constructed in this study has increased by 3.24%, 4.58%, and 6.17%, respectively, compared to the control model’s. Meanwhile, the on-time delivery rate reaches 92.13% and 91.75% across two datasets, both above 91%. The task delay rates are 7.69% and 8.67%, showing significant advantages over the comparison models at 10.45% and 11.75%, respectively. These results indicate that the proposed model can achieve efficient allocation of production resources and dynamic responsiveness, thereby improving production line efficiency and offering a new approach to intelligent manufacturing scheduling.
journal: Journal of Engineering, Project, and Production Management

title: A Multi-Layer Contextual Model for Managing Data Overload in Smart Hydroponics
abstract: The widespread use of the Internet of Things (IoT) in hydroponic agriculture allows continuous monitoring of environmental conditions and provides real-time information to support crop management. However, the increasing amount of sensor data generated makes the monitoring process more complex as users need to interpret multiple environmental parameters simultaneously. Existing hydroponic monitoring systems focus on data collection and visualization, while the management and information delivery aspects to reduce data overload are still limited. This study proposes a multi-layer contextual model to manage environmental information in an intelligent hydroponic monitoring system. The model consists of five interconnected layers (Power, Sensor, Communication, Database and Visualization), which support the process of acquisition, validation, management and contextual data delivery. To validate the proposed model, a solar-powered IoT hydroponic monitoring system integrated with an Augmented Reality (AR) application was developed based on Situation Awareness Theory. Using the System Usability Scale (SUS), the prototype was assessed by three domain experts. The results achieved an average usability score of 85.83, which reflects excellent usability. The results indicate that the proposed model improves organisation and presentation of environmental information by prioritising contextually relevant data rather than displaying all available sensor readings at once. This enables users to identify important environmental conditions efficiently and supports more effective monitoring. This approach helps to reduce data overload and provides a practical framework that can support the development of IoT-based smart agriculture applications in the future through the integration of anomaly detection techniques and predictive analytics.
journal: Journal of Information and Communication Technology

title: Towards smart agro-ecotourism: a systematic review and integrated framework for sustainable agrotourism
abstract: The purpose of this research is to define the emerging, integrated field of smart agro-ecotourism (SAE) by systematically reviewing two parallel literatures: smart agriculture (SA) and smart ecotourism (SE). Building on this synthesis, the study proposes a conceptual framework for merging digitalisation with environmental responsibility in Indonesian agrotourism. A systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A structured search of the Scopus database identified applications of the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), and data analytics for environmental sustainability across both domains, and a thematic synthesis was performed on 80 included studies. The results show two technologically mature but conceptually unconnected research streams: smart agriculture, oriented towards production-side resource management, and smart ecotourism, oriented towards conservation-side visitor management. Cross-referencing this technological literature against existing agro-ecotourism frameworks indicates that none currently treats digital integration as a structural dimension. Drawing on this gap and on a case of practical, bottom-up integration identified in Rancamaya, Bogor, the study proposes a three-layer SAE conceptual framework and derives Pentahelix-based recommendations for its implementation in Indonesia. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first systematic review to bridge the smart agriculture and smart ecotourism literatures and to formally propose an integrated SAE framework.
journal: Issues and Perspectives in Business and Social Sciences

title: Long-term crop residue management drives soil aggregation and carbon–nitrogen retention in a calcareous rice–wheat system of the eastern Indo-Gangetic Plains
abstract: Rising food demand and intensive agricultural practices that reduce soil organic matter and soil structural stability threaten sustainability. Long-term crop residue management is considered a key strategy for restoring soil health and enhancing carbon sequestration in the calcareous soils of Indo-Gangetic Plains; however, its effects on aggregate-mediated carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) retention across soil depths remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the impact of 30 years of residue management on soil aggregation, aggregate-associated organic carbon and nitrogen, bulk soil properties, and soil organic carbon (SOC) and total nitrogen (TN) stocks in a rice–wheat cropping system (RWCS). Five treatments comprising uncultivated soil (UN), no residue addition (R 0 ), and 25% (R 1 ), 50% (R 2 ), and 100% (R 3 ) residue addition, respectively, were assessed across four soil depths (0–5, 5–15, 15–30, and 30–60 cm). Residue addition reduced bulk density and increased mean weight diameter, geometric mean diameter, macroaggregate proportion (Ma), and aggregate ratio, with the greatest improvements observed under R 3 . Aggregate-associated SOC and TN increased consistently with residue addition across all depths and aggregate size fractions. Higher Ma formation promoted the accumulation and physical protection of C and N, resulting in significant improvement in SOC and TN in bulk soil, stratification ratios, and enzyme activities. The total SOC stock increased from 34.25 Mg ha⁻¹ under R0 to 62.15 Mg ha⁻¹ under R 3 , while SOC sequestration rate increased from 0.11 to 1.04 Mg ha⁻¹ year⁻¹. Redundancy analysis revealed strong associations between crop residue input, aggregate stability, aggregate-associated C and N, and SOC and TN stocks. Partial least squares structural equation modeling demonstrated that residue-derived C inputs enhanced SOC and TN stocks primarily through better soil aggregation. These findings underscore long-term residue addition as a viable strategy for improving soil structure, C and N retention, and SOC sequestration in calcareous RWCS under comparable agro-climatic conditions.

title: Genetically supported protein signals and ferroptosis-related cell states in human intervertebral disc degeneration: local pQTL–FinnGen screening integrated with nucleus pulposus single-cell RNA sequencing
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) involves nucleus pulposus (NP) cell dysfunction, inflammatory remodeling, and oxidative stress. Genetic support for circulating protein signals and their cell-type-specific context remains incompletely defined. We integrated deCODE cis-pQTL data with FinnGen R12 M13_INTERVERTEB and human NP scRNA-seq (GSE153066). Local MR screening used harmonized variants with Benjamini–Hochberg correction. The scRNA-seq analysis retained 70,622 cells from 16 libraries and used library-level pseudobulk comparisons. A qPCR validation experiment in PMA-differentiated THP-1 cells (ATCC TIB-202) evaluated MST1, SAA1, BPI, and GCLM under an inflammatory condition. Four multi-SNP signals passed correction: MST1 showed higher endpoint odds (OR = 1.057, q = 4.15 × 10−6), whereas DLK1 (OR = 0.933, q = 0.016), ITIH1 (OR = 0.926, q = 0.016), and SAA1 (OR = 0.927, q = 0.023) showed inverse associations. TP53I3 and BPI remained nominal exploratory signals. TFRC showed a BH-positive single-SNP result (OR = 1.471, q = 0.023). ScRNA-seq resolved eight broad cell populations and demonstrated between-library heterogeneity; nominal macrophage-composition and selected expression differences did not survive within-panel correction. In the qPCR experiment, relative expression was 1.34 for MST1, 0.31 for SAA1, 3.46 for BPI, and 1.70 for GCLM (control = 1.0; n = 4 independent biological replicates/group; all Welch P < 0.001), consistent with the scRNA-seq directions. The study identifies genetically supported protein signals and ferroptosis-related cellular expression patterns while separating genetic screening from transcriptomic localization. The qPCR experiment provides orthogonal experimental support for selected candidate expression changes in the THP-1 inflammatory model.
journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology

title: A bottom-up quantification of greenhouse gas emissions and mitigation potential in Kenya's crop and livestock systems
abstract: Accurate quantification of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from agriculture is critical for establishing credible baselines, identifying emission hotspots, and prioritizing mitigation strategies. In Kenya, most agricultural emission estimates have relied on nationally aggregated activity data and Tier 1 emission factors, which limit the representation of spatial heterogeneity and management effects. This study employed a spatially explicit bottom-up framework that combines IPCC default and default-derived parameters and emission factors, empirical model-derived approaches, and regionally differentiated livestock parameters, integrating subnational production data, management practices, and emission intensities to generate county-level estimates for major crop and livestock systems. In 2021, total agricultural emissions were estimated at 26.74 Mt CO 2 e, with livestock accounting for 22.90 Mt CO 2 e (86%) and crops accounting for 3.83 Mt CO 2 e (14%). Maize represented the largest share of crop emissions (38.9%), while rice exhibited the highest emissions per unit area (3.6 t CO 2 e ha −1 ). Emissions were spatially concentrated, with a small number of counties responsible for a disproportionate share of the national total. Scenario analysis revealed substantial mitigation potential in both sectors. For maize, optimized nitrogen management reduced emissions by 100–140 kg CO 2 e ha −1 , and integrated strategies achieved reductions exceeding 200 kg CO 2 e ha −1 ; in rice the corresponding reductions were 279 and 303 kg CO 2 e ha −1 . In cattle systems, to which the livestock mitigation analysis was restricted, fodder-based and residue-based feeding strategies, as well as anaerobic digestion, demonstrated the highest mitigation potentials, with reductions varying across grazing, mixed, and stall-fed systems. Qualitative marginal abatement comparisons suggest that management-based interventions are relatively low-cost and scalable, while integrated or technology-intensive measures achieve greater reductions but require stronger enabling conditions. These results show that spatially explicit bottom-up accounting improves upon nationally aggregated Tier 1 inventories without constituting a complete Tier 2 assessment and provides a stronger basis for prioritizing mitigation pathways.

title: MR-supported candidate genes and pathway analysis between ischemic stroke and osteoporosis: an integrated multi-omics study
abstract: The global prevalence of ischemic stroke (IS) and osteoporosis (OP) is rising, posing significant public health challenges in aging populations. We aimed to uncover shared genetic factors and elucidate the molecular mechanisms linking IS and OP to identify potential targets for integrated preventive and therapeutic interventions. A comprehensive multi-omics analysis was performed to assess associations and molecular pathways connecting IS and OP. Summary statistics for IS and OP were integrated with expression quantitative trait loci data from the eQTLGen consortium (n = 4,463) to identify common significant single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) related to both diseases. Follow-up transcriptomic profiling and single-cell RNA sequencing were employed to investigate functional pathways, regulatory networks, and cell-type-specific expression patterns associated with these loci. Finally, the expression levels of shared molecules were confirmed using animal models, and subsequent functional analyses were conducted on these genes. Two-sample Mendelian randomization identified FCGR2B and CYBB as exploratory MR-supported candidate genes with shared eQTL instruments. Transcriptome-wide analysis linked these loci to immune-metabolic pathways, including oxidative stress response (FDR = 0.003) and interferon-γ signaling (FDR = 0.01). Mouse-derived ischemic-stroke single-cell RNA-seq provided exploratory cell-type localization: Fcgr2b and Cybb were preferentially enriched in monocytes and macrophages (FDR < 0.05), whereas Sirt1 was predominantly localized to endothelial cells and tissue stem cells in the diseased mouse microenvironment. Of note, the osteoporosis single-cell dataset (GSE147287) contained only one OP patient, and its cell-type patterns should therefore be interpreted as exploratory case observations rather than generalized findings. Regulatory network analysis identified the cisbp:M1399 transcription factor motif (NES = 4.12) with the highest enrichment score, which is predicted to separately regulate the transcription of FCGR2B, CYBB and SIRT1 . Pathway enrichment analysis revealed metabolic reprogramming (AUC = 0.78, p=0.004) as a key mechanistic node differentiating high-and low-expression cell groups. The expression levels of the shared molecules were validated in a mouse model. This multi-omics study implicates immune-metabolic dysregulation as a shared pathological feature of ischemic stroke and osteoporosis. FCGR2B , CYBB and SIRT1 are exploratory MR-supported candidate genes putatively associated with both diseases, offering potential clues for dual-purpose preventive and therapeutic strategies for age-related IS-OP comorbidity.

title: A humanized eNAMPT -neutralizing monoclonal antibody reduces cancer-induced bone pain and osteoclastogenesis in murine breast cancer model
abstract: Cancer-induced bone pain (CIBP) is a common symptom among patients with metastasized cancer, however, health professionals often face challenges in managing patients’ pain. Extracellular nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (eNAMPT) is a DAMP overexpressed in metastatic breast carcinoma that binds to Toll-Like Receptor 4 (TLR4) to potentially trigger a signaling cascade through Nuclear Factor kappa β (NFk- β ) inducing inflammation, osteoclastogenesis, and contributing to CIBP. To assess the impact of eNAMPT on CIBP and to identify alternative therapeutic options, ALT-100, an eNAMPT-neutralizing monoclonal antibody, was tested in murine and cell-based models. First, eNAMPT synthesis and secretion by EO771 breast adenocarcinoma cells and its modulation by ALT-100 were assessed using eNAMPT ELISA. Next, recombinant eNAMPT-induced osteoclastogenesis and its inhibition by ALT-100 were evaluated in RAW 264.7 osteoclast precursor cells using TRAP staining. In vivo , female C57BL/6J mice underwent intramedullary femoral injection of EO771 cells to establish CIBP or SHAM surgery. One week later, mice received ALT-100 (4 mg/kg, ip) or saline control, followed by longitudinal assessment of pain-related behaviors and femoral radiographs. The eNAMPT ELISA assay revealed that EO771 cells synthesize and secrete eNAMPT in a time-dependent manner maximal at 48 h, which were reduced by ALT-100 mAb. In RAW 264.7 cells, recombinant eNAMPT significantly increased TRAP activity, while co-administration of ALT-100 significantly reduced this effect. In the murine CIBP model, ALT-100 significantly reduced pain-related behaviors compared to saline control mice in the cancer group. Moreover, radiographic analysis demonstrated that ALT-100 mitigates cancer-induced bone loss. These data show that ALT-100 exhibits antinociceptive effects in a CIBP murine model and inhibits eNAMPT-induced osteoclast differentiation. Our results indicate that blockade of eNAMPT can potentially serve as an alternative clinical strategy for treating CIBP.

title: Improving farm productivity and profitability through AI diffusion: evidence from Punjab, Pakistan
abstract: Agriculture remains central to Pakistan's economy, with Punjab accounting for the largest share of national crop production. Despite the rapid global advancement of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled agricultural technologies, their diffusion across farms in developing economies remains uneven and underexplored. This study examines the extent of AI diffusion among farmers in Punjab, Pakistan, and assesses its associations with perceived farm productivity and profitability. Drawing on Diffusion of Innovations (DoI) theory, complemented by the Resource-Based View (RBV) and the Technology-Organisation-Environment (TOE) framework, the study adopts a quantitative, cross-sectional design using survey data from 101 farmers. The findings indicate that while awareness and perceived benefits of AI are relatively high, actual adoption remains moderate (AI Diffusion: M = 18.27, SD = 3.71), indicating a gap between perceived value and implementation. AI diffusion was positively correlated with perceived farm productivity ( r = 0.617, p < 0.001) and perceived farm profitability ( r = 0.607, p < 0.001). The findings therefore demonstrate statistically significant associations between greater AI diffusion and stronger perceived farm performance, while not establishing causal effects. The observed perception-adoption gap is consistent with structural barriers identified in previous research, including high investment costs, limited digital infrastructure and technical capability constraints. The study contributes context-specific evidence on digital agriculture in a developing economy by jointly examining AI diffusion, productivity and profitability. The findings highlight the importance of infrastructure, institutional support and capability development in facilitating wider and more effective adoption of AI-enabled agricultural technologies.

title: Deep learning–based pavement crack classification and road condition assessment for intelligent transportation infrastructure
abstract: Efficient maintenance of road infrastructure is essential for ensuring traffic safety, preserving pavement serviceability, and supporting the long-term sustainability of transportation networks. However, conventional pavement inspection mainly relies on manual visual assessment, which is time-consuming, costly, and subjective. This study proposes a deep learning–based framework for automated pavement crack classification and road condition assessment. The proposed framework uses real-world pavement images collected through the Multifunctional Pavement Assessment System (SMAC). Transfer learning was applied using ResNet50 and EfficientNet-B0 architectures to classify six pavement surface categories. Data augmentation and weighted cross-entropy loss were employed to improve robustness and address class imbalance. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrix analysis. A Road Condition Index (RCI) was then formulated from the classification results to support maintenance prioritization. EfficientNet-B0 achieved an overall classification accuracy of 89.8%, outperforming ResNet50 (73.3%). It obtained F1-scores of 0.92 for alligator and longitudinal cracks, 0.93 for transverse cracks, and 1.00 for non-cracked pavement surfaces. The proposed RCI successfully differentiated pavement degradation levels and supported maintenance prioritization. The proposed framework provides an intelligent, interpretable, and practical solution for pavement crack classification, road condition assessment, and maintenance-oriented decision support. These results demonstrate the potential of deep learning for scalable pavement monitoring and more efficient infrastructure management within intelligent transportation systems.

title: The effect of rural tourism on rural prosperity: evidence from China on agricultural labor productivity, incomes, and household food consumption
abstract: Policy support in China has disproportionately favored rural tourism as a core pillar of rural revitalization. However, its net effect on agricultural labor productivity, rural income, and household consumption remains empirically untested. This study examines how rural tourism expenditure affects these three dimensions of rural prosperity and evaluates alternative policy instruments to maximize developmental benefits. The analysis employs a dynamic autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) simulation model using annual Chinese data from 1994 to 2023. The findings reveal that an increase in rural tourism expenditure significantly reduces agricultural labor productivity, rural household income, and rural household consumption in both the short run and the long run. A positive shock to rural tourism expenditure similarly generates a negative response across all three outcomes, with the effects persisting over the forecast horizon. These results suggest that the net effect of rural tourism expansion on rural prosperity is consistently negative, challenging the conventional assumption that rural tourism serves as an unconditional driver of rural development. The findings call for conditional tourism subsidies, complementary investments in agricultural capital, and spatially differentiated rural development policies that safeguard agricultural livelihoods while permitting tourism to develop only where it does not displace farming.

title: How institutional digitalization reshapes entrepreneurial activity in new agricultural business forms: quasi-natural experimental evidence from China's Digital Village Pilot Policy
abstract: New agricultural business forms are a key driving force for developing countries to overcome the constraints of traditional agriculture and achieve sustainability in food systems. However, it remains unclear whether institutional digitalization can effectively stimulate entrepreneurial vitality in new agricultural business forms. This study develops a theoretical framework of “opportunity creation–opportunity identification–opportunity transformation” and treats China's Digital Village Pilot Policy (DVPP), implemented in 2020, as a quasi-natural experiment. Based on panel data from 1,743 counties in China from 2014 to 2023, this study employs Double Machine Learning (DML) and Spatial Durbin Difference-in-Differences (SDM-DID) models, among other methods, to systematically identify the impact, transmission mechanisms, heterogeneous effects, and spatial spillover effects of institutional digitalization on Entrepreneurial Activity in New Agricultural Business Forms (EANA). The results reveal that: (1) DVPP significantly enhances EANA, and this finding remains robust after a series of tests, including placebo tests, Propensity Score Matching–Difference-in-Differences (PSM-DID), Synthetic Control Method–Difference-in-Differences (SCM-DID), and instrumental variable (IV) estimation; (2) agricultural technological innovation, digital infrastructure development, and digital financial development serve as mediating mechanisms; (3) the policy effects are more pronounced in counties with higher levels of digital access, better-developed transportation infrastructure, and higher levels of digital financial development, exhibiting a pattern of Central > Western > Eastern regions, and are significantly stronger in areas with advantages in characteristic agricultural products; (4) DVPP generates a significant negative spatial spillover effect on EANA in neighboring counties. This study expands theoretical understanding of the relationship between institutional digitalization and entrepreneurship in new agricultural business forms and provides empirical evidence for China and other developing countries to optimize digital rural development and foster new agricultural business forms.

title: Turning dirt into gold: the business case of soil carbon for agrarian pathways in arid climate
abstract: Agricultural carbon sequestration offers considerable potential for mitigating anthropogenic climate change, particularly in the low-organic-carbon soils of the Middle East. This study presents a foundational scenario-based assessment of soil carbon sequestration and economic feasibility. Crop production and market datasets from Jordanian statistics (1998–2023) were used to estimate potential soil carbon sequestration and economic performance. Using benchmarks from literature in comparable agroecological regions, four soil carbon management practices were evaluated across multiple crops for their carbon storage potential using Monte Carlo uncertainty and sensitivity analysis. Sensitivity of economic performance was assessed under optimistic/pessimistic scenarios. Among the evaluated practices, the highest carbon sequestration rate was achieved through increased Soil Organic Carbon (SOC), reaching a maximum of 27.44 metric tons of CO₂ per hectare per year (tCO₂/ha/year) under the high scenario for cucumbers. In contrast, barley showed the highest sequestration rate at 0.45 tCO₂/ha/year under increased SOC in the high scenario. Sensitivity analysis showed that ±20% uncertainty in the management coefficients resulted in practice-specific changes of 1.11 tCO₂/ha/year for increased SOC and 0.46 tCO₂/ha/year for improved cropland management. Horticultural crops, particularly cucumbers and lemons, exhibited the highest sequestration rates and strongest responses to management interventions. Field crops such as wheat, barley, and olives demonstrated lower, more stable sequestration rates. Economic analysis revealed that cucumbers, grapes, potatoes, and Open-field farming (OFF) tomatoes achieved the highest tri-pillar performance (net and adjusted profits and break-even cost) alongside effective carbon sequestration. These findings highlight that crop choice is a primary determinant of both crop profitability and sequestrated carbon potential and feasibility, with significant implications for climate-smart agriculture, carbon credit mechanisms, and intensification strategies in data-scarce regions. While empirical field validation remains a future priority, this model-based study provides a screening-level theoretical baseline to guide targeted research and investment in arid agricultural systems.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns, regional differences, and influencing factors of the integration of digital economy and agricultural industry in China
abstract: The integration of digital economy and agricultural industry (IDEAI) is a crucial pathway for promoting rural revitalization and building a strong agricultural sector. This paper explores the intrinsic mechanisms of IDEAI and constructs an evaluation index system. Using the CRITIC weighting method, Dagum Gini coefficient, and GTWR model, it analyzes the level and influencing factors of IDEAI in China from 2013 to 2022. The results show: (1) The level of IDEAI has been continuously rising, but the overall level remains relatively low. Spatially, it generally exhibits a pattern where the eastern region leads, while the central and western regions strive to catch up. (2) The overall disparity in the level of IDEAI shows a declining trend. There exists a mutually reinforcing dynamic interactive effect between agricultural digital industrialization (ADI) and agricultural industrial digitalization (AID). Inter-regional differences being the primary cause of the overall disparity. (3) Technological innovation, market demand, and government guidance were positively associated with IDEAI. Financial services had a time-varying association: positive before 2018 and weaker or negative thereafter. Scale operation was negatively associated with IDEAI in the baseline specification, although this relationship may be nonlinear. Accelerating the integrated development of IDEAI still requires continuous efforts to promote the coupling of policies, markets, capital, and technology, establish cross-regional cooperation mechanisms, and achieve coordinated development across all regions.

title: Digital technology, agricultural resilience, and food security: a mini review
abstract: Digital technologies are increasingly deployed to strengthen food security under climate stress, resource constraints, and geopolitical disruption. This review synthesizes two largely separate bodies of scholarship: an international literature on digital agriculture and the four classical dimensions of food security, and a rapidly expanding Chinese literature on the digital economy and agricultural economic resilience. Three claims emerge. First, digital technologies strengthen all four dimensions of food security through distinct mechanisms: (1) availability through productivity and input-use efficiency gains, which operate mainly through institutional intermediation, including land transfer, socialized services, industrial integration, and human capital, rather than through adoption alone; (2) access through market information and digital finance; (3) stability through traceability, early-warning systems, and insurance; (4) and utilization through traceability, nutrition information, and mobile payments. Second, quasi-experimental evidence shows that digital infrastructure, digital finance, and artificial intelligence raise the resilience of grain production and value chains, mainly through socialized services, land transfer, industrial integration, and human capital rather than adoption alone. Third, the benefits are conditional and unevenly distributed: the direction of spatial spillovers depends on absorptive capacity, market integration, and factor mobility.

title: Agricultural Machinery Socialization Services and the Spatial Allocation of Grain Output Relative to Cultivated Land Area: Evidence from China
abstract: The spatial allocation of grain output relative to cultivated land resources is important for understanding regional grain production patterns. This study uses panel data from 30 Chinese provinces during 2010–2022 to examine the relationship between agricultural machinery socialization services (AMSS) and the relative spatial allocation index (RSAI). The results show that (i) areas with higher levels of AMSS and RSAI are mostly in the east, while those with lower levels are mainly in the west; (ii) AMSS is positively associated with RSAI, with the share of the three major staple grains in the cropping structure (SGS) and planting and harvesting mechanization alignment (PHMA) serving as two mediating channels that generate positive indirect effects; (iii) the positive effect of AMSS is significant across all quantiles, with stronger effects at the lower quantiles. Regional heterogeneity analysis further indicates a stronger positive association between AMSS and RSAI in the central-eastern region (CER) and the Major Grain Production Area (MGPA); and (iv) the SAR model yields a positive indirect effect at the 10% significance level, providing qualified support for spatial spillovers. These findings provide empirical evidence for understanding the relative spatial allocation of grain output and formulating regionally differentiated agricultural machinery service policies.

title: How Does the Adoption of Digital and Intelligent Technologies Affect Farmers’ Farmland Rental-In Behavior? Evidence from Grain-Growing Farmers in China
abstract: Farmland rental is an important means of optimizing agricultural land allocation and promoting appropriately scaled farming. Against the backdrop of accelerating digital and intelligent transformation in agricultural, how digital and intelligent technology (DIT) adoption relates to farmers’ farmland rental-in behavior require clear theoretical explanation and empirical validation. Using 2024 survey data from 385 grain-growing farmers in Jiangsu Province, China, this study examines the relationship between DIT adoption and farmland rental-in behavior using Probit, endogenous switching regression, IV-Probit, and conditional mixed-process models. The results show that DIT adoption is significantly and positively associated with both farmland rental-in decisions and rented-in scale. These findings remain robust across alternative samples and estimation specifications. Heterogeneity analyses indicate that this positive association is more pronounced for production-oriented than information-oriented DIT applications, for farms with larger baseline operational scales than smallholders, and for households with lower aging ratios. Mechanism analyses suggest that DIT adoption corresponds to farmland rental-in primarily through labor substitution effects and transaction cost reductions in rural land markets. This study extends farmland rental research to the context of agricultural digitalization, offering empirical insights for advancing digital agriculture, improving farmland rental markets, and fostering appropriately scaled farming operations.

title: RGB UAV Imagery for Crop Monitoring and Decision Support in Precision Agriculture
abstract: Digitalization and data-driven decision-making are transforming modern agriculture, where rapid and high-resolution assessment of crop condition is essential for optimizing field interventions. Multispectral approaches such as satellite-derived normalized difference vegetation index are widely used; however, their spatial resolution and temporal availability may limit the detection of fine-scale variability within agricultural fields. This study investigates the capability of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-acquired red, green, and blue (RGB) imagery to provide relevant information regarding crop condition. Two autumn crops, wheat and rapeseed, located in Olt County, Romania, were analyzed. The acquired images were processed photogrammetrically to generate orthomosaics, followed by the extraction of vegetation indices derived from the visible spectrum, namely Excess Green Index and Visible Atmospherically Resistant Index. Both indices provided meaningful information on vegetation condition, with the latter exhibiting enhanced sensitivity to intra-field variability. The UAV-derived Excess Green Index and Visible Atmospherically Resistant Index maps revealed spatial variability that was not equally distinguishable in the satellite Normalized Difference Vegetation Index data, particularly for the wheat crop. Individually, the two RGB vegetation indices classified approximately 16% of each analyzed field as vulnerable. These vulnerable regions represent relative, image-based spectral anomalies rather than independently validated indicators of physiological crop stress, nutrient deficiency, or yield loss. Following rule-based fusion and the removal of isolated detections, 21.55% of the wheat field and 19.75% of the rapeseed field were identified as spatially coherent vulnerable areas. The resulting maps were subsequently converted into machinery-oriented candidate intervention zones, supporting an illustrative simulation of how spatially differentiated field information could be integrated into conventional agricultural equipment. These findings demonstrate that UAV-based RGB imagery can provide spatially explicit information for crop monitoring and can support the identification of candidate areas for subsequent field verification and precision-agriculture decision-making.

title: Development of an IoT-Driven Smart Agricultural Management System Using Mecanum Drive Robotic Arm Manipulators for Precision Farming: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT), robotics, and artificial intelligence have only recently converged in agriculture, driven by the need for sustainable, resilient food systems. Precision farming demands real-time physical action, not just data-driven insight, yet existing agricultural robotic systems rarely integrate omnidirectional mobility, dexterous manipulation, and environmental awareness for complex tasks in unstructured farming environments. This systematic literature review examines the state of the art in IoT-enabled smart agricultural management systems that combine Mecanum-wheel mobile platforms with multi-degree-of-freedom (DoF) robotic arm manipulators. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we analysed 81 peer-reviewed articles (2015–2025) from Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore. By design, every included study employs Mecanum-wheel mobility, since this was a required inclusion criterion; this reflects our deliberately narrow scope rather than the adoption rate of Mecanum wheels in agricultural robotics generally, which the wider excluded literature suggests remains comparatively low. We synthesise key mathematical models, Mecanum inverse/forward kinematics, 6-DoF Jacobian matrices, LoRaWAN link budget analysis, and closed-loop PID control across sensing, mobility, manipulation, integration, and validation. This synthesis reveals five recurring limitations: poor terrain adaptability of Mecanum rollers in muddy fields, communication latency exceeding 1 s in long-range protocols, absent force feedback in most manipulator designs, and 28–42% performance degradation under field versus laboratory conditions. Few studies report true closed-loop operation where sensor data directly triggers robotic action, and smallholder farmers, particularly in developing economies such as Nigeria, remain excluded from these technologies due to cost, energy, and usability barriers. To address these gaps, we propose a modular system architecture featuring solar-assisted Mecanum mobility, a 6-DoF force-controlled arm with quick-change end-effectors, hybrid LoRaWAN/Wi-Fi 6 communication, edge AI (NVIDIA Jetson), and a multilingual cloud dashboard laying a foundation for scalable, inclusive agricultural robotics. This proposed architecture is a conceptual direction motivated by the review’s findings and is not itself an empirical outcome of the systematic review.

title: Method-Based Multi-Objective Parameter Co-Calibration of Dryland Wheat Yield and Protein Content
abstract: Water and nitrogen availability jointly influence dryland wheat yield and grain protein formation; the ability of crop models to simulate the synergistic effects of these two factors depends on the accuracy of key parameters. However, the large number of model parameters and their complex interactions make parameter screening and calibration challenging. In this study, the model was calibrated using annual yield records for dryland wheat in Anding District, Dingxi City, and Gansu Province, from 2015 to 2019, along with field observation data (grain protein content) from Anjiagou Village, Fengxiang Town, and Anding District, collected during the same period. The model was then validated using independent data from two growing seasons (2020–2021) in the same study area. Based on the Agricultural Production sIMulator Next-Generation (APSIM NG) and using water–nitrogen response as the foundation, a multi-objective parameter calibration framework was developed with yield and grain protein content as calibration targets. The extended Fourier amplitude test (EFAST) was used to screen key model parameters, and the performance of the DREAM–zs algorithm, the Nelder–Mead simplex algorithm, and the multi-objective rime optimization algorithm (MORIME) in calibrating these parameters was compared and analyzed. All three algorithms reduced the simulation error in yield; for grain protein content, the Nelder–Mead and MORIME algorithms reduced the simulation error, while DREAM-zs did not. The simulation accuracy of the Nelder–Mead and MORIME algorithms was generally similar, but MORIME yielded a set of Pareto solutions that characterized the trade-off between the simulation accuracy of yield and grain protein content; therefore, its parameter solutions were selected for independent validation. The validation results showed that the RMSE for yield decreased from 248.45 kg hm−2 to 213.90 kg hm−2, and the NRMSE decreased from 12.60% to 10.85%; for grain protein content, the RMSE decreased from 0.280% to 0.250%, and the NRMSE decreased from 1.86% to 1.66%. Furthermore, the incorporation of parallel computing reduced MORIME’s runtime by 82.99%. The study demonstrates that MORIME with parallel computing can provide methodological support for the multi-objective, efficient optimization of crop model parameters.

title: Temporal Multi-Scale Spatio-Temporal Network (TMST): Polarization–Temporal Feature Selection and Multi-Scale Spatiotemporal Fusion for Crop Mapping
abstract: Accurate and timely crop mapping supports agricultural resource management, yield prediction, and food security decision-making. In this study, we propose the Temporal Multi-scale Spatio-Temporal Network (TMST), a crop mapping method that integrates multi-source remote sensing time series through polarization–temporal feature selection and multi-scale spatiotemporal fusion. TMST combines Sentinel-1 dual-polarization synthetic aperture radar (SAR), Sentinel-2 multispectral data, and vegetation indices. Its Temporal Feature Importance Explainer (TFIExplainer) selects informative polarization–time features, the Multi-Scale Attention Aggregation (MSAA) module enhances spatial representations, and the Spatio-Temporal Feature Encoder (STFE) models long-range spatial dependencies and phenological dynamics; a composite loss improves minority-class and difficult-pixel recognition. On the Xinxiang dataset, TMST achieved an overall accuracy (OA) of 0.8625 and a mean F1-score (mF1) of 0.8329. Module and data-source ablations suggested benefits of the combined modules and multi-source fusion, while a cropland mask reduced non-cropland misclassification. In direct cross-dataset evaluation, models trained on a self-constructed Austrian dataset and tested on the radar-extended Panoptic Agricultural Satellite Time Series (PASTIS-R) dataset showed that TMST outperformed the evaluated baselines under the specified source–target setting. Annual mapping of Xinxiang for 2019–2023, using year-specific samples and independently trained models, provided map-based estimates of regional cropping structures and spatial patterns. Under the evaluated settings, TMST provides an effective approach to crop classification and annually updated crop mapping.

title: Estimation of Soil Water Content in Winter Wheat Field at Jointing Stage Using Multi-Source Features and Machine Learning
abstract: Accurate and timely monitoring of soil water content (SWC) plays an essential supporting role in crop irrigation management and smart agricultural practice. Remote sensing technology provides rapid and convenient approaches to large-scale farmland SWC estimation or inversion. However, existing mechanistic modeling methods are limited by parameter localization and land surface heterogeneity, while machine learning data-driven methods lack quite good physical interpretability. To address deficiencies in single data-driven methods and single vegetation microwave scattering models, and explore the estimation effect of different feature variables in machine learning. This study proposes an innovative estimation model that integrates machine learning strategies and multi-source features, including spectral indices and features derived from the classic water cloud model (WCM). The novelty of the proposed model lies in balancing physical interpretability and data-driven accuracy, namely extracting relevant soil backscattering parameters through WCM, which are then used as input features in the machine learning. A combination of field-measured data and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) multi-source remote sensing data, including multispectral and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data, was acquired synchronously at the jointing stage of winter wheat. Through extracting variables such as the SAR microwave backscattering coefficient and the optical vegetation index, and conducting feature screening and parameter sensitivity analysis, we optimized the input variable sets of models based on back-propagation (BP) neural network, support vector regression (SVR) and random forest (RF) algorithms. The study results showed that the established estimation model had excellent estimation performance, especially for the RF algorithm, with the highest R2 of 0.855, lowest MAE of 0.0212 cm3/cm3, and lowest RMSE of 0.0253 cm3/cm3. It was also shown that different feature input schemes have obvious effects on SWC estimation performance. On the whole, RF had the best estimation accuracy, followed by SVR and then BPNN. This study demonstrated that models integrating multi-source remote sensing data and machine learning could enhance SWC estimation ability for winter wheat fields, and could also serve as a promising approach for SWC monitoring in winter wheat fields in the North China Plain.

title: Fusion and Feature Selection of Frozen Foundation Models for In-the-Wild Plant Disease Recognition
abstract: Image-based recognition can help growers diagnose plant diseases early. Classifiers trained on laboratory leaf images, however, lose accuracy on field photographs. Frozen foundation models provide features for field photographs, but fusing several of them increases the feature dimension. In this study, we concatenated the features of ten frozen backbones from five pretraining families into a 9472-dimensional vector. We reduced this vector to the size of one backbone by feature selection or projection and classified it with a linear probe. The main results on three field datasets are means over 30 repetitions. On the official PlantWild test split, early fusion reached 81.4% accuracy and late fusion 81.7%, against 76.7% for the best single backbone. To our knowledge, these are the highest accuracies reported on this split. L1-penalized feature selection to 1536 dimensions reached 80.6%, compared with 80.2% for the previous best method at 2816 dimensions. On PlantWild, L1 selection took its largest shares from the backbones that contributed most, whereas relevance filters concentrated on two backbones that contributed less. Removing the two backbones that L1 selection used least lowered the macro-averaged F1 score by at most 0.002 on any dataset and left eight backbones at inference.

title: Requirements Engineering with Generative AI: A Systematic Literature Review of Using AI Agents for Requirements Engineering Automation
abstract: Requirements development is a critical phase of software development, as the requirements developed during this phase provide the foundation for subsequent project activities. Because software requirements are predominantly expressed in natural language, automation of requirements engineering (RE) activities has historically been challenging. Recent advances in the natural language processing capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs), however, have created new opportunities for automating RE tasks through AI agents. Accordingly, research on LLM-supported, agent-based RE automation has grown substantially in recent years. This study presents the results of a literature review of research on LLM-supported agent-based automation of software requirements engineering. The review identified 50 studies, of which 24 propose or describe agent-based architectures for RE automation, while the remaining 26 introduce benchmarks, baselines, evaluation environments, or comparative approaches for assessing agent-based solutions. The 24 studies describing an agent-based architecture are classified according to the requirements activities defined in the Software Requirements knowledge area of SWEBOK V4.0a, namely requirements elicitation, analysis, specification, validation, and tracing. Our analysis identifies the dominant agent architectures employed across RE activities, recurring design patterns, evaluation approaches, and key limitations of agent-based RE systems. Although significant advances have been made, several critical challenges remain, including hallucinations, scalability, and the lack of standardized evaluation frameworks. These findings highlight important directions for future research toward reliable, scalable, and systematically evaluated AI agent-based automation of software requirements engineering.

title: Dynamic Response Mechanism of Retaining Structures of Soft-Soil Foundation Pits Subjected to Traffic Loads
abstract: Urban soft soils exhibit high compressibility, low shear strength, and significant rheological characteristics, making roadside foundation pits highly susceptible to cyclic traffic disturbances. Repeated vehicle excitation easily induces abnormal deformation and internal force variation in retaining structures, threatening pit stability. To clarify the quantitative response mechanism of soft-soil foundation pits under multi-parameter traffic loads, this study establishes a refined three-dimensional numerical model using PLAXIS 3D Advanced CONNECT Edition V22, based on a typical coastal soft-soil excavation project in Guangdong Province. Different from previous simplified traffic-load simulations, the numerical model incorporated the soil small-strain stiffness constitutive model and realized the coupling of groundwater seepage and dynamic load fields. The influences of four key parameters, namely excavation depth, static vehicle load, dynamic load amplitude, and load frequency, on the deformation and internal force evolution of retaining walls were systematically analyzed. Quantitatively, the traffic-load contribution ratio averaged 27.86% for the additional structural responses. Parametric comparison shows that excavation depth dominates the bending moment response, while static vehicle load is the primary factor controlling wall deformation. Dynamic load amplitude and frequency produce relatively minor and comparable influences. Based on a clear decomposition method of static and dynamic load effects, static vehicle load accounts for 80–90% of the total structural response (wall displacement and bending moment), whereas the dynamic increment induced by pavement unevenness only contributes 10–20%. This study clarifies the differentiated contribution mechanism of multi-factor traffic loads and provides a scientific reference for dynamic simulation, structural optimization, and construction risk control of urban soft-soil foundation pits under vehicle cyclic loads.

title: Genome-Wide Association Mapping of Low-Nitrogen Tolerance in Hexaploid Oat Identifies a Suggestive Candidate Locus near P5CDH Associated with Root Dry Weight
abstract: Background/Objectives: Optimizing nitrogen fertilizer efficiency is crucial for sustainable agriculture, but the genetic basis of low-nitrogen (LN) tolerance in oat (Avena sativa L.), an important forage and grain crop, remains poorly characterized. Methods: This study investigated eleven LN tolerance phenotypes across 103 oat accessions using high-density resequencing markers, mixed-model association mapping (MLM), a FarmCPU sensitivity analysis, and Bayesian genetic architecture inference (BSLMM). Results: No locus achieved genome-wide Bonferroni significance, and Bayesian estimates indicated a low-to-moderate model-based PVE (0.10–0.23) with no clearly identified major-effect locus, suggesting that genomic selection represents a plausible future direction for LN tolerance in oat. At a suggestive threshold (p < 1 × 10−5), a cross-model intersection nominated a hypothesis-generating locus at 1D:349,799,042 associated with root dry weight. This locus showed haplotype-level phenotypic segregation (Wilcoxon p = 1.36 × 10−5) on the discovery panel and concordant signals between the two models (r = 0.92). The nearest nitrogen-metabolism-related gene, P5CDH (22.7 kb away), encodes Δ1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate dehydrogenase, which catalyses the terminal step of proline catabolism, and its wheat ortholog was significantly down-regulated under nitrogen deficiency. Conclusions: These findings provide a testable hypothesis linking proline catabolism to oat root plasticity under low nitrogen and a framework for validation in larger panels.

title: Predictive Modelling of the Surface Microgeometry of Laser-Modified Biocompatible Ti-TiB2 Powder Metallurgy-Based Composites
abstract: This paper deals with the surface functionalization of a biocompatible powder metallurgy-based Ti-TiB2 composite prepared by spark plasma sintering, utilizing a nanosecond fibre laser operating at a wavelength of 1064 nm in an ambient atmosphere. The effects of laser pulse energy (Ep), longitudinal laser beam spot overlap (OL), and transverse spot overlap (OT) on the integrity of laser-treated surfaces were investigated using a Box–Behnken experimental design to identify how these process parameters govern the amplitude and spatial roughness metrics strongly correlated with surface osseointegration. Statistical learning-driven analyses were performed to evaluate the predictability and overall functional dependency of the observed data, including Ordinary Least-Squares and regularized linear regression analyses, analysis of variance, and model evaluation using two approaches: first, by training and testing on the entire dataset to assess the in-sample fit, and second, via Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation to evaluate the model’s generalization performance. An underlying linear dependency was demonstrated for Rsm with predictors Ep and OL, and no statistical significance was found for the predictor OT. For Rsm, the model retained moderate predictive performance under LOOCV, despite the limited number of independent experimental observations.

title: Wool–Poly(lactic acid) Biocomposite Mats as Degradable Sulphur Carriers: Effects on Forage Elemental Composition and Material Degradation
abstract: Low-grade sheep wool is an underused, keratin-rich by-product whose cystine-derived sulphur could be returned to agricultural soils. Carded wool was bonded with sprayed poly(lactic acid) (PLA) hot-melt to obtain porous wool–PLA biocomposite mats, which were exposed in field soil, in a pasture-grass composter and under soil-free outdoor conditions. The elemental composition of the wool, soil, forage, composting material and exposed mats was determined by ICP-OES after 60 days of exposure; each reported value is the mean of at least three analytical determinations, whereas the field layout comprised one plot per treatment. Forage from the plot with buried mats contained 47.8% more S and 21.9% more K than forage from the untreated plot, whereas Ca, Mg, B and Mo concentrations were lower; because the plots were not replicated, these differences are reported as preliminary observations rather than as demonstrated treatment effects. After composting, the mats retained only 17–23% of their initial storage modulus between −30 and 50 °C, while the relaxation of the PLA phase shifted by 7–10 °C towards higher temperatures. The water contact angle decreased from 72.3 ± 10.0° to 55.7 ± 12.1° (six droplets on one mat per condition), while the stylus roughness did not change appreciably. Digital microscopy revealed swelling, fissuring, cavities and fibre exposure along wool–PLA interfaces. A coupled mechanism of PLA ester hydrolysis and keratinolytic release of sulphur is proposed as a working hypothesis that is consistent with, but not yet proven by, the present data. The results support wool–PLA mats as temporary, degradable carriers of keratin-bound sulphur; replicated field trials with yield, nutrient uptake and soil measurements, together with direct degradation markers, are required before any fertilising or soil-improving effect can be claimed.

title: Integrated Molecular and Physiological Mechanisms Underlying Rice Adaptation to Heat, Salinity, and Drought Stress
abstract: Rice faces increasing threats from climate change, driven by heat, salinity, and drought stresses. Although researchers have extensively studied individual stresses, growing evidence indicates that combined stresses elicit unique physiological, biochemical, and molecular responses that single-stress studies cannot predict. This review comprehensively synthesizes current knowledge of the integrated signaling networks and adaptive mechanisms underlying rice responses to heat, salinity, and drought stress, with particular emphasis on stress crosstalk and multi-stress responses. We examine the roles of mechanosensitive ion channels, calcium signaling, salt overly sensitive (SOS) pathway, heat shock response regulators, mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascades, and ABA-dependent and -independent signaling networks in stress tolerance systems. Furthermore, we discuss major adaptive responses involving reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis, osmoprotectant accumulation, antioxidant defense systems, and phytohormone crosstalk involving abscisic acid, auxin, salicylic acid, cytokinin, brassinosteroids, ethylene, and gibberellins. Particular attention is given to the detrimental effects of combined stresses on growth, development, and yield. In addition, recent advances in enhancing stress tolerance through CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing, marker-assisted breeding, and molecular marker technologies are also highlighted. Despite significant progress, critical knowledge gaps remain regarding primary stress-sensing mechanisms, epigenetic stress memory, organelle-specific signaling, and the translation of laboratory findings to field conditions. By integrating current knowledge across molecular, physiological, and breeding perspectives, we provide a comprehensive integrated signaling network model and crosstalk among signaling pathways for understanding rice adaptation to combined stresses and highlight potential strategies for enhancing crop resilience and global food security.

title: Analysis of Sea Cliff Erosion Measured Using UAV Photogrammetry
abstract: The erosion of coastal chalk cliffs is a significant concern for communities in Northern Europe, with rates of retreat varying widely depending on local conditions. This study presents six years of UAV photogrammetry monitoring of chalk cliffs in Sussex, UK, producing 2.5D change detection maps to quantify erosion at Telscombe and Peacehaven. The results demonstrate a strong correlation between rates of lower-cliff erosion and wave energy at Peacehaven, with an r2 value of 0.82. However, periods of intensive mass-wasting can render these relationships unreliable. The relationship for Telscombe, which experiences much more mass-wasting, demonstrates an r2 of 0.37, which improves to 0.48 with the removal of an outlier. Cumulative erosion patterns follow a gradualistic trend, superimposed by episodic mass-wasting, with lower-cliff erosion rates increasing by approximately 3.2 times during storm-forced high-energy intervals compared to stable periods. A similar pattern is seen for mass-wasting events, although erosion intensities may be more than 6 times greater during periods of storminess. These findings highlight the role of storminess in accelerating erosion in the coastal zone.
