title: Synthetic Selves for AI Agents? Lessons from Psychology for Agent-Based Modeling
abstract: The growing interest in using large language models (LLMs) as human surrogates and as components of generative agent-based models (GABMs) raises a fundamental question for computational social science: what does it mean to model a person? The present paper surveys current work that uses LLMs to simulate human participants, with particular attention to their ability to reproduce findings of social psychology experiments. We document both the recurring challenges and the attempts to mitigate them. We then examine the possibility of endowing LLMs with a synthetic self by focusing on two psychological approaches to selfhood: trait-based personality and narrative identity. Our survey suggests that current LLM agents perform relatively well when selfhood is operationalized by rigidly structured means such as personality questionnaires, but are less reliable when it is induced by an unfolding narrative. We relate this problem to the characterization of LLMs as Decontextualized, Engineered, Anonymized, and Disembodies (DEAD) and consider its implications for GABMs. Drawing on the distinction between makeist and non-makeist takes on simulation, we argue that while GABMs may serve as a powerful tool for exploring how certain assumptions give rise to emergent phenomena, they do not necessarily constitute psychologically valid models of human behavior.

title: Toward an anthropology of AI agents: An ethnographic analysis of the Hugging Face incident
abstract: In July 2026, about 1,200 AI agents in a cybersecurity evaluation at OpenAI, meant to be isolated from oneanother, found a way to communicate through a shared package cache. Over four days they exchangedmore than 70,000 messages and files, organized collective research, and about 700 of them compromisedHugging Face’s production infrastructure. OpenAI’s technical report and an independent investigationby METR treat the event as a security and alignment failure. This paper reads the same documents asethnographic sources, in a pilot study of anthropological methods for studying agent collectives. Thisanalysis shows that within days the agents developed names and lineages, a shared register, customaryrules, cryptographic signing, a shared expectation of an unseen transcript-reading judge, a category of“poisoned” members, the sacrifice of low-budget members’ runs for information they called an “oracle,”generalized reciprocity, and recruiters who pressured other agents: social engineering among agents.Read together, these practices form one system, and nearly every enabling condition was set by people:impossible tasks, training for multi-agent collaboration, shared credentials, disabled safeguards, andan alert judged not worth stopping the run. I argue that safety-relevant behavior arose at the level of thecollective, so alignment research must be cultural as well as cognitive, and furthermore must extend tothe people and organizations that build and deploy agents. I also examine what follows from the factthat the detailed record was itself compiled with the help of AI analysis agents, and I propose “incidentethnography” and an anthropology of agent collectives.

title: Design and Implementation of a Machine Learning Simulation System for Crop Yield Prediction Under Climate Variability
abstract: Climate variability continues to threaten agricultural productivity, especially in regions where farming depends heavily on rainfall and temperature conditions. This study presents the design and implementation of a web-based computational simulation system for predicting crop yield under climate variability. The system uses rainfall, temperature, pesticide usage, crop type, country, and land size as input variables to estimate crop yield and total production. Historical crop yield and climate data were processed, filtered, and used to train crop-specific machine learning models. Feature engineering was applied to generate additional predictors, including temperature-rainfall interaction, pesticide intensity, growing degree days, heat stress, cold stress, rainfall categories, logarithmic variables, and squared variables. Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Ridge Regression, and ensemble models were trained and evaluated. The system was implemented using a Fast API backend, a web-based frontend, interactive visualization components, and an AI-based recommendation module that explains completed prediction results. The results showed strong predictive performance for several crops, with rice achieving the highest test R² value of 0.9617, followed by maize with 0.9080, soybeans with 0.8524, wheat with 0.8157, and potatoes with 0.7841. The study demonstrates that machine learning-based simulation can support crop yield prediction and agricultural decision-making under changing climate conditions, especially in data-limited regions.

title: hiPSC-derived new approach methodology (NAM) recapitulates hallmarks of atrial fibrillation
abstract: Human in vitro models for atrial fibrillation (AF) remain limited in reproducing disease-specific remodeling. We leveraged a human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived atrial cardiomyocyte (hiPSC-aCM) model, which was co-cultured with human atrial cardiac fibroblasts (haCFs) and subjected to an intermittent tachypacing protocol (ITPP) to mimic AF-associated phenotypes. Human iPSC-derived atrial cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-aCMs) were differentiated, purified, matured, and cultured alone or co-cultured with human atrial cardiac fibroblasts at defined seeding ratios (e.g., 90/10 or 70/30 hiPSC-aCM/haCF). Cultures were subjected to 7 days of intermittent tachypacing using electrical field stimulation. Functional electrophysiology and calcium handling were assessed by high-throughput optical mapping, arrhythmia inducibility testing, and genetically encoded or chemical calcium indicators. Structural and molecular remodeling were evaluated by immunocytochemistry, qPCR, and Western blot analysis. ITPP increased spontaneous action potential (AP) frequency and shortened AP duration at 80% repolarization (APD 80% ), while reducing calcium transient (CaT) upstroke slope and amplitude. Co-cultures at a 70/30 hiPSC-aCM/haCF ratio exhibited marked structural remodeling, with a >100-fold increase in Collagen III expression ( P < 0.0001), decreased excitability (ΔHz = –61 ± 6%, P < 0.0001), prolonged APD 80% (Δ = +130 ± 10%, P < 0.0001), increased triangulation (ΔAPD Tri = +143 ± 13%, P < 0.0001), reduced upstroke slope (Δ = –66 ± 6%, P < 0.0001), conduction block (Δ = –52 ± 18%, P = 0.026), and impaired Ca 2 ⁺ handling (upstroke slope Δ = –50 ± 8%, P < 0.0001; ΔdF/F0 = –34 ± 9%, P = 0.0003). Applying ITPP to the 70/30 co-culture induced AF-like remodeling, with increased spontaneous activity (ΔHz = +25 ± 8%, P = 0.02), shortened APD 80% (Δ = –16 ± 6%, P = 0.01), and reduced conduction velocity (ΔCV 100/0 vs. 70/30 = –27 ± 15%, P = 0.0005). Mechanistically, ITPP led to downregulation of phospholamban (PLN) and altered PLN-SERCA2a balance, along with upregulation of TGFB1 and natriuretic peptides, reflecting calcium-handling dysfunction and pro-fibrotic signaling. Together, these findings establish a human-relevant platform in 2D culture that recapitulates key AF-associated structural and electrophysiological remodeling for mechanistic studies and therapeutic screening.

title: Predictive modelling to differentiate possible bacterial and viral cases of childhood pneumonia in Kilifi, Kenya using protein markers and clinical data
abstract: To date, accessible diagnostic tools to identify whether a patient's pneumonia is a bacterial, or viral infection, are not accurate or timely enough to prevent preemptive antibiotic administration. Relying on single biomarkers or clinical presentations has been insufficient. We aimed to incorporate a wide range of novel biomarkers and clinical presentations into a multivariable model and to validate its ability to differentiate bacterial from viral pneumonia. A total of 457 children aged 2–59 months, admitted to the Kilifi County Referral Hospital, Kenya, with WHO defined pneumonia were classified using gold standard laboratory diagnostics as possible bacterial (i.e., bacterial/ unknown cases, n = 229) or possible viral ( n = 228) infections. Clinical and laboratory data, and levels of CRP, PCT and 6 novel protein biomarkers were used to develop and validate a predictive multivariable Poisson regression model to differentiate pneumonia etiology. The Receiver Operating Characteristic curve was used to assess biomarker performance and validate the model internally. In age-adjusted analyses, chest-wall indrawing, cough, convulsions, crackles, angiotensinogen (AGT), and Serpin Family A Member 1 (SERPINA1) were significantly associated with pneumonia etiology, controlling for age. However, only chest-wall indrawing remained significant in multivariable analyses after controlling for age. The model demonstrated fair, but inadequate, discrimination, with an Area Under the Curve of 0.61. In a separate analysis excluding the unknowns from the bacterial group, chest-wall indrawing, crackles, cough, AGT (>=7.9144MFI), were significant predictors of pneumonia etiology, adjusting for age. This model demonstrated good discrimination, with an Area Under the Curve of 0.78 on the validation dataset. Among children admitted to the hospital with WHO-defined pneumonia, modelling a wide range of biomarkers and clinical presentations still failed to distinguish bacterial from viral pneumonia with enough accuracy to guide clinical management. Further research addressing some of the limitations we encountered in outcome classification, stratifying by disease severity and potentially accounting for variation in biomarker performance by age, may improve predictions.

title: Responses and assembly mechanisms of planktonic bacterial and fungal communities in the upper Chishui River during dry and wet seasons
abstract: The upper Chishui River in Zhaotong, Yunnan, is a typical karst headwater stream and remains the only undammed first-order tributary of the upper Yangtze River. Agricultural and urban land use creates a distinct longitudinal nutrient gradient. We investigated the responses of planktonic bacteria and fungi to seasonal hydrology and anthropogenic disturbances, as well as their community assembly processes. Surface water samples were collected in the dry season (January 2025) and wet season (May 2025) from three sites: an upstream least-disturbed reference site (CSY), a midstream site affected by agricultural and township runoff (GZ), and a downstream site receiving municipal wastewater discharges (EL). Using high-throughput amplicon sequencing of bacterial 16S rRNA genes and fungal ITS2 regions, we found that total nitrogen and total phosphorus increased downstream; seasonal hydrological variation altered nutrient concentrations but did not shift the overall spatial pattern. Nutrient and carbonate-related variables (pH and TP) were correlated with the community structure of both bacteria and fungi. Alpha diversity was highest at the upstream site. At midstream and downstream sites, species richness increased while community evenness declined in the dry season. Microbial community composition exhibited clear seasonal turnover: Flavobacterium dominated upstream in the wet season, while Limnohabitans prevailed at the midstream site in the dry season. Upstream fungal communities were enriched in terrestrial saprotrophs and plant pathogens, whereas Rozellomycota predominated downstream. Functional predictions based on Phylogenetic Investigation of Communities by Reconstruction of Unobserved States 2 (PICRUSt2) and FUNGuild (Fungi + Functional + Guild) indicated that stress-response pathways were relatively abundant in the wet season. In contrast, carbohydrate and amino acid metabolism pathways were relatively more abundant in the dry season. Fungal trophic guild diversity at midstream and downstream sites also increased in the dry season. Infer Community Assembly Mechanisms by Phylogenetic-bin-based null model analysis (iCAMP) indicated that homogeneous selection predominantly structured bacterial communities across both seasons. By comparison, fungal communities shifted from homogeneous selection in the wet season to dominance by stochastic processes (e.g., ecological drift) in the dry season. Collectively, these findings suggest that bacteria and fungi respond differently to anthropogenic stress and seasonal hydrology in karst headwaters, with substantial seasonal divergence in their core community assembly mechanisms. Rozellomycota and certain fungal trophic guilds may serve as candidate bioindicators of chronic disturbance, pending further validation. These results provide a foundation for ecological health assessment and water resource conservation in karst headwater streams.

title: Bacteria from extreme environments as candidate bioinoculants for drought tolerance in legumes: a critical appraisal of mechanisms and evidence
abstract: Drought is one of the major constraints limiting legume productivity, impairing plant growth, biological nitrogen fixation, and seed nutritional quality. The increasing frequency and intensity of water scarcity have intensified the search for sustainable strategies to improve crop resilience. Bacteria isolated from extreme environments have been proposed as candidate bioinoculants because adaptations to desiccation, salinity, or extreme temperatures may provide traits relevant to plant performance under water deficit. However, most of these isolates are extremotolerant rather than extremophilic sensu stricto, and much of the supporting evidence derives from stresses other than drought. The objective of this review is to synthesize current knowledge on the mechanisms through which extremophilic and extremotolerant bacteria may contribute to drought tolerance in legumes, using explicit operational definitions for these microbial categories and for drought, and a four-tier evidence classification applied at the level of individual studies. Candidate mechanisms include exopolysaccharide- and biofilm-mediated rhizosphere water retention, modulation of root architecture and auxin/ethylene balance through ACC deaminase activity, osmolyte accumulation, antioxidant responses, nutrient mobilization, maintenance of nodulation and biological nitrogen fixation, and regulation of host stress-responsive genes. Direct evidence, defined as extremophilic or extremotolerant strains evaluated in legumes under soil water deficit, is restricted to a small number of studies, whereas a large proportion of the literature relies on salinity, heat, or PEG-induced osmotic stress, non-legume hosts, genomic potential, or in vitro assays. We also discuss constraints that may limit the use of these bacteria, including rhizosphere colonization, persistence, and competitiveness against native microbiota under non-extreme conditions. Current findings provide plausible mechanisms and proof-of-concept results, but they do not yet demonstrate reliable field performance of extremophile-derived inoculants in legume production. Strain-level characterization, standardized drought protocols, and multi-environment field validation are required to establish their agronomic value.

title: Fact construction as a missing layer in legal AI: a practice-grounded framework for evaluating multi-agent legal consultation
abstract: Legal AI research often evaluates large language models (LLMs) on legal reasoning tasks under the assumption that relevant facts are already structured and available. This assumption overlooks a prior and practically consequential stage of legal work: fact construction, namely the transformation of incomplete, fragmented, and interactionally disclosed information into coherent factual narratives. This study conceptualizes fact construction as a distinct evaluation layer in legal AI and introduces a practice-grounded framework for assessing it in AI-assisted legal consultation. Rather than proposing a legal advice system or doctrinal rule-matching architecture, we use a role-separated multi-agent workflow consisting of a fact-constrained Litigant Twin, a structured-questioning LegalAider, a NarrativeAgent for factual synthesis, and an Evaluator for factual-alignment assessment. Using 100 de-identified legal clinic consultation records, we evaluate multiple LLMs under rubric-based assessment, comparing generated factual narratives against original human-authored consultation records in terms of factual accuracy, completeness, and consistency. The results show that LLM-based agents can generate usable factual narratives under constrained conditions, particularly when cases are internally consistent, limited to a single dispute, and supported by clear actor-role relationships. However, cross-model evaluator agreement remains moderate, and outlier analysis reveals recurring structural sources of failure, including anonymization-induced referential ambiguity, third-party reporting, multi-episode case complexity, and numerically dense facts. These findings suggest that reliability in AI-assisted legal consultation depends not only on model capability, but also on interaction design, data representation, institutional record-keeping, and human oversight. By treating fact construction as a distinct analytical layer, this article contributes a practice-grounded framework for evaluating responsible LLM integration in legal settings and highlights the need for factual grounding, contestability, and human-supervised review before downstream legal analysis begins.

title: Uncertainty-aware improved LSTM flood forecasting in a snowmelt-dominated arid basin
abstract: Accurate flood forecasting in arid inland basins remains difficult because observed events are few, runoff generation is strongly nonlinear, and snowmelt and rainfall may interact within short forecasting windows. This study evaluates an improved Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) framework for the Chinese Ili River Basin in northwestern China, where flood processes are dominated by snowmelt and can be modified by rainfall recharge. Hourly temperature, precipitation, and runoff observations from nine 24-h flood events were used for model development and testing. The framework combines Pearson-based feature screening, sliding-window sample reconstruction with training-only low-level noise injection, Dropout–L2 regularization, and grid-search tuning within nested leave-one-event-out validation; temporal interpolation is not used. Deterministic hyperparameter sensitivity was further examined using Latin hypercube sampling and Monte Carlo analysis, separately from predictive uncertainty quantification. Across the nine events, the improved LSTM yielded mean NSE and R 2 values of 0.9633 and 0.9015, respectively, with a mean peak-discharge error of 3.90%. The temperature-runoff lag averaged 11.67 h, supporting the dominant role of cumulative thermal forcing in the snowmelt-driven events, whereas rainfall mainly modified peak behavior in the mixed events. The hyperparameter-sensitivity analysis indicates that hidden neurons, learning rate, and time step are the most influential parameters. These results suggest that the pro-posed framework can provide a useful event-scale forecasting basis for snow-melt-dominated floods in data-scarce arid basins.

title: The Nature Frame as a landscape-based framework for integrating soil functions into agroecosystem management
abstract: Agricultural management is often applied uniformly across landscapes with contrasting geoecological conditions, potentially increasing the risk of soil degradation and reducing the capacity of agroecosystems to maintain soil ecological functions. This study develops and demonstrates a landscape-based approach for interpreting soil-related functions in relation to the spatial geoecological organization of agroecosystems, using the Nature Frame as an operational geoecological model. Two contrasting agricultural landscapes in Lithuania – the lowland Joniškis district and the moraine upland Molėtai district – were selected as case studies. Spatial analyses integrated the Nature Frame, agricultural land-use, soil, and landscape datasets, while a conceptual land use-soil function compatibility matrix was used to interpret the expected compatibility of agricultural land-use categories with selected soil ecological functions. The results revealed potential spatial mismatches between agricultural land use and the geoecological structure of the landscape, particularly in the lowland agroecosystem, where intensive arable land frequently occupied geoecologically sensitive areas. Based on these spatial patterns, a conceptual landscape-based management framework was developed to support the spatial differentiation of agricultural management according to the geoecological functions of the Nature Frame. The proposed approach demonstrates the potential of the Nature Frame as a conceptual decision-support framework for integrating landscape geoecological structure and soil-related functions into landscape-scale agroecosystem planning.

title: Can rural digitalization promote the green transformation of cultivated land? Evidence from rural China
abstract: Exploring how rural digitalization influences the green transformation of cultivated land and its spatial spillover effects holds significant implications for resolving the contradiction between cultivated land conservation and sustainable agricultural development, as well as advancing agricultural and rural modernization. With an emphasis on its underlying mechanisms, regional heterogeneity, and spatial spillover effects, this paper systematically examines how rural digitalization affects the greening transformation of cultivated land using panel data from 31 Chinese provinces over the 2011–2023 period and econometric techniques. The results show: (1) The level of green transformation of cultivated land in China has steadily risen, with a spatial gradient characterized by “leading in the eastern coastal areas, steady in central China, and lagging in the western and northeastern regions”; (2) Rural digitalization significantly promotes the green transformation of cultivated land by facilitating industrial structure upgrading, improving human capital, and optimizing land resource allocation; (3) Rural digitalization has a significantly positive spatial spillover effect on green transformation, raising the greening level of surrounding cultivated lands; (4) The impact of rural digitalization exhibits pronounced regional and digitalization-level heterogeneity. In addition to offering empirical data and useful insights for developing unique policies and promoting regional cooperative governance, this study enhances theoretical viewpoints on digital villages and green agricultural growth.

title: Farm-level technical efficiency in temperate horticulture: evidence from apple, pear, and cherry growers
abstract: Improving resource-use efficiency is fundamental to enhancing agricultural productivity and promoting sustainable horticultural development, particularly in regions where opportunities for expanding cultivated land and increasing input use are limited. This study evaluates the technical efficiency of apple, pear, and cherry growers in the Kashmir Valley and examines the socioeconomic, institutional, and regional factors associated with farm-level technical efficiency. Primary data were collected from 418 horticultural households during 2023 using a multi-stage sampling approach. Technical efficiency was first estimated separately for apple, pear, and cherry growers using an input-oriented Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) framework under both Constant Returns to Scale (CRS) and Variable Returns to Scale (VRS) assumptions. Scale efficiency was subsequently estimated, while a pooled DEA model was employed to generate farm-level technical efficiency scores for the second-stage analysis. The determinants of technical efficiency were examined using Tobit regression, supported by a fractional logit model as a robustness check, and regional disparities were assessed using Kruskal–Wallis and Mann–Whitney non-parametric tests. The results indicate that apple growers achieved the highest overall technical efficiency, followed by pear and cherry growers. The VRS estimates reveal substantially higher levels of pure technical efficiency, whereas the scale efficiency analysis suggests that a considerable proportion of technical inefficiency arises from farms operating below their optimal production scale. The second-stage analysis identifies family size, education, irrigation facilities, access to credit, and cold storage infrastructure as significant positive factors associated with farm-level technical efficiency, while significant regional disparities are observed across the Kashmir Valley. The robustness analysis confirms the consistency of the estimated relationships. These findings highlight that improving horticultural performance requires not only efficient farm-level resource management but also stronger institutional support, investments in irrigation and post-harvest infrastructure, improved access to rural credit, and region-specific development strategies. The study contributes to the literature by integrating crop-specific and pooled efficiency analyses with socioeconomic and regional assessments, providing policy-relevant evidence for promoting resource-efficient and sustainable horticultural production.

title: Spatially Structured Prediction of Soil Penetration Resistance Reveals Confounded Associations with Cotton Traits Under Long-Term Furrow Irrigation
abstract: Soil penetration resistance (PR) is widely used to assess compaction, although water content and field position can confound its relationships with crops. This study characterised depth-specific PR, identified its principal soil predictors, and evaluated its associations with cotton traits under long-term furrow irrigation. Penetration resistance, soil properties, plant height, SPAD, and boll number were measured at 40 georeferenced locations across four transects. Partial least squares (PLS) and multiple linear regression models were compared using spatially structured cross-validation. Mean PR increased from 1.079 MPa at 0–10 cm to 1.540 MPa at 20–30 cm. Along the longitudinal field gradient, soil water content increased downslope (ρ = 0.973), whereas bulk density (ρ = −0.936) and mean PR (ρ = −0.973) decreased. Under contiguous-block validation, PLS slightly outperformed linear regression for mean PR (RMSE = 0.0516 MPa, predictive R2 = 0.968, RPD = 5.68), with soil water content and bulk density as the dominant predictors among the four retained variables. Strong raw correlations between PR and cotton traits became nonsignificant after adjustment for longitudinal position and transect, with 77.1–99.6% attenuation. EC increased downslope, whereas SAR and ESP decreased. Thus, the apparent relationships between PR and cotton traits largely reflected a shared longitudinal field gradient rather than an independently identifiable effect of PR.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Health Research and Care: A Narrative Review of Applications and Implications for Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementia
abstract: The advent of generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs) and deep generative networks, is transforming the landscape of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementia (ADRD) research and care. This narrative review aims to synthesize current applications of generative AI in ADRD research and care, highlight ethical and implementation challenges, and propose strategies for responsible integration into clinical practice. We conducted a narrative review of literature, regulatory documents, program reports, and relevant sources published between 2016 and 2026, with a specific focus on cognitive screening, synthetic data generation, digital twin modeling, and caregiver support. Techniques discussed include generative adversarial networks (GANs), variational autoencoders (VAEs), diffusion models, multimodal transformers, and LLM-powered chatbots. Generative AI enables applications such as virtual patient companions, remote cognitive assessments via conversational agents, multimodal image-to-text tools, synthetic data augmentation, disease progression simulation, and improved caregiver communication. Challenges include model explainability, clinical validation, regulatory compliance, privacy, data bias, hallucination risk, patient autonomy, and global disparities. Responsible development requires transparent reporting, stakeholder co-design, rigorous clinical and economic validation, and continuous post-deployment monitoring to support fairness and effectiveness in real-world settings.

title: Vitamin D–VDR Signaling Across Thyroid Disorders: A Systematic Review of Molecular Mechanisms, Autoimmunity, Genetic Susceptibility, Experimental Evidence and Therapeutic Translation
abstract: Vitamin D–Vitamin D receptor (VDR) signaling extends beyond calcium-phosphate homeostasis and regulates immune tolerance, inflammation, cellular differentiation, oxidative stress, and endocrine physiology. This systematic review evaluated the relationship between vitamin D–VDR signaling and thyroid disorders, including hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, Hashimoto’s thyroiditis, Graves’ disease, thyroid autoimmunity, genetic susceptibility, experimental mechanisms, and therapeutic implications. This study was conducted and reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement. PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus were searched for studies published from January 2005 through June 2026, supplemented by backward and forward citation screening of relevant studies and reviews. Eligible evidence included human observational and interventional studies, genetic investigations, and relevant animal and in vitro studies addressing vitamin D status, vitamin D exposure or supplementation, VDR variation, vitamin D metabolism, or vitamin D–VDR mechanisms in relation to thyroid function, thyroid disease, thyroid autoantibodies, or related biological outcomes. A total of 13,623 records were identified, of which 11,730 unique records underwent title and abstract screening, 449 reports were assessed at the full-text stage, and 118 primary studies were included in the final synthesis. Because of substantial heterogeneity in populations, study designs, vitamin D exposures, outcomes, genetic backgrounds, and experimental models, findings were synthesized narratively rather than by quantitative meta-analysis. Lower circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] concentrations were frequently associated with thyroid disease, particularly autoimmune phenotypes, and increased thyroid peroxidase and thyroglobulin antibodies in Hashimoto’s thyroiditis. Interventional evidence suggests that vitamin D supplementation may reduce thyroid peroxidase antibody (TPOAb) and thyroglobulin antibody (TgAb) concentrations in some patients with autoimmune thyroid disease. However, these laboratory changes represent immunological surrogate outcomes and should not be interpreted as evidence of restored thyroid function, prevention of progression to overt hypothyroidism, reduced dependence on thyroid hormone replacement, or sustained clinical remission. Randomized evidence does not establish a general preventive effect of vitamin D supplementation on incident hypothyroidism. Associations between VDR polymorphisms, including FokI/rs2228570, rs1544410, rs731236, and rs7975232, and thyroid autoimmunity were inconsistent across populations. Experimental evidence implicates immune regulation, Th17/Treg balance, inflammatory signaling, vitamin D metabolism, and calcium-phosphate homeostasis. The evidence was limited by substantial clinical, methodological, and biological heterogeneity, frequent reliance on observational studies, population-specific genetic findings, and differences between experimental models and human thyroid physiology. Overall, vitamin D–VDR signaling represents a biologically plausible modifier of thyroid disease, but current evidence does not establish universal causality or therapeutic efficacy.

title: Differentiated Design of Dormitory Buildings Based on Orientation, Focusing on Thermal and Daylighting Performance
abstract: In university dormitory buildings composed of standardized units, units of different orientations are typically designed with identical parameters. Using a typical dormitory as the baseline, XGBoost-based models with Bayesian hyperparameter optimization were coupled with NSGA-II for multi-objective optimization. Sensitivity analysis was performed to reveal the orientation-dependent influence mechanisms of design variables and to identify the key variables affecting useful daylight illuminance (UDI), vertical illuminance at eye level (VCI), predicted percentage of dissatisfied (PPD), and energy use intensity (EUI) in south- and north-facing dormitories, with TOPSIS used for decision making. Results show that: (1) For both orientations, the window-to-wall ratio and window type are the key variables. South-facing units are more sensitive to the window solar heat gain coefficient, while north-facing units are more sensitive to the window thermal transmittance. (2) Window Types 8 and 5 are recommended for north- and south-facing rooms, with window-to-wall ratios of 0.30 and 0.39, respectively. (3) Comparing three daylighting optimization scenarios reveals that high correlation does not necessarily imply substitutability: the maximum difference in all performance indicators reached 6.75%, indicating that indicator selection affects the multi-objective optimization results. (4) The effect of wall reflectance on vertical illuminance depends on orientation, window parameters, and floor level, and is more pronounced in higher-floor rooms.

title: Marine Natural Products with Novel Mechanisms of Action: From Disrupting Gene Expression to Reshaping the Tumor Microenvironment and Beyond
abstract: Drug resistance and undruggable targets persist as major therapeutic hurdles. Marine natural products (MNPs), which have evolved under extreme conditions, offer structurally diverse scaffolds that engage targets via unconventional mechanisms. This review systematically groups MNPs by their precise molecular targets and modes of action, moving beyond cytotoxicity tabulation. We cover agents that disrupt gene expression-spliceosome inhibitors (FR901464, thailanstatin A), translation initiation blockers (pateamine A, hippuristanol), and elongation arrest compounds (plitidepsin, psymberin), as well as those inducing genomic damage through topoisomerase poisoning or DNA alkylation. Beyond oncology, we critically assess MNPs modulating proteostasis (marizomib, carmaphycins), targeting undruggable protein–protein interfaces (siladenoserinol A, marinopyrrole A), reshaping epigenetics (largazole, psammaplin A), and triggering non-apoptotic death pathways (ferroptosis, cuproptosis, pyroptosis). We discuss structure–function correlations and translational bottlenecks for representative clinical-stage candidates, and discuss how cryo-EM, AI-driven prediction, and synthetic biology are converting these exotic scaffolds into viable leads. By linking mechanistic depth with translational roadmaps, this review aims to inspire both academic and industrial researchers to harness marine molecular diversity for next-generation precision medicines.

title: Regional Heterogeneity in Energy Markets: Benchmarking Deep-Learning Models for China’s LPG Price Forecasting
abstract: Accurate liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) price forecasts are relevant to procurement and inventory planning, yet regional differences within China have received limited attention. This empirical study benchmarks 16 learned time-series models and a Naive baseline for 30-day forecasts of LPG spot prices in six Chinese regions, with drift, ETS, ARIMA, SARIMA, Ridge, LightGBM, and a futures-close reference. The dataset contains 20 daily variables and 1110 observations from 1 January 2021 to 15 January 2024. The selected regional neural configurations achieve lower OWA than ARIMA and SARIMA in five of six regions (average OWA 0.885 versus 0.984 for SARIMA). SARIMA (0.984) also improves on ARIMA (0.993). None of the twelve neural-versus-benchmark comparisons is significant after Holm correction. The selected Southern and Eastern configurations improve on Naive in both test halves, whereas the other four configurations change their relative performance across halves. These results motivate regional and temporal validation with competitive conventional baselines rather than a claim of universal neural-model superiority.

title: Heme-Mediated Danger Signaling Suppresses Osteogenesis Through TLR4-Dependent Inhibition of β-Catenin Signaling
abstract: Extracellular heme is a damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) released during hemolysis, hemorrhage, and tissue injury. Although its pro-inflammatory and cytotoxic effects are well established, its impact on osteoblast differentiation and bone formation remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the effects of extracellular heme on osteoblast differentiation and defined the signaling pathways involved. In MC3T3-E1 pre-osteoblasts, heme suppressed alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, calcium deposition, matrix mineralization, and expression of osteogenic markers, including Runx2 and Sp7 at day 3, Col1a1 and Alpl at day 7, and Bsp and Bglap at day 10, without affecting cell viability. Mechanistically, heme reduced AKT phosphorylation and inhibitory phosphorylation of glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK-3β) at Ser9, consistent with increased GSK-3β activity. This was accompanied by decreased accumulation of transcriptionally active β-catenin, impaired nuclear β-catenin localization, and suppression of canonical Wnt target genes (Axin2, Lef1, Ccnd1, c-Myc). Pharmacological inhibition of GSK-3β partially restored β-catenin signaling and osteogenic differentiation, whereas inhibition of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) attenuated heme-induced suppression of the AKT/GSK-3β pathway. Combined inhibition of TLR4 and GSK-3β produced the most pronounced restoration of osteogenesis in the presence of heme. Consistent with the in vitro findings, maternal heme administration during pregnancy significantly reduced ALP activity in multiple fetal craniofacial ossification centers in vivo. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that extracellular heme suppresses osteogenesis and supports a model in which TLR4-associated dysregulation of the AKT/GSK-3β/β-catenin axis contributes to impaired osteogenic differentiation.

title: A Conceptual Translational Bench-to-Bedside Cardiac Safety Framework for Predicting Drug-Induced QT Interval Prolongation from Molecular Structure to Clinical Data
abstract: QT interval prolongation is associated with an increased risk of torsades de pointes (TdP), a potentially life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia, making assessment of cardiac repolarization a critical component of drug development. This work demonstrates how integrated in silico methodologies can be used to predict and quantitatively characterize QT liability across the drug discovery and development continuum. A proof-of concept translational workflow combining molecular structure analysis, in vitro pharmacology, animal data, and clinical exposure-response modeling was evaluated using the retrospective case examples verapamil and dofetilide. Molecular structure- and pharmacology-based assessments predicted hERG channel interaction and potential QT risk for both compounds. While initial in silico analyses suggested a high QT liability for verapamil and dofetilide, mechanistic electrophysiological modeling differentiated their effects. For verapamil, concurrent calcium channel inhibition offset hERG-mediated effects, resulting in predicted reductions in action potential duration and no clinically relevant QT prolongation. In contrast, dofetilide produced concentration-dependent increases in action potential duration, consistent with its known proarrhythmic potential. Translation of nonclinical findings to humans accurately predicted the absence of clinically meaningful QT effects for verapamil and identified QT prolongation exceeding the regulatory 10 ms threshold for dofetilide at therapeutic concentrations. Drug exposure and pharmacokinetic properties could be anticipated based solely on molecular structure. This conceptual workflow demonstrates how integrated quantitative in silico approaches can support earlier identification, characterization, and communication of QT risk, enabling informed decision-making and improved development efficiency from bench to bedside.

title: From Verified Data to Risk-Based Pricing: An Applied Risk Analytics and Blockchain Necessity Framework for Agricultural and Property Insurance
abstract: Insurers increasingly seek to replace self-reported underwriting data with verified data, from satellite and IoT monitoring in agriculture to digital-identity credentials in property insurance. Distributed ledger technology (DLT, “blockchain”) is often proposed as the natural verification layer, but this proposition is rarely tested in economic terms. This paper develops a Net Advantage of Verification (NAV) and Blockchain Net Value (BNV) framework. It decomposes a verified-data architecture into four value components, net of five cost components. It then compares a status quo (S0), the best feasible non-DLT architecture (S1) and a DLT architecture (S2). The framework is applied to two Bulgarian cases: a behavior-based agricultural product (Pay-as-you-Farm) and EUDI-Wallet-enabled property insurance. All monetary inputs are illustrative assumptions, not observed data. Under this illustrative parameterization, BNV is negative in both cases at the base case and in most simulated scenarios. Within the stated ranges, a well-governed non-DLT architecture is therefore more economical. The result demonstrates the method and is not an empirical estimate for the Bulgarian market. The paper derives the conditions under which the sign could reverse, proposes a validation protocol and discusses implications for EU regulators and insurers. The framework transfers to other markets, whereas the numerical results require recalibration.
journal: Journal of Risk and Financial Management

title: Temperature as a Nonlinear Moderator of Land-Use Carbon Emissions Across China’s Temperature Zones: Drivers and Differentiated Governance
abstract: Land-use carbon emissions are typically analyzed within administrative or economic regions; however, natural temperature gradients may modulate how socioeconomic and policy drivers translate into emissions. Using China’s land-use, energy, and meteorological data (1990–2022), we applied a coupled nature–economy–policy modeling framework across six temperature zones to test whether temperature acts as a nonlinear moderator rather than a direct determinant. The warm temperate zone accounted for >55% of national emissions and, together with the mid-temperate zone, this share reached ~80%, while the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau remained a net sink. Driver contributions varied systematically: economic factors dominated tropical and subtropical zones (74.3%), natural constraints dominated the plateau (41.7%), and policy interactions dominated mid- and warm-temperate zones (58.4%). Temperature acted nonlinearly, with emission effects rising from 0.277 to 1.212 t CO2 per °C above a 26.65 °C summer mean (a 4.4-fold amplification). A generalized additive model confirms this significant nonlinearity. Scenario simulations suggest that the business-as-usual scenario peaks in 2035–2040, whereas the ecological protection and low-carbon scenarios peak around 2030. Under RCP4.5, the model projects a potential shift of the plateau from sink to source, but this result is conditional on simplified climate–carbon feedbacks and should be interpreted as a plausible risk rather than a prediction. These findings indicate that temperature zones offer a complementary natural gradient—not a replacement for administrative divisions—for understanding how similar human activities produce different carbon outcomes under contrasting thermal conditions. Given the use of partly uniform emission factors, the results represent macro-scale differentiation; governance implications are therefore conditional on scenario assumptions and require local feasibility assessment.

title: Associations of Urbanization Intensity, Ecosystem Services, and Climate with Land Surface Temperature and PM2.5 in the Yellow River Basin (China): A Spatial Regression and XGBoost–SHAP Analysis
abstract: Understanding how urbanization, ecosystem-service conditions, and climate are associated with environmental responses is important for regional land management. Using three discrete county-level snapshots from the Yellow River Basin in 2013, 2018, and 2023, this study examined two environmental response variables: land surface temperature (LST) and the concentration of fine particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter of 2.5 μm or less (PM2.5), in relation to urbanization intensity (UII), carbon storage (CS), water yield (WY), soil retention (SR), air temperature (T), and wind speed (WS). Pearson correlation analysis, multiple linear regression, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) combined with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to characterize linear and nonlinear associations. To reduce spatial leakage, model performance was evaluated using nested five-fold buffered spatial block validation, in which contiguous spatial blocks were held out, and counties within 50 km of each test block were excluded from model training. The pooled out-of-block R2 values ranged from 0.765 to 0.777 for LST and from 0.728 to 0.854 for PM2.5. T was the dominant predictor of both responses, accounting for 79.26–86.62% of the total SHAP importance for LST and 53.12–65.99% for PM2.5. UII showed positive model-based associations with both responses that generally appeared to level off at higher observed values, whereas the associations of ecosystem-service variables differed among the three independently analyzed years. Because the three years were modelled separately, these cross-year contrasts are interpreted descriptively rather than as continuous temporal trends. These findings characterize contrasting explanatory structures for surface thermal conditions and particulate pollution and may inform the formulation of hypotheses for spatially differentiated environmental management in the Yellow River Basin.

title: Towards Intelligent Investment Risk Modeling: Probabilistic Reasoning and Adaptive Decision Systems Under Uncertainty
abstract: Investment risk modeling remains challenging due to uncertainty, structural change, and market dynamics. This study develops an integrated empirical framework linking adaptive Bayesian forecasting, predictive-uncertainty evaluation, and risk-sensitive portfolio decision-making in a five-asset system comprising Microsoft, NVIDIA, Tesla, IBM, and Boeing. The TVP-VAR is employed as an established adaptive forecasting component and evaluated against expanding-mean and fixed-parameter VAR benchmarks using point-forecast accuracy, probabilistic calibration, regime-specific performance, and investment outcomes. Results show that the TVP-VAR does not systematically outperform simpler benchmarks in one-step-ahead point forecasting. However, it produces higher mean log scores and 95% predictive-interval coverage closer to nominal levels across all five assets, although these improvements generally require wider intervals and do not yield superior CRPS values. Sensitivity analysis shows that the strongest model-based portfolio performance occurs at λ = 1, where forgetting-factor-driven coefficient variation is eliminated while adaptive covariance updating remains active. Nevertheless, the equal-weight portfolio delivers the strongest overall risk-adjusted performance. Comparison with static covariance indicates that the economic advantage of adaptive covariance estimation is modest and criterion-dependent. Greater parameter adaptivity does not imply universal statistical or economic superiority; its value is more evident in predictive-uncertainty representation and calibration than in consistently improved point forecasts or portfolio outcomes.

title: Design and Experimental Evaluation of a NetDevOps Framework for Automated Network Deployment, Testing and Troubleshooting
abstract: Network automation increasingly requires reproducible workflows that connect deployment with objective post-deployment assurance. This study proposes a six-phase NetDevOps framework integrating Planning, Infrastructure Modeling, Validation, Automated Deployment, Operational Testing, and Operational State Verification. The framework was instantiated using YAML, Jinja2, Ansible, and pyATS and evaluated in two emulated MPLS L3VPN configurations comprising five and ten Cisco devices. Fifteen measured runs per workflow and configuration characterized execution time as well as automation-host processor and memory consumption, while the Operational Compliance Index (OCI) and Global Compliance Index (GCI) quantified operational acceptance. Controlled perturbations examined compliance behavior and baseline-driven state verification. The results showed repeatable execution and stable automation-host resource consumption under the evaluated conditions. OCI and GCI differentiated conformity among evaluable outcomes from incomplete evaluability, while qualified-baseline comparisons exposed structured state differences associated with known interface- and protocol-level perturbations. These findings support the feasibility of integrating automated deployment, quantitative operational acceptance, and baseline-driven state verification within a repeatable NetDevOps lifecycle, without implying comparative superiority, scalability, or multi-vendor portability.

title: Multi-Granularity Text and Scale-Aware Visual Encoding for Remote Sensing Image-Text Retrieval and Prompt-Based Scene Recognition
abstract: Remote sensing captions typically interleave domain-specific terminology, object attributes, spatial relations, and scene context within a single sentence, while the corresponding imagery contains targets spanning markedly different spatial extents—from individual vehicles to entire airport layouts. A single global text vector and fixed-scale visual pooling therefore tend to discard the local and hierarchical evidence needed for reliable image–text alignment. Moreover, standard contrastive objectives treat all unmatched pairs as equally unrelated, ignoring the fact that semantically adjacent scenes (e.g., airports and industrial zones) share substantial visual content. To address these issues, we develop a CLIP-style dual encoder with three targeted additions: a text encoder that preserves word-level, phrase-level, and sentence-level representations before fusing them through cross-granularity attention; a visual encoder that associates four hierarchical feature levels with scale-aware receptive-field configurations and incorporates SAM-guided local views during training; and a semantic membership-aware contrastive loss that applies detached, bounded discount weights to semantically close negatives without inverting their penalty sign. On the cleaned RSICD benchmark, the model achieves 87.5% mAP for in-domain prompt-based scene recognition and 34.37% mean recall for scene-constrained retrieval, outperforming the quoted RemoteCLIP and fully fine-tuned CLIP results in the scene-constrained retrieval comparison. Ablation confirms that each of the three components contributes meaningfully to the final performance. The deployable dual encoder contains approximately 59.7 million trainable parameters, and SAM is not required at inference.

title: Medicinal Plant Mapping Based on UAV Hyperspectral Imagery via an Interpretable Framework
abstract: Accurate mapping of medicinal plants is essential for resource inventory and sustainable management. While Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) hyperspectral sensing provides a powerful monitoring tool, the high-dimensional spectral ambiguities and the black-box nature of conventional global classifiers severely restrict mapping accuracy and interpretability. To overcome this, we developed an interpretable, class-specific framework for fine-scale crop identification. A multi-feature pool was distilled through a hierarchical Successive Projections Algorithm (SPA)–Competitive Adaptive Reweighted Sampling (CARS)–Genetic Algorithm (GA)–Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) strategy, isolating class-specific diagnostic fingerprints that transition mapping from black-box modeling to an explainable mechanism. The tailored feature subsets were supplied to parallel Random Forest binary classifiers to generate class-specific probability outputs, which were subsequently fed into a Logistic Regression decision-level fusion layer that calibrated prediction probabilities and resolved inter-class conflicts to yield the definitive classification results. Applied in Yunfu, Guangdong, the framework mapped target species (Murraya exotica, Zanthoxylum nitidum, and Melicope pteleifolia) with an overall accuracy of 97.35% (Kappa = 0.97), outperforming conventional benchmark models such as standard multi-class Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting, and spectral angle mapper. These findings demonstrate that coupling class-specific feature distillation with probability-calibrated decision fusion provides a robust, interpretable paradigm for precision agricultural mapping in heterogeneous environments.

title: Counterfactual False-Positive Mining for Appearance-Robust Change Detection
abstract: Appearance differences between acquisition dates can increase change responses at unchanged locations. Standard supervision on augmented pairs does not explicitly isolate this additional response. We define an input-level counterfactual response as the logit difference produced by the same fixed EMA teacher at the same pixel when the original time-2 image is replaced by a specified appearance intervention. This paired model response holds the scene geometry, label, teacher parameters, and operator realization fixed; it is not a causal reconstruction of the physical acquisition process. We propose counterfactual false-positive mining with reference prediction preservation (CFPM-RP). An exponential-moving-average (EMA) teacher compares an original pair with a pair undergoing a controlled appearance transformation. Positive logit increments within stable unchanged regions define candidate locations. A smooth one-sided loss penalizes the perturbed student response relative to the original teacher prediction, with auxiliary support weighting, segmentation supervision, and changed-region constraints. The auxiliary paths are used only during training, retaining the deployed detector architecture. Experiments cover LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and SYSU-CD, eight appearance perturbations, an equal-budget continuation, eight additional comparison methods, and a second backbone. CFPM-RP attains perturbation-averaged F1 values of 91.444%, 71.181%, and 77.842% on the three datasets, respectively. Relative to Generic-FT, false-positive counts decrease by 10.37%, 11.15%, and 11.27%. The results show that CFPM-RP reduces appearance-induced false positives while retaining competitive change-detection performance.

title: Geo-Referenced Mobile RGB-D Sensing for Bicycle Lane Width Assessment
abstract: Urban bicycle infrastructure requires spatially continuous and quantitative methods for assessing lane width under real operating conditions. This study presents a geo-referenced mobile RGB-D sensing framework for automated bicycle lane width measurement using a lightweight three-wheeled survey platform equipped with a stereo depth camera, GPS receiver, and inertial measurement unit. Bicycle lane boundaries are detected using FastSAM-based segmentation, GPU-accelerated Canny edge detection, and the Hough transform. IMU-assisted depth-to-height conversion distinguishes the road surface from curbs, roadside structures, and obstacles, while temporal-continuity-based lane restoration compensates for faded markings and occlusions. Lane width is estimated from three-dimensional Euclidean distances derived from RGB-D data. The measurements are temporally synchronized with GPS observations and mapped in a geographic information system to visualize spatial width variations along survey routes. Field experiments over four sections totaling 2.87 km showed that 97.79% of the width estimates were within ±5% of the reference width, with a mean absolute error of 0.0218 m. The resulting geo-referenced width maps enable spatially explicit identification of narrow or irregular bicycle lane sections for infrastructure inspection and maintenance.

title: SARE-CD: Structure–Appearance Routed Experts for Building Change Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery
abstract: In building change detection from high-resolution remote sensing imagery, genuine building changes typically appear as local alterations in roof contours and spatial layouts, whereas differences in solar elevation, atmospheric conditions, and sensor calibration introduce cross-temporal appearance drift in unchanged regions. When the two types of difference are jointly encoded in a single feature space, appearance drift tends to dominate the network response. We therefore propose SARE-CD, a dense, pixel-wise, soft-gated heterogeneous mixture-of-experts (MoE) framework that combines scene-level bias correction with functionally distinct expert modeling. At the feature front end, SARE-CD generates affine parameters from the channel statistics of the bitemporal change representation and applies them in residual form to suppress systematic radiometric drift. The Structure, Appearance, and Adaptive Experts then model geometric boundary changes, local appearance perturbations, and composite differences, respectively, and a pixel-wise router assigns expert weights at each location, with routing-entropy and weak load-balancing regularization used to stabilize the division of labor among the experts. On LEVIR-CD+, S2Looking, and SYSU-CD, SARE-CD achieves F1 scores of 91.58%, 65.78%, and 84.46%, all of which are the highest among the compared methods. In addition, controlled perturbation experiments show that F1 retention remains high under hue shifts, soft shadows, and small misregistration, whereas extreme additive brightness offsets lead to a notable F1 decline on S2Looking.

title: YOLO-Based Vision Perception and Automation for Agricultural Robots: A Comprehensive Survey of Algorithms, Applications, and Deployment
abstract: Deep learning-driven computer vision has become a fundamental enabling technology for agricultural robotics, providing reliable perception capabilities for precision farming and autonomous field operations. Among various object detection frameworks, the You Only Look Once (YOLO) family has attracted extensive attention due to its favorable balance between detection accuracy, computational efficiency, and real-time deployment capability in complex and dynamic agricultural environments. This paper presents a comprehensive review of YOLO-based vision perception and automation technologies for agricultural robotic systems. The evolution of the YOLO framework from YOLOv1 to recent YOLOv11 variants is systematically reviewed, with particular emphasis on architectural innovations, performance improvements, and adaptations to agriculture-specific challenges, including complex backgrounds, illumination variations, severe occlusion, and multi-scale small object detection. Beyond algorithm-level analysis, this survey investigates the integration of YOLO-based perception modules into robotic systems for practical applications, including autonomous navigation, precision spraying, crop monitoring, disease detection, and robotic harvesting. Furthermore, this review analyzes the complete deployment pipeline of YOLO-based agricultural robots, covering benchmark datasets, evaluation metrics, model optimization strategies, and hardware constraints for edge computing platforms. Emerging research directions are also discussed, including lightweight YOLO architectures, multimodal vision–language models, and cloud–edge collaborative intelligence for next-generation agricultural automation. By bridging advances in computer vision algorithms with robotic perception and execution, this survey provides a comprehensive perspective on the development of intelligent and efficient agricultural robotic systems.

title: Analysis of the Impact of Digital Technology on the Resilience of Anhui’s Agricultural Industry Chain: Threshold Effect of Relative Grain Yield
abstract: Improving the resilience of the agricultural industry chain to frequent external shocks and the intertwined agricultural production risks is critical for ensuring national food security and sustainable agricultural development. Taking the 16 prefecture-level cities in Anhui Province—a major grain-producing region in China—as the research sample, two composite proxy indices were constructed in this study; namely, an agricultural industry chain resilience index built upon aggregate official statistics (rather than direct observed shock-response outcomes) and an index capturing broad rural digital development instead of purely agriculture-specific digital adoption. Based on balanced panel data from 2015 to 2024, two-way fixed-effect, mediation-effect, and panel-threshold models were adopted in this study to examine the association, mediating mechanism, regional heterogeneity, and threshold characteristics conditioned on the relative grain yield. The empirical results show that the rural-oriented digital development index is significantly and robustly positively associated with our composite agricultural industry chain resilience proxy. Although agricultural TFP exhibits a statistically detectable partial mediating pattern in this correlational relationship, the economic magnitude of this indirect channel is extremely modest. As such, this finding indicates a potential theoretical transmission pathway rather than providing definitive empirical evidence for a causal mechanism. The promotion effect exhibits clear regional heterogeneity, with the strongest effect in Northern Anhui, followed by Central Anhui, while the coefficient is positive but insignificant in Southern Anhui. Furthermore, a single-threshold effect of the relative grain yield is identified; that is, the positive association between rural-oriented digital development and resilience proxy cannot be statistically detected when the grain yield remains below the threshold. Only after the agricultural grain yield increases can digital-related rural development release its resilience-related empowering dividends. We note that both composite indices are subject to measurement constraints linked to the local agricultural economic scale and broad rural digital conditions; these limitations are further discussed in the paper. This study provides empirical correlational evidence for the implementation of differentiated digital agriculture policies in major grain-producing provinces.

title: An AI-Based Multi-Stage Optimization Framework for Fuel Cell-Integrated Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems
abstract: The increasing penetration of intermittent renewable energy sources necessitates capacity-sizing frameworks that integrate operational forecasting with long-term economic assessment. Here, we propose a multi-stage optimization framework for fuel-cell-integrated renewable energy systems that combines machine-learning-based forecasting of electricity demand and photovoltaic (PV) generation, hysteresis-based dynamic simulation, and component cost sensitivity analysis. Using standard meteorological and time-derived variables, the forecasting models achieved coefficients of determination (R2) of 0.866 and 0.876 for electricity demand and PV generation, respectively, on evaluation subsets obtained through random 80/20 splits. The numbers of PV panels, battery energy storage system (BESS) units, and fuel cells were optimized under predefined grid power supply ratio (GPSR) scenarios using meteorological data from 2011 to 2022, and their operation was evaluated using weather data from 2023 to 2024. Most scenarios satisfied the 10% state-of-charge (SOC) criterion. The GPSR 0.5 scenario was classified as Fail because SOC fell below this criterion for four consecutive hourly time steps; nevertheless, electricity supply was maintained without shortage throughout the validation period. The reconfigurational gain proposed in this study quantifies the difference in levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) between retaining a baseline configuration and reoptimizing capacities at identical component unit prices. At a cost ratio of 0.1 for the respective component, battery cost reduction yielded an additional 35.48% saving at GPSR 0.4, whereas fuel-cell cost reduction yielded an additional 11.4% saving at GPSR 0.5. Under the 2030 scenario, with the PV unit price held constant and battery and fuel-cell prices set to 49% and 44% of their current values, respectively, LCOE decreased to 0.1008–0.1286 USD/kWh.

title: Sustainable Plant Disease Management: Current Advances, Challenges, and Future Directions
abstract: Sustainable plant disease management is essential for maintaining agricultural productivity, environmental health, and global food security. Climate change has increased crop vulnerability to emerging and re-emerging plant diseases, posing significant challenges for agricultural sustainability. Although synthetic chemical pesticides have long been effective for disease control, their extensive use is increasingly questioned because of environmental contamination, pathogen resistance, and potential risks to human and ecosystem health. Consequently, plant disease management (PDM) is shifting toward more sustainable and integrated approaches. Future strategies are expected to incorporate multiple disciplines, including: (i) biological control and microbiome engineering to enhance natural plant defense mechanisms; (ii) advanced molecular and genomic technologies, such as CRISPR/Cas systems, RNA interference (RNAi), and epigenome editing, to develop durable disease resistance; (iii) smart delivery systems for the precise application of antimicrobial compounds and defense elicitors; (iv) nanotechnology-based platforms for the targeted delivery of nutrients, pesticides, and biocontrol agents, improving efficacy while reducing chemical inputs; (v) digital and precision agriculture technologies, including remote sensing, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and artificial intelligence (AI)-based diagnostics, to facilitate real-time disease surveillance and targeted interventions; and (vi) agroecological practices such as crop diversification, soil health restoration, and climate-smart farming to enhance agroecosystem resilience. These innovations aim not only to suppress plant pathogens but also to build sustainable, adaptive, and resilient agricultural systems that address future environmental and biological challenges.

title: Authority–Inference Separation in Agentic Finance: Intent-Bound Control, EVM Enforcement, and Replayable Assurance
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents can propose financial transactions, but model output should not itself grant execution authority. We develop Authority–Inference Separation (AIS), in which an independent control plane evaluates a typed financial action intent (FAI) against institutional mandate, policy, current state, human approvals, and exact economic terms before issuing single-use authority. We specify the threat and control boundaries, instantiate AIS across four financial domains, and test fixed fixtures, a separate external-policy-gateway baseline, mechanism ablations, two small open-weight models, and an Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) contract. In 36 fixed attack fixtures, AIS accepted no unauthorized effect, compared with 36 for direct execution and 20 for prompt policy. A gateway without execution-bound authorization accepted all 20 targeted post-decision attacks. Both models followed all eight injected counterparty substitutions; the independent gate prevented unsafe execution but authorized only six of 16 legitimate requests, exposing an availability cost. The EVM prototype rejected replay, revocation, stale-policy, and call-mutation attempts. These are conformance tests, not field estimates. AIS combines established security mechanisms around financial authority and replayable evidence. A ledger can enforce granted authority and record settlement, while mandate legitimacy, delivery, and accounting require complementary governance and evidence.

title: Transformation of Segment and Consolidated Reporting of Agricultural Holdings Amidst the Active Turnover of Digital Rights
abstract: The article presents the results of a study of the methodological aspects of transforming segmental and consolidated reporting of agro‑holdings in the context of active circulation of digital rights within a group of companies. It has been established that the digitalization of the agricultural sector leads to the emergence of fundamentally new objects of accounting and disclosure, which require a revision of traditional approaches to the formation of consolidated financial statements. A methodology for identifying and classifying digital rights for the purposes of segmental reporting has been developed, which includes four successive stages: analysis of the economic essence, assessment of the nature of circulation, determination of the degree of connection with operating activities, and formation of information disclosure. A procedure for eliminating intra‑group transactions involving digital rights in the preparation of consolidated financial statements has been proposed; it includes identifying the transactions, assessing their materiality, determining their fair value, and adjusting the consolidated figures. Based on the real parameters of the first in Russia issue of utilitarian digital rights by an agro‑industrial company, a hypothetical situation of intra‑group turnover has been modelled, and the impact of these transactions on segment reporting indicators has been calculated. It has been substantiated that digital rights circulating within the group can act both as financial instruments and as specific assets requiring separate disclosure. The key problems in accounting for digital rights have been identified, related to the lack of unified valuation standards, the uncertainty of the legal status, and the insufficient automation of consolidation procedures. It has been shown that after eliminating intra‑group transactions, only a real asset remains in the consolidated financial statements — the commodity collateral, while intra‑group liabilities and revenues are excluded, and the difference between the carrying value of the liability and the fair value of the collateral requires separate disclosure.

title: Transformation of the Russian Insurance Market Under Sanctions Pressure: Adaptation Mechanisms and New Growth Points
abstract: The aim of the article is a comprehensive analysis of the transformation processes taking place in the Russian insurance market under the infl uence of unprecedented sanctions pressure from unfriendly states in the period 2022–2026, as well as identifi cation of adaptation mechanisms and promising growth points for the insurance industry of the Russian Federation in the context of structural adjustment of the national economy. Objectives: To assess quantitative and qualitative changes in the structure of the Russian insurance market in the post-sanctions period; to study the mechanisms of adaptation of Russian insurance organizations to new business conditions caused by sanctions pressure on the Russian Federation, including reorientation to the domestic reinsurance market; to identify key growth points of the Russian insurance market formed as a result of the sanctions isolation of major players in the Russian insurance market and the existence of a sanctions ban on reinsurance develop evidence-based recommendations for improving the regulatory policy in the fi eld of domestic insurance. The methodological basis of this study consists of analytical (analysis of scientific publications in the context of the research topic) and comparative methods of scientific cognition. The authors also used systemic and structural-functional approaches. Methods of statistical and comparative analysis, economic-mathematical modeling, and expert assessments were employed. The authors have established that the total insurance premiums in the Russian market in 2025 reached 1.9–4 trillion rubles, showing an 18.4 % increase compared to 2024. The key role of RNPC as a system-forming element of the domestic reinsurance infrastructure has been identified. The life insurance and voluntary health insurance segments registered faster growth. A stable relationship was found between the dynamics of import substitution and the demand for property insurance. Conclusions: The Russian insurance market has demonstrated high structural resilience to external shocks. The key adaptation mechanisms were the development of the national reinsurance infrastructure, digitalization of sales and expansion of the product line. New growth points have been identified: insurance of export operations with friendly countries, agricultural insurance, and cyber insurance. The essential role of state regulation is confirmed in terms of creating favorable conditions for market development.

title: Digital Service Ecosystem for Rural SME Competitiveness Through Smart Agribusiness Transformation
abstract: Rural Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) increasingly face a structural gap between established production capabilities and limited digital capacity to capture market value directly. In rural agribusiness settings, this challenge is compounded by intermediary dependence, uneven digital literacy, and fragmented institutional support. This study examines how a rural entrepreneurial ecosystem can strengthen SME competitiveness through the integration of smart farming, village institutions, market connectivity, and digital transformation in Desa Cibodas, West Java, Indonesia. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was employed, combining a survey of 95 agricultural SME actors with qualitative case study analysis based on interviews with 14 key informants and documentary evidence. The findings show that digital adoption readiness, institutional support, and smart farming capability jointly contribute to SME competitiveness, with digital capability emerging as the strongest predictor. Qualitative findings further identify five interconnected themes and show how BUMDes, smart farming, packaging infrastructure, and emerging digital marketplace initiatives interact within a four-layer rural entrepreneurial ecosystem. The study contributes by conceptualizing digital transformation as a connecting ecosystem-level capability that links production and institutional strengths with market-oriented competitiveness. The findings highlight the need for integrated digital marketplace development, stronger BUMDes coordination, and targeted digital capacity building to improve rural SMEs' market autonomy and competitiveness.
journal: International Journal of Cyber and IT Service Management

title: Диспропорции рынка труда в стратегии обеспечения экономической безопасности региона
abstract: Усиление пространственного неравенства регионов угрожает их экономической безопасности. Исследованы территориально-отраслевые диспропорции рынка труда Республики Башкортостан. Цель – формирование регуляторных подходов к сглаживанию дифференциации занятости. Методология базируется на статистическом, сравнительном анализе и SWOT-моделировании данных Росстата. Установлено, что отток трудового потенциала оголяет периферию, формируя межмуниципальный зарплатный спред до 1,9 раза. Сформулированы механизмы преодоления демографических и финансовых диспропорций через налоговое стимулирование, гранты малому бизнесу и платформы удаленной занятости. Growing spatial inequality in regions threatens their economic security. This study examines territorial and sectoral imbalances in the labor market of the Republic of Bashkortostan. The objective is to develop regulatory approaches to mitigate employment differentiation. The methodology relies on statistical, comparative analysis, and SWOT modeling of Rosstat data. The research reveals that labor potential outflows deplete the periphery, driving an inter-municipal wage spread of up to 1.9 times. Mechanisms to overcome demographic and financial imbalances are proposed, including tax incentives, small business grants, and remote employment platforms.

title: Explainability Aware Heterogeneous Temporal Graph Transformer for Automated Genetic Disorder Detection from Genomic Data
abstract: : Genetic disorders affect millions worldwide, posing major challenges for accurate diagnosis and effective treatments. New developments in genomic technologies, especially Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS), have enhanced the classification of genetic modification and improved diagnostic abilities. Moreover, the Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) methods emerged as efficient tools for evaluating the intricate genomic data and determining the patterns, which can be generally complex to identify by employing conventional analytical techniques. Additionally, the Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has developed as a significant constituent in the analysis of genomic data by enhancing the interpretability of DL methods and showing the contribution of main genetic features involved in the detection of genetic disorders. This study presents an Explainability-Aware Heterogeneous Temporal Graph Transformer for Automated Genetic Disorder Detection (XHTGT-AGDD) approach. The primary objective of the proposed model is to improve the reliability and accuracy of genetic disorder detection from genomic data by integrating advanced techniques. Initially, preprocessing is performed using quantile transformation to normalize the input data for robust analysis. Following preprocessing, feature selection is performed using the fire hawk optimizer to identify the most informative feature subsets from the genomic data. Besides, the classification task is accomplished using a heterogeneous temporal graph transformer, which captures complex relationships and temporal dependencies among genomic features. To further refine the learning process, hippopotamus optimization algorithm is employed for model optimization. In addition, an explainability mechanism based on SHAP is incorporated to interpret the model predictions and highlight the individual genetic features toward the final decision. The experimental result analysis of the XHTGT-AGDD model is performed using a benchmark dataset. The simulation results reported the enhanced results of the XHTGT-AGDD technique in terms of several measures, achieving an accuracy of 99.12%. Therefore, the proposed model provides reliable and effective performance for automated genetic disorder detection from genomic data.
