We state clearly which quantities in the case study are computed from data and which are simulated governance inputs, and we discuss the design limits of a single-dataset evaluation.

title: Black-Box Red-Teaming of Multi-Agent Systems via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in multi-agent systems (MAS) to accomplish complex tasks. Prior black-box red-teaming attacks mainly focus on single agents, but we find that these methods are far less effective in MAS, where multiple sub-agents may not directly interact with the user. Therefore, we introduce ReMAS, the first reinforcement learning-based red-teaming framework tailored to MASs, which fine-tunes attacker LLMs to generate effective adversarial prompts for system prompt extraction. The framework follows a two-step process: first, a rewrite stage refines base attack prompts to increase extraction success, and second, a template generation stage constructs attack templates that improve the likelihood of invoking specific sub-agents and thus revealing their system prompts. Extensive experiments show that our method substantially improves attack success rates compared to existing black-box attacks, with transferability across different backend LLMs and MAS structures. These results underscore the vulnerabilities of multi-agent systems and the importance of developing stronger defenses against adaptive black-box adversaries.

title: Unit-Aware Differentially Private Quantum Machine Learning for Clinical and Wearable Health Data
abstract: Clinical registries and wearable sensors support early health-risk assessment, yet models trained on these records may leak sensitive information when released. Differential privacy (DP) bounds this leakage by injecting noise whose total magnitude grows with the number of trainable parameters, a cost especially severe for small health cohorts. This motivates parameter efficient models including quantum machine learning (QML), whose variational circuits can represent complex decision boundaries with few trainable parameters. It raises a question: at matched input dimensionality and privacy budget, does a quantum model retain more utility than a classical one? We investigate this question on three clinical cohorts and one wearable cohort, treating each clinical record or participant as a privacy unit. We compare capacity-matched quantum, multilayer perceptron, and logistic regression models across five privacy budgets and five seeds. The quantum model leads on three clinical cohorts by up to 0.104 ROC AUC averaged across budgets; however, trails on the wearable cohort, where the small number of participants requires substantial noise. No difference survives Holm correction across 24 tests, so these results indicate a trend rather than a quantum advantage. An analytic gradient bound shows that lower clipping thresholds can improve utility by reducing noise despite clipping bias. Finally, an experiment on IBM quantum computer (ibm_fez, a 156-qubit superconducting processor) using eight fixed test cases yields mean absolute probability errors of 0.046 (private) and 0.063 (non-private) relative to simulation, supporting the feasibility of inference on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/TITANS-Lab-Artifacts/DP-QML-Health.

title: Attention-based Classification for Indirect Prompt Injection
abstract: Indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks, in which adversarial instructions are embedded in external data processed by a language model, pose a significant threat to the integrity of deployed LLM agents. Attention Tracker (Hung et al., 2025) is a recently proposed white-box detection method that identifies prompt injection attacks by monitoring how a model's attention is distributed between user task tokens and data tokens, claiming dataset-agnostic detection via a scalar focus score threshold. In this paper, we provide the first evaluation of Attention Tracker in a realistic agentic IPI setting using the AgentDojo benchmark, finding that the dataset agnosticism claim does not hold. We find that in agentic environments, long structured tool outputs subvert the fundamental assumptions Attention Tracker makes about attention that the method depends on and produces near-chance detection on AgentDojo across most model families. We propose AttnDA, an extension replacing the scalar threshold with a Fisher Linear Discriminant Analysis classifier over the per-head focus score vector, and evaluate both methods in a cross-dataset setting spanning four benchmarks. AttnDA improves detection performance across agentic and tool-integrated benchmarks, though transfer to AgentDojo remains challenging regardless of classifier choice. A covariance ablation further shows that removing inter-head correlation structure substantially contributes to performance, with complex covariance assumptions causing significant degradation on cross-domain data. These results indicate that the attentional distraction signal underlying focus-score-based detection does not transfer reliably to agentic environments, and that learned linear classifiers over head-level attention features offer improved detection performance, provided training data from the target deployment domain is available.

title: Diffusion Sensitivity Geometry and Strong Duality for Optimal Privacy-Utility Tradeoffs
abstract: Existing approaches to differential privacy in diffusion models rely on loose sensitivity bounds and isotropic Gaussian noise, leading to unnecessary estimation error. We develop a framework for the optimal privacy-utility tradeoff of ideal diffusion denoisers, replacing conservative bounds with exact sensitivity characterizations and provably optimal noise calibration. First, we show that worst-case sensitivity over datasets of arbitrary size can be characterized exactly using only two records. For a data domain of size $m$, this reduces the analysis to at most $m(m-1)$ constraints, regardless of dataset size. Our characterization can be arbitrarily tighter than conventional diameter-based sensitivity bounds, revealing potentially unbounded improvements in noise calibration. Second, we obtain exact privacy guarantees for Rényi, approximate, and Gaussian differential privacy, as well as mutual-information privacy for binary records, avoiding the looseness of previous generic privacy conversions. Finally, we show that the minimum achievable weighted mean-squared error can be computed through a semidefinite program and prove strong duality, providing certificates of global optimality.

title: When AI Gets Cheaper, Do Prices Follow? Information Delays and Algorithmic Pricing
abstract: We examine whether lower costs of running AI models lead to lower prices, and whether delays in observing competitors' prices and limits on price changes affect how much consumers benefit. We study a simulated market with two differentiated sellers, logit demand, and tabular Q learning. A factorial experiment varies the age of rival price information, how often sellers can revise prices, whether production costs fall, and differences in firm quality and costs. We evaluate policies trained on 60 paired market seeds in each of 16 conditions, for 960 training runs, and measure expected consumer surplus after learning ends. In the main setting with identical firms and falling costs, the estimated interaction between information delay and repricing frequency on consumer surplus is -0.00025 normalized units, with a 95% paired seed bootstrap interval of [-0.0402, 0.0393]. The interval includes zero, as do intervals for tests of whether the interaction changes with the cost regime or differences between firms. With the shortest information delay and the ability to revise prices every period, average price reductions equal 55.6% and 44.0% of the imposed cost reduction for the two firms. Mean consumer surplus under the learned policies is below the corresponding static grid Nash benchmark in all 16 conditions. The findings show that simulated cost savings need not be fully passed on to buyers. They do not establish collusion or describe pricing by actual AI providers.

title: Securing Agentic Commerce Through Behavior-Aware Fraud Detection and Cybersecurity for Trusted AI-Agent Payment Authorization
abstract: The growing use of autonomous artificial intelligence agents in digital commerce creates new security concerns involving agent impersonation, unauthorized payments, compromised agents, and misuse of delegated authority. This research introduces the Autonomous Commerce Agent Guard System (ACAGS), a cybersecurity framework combining supervised machine learning, behavioral analytics, agent-specific authorization controls, and explainable AI. The framework was evaluated using synthetic financial transaction data augmented with simulated agent characteristics and five adversarial scenarios. XGBoost was selected following comparisons with alternative classifiers. Across ten experimental runs, behavioral features improved mean F1-score from 52.12% to 67.49%, with agent-specific features increasing performance to 69.46%. The framework achieved detection rates of 99.77% for abnormal agent behavior, 99.73% for impersonation, and 100% for malicious delegation and authorization-scope violations. Compromised-agent detection reached 72.27%. ACAGS also supported APPROVE, REVIEW, and REJECT authorization outcomes, with SHAP explanations providing model interpretability. The results demonstrate the potential of combining behavioral intelligence and delegated authorization controls to strengthen simulated agentic-commerce payment security, while highlighting the need for validation using real-world transactions.

title: Reconstructing speech influence in English-language media discourse: an evidence-based analytical model and practical interpretation tasks
abstract: Media messages influence interpretation not only through explicit argument but through patterns of thematic prominence, evaluative lexis, agency representation, metaphor, presupposition and the distribution of reported voices. Their pragmatic organisation becomes visible when individual linguistic choices are connected with the communicative context and with one another. An integrated Evidence-to-Influence Reconstruction Matrix combines perspectives from discourse studies, framing theory, appraisal, pragmatics, argumentation and multimodal analysis. The matrix relates communicative context, inferred intention, strategic orientation, tactical realisation, linguistic and visual evidence, implicit meaning and anticipated audience positioning. Its application to verified reporting on the Nordic heatwave of July 2025 differentiates scientific attribution from journalistic framing without equating evaluative language with manipulation. Three analytical tables and a sequence of eight interpretation exercises specify how universalisation, evaluative intensity, metaphorical representation, source attribution, grammatical agency and presupposition can be connected to evidence-based explanations. The conceptual contribution concerns the systematic distinction between identifying a discourse device and reconstructing its contextual function. Interpretative adequacy depends on the strength of textual evidence, consideration of alternative readings and separation of anticipated pragmatic positioning from observed audience effects. The resulting framework provides a coherent basis for close analysis of English-language media discourse and for the design of demanding, verifiable interpretation tasks.

title: Preprocessing approaches for MRI images for deep learning algorithms
abstract: This study investigates the intelligent analysis of MRI radiomic features for early and accurate breast cancer detection. It outlines methods for extracting high-dimensional radiomic characteristics (shape, texture, intensity, and gray-level dependencies) and processing them using machine learning algorithms. Integrating radiomics with AI models enables precise differentiation of benign and malignant lesions, improves non-invasive diagnostic accuracy, and serves as a decision-support tool for radiologists.

title: Improving the Organizational and Methodological Mechanisms for Formulating Accounting Policies and Strengthening Accounting Controls in Agricultural Enterprises
abstract: This study examines the organizational and methodological mechanisms for formulating accounting policies and strengthening accounting controls in agricultural enterprises. The research employs comparative analysis, documentary examination, systematic assessment, and conceptual modelling to identify existing accounting challenges and develop recommendations for their improvement. Based on the available case materials relating to “Tarakkiyot” farm in Nishon district, Kashkadarya region, Uzbekistan, the study identifies key priorities for improving primary accounting documentation, crop-specific analytical accounting, document circulation, and inventory verification. An integrated organizational and methodological framework is proposed to coordinate accounting-policy formulation, transaction recording, internal control procedures, and financial reporting. The scientific contribution of the study lies in developing a systematic approach that integrates accounting methods and control mechanisms while considering the specific characteristics of agricultural production. The findings provide a methodological foundation for enhancing the reliability, transparency, and managerial usefulness of accounting information in agricultural enterprises. The proposed framework requires further empirical validation.
journal: Academic Journal of Digital Economics and Stability

title: Grid-spacing sensitivity of Rossby wave breaking to mesoscale diabatic processes
abstract: Forecast busts – episodes of abnormally low forecast skill – remain a persistent challenge for numerical weather prediction despite steady improvements in forecasting skill. Previous studies have highlighted the roles of moist mesoscale processes and diabatically generated potential vorticity (PV) anomalies in triggering rapid error growth and downstream circulation misrepresentation, processes whose representation is highly sensitive to model grid spacing. In this study, we select three events that were classified as forecast busts in the Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) and investigate their sensitivity to horizontal grid spacing. The cases comprise (i) the explosive cyclogenesis of Storm Dennis (February 2020), (ii) a blocking event following the extratropical transition of Hurricane Franklin (September 2023), and (iii) a June 2020 event characterized by ridge amplification due to a warm conveyor belt (WCB) over the North Atlantic. For each case, we use IFS initial conditions and perform global ICON ( Icosahedral Non-hydrostatic model) ensemble forecasts with horizontal grid spacings ranging from 40 to 2.5 km. We evaluate forecast skill against ERA5 reanalysis using anomaly correlation coefficients (ACC) of 500 hPa geopotential height. Across all cases, forecast busts are consistently linked to diabatically generated upper-level negative PV anomalies originating from strong latent heat release in organized convection, including mesoscale convective systems (MCSs), extratropical cyclones, and WCB ascent. These PV anomalies modify the upper-level waveguide, perturb the jet stream, and amplify downstream Rossby wave packets, degrading medium-range predictability. Decreasing horizontal grid spacing systematically improves the representation of diabatic processes, enhances the spatial extent and intensity of upper-level negative PV anomalies, and reduces wave-amplitude error growth. We observe that kilometer-scale simulations with horizontal grid spacing ≤5 km consistently yield the highest forecast skill, with substantial ACC improvements relative to coarser-resolution simulations. All three case studies systematically show that mesoscale diabatic processes are a primary source of forecast error in bust situations, and that kilometer-scale global simulations significantly improve the representation of scale interactions governing Rossby wave amplification. These findings underscore the importance of kilometer-scale simulations for reliably representing scale interactions in strongly diabatic flow regimes. They are not only important for weather forecasting but also for climate simulations which feature long-standing deficiencies in capturing Rossby wave breaking and associate extreme weather events.

title: Engineering Intelligent Decision-Support Systems for Sustainable Crop Productivity in Emerging Economies
abstract: Developing economies face major challenges in achieving sustainable agricultural productivity, including poor infrastructure, climate change and poor resource use. Intelligent decision-support systems (IDSS) provide a data-driven approach to enhancing agricultural management practices, resulting in enhanced crop production, resource efficiency, and resilience to environmental issues. This paper discusses the engineering principles of IDSS in agriculture with a focus on the application of Internet of Things (IoT) sensor networks, cloud computing, machine learning methods, and geospatial analysis. The research looks in detail at models for forecasting crop production, controlling diseases and pests, scheduling irrigation and optimising nutrients. We study architectural issues in depth, including modularity, scalability, interoperability and energy-efficient design. The paper discusses challenges faced by the developing economies like limited connectivity, diversity of data sources and cyber security threats and suggests strategies to overcome them. In this paper we propose a reference framework for the combination of edge intelligence, predictive analytics and user-centric decision dashboards that facilitate smallholder farmers and agribusiness actors to make informed, timely and sustainable decisions. Results suggest that well-designed IDSS can increase efficiency of water and fertiliser use by up to 40%, decrease crop losses due to biotic and abiotic stresses, and increase total productivity. This review further contributes to the literature by providing a systematic engineering perspective on the design, implementation, and improvement of IDSS for agricultural systems in resource-limited settings.
journal: ABUAD Journal of Engineering Research and Development (AJERD)

title: Business Model Sustainability under Mature Market Competition in China's New Energy Vehicle Industry A Comparison of BYD and NIO
abstract: China's new energy vehicle market has shifted from rapid expansion toward mature-market competition, placing simultaneous pressure on pricing, research and development expenditure, and service investment. Using comparative case analysis, this study applies Porter's Five Forces, value-chain analysis, and the value, rarity, imitability, and organization (VRIO) framework to compare BYD's vertically integrated model with NIO's ecosystem-based operating model. The findings indicate that BYD's coordination of batteries, electric drives, power semiconductors, and vehicle manufacturing creates cost and iteration advantages from key components through large-scale production. These benefits are nevertheless constrained by multi-brand complexity, service demands, and technology-path lock-in. NIO differentiates itself through battery swapping, direct service channels, software, and user communities, thereby sustaining post-purchase engagement; however, the durability of this model depends on user density, network utilization, and open standards. Under current conditions, vertical integration is more resilient in cost control, profitability, and overseas replication, whereas ecosystem operations offer greater potential in intelligent technologies, software, and user relationships. Manufacturing-oriented firms should pursue selective integration while strengthening software-enabled services. Ecosystem-oriented firms should improve the utilization of energy-replenishment assets, expand standards-based collaboration, and convert user experience into recurring revenue.
journal: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Why Customers Welcome or Resist AI Salespeople: Formation Mechanisms of Algorithm Aversion and Algorithm Appreciation in Large Language Model Sales
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) now answer product questions, recommend items and help close deals in online shops, banks and telecom services. Customers react to these AI sales agents in two opposite ways. Some avoid them, a pattern researchers call algorithm aversion, while others prefer them to human advice, a pattern called algorithm appreciation. This paper reviews the main empirical studies on both patterns and asks how each one forms when the "algorithm" is a conversational sales agent. Drawing on research in judgment and decision making, consumer behavior and human computer interaction, it proposes a framework with three layers. The first layer contains the cues that an LLM sales agent gives off. The second layer contains five psychological pathways that operate during the conversation: competence belief, error sensitivity, empathy and uniqueness concern, social presence, and perceived control. The third layer contains situational conditions such as product type, the timing of AI identity disclosure, the customer's emotional state and prior AI experience. Six propositions are derived. The paper argues that aversion and appreciation are not fixed traits of customers but outcomes of how these layers combine in a particular sales encounter, and it discusses implications for firms and for future student research.
journal: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Urban Computing Infrastructure and the Integration of Digitalisation and Green Development in Enterprises
abstract: One of the main problems of the digital economy in recent years is how to achieve the combined development of digitalisation and green transformation in enterprises. Based on the data of Chinese A-share listed companies, this paper will systematically study the impact, transmission mechanism and heterogeneity of urban computing infrastructure on enterprise integration in digital and green development over time using a time-fixed-effects model. Based on the above results, it can be concluded that the urban computing infrastructure has a positive effect on enterprises' integration of digital and green development, and this effect is robust to all kinds of sensitivity tests, such as adding control variables, changing the sample period, modifying standard errors, lagging explanatory variables and including industry fixed effects. Based on the analysis of the mechanism, the computing infrastructure will reduce financing constraints, promote the integration of industry and increase real-economy industrial upgrading and enterprise innovation. Based on the test of heterogeneity, the positive effect is relatively strong for non-state-owned enterprises and in non-competitive industries. This paper provides empirical evidence on the use of computing infrastructure for digital-green development in enterprises and offers policy recommendations to help the government tackle the problem of carbon emissions from infrastructure construction by means of differentiated policies.
journal: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: AI in the Game Industry: Latest Research Advances and Future Direction
abstract: The paper is a summary of the current developments of AI in the gaming sector between 2023 and 2026, including automated generation of content, intelligent game agents (NPCs) and large language models (LLMs), game testing and quality assurance by means of AI, modeling of players and dynamic difficulty management, as well as reorganization of the industry and the new concept of the so-called AI-native games. This study reveals that the use of AI will not be used to assist in the creation of contents but rather become part of the core elements of game mechanics. Real-time diffusion models can model game engines (GameNGen), LLM agents are already implemented in commercial QA systems (TITAN framework), reinforcement learning and player modeling can be applied to adjust the difficulty of the game dynamically based on the data. At the same time, there exists a discussion in the field of efficiency of the process, the creative aspect of it, and how much restructuring of the organization should be done. The authors also suggest some of the criteria which can be used to determine whether a game is an AI-native game (counterfactual testing) and indicate the open issues like automatic playability tests, user acceptance, safety of the contents and ownership of the copyright.
journal: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Managerial Innovation as a Lever for Digital Transformation Success: Toward an Integrated Organizational Value Creation Framework
abstract: The accelerating pace of digital transformation has fundamentally restructured competitive landscapes across industries, compelling organizations to reconsider not only their technological investments but, more critically, their managerial architectures and innovation capacities. While extant scholarship has extensively examined the technological dimensions of digital transformation, comparatively limited attention has been devoted to managerial innovation as a primary enabling condition for sustained digital transformation success. This article addresses that gap by developing a theoretically grounded, integrative conceptual framework—the Integrated Organizational Value Creation Framework (IOVCF)—that articulates the causal pathways through which managerial innovation drives digital transformation and ultimately generates organizational value. Anchored in four complementary theoretical perspectives—Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the Resource-Based View (RBV), Organizational Change Theory, and Socio-Technical Systems Theory—the framework models a cascading logic: managerial innovation cultivates organizational capabilities (agility, learning, adaptability, and collaborative intelligence), which in turn facilitate digital transformation success (technology adoption, process digitalization, data integration, and digital innovation), culminating in multi-dimensional organizational value creation (operational performance, resilience, stakeholder satisfaction, and sustainable competitive advantage). Twelve formal research propositions are derived and theoretically justified. Managerial implications emphasize that digital transformation leaders must invest in organizational redesign, agile management practices, digital culture formation, knowledge management systems, employee empowerment, and collaborative ecosystems alongside—and often prior to—technology deployment. A rich agenda for future empirical research is outlined, encompassing cross-national validation, SME contexts, AI-enabled transformation, and sustainability-oriented digital strategies.
journal: International Journal of Automation and Digital Transformation

title: An Integrated XAI-RL Architecture for Ethical Decision-Making in Autonomous Robots
abstract: Can a robot's ethical reasoning be transparent without slowing it down? That is the question we set out to answer. Autonomous robots now make decisions that affect people's lives, and if we cannot understand how they decide, trust becomes a serious problem. We built a unified architecture that couples Explainable AI (XAI) with Reinforcement Learning (RL) through three connected components: a Perception Layer for situational awareness, a Decision Reasoning Layer that breaks agent utility down into measurable ethical sub-rewards (safety, fairness, and well-being), and a contrastive Explainability Engine grounded in a real-time Ethical Ledger. We tested it against Black-Box RL and two post-hoc XRL baselines (LIME and SHAP) across two simulation environments and a physical robot pilot on a TurtleBot3 platform. Our system reached 92±3% ethical alignment in simulation and 89±4% on the physical platform, beating every baseline (p < 0.01 throughout). In a controlled, IRB-approved user study (N=128), participants rated it higher on trust (4.5±0.4), understandability (4.6±0.3), and perceived safety (4.4±0.5) than the alternatives. Explanations were also fast: 4.2±0.6 ms on average, versus 18.3±2.1 ms for SHAP and 12.7±1.8 ms for LIME on the same hardware—well within real-time limits. An ablation study and sensitivity analysis back up these architectural choices.
journal: International Journal of Automation and Digital Transformation

title: From Emotion to Expression: The AL–DL–CL Framework for Understanding Communication in the Age of AI and Digital Media
abstract: Rapid progress in digital media and artificial intelligence is transforming human communication, facilitating the rapid exchange of messages and minimizing the chances of reflective interpretation. Existing theories in linguistics, psychology, and cultural studies address the structural, cognitive, or social aspects of language, yet fail to explain how emotional processing, internal linguistic structuring, and culturally mediated communication function as a coherent, dynamic system. Through this model, the authors present the AL–DL–CL framework that explores how three layers are engaged in a process that results in communication, through a recursive interaction between the Automatic Layer (AL), the Deliberate Layer (DL), and the Cultural Language Layer (CL). In such a process, the affective or unconscious processes in AL are consistently reframed into structured internal representations via DL, and through CL, and translated back into culturally-expressed language serves as a feedback mechanism, with a tendency to modify cognition and emotional response. Based on a multi-method exploratory approach of sequential cultural transmission, clinical case study analysis, and group-based validation, the results indicate that language is not so much a static container for meaning as a process of reconstruction that is molded by the dynamic interaction between emotion, cognition, and culture. This model also demonstrates how digitally mediated communication can amplify AL-directed reaction and limit DL-level thinking, which increases the potential for misinterpretation, polarization, or misinformation. The AL–DL–CL framework provides guidance in a unified theoretical perspective around language emergence, responsible AI design and digital literacy and intercultural discourse based on the continuous transformation system of communication, and not on the linear encoding.
journal: International Journal of Civilizations Studies & Tolerance Sciences

title: Соціальні інвестиції та соціальний захист як стратегічна розвилка політики ЄС у сфері соціальної економіки
abstract: The European Social Model is evolving under the simultaneous pressure to expand social investment and preserve the protective functions of welfare states amid fiscal constraints and new social risks. The purpose of the study is to theoretically substantiate the relationship between social investment and social protection in EU policy and to develop a conceptual model for reconciling these logics at the supranational level. The study is theoretical and is based on a systemic approach, critical analysis of academic literature and EU policy documents, qualitative comparative analysis of welfare-state models, typologisation, and conceptual modelling. The study clarifies the functional relationship between social investment and social protection; systematizes four welfare-state transformation scenarios along two dimensions – the dynamics of social investment and social protection; and identifies an institutional mechanism for reconciling these logics through interconnected strategic, instrumental, and operational levels. The scientific contribution lies in advancing a scenario-based approach to EU social policy analysis by integrating a matrix of social investment and social protection dynamics with a three-level model of supranational policy coordination. The proposed framework uses scenario configurations to differentiate policy priorities, identify relevant policy instruments, and inform subsequent adjustments through monitoring and feedback. This integration represents a conceptual analytical contribution rather than an empirically validated mechanism of policy effectiveness. The migration dimension is interpreted as an application of this framework to the integration of migrants’ human capital rather than as an independent element of theoretical novelty. The theoretically grounded proposition that simultaneous development of investment and protective logics is preferable requires further empirical verification using data from EU Member States. The practical relevance lies in the potential application of the proposed framework to the analysis of social-policy trajectories and the design of Ukraine’s social recovery.
journal: Bulletin of the Academy of Labor, Social Relations and Tourism. Series: Economics, Psychology and Management

title: Localizing Early Numeracy Policy in Decentralized ECE Systems: Evidence from Indonesia
abstract: Early numeracy is central to school readiness and educational equity, yet national policies may be implemented unevenly across geographically and institutionally diverse early childhood education (ECE) settings. This study examined the implementation of Indonesia's 2024 early literacy-numeracy policy in urban, rural, and remote settings in West Nusa Tenggara and explored the feasibility of the LENTAS (Locally Contextualized Early Numeracy with Technology Support) model. A convergent concurrent mixed-methods design combined policy and document analysis, a teacher-parent survey, interviews with 15 key informants, focus groups with 50 parents or caregivers, and an embedded single-group pre-post pilot involving 60 children and six teachers across three ECE sites. Of 900 survey questionnaires distributed, 662 complete responses were included in the final analysis; the remaining 238 were incomplete or not returned. Findings showed an implementation gradient favoring the urban site, where teacher preparation, materials, infrastructure, and family-engagement mechanisms were stronger. Rural and remote implementation was constrained by limited professional support, unreliable infrastructure, restricted access to learning materials, and weaker cultural and linguistic alignment. LENTAS integrated culturally familiar play-based activities, offline-first technology, structured parent engagement, and continuous teacher mentoring. Descriptively, the proportion of children meeting the count-to-ten criterion increased from approximately 75% to 85% in Mataram, from 60% to 78% in East Lombok, and from 50% to 80% in remote Sumbawa. These preliminary changes should not be interpreted as causal effects because the pilot was small and lacked a comparison group. Equitable implementation therefore requires differentiated, sustained support for teachers, locally relevant resources, offline-capable technology, family-community partnerships, and stronger local coordination.
journal: Journal of Hunan University Natural Sciences

title: Continual Skill Adaptation for AI Agents Under Changing Tools and Policies: Selective Retention, Repair, and Retirement
abstract: AI agents increasingly maintain reusable skill libraries that encode procedures, tool interactions, and policy-dependent behavior. These libraries operate in environments where software dependencies evolve and governing policies are revised. Maintaining a skill therefore requires distinguishing behavior that must be retained, behavior that requires repair, and behavior that must be retired. Conventional regression-based adaptation is poorly suited to this setting when historical tests themselves encode superseded requirements. We introduce SkillShift, a benchmark comprising 60 reusable skills, 236 behavioral components, and 27 distinct real, dated change events (28 family-level transitions) across Python libraries, runtime environments, and published security policies, with executable validation, version-pinned environments, and a chronological evaluation protocol. We also introduce SkillLedger, which associates skill components with version-indexed evidence and selectively quarantines tests whose governing requirements have changed. Conventional regression gating never retired prohibited behavior while historical tests remained authoritative. SkillLedger addresses this limitation and improves repair after policy changes by 22.0 percentage points over a refreshed regression-gate baseline. However, the refreshed gate matches SkillLedger on retirement after policy changes and retains far more valid behavior (99.5% versus 82.9%). Most of SkillLedger’s accidental losses come from withholding working skills whose historical tests, often invoking removed APIs, kept failing. Further experiments expose limitations in conditional policy interpretation, structured-output parsing, and task-time retirement instructions. These findings establish a broader limitation of continual agent adaptation: the evidence used to validate a skill may become obsolete independently of the skill’s intended behavior. Reliable skill maintenance therefore requires evaluating the continuing validity of both behavioral requirements and their supporting tests.

title: ОСНОВЫ АРХИТЕКТУРЫ МУЛЬТИАГЕНТНОЙ СИСТЕМЫ ПРОВЕРКИ ОТЧЕТОВ ОБ ОЦЕНКЕ - РАЗДЕЛЕНИЕ ДЕТЕРМИНИРОВАННОГО И ГЕНЕРАТИВНОГО КОНТУРОВ
abstract: Автор рассматривает вопросы, связанные с автоматизированной проверкой отчетов об оценке и заключений их экспертиз. Анализирует проблемы использования как полностью детерминированных средства проверки, так и основанных только на использовании больших языковых моделей (LLM). Для устранения выявленных проблем предлагает использовать гибридную мультиагентную архитектуру, включающую как детерминированные инструменты, так и генеративные модели искусственного интеллекта, применение которой способствует решению задач прослеживаемости и воспроизводимости выводов проверки. Особенностью архитектуры является запрет на диалог агентов, вместо которого используется система артефактов. The author examines issues related to the automated verification of appraisal reports and their expert opinions. He analyzes the challenges of using both fully deterministic verification tools and those based solely on large-scale language models (LLM). To address these challenges, he proposes a hybrid multi-agent architecture, incorporating both deterministic tools and generative AI models. This architecture facilitates traceability and reproducibility of verification findings. A key feature of this architecture is the prohibition of interagent dialogue, which is replaced by a system of artifacts.
journal: Property relations in the Russian Federation

title: When AI Delegation Becomes Dependence: Administrative Judgment at Risk
abstract: Public organizations can delegate cognitive work to artificial intelligence while losing the capacity to scrutinize or resume that work. When does useful delegation become institutional dependence? This article develops a theory of institutional AI dependence as a task–role–workflow configuration combining substantial delegation of core cognition with insufficient task-required review or recovery capacity. It distinguishes two vulnerabilities: inadequate challenge during AI-supported work and inadequate capacity to continue judgment-intensive work when the system is unavailable. Extensive delegation with adequate distributed expertise and tested recovery constitutes managed delegation. Integrating cognitive offloading, automation, organizational learning, and public-administration research, the article extends Song et al.’s (2026) account of epistemic authority to organizational workflows and distinguishes perceived credibility from procedural authority embedded in defaults and override rules. Seven propositions connect practice displacement, challenge behavior, knowledge retention, subsequent delegation, and responsibility–control alignment. They specify how task-relevant practice, diagnostic feedback, and transferable knowledge shape retained capacity over time. The contribution is a task-relative diagnosis of threatened administrative judgment and a set of testable formation mechanisms. The framework guides public organizations in governing current agentic systems and preparing review and recovery arrangements for more capable AI.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Smart Technologies in the Hospitality Industry
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and smart technologies are transforming the way hotels function, but most studies have focused on a single application and do not quantify its operational value end to end. In this paper, we present and test five AI modules: using a common, simulated booking dataset for a resort hotel as well as for a city hotel (2015-2017) and a strict temporal train/test split, an integrated fourlayer framework (data and sensing, AI analytics, decision and automation, value) is proposed. For booking cancellation prediction, a gradient-boosting model yields well-calibrated results with an AUC of 0.845 [95% CI 0.841–0.848], with lead time, deposit policy, and distribution channel as the most important predictors. Classical methods, for forecasting occupancy from reservations made on the books, give the best results for periods up to 1 week before arrivals; by contrast, a gradient-boosting model produces accurate results at longer lead times, about 30 days prior to arrivals at the resort (MAPE 4.4% vs. 11.8% at 90 days prior). An ML risk-based overbooking policy can improve net room revenue by 0.55% and 0.32% (resort and city, respectively) compared with the historical policy and achieve 57–59% of the value of perfect information. The "K-means Segmentation" method shows 4 segments that guests can act on. Based on an hourly smartroom simulation, IoT based HVAC control saves 23.4% energy, while AI-based HVAC predictive pre-conditioning continues to save 21.2% energy without sacrificing guest comfort. Findings reveal that the value of AI within the hospitality sector depends on the horizon as well as context and integration, and offer practitioners and researchers benchmarks and open code.

title: Establishment of Rabbit Formative-like Pluripotent Cells by Bidirectional Modulation of WNT Signaling Pathway
abstract: The generation of embryonic stem cells (ESCs) with full developmental capacity and robust chimera-forming potential remains a major bottleneck for most non-rodent mammalian species, including rabbits, an important animal for both biomedicine and agriculture. Formative pluripotency is a unique intermediate state bridging the naive and primed pluripotent states, which is defined by distinct molecular signatures, intrinsic competence for primordial germ cell (PGC) specification, and unique developmental adaptability to early embryonic microenvironments. Here, we developed a novel culture medium termed KFiC, which could bidirectionally and coordinately modulate the WNT/β-catenin signaling pathway via combined treatment of the WNT activator CHIR99021 and the inhibitor IWR-1. The KFiC culture system enables efficient derivation and stable long-term self-renewal of rabbit embryonic stem cells (rbESCs) with consistent formative-like pluripotent characteristics. KFiC-cultured rbESCs (KFiC-rbESCs) form compact, undifferentiated colonies, maintain intact genomic stability, and recapitulate the transcriptional landscape of pre-implantation epiblast cells, accompanied by sustained high expression of the key formative pluripotency marker OTX2. Functionally, KFiC-rbESCs possess efficient PGC differentiation competence and extensively contribute to embryonic development after microinjection into rabbit morulae, displaying their superior developmental plasticity. Notably, the KFiC system can stabilize an intermediate formative-like pluripotent state in mouse, human, and pig pluripotent stem cells, and KFiC-adapted mouse ESCs retain potent chimera-forming ability. Collectively, this study establishes a reliable culture platform for generating and maintaining formative-like rbESCs. This cross-species-compatible system provides a promising foundation for further optimizing naïve-level pluripotency in rbESCs and facilitates the generation of genetically engineered rabbit disease models.

title: Decision benchmarking reveals when protein foundation models add experimental value
abstract: Protein engineering is shifting from model-based variant scoring to deciding what to measure next. This exposes a limitation of fixed-dataset benchmarks, which rank predictors without showing when their advantage survives as evidence accumulates. We therefore introduce decision benchmarking across 217 ProteinGym assays, 2.47 million variants and 95 predictors to evaluate whether models and measurements improve decisions at matched cost. Zero-shot accuracy explained less than one-fifth of the variation in discovery after calibration. Calibrated priors exceeded budget-matched additivity at 20-100 measurements, but the advantage narrowed as component measurements accumulated. Measured additivity then overtook zero-shot models after 50-100 measurements for top-variant discovery and around 500 for global ranking. The same principle showed that double-mutant measurements improved prediction in models using mutation identity, whereas prediction-guided acquisition improved discovery. Evidence-based routing improved strategy selection. Decision benchmarking thus identifies which strategy adds value given the information already available and the decision that follows.

title: Global population genomics and pangenome of the clubroot pathogen link clonal expansion and effector diversification to resistance breakdown in canola
abstract: Clubroot disease, caused by the obligate biotrophic protist Plasmodiophora brassicae, threatens Brassica crops worldwide. Novel pathogen virulence frequently breaks resistance in agricultural crops, and yet explanations for isolate evolution remain unknown. We combined whole-genome sequencing of 192 isolates from 24 countries with a pangenome analysis of 55 high-quality complete or nearly complete genome assemblies and performed functional effector analyses to investigate potential mechanisms of virulence emergence. Three major phylogenetic clusters were identified, including two highly clonal lineages with contrasting virulence profiles, and a genetically diverse population retaining signatures of recombination. Our findings support a model in which genome-wide purifying selection maintained core genome integrity, while effector genes evolved under less constraint. Despite a compact closed pangenome, we identified chromosome 17 as a major hotspot of single nucleotide and structural variations, transposable elements and expansion of ankyrin-repeat effectors. Within the variable chromosome 17, PbAnk2 alleles from virulent and avirulent isolates encoded proteins with distinct predicted structures. PbAnk2 interacted with the Arabidopsis co-chaperone DJC31 in yeast two-hybrid and BiFC assays, whereas co-immunoprecipitation did not detect an interaction for the allele found in isolates that break CRa-mediated resistance, suggesting that allelic variation may alter PbAnk2’s association with DJC31. These findings reveal the clonal expansion of virulent isolates and connect it to effector diversification that led to resistance breakdown and establish a genomic framework for pathogen surveillance and durable clubroot resistance.

title: Capturing Spatial Heterogeneity Using UAV-Derived Multispectral Phenotypes and Random Regression Models Improves Genetic Evaluation in Alfalfa Breeding Trials
abstract: Spatial heterogeneity is a major source of environmental noise in field trials, reducing genetic evaluation accuracy. Conventional spatial correction methods use field layout and plot proximity but often fail to capture in-season dynamics or leverage temporal data from high-throughput phenotyping. We hypothesized that longitudinal UAV-derived multispectral measurements could characterize field-scale environmental heterogeneity and improve genetic evaluation in breeding trials. Multispectral imagery was collected throughout the growing season across eight alfalfa trials in New York and New Mexico (2022–2023). Vegetation indices were evaluated for heritability and association with biomass yield using univariate and multi-trait models. Longitudinal measurements were modeled with random regression (RR) to estimate plot-specific permanent environmental effects (PEE), incorporated into genomic mixed models within a two-stage framework. Model performance was compared with conventional autoregressive (AR) and baseline (no correction) models using metrics of consistency and accuracy of estimated genetic effects across replicates. Vegetation indices showed moderate to high heritability, with GNDVI consistently outperforming NDVI and NDRE. Both univariate and multi-trait analyses revealed substantial spatial variability, particularly in New Mexico trials. RR-derived PEE captured field-scale spatial patterns and improved genetic signal recovery relative to baseline and AR models, with the largest gains under strong spatial heterogeneity and comparable performance where variability was limited. The RR framework improved reproducibility of genetic effect estimates across independent field subsets without compromising agreement with full-trial evaluations. These findings show that integrating UAV data via random regression enhances genetic signal recovery and selection accuracy, with broader potential for precision agriculture and biosensor-driven crop management.

title: Plasma Neurofilament Light Chain is Markedly Elevated in General Hospital Inpatients with Delirium
abstract: Objective: To determine whether plasma neurofilament light chain (NfL) and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) are elevated in hospitalised patients with delirium relative to patients with dementia and primary psychiatric disorders (PPD). Methods and analysis: This was a cross-sectional observational study conducted at the Royal Melbourne Hospital, Melbourne, Australia, between April and October 2024, with comparator samples from a research biobank. In Phase 1 (Delirium Discovery Cohort), we measured plasma NfL and GFAP using the Single molecule array (Simoa) platform in hospitalised patients with delirium and compared them with dementia and PPD groups. Biomarker concentrations were the primary outcome and were compared using general linear models adjusted for age, sex, and estimated glomerular filtration rate, with bootstrapped confidence intervals. Discriminative performance was assessed as a secondary outcome using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. In Phase 2, we applied this threshold to independent dementia and PPD groups. Results: In Phase 1 (n =176), inpatients with delirium showed higher concentrations of both NfL and GFAP than patients with dementia ({beta} = 0.78; 95% CI [0.37, 1.20] and {beta} = 0.39 [0.07, 0.73] respectively) or PPD groups ({beta} = 1.17; [0.69, 1.66] and {beta} = 0.83 [0.51, 1.24] respectively). ROC curve analysis for differentiating delirium from dementia and PPD groups yielded an optimal NfL threshold of 24.1 pg/mL (AUC = 0.89, 96% sensitivity, 70% specificity). In comparison, GFAP showed lower accuracy (AUC = 0.85), and combining NfL with GFAP (AUC = 0.90) did not significantly improve performance. In Phase 2 (n = 154), the NfL threshold of > 24 pg/ml maintained strong performance (AUC = 0.95, 96% sensitivity, and 77% specificity). Conclusions: Plasma NfL shows promise as a biomarker for delirium in hospitalised patients, distinguishing it with high sensitivity from patients with dementia and PPD. Larger multicentre studies are needed to refine cut-offs, evaluate temporal dynamics, and determine integration into acute hospital delirium pathways.

title: University Naming as Governance: Institutional Continuity, Policy Variation, and Organizational Change
abstract: The intensity of debates around university naming practices has increased as these institutions address their historical connections to slavery, segregation, settler colonialism, scientific racism, and exclusion. However, having a documented naming policy does not guarantee continuous, transparent, or significant review processes. This theory-building comparative document analysis explores naming governance at fifteen American universities. The study employs a preregistered-style audit trail and directed qualitative content analysis to examine policies, board actions, committee reports, and official statements, coding eleven dimensions across formal rule structures, processes, and outcomes. Findings illustrate a pattern of policy decoupling: although historical criteria, evidence standards, and review committees are often formalized, their activation typically requires petitions, controversies, or leadership discretion. Within the sample, only one institution employs a routine review on the trigger/periodic-review/appeal dimension. The Routine Stewardship Model explains this asymmetry by examining how activation, procedures, and outcomes are coupled. It offers a framework to differentiate between policy adoption and institutionalized practice and identifies practical design elements—such as recurring review triggers, role separation, public rationales, and mandatory decisions—that may enhance accountability in naming governance, reducing crisis dependence.
journal: Theory and Practice in Social Studies

title: The Two Sides of Sovereign Balance Sheets: How Much Do Government Financial Assets Tell Us About r − g?
abstract: Governments hold large stocks of financial assets, yet debt rules and sustainability assessments look almost only at what they owe. This paper asks whether the asset side of public balance sheets tells us something about the interest–growth differential, r−g, that debt alone does not. We follow 17 advanced economies from 2000 to 2026 with sparse dynamic factor models, which let the states governing r−g emerge from the data instead of being imposed through debt ratios. The answer is more uncertain than either side of the debate assumes. On whether the asset side adds information beyond debt, a pre-specified forecast test is inconclusive: it finds no evidence that it does for r−g a year ahead, though it could not reliably have detected information large enough to move a one-year debt projection by the smallest annual adjustment the EU debt safeguard demands. A second comparison, on a consistently measured r−g, can neither confirm nor rule out information of that size. Nor is the asset side shown to matter differently when debt is high: the link between asset accumulation and long-term yields is not established to change with the debt burden. Countries respond to common forces in ways a weak test cannot tell apart, yet their coefficients differ for every variable. Applied to fiscal anchors, net and gross debt measures disagree in about one country-quarter in seven, showing where each would bind. The paper maps how much the asset side can, and cannot yet, tell us about debt sustainability.

title: OCR + Generative AI Powered Prescription to Explanation System
abstract: Healthcare systems produce and manage lots of highly sensitive information, especially in the form of prescriptions and other documents related to patients' private data. However, due to the nature of handwritten medical prescriptions and medical jargon, patients often find it difficult to follow medication instructions. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is still in its nascent phase of digitizing handwritten prescription documents into text. Furthermore, the traditional OCR systems are noisy and difficult to understand when it comes to recognizing the handwriting of doctors to understand medical prescriptions properly. This paper utilizes Generative AI to test the ability of LLMs in conducting OCR on handwritten text and analyze its performance, and merge OCR with Generative AI to analyze and extract medicines from prescriptions in order to give a detailed and specialized description of the medicine to the user The paper further analyzes some OCR methods for text extraction from medical prescriptions and compares their performance. It has also been demonstrated that the usability of prescription data and the possibility of misinterpretation of medication is decreased when OCR is combined with Generative and Agentic AI. Thus the combination of artificial intelligence and OCR will help improve the understanding of patients and the accessibility of digital healthcare.
journal: International Journal of Data Processing & Networking

title: Development of an Integrated Web-Based Partnership Management Information System for PHRI Bekasi City
abstract: Professional associations require integrated information systems to improve administrative efficiency and support digital transformation. However, the Indonesian Hotel and Restaurant Association (PHRI) Bekasi City still manages membership administration, membership fee payments, organizational information dissemination, and hotel occupancy reporting through separate and predominantly manual processes, resulting in inefficient data management and delayed administrative services. This study aims to develop an integrated web-based Partnership Management Information System to streamline administrative processes and enhance organizational services. The project was governed using the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK) framework for initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, and closing, while the Waterfall model guided sequential software development. Laravel was employed as the web application framework, MySQL as the database management system, Bootstrap for the user interface, and the Midtrans payment gateway for digital membership fee transactions. Functional evaluation was conducted through User Acceptance Testing (UAT) with the PHRI Bekasi City management board, while technical performance was evaluated using Google PageSpeed Insights. The developed system successfully integrated membership management, digital membership cards, digital payment processing, organizational information management, and hotel occupancy reporting into a single platform. UAT results showed very good scores across functionality (93%), performance (92.5%), interface (91%), and efficiency (97%), while Performance Testing indicated strong results on desktop and good results on mobile devices. These findings demonstrate that the proposed system effectively supports the digital transformation of partnership management and provides a practical reference for implementing integrated information systems in similar professional organizations.
journal: Journal of Engineering Technology and Science Integration

title: Balanced Regional Growth in China through Optimized Resource Allocation and Industrial Restructuring
abstract: In the process of industrialization in China, the intervention of administrative forces in the factor market has resulted in the mismatch of resources and the imbalance of industrial layout, which is closely related to the long-standing gap between the eastern region and the central and western regions. This paper is a structured narrative literature review, which examines how optimizing resource allocation and industrial restructuring can promote more balanced regional growth in different stages of industrialization, and accordingly puts forward differentiated factor allocation strategies. The research comprehensively uses four classical frameworks, namely, Petty-Clark's Law, Hoffmann's Law, the Solow Growth Model and the Lewis Dual Economy Theory, and combines with the empirical research on resource allocation and regional growth in China in recent years. Evidence shows that resource allocation following the natural law of industrial evolution is often associated with lower regional imbalance. This paper interprets the existing literature as pointing to two regional patterns: some eastern regions may face the problems of improper upgrading order and insufficient support for innovation activities, while many central and western regions may show weak industrial capabilities and the outflow of skilled labor and capital. Accordingly, this paper puts forward targeted policy suggestions for various regions that match the stage.

title: Soil Salinity under Climate Change in Pakistan: Emerging Challenges and Sustainable Management Approaches for Agriculture
abstract: Soil salinity is a major constraint to agricultural productivity, soil health, and food security in Pakistan, particularly under changing climatic conditions. Rising temperatures, increased evapotranspiration, irregular precipitation, droughts, flooding, and sea-level rise can intensify salt accumulation and alter soil–water interactions. This review examines the emerging challenges associated with climate change and soil salinity in Pakistan, focusing on their impacts on soil properties, crop physiology, agricultural production, and rural livelihoods. It discusses the mechanisms of soil salinity and sodicity, their spatial distribution, and the interactions among climate variability, irrigation practices, groundwater quality, and secondary salinization. Furthermore, sustainable management approaches are evaluated, including gypsum application, organic amendments, integrated nutrient management, efficient irrigation, drainage improvement, and appropriate leaching strategies. Climate-resilient approaches, such as conventional crop breeding, modern biotechnology, halophyte utilization, plant growth-promoting microorganisms, and mycorrhizal associations, are also explored. The review highlights the potential of remote sensing, geographic information systems, precision agriculture, and predictive modelling to support salinity monitoring and site-specific management. Despite these opportunities, important challenges remain, including insufficient long-term monitoring, limited region-specific data, economic constraints, and gaps in farmer awareness and institutional coordination. Addressing these challenges requires integrated research, effective agricultural policies, improved extension services, and collaboration among researchers, policymakers, and farming communities. Prioritizing locally adapted, economically feasible, and environmentally sustainable interventions can strengthen agricultural resilience, restore salt-affected soils, and protect freshwater resources. Overall, integrating climate adaptation with sustainable soil and water management is essential for maintaining agricultural productivity and improving long-term food security in Pakistan.
journal: Kashmir Journal of Academic Research and Development

title: Academic Integrity at a Crossroads: Examining the ‘Sex-For-Grades’ Phenomenon at a Selected Institution in Masvingo Province, Zimbabwe
abstract: The phenomenon known as "sex-for-grades" presents a significant challenge within tertiary institutions, including universities, polytechnics, teacher training colleges, nursing schools and agricultural colleges. This study investigates the prevalence of the sex-for-grades phenomenon experienced by female students at a university located in Masvingo Province in Zimbabwe. Employing an exploratory qualitative design, the research purposively selected a sample of 25 female students and collected data through semi-structured questionnaires and interviews. The questionnaire was disseminated via digital platforms, including university email communications and learning management systems, as well as through in-person visits conducted between May and August 2025. Open-ended responses and qualitative feedback obtained from participants were analyzed thematically, allowing for the identification of recurring patterns and contextual insights. The findings indicate a pervasive culture of verbal, visual and online harassment, which is further exacerbated by cultural stigma and a fear of reprisal. The consequences of these incidents include significant psycho-emotional trauma, diminished academic performance, weakened social connections and increased vulnerability among the affected students. This study advocates for universities to adopt comprehensive sexual harassment policies, establish clear reporting mechanisms, ensure the provision of safe and dignified learning environments, impose stringent sanctions on perpetrators to restore confidence in institutional responses and provide specialised training on sexual harassment for academic staff.

Modelling the determinants of innovative teaching practices among primary school teachers in Oman through a multi-group analysis using PLS-SEM
abstract: In this research, the factors influencing innovative teaching practices among primary school teachers in Oman were explored, with specific references to transformational leadership, school climate, teacher self-efficacy, and organizational learning, considering gender as a moderating variable. The study aims to fill a significant gap in the literature by addressing the issue of leadership, organizational, and individual factors influencing innovative behavior in teachers working in the context of Omani schools. The design used was quantitative and cross-sectional; the data were collected from 368 primary school teachers in Muscat using a structured questionnaire that was tested and validated based on expert reviews and reliability testing. The data analysis was performed using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) of SmartPLS 4 based on the existing analytical principles. The results reveal that transformational leadership is significantly and positively associated with innovative teaching (β = 0.128), and teacher self-efficacy is strongly and positively associated with innovative teaching (β = 0.749). In contrast, school climate and organizational learning did not show statistically significant direct associations. The multi-group analysis also demonstrates gender differences in the way people respond to the determinants of critical significance, which supports the necessity of differentiated approaches and inclusivity. This research adds to the paucity of existing empirical research on educational innovation in Oman by identifying teacher self-efficacy as the strongest individual-level correlate of innovative teaching alongside transformational leadership, and points out the significance of gender as a contextual moderator of the leadership-innovation and self-efficacy-innovation relationships. The results provide practical information to policymakers and school leaders who want to support innovative teaching from the angles of transformational leadership development, specific professional learning, and gender-sensitive approaches.

title: Revealing the spatial heterogeneity of pine wilt disease spread in China through Geographical Pattern Causality analysis.
abstract: Pine wilt disease (PWD) is one of the most destructive invasive forest diseases in China, yet the environmental drivers underlying its spatially heterogeneous spread remain poorly understood. This study aimed to characterize the spatial and temporal patterns of natural PWD dispersal, identify persistent hotspots, and determine region-specific environmental drivers of PWD habitat suitability. We developed an integrated framework combining dispersal screening, biomod2 ensemble modelling, SaTScan spatiotemporal scan statistics, and Geographical Pattern Causality (GPC) analysis to examine PWD spread and its environmental drivers at national and regional scales. Natural dispersal increased markedly after 2016 and reached a peak of 9728 newly affected subcompartments in 2020. At the national scale, Altitude, mean diurnal temperature range (Bio2), and normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) were the dominant determinants of habitat suitability, with relative importance values of 27.52%, 25.29%, and 21.87%, respectively. However, GPC analysis confirmed pronounced spatial heterogeneity among the SaTScan-identified hotspot regions during the outbreak period. In hotspot region A, Aspect and Slope showed the strongest positive causal relationships on PWD suitability, with causal strengths of 0.361 and 0.284, respectively. In contrast, Altitude and Slope showed strong negative effects in hotspot region C, with strengths of 0.591 and 0.520, respectively. Wind speed showed negative causal relationships with PWD habitat suitability across all hotspot regions. These findings demonstrate that the environmental drivers of PWD vary substantially across spatial scales and hotspot regions, highlighting the importance of incorporating regional heterogeneity into PWD monitoring, risk assessment, and differentiated management.

The perceived impact of extreme weather events on care for people with HIV or tuberculosis and HIV in Zimbabwe: a survey-based multicentre cross-sectional observational study and formative evaluation.
abstract: BACKGROUND The growing threat to health systems posed by extreme weather events (EWEs) disproportionately affects people living with HIV and tuberculosis disease in high-burden, low-resource settings. In Zimbabwe, for example, the 2023-24 El Niño-induced drought intensified food insecurity and reduced access to clinics and medication for such vulnerable populations. We aimed to conduct a formative evaluation to assess the perceived impact of climate change and EWEs on HIV and tuberculosis determinants and service delivery and identify potential climate-adaptive health-service strategies. METHODS In this survey-based multicentre cross-sectional observational study with a formative evaluation supplemented by qualitative data, we surveyed people living with HIV from Sept 19 to Dec 19, 2024, across 321 clinics in Zimbabwe to describe their perceived impact of EWEs on their health. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling. The inclusion criteria were being diagnosed with HIV, being older than 18 years, and receiving HIV care at Organization for Public Health Interventions and Development (OPHID) clinics during the study period. Individuals who were not receiving HIV care at an OPHID clinic or who were younger than 18 years were excluded. A client satisfaction survey was used to collect data from in-person surveys. The survey included questions related to the general effects of EWEs, such as drought, extreme heat, and flooding; how EWEs had affected HIV or tuberculosis care; and what, if any, services were currently available or should be made available to mitigate climate impacts on health. We also conducted six focus group discussions (FGDs; five to eight participants per group) between March 12 and May 12, 2024, across the Bulilima, Mangwe, and Matobo districts. We used a convenience sampling approach to select patients who had visited the health facility for medical check-ups, medication resupply, or viral load testing, as recorded in clinical registers and verified by clinical staff. Eligible participants for the FGDs were adults (≥18 years) with HIV, or with current or previous tuberculosis treatment, receiving care at the study facility during the recruitment period; those under 18 years or not receiving care at the facility were excluded. Participants' sex was self-reported at enrolment. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively, whereas FGD data were analysed using a modified framework approach. The main outcomes were the perceived impact of climate change and EWEs on HIV and tuberculosis determinants and service delivery outcomes, as reported by affected communities, and community-prioritised mitigation strategies to feasibly address climate-sensitive determinants and barriers to care. FINDINGS Among 1804 eligible participants approached across 15 districts, all completed the survey and were included in the analysis. Most survey participants (1363 [75·6%] of 1804 participants) reported noticing changes in climate over the past 5 years; of these 1363 participants, 900 (66·0%) were female and 1024 (75·1%) participants reported disruptions to their HIV care during the time they noticed changes in climate. Survey respondents reported that climate-related disruptions were associated with increased food insecurity (reported by 877 [85·6%] of 1024 participants) and water shortage (667 [65·1%] of 1024 participants). Qualitative analysis confirmed that the barriers to HIV and tuberculosis care from EWEs included widespread food insecurity, crop failures, and livestock deaths, with consequent effects on income leading to challenges in paying for food and transportation to clinics. Participants highlighted the need for expanded services that facilitate social and economic wellbeing, including nutrition support, water access, transportation, and income-generating activities, and decentralised models of health-care delivery. INTERPRETATION Extreme heat and drought affect food and water security and have financial implications, creating challenges for patients to access care in Zimbabwe. Our findings underscore the urgent need for integrated, climate-adaptive strategies to maintain HIV and tuberculosis care in such climate-vulnerable regions. title: 660 nm LED preconditioning programs mitochondrial signaling in BMSCs for functional tracheal cartilage regeneration.
abstract: Stem-cell-based cartilage regeneration is limited not only by cell delivery, but also by the difficulty of establishing a stable and functionally competent regenerative cell state before implantation. Here, we report a photonic mitochondrial programming strategy in which 660 nm light-emitting diode (LED) irradiation preconditions bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) to enhance functional tracheal cartilage regeneration. BMSCs were seeded onto egg white-derived ring-shaped porous scaffolds and exposed to defined 660 nm LED irradiation before implantation. Among the tested irradiation conditions, 15 J/cm2 optimally promoted BMSC proliferation, chondrogenic differentiation and cartilage-like extracellular matrix deposition, while suppressing fibrotic, hypertrophic and matrix-degrading phenotypes. Mechanistically, 660 nm LED irradiation enhanced cytochrome c oxidase (CCO) activity, mitochondrial membrane potential, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production and respiratory function, accompanied by moderate reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling. This mitochondrial bioenergetic-redox response activated the PI3K/Akt/mTOR/GSK3β-SOX9 axis, thereby promoting type II collagen, aggrecan and glycosaminoglycan-rich matrix formation. Pharmacological inhibition of ROS signaling, mitochondrial activity, PI3K or mTOR attenuated the LED-induced chondrogenic program. In a rabbit tracheal cartilage ring defect model, 15 J/cm2-preconditioned BMSC-scaffold constructs improved cartilage-like tissue formation, airway epithelial repair, lumen patency and mechanical support after 30 days of observation. These findings support 660 nm LED irradiation as a controllable mitochondrial preconditioning strategy for stem-cell-based functional cartilage regeneration.

title: A CNN-based mapping approach for aeolian dunes in Arctic Sweden
Considering counterfactual prediction models in sleep research: A demonstration of incident stroke prediction in an observational cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE Data-driven risk prediction algorithms are increasingly common. However, studies suggesting that a single set of variables are most "important" within a given risk prediction model ignore the reality that other equally useful models containing entirely different features may exist. We aim to use a novel approach (Model Path Selection) to demonstrate that, for any given health outcome, there are likely many comparable counterfactual models including different sets of variables. We focus on incident stroke as a scientifically meaningful outcome to motivate this demonstration. METHODS Model Path Selection uses an iterative model-building procedure to illustrate a set of counterfactual prediction models ("paths"). We applied Model Path Selection to Sleep Heart Health Study data (N = 4,512 adults) to predict 5-year incident stroke, considering 30 features comprising demographics, self-reported and measured medical risk factors, polysomnography, and self-reported sleep. Area Under the Curve was estimated for each resulting path based on 10-fold cross-validation. RESULTS Model Path Selection identified 61 unique counterfactual models. 13 of these achieved Area Under the Curves between 0.81 and 0.82. Area Under the Curves of the remaining models ranged from 0.53 to 0.68 (median 0.61). All 13 top models included age plus various combinations of other features (polysomnography indices, body mass index, and/or the Short Form 36 mental and physical component scores). CONCLUSIONS Model Path Selection can illuminate counterfactual prediction models, differentiate features that may be uniquely predictive from those that can be swapped out with other features, enhance reproducibility, inform the design of clinically practical predictive tools, and suggest sleep-related risk factors to be targeted for health promotion.
