title: Adaptive Long-range UAV Flight Planning using Monte Carlo Search Trees
abstract: Long-range fixed-wing UAV missions require energy-efficient, dynamically feasible trajectories that can adapt online to evolving wind and airspace constraints. We present a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)-based framework that addresses this challenge by formulating mission planning as a finite-horizon Markov decision process incorporating aircraft kinematics, onboard energy dynamics, forecast wind fields, terrain, and time-varying no-fly zones. The MCTS planner searches over waypoint references generated by pre-stabilizing feedback controllers and a constraint-aware navigation field, yielding dynamically feasible trajectories. Simulation results from medical delivery scenarios show that the MCTS planner outperforms baseline geometric planners and population-based optimization algorithms. Moreover, the MCTS planner can be used in closed-loop to rapidly compute safe diversion trajectories under evolving constraints.

title: Agripass - A Digital Passport for Agricultural Products Using AI-Based Quality Assessment
abstract: . Abstract— Agripass is an AI-driven farm-to-fork traceable system that aims to improve the safety and integrity of the farm to fork food supply chain. The system provides a secure digital chain for every consignment of produce right from the harvesting stage itself. The farmers are required to provide all the required information of the produce such as type of produce, soil type, pesticide use, date of harvesting, location, and images of the produce through a role-based web interface. An AI-driven module is also integrated into the system to analyze the uploaded image and provide a quality grades A, B, C to enable a quick and impartial assessment at the source level itself. After the successful completion of the registration process, the system provides a unique QR code that acts as a digital passport for the produce. As the produce passes from distributors to retailers, each handler scans the QR code and records details about how the items were transported, stored, and handed over. Because of this step-by-step update, the journey of the product stays clear. Buyers can scan the same QR code on their phones to quickly check the product’s background, including its main details, movement through the supply chain, and the quality score given by AI. Going forward, Agripass may be upgraded by introducing blockchain to better protect stored records from unauthorized changes. The system could also work with IoT sensors and more refined AI techniques to keep track of product conditions in real time and improve the reliability of quality assessment
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: A Systematic Review of Data Mining Frameworks and AIEnabled Neural Network Technologies for Environmentally Sustainable Indian Agriculture: Trends, Challenges, and Future Directions
abstract: Agriculture remains the backbone of the Indian economy, contributing significantly to food security, employment, and rural development. However, increasing climate variability, soil degradation, water scarcity, pest infestations, fragmented landholdings, and the growing demand for sustainable food production have created substantial challenges for conventional farming practices. The rapid advancement of Data Mining, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Deep Learning (DL) technologies has transformed precision agriculture by enabling intelligent analysis of large-scale agricultural data and supporting evidence-based decision-making. This systematic review critically examines recent developments in Data Mining frameworks and AI-enabled neural network technologies for environmentally sustainable Indian agriculture. The review synthesizes contemporary research on data acquisition, preprocessing, feature engineering, classification, clustering, association rule mining, regression analysis, and predictive analytics, together with advanced neural network architectures such as Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), Transformer models, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) [2], [3], [15], [18], [20], [21], [22], [43]. Furthermore, it evaluates their applications in crop yield prediction, soil health monitoring, intelligent irrigation, crop disease detection, weather forecasting, precision nutrient management, climate-resilient farming, and environmental sustainability [5], [11], [16], [24], [30], [36], [37]. The review identifies current research trends, methodological limitations, implementation challenges, and emerging opportunities while highlighting the need for scalable, interpretable, and resourceefficient intelligent agricultural systems tailored to India's diverse agro-climatic conditions. Finally, future research directions are proposed, emphasizing hybrid AI frameworks, Explainable AI, Edge Intelligence, Federated Learning, multimodal data integration, and sustainable decision-support systems. The findings provide a comprehensive knowledge base for researchers, policymakers, and agricultural practitioners seeking to develop intelligent, environmentally responsible, and sustainable agricultural ecosystems.
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Multi-Crop Irrigation Need Classification Based on Machine Learning with an Indonesian-Language GenAI-UX Recommendation Layer
abstract: Inefficient irrigation water use remains a critical challenge in Indonesian agriculture, and the complexity of raw sensor data hinders adoption by smallholder farmers who lack data-analysis skills. This study develops an intelligent irrigation Decision Support System that integrates interpretable Machine Learning with an Indonesian-language GenAI-UX recommendation layer, using a publicly available multi-crop irrigation scheduling dataset (501 records, nine crops) with an analytical focus on paddy and maize. Four components are combined into one pipeline: (i) irrigation-need classification compared across six algorithms; (ii) regression of a continuous water-requirement score; (iii) sensor-anomaly detection using Isolation Forest cross-validated with the Interquartile Range method; and (iv) a rule-based natural-language recommendation layer whose operating point is optimized by a Genetic Algorithm. Validity was safeguarded through stratified five-fold cross-validation and leakage-controlled preprocessing. Gradient Boosting achieved the best classification performance (F1-score 0.980; cross-validated F1 0.963), Random Forest Regressor reached R square of 0.807, Isolation Forest agreed with IQR outliers at 95.2%, and the Genetic Algorithm attained a confidence of 0.993 within realistic agronomic bounds. In an illustrative usability evaluation, the GenAI-UX interface obtained the highest System Usability Scale score (Good category). The results indicate that pairing accurate, interpretable models with a language-based delivery layer can transform complex sensor data into actionable irrigation recommendations, lowering the adoption barrier for non-technical users. Field validation with real respondents and edge deployment are identified as the next steps.
journal: Journal of Applied Informatics and Computing

title: Effects of Digitalization on Agricultural Value Added in Türkiye: An ARDL Approach
abstract: Agricultural digitalization has become an important part of productivity growth and sustainable development of agriculture. However, empirical evidence remains mixed about how different dimensions of digitalization affect agricultural value added. This study looks at the short-run and long-run effects of digitalization on agricultural value added in Türkiye, by using annual data for the period 2001–2023. Agricultural value added is used as the dependent variable, while Internet use and fixed broadband subscriptions stand for two indicators of digitalization. Fertilizer consumption and rural population are added as control variables. The Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) bounds-testing approach is used to estimate both the long-run relationship and the short-run dynamics among the variables. The bounds test provides evidence of a long-run relationship at the 10% significance level, although the result is inconclusive at the 5% level. In the long-run estimates, Internet use has a positive but statistically insignificant coefficient, while fixed broadband subscriptions have a positive and statistically significant coefficient. Fertilizer consumption has a negative but statistically insignificant coefficient, whereas rural population has a negative and statistically significant coefficient. The Error Correction Model (ECM) shows that short-run deviations from the long-run relationship are corrected over time, with a negative and statistically significant error-correction coefficient. The diagnostic tests indicate no evidence of serial correlation or heteroskedasticity, while the CUSUM tests support parameter stability. An additional analysis using mobile cellular subscriptions extends the sample period and shows that the results are sensitive to the digitalization indicator used. In this alternative specification, the bounds test does not provide evidence of a long-run relationship. The findings therefore do not support a uniform relationship between digitalization and agricultural value added. Instead, the results vary across digitalization indicators and model specifications. Rather than combining digitalization measures into a single ICT indicator, the study examines alternative digitalization measures separately to assess whether the results depend on the indicator used.

title: Practices and Awareness of Drone-Based Pesticide Application Service Providers in Türkiye: A Survey Study
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly used for pesticide application due to their operational flexibility, high field capacity, and ability to operate without direct contact with crops or soil. However, information regarding the actual field practices of commercial UAV spraying service providers remains limited. This study aimed to characterize current commercial UAV spraying practices, operational parameters, technical constraints, and environmental risk awareness in Türkiye through a cross-sectional descriptive survey of 71 active operators in May to August 2026. UAV spraying reached a considerable operational scale, with 67.1% of service providers treating ≥500 ha annually, mainly in wheat (88.4%) and maize (76.8%). Most operators used flight heights of 2–4 m (85.9%), speeds >5 m s⁻¹ (57.1%), and application rate of 10–30 L ha⁻¹ (88.7%).Only 14.1% performed calibration before every application. Wind-induced drift (80.3%) and limited battery life (64.8%) were the main operational constraints, while spraying-system failures were the most frequently reported technical problem (57.7%). Although wind speed was considered by 98.6% of operators, relative humidity was considered by only 16.9%. Applications were frequently conducted in or near areas with beekeeping activities (78.6%) and residential areas (61.4%). UAV spraying is now used on a considerable scale in Türkiye and has become an important part of the digitalization of agriculture. However, current field practices do not always follow the recommended application conditions, indicating a need for better standardization. Further development of UAV-specific technical standards, pesticide application and dose guidelines, operator training, and field-based R&D is therefore needed to improve application performance, reduce environmental risks, and ensure the safe and sustainable use of UAVs in agricultural spraying.

title: SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT OF THE AGRO-INDUSTRIAL COMPLEX THROUGH INNOVATION AND DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES
abstract: Sustainable development of the agro-industrial complex requires aligning production efficiency, natural resource conservation, and access to economic opportunities. This study identifies conditions for effective use of innovations and digital technologies and proposes an assessment model for Kazakhstan. The methods comprise an analytical literature review, document analysis, and descriptive processing of official statistics. The quantitative evidence covers investment in agriculture, forestry, and fishing in 2024–2025 and adoption of water-saving technologies in 2023–2025. Investment increased from KZT 737.9 billion to KZT 1,153.6 billion, or 56.3% in current prices, with volume growth of 51.8%. The share of own funds fell from 59.19% to 54.61%, but it remained the leading financing source. The area covered by water-saving systems increased from 237.1 to 543.5 thousand hectares, a 129.2% increase. These indicators describe modernisation conditions and technical coverage but do not establish a causal effect of digitalisation. An analytical model links observation, data validation, decision-making, implementation, and outcome measurement. The proposed indicators cover economic, environmental, social, and organisational dimensions. Practical applications involve assessing total ownership costs, resource intensity, accessibility of adoption, and service reliability. Regional adaptation, cooperative equipment use, and information system interoperability are justified. The contribution is the distinction between digital equipment deployment and sustainable operational outcomes. The absence of farm microdata and a comparable control group limits the study. Further validation requires observations across several production seasons and assessment of costs, resources, and outcomes before and after technology adoption.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN MANAGING LOGISTICS COSTS OF THE AGRO-INDUSTRIAL COMPLEX
abstract: The study examines artificial intelligence not as a general digitalisation factor, but as a tool for management accounting and operational control of logistics costs in the agro-industrial complex. The relevance stems from the spatial dispersion of agricultural production, seasonality, perishability, high transport intensity, and the growing need to integrate accounting data with real-time logistics information. The aim is to develop a cost-control framework that identifies where AI affects total logistics cost and what accounting indicators should be used to measure this effect. The empirical context is based on official data on Kazakhstan’s transport and agricultural digitalisation in 2025–2026, OECD materials, and peer-reviewed studies of AI in supply chain management and agri-food systems. The methodological design combines secondary data analysis, functional decomposition of logistics costs, cost-driver mapping, plan– fact variance analysis, and process-based modelling. The article distinguishes six cost blocks: transportation, warehousing, inventory holding, handling, product losses, and administrative and information costs. A three-level analytical framework is proposed: operational event → cost driver → financial indicator. On this basis, an AI-enabled logistics cost control architecture is developed in which ERP/TMS/WMS/IoT data feed forecasting, anomaly detection and optimisation algorithms. At the same time, the output is evaluated through accounting KPIs rather than technological metrics alone. Current data from Kazakhstan show that 648 agricultural producers already use digital technologies and AI-related tools, while the e-Agriculture ecosystem is moving toward integrated data management and sectoral AI analytics. The practical contribution is a methodology for selecting AI use cases based on their expected impact on specific cost drivers and for integrating AI outputs into management accounting and logistics control.

title: INNOVATIVE DEVELOPMENT OF KAZAKHSTAN'S GRAIN SECTOR: TRENDS, CHALLENGES, AND STRATEGIC PRIORITIES
abstract: The study examines and substantiates innovative solutions for the sustainable development of Kazakhstan's grain sector and identifies key areas to improve its efficiency and competitiveness amid modern economic and technological challenges. Research methodology. The research methodology consists of general scientific and special methods that enable a comprehensive assessment of the state and development prospects of Kazakhstan's grain sector, as well as substantiate directions for implementing innovative solutions. We used systematic and structural-functional analysis to view the grain sector as a complex socio-economic system of interrelated elements. We used economic and statistical methods to analyse the dynamics of gross grain harvest, yield, and export volumes for 2020-2025, based on data from the Bureau of National Statistics of the Agency for Strategic Planning and Reforms of the Republic of Kazakhstan. The comparative method allowed us to compare Kazakhstan's innovation activity and yield with indicators from leading countries in the grain market. We used expert assessments and scenario forecasting to develop expected innovation outcomes in the short and long term-the study's originality and value. The originality of this study lies in an integrated approach to substantiating innovative solutions for developing Kazakhstan's grain sector, taking into account modern global challenges, including the digitalisation of agricultural production, climate change, and the transformation of global food markets -the results of the study. The study found that Kazakhstan's grain sector has significant development potential. However, insufficient technological equipment, dependence on natural and climatic conditions, and uneven adoption of innovations largely limit its effectiveness. The analysis showed that the key to increasing the industry's competitiveness is digitalising agricultural production, adopting modern agricultural technologies, and developing grain storage and logistics infrastructure. The paper shows that introducing innovative solutions such as precision farming, automation of production processes, digital monitoring and management platforms, and resource-saving technologies contributes to higher yields, lower production costs, and improved product quality. Developing these areas not only increases the efficiency of domestic production but also strengthens Kazakhstan's export position in the global grain market. In addition, the study identified the significant role of government support and institutional mechanisms in stimulating industry innovation. The study shows that improved financing, subsidising, innovation mechanisms, and human resource development are necessary conditions for sustainable growth in the grain sector. The results confirm that integrated implementation of innovative solutions is a key factor in improving the efficiency, sustainability, and competitiveness of Kazakhstan's grain sector in the long term.

title: Deep learning-based genetic disease prediction with Monte Carlo (MC) dropout uncertainty estimation: a comparative study with classical machine learning baselines
abstract: Background: Deep neural networks have been successfully applied to structured clinical data with a good predictive performance, but their point predictions do not reflect an indication of confidence, which limits their trustworthiness in screening for genetic conditions where an overconfident misclassification may delay the appropriate confirmatory testing or intervention. Methods: A feed-forward neural network (128-64-32 hidden units, batch normalization, and dropout p = 0.3) was trained to classify patients into five genetic-disease-associated groups based on twelve regularly accessible clinical and molecular biomarkers, using a publicly available, pre-labelled structured biomedical dataset (n = 1,000) whose real-world clinical vs. synthetic provenance could not be independently confirmed (see Section 2.1 and Limitations). Performance was assessed using stratified 5-fold cross-validation versus four traditional baselines (logistic regression, random forest, SVM, gradient boosting; McNemar’s test for pairwise significance). We quantified predictive uncertainty using Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout (T up to 200 stochastic passes), decomposed it into epistemic and aleatoric components, and evaluated it thru calibration analysis (ECE, MCE, Brier score, negative log-likelihood), an uncertainty-quality analysis (low/medium/high uncertainty strata), a selective-prediction (risk-coverage) analysis, a seven-configuration ablation study, and robustness testing across random seeds, reduced training data, and Gaussian feature noise. Results The developed network achieved 94.30% +- 1.36% cross-validated accuracy which was statistically comparable to logistic regression (p = 0.092) and gradient boosting (p = 0.238) but considerably inferior to random forest (95.50% +- 1.26%, p = 0.0018) and SVM (95.30% +- 1.36%, p = 0.0063). MC-Dropout obtained 93.33% accuracy (macro F1 = 0.933, macro ROC-AUC = 0.971, MCC = 0.917) with ECE = 0.076 on a held-out test partition—numerically the highest (worst) ECE among the six model/inference configurations evaluated, exceeding all four classical baselines (ECE 0.024–0.066), although MC-Dropout inference reduced negative log-likelihood substantially relative to deterministic inference (0.370 vs. 0.445), indicating its calibration benefit is concentrated in reducing the penalty for confident errors rather than in bin-wise confidence-accuracy alignment. Errors were about twice as likely in the highest (most uncertain) tercile of predictions than in the lowest (12.0% vs. 6.0% mistake rate), and 60% of all misclassifications were within the high-uncertainty group. Removing the most doubtful 20%–30% of predictions yielded a retained-sample accuracy of above 95%. Accuracy and calibration were consistent across five random seeds (93.07%) and deteriorated gracefully with increasing predictive entropy under synthetic feature-noise perturbation. Conclusion: On this structured, moderate-sized genetic-disease benchmark dataset—evaluated entirely through internal computational validation, without external or prospective clinical testing—classical machine learning algorithms achieved statistically comparable or slightly higher raw classification accuracy than this deep learning approach under standard, non-tuned hyperparameters for all models.

title: Technological frontiers driving new insights in plant RNA biology
abstract: Recent technological innovations in high-throughput sequencing have reshaped our understanding of plant RNA biology, revealing complex regulatory layers beyond primary genetic sequences. In this mini-review, we highlight how emerging methodologies ranging from nascent RNA profiling to direct long-read sequencing have uncovered novel roles for non-coding RNAs, enhancer elements, alternative splicing/polyadenylation, and epitranscriptomic marks in RNA transcriptional control and stress adaptation. For each technique driving these fundamental advances, we provide a brief overview outlining the methodologies and their respective advantages and limitations, guiding the optimal tool for future RNA research. Finally, we propose how integrating these technologies into combinatorial studies will advance a unified, system-wide model of plant RNA dynamics, as well as the potential to resolve co-occurring RNA modifications in the context of an epitranscriptomic “epi-code” governing post-transcriptional fate. Bridging these molecular mechanisms will be crucial for understanding phenotypic plasticity and enabling targeted (epi)transcriptomic engineering to develop climate-resilient crops.

title: Towards digital agriculture: uncovering the drivers and barriers to the adoption of digital agricultural technologies
abstract: Accurately identifying the driving and hindering factors of agricultural digital technology adoption is the key to overcoming the “last mile” challenge in agricultural technology diffusion. Based on the evolutionary game theory of scale-free complex networks, this paper constructs an actor network for agricultural technology adoption to analyze its multidimensional mechanisms of influence in depth. The results indicate that while government subsidies provide short-term incentives for technology diffusion, their sustainability is limited. Agricultural technology advantages serve as the core driver, transforming exogenous technology into an endogenous growth engine. Conversely, the information gap, the perception of high risk, and high costs hinder farmers’ willingness to adopt these technologies. This study expands the application boundaries of complex network theory in agricultural technology adoption, reveals the operational laws governing driving and hindering factors, and provides a valuable reference for optimizing agricultural technology adoption strategies.

title: Return-home entrepreneurship and rural economic resilience: evidence from China's National pilot program
abstract: We study whether policies that encourage migrants to return home and start businesses strengthen rural economies. We treat China's national return-home entrepreneurship pilot, introduced in cohorts in 2016 and 2017, as a quasi-natural experiment and assemble an unbalanced panel of 2,097 counties, county-level cities, and urban districts from 1999 to 2023. A staggered difference-in-differences design indicates that pilot designation is positively associated with a principal-component index of rural economic resilience capacity and that the estimated effect emerges with a lag. The joint test of all pretreatment coefficients does not reject equality to zero at the 5% level, although it is marginal at the 10% level; a negative pooled long-lead estimate therefore continues to warrant caution. Alternative staggered-adoption estimators, resilience indices that exclude development-oriented components, a sample restricted through 2021, and a complete-case regression using only original non-interpolated observations all remain positive. Channel regressions show that the pilot raises the secondary- and tertiary-sector share and the China Rural Agriculture-Related Innovation Index, although these patterns do not establish causal mediation. Digital financial inclusion is not robust to county and year fixed effects. Formal between-group tests indicate significant regional and poverty-status differences, but not significant grain-production or labor-export differences; Hypothesis IV is therefore only partially supported. The national pilot ended in 2021, but return-home entrepreneurship policy continued through institutionalized support and nationwide promotion of the pilot experience. Accordingly, estimates after 2021 capture the persistent differential associated with earlier pilot designation in an environment of policy continuation and diffusion. Overall, the evidence is consistent with human-capital return and factor reallocation strengthening observed dimensions associated with rural economic resilience capacity, while the pooled long lead and the reduced coverage of the raw complete-case sample remain important qualifications.

title: Agri-Synergy: A Hardware–Software Co-Designed Hybrid IoT System for Sensor Interface Standardization and LLM-Driven Interactive Decision Support
abstract: This paper presents Agri-Synergy, a hybrid Internet of Things (IoT) system featuring a hardware–software co-design to tackle sensor data heterogeneity and the barriers to effective AI-driven decision support in smart agriculture. Unlike software-based data harmonization, we propose a universal sensor printed circuit board (PCB) with RS485/Modbus interface for hardware unification, complemented by on-node edge processing that ensures standardized data from source. To lower the entry barrier for farmers, the system integrates the DeepSeek large language model (LLM) API, combining static agricultural knowledge with real-time sensor data, for context-aware, natural language-based decision support, functioning without local model deployment. Field deployment showed reference-verified sensor accuracy predominantly within manufacturer specifications, stable 4G connectivity during the 4-h benchmark but intermittent dropouts during the 20-day deployment, and remote-control success rates of 96% (normal) and 80% (weak signal at 300 m). Multi-node concurrent transmission resulted in average latency of 238.0 ± 27.1 ms and packet loss below 0.5%. The system achieves a 3–5× cost reduction compared to commercial platforms. These results demonstrate that addressing data heterogeneity from source through hardware unification and software edge processing, while leveraging AI to lower the barrier to system adoption, provides a more reliable foundation for data synchronization and accessible AI-driven analytics.

title: Formononetin Protects Osteoblasts Against Oxidative Stress and Attenuates Ovariectomy-Induced Bone Loss in Association with MAPK/AP-1 and NRF2 Signaling
abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) is associated with estrogen deficiency and oxidative stress (OS), which impair osteoblast survival and osteogenic function. Formononetin (FMN) is a phytoestrogen with antioxidant properties, but its protective effects on osteoblasts under OS and the signaling pathways associated with these effects remain incompletely understood. Here, we evaluated the effects of FMN in ovariectomized (OVX) mice and in a tert-butyl hydroperoxide (t-BOOH)-induced oxidative injury model in MC3T3-E1 cells. Bone microarchitecture, histology, serum OS markers, cell viability, reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, apoptosis, mitochondrial morphology, and osteogenic differentiation were assessed. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, RNA sequencing, Western blotting, and pharmacological pathway-modulation experiments were used to investigate signaling changes associated with FMN treatment. FMN attenuated trabecular bone deterioration and systemic oxidative imbalance in OVX mice. In MC3T3-E1 cells, FMN improved cell viability, reduced ROS accumulation and apoptosis, alleviated mitochondrial damage, and preserved osteogenic differentiation following t-BOOH exposure. FMN treatment was accompanied by reduced phosphorylation of extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2), p38, and c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK), together with reduced expression of activator protein 1 (AP-1)-related proteins, including c-Fos, c-Jun, and phosphorylated c-Jun. Pharmacological reactivation of p38/JNK signaling with anisomycin attenuated several antioxidant, anti-apoptotic, and pro-osteogenic effects associated with FMN treatment, whereas nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) inhibition partially diminished FMN-mediated protection. Collectively, these findings support an association between the protective effects of FMN and modulation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK)/AP-1 and NRF2-associated signaling.

title: ERK5 Signaling and Ferroptosis in Bone Homeostasis: Emerging Connections and Therapeutic Perspectives
abstract: Bone homeostasis depends on coordinated activity among bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, osteoblasts, osteocytes, and osteoclasts. Disruption of this cellular network contributes to osteoporosis, impaired fracture repair, and other skeletal disorders, while redox stress and regulated cell-death programs increasingly appear to shape the behavior of these skeletal populations. Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by phospholipid peroxidation and failure of antioxidant defenses. Preclinical studies indicate that ferroptotic injury can compromise osteogenic differentiation, osteoblast function, and osteocyte integrity; in osteoclasts, the biological effect is more model-dependent. Extracellular signal-regulated kinase 5 (ERK5/MAPK7) integrates mechanical, oxidative, inflammatory, and metabolic cues, but skeletal studies have reported divergent effects across genetic, pharmacological, developmental, and mechanically stimulated models. Direct evidence that ERK5 regulates ferroptosis in skeletal cells is still lacking. This review evaluates ferroptosis and ERK5 signaling as potentially interacting stress-response systems, separates established findings from indirect and hypothetical links, and examines how ERK5-dependent stress adaptation, mitochondrial regulation, and metabolic state may modify ferroptotic susceptibility. We propose that ERK5 may shift the threshold between adaptive survival and ferroptotic injury in a cell-, stress-, and disease-stage-dependent manner, providing a testable framework for skeletal degeneration and regeneration.

title: Compound Hot–Dry Extremes in Southeastern Europe: From Observed Trajectories to Future Projections and Agricultural Vulnerability in Romania
abstract: Compound hot–dry extremes (CHDEs)—manifested through the concurrent occurrence of extreme daily atmospheric temperatures and precipitation deficits (D-CHDEs: daily maximum temperature Tmax ≥ calendar-day 90th percentile, TX90p, and daily precipitation RR 85% rainfed). These findings underscore the critical imperative for modernized pressurized irrigation networks, agro-genetic adaptation, and targeted policies within the EU Common Agricultural Policy (CAP).

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Two Multimodal Artificial Intelligence Systems Versus Dental Students in Endodontic Radiographic Classification
abstract: Objectives: Multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly used to support image interpretation in dentistry, but evidence regarding their diagnostic performance on endodontic radiographs remains limited. This study compared the diagnostic accuracy of two general-purpose multimodal AI systems with that of undergraduate and postgraduate dental students and evaluated whether image cropping influenced AI performance. Methods: Fifty anonymized periapical radiographs were retrospectively selected, with 10 cases in each of five predefined endodontic diagnostic categories. Reference diagnoses were established by consensus between two experienced endodontists. ChatGPT version 5.2 and Gemini version 3 independently classified each case using both full-size and tooth-cropped images and a standardized prompt. Twenty-five fifth-year undergraduate dental students and 20 postgraduate students in clinical endodontics classified the full-size images. Overall and category-specific accuracies were calculated, and agreement with the reference standard was assessed. Results: Overall accuracy was highest among postgraduate students (84.9%), followed by undergraduate students (78.7%). Gemini achieved accuracies of 72.0% with full-size images and 82.0% with cropped images, whereas ChatGPT achieved 68.0% and 50.0%, respectively. Cropping significantly reduced ChatGPT accuracy (p = 0.0117) but did not significantly affect Gemini performance (p = 0.3018). Diagnostic accuracy varied substantially across categories. Agreement with the reference standard for the AI systems ranged from 50.0% to 82.0%. Conclusions: Diagnostic performance depended on the evaluator, AI system, image format, and diagnostic category. Postgraduate students showed the highest overall accuracy, while AI performance was heterogeneous and did not consistently exceed that of trained human observers. General-purpose multimodal AI may support supervised radiographic interpretation and education, but it should not replace comprehensive clinical assessment or professional judgment.

title: Two-Stage Distributionally Robust Optimization for Secure Operation of Provincial Power Grids with High Renewable Penetration
abstract: Provincial power grids with high wind and photovoltaic penetration face poor out-of-sample security under limited data, whereas robust scheduling can be overly conservative. This study develops an integrated scheduling framework for secure provincial-grid operation using established two-stage Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization. The first stage determines the day-ahead schedule and reserves flexibility. After renewable forecast errors are observed, the second stage adjusts generation, renewable curtailment, reserve deployment, and energy storage charging and discharging. A Wasserstein ambiguity set is constructed from synchronized error samples. The model jointly enforces plant output, ramping, line flow, incremental loss, reserve, and storage state constraints. Dual reformulation and linearization yield a mixed-integer linear program. For the four selected day-specific cases, the estimated reductions in power-shortage frequency relative to sample-based stochastic optimization are 61.24%, 67.39%, 39.01%, and 56.11% in spring, summer, autumn, and winter, respectively. The maximum winter reserve shortfall decreases from 32.69 MW to 5.51 MW, accompanied by lower real-time balancing requirements. Compared with the robust optimization benchmark, the reported schedules and ex post revenue profiles indicate greater revenue opportunities for some renewable generators. These results demonstrate the framework’s potential to balance operational security and renewable generation revenue opportunities in provincial-grid scheduling under limited data.

title: Do Machine Learning Models Beat a Constant Benchmark When Forecasting Next-Month Hurst Exponents? Evidence from Saudi-Listed Firms
abstract: Financial forecasting under uncertainty is fundamental to strategic investment decision making. Among the factors that influence investment decisions, market efficiency plays a critical role because it determines whether historical information can provide predictive value for future market behavior. The Hurst exponent is widely used to measure persistence and weak-form market efficiency, where values close to 0.5 indicate random behavior and values above or below 0.5 indicate persistent or mean-reverting dynamics. Despite extensive research using the Hurst exponent to characterize market persistence and market-efficiency-related behavior, limited studies have investigated whether future Hurst exponent estimates can be forecast using machine learning techniques and whether these models can outperform a simple constant benchmark. This study addresses this gap by developing a machine learning framework to forecast the next-month Hurst exponent using firm-level descriptive, financial, technical, and statistical indicators and comparing their performance against a constant benchmark. A dataset comprising 141 Saudi-listed companies, 705 firm-month observations, approximately 147 predictor variables, and five monthly periods was constructed. Monthly Hurst exponent values were estimated using the Rescaled Range (R/S) method and used as the target variable. Linear Regression, Ridge Regression, Elastic Net, Support Vector Regression (SVR), Random Forest, and XGBoost were evaluated using an expanding-window time-series validation strategy with two chronological forecast origins. Model performance was assessed using Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and the coefficient of determination (R2). None of the evaluated machine learning models outperformed the constant benchmark, which achieved the lowest RMSE (0.227) and MAE (0.179). Ridge Regression performed relatively best among the machine learning models, with an RMSE of 0.236 and an MAE of 0.187, but it still failed to improve upon the benchmark, and all evaluated machine learning models produced negative R2 values. These results indicate that the selected firm-level descriptive, financial, technical, and statistical indicators provided limited incremental forecasting value relative to a simple constant benchmark within the adopted empirical design. Given the five-month observation period and limited number of chronological forecast origins, the findings are best interpreted as exploratory evidence regarding the ability of machine learning models to outperform a constant benchmark in forecasting next-month Hurst estimates, rather than as definitive evidence concerning market efficiency or the general predictability of financial markets. The study provides an empirical benchmark for future investigations into forecasting Hurst exponent estimates and changes in market persistence.

title: Land Use Transformation in Global Agri-Food Systems: China’s Role, Trade-Related Exposure, and Sustainable Land Use Pathways
abstract: Global agri-food systems increasingly spatially separate places of production and consumption, which is why national stabilization of agricultural land does not necessarily mean a reduction of the overall pressure on land resources. The aim of this paper is to link long-term cropland changes with crop production dynamics and international trade links. Digital paths are considered qualitatively as a supplementary interpretive layer, with a special focus on China. The primary land-use layer is based on FAOSTAT land use data for 2001–2023 and includes 218 countries and territories with complete endpoints. Production-land decoupling was analyzed in a narrower, fully reproductive sample of 140 countries. In the baseline classification, 44.3% of countries showed relative and 27.1% absolute decoupling; agreement with the baseline regimen was 95.0–97.9% with alternative thresholds and 91.4% when individual endpoints were replaced by 3-year averages. The validation sample is not compositionally neutral in relation to the 78 units without full production reconstruction; the median cropland change was +5.92% vs. −1.44% (Mann–Whitney U = 7350; p < 0.001), which is why the mode shares were not generalized to all 218 units. Between 2001 and 2023, China reduced cropland by 2.34%, while the Crop Production Index increased by 78.83%, which corresponds to absolute decoupling; the same regime is maintained in the three-year robustness specification. Among the top five sources of Chinese food imports in the WITS/UN Comtrade validation, the United States, Thailand, and Canada show absolute decoupling, while Brazil and Indonesia combine strong output growth with further cropland expansion and relative decoupling. The present results support a clear distinction between territorial production-land decoupling, trade-linked exposure, and full consumption-based land footprint. Digitization is not tested in this paper as an empirical determinant of land changes; it is considered as a potential, conditional mechanism based on the existing literature, while the empirical findings of this paper refer to patterns of land change, production, and trade-related exposure.

title: Long-Term Dynamics of Ulva prolifera Blooms in the Yellow Sea and Their Environmental Associations: Insights from Multi-Source Remote Sensing
abstract: Recurrent Ulva prolifera (U. prolifera) green tides in the Yellow Sea have become a persistent coastal ecological problem, yet their long-term phenological changes and responses to environmental variability remain insufficiently understood. Here, we reconstructed the spatiotemporal dynamics of U. prolifera from 2008 to 2025 using multi-source satellite observations. Floating algae were detected using the Floating Algae Index (FAI) or Alternative Floating Algae Index (AFAI), and subpixel coverage was estimated using linear spectral unmixing. The results showed that MODIS-derived green tide extent expanded markedly, reaching 886.13 km2 in 2021. June exhibited the strongest long-term increasing trend. VIIRS observations showed broadly similar spatial and interannual bloom patterns over 2016–2025, while hourly GOCI-II observations revealed pronounced intraday variability which coverage generally increasing from morning to noon or afternoon. Environmental analyses demonstrated that bloom variability was jointly regulated by multiple environmental factors, including nonlinear relationships with sea surface temperature, pH, and dissolved oxygen, as well as linear effects of salinity and silicate. The multivariable model explained 70.7% of the observed variation in bloom area, highlighting the importance of coupled physical and biogeochemical controls. These findings indicate that Yellow Sea green tides are becoming increasingly persistent under changing environmental conditions. Multi-source satellite monitoring can inform adaptive management that combines nature-based solutions (NbS), including source-region nutrient reduction, optimized aquaculture structures, ecological polyculture with competitive macroalgae, hydrodynamic-based interception, and sustainable biomass utilization. Such approaches may reduce bloom risks while enhancing coastal ecosystem resilience and transforming U. prolifera management from passive removal toward proactive ecological regulation.

title: Contrasting Seasonal Chlorophyll-a Dynamics in Tibetan Plateau Lakes Driven by Climate-Dependent Thermal and Mixing Processes
abstract: The Tibetan Plateau (TP) hosts the world’s largest and highest-altitude plateau lake system, whose ecosystems are highly sensitive to climate change. Chlorophyll-a (Chl-a), as a key indicator of phytoplankton biomass and lake trophic status, exhibits pronounced changes in response to long-term climatic and environmental changes. However, knowledge of its seasonal variations in TP lakes remains limited due to a shortage of high-time-resolution analyses based on in situ observations and remote sensing inversion. In this study, we compiled in situ Chl-a data from 95 lakes and combined them with Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) ocean-color bands (B8–B16) and the Climate Change Initiative (CCI) Chl-a product to develop a back-propagation neural network model specifically for oligotrophic plateau lakes. The model demonstrated excellent performance across training, testing, and independent validation datasets (R2 = 0.82–0.84; RMSE = 0.44–0.49 μg L−1), confirming its suitability for regional-scale retrievals. Independent external evaluation using 24 observations from 8 TP lakes excluded from model development yielded R2 = 0.85 and RMSE = 0.24 μg L−1. Using this model, we reconstructed Chl-a concentrations during the ice-free period (26 May to 9 December) from 2000 to 2022 for 163 lakes larger than 50 km2 and systematically analyzed their seasonal dynamics within the ice-free period and controlling factors. The mean Chl-a concentration across all study lakes was 1.43 μg L−1, with concentrations significantly higher in autumn (September–November) than in summer (June–August). Fuzzy c-means clustering classified the seasonal dynamics into two groups: Class I lakes (94 lakes, 60%), peaking in August and mainly located in the westerlies-dominated region (88%), were primarily influenced by air temperature, solar radiation, and water temperature; whereas Class II lakes (69 lakes, 40%), peaking in November and predominantly distributed in the monsoon-dominated region (72%), were mainly driven by wind speed and mixed-layer depth. From 2000 to 2022, the timing of Chl-a peaks exhibited contrasting trends, advancing in Class I lakes and delaying in Class II lakes. These results showed the ability of remote sensing to monitor seasonal Chl-a dynamics and regional differentiation in the TP lakes, and their underlying climatic and limnological drivers, as well as high-altitude lake responses to global climate change.

title: QASHI: Quality-Aware Scale-Protected Hybrid Inference for Small-Object Detection in Optical and SAR Remote Sensing Imagery
abstract: Object detection in high-resolution remote sensing imagery faces a resolution–context trade-off: resizing weakens small objects, whereas cropping can truncate targets and remove context. We present QASHI, a detector-retraining-free hybrid inference framework combining a full-image view, four overlapping tiles, and at most three additional regions of interest (ROIs). Quality-Aware Density (QAD) prioritizes local re-inference by combining small-candidate density with weak responses, candidate competition, and full/tile prediction inconsistency. Graph-based ranking correction, bounded BoxVote refinement, and scale-protected routing integrate local predictions with full-image context. Experiments cover VisDrone2019-DET, DIOR, SeaDronesSee v2, and SRSDD-v1.0 with two RT-DETR detectors. On VisDrone-val with RT-DETRv4-S, QASHI improves AP by 2.84 points over the SAHI baseline while reducing mean latency by 14.40%. Relative to Full, it gains 5.74 AP points at 4.52 times the latency. Selector ablations and local parameter analyses characterize how region priority and fusion settings affect detection accuracy and computational cost. On SRSDD, display-domain image-quality sensitivity tests with RT-DETR-R50 yield higher mean perturbed AP (32.52 versus 31.41), with relative AP retention of 93.44% versus 93.98%. QASHI combines prediction-guided local processing and source-aware fusion to improve remote sensing detection through inference-time use of a fixed detector.

title: DMFNet: Phase-Enhanced Multi-Level Deformable Fusion for Multimodal Remote Sensing Classification
abstract: The collaborative classification of hyperspectral images (HSI) with a complementary modality such as light detection and ranging (LiDAR) or synthetic aperture radar (SAR), which is known as multi-source remote sensing image classification (MRSIC), can combine rich spectral information with structural cues and is helpful for the recognition of complex ground objects. However, effectively incorporating these structural cues into multi-level spectral-spatial features and modeling their spatial relationships remain challenging under limited training samples. To address these problems, a multi-level convolutional collaborative classification network based on the DefMamba fusion mechanism (DMFNet) is proposed in this paper. First, monogenic phase congruency (MPC) responses are added to the complementary modality to enhance its structural information. Then, a dual-branch feature extraction module is constructed to derive multi-level features from HSI and the enhanced complementary modality and aggregate them into a joint representation. Finally, a DefMamba fusion module applies deformable selective scanning to the aggregated features, so as to adaptively model spatial dependencies according to the fused content. Experiments on three public multimodal remote sensing datasets, covering both HSI–LiDAR and HSI–SAR settings, demonstrate that DMFNet achieves the highest mean overall accuracy among the compared methods with 10 labeled training samples per class, with the largest improvement on the HSI-SAR scene. Additional experiments on Houston 2018 further evaluate its classification performance on a large-scale scene.

title: Revealing the Hidden Archaeological Landscape of Ancient Colchis Using Multispectral and Thermal UAV Remote Sensing
abstract: This study investigates the potential of integrated multispectral and thermal UAV remote sensing for detecting and mapping hidden archaeological structures of Proto-Colchian and Colchian settlement systems of the 3rd–1st millennium BCE, within the Rioni River basin in western Georgia. Characteristic settlement mounds (Dikhagudzuba), moats/ditches, and possible paleochannel networks represent a unique example of large-scale adaptation to waterlogged environments, and limited archaeological excavations have significantly hindered the identification and interpretation of these buried landscape features. Pilot UAV surveys were conducted at four archaeological sites differing in location, geomorphological setting, land use, and degree of preservation using DJI Mavic 3M multispectral and DJI Matrice 4T thermal UAV platforms. Multispectral imagery enabled the detection of vegetation and soil-moisture anomalies associated with buried ditches, embankments, canals, and settlement structures, while thermal data revealed differences in thermal inertia related to subsurface archaeological remains and palaeohydrological features. The study covered approximately 15.4 ha and produced 5836 RGB, 2219 multispectral, and 3617 thermal images with spatial resolutions ranging from 1.87 to 4.61 cm. The integration of high-resolution elevation models, RGB imagery, vegetation indices (ExG and normalized EVI2), and thermal data enabled the identification and characterization of microtopographic, vegetation, moisture, and thermal anomalies associated with archaeological and palaeohydrological features. The investigated mounds cover 2754–4685 m2, reach approximately 9–10 m in height, and are surrounded by moats/ditches covering 4265–6520 m2 and ramparts reaching approximately 2–3.5 m in height. The results demonstrate that combined UAV-based multispectral and thermal remote sensing provides a highly effective non-invasive tool for archaeological prospection in dynamic wetland landscapes. The proposed approach significantly improves the detection of buried archaeological features and paleochannels, while also supporting landscape-scale analyses, monitoring of archaeological heritage, and the development of predictive archaeological models for western Georgia.

title: From Remote Sensing Accuracy to MRV Readiness: A Systematic Review and GeoAI Framework for Tropical Forest Biomass Estimation
abstract: Remote sensing combined with machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) is widely used to estimate tropical forest aboveground biomass (AGB), yet it is unclear how fully published studies document the evidence that Measurement, Reporting and Verification (MRV) of forest carbon would require. We assessed this reporting evidence using a five-dimension framework (accuracy reporting, uncertainty quantification, spatial validation, temporal consistency and transparency) applied to a systematically identified set of empirical studies. From 1706 records retrieved from Scopus and Lens.org on 4 March 2026, 1146 unique works were screened against a locked eligibility codebook; 153 reports were assessed in full text where accessible, and 59 empirical ML/DL remote-sensing AGB studies in tropical or subtropical forests formed the core review set. For each dimension we coded evidence as confirmed, reported as absent, insufficient or inaccessible, and report the share of studies between the confirmed count and the confirmed-plus-undetermined count. Accuracy metrics were reported in 66–88% of studies, but spatially independent validation was confirmed in only 32–42%, spatially explicit or area-level uncertainty in 44–54%, multi-date analysis with an explicit consistency method in 14–22%, public code in 14–29% and public reference data in 15–29%. Only 12 studies confirmed both independent validation and propagated uncertainty. The results describe the evidence reported in research papers and do not assess compliance of any product with a carbon standard. Screening and evidence extraction were AI-assisted against a fixed codebook with a verbatim evidence phrase for every decision, and a stratified sample of 60 screening decisions was independently verified by two co-authors (agreement 88% and 78%). We recommend that biomass studies intended to inform MRV report spatially blocked or independent-site validation, propagate uncertainty to area totals, and release code and reference data.
