title: Editing as Language: Teaching LLM Agents a Grammar for Native Context Editing
abstract: A synopsis in novels folds a story into a few lines; a function in code gathers many steps with a single execution. Context editing is native to language itself. In this paper, we propose the Native Context Editing (NCE) framework, which gives language model agents a grammar for natively editing their own context. By encoding context-editing operations in a grammar of dedicated special tokens, we teach the agents to invoke edits through the language itself. We train agents on iteratively constructed trajectory segments, with each teacher edit conditioned on the evolving context. This establishes context editing as an atomic and inherent capability of LLM agents, enabling them to dynamically modify their context as they generate responses over long-horizon reasoning and interaction. Compared with context-editing methods that learn to generate tool-use code within specific external harness environments, our approach integrates context editing as an internal mechanism of the model's native generation process, enabling better generalization across diverse real-world workflows. On four long-horizon agentic benchmarks (Terminal-Bench 2.0, SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Multilingual, and SWE-bench Pro), NCE improves the average task success rate over the base model by 5.6 percentage points for LongCat-Flash-Lite-Sparse and by 4.5 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, while reducing average token usage by 36% and 15%, respectively.

title: Tricking Synthetic Image Detectors with Amortized Generative Attacks
abstract: Rapid advances in image synthesis have increased the need for reliable synthetic-image detectors, yet their robustness to transferable attacks remains incomplete and understudied. Existing evaluations generally examine whether an attack constructed against one detector transfers to another, but rarely isolate how its effectiveness changes when the attacked images originate from different generators. We conduct a systematic evaluation of three representative attacks: two iterative perturbation-based methods, MIG and MuMoDIG, and the amortized generative attack Tricker. Across four detectors and five generators spanning diverse architectures, we introduce a two-axis evaluation protocol that independently varies the surrogate detector used to construct or train the attack and the generator supplying its input images. We assess attack effectiveness, cross-detector transferability, perceptual quality, runtime, and interaction with common post-processing operations. We revisit Tricker and show that its data and training requirements can be substantially reduced, enabling broader and more efficient evaluation. Our results demonstrate that transferability is not a detector-only property: the input-generator distribution strongly influences both evasion effectiveness and attacked-image quality. MIG and MuMoDIG exhibit pronounced dependence on the detector--generator pair, whereas Tricker provides more uniform white-box evasion and image quality. We additionally observe that post-processing maintains the asymmetric transferability topology. These findings expose a neglected dimension of attack evaluation and motivate transfer-aware protocols that jointly account for detector and generator variation. We will release our code, evaluation data, and trained attack models with a responsible-use statement.

title: Voice-Based AI Feedback in Higher Education: A Field Study on Quality and Actionability
abstract: Student feedback is a critical input for continuous improvement in higher education, yet traditional end-of-semester written surveys suffer from low response rates, superficial answers, satisficing, and limited actionability. Voice-based conversational AI agents can conduct structured interviews at scale, asking open-ended questions and probing follow-ups, and may capture richer qualitative feedback than written instruments. This research proposal asks what characteristics, depth, and strategic value feedback collected through voice-based conversational AI agents has in higher education, and whether such agents elicit detailed, honest, and actionable feedback that can support instructional improvement and institutional learning. Drawing on survey-mode-effects research, the Computers As Social Actors (CASA) paradigm, and dynamic capabilities theory, we develop three hypotheses on elaboration, social presence and disclosure, and actionability. A completed technical pilot at the Technical University of Munich established the feasibility of telephone-based AI interviews; the main field study is planned for the "Advanced Leadership Communication" course at MIT Sloan with approximately 60 students, using a convergent mixed-methods design and a four-dimensional coding framework for actionability (specificity, thematic richness, constructive orientation, contextual depth). The study extends CASA theory to evaluative educational settings, characterizes voice-based AI as a distinct feedback modality, and links micro-level feedback quality to institutional sensing capabilities.

title: Learning Which Device to Call: Online Tool Grounding for LLM Agents in IoT
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) gives large language model (LLM) agents access to physical observations, but one requested capability is usually offered by several devices, and the agent's plan does not say which one to call. Existing work retrieves relevant tools and checks plan feasibility, without learning which eligible device returns a useful observation. Unlike previous works, we study online tool grounding: binding an already specified tool call to one physical endpoint under service cost and device participation constraints. We propose a framework that learns which physical device should execute each agent-issued call. It formulates selection as a contextual bandit problem and combines adaptive context partitions with hierarchical endpoint trees, so that execution feedback is reused across related requests and devices. Selection balances task success against service cost while respecting device capability, authorization, battery reserves, and availability. Gaussian reward aggregation provides an optional mechanism for protecting individual feedback values. Theoretical results establish a finite-horizon regret bound and differential privacy for released reward statistics under fixed, reward-independent assignments. In a simulated loading-dock workload, the proposed router achieves higher step success and better cost-adjusted service, at lower simulated device energy and latency, than nearest-device, advertised-quality, UCB1, and LinUCB selection.

title: Industrial Agentic AI: LLM-Driven New-Generation Agents for Smart Manufacturing
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are enabling agents to move beyond predefined workflows toward autonomous planning and execution, creating new opportunities for smart manufacturing. However, dynamic environments, complex physical constraints, and stringent reliability requirements hinder the direct deployment of general-purpose agents in smart manufacturing. This article presents a systematic overview of LLM-driven industrial agents. First, we analyze five key challenges and discuss the concept and core characteristics of industrial agents. We then establish a unified taxonomy covering application scenarios, embodiment forms, and five capability levels. Next, we propose a four-layer system architecture and detail its core modules and operational mechanisms for closed-loop task execution. Finally, we review representative applications across the industrial lifecycle and outline future research directions. This article provides a structured reference for the design, development, and application of industrial agents.

title: MAMath-Bench: Process-Aware and Robust Evaluation of Multimodal Multi-Agent Mathematical Reasoning
abstract: Mathematical reasoning is a fundamental capability for educational applications of Large Language Models (LLMs), where reliable problem solving requires not only correct answers but also coherent and verifiable reasoning processes. Multi-agent systems (MASs) have shown growing potential in this domain by leveraging collaboration and verification among multiple LLM agents. However, existing evaluations primarily focus on the correctness of final answers in text-only settings, offering limited insight into multimodal reasoning capabilities, the reliability of intermediate reasoning steps, and robustness against reasoning errors. To address these limitations, we introduce MAMath-Bench, a process-aware benchmark designed to evaluate the multimodal mathematical reasoning capabilities of MASs. MAMath-Bench comprises 1,003 problems spanning 11 mathematical categories, multiple difficulty levels, and several modalities, including text, images, and audio. It features fine-grained milestone annotations to evaluate systems across three dimensions: problem-solving correctness, reasoning-process reliability, and robustness to adversarial reasoning-chain perturbations. Our evaluation yields three key findings. First, multi-agent collaboration does not consistently improve final-answer accuracy over strong single LLMs. Second, collaboration can substantially enhance the coverage of intermediate reasoning, but such gains may come at the cost of increased reasoning redundancy. Third, current systems remain vulnerable to adversarial reasoning errors, particularly those involving subtle structural perturbations. The dataset is available at https://github.com/mira-ai-lab/AgentMath.

title: From Last-Layer to Cross-Layer: One-Shot Joint Classifier Reconstruction for Federated Learning
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training while preserving data privacy. However, non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data inevitably introduces classifier bias, leading to significant performance degradation. Existing studies primarily focus on calibrating or reconstructing the classifier after FL training to alleviate this bias. We find that the last-layer representations of the global model are often suboptimal for establishing a global decision boundary. Instead, classifiers constructed based on intermediate-layer representations can achieve superior performance. This finding provides a critical insight into overcoming the performance bottleneck inherent in existing paradigms. Nevertheless, identifying the optimal layer without auxiliary datasets or prior knowledge remains a formidable challenge. In this paper, we propose FLARE (Federated Cross-Layer Joint ClAssifier REconstruction) which rethinks classifier reconstruction from a cross-layer perspective and generalizes ridge regression to jointly exploit cross-layer representations, thereby surpassing the performance of any individual layer. Specifically, after FL training, clients perform only a single forward pass to extract class-conditional statistics from predefined layers. The server aggregates these statistics to construct a joint cross-layer ridge classifier, where an adaptive coupling coefficient regulates cross-layer correlations, thereby facilitating the integration of complementary discriminative information. Extensive experiments across 11 datasets, 8 model architectures, and diverse data heterogeneity scenarios demonstrate that FLARE, as a plug-and-play post-processing method, improves accuracy by 11.35% with only one additional communication round.

title: Dynamic System Inspired Continuous Large Language Model for AI4Science Tasks
abstract: Scientific foundation models increasingly operate on continuous phenomena, yet still use discrete residual computation. We ask whether pretrained residual transformations can support additional latent computation without expanding the backbone. To test this possibility, we introduce Continuum-LM, which reuses these transformations as dynamical operators in a continuous-depth language model. Its hidden states evolve through an ordinary differential equation evaluated by higher-order numerical integration, with solver order and step size controlling computation. Across eight scientific tasks, Continuum-LM trains stably and improves mean exact-match accuracy by 7.77 and 10.96 percentage points over discrete counterparts at the 0.6B and 1.7B scales, respectively. At 0.6B, it also outperforms an Ouro-style recurrent control under matched parameter and residual-function evaluation budgets. Together, these results support extensible computational depth through parameter reuse, identifying continuous hidden-state evolution as a practical design dimension for scientific language models beyond parameter scaling.

title: Do LLMs Really Lack Difference Awareness? Uncovering Heuristic Substitution in Group-Differentiating Fairness
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the issue of difference awareness in LLMs, defined as a model's ability to recognize and acknowledge meaningful differences between social groups in fairness decision-making. Previous studies have consistently shown that models perform poorly on such tasks, a finding commonly attributed to a lack of difference awareness. We propose an alternative account, which we term Fairness Heuristic Substitution: difference awareness is not necessarily absent, but the complex demand of simultaneously identifying relevant group differences and determining their implications for fairness decisions may lead models to substitute the simpler, more accessible equal-treatment heuristic, i.e., formal equality. Based on this hypothesis, we introduce TDD, a Two-stage Distinguish-Decide framework that explicitly decomposes fairness reasoning into first distinguishing contextually relevant group differences and then making the corresponding decision, thereby discouraging reliance on formal-equality shortcuts. (i) Across four benchmarks and ten models ranging from billions to trillions of parameters, TDD significantly outperforms one-stage baselines, even one strengthened through simulated test-set leakage. (ii) Combining TDD with neuron-level contrastive probing provides mechanistic evidence consistent with the Fairness Heuristic Substitution hypothesis by revealing two signatures of the formal-equality: a compact, locally coordinated representational structure and a pronounced activation bias under default reasoning. (iii) TDD's stage-wise decomposition uncovers overlooked failure modes in fairness reasoning, including heuristic displacement and misaligned stage dynamics.

title: FoundPDE: A generative foundation model for data-driven symbolic discovery of partial differential equations
abstract: Discovering governing partial differential equations (PDEs) from observed data is a central inverse problem in computational science and engineering: the goal is not only to predict trajectories, but to identify interpretable symbolic laws that can be analyzed and reused. Existing PDE discovery methods often depend on hand-designed libraries, accurate numerical derivatives, or per-equation symbolic search, making them fragile under sparse observations, noisy data, broad equation families, and unseen symbolic compositions. Here, we introduce FoundPDE, a pretrained data-to-symbol foundation model for PDE discovery. FoundPDE maps discretized spatio-temporal trajectories to symbolic equations with a transformer, uses Fourier and first-order spatial-derivative augmentation to expose complementary trajectory information, refines numerical coefficients, and supports downstream extension with improved generalization through few-shot fine-tuning and hierarchical discovery. On a clean in-domain benchmark spanning 20 PDE families, our model reaches 97.50% type recognition. Under coefficient shifts beyond the training support, type recognition remains 90.53%; under multiplicative Gaussian noise on the model input, it is 94.43% at a 2% noise level but falls to 52.09% at 10%. For unseen composite equations, few-shot fine-tuning reaches over 90% exact recovery on four held-out families, and we further develop a hierarchical discovery algorithm that recovers two-term composites without fine-tuning FoundPDE. By amortizing symbolic discovery across equation families, FoundPDE shifts PDE discovery from per-dataset search toward a reusable pretrained model that extends to new physics with limited additional data, a step toward foundation models that uncover interpretable governing laws directly from scientific data.

title: Towards Industry 5.0 in South Africa: A Strategic Framework for Readiness and Adoption
abstract: This paper explores South Africa's readiness for transitioning from Industry 4.0 to Industry 5.0, focusing on the development of a strategic framework that emphasises human-centric, resilient, and sustainable industrial practices. While Industry 4.0 revolutionises manufacturing through automation, AI, and IoT, Industry 5.0 enhances this paradigm by promoting collaboration between humans and machines, ethical technology use, and environmental consciousness. Drawing from theoretical models such as Fit-Viability and Task-Technology Fit (TTF), the study identifies five critical factors that influence Industry 5.0 adoption in South Africa: technological infrastructure, human capital, policy frameworks, economic feasibility, and energy reliability. It further analyses key enablers, including AI integration, green innovation, and digital literacy, while highlighting systemic challenges like infrastructure gaps, skills shortages, and regulatory uncertainty. Sectoral case studies in banking, manufacturing, mining, and agriculture reveal uneven uptake of Industry 4.0 technologies, signalling both potential and limitations for Industry 5.0. The paper also examines the role of the Just Energy Transition (JET), hydrogen economy, and off-grid renewable energy in fostering sustainable industrialisation. Education reform and cultural transformation within industries are deemed essential to bridge existing gaps. The implications of non-adoption are severe, ranging from economic marginalisation to increased inequality and reduced foreign investment. The study concludes by advocating for policy alignment, cross-sector collaboration, and targeted investment to facilitate South Africa's transition. It recommends integrating elements of Society 5.0 to further promote inclusivity, digital public services, and long-term sustainability, positioning South Africa to thrive in the evolving global industrial landscape.

title: CONDITIONS FOR THE FORMATION OF MELIORATIVE REGIMES OF SOILS IN RICE IRRIGATION SYSTEMS
abstract: This study systematizes and quantitatively evaluates the main factors determining soil reclamation conditions and rice productivity in the Krasnodar Krai–Russia’s leading region for rice grain production. Based on a synthesis of literature materials, regulatory data and observational results from rice irrigation systems in the Lower Kuban, an analysis was conducted of three groups of factors: natural (temperature regime, photosynthetically active radiation), land reclamation-related (particle size distribution, soil salinity, irrigation water quality, drainage), and technological (crop rotation, drainage and discharge network operation, field layout). Empirical relationships between rice yield and soil salinity, the Stebler irrigation coefficient, the specific length of the collector-drainage network, and the layout defect criterion have been summarized. Using digital models of two real fields (Robur software, 20×20 m grid), it is shown that increasing the planning error from ±5 to ±15 cm reduces the predicted yield from 6,47 to 4,04 t/ha (by 37,6%). It has been established that the limiting factor for rice productivity in the region is not heat availability, but rather a combination of managed land reclamation and technological conditions.

title: Genetic Algorithm-Based Feature Selection and Random Forest Modelling of Agricultural Biotechnology Adoption and Crop Yield in Tamil Nadu
abstract: This research paper attempts to identify the Biotechnology inputs such as tissue-culture seedlings, improved seed, microbial biofertilisers and bio pesticides are promoted widely in Tamil Nadu, yet their combined association with crop performance is seldom examined across many crops at once. This study analyses 6,500 farm-level records covering 38 districts, 14 crops and the years 2021–2025 (a simulated research dataset) and introduces a relative yield index (RYI) that expresses each yield as a ratio to its crop median, so that crops with very different absolute yields can be compared. A genetic algorithm (GA) searches the space of 41 candidate predictors, using cross-validated Random Forest accuracy with a small size penalty as fitness, and a final Random Forest is trained on the selected subset. The GA retained 23 predictors (a 43.9% reduction) and reached a hold-out R² of 0.382 and RMSE of 0.140, against 0.367 and 0.141 for a Random Forest on all predictors; gradient boosting scored highest (R² = 0.418). Tissue-culture seedlings (+10.1%, Cohen d = 0.58) and improved seed (+7.2%, d = 0.40) were linked to a higher RYI, whereas farmer training showed no detectable effect. Irrigation source was the dominant predictor: drip or sprinkler farms exceeded rain fed farms by 27%.

title: Complexity-Aware Geographic Fairness in Crop Yield Prediction Using Diversity-Weighted Learning
abstract: Machine-learning models for crop yield prediction are usually judged by overall accuracy alone, which hides large differences in prediction quality between regions. This study shows that a standard Random Forest with an aggregate R² of 0.935 can be misleading: state-level MAE ranges from 0.168 t/ha to 2.505 t/ha, a 14.9-fold gap that the overall score conceals. Two independent structural factors underlie this imbalance: the number of records per state (data-volume imbalance) and the agricultural complexity of each state, both of which can be observed in any census or statistical record. To address both at once, a Complexity-Aware Geographic Fairness (CAGF) framework is presented that combines a Crop Diversity Index based on Shannon entropy with inverse-frequency sample re-weighting. Four architectures (Random Forest, XGBoost, SVR and MLP) are evaluated under three training regimes (unweighted baseline, inverse-frequency weighting and CAGF) using expanding-window temporal cross-validation, and TreeSHAP attribution shows that CAGF directs model attention toward crop-specific regional patterns. For XGBoost, CAGF gives the best overall accuracy among the three regimes (R² = 0.918; MAE = 1.299 t/ha) together with a lower geographic Gini of prediction error than the unweighted baseline (GGPE = 0.289 versus 0.293), so fairness improves without any loss of accuracy.

title: Optimizing Agentic Artificial Intelligence to Improve Business Process Automation Efficiency through Modern Digital Technology
abstract: In the era of digital transformation, traditional Business Process Automation (BPA) still faces limitations in handling dynamic, unstructured, and complex decision-making tasks. Agentic Artificial Intelligence (Agentic AI), which is characterized by autonomous agents capable of advanced reasoning, dynamic planning, and multi-step workflow execution, is considered a promising approach to improving the efficiency and adaptability of enterprise operations. This study aims to examine how Agentic AI can be optimized to improve BPA performance within modern digital ecosystems. Using a qualitative approach through a literature study, this paper synthesizes recent academic literature, theoretical models, and technological frameworks related to intelligent automation. The review indicates that integrating Agentic AI into enterprise business architectures has the potential to move beyond rigid, rule-based automation by enabling adaptive problem-solving, real-time context awareness, and cross-system collaboration. The reviewed literature also suggests that autonomous agents may help reduce operational bottlenecks, lower human intervention in routine cognitive workflows, and support more efficient resource allocation across organizational functions. In addition, this study identifies key implementation challenges, including system interoperability, algorithmic transparency, data privacy risks, and the governance mechanisms required for secure deployment. This study contributes to the literature on enterprise automation by proposing strategic considerations for organizations that seek to use digital technology to build more resilient, scalable, and intelligent business processes. Because this is a literature-based study, the findings are conceptual and do not provide empirical evidence of efficiency gains.

title: Analysis of post-adoption behaviors of climate change adaptation strategies among smallholder farmers: Evidence from Burkina Fa-so
abstract: Enhancing long-term adaptation to climate change in developing countries requires an under-standing of farmers’ post-adoption behaviors. This study examines the factors influencing post-adoption decisions, namely substitution, maintenance, combination, and abandonment, across soil and water conservation techniques (SWCTs), agroforestry, crop associations, and improved seed varieties in climate-vulnerable contexts. Using a multinomial logit model with sample-selection bi-as correction and data from the Permanent Agricultural Survey covering 13,030 farmers in Burkina Faso from 2015 to 2019, the findings reveal that men are more likely to maintain, substitute, or combine SWCTs, agroforestry, and crop associations rather than abandon them, while age and education exhibit practice-specific effects. Land ownership, labor availability, farm size, and external support are associated with greater continuation, substitution, or combination for several practices rather than abandonment. Climatic shocks also generate differentiated responses, with drought increasing the likelihood of SWCT abandonment, while crop associations are less likely to be abandoned in Sahelian and Sahelo-Sahelian zones. These findings highlight the need for post-adoption policies that complement initial adoption support through tailored extension services, improved access to productive resources and institutional support, and geographically and climatically differentiated interventions to sustain and adjust existing adaptation strategies.

title: Comparative genomic characterization and germination-associated expression of DET2 and CER10 related reductases in Chenopodium quinoa.
abstract: Genome annotations frequently group DEETIOLATED2 (DET2), ECERIFERUM10 (CER10), and related proteins under broad steroid-reductase-like designations, despite experimentally characterized members participating in distinct metabolic pathways associated with plant development and environmental responses. Here, we comparatively characterized DET2 and CER10 related reductases in Arabidopsis thaliana, Amaranthus hypochondriacus, and the allotetraploid crop Chenopodium quinoa. Phylogenetic analysis resolved five groups and clearly separated DET2-like and CER10-like proteins. Conserved motifs, exon-intron organization, local microsynteny, and predicted membrane topology and protein structure further supported this distinction and the retention of paired quinoa loci following allopolyploidization. Public expression datasets revealed marked transcriptional differences among family members. Germination and expression analyses were subsequently performed in the quinoa accessions Giza1 and Puno (Q04), which showed contrasting responses to 250 mM NaCl. Q04 maintained rapid germination under salinity, whereas Giza1 displayed a pronounced delay and reduced final germination. Among four genes analysed by RT-qPCR, CqCER10.1 showed the clearest accession- and time-dependent expression pattern. Under 250 mM NaCl, CqCER10.1 transcript levels were significantly higher in Q04 than in Giza1 during early germination, coinciding with the markedly faster and more successful germination of Q04 under salinity. In Giza1, CqCER10.1 accumulation occurred later, broadly following its delayed germination progression. CqCER10.2 and CqDET2.2 remained weakly expressed, whereas CqDET2.1 accumulated mainly at later stages. Given the contrasting behaviour of the CER10-like copies (homoeologs), comparative analysis of their upstream regions in the QQ74 reference genome revealed substantial sequence divergence together with locally conserved regions and putative cis-regulatory elements. Overall, these results refine the classification of DET2- and CER10 related reductases in quinoa and reveal pronounced transcriptional asymmetry among retained gene copies. CqCER10.1 expression was associated with the contrasting germination behaviour of Giza1 and Q04, particularly under salinity. Whether this association reflects developmental progression, accession-specific regulation under salinity, or both remains to be determined.

title: Modeling associations between windbreak density and wind-driven crop losses using graph convolutional networks across four U.S. Great Plains states
abstract: Wind damage has long posed economic challenges for farmers. To minimize their impacts, farmers practice planting rows of trees around the farm.Query However, the economic benefits of these windbreaks at the regional scale remain underexplored. Specifically, there is a lack of large-scale quantitative analyses of the effects of windbreaks on wind-related crop losses. We present a machine-learning technique to analyze the relationship between windbreaks and wind-related crop loss (crop indemnity) in four US Great Plains states: Kansas, Nebraska, South Dakota, and North Dakota. We analyze the relationships among tree density, wind speed (gust), and indemnity for a subset of crops, i.e., corn, soybean, wheat, and sunflower, based on data from 2015 to 2021. To capture spatial dependencies, we develop a graph convolutional network (GCN) where counties are modeled as nodes connected by geographic adjacency. This approach accounts for localized wind patterns and tree coverage, shows robustness over different settings, and achieves better performance compared to baselines. A perturbation-based training method is used to enhance model explainability. Consistently, regions with greater tree density exhibited lower predicted indemnity losses, while areas with stronger winds faced higher risks. These findings are consistent with the hypothesis that windbreaks may provide dual environmental and economic benefits, though causal attribution requires farm-level study designs.

title: Multi-Perspective explainability in traffic prediction: A neuro-symbolic approach using CNN-LSTMs and concept lattices
abstract: The rapid urbanization and continuous growth of vehicle ownership have escalated traffic congestion into a critical socioeconomic challenge, resulting in massive productivity losses and environmental degradation. To establish effective Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), reliable and accurate traffic forecasting is paramount. While deep learning (DL) algorithms, particularly Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), have established themselves as state-of-the-art for spatiotemporal sequence forecasting, their inherent “black-box” nature severely limits their practical deployment in high-stakes traffic management. Decision-makers require transparent, qualitative reasoning behind algorithmic forecasts. Current post-hoc numerical Explainable AI (XAI) methods, such as SHAP and Integrated Gradients (IG), quantify feature attribution but fail to provide structured, human-readable rule mapping. To bridge the gap between predictive performance and model transparency, this paper proposes a novel Neuro-Symbolic Explainable Deep Learning framework. We integrate the statistical learning power of a hybrid CNN-LSTM architecture (the ’Neural’ component) with the rigorous logical reasoning of Formal Concept Analysis (the ’Symbolic’ component). Validated on an extensive real-world, five-year multivariate dataset from PLUS Malaysia Berhad (encompassing 73,891 aggregated records across multiple vehicle classes), the CNN-LSTM consistently outperforms standalone LSTM, BiLSTM, and GRU baselines, achieving the lowest Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). Furthermore, the synthesis of FCA with SHAP, LIME, and IG establishes a consensus view of feature importance, explicitly proving that the hybrid predictive-symbolic framework yields robust, highly accurate, and thoroughly interpretable forecasts suitable for modern ITS architectures.

title: Real-time table tennis detection and motion trajectory forecasting using improved YOLOv8 and GRU
abstract: To enhance the perception and prediction performance of table tennis perception and future movement, this study presents a framework for detecting and predicting the future movement of the table tennis game based on an optimized version of YOLOv8 and the Gated Recurrent Unit. On the detection side, this study designs a detail-preserving and motion-consistency-enhanced YOLOv8. The network introduces a P2 high-resolution branch, spatial rearrangement downsampling, lightweight cross-scale attention, and motion-consistency confidence recalibration to strengthen feature representation and interference suppression for high-speed small targets. On the forecasting side, this study develops a Physics-constrained Transformer-Gated Recurrent Unit network. This network uses constant acceleration Kalman filter algorithm, time-based feature learning, residual correction mechanism, and bounce-on-table constraint for predicting future trajectories. The experiment result shows that using an improved detection network yields an F1 score of 95.36% under blurred and occluded scenarios. The normalized ball-center error decreases to 0.52%, and the inference speed reaches 151.98 FPS. For motion trajectory forecasting, the average displacement error within a 300 ms interval is 44.91 mm, while the landing-point error is 50.68 mm. The physical violation rate is only 3.12%, and the recovery rate under controlled missing observations reaches 90.61 ± 1.05%. These findings prove that the introduced model is able to provide significantly more robust high-speed detection of table tennis as well as more physically realistic long-term trajectory forecasting. The model is thus able to offer reliable technical assistance in intelligent training and match analysis. Not applicable.

title: Operation state gated topology aware multimodal fusion for simulation based active distribution network risk assessment
abstract: Active distribution planning requires day-ahead identification of buses exposed to voltage and loading stress. Separating injection forecasting from feeder simulation leaves the contribution of multimodal fusion to node-risk estimation unresolved. We develop OSTMF-Net, an operation-state-gated topology-aware multimodal fusion network that combines temporal and graph experts through convex, residual and direct heads selected on a chronological validation holdout. Public load and NASA POWER weather variables are mapped to the IEEE 123-node OpenDSS feeder. Quasi-static time-series simulations generate deterministic 24-h absolute-risk and positive-increment targets under base, high-photovoltaic, heavy-load and combined-stress conditions. Evaluation measures agreement with OpenDSS-derived risk surrogates within this reproducible simulation benchmark. Among matched fusion methods across eight correlated scenario-target cases, OSTMF-Net obtains the lowest root mean square error (RMSE) in six and remains within 1% of the lowest value in seven. Mean case-wise RMSE reductions are 9.77%, 17.37% and 3.72% relative to a validation-selected expert, uniform averaging and linear stacking, respectively; gains over stacking concentrate in absolute-risk cases. A matched state-adaptive control yields mean RMSE 0.03460 versus 0.03080 for OSTMF-Net. Forecast perturbations, sensor-input corruption and label sensitivity assess robustness to input and target changes. On a disjoint 2013 chronology on the same feeder, OSTMF-Net records RMSE 0.03067, high-risk F1 0.795 and Top-10 agreement 1.000. The results connect complementary temporal and topology information with state-dependent correction, supporting auditable day-ahead bus-risk screening on the evaluated OpenDSS benchmark.

title: A cross-domain review of artificial intelligence techniques for iot security, computer networks, image processing and smart agriculture in connected environments
abstract: The rapid digitization of modern systems has increased the demand for intelligent, adaptive, and data-driven solutions across connected systems. However, these domains face persistent challenges such as heterogeneous datasets, limited labeled data, real-time processing constraints, privacy concerns, model interpretability, and poor generalization across environments. This review examines the application of major Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques for solving classification, prediction, optimization, anomaly detection, routing, image analysis, and decision-support problems. The empirical patterns across the literature are summarized cautiously across studies. General lessons that emerged across the reviewed domains were also presented. Overall, the review provides researchers with a concise foundation for understanding current AI methods, their practical limitations, and future research directions in the aspect of connected environments. This article has tried to clarify various aspects and overall issues related to the use of AI techniques in computer networks, image processing and computer vision, smart agriculture and related intelligent systems. The authors believe that this is a comprehensive and integrated survey of these AI techniques in a number of application domains, with an emphasis on their practical suitability, their current empirical limitations, and future research directions. Thus, the article is informative to researchers in the field and may be a guide to future research on the development of robust, interpretable, scalable, and context-aware AI-based connected systems.

title: Digital visual transmission and watermark protection of intangible cultural heritage art images based on the HAIWAN method
abstract: The art images of intangible cultural heritage undergo composite interference while being transmitted digitally. Current approaches use differentiable attack layers for adversarial attacks, but the problem is that the attack layer does not capture composite transmission distortion sufficiently. This study focuses on intangible cultural heritage images and proposed a highly applicable and highly imperceptible guided watermark attack simulation network algorithm and a Hybrid-Adaptive Image Watermark Attack Network-guided dual-domain robust blind watermarking protection model. The former continuously generates strong attack samples during training through local stability enhancement, multi-scale context aggregation, and constrained downsampling. The latter exploits the low-frequency subband in the luminance component for the wavelet transform and the frequency domain coefficients in the discrete cosine transform as dual-domain carriers, together with a channel attention embedding enhancement unit for end-to-end cooperative optimization. Experimental results show that the HAI-WAN attack samples retain a wPSNR of 35.72 dB, while their BER and NC values on three representative images range from 18.18 to 20.98% and from 75.21 to 77.97%, respectively. Compared with WatermarkAttacker and WEvade, HAI-WAN causes greater watermark extraction errors, although the remaining NC values indicate that the watermark is not completely removed. The error bit rate of the proposed model decreases to 0.0169, and the watermark detection accuracy reaches 98.68%. After introducing attack simulation training, the error bit rate under strong perturbation decreases from 15.48–29.87% to 9.86–20.74%. This technique addresses the issue of achieving a trade-off between the visual quality of art images of intangible cultural heritage and copyright marks’ robust recovery under complicated transmission situations. Not only can it protect the authenticity of intangible cultural heritage art in exhibitions, but it can also offer low latency and convenient support in media integrated communications for copyright verification.

title: Current applications of artificial intelligence for advancing agriculture, sustainability and climate mitigation
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping agriculture by enabling data-driven decision-making across crop production systems and supporting the transition toward more sustainable, resilient, and climate-smart farming. This review critically synthesizes advances in AI applications spanning precision irrigation, nutrient and soil management, yield prediction, pest and disease monitoring, computer vision, autonomous agricultural robotics, and large language model (LLM)-based decision support systems. Beyond summarizing technological developments, the review evaluates their practical deployment, emphasizing that successful agricultural AI depends not only on predictive accuracy but also on model generalizability, explainability, economic feasibility, interoperability, and integration with existing agronomic knowledge. Emerging technologies including Vision Transformers, foundation models, Digital Twins, multimodal AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and federated and continual learning—are discussed as important directions for overcoming limitations related to data scarcity, environmental variability, and scalable field implementation. The review highlights that responsible AI adoption requires transparent governance frameworks addressing data ownership, privacy, algorithmic fairness, cybersecurity, and equitable access, particularly for smallholder farming systems. Although numerous AI models report outstanding performance, widespread agricultural adoption remains constrained by cross-region validation, fragmented datasets, infrastructure requirements, and insufficient real-world deployment. Future progress will depend on multidisciplinary collaboration integrating advances in artificial intelligence, sensing technologies, robotics, crop science, and agricultural engineering to develop robust, trustworthy, and farmer-centered decision-support systems. By critically evaluating technological innovations and implementation challenges, this review provides a framework for understanding the current state of AI in agriculture while identifying research priorities that will shape the next generation of sustainable and climate-resilient agricultural systems.

title: Nature based strategies for heat and drought resilience in fruit crops through genotype environment and management interactions
abstract: Climate change increasingly threatens fruit crop productivity by disrupting physiological, biochemical, and cellular processes that govern heat and drought tolerance. Yet efficacy of proposed interventions varies widely and is rarely explained by a unifying conceptual framework. Existing literature largely evaluates microbial inoculants, biostimulants, phytohormonal agents, and physical stress-mitigation strategies in isolation, obscuring their mechanistic overlap and the reasons for inconsistent field performance. This narrative review addresses that gap by synthesizing peer-reviewed literature within a genotype × environment × management (G×E×M) framework, examining plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria, arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi, synthetic microbial consortia, non-microbial biostimulants, phytohormonal priming agents, and antitranspirants alongside agroecological and crop-specific case studies. The synthesis indicates that these interventions converge on shared redox, hormonal, and osmotic regulatory networks, and that integrated, context-specific approaches consistently outperform single interventions in improving photosynthetic performance, water-use efficiency, and fruit yield and quality under stress. However, translation to commercial orchards remains constrained by microbiome instability, genotype-dependent responses, formulation and delivery limitations, and the absence of standardized multi-environment validation. Future progress requires predictive, systems-based research integrating multi-omics profiling, microbiome engineering, precision management, and improved delivery formulations to enable scalable, evidence-based climate-resilient fruit production. As a narrative rather than systematic review, this synthesis provides a conceptual foundation for guiding future predictive modelling and field validation.

title: Differential Cerebral Perfusion Patterns Across Migraine Phenotypes: An Exploratory ASL MRI Study.
abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES This study aims to characterize cerebral blood flow (CBF) alterations across migraine phenotypes and determine whether perfusion measures provide additional information for phenotype differentiation. MATERIALS AND METHODS The final cohort comprised 143 patients with migraine and 49 healthy controls who underwent three-dimensional pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (ASL) MRI. Voxel-wise analyses of normalized CBF (nCBF) were performed to identify phenotype-related perfusion alterations. Sensitivity analyses repeated the voxel-wise comparisons with phenotype-appropriate clinical covariates. Exploratory correlation analyses examined associations between regional perfusion and clinical characteristics. Logistic regression was further used to assess whether perfusion measures provided additional information for differentiating migraine with aura (MA) from migraine without aura (MO). RESULTS Compared with healthy controls, migraine patients with depressive symptoms showed reduced nCBF in a right hippocampus-parahippocampal cluster (Cluster 1) in the primary voxel-wise analysis; however, this finding did not survive additional adjustment for sleep quality. Lower Cluster 1 nCBF was associated with greater headache frequency. Compared with MO, patients with MA showed increased nCBF in a right cerebellar-occipitotemporal cluster peaking in the right cerebellar Crus I (Cluster 2), and this difference remained significant after additional adjustment for sleep quality, medication-overuse headache status, and preventive medication exposure. Within the MA group, higher Cluster 2 nCBF was associated with greater headache intensity. In exploratory logistic regression analysis, the combined clinical-imaging model showed a higher apparent area under the curve (AUC) than the clinical model alone. CONCLUSION Clinically relevant migraine phenotypes showed distinct patterns of regional cerebral perfusion. These findings highlight the importance of considering clinical heterogeneity in migraine neuroimaging and suggest that ASL-derived perfusion measures may provide complementary biological information for phenotype characterization, particularly with respect to aura status.

title: A natural neuronal receptor-derived MRI probe targets β-amyloid oligomers for the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Early-to-mid detection of Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains challenging because clinically used amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) probes primarily visualize fibrillar β-amyloid (Aβ) deposits and require radioactive isotopes. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers a radiation-free alternative, but its application in molecular AD diagnosis is limited by insufficient blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration and poor specificity toward early-to-mid Aβ species. Here, we developed a BBB-crossing liposomal MRI probe, Lipo@D1D2-Gd, by integrating a natural Aβ oligomer-binding receptor domain with a gadolinium chelator. The extracellular D1D2 domains of human leukocyte immunoglobulin-like receptor B2 (LilrB2), a neuronal receptor that recognizes neurotoxic Aβ oligomers, were recombinantly produced and bioorthogonally conjugated with a gadolinium chelator. The resulting D1D2-Gd retained its Aβ-binding capability and MRI contrast activity. To enable brain delivery, D1D2-Gd was encapsulated within maltose-functionalized PEGylated liposomes designed to facilitate BBB transport. After intravenous administration to 4-month-old 5xFAD mice, Lipo@D1D2-Gd crossed the BBB, accumulated in Aβ-rich brain regions, and generated MRI contrast enhancement that differentiated 5xFAD mice from wild-type controls. Systemic safety evaluation showed no obvious hematological, biochemical, or histological toxicity. This study establishes a receptor-derived, BBB-crossing biomaterial platform for radiation-free molecular imaging of early-to-mid AD-associated Aβ pathology. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: 1) Promising Targeting Strategy: We repurposed a human-derived natural receptor domain (LilrB2 D1D2) as a targeting module for β-amyloid (Aβ) oligomers, a key pathogenic species in Alzheimer's disease (AD). 2) Non-invasive MRI Approach: We constructed a liposomal probe designed to deliver the Gd-labeled targeting agent to the brain, enabling the detection of Aβ-associated pathology in 4-month-old 5xFAD mice via non-radioactive MRI, well before overt cognitive decline. 3) Experimental Validation: We demonstrate the probe's association with Aβ oligomers/plaques, effective BBB crossing, differences in MRI signals between AD model and wild-type mice, and an initially favorable biosafety profile, with no observed toxicity under the tested conditions. 4) Clinical Translation Potential: Our work presents a promising pathway toward a safe, accessible, and early-to-mid-stage AD screening tool, with the potential to facilitate population-wide screening and earlier therapeutic intervention.

title: Dermoscopy of intraepidermal keratinocytic neoplasms in solid organ transplant recipients: a single-center prospective real-world study supported by machine learning.
abstract: BACKGROUND Actinic keratoses (AKs) and Bowen disease (BD) are precursors of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) and are particularly relevant in solid organ transplant recipients (SOTRs) because of chronic immunosuppression. Early, accurate diagnosis is essential. Dermatoscopy is the most widely used and validated noninvasive diagnostic tool, although most studies have involved immunocompetent patients. OBJECTIVES To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of dermatoscopy in differentiating AK from BD in SOTRs, assess established dermoscopic criteria in this population, and compare the performance of expert observers, logistic regression, and machine learning models. METHODS We conducted a prospective observational study of 38 lesions clinically classified as AK or BD in SOTRs. Each lesion was assessed dermatoscopically by 3 blinded experts using 13 predefined criteria and subsequently biopsied for histopathological confirmation. Analyses included logistic regression, interobserver agreement, diagnostic performance, and evaluation of random forest models using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values. RESULTS We evaluated 38 lesions in 36 patients; 22 were histopathologically diagnosed as BD (58%) and 16 as AK (42%). Dermoscopic sensitivity and specificity for BD were 61% and 79%, respectively (positive predictive value, 81%; negative predictive value, 58%). For AK, sensitivity was 79% and specificity was 61%. Logistic regression identified the strawberry pattern, thick white-yellow scales, and glomerular vessels as significantly associated with BD. SHAP analysis supported these associations but also identified differences between human and model-based feature interpretation. CONCLUSIONS Established dermoscopic criteria may underestimate lesion severity in SOTRs, particularly for BD. Some features traditionally associated with AK, including the strawberry pattern and rosettes, were more indicative of BD in this cohort. Diagnostic algorithms require further validation in immunosuppressed populations, and explainable machine learning may provide complementary diagnostic insights.

Methylmercury accumulation patterns in Coix lacryma-jobi L. and its associated human exposure risks.
abstract: Mercury (Hg) pollution endangers the environment and human health. Coix (Coix lacryma-jobi L.), an important medicinal and edible crop, requires study of its Hg, particularly methylmercury (MeHg) accumulation characteristics and exposure risks. Paired coix plants and rhizosphere soils were collected from cultivation areas in Southwest China to assess inorganic Hg (IHg) and MeHg distribution and transfer in root, stem, leaf and grain. Combined with partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM), we quantified the effects of soil properties, bioavailable Hg fractions, and dissolved organic carbon on Hg transportation and accumulation in the soil-coix system. Across tissues, MeHg exhibited stronger bioconcentration than IHg. Approximately 55% of coix grain samples had MeHg bioconcentration factors (BCFs) exceeding 1 (mean = 3.44, comparable to MeHg-sensitive rice); coix grain accumulated MeHg, yet its MeHg concentration (0.281 ± 0.215 µg/kg) remained lower than rice from heavily Hg-contaminated sites. The positive correlations of MeHg concentrations between coix grain and leaf (p < 0.05), and particularly between leaf and rhizosphere soil (p < 0.001), suggest that rhizosphere soil is the primary source of MeHg accumulated in coix grain. In contrast, leaf IHg levels (61.3 ± 46.7 µg/kg) were significantly higher than those in stem and root tissues, and the IHg translocation factors (TFs) from root to aboveground tissues were low. Dietary coix intake was the primary Hg exposure pathway for residents. Although the non-carcinogenic hazard quotients for residents were below the safety threshold (HQ < 1), children faced greater IHg and MeHg health risks. This study is the first to clarify the differential accumulation mechanisms of IHg and MeHg in coix, and informs safe coix production, soil Hg monitoring, and dietary Hg risk management.

Combining value-at-risk and expected-shortfall forecasts via the model confidence set
abstract: To comply with increasingly stringent international standards in risk management and regulation, several approaches have been developed in the literature for forecasting tail-risk measures such as Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall (ES). However, the accuracy of these measures can be significantly affected by multiple sources of uncertainty, including model misspecification, data limitations and estimation procedures. To address these challenges and enhance the predictive performance of individual models, this study introduces novel forecast combination strategies based on the Model Confidence Set (MCS) methodology. Specifically, a strictly consistent joint VaR-ES loss function is employed to identify the best-performing models, which constitute the Set of Superior Models (SSM). Subsequently, the VaR and ES forecasts of the models included in the SSM are combined using various weighting schemes. An empirical analysis based on nine stock market indices at the 2.5\% and 1\% risk levels provides evidence that the proposed combined predictors are a robust alternative for forecasting tail-risk measures, successfully passing standard backtests and consistently entering the SSM of the MCS.

Liver-specific amino acid metabolism impacts on efficacy of cancer immunotherapy.
abstract: The combination immunotherapies, including those with atezolizumab and bevacizumab (Atez/Bev), have become standard therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, its efficacy remains limited and reliable biomarkers are lacking. In this study, we analyzed paired tumor and background liver tissues from Atez/Bev-treated HCC patients and found that high programmed cell death-1 (PD-1) expression in CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) correlated with therapeutic response independent of etiology. RNA sequencing on the tumor samples revealed that the branched-chain amino acid (BCAA)-related metabolic pathway was enriched in the group with high PD-1 expression in CD8⁺ TILs. Along with in vitro experiments, we identified the importance of BCAAs for activation and differentiation of CD8+ T cells. In addition, BCAA metabolism was related to response to PD-1 blockade in not subcutaneous but intrahepatic mouse model-specific manner. Actually, public dataset analyses revealed that high expression of BCAT1, a key enzyme in BCAA metabolism, was associated with poor prognosis in HCC, but not in other cancer types. These findings suggest the importance of liver-specific BCAA metabolism in antitumor immunity and highlight the need to assess the tumor microenvironment within its organ-specific metabolic context.

title: CXCL14+ fibroblasts promote development of IBD-associated fibrosis and cancer by interacting with SPP1+ macrophages via collagen IV secretion.
Recent advances in coarse-grained simulations of nucleic acid condensation.
abstract: Biomolecular condensates, formed through phase separation of multivalent biomolecules, play essential roles in cellular processes such as stress response, RNA processing, transcriptional control, and genome organization. Nucleic acids are increasingly recognized as important drivers and regulators of condensate formation and dynamics. This review examines recent advances in coarse-grained molecular simulations of dynamic nucleic acids and their phase transitions. We survey established computational frameworks validated against experimental data and discuss emerging applications that address increasingly complex systems. Existing studies reveal that base-mediated interactions emerge as dominant drivers in homotypic nucleic acid condensation and that simulation resolution fundamentally determines which physical phenomena are accessible and observable. We underscore that different modeling approaches at various resolutions provide complementary insights into nucleic acid condensation mechanisms and the driving forces. We emphasize the opportunities and challenges in extending these frameworks to capture the complexity of nucleic acid-mediated phase separation in biological contexts, while identifying important gaps in current modeling capabilities. Overall, molecular simulations at multiple scales have proven to be powerful tools for elucidating the mechanistic principles underlying nucleic acid condensates and their cellular functions.

title: Numerical estimation of the capture ability of Neptunian mean motion resonances II. Influence of eccentricity and inclination
abstract: Evaluating the ability of Neptunian mean-motion resonances (MMRs) to capture small bodies is an important step in reconstructing the evolutionary history of the early Solar System. Building on a previous planar model, this study extends the investigation of MMR capture during Neptune's migration to the three-dimensional case, systematically analyzing the effects of the small objects' eccentricity, e, and inclination, i. Through numerical simulations with different migration rates, we obtain the distribution of capture probabilities for 12 MMRs on the e-i plane. The results show that increasing i narrows the ``inevitable capture zone'' (strong MMRs and/or slow migration) and raises the lower e threshold for capture (weak MMRs and/or fast migration), while it may also expand the upper e limit for capture. When the resonance order reaches three, the e-i plane further differentiates into several regions, which are closely related to the types of resonant angles. The emerging i-dominated region, along with its inevitable capture zone, makes third-order MMRs the most likely to benefit from higher inclination, as well as the most likely to host mixed-type resonators. Finally, using a hypothetical planetesimal distribution, we calculated the capture probability and efficiency for each MMR, finding that a cold disk favors strong MMRs, whereas a hot disk reduces differences among MMRs and across migration rates. In the future, a better determination of the population associated with different MMRs and different types of objects will help us understand the dynamical excitation state of the primordial disk in the early Solar System.

title: Research on the multidimensional impact effects of the rural digital economy on the resilience of agricultural development: evidence from 30 provinces in China
Automatic Gravel Road Dust Monitoring Analysis Using Deep Learning Models and Small Uncrewed Aircraft Systems
abstract: Gravel, unsurfaced, or unpaved road networks account for 35% of the total roadways in the US, with some states such as Iowa having about 60% of their roadways unpaved, and regular monitoring is required to maintain and extend their service life. Among the major types of gravel road distress, dust clouds from passing traffic can cause significant environmental problems, impair visibility, and pose health risks to human respiratory systems. Popular technical manual for unsurfaced road maintenance management typically recommend assessment of dust-severity levels based on the severity of a dust cloud produced by a vehicle driving at 40 km / h ( 25 mi / h ). Because this method exposes assessors to unsafe conditions, its use is impractical for long road networks and high-dust severity conditions, so there is a need to explore automated and remote-sensing techniques for rating dust severity. Although previous studies have employed image-processing techniques to assess dust levels from images captured by vehicle-mounted cameras, dust accumulation on windshields and unstable camera attachments have reduced the reliability of such data collection. To address these limitations, this paper investigates the application of small uncrewed aircraft systems (sUAS) in rating dust clouds generated by traffic at various speeds. For this experiment, we collected dust data using sUAS from three gravel roads in Iowa and applied deep-learning models, specifically You Only Look Once version 8 large (YOLOv8l), to detect the truck driven for dust activation and residual network (ResNet) models to classify the level of dust severity in each sUAS video frame. The ResNet-152 classification model achieved the best result on the test data set with a weighted F1-score of 0.9867, highlighting a promising outcome for adoption of sUAS for dust monitoring.

title: Utilization of Copper Tailings in Structural Ceramsite: Processing Optimization, Mechanical Performance, and Sustainability Assessment
abstract: The accumulation of copper tailings (CTs) has become a serious environmental challenge, and their recycling into building materials offers a practical way to reduce waste and support sustainable construction. This study examines the preparation of ceramsite from copper tailings, fly ash, and bentonite. The work aims to produce aggregates with high strength suitable for concrete applications. A uniform experimental design was used to explore how raw material ratios, sintering temperature, and sintering time influence the properties of ceramsite, while data analysis and process optimization were supported by regression-based modeling and numerical optimization techniques. The optimized ceramsite exhibited high compressive strength and very low water absorption. It had a dense matrix, contributing to its strength and durability. Microstructural investigations using X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and energy-dispersive spectroscopy revealed the presence of quartz, feldspars, mullite, and corundum, with mullite and corundum playing a key role in improving strength. To evaluate practical performance, concrete specimens were prepared with varying volumetric replacement ratios of ceramsite and tested for their mechanical properties. Results demonstrated that replacing ordinary crushed stone with ceramsite significantly enhanced both compressive and flexural strength. The greatest improvements appeared at moderate replacement levels, and overall performance still surpassed conventional concrete even at higher ratios. In addition, carbon emission assessments confirmed that producing ceramsite from CTs generated substantially lower emissions compared with traditional aggregates, supporting its role as a green material. Overall, this work demonstrates a promising pathway for recycling industrial waste into high-quality construction materials, providing both environmental and engineering benefits.
journal: Journal of Materials in Civil Engineering

title: Multidimensional Urban–Rural Integration Based on Factor Flows and Its Effects on Landscape Patterns: A Case Study of Nanjing, China
abstract: Urban–rural integration (URI) refers to coordinated development between cities and rural areas. While existing research addresses URI quantification, effects, and optimization, gaps remain in quantifying URI from the perspective of factor flows, analyzing its distribution across urban–fringe–rural regions, and examining URI’s impact on landscape patterns. This study analyzed Nanjing, which is a typical metropolitan city of China, using a machine learning method to identify urban, fringe, and rural areas, quantifying URI from economic, social, and spatial dimensions, and applied a Random Forest regression model combined with Shapley additive explanations analysis to examine URI’s influence on landscapes. Findings include the following: (1) Nanjing’s urban, fringe, and rural areas occupied 18.3%, 29.0%, and 52.7% in 2022, respectively. (2) Urban area had the highest URI estimations of all dimensions. Fringe area held the medium values, with lower social and spatial integration. URI in rural areas was the weakest. (3) URI showed significant effects in fringe and rural areas. In fringe zones, ecological land division was positively correlated with spatial integration, while construction land patterns were influenced by multidimensional URI dynamics. In rural zones, construction land connectivity was shaped by the synergy of spatial and social integration and service facility distribution. (4) Based on these findings, a differentiated zoning strategy was proposed to guide region-specific integration and landscape optimization. This study provides a new perspective on understanding URI, offering both theoretical and practical implications for landscape optimization.
journal: Journal of Urban Planning and Development

title: Distribution and Properties of Defects in Sewer Systems: An Analysis of Auckland’s Sewer Network
abstract: Sewer systems are essential for public health and environmental protection; however, they deteriorate over time, potentially leading to significant impacts. Although numerous models have been developed to assess pipe condition, most rely on aggregated closed-circuit television (CCTV) scores and do not incorporate detailed defect-level analysis. Although defect-based approaches have shown strong potential, they often don’t account for defect properties, leaving a gap in the comprehensive analysis of individual defect types and their characteristics. This study addresses this gap by conducting a descriptive analysis of sewer defect types and their properties across different pipe materials. The analysis is applied to CCTV data from Auckland’s sewer network, covering five pipe materials: three rigid—asbestos cement (AC), concrete (CONC), and vitrified clay (VC)—and two flexible—polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and polyethylene (PE). The analysis includes an assessment of data set representativeness and a graphical evaluation of defect patterns. The results reveal clear material-dependent patterns. Rigid pipes exhibit higher defect densities and are mainly affected by Joint Faulty and Root Intrusion defects, likely related to their short, segmented construction. In flexible pipes, PVC is also strongly affected by Joint Faulty, whereas PE is predominantly affected by Dipped Pipe. Defect property analysis further highlights distinct patterns. Cracks tend to be larger in PVC pipes, whereas Surface Damage is more pronounced in rigid pipes. Spatial analysis shows that Joint Faulty defects mainly occur at pipe ends, whereas Debris Grease and Surface Damage are typically observed near the pipe inlet and often extend along the pipe length. Circumferential analysis showed that mechanically induced defects (e.g., Joint Faulty and cracks) tend to occur near the pipe top, whereas Obstructions and Surface Damage concentrate at the pipe bottom. These findings provide new insights into sewer deterioration processes, support more informed decision-making, and offer a transferable methodology for application to other drainage systems.
journal: Journal of Water Resources Planning and Management

title: Estimating the threat of AI-agent responding across online survey platforms.
abstract: Recent research and advances in LLMs have led to widespread concern that AI agents could pose as human online survey-takers. However, it remains unclear how prevalent AI agents are on survey research platforms and how to effectively detect AI agents. We validated a series of AI detection tests that effectively separated verified-human participants from both prompted commercial and purpose-built AI agents. Using these tests, we collected surveys on seven online platforms and find wide variation in rates of respondents failing AI tests, ranging from 6 to 41% across platforms (compared to a 2.4% false-positive rate for in-person human participants). We further demonstrate that undetected AI agents can impact the results of online surveys. Our findings suggest that while there is an urgent need for AI detection tests and consistent, systematic monitoring of data quality on online platforms, some platforms currently appear to provide data with a low rate of AI agents.

title: From Pest Control to Health Protection: A Health-Based Hierarchy of Control for Sustainable Agriculture.
abstract: The widespread reliance on synthetic pesticides remains a defining feature of modern agriculture, particularly in tropical and export-oriented farming systems. While these chemicals have contributed to yield stability and pest suppression, their long-term consequences for farmer health, environmental integrity, and food system sustainability remain insufficiently integrated within existing agricultural decision frameworks. In Malaysia and similar middle-income agricultural economies, synthetic pesticide adoption rooted in colonial-era agrochemical trials and intensified through the expansion of herbicides such as glyphosate, has fostered structurally chemical-dependent farming practices. These practices disproportionately transfer occupational and environmental health risks to farmers and rural communities. Current approaches to pesticide management, including Integrated Pest Management (IPM) and regulatory risk assessment, provide important but fragmented solutions. IPM primarily prioritizes pest control and crop protection outcomes, while regulatory frameworks focus on product-level hazard and safety thresholds that may not fully capture cumulative, route-specific exposures in real-world farming conditions. Consequently, no unified framework explicitly positions human health protection as the central organizing principle of pesticide decision-making. This paper proposes a Health-based Hierarchy of Control for Sustainable Agriculture, adapted from occupational safety and health principles and informed by environmental health and chemical risk assessment logic. The framework prioritizes system-level ecological design and non-chemical controls, positioning chemical intervention as a least-preferred, last resort option. By reframing pesticide use through hazard elimination and exposure prevention, the model offers a structured decision logic for agricultural health, policy development, and future empirical validation.
