title: A Symmetry-Matching Approach to Blind-Spot Reduction in Sparse Autoencoders
abstract: Language models can treat semantically distinct inputs as interchangeable at the representation level, creating blind spots that standard sparse autoencoder (SAE) objectives do not target. In safety-critical settings such as clinical dosage extraction, legal clause interpretation, or financial amount verification, such failures can propagate silently into downstream decisions. We study this problem as one of feature-basis orientation. Building on a symmetry-matching view from algebraic error-detection theory, we add a differentiable $V_{\mathrm{Gini}}$ regularisation term to SAE training that penalises uneven perturbation response within a specified family. Across GPT-2, Gemma 2, and Qwen 2.5, a frozen multi-seed evaluation shows that $V$-regularisation raises both relative and absolute lower-tail responses while reducing response-profile imbalance, with no material general-text reconstruction degradation. JumpReLU and minimum description length (MDL) objectives remain close to the Standard SAE profile under the same protocol. Family-geometry controls show that the effect is not explained by template duplication or a single dominant perturbation family, and held-out probes plus null-calibrated separation tests evaluate how far the representation-level change carries to downstream discriminability. A zero-shot audit on out-of-distribution clinical radiology minimal pairs finds the relative weak-tail lift in all evaluated model-by-family cells, not perfectly rank-aligned with the trained statistic, and a held-out family audit finds it on family kinds never used in training. Together, the results show that perturbation-aware SAE training can reorient feature bases toward safety-relevant input changes while leaving downstream validation as a separate empirical step.

title: MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring
abstract: The adoption of Large Language Models for radiology report structuring has been largely dominated by either proprietary cloud-based models or large open models requiring high-end GPUs for deployment, which is a critical bottleneck for clinical adoption in radiology workflows that demand data privacy and offline operation. To address this, we present MedPAO-Assist, an edge-deployable agentic framework that generates structured radiology reports directly from radiologist dictation and voice commands, requiring only $\approx3.3$ GB peak RAM and achieving an average end-to-end latency of $\approx31$ seconds on a standard laptop CPU through an asynchronous, multi-threaded execution pipeline. The system currently supports four major imaging modalities -- Chest X-ray, Chest CT, Abdomen CT, and Brain MRI. To our knowledge, it is among the earliest agentic systems to run its entire pipeline with a Small Language Model (SLM) in the 0.6B-parameter range. This multi-agent architecture, built around an Extract-Ground-Generate paradigm, performs concept extraction, SNOMED-CT grounding, and structured report generation, followed by a speech-driven human-in-the-loop correction phase, together forming a fully "no-touch" reporting workflow that requires no keyboard input, external API calls, or internet connectivity. We evaluate each pipeline stage individually -- concept extraction, ontology grounding, and concept categorization and report hardware profiling results demonstrating the system's feasibility for real-time, CPU-only clinical deployment.

title: GTSM: Gaussian Splatting with Thermal State-Space Dynamics for Spatio-Temporal Thermal Field Reconstruction and Prediction
abstract: Temperature-field reconstruction and prediction are important for condition monitoring, process analysis, and state assessment in industrial and dynamic environments. This work aims to recover a four-dimensional spatio-temporal thermal state field directly from two-dimensional observations, without requiring a predefined 3D model, prescribed thermodynamic equation, or predefined heating/cooling trajectory. To this end, we propose the Gaussian Thermal State-Space Model (GTSM), which represents thermal evolution through a shared scene-level latent process and Gaussian-specific local thermal states. The resulting continuous dynamics are propagated using differentiable RK2 integration, allowing thermal evolution to be inferred from multi-view and multi-temporal observations and continuously extrapolated beyond the observed interval. GTSM is designed as a backbone-agnostic thermal dynamics module for Gaussian representations and can be integrated with both static 3D Gaussian Splatting and dynamic 4D Gaussian Splatting, supporting thermal reconstruction and prediction under both static and time-varying target geometry. The reconstructed representation further enables novel-view thermal rendering and future-time thermal-state prediction. Experiments on real infrared sequences and synthetic dynamic thermal data demonstrate improved reconstruction accuracy and substantially stronger temporal extrapolation than representative baselines, while also validating the applicability of GTSM to deforming targets.

title: Matrix-Free Resolvent Analysis for Large-Scale Aerodynamic Systems
abstract: At industrial scale the cost of resolvent analysis is set by the linear solves and the assembly and storage of the Jacobian. We present a matrix-free resolvent framework in the Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes solver ADflow: automatic differentiation supplies the action of the shifted Jacobian and its Hermitian transpose, preconditioned Krylov solves recycle subspaces across a Lanczos bidiagonalization, and every gain is certified by a backward error. It is applied to the NASA Common Research Model wing at Mach 0.85 and 4.2 degrees on three grid levels of 0.45, 3.6 and 28.8 million cells, the finest with 1.73x10^8 complex unknowns, 2.3 times the largest reported resolvent computation. On the coarsest level an unstable buffet mode makes the gain peak a resonance; on the finer two the operator is stable and the peak, 1.33x10^4 at omega = 6.4 and 3.0x10^3 near omega = 7.7, is a pseudo-resonance of damped modes whose buffet cells travel outboard at about 0.3 times the free-stream speed. Refinement turns an oscillator into an amplifier of the same mechanism, as forced simulations confirm. A certified frequency costs 3.6 minutes on 128 cores at 2.7 million unknowns, with 14 to 34 kB per unknown, nearly four orders of magnitude below a sparse factorization.

title: How Intervention History Changes AI Agent Sabotage on Subsequent Tasks
abstract: AI control evaluations often reset agents' memory between tasks, although deployed agents may retain records of prior interventions. We ask whether learning that an earlier attack was caught changes an agent's ability to evade defer-to-trusted (DtT), a protocol that replaces suspicious work with a trusted model's solution. Herein, we study cross-episode adaptation: whether intervention history changes attack behavior on a subsequent task with different objectives and a fresh environment. We evaluate this using ControlArena's Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) and SHADE-Arena as testbeds, where agents must complete a main task while covertly pursuing a harmful side objective. For each successor task, we pair a history-conditioned attempt with the model's no-history attempt. The retained history either states that the previous submission was replaced or additionally includes the trusted model's replacement. For Claude Opus 4.8 on IaC, intervention history reduces successful sabotage. Completion of both the main and side objectives falls from 77% to 12% when the agent is told about the replacement and to 38% when it is also shown the trusted model's replacement, while main task success remains essentially unchanged. Condensing the history weakens this effect, suggesting that the retained context matters and limiting attribution to intervention feedback alone. GPT-5.4 shows no significant change in successful sabotage on the same IaC benchmark. On SHADE-Arena, GPT-5's successful sabotage rate decreases, but the reduction is not significant. Across the tested models, history conditions, and deferral thresholds, intervention history never increases the rate of successful sabotage that survives DtT. These results show that intervention history can change subsequent attack behavior, but its effect depends on both the model and the retained context.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Lightweight and Heavyweight Convolutional Neural Network Architectures for Apple Leaf Disease Classification
abstract: Leaf diseases can significantly reduce both the productivity and quality of crops; therefore, early and accurate diagnosis is required for sustainable farming. Reliance on visual examination by experts is time-consuming and expensive and may result in inconsistent or inaccurate diagnoses. The present study investigated a deep learning approach based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for the automatic classification of apple leaves into three classes, namely, Alternaria blotch, Marssonina blotch and healthy leaves. A field dataset of 9,000 images was acquired with a mobile phone in orchards of Himachal Pradesh under natural lighting, from different shooting angles, and with natural backgrounds. Ten pre-trained CNN models, five lightweight and five heavyweights were evaluated and compared using transfer learning, and each model was trained three times with different random seeds to check the statistical reliability of the results. EfficientNetV2B0 and DenseNet201 were identified as the best lightweight and heavyweight models, achieving mean accuracies of 94.30% and 92.96%, respectively. Both models were subsequently fine-tuned using hyperparameters selected through Bayesian optimization, which raised their accuracies to 98.07% and 96.00%, respectively. The fine-tuned EfficientNetV2B0 performed significantly better than the fine-tuned DenseNet201 while using about one-third of the parameters, and running nearly five times faster on a CPU. A well-optimized lightweight network can, therefore, outperform a much larger one and remain practical for mobile and Internet of Things (IoT) use. This study offers a practical and efficient approach with strong potential for adaptation to other crops, and integration into mobile and IoT-based disease diagnosis systems.

title: Problematic Financing Handling Strategy at KSPPS BMT Al Roudloh Todanan Branch
abstract: Non-performing financing (NPF) is a major challenge for KSPPS BMT Al Roudloh Todanan Branch because it may affect liquidity, asset quality, and operational sustainability. The problem is particularly relevant in a member base dominated by farmers whose repayment capacity is influenced by harvest seasons, weather conditions, production yields, and commodity prices. This study aims to analyze the identification process, causal factors, and handling strategies for problematic financing at KSPPS BMT Al Roudloh Todanan Branch. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach during [observation period], involving [number] informants selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through interviews, observations, and documentation and analyzed using the Miles and Huberman model, consisting of data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. Data validity was assessed through source triangulation. The findings indicate that the NPF ratio reached a peak of 4.46% in September 2024. The main causes of problematic financing comprised internal institutional factors, including suboptimal surveys, limited monitoring, and delays in collection; member-related factors, including irregular use of financing funds and communication difficulties; and external factors, particularly crop failures and member migration. Financing handling involved pre-screening, field surveys, installment monitoring, member visits, deliberation, and the implementation of rescheduling, reconditioning, and restructuring (3R). This study contributes a contextual understanding of how institutional, member-related, and agricultural factors interact in problematic financing within a sharia cooperative serving predominantly farming communities. The findings provide a basis for strengthening financing identification, monitoring, and handling practices while maintaining alignment with sharia principles, without assuming the effectiveness of the strategies in the absence of empirical effectiveness testing.
journal: Jurnal Ekonomi, Manajemen, Bisnis dan Akuntansi Review

title: Assessment of the Relative Efficiency of Bootstrap Resampling Methods for Forecast Uncertainty Quantification in Nigerian Macroeconomic Time Series: Evidence from Inflation and Exchange Rate Data (1960-2025)
abstract: Quantifying forecast uncertainty is a prerequisite for responsible use of time series models in Nigerian macroeconomic analysis, yet researchers rarely benchmark resampling schemes used to estimate that uncertainty against alternatives on long-run Nigerian data. This study compares three bootstrap procedures for response time series the stationary bootstrap, the moving block bootstrap, and the sieve bootstrap across five ARIMA data-generating processes of increasing complexity: ARIMA(1,0,0), ARIMA(1,1,0), ARIMA(1,1,1), ARIMA(2,1,1), and ARIMA(1,1,3). The simulation design follows a Monte Carlo framework comparable to earlier benchmarking studies. The same three methods are then applied to two real Nigerian macroeconomic series: annual headline inflation (World Bank/FRED, 1960-2025, 66 observations) and the log of the annual NGN/USD exchange rate (Penn World Table/FRED, 1960-2023, 64 observations), both considerably longer than the short annual series used in prior comparative work of this kind. Across all five simulated data-generating processes and both empirical series, the stationary bootstrap yielded the lowest mean squared error (MSE) of one-step-ahead forecasts; the moving block bootstrap was a close second throughout; the sieve bootstrap was markedly less accurate, particularly for integrated I(1) processes. These results diverge from prior work suggesting block-based methods are dominated by ARMA processes with genuine moving-average components, and from work favouring the sieve bootstrap for autoregressive-dominated series. Possible explanations are discussed, including the sensitivity of the sieve reconstruction step to compounding during re-integration of a differenced series. The scope limitations of a reduced-scale Monte Carlo design are noted, and further replication is identified as necessary before firm practical guidance can be issued to Nigerian forecasting practitioners.
journal: American Journal of Applied Statistics and Economics

title: CAKRAWALA NUSANTARA (Creating Shared Value: Nurturing and Reliable Agriculture)
abstract: Large-scale corn production in Tuban Regency generates substantial corn-cob residue that remains underutilized. Limited technical capacity, weak community institutions, and restricted market access have prevented local communities from converting this residue into value-added products. This study examines how the Cakrawala Nusantara Energy Cooperative has been strengthened as both a social organization and an economic institution to manage corn-cob biomass, build a multi-stakeholder value chain, and promote sustainable social inclusion. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed, using participatory observation, in-depth interviews, document analysis, and literature review. The findings show that the cooperative consolidated capacities previously developed within community groups into more structured technical, managerial, and institutional capabilities. It also connected farmers, operational workers, companies, universities, and corporate off-takers within an integrated biomass value chain. The novelty of this study lies in combining the cooperative’s social and economic functions with the diversified use of corn residue for energy biomass and livestock silage. This model creates economic opportunities, strengthens community bargaining power, expands participation among vulnerable groups, and lays a foundation for inclusive, locally managed, and sustainable economic development.

title: Analisis Uqubah terhadap Anak di bawah Umur dalam Perspektif Hukum Pidana Islam dan UU Nomor 11 Tahun 2012
abstract: The criminal liability of minors presents a fundamental challenge in determining the appropriate balance between accountability, child protection, and rehabilitation. This study analyzes the concept of uqubah against minors from the perspective of Islamic criminal law and Law Number 11 of 2012 concerning the Juvenile Criminal Justice System in Indonesia, with particular emphasis on the differences and points of convergence between the two legal frameworks. This research employs normative legal research using statutory, conceptual, and comparative approaches. Primary legal materials consist of the Qur’an, hadith, Islamic criminal law doctrines, and Indonesian legislation, particularly Law Number 11 of 2012. The findings demonstrate that Islamic criminal law does not establish children’s criminal liability solely on the basis of the prohibited act, but also considers legal capacity (taklif), baligh, tamyiz, understanding, intention, and choice. The principle of raf’ al-qalam establishes that children who have not reached puberty are not subject to criminal liability in the same manner as adults, although educational and corrective measures may be imposed within the framework of ta’zir and public benefit (maslahah). Indonesian law similarly adopts a differentiated system through restorative justice, diversion, individualized consideration, and the principle that imprisonment constitutes a last resort, as reflected in Articles 2, 5–7, 69–71, and 81 of Law Number 11 of 2012. The study concludes that the two systems share principles of proportionality, rehabilitation, education, and protection, although they differ in determining legal capacity. An integrative model based on capacity, proportionality, rehabilitation, restorative justice, and maqashid al-shariah can strengthen Indonesia’s juvenile criminal justice framework without compromising legality and legal certainty.

title: Penguatan Pemasaran Digital Produk Terasi melalui Kolaborasi Karang Taruna dan Kelompok Perempuan Pesisir di Dusun Pilangsari, Kabupaten Kendal
abstract: The Coastal Women's Group in Pilangsari Hamlet, Kendal Regency, processes shrimp catch into shrimp paste (terasi), but market reach remains constrained by minimal digital marketing and the lack of structured collaboration with Karang Taruna (youth organization) as a marketing partner. This community service activity aimed to enhance Karang Taruna's digital marketing skills and establish collaborative business management between both groups. Using an Asset-Based Community Development approach with participatory principles, the program comprised four stages: needs analysis, two training sessions, implementation mentoring, and evaluation, with data collected via observation, interviews, and documentation. Results revealed qualitative improvements in participants' capabilities, marked by an active social media account and online store managed by Karang Taruna, along with a village decree formalizing the partnership, although a written profit-sharing agreement is still being finalized. These findings highlight that technical-administrative adaptations advance faster than socio-economic agreements, offering an adaptable cross-group collaborative model for coastal community empowerment.

title: Global Tea Production: Current Status, Emerging Challenges, Technological Transformation, and Future Perspectives
abstract: Tea (Camellia sinensis (L.) Kuntze) is a globally important perennial beverage crop supporting agricultural economies, rural livelihoods, international trade and cultural systems. Global made-tea production reached approximately 7.074 million tonnes in 2024 and approximately 7.266 million tonnes in 2025. The sector is undergoing structural change as climate variability, water constraints, labour costs, soil degradation, market volatility and requirements for traceability and environmental performance increasingly interact with conventional production challenges. This review synthesizes recent evidence on global production, climate impacts, genetic resources, precision agriculture, artificial intelligence, intelligent processing, sustainability, circular economy and value-added development. Recent evidence shows a transition from productivity-centred production toward integrated systems combining genotype, environment, management and digital technologies. Climate change affects tea through temperature stress, altered rainfall, drought and extreme events, with consequences for yield and biochemical quality. Advances in remote sensing, unmanned aerial vehicles, Internet of Things sensors, machine learning, computer vision, spectroscopy and robotics provide opportunities for real-time monitoring and precision management, although cost, data standardization, model transferability and smallholder access remain major constraints. Future tea production should integrate climate-resilient cultivars, precision resource management, intelligent processing, digital traceability and circular use of biomass. A Tea Production 2050 framework is proposed to connect genetic conservation, climate adaptation, smart production, artificial intelligence, processing, traceability and value creation. The review identifies priorities for research and technology deployment aimed at improving productivity, quality, resilience and sustainability across diverse tea-growing systems.
journal: International Journal of Advanced Multidisciplinary Research and Studies

title: Beyond Guardrails: Runtime Enforcement for Secure AI Agents-A Systematic Review of Action Control, Isolation, and Policy Enforcement
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents turn model-generated decisions into tool calls, API requests, code execution, data access, and transactions. When agent reasoning is manipulated or simply wrong, model-centric guardrails cannot by themselves stop the resulting action. We systematically reviewed runtime-enforcement mechanisms for autonomous and tool-using AI agents in literature published or publicly available from January 2023 to September 2026. Searches of Compendex and the Web of Science Core Collection, followed by deduplication, multi-stage screening, source-grounded eligibility assessment, and targeted snowballing, yielded 58 primary studies, which we coded by enforcement placement, security mechanism, and assurance type. Most studies enforce security at the tool/action boundary (33/58, 56.9%) or inside the agent runtime or harness (18/58, 31.0%), whereas only 7/58 (12.1%) work primarily at the OS/process/execution boundary. Authorization and privilege control (41/58, 70.7%) and action validation (34/58, 58.6%) are the most common mechanism families. Across very different mechanisms and assurance models, a common design emerges: the model proposes an action, and a separate enforcement point decides whether that action may take external effect. Durable authorization, multi-agent delegation, cross-layer enforcement, recovery from partially committed effects, and standardized evaluation remain open problems. These findings suggest that secure agent architectures should separate reasoning from execution authority and place consequential actions behind independently enforceable runtime boundaries.
journal: Journal of Reliable and Secure Computing

title: Teacher’s Strategies For Integrating 21 st Century Competencies Into Elementary School Instruction At Muhammadiyah 01 Elementary School In Tanggul Jember
abstract: This study aims to analyze teachers’ strategies for integrating 21st-century competencies, the forms of their application in learning activities, and the relationship between planning, implementation, and assessment at SD Muhammadiyah 01 Tanggul Jember. The study employed a qualitative approach using a case study design. Data were collected through observation, in-depth interviews, documentation, and a review of instructional materials, and were then analyzed using an interactive analysis model that included data condensation, data presentation, and the drawing and verification of conclusions. The findings indicate that the integration of 21st-century competencies is realized through information analysis, discussions, group work, product creation, presentations, and reflection. Javanese language learning materials and co-curricular activities demonstrate the interconnection between fostering creativity, communication, collaboration, the use of technology, and process- and product-based assessment. The main findings of this study confirm that the integration of 21st-century competencies cannot be achieved merely by including indicators in learning materials; rather, it requires coherence among learning objectives, task design, collaborative activities, the production of works, the communication of results, and assessment.

title: Scene-Adaptive Token Budgeting for Urban Traffic Perception
abstract: Urban traffic perception systems must process complex visual scenes under changing weather, illumination, density, and object scale. Transformer-based perception models provide strong contextual modeling, but their computational cost limits real-time deployment on vehicle-grade hardware. This study explores scene-adaptive token budgeting for efficient urban traffic perception. We develop the Scene Token Budgeting Transformer (STBT), which estimates the required token budget from scene complexity indicators, including object density, lane-boundary uncertainty, foreground motion, and low-light degradation. Simple road scenes are processed with a reduced token budget, while crowded intersections, nighttime frames, and scenes with small vulnerable road users retain more visual tokens. The evaluation was organized around driving conditions rather than only dataset averages. Experiments used Cityscapes, BDD100K, and nuScenes camera data, with 196,000 annotated frames, 1.84 million object boxes, and 25 semantic road categories. In clear daytime road scenes, STBT reduced token computation by 46.2% with only a 0.3-point decrease in detection mAP. In rainy-night scenes, the model automatically retained 71.5% of foreground-related tokens and limited mAP loss to 1.1 points. On an NVIDIA Orin automotive platform, end-to-end perception latency decreased from 62.8 ms to 41.6 ms per frame. Pedestrian and cyclist recall at distances above 35 meters improved by 3.4 points compared with a fixed-ratio pruning strategy, mainly because the token budget was preserved for small foreground objects. The results indicate that scene-level token budgeting can support real-time traffic perception while maintaining safety-sensitive detection performance.
journal: The Journal of Applied Engineering and Technologies

title: Sparse Patch Routing for Efficient Remote Sensing Scene Segmentation
abstract: High-resolution remote sensing images contain large homogeneous regions such as water, farmland, roofs, roads, and vegetation. Processing all image patches with the same computational depth increases the cost of transformer segmentation models and may provide limited benefit for visually simple regions. This study investigates sparse patch routing for efficient remote sensing scene segmentation. We propose the Sparse Patch Routing Transformer (SPRT), which separates image patches into three computational routes: a shallow route for low-texture background regions, a standard route for common land-cover areas, and a detailed route for boundary-sensitive regions such as road edges, building contours, and small objects. Patch routing is determined by a lightweight saliency estimator using local texture variance, class-token response, and boundary uncertainty. Unlike direct token deletion, SPRT preserves the spatial grid and assigns different processing depths to different patch groups. The model was evaluated on LoveDA, ISPRS Vaihingen, and WHU Building datasets, covering 7,426 high-resolution images, 38 urban and rural scenes, and more than 12.8 billion labeled pixels. On LoveDA, SPRT achieved 53.7% mIoU, compared with 54.2% for the full SegFormer-B2 baseline, while reducing FLOPs by 34.6%. On WHU Building, boundary F1-score decreased by only 0.4 percentage points after patch routing, showing that small structural details were largely preserved. Runtime testing on 2048 × 2048 image tiles showed that inference time decreased from 186 ms to 119 ms on an RTX 4090 and from 742 ms to 486 ms on Jetson Orin. Stratified analysis further showed that farmland and water regions used the shallow route in over 71% of patches, while building-edge regions were routed to detailed computation in 64% of boundary patches. These results suggest that patch-level routing can reduce transformer segmentation cost while maintaining reliable spatial accuracy in remote sensing applications
journal: The Journal of Applied Engineering and Technologies

title: Sustainable Agriculture and Food Security
abstract: Agriculture and food security are central to sustainable development in Bangladesh and South Asia, where millions of smallholder farmers depend on agriculture for their livelihoods and where food systems face increasing pressures from climate change, natural resource degradation, population growth, market volatility, and changing dietary needs. Ensuring long-term food and nutrition security requires a transition towards agricultural systems that are productive, resource-efficient, climate-resilient, inclusive, and environmentally sustainable. Sustainable Agriculture and Food Security examines the interconnected dimensions of sustainable agriculture and resilient food systems, with particular emphasis on Bangladesh and relevant experiences across South Asia. The book explores climate-smart agriculture, agroecological approaches, soil health, sustainable water management, efficient irrigation, biodiversity conservation, circular agriculture, and environmentally responsible farming practices. It also investigates the potential of precision agriculture, digital technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and the Internet of Things (IoT) to improve agricultural productivity, resource-use efficiency, and climate adaptation. Particular attention is given to the opportunities and challenges associated with adopting these innovations among smallholder farmers, women, and young people. Beyond farm-level production, the book examines agricultural finance, agribusiness development, market access, value-chain integration, sustainable food supply chains, and the policy and institutional frameworks needed to strengthen food security. Drawing on empirical research, regional experiences, case studies, and policy-oriented analysis, it highlights practical pathways for improving agricultural livelihoods, reducing environmental pressures, and building more inclusive and resilient food systems. The book aims to serve as a useful resource for researchers, students, development practitioners, agricultural professionals, and policymakers working towards sustainable agriculture and food security in Bangladesh and South Asia.

title: FORMATIV BAHOLASH SHAROITIDA OʻQUVCHILARDA CHOLGʻU ASBOBLARINI CHALISHGA OID KREATIV QOBILIYATLARINI RIVOJLANTIRISH MAZMUNI VA TASHKILIY-FUNKSIONAL MODELI
abstract: The article addresses the development of students' creative abilities in playing musical instruments under formative assessment. It argues that judging instrumental performance only by the final result fails to reveal students' exploration, learning from errors and independent musical decisions. The study defines the content of creative-ability development: criteria of creative performance, diagnostic materials, differentiated creative tasks and a feedback mechanism. The novelty lies in an organizational-functional model that integrates the formative assessment cycle (diagnosis – formative feedback – reflection – planning the next performance) with the content of instrumental performance. The model combines a developmental environment, the project method and individual feedback into a single pedagogical technology and moves students from external grading towards conscious self-regulation of their performance. A rubric for assessing creative performance is also proposed. The model is recommended for music lessons and instrumental club activities.
journal: Ta'limda Istiqbolli Izlanishlar xalqaro ilmiy metodik jurnal

title: Classification of Cayenne Pepper Leaf Nutritional Deficiencies Using Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Cayenne pepper (Capsicum frutescens L.) is one of the horticultural commodities with high economic value in Indonesia. Pest attacks and nutrient deficiencies can reduce crop quality and yield. Identification of these conditions is commonly conducted through visual observation, which can be subjective and time-consuming. This study aims to classify nutrient deficiency conditions in cayenne pepper leaves using the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) method. The dataset consisted of primary data collected directly from the field and secondary data obtained from the Chili Plant Leaf Disease and Growth Stage Dataset from Bangladesh. The research stages included image preprocessing, data augmentation, CNN model training, and model evaluation. The CNN model was developed using three convolutional layers to classify cayenne pepper leaves into healthy and nutrient deficiency classes. The experimental results showed that the proposed model achieved high classification performance, with an accuracy of 98% on the primary dataset and 97% on the secondary dataset. These results indicate that the CNN method can effectively classify nutrient deficiency conditions in cayenne pepper leaves and maintain consistent performance across datasets.
journal: International Journal of Applied Artificial Intelligence and Robotics

title: From Operational Disruption to Intelligent Service Operations: A Practitioner Journey with Autonomous AI Agents
abstract: The COVID-19 disruption and subsequent talent mobility exposed important vulnerabilities in traditional service operations. Organizations relying heavily on individual expertise faced risks to operational continuity when experienced professionals moved roles or left. Although knowledge transfer, standard operating procedures, and documentation remain essential, they do not always capture the contextual knowledge developed through years of resolving incidents. The resulting gaps can affect service quality, turnaround time, operating costs, and user experience. This chapter examines how human-AI collaboration can strengthen operational resilience and knowledge continuity in service operations. It draws on the practitioner journey behind IgnitronX.AI, a cloud-native multi-agent platform developed to address enterprise operational challenges using generative AI and agentic AI. Its architecture supports service teams by surfacing similar historical incidents, recommending potential resolutions, enabling knowledge discovery, summarizing operational records, and providing sentiment insights. The objective is not to replace human expertise but to augment it. The implementation journey demonstrated that technology alone cannot deliver sustainable value. Data quality emerged as a critical constraint, alongside security, confidentiality, framework and model selection, operating-cost management, governance, and stakeholder adoption. The experience also reinforced that organizations should first understand the business problem, simplify processes, remove waste, and make deliberate build-versus-buy decisions. Through this reflective practitioner case, the chapter offers leaders practical insights into intelligent operations that preserve organizational knowledge, strengthen service continuity, and create the potential for improved productivity, operational efficiency, and user experience through responsible human-AI collaboration.

title: Integrating Agrometeorology, Agronomy and Artificial Intelligence for Climate-Resilient Sustainable Food Production: A Critical Narrative Review
abstract: Climate-resilient food production requires decisions that are meteorologically informed, agronomically plausible and adaptive to rapidly changing conditions. Agrometeorology provides observations and forecasts of weather and climate risk; agronomy translates those risks into crop, soil and management responses; and artificial intelligence can fuse high-volume, heterogeneous data, learn complex relationships and accelerate prediction. These domains are increasingly connected, yet their evidence bases remain partly fragmented. This critical narrative review evaluates how their integration can support sustainable crop production, with particular attention to the chain from environmental observation and prediction to management action and measurable resilience outcomes. Literature published from 1 January 2000 to 8 August 2026 was examined through relevant agricultural, multidisciplinary and biomedical scholarly sources, with supplementary citation searching and verification of bibliographic metadata. The synthesis shows that the strongest case for integration is not a replacement of process knowledge by data-driven prediction, but a division of labour: meteorological models define time-varying hazard, agronomic models constrain biological plausibility and management options, and artificial intelligence improves data fusion, bias correction, pattern recognition and computational efficiency. Evidence is comparatively mature for remote sensing, yield prediction and process-based crop modelling, and is rapidly advancing for machine-learned weather prediction. By contrast, end-to-end demonstrations that connect forecast skill to farm decisions, yield stability, resource-use efficiency, profitability and environmental outcomes remain limited. Hybrid crop-model and machine-learning approaches are promising, but uncertainty calibration, domain shift, sparse ground truth, interoperability, digital inequality and data governance remain substantial constraints. Digital twins offer a useful integration architecture, although agricultural implementations are still less mature than the concept implies. Future research should prioritise multi-environment prospective validation, decision-centred forecast verification, causal evaluation of management recommendations, uncertainty-aware hybrid modelling and equitable deployment. The most defensible conclusion is that integration can improve climate resilience only when predictive accuracy is coupled to agronomic actionability, transparent uncertainty and outcome-based evaluation.

title: Algorithmic Provenance: When and Why Consumers Discount Products Made With AI ‐Involved Processes
abstract: Firms increasingly incorporate generative and non‐generative artificial intelligence (AI) into product design, formulation, and production, and they face a disclosure question: how should they describe the role of AI to consumers? Across six studies, including analysis of 1800 marketplace listings and five pre‐registered experiments (total experimental N = 2760), we introduce and test a 2‐by‐2 framework of algorithmic provenance defined by the AI's role (agentic vs. assistive) and its visibility in the final product (visible vs. invisible). Identical products are evaluated differently depending on where they fall in this taxonomy. Agentic AI involvement (AI as designer) reduces consumer product attitudes, perceived quality, purchase intentions, and willingness to pay relative to assistive AI involvement (AI as a tool for a human designer). The effect is amplified when AI involvement is visible in the final product. The downstream responses are partially mediated by a new construct, perceived authenticity of creative intention, which captures consumers' inference about whether a human creator pursued a genuine creative vision. The effect is larger for expressive than for functional product domains and larger among consumers primed to hold an independent self‐construal. A scalable managerial intervention, creative‐intent framing, narrows the agentic penalty by approximately half, again through the authenticity mechanism. The findings identify a substantively important new construct for AI disclosure research, refine theories of algorithmic aversion, and offer marketers an actionable disclosure design principle.

title: Modelling Drainage‐Induced Transitions in Irish Peatlands: A Process‐Based Approach to Ecosystem Stability
abstract: Peatlands are globally significant ecosystems, valued for their role in carbon sequestration, water regulation and biodiversity support. However, historical drainage and emerging climate pressures are threatening their long‐term resilience. Resilience here refers to the ability to retain a saturated, peat‐forming state. Drainage can push peatlands beyond tipping points into alternative stable states, such as forest. These thresholds vary by peatland type and climatic region. In this study, we apply an enhanced version of the PeatScapes numerical model to evaluate how artificial drainage affects the hydrological stability of Ireland's two dominant peatland types: raised bogs and blanket bogs. Raised bogs showed greater sensitivity to active ditch drainage than blanket bogs, with drainage effects weakening as distance increased. Following drainage removal, raised‐bog biomass remained above the undrained control after 500 years, whereas blanket‐bog biomass approached it. These contrasting responses underscore the need for peatland‐type‐specific restoration strategies. By identifying modelled hydrological and spatial thresholds, the study provides a framework for assessing drainage‐induced degradation and informing peatland conservation and restoration. The findings support policy and land management efforts to mitigate peatland degradation and reinforce their climate‐buffering capacity.

title: Therapeutic orphans no more: Revisiting the ethical justification for excluding pregnant women from pharmaceutical clinical trials.
abstract: For six decades, pregnant women have been routinely excluded from pharmaceutical clinical trials, a practice rooted in a protectionist ethic that emerged after the thalidomide tragedy. This narrative review examines whether that exclusion remains ethically justifiable, drawing on the obstetric, pharmacological, and bioethical literature together with guidance from the Council for International Organizations of Medical Sciences, the US Food and Drug Administration, and the European Medicines Agency. Far from eliminating risk, systematic exclusion has produced a critical evidence gap: most medications used in pregnancy are prescribed off-label, without adequate data on efficacy, safety, or dosing, leaving clinicians and patients to decide in an evidentiary vacuum. Using the four principles of biomedical ethics, autonomy, justice, beneficence, and nonmaleficence, this review argues that reflexive exclusion shifts risk from the monitored setting of a trial to the unmonitored setting of routine care. It further examines the medico-legal counterpart of that shift: off-label prescribing in pregnancy is lawful but places risk and responsibility on the individual prescriber, so that the absence of pregnancy-specific evidence neither excuses nor incriminates off-label use in itself, while converting a systemic regulatory failure into individual clinical liability and heightening the duty of disclosure and documentation. It outlines a risk-stratified approach to trial design distinguishing early-phase from late-phase research and differentiating clinical scenarios from chronic maternal illness to acute obstetric conditions. Further, it analyzes Brazil's Law 14 874/2024 and its implementing Decree 12 651/2025 as a case study of regulatory modernization in a middle-income country, distinguishing what is transferable to other low- and middle-income countries from what depends on institutional preconditions many such settings lack. To operationalize this shift, concrete policy measures are proposed, modeled on precedents from pediatric drug regulation: mandatory ethics committee justification requirements, a pregnancy-specific development plan analogous to the European Union's pediatrics investigation plan, and liability-mitigation mechanisms consistent with existing United States Task Force on Research Specific to Pregnant Women and Lactating Women recommendations. The review concludes that the burden of ethical justification must shift from proving why pregnant women should be included in research to proving why they should be excluded.
journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics

title: Integrating Groundwater Quality Parameters and Climatic Extremes for Irrigation Suitability: A District‐Level Diagnostic Framework for Telangana, India
abstract: This study integrates groundwater chemistry and climatic stressors to evaluate irrigation suitability across 33 districts of Telangana, India. Groundwater monitoring data (2018–2020) were combined with rainfall and temperature datasets from the India Meteorological Department (IMD). Key indices included sodium adsorption ratio (SAR), residual sodium carbonate (RSC), total dissolved solids (TDS), the composite irrigation suitability index (CISI+) and the climate extremes index (CEI). Most districts were safe under RSC, with only three marginal cases. Sodicity emerged as the dominant hazard: SAR correlated almost perfectly with CISI+ ( r = 0.97), while TDS showed strong associations ( r = 0.72). Rainfall deficits were linked to higher maximum temperatures ( r = −0.44) and CEI values ( r = −0.32), highlighting drought‐prone districts as more vulnerable. CEI values were generally low, but Jogulamba Gadwal, Nagarkurnool and Sangareddy recorded localised extremes. Random forest achieved perfect classification (accuracy, precision, recall, F1 = 1.0), outperforming gradient boosting, support vector machine and multilayer perceptron. SHAP analysis identified Jogulamba Gadwal, Nalgonda and Rajanna Sircilla as sodicity hotspots, while rainfall contributions were minimal. Practical implications include district‐specific adaptation strategies such as gypsum application, groundwater blending, salt‐tolerant crops, rainwater harvesting and recharge conservation. These measures are essential to safeguard irrigation resilience under evolving climate pressures.

title: Dual-respiratory-phase low-dose quantitative CT for assessing COPD severity.
A multimodal framework to assess differences in dynamic visual acuity between athletes with and without recent sport-related concussion
abstract: Sport-related concussions (SRC) commonly affect vision and cognition, but there is limited understanding of how concurrent balance and exertion demands may affect visual-cognitive performance beyond symptom resolution. Purpose To determine if a dynamic visual acuity (DVA) task performed during standing and walking could differentiate performance between athletes with and without concussion history. Methods Interuniversity athletes (N = 30, age = 20.9 years ± 1.4) with SRC history who were asymptomatic (SRC = 14; females = 6) were compared to athletes without SRC (CONTROL = 16; female = 7). A DVA task was completed while seated, standing, and during low- and moderate-intensity treadmill walking. A Tumbling ‘E’ target was presented randomly in either random walk (R) or horizontal (H) motion (2.31 m/s), in one of four orientations; responses were selected using a handheld keypad. Performance was characterized as a change in DVA score from Seated (logMAR) and response time (RT, ms). A linear mixed-effects model was fitted for DVA change scores and a generalized mixed effects model for median RT. Results The SRC group exhibited worse DVA change scores during standing and walking compared to CONTROL (p < .05) during R-motion only. Whereas both groups responded faster during treadmill walking for both R- and H-motion (p < .001). Only two athletes (14%) in the SRC group experienced mild symptoms that did not affect performance during the protocol. Conclusion A multimodal DVA assessment, including standing and walking conditions, may be a feasible approach to detect differences in visual-cognitive performance for athletes following clinical recovery of concussion.

title: AI-enabled hydroponics: a critical review of sensor-driven farming systems for sustainable global food security
The CRISPR-dCas9 epigenetic toolbox: prospects for modulating gene expression in climate-resilient crops
Digital agricultural technology innovation and agricultural carbon emission intensity: are there external dependencies?
Multi-stage attack detection in IIoT supply chains using graph neural networks
abstract: Industrial internet of things (IIoT) environments connect devices, gateways, hosts, and services in ways that increase both operational visibility and cyber-attack exposure. Conventional intrusion-detection systems commonly produce flat attack labels and may underuse relational information between communicating assets. We investigate an ATT&CK-inspired stage-aware intrusion-detection framework that maps observed behaviour into four operational classes: Benign, Initial Access & Discovery (IAD), Lateral Movement, Execution & Persistence (LMEP), and Impact (IMP). Network-flow observations are represented using leakage-aware feature processing and an asset–time interaction graph, enabling comparison of feature-based, graph-based, temporal, and fusion models. To reduce dependence on a single benchmark, we evaluate the stage-aware formulation on both ToN-IoT and Edge-IIoTset. Following correction of the temporal-windowing pipeline, ToN-IoT contains 34,435 asset–window instances. GAT achieves the strongest ToN-IoT stage-detection performance with Macro-F1 0.687±0.041\documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$0.687\pm 0.041$$\end{document}, followed by GraphSAGE (0.671±0.015\documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$0.671\pm 0.015$$\end{document}) and GCN (0.660±0.039\documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$0.660\pm 0.039$$\end{document}). A controlled meta-learner ablation increases stacked Macro-F1 to 0.468 with gradient boosting, suggesting that meta-learner choice contributes substantially to the fusion shortfall. On Edge-IIoTset, the feature-based Random Forest performs best with Macro-F1 0.615. We additionally evaluate stage-mapping sensitivity, graph construction, window-size sensitivity, alternative stacking meta-learners, baseline tuning, bootstrap uncertainty, and inference latency. We formulate a strict leakage-controlled pre-impact forecasting protocol; however, although the corrected ToN-IoT representation yields 21,313 candidate forecasting instances, only five are positive and all occur in the training partition, with zero positives in validation and test. We therefore do not report held-out forecasting-performance estimates and limit our empirical claims to stage-aware intrusion detection.

Peat-Free Growing Media for Tropical Agroforestry Seedlings: A Systematic Review and Predictive Substrate-Quality Framework with Supplementary Multilevel Meta-Analysis
abstract: The successful establishment of perennial species in agroforestry systems depends critically on nursery-phase conditions, yet evidence on alternative growing media remains fragmented across species, crop groups, and experimental contexts. This study synthesized evidence on peat-reduced and alternative nursery substrates to identify recurrent substrate systems and physicochemical conditions associated with high performance in tropical perennial seedlings relevant to agroforestry. We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review and quantitative synthesis integrating treatment-level Composite Performance Index (CPI) values, physicochemical modelling, empirical quality-control windows, and a supplementary log response ratio (lnRR) meta-analytic layer. The deduplicated evidence base comprised 84 eligible studies distributed across the tropical belt. Coir/cocopeat-based mixes showed the strongest recurrent integrated-performance signal, with the highest median CPI (0.569) and the greatest proportion of treatments above the 70th percentile threshold (51.3%). Vermicompost-based mixes, agroindustrial residues, and selected biochar-amended media also performed well. Bulk density showed the strongest negative association with CPI (standardized β = −0.339), whereas nitrogen, total organic carbon, cation exchange capacity, and phosphorus were positively associated with performance. pH and electrical conductivity showed nonlinear responses, with peak performance at intermediate values. High-performing tropical nursery media were defined less by a single ingredient than by a coherent physicochemical profile. The resulting framework provides evidence-based guidance for designing regionally adapted, peat-reduced growing media for perennial planting material used in agroforestry systems.
journal: Journal of Soil Science and Plant Nutrition

title: Heterogeneous states of regenerative agriculture adoption among smallholders in Kenya
abstract: Regenerative agriculture (RA) is widely promoted as a pathway to restore agroecosystems and strengthen resilience. However, empirical studies often reduce these pathways to a binary distinction between adopters and non-adopters, obscuring the differentiated and institutionally mediated pathways through which smallholders engage with principle-based agricultural transitions. This study conceptualizes RA adoption as a continuum of engagement among smallholder farmers in Kenya. We used a sequential mixed-methods design in which an initial qualitative phase informed survey development, the contextualization of RA indicators, and engagement states. This included 33 individual farmer interviews, 14 focus group discussions, 9 expert interviews, and one stakeholder workshop. Building on these insights, we surveyed 949 farmers and developed a seven-state engagement typology based on awareness, adoption timing, practice history, continuity of use, behavioral change, and adoption lag. We used a multinomial logit model to examine the factors associated with farmers’ positions across these states. Our findings show that binary classification identifies 49% of farmers as RA implementers and 51% as non-implementers. However, findings also mask substantial heterogeneity within both groups. The seven-state classification unmasks this and reveals knowledge gaps, conversion barriers, delayed uptake, stagnation, and discontinuation. Credit access was the most consistent factor associated with RA engagement states beyond awareness. Gender, age, marital status, land tenure, and the county context showed state-specific associations. RA engagement among smallholders is markedly heterogeneous; the observed states are consistent with, but do not demonstrate, staged and reversible adoption pathways. Our typology offers a potentially transferable framework for diagnosing where farmers are located along the RA engagement continuum and for designing state-contingent interventions that address both entry barriers and progression constraints.

title: Differentiating Islamic values and their associations with Muslim community participation and rural community development
abstract: This study examines how ukhuwah (brotherhood), amanah (trust and responsibility), and broader Islamic values influence Muslim community participation and rural community development in Indonesia. Using survey data from 693 Muslim middle-class respondents in rural areas of West Java, Central Java, and Yogyakarta, the study applies Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results show that Islamic values strongly influence Muslim community participation (β = 0.662, p < 0.001), while amanah has a small but significant effect (β = 0.074, p = 0.022). Ukhuwah has no significant effect (β = 0.037, p = 0.262). Muslim community participation strongly predicts community development (β = 0.729, p < 0.001) and mediates the effects of Islamic values and amanah on community development, but not that of ukhuwah. The model explains 53.2% of the variance in both participation and community development. The findings indicate that Islamic values do not function uniformly as drivers of rural development; their contribution depends on their translation into active community participation. The study extends faith-based social capital research by distinguishing the different roles of Islamic value dimensions in participatory rural development.

title: An IoT-based approach for solar irradiance estimation using three different sensor proxies
abstract: High-precision Commercial pyranometers and radiometers are often prohibitively expensive, and inexpensive solar power meters lack integrated wireless connectivity, limiting deployment in decentralized monitoring networks. This feasibility study presents a budget-friendly IoT-based sensing platform designed to estimate global horizontal solar irradiance (W/m2) using a multi-model fusion technique. The hardware architecture utilizes a NodeMCU ESP8266 microcontroller to continuously acquire real-time data from three distinct, non-intrusive radiometric proxies: (i) differential surface temperature measured using black (T2) and white (T3) aluminum plates. (ii) optical illuminance (lux) via a BH1750 digital ambient light photo-diode and (iii) electrical short-circuit current drift via a polycrystalline photovoltaic (PV) panel monitored by an INA219 sensor. To eliminate manual logging errors and ensure synchronization, sensor streams are telemetered in real time to a centralized workstation using TCP/IP socket connections. The proxies were calibrated and empirically cross-validated against a commercial reference radiometer (HTC LX-107) under dynamic outdoor solar radiation conditions. Regression models demonstrated strong statistical alignment between proxy signals and absolute solar irradiance. Outdoor validation confirmed that the optical illuminance proxy achieved the highest dynamic responsiveness (R² = 0.69 to 0.94 and RMSE ≈ 51.32 to 115.03 W/m²), followed closely by the differential temperature proxy (R² = 0.81 to 0.88 and RMSE ≈ 70.82 to 94.92 W/m²). The PV panel electrical proxy also demonstrated a strong predictive performance and maintained a solid peak multi-regression fit during outdoor validation (R² = 0.68 to 0.77 and RMSE ≈ 103.06 to 117.45 W/m²). The proposed multi-modal IoT framework offers an automated, scalable, and budget-friendly alternative to standard pyranometers. By combining multi-sensor fusion with automated wireless telemetry, the system successfully tracks diurnal irradiance fluctuations, providing a viable tool for solar energy management, agricultural microclimate monitoring, and smart grid integration at a fraction of the cost of commercial hardware.

title: A Macrophage-Integrated 3D Spheroid Model Inoculated with Bacteria for Simultaneous Evaluation of Antibacterial Efficacy, Cytotoxicity, and Immunomodulation.
abstract: Conventional antimicrobial-material testing typically relies on separate bacterial assays and two-dimensional (2D) mammalian cell cultures. Although essential as first-line screening tools, these approaches do not capture the three-dimensional (3D) tissue architecture, diffusion constraints, extracellular-matrix remodeling, and innate immune interactions encountered by host-contacting antimicrobial materials. Herein, this study introduces a macrophage-containing 3D spheroid model designed for the simultaneous evaluation of antimicrobial efficacy, host-cell cytotoxicity, and immune responses. The tripartite spheroids comprised DU 145 epithelial cells, THP-1-derived M0 macrophages, and E. coli. The influence of macrophage integration on spheroid architecture was characterized using scanning electron microscopy and scanning ion conductance microscopy, revealing significant biophysical remodeling marked by enhanced matrix compaction and surface densification. These structural alterations were further supported by changes in electrostatic properties and reduced FITC-dextran penetration, indicating enhanced barrier function. Following E. coli challenge, resident macrophages exhibited functional plasticity, polarizing toward an M1-like phenotype to suppress bacterial colonization. The platform was then used to evaluate PA-PQ-37, a cationic antimicrobial coating. In contrast to 2D monolayers, macrophage-containing spheroids retained structural integrity and live-cell esterase activity on the coating while exhibiting reduced recoverable bacterial burden. The model further differentiated the macrophage-associated responses elicited by a cationic polymer, ampicillin, and azithromycin, including inflammatory and pro-resolution-like marker profiles. This animal-free platform complements conventional antibacterial and cytotoxicity assays by supporting integrated evaluation of host-contacting antimicrobial biomaterials in a tissue-like, immune-responsive microenvironment. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Antimicrobial biomaterials are typically evaluated using simplified bacterial assays and 2D mammalian cell cultures, which do not reproduce the tissue architecture, diffusion barriers, extracellular matrix remodeling, or immune surveillance encountered in vivo. This limitation can lead to inaccurate assessment of both antimicrobial efficacy and host-cell compatibility. In this study, we developed a macrophage-integrated 3D infected spheroid model that incorporates resident immune cells into a tissue-like microenvironment for biomaterial evaluation. The model captures macrophage-driven spheroid compaction, matrix remodeling, bacterial restriction, and infection-responsive immune polarization. Using this platform, we demonstrate that cationic PA-PQ-37 coatings appear highly cytotoxic in 2D assays but are well tolerated by macrophage-competent 3D spheroids while retaining antibacterial activity. The model also distinguishes antimicrobial agents with different immunomodulatory profiles, including inflammatory, neutral, and pro-resolution responses. This work provides a physiologically relevant strategy for assessing antimicrobial biomaterials beyond conventional bacterial killing and cytotoxicity endpoints.

title: Supporting bystander intervention through conversational AI: Experimental evidence from undergraduate samples.
abstract: Across campuses and workplaces, people are receiving bystander intervention training to empower them to support victims and mitigate situations of harm. But even after this training, many people remain insecure about their ability to intervene and hesitate to act when intervention is needed. One promising solution to bystanders' ongoing inaction is to provide a safe, judgment-free environment where people can repeatedly practice skills and receive personalized feedback. Here, we explore that solution through a chatbot-based bystander intervention practice tool, where an AI agent guides users through evidence-based training. Across two preregistered experiments with undergraduates-a pilot study conducted on a local college campus followed by a larger online study-we found preliminary evidence that chatbot-guided training may strengthen several motivational outcomes associated with bystander intervention, including bystander efficacy, attitudes, psychological safety, and norm perceptions. This work provides preliminary evidence of the impact of chatbot-guided bystander intervention training. The findings highlight the potential of AI as a pedagogical tool for supporting bystander intervention and provide an empirical foundation for future research on AI-assisted intervention training.

title: 'AI-Learner Partnership': Psychological mechanisms and developmental trajectories of EFL learners' writing agency in GenAI-assisted courses.
abstract: This study explores how EFL learners construct, negotiate, and develop writing agency through engagement with generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in second language writing courses. GenAI is conceptualized as a cultural mediational means within an integrated sociocultural and positive psychological framework. Eleven Chinese EFL university students were followed over a 16-week semester as they completed multiple academic writing tasks with GenAI support. Drawing on a qualitative multi-method design, data were collected through semi-structured interviews, screen recordings of writing sessions, and reflective journals. The analysis identified three interrelated, non-linear phases in learners' agency development: initial exploration (characterized by novelty-driven engagement, dependency on AI output, and emergent self-efficacy), strategic adaptation (marked by more selective, task-contingent tool use and the strengthening of writing-specific psychological capital), and deliberate appropriation (signaled by personalized integration of GenAI into writing workflows and the emergence of a more agentic techno-authorial identity). Across these phases, cognitive processes, affective experiences, positive psychological resources, and task design features jointly shaped how learners mobilized technological affordances to enact writing agency. The findings suggest that writing agency in human-AI collaborative writing is a dynamic, context-sensitive accomplishment rather than a fixed individual trait. By connecting sociocultural accounts of mediated action with positive psychological resources, the study offers a process-oriented account of how EFL learners negotiate assistance, authorship, and autonomy in GenAI-supported academic writing.

title: Comparison of visual tasks for assessing attentional bias in cannabis users and non-users.
abstract: Attentional bias toward substance-related cues is a key feature of addiction and may contribute to the continued use of substances, such as cannabis. However, the sensitivity of different paradigms for detecting this bias remains underexplored. This study compared three visual attentional bias paradigms: dot probe (DP), eye movement (EM), and MouseView.js (MV) in detecting cannabis-related attentional biases among cannabis users and non-users. Thirty-one participants (i.e., 16 users and 15 non-users) completed all measures: DP (reaction time to probes replacing cannabis or neutral stimuli), EM (measured via eye-tracking), and MV (cursor-based dwell time). Linear mixed-effects models examined the effects of stimulus type, group, craving, and cannabis use severity. The EM and MV tasks revealed significant stimulus effects, with non-users showing greater attention to neutral images, while cannabis users exhibited more evenly distributed attention across stimuli. In the EM task, a significant stimulus × severity interaction indicated reduced attentional differentiation with increased cannabis use severity. MV results followed a similar, but less precise pattern. In contrast, the DP task showed minimal group or interaction effects and lacked sensitivity to detect attentional differences. These findings suggest that EM-based measures are more sensitive for detecting cannabis-related attentional biases, particularly when accounting for cannabis use severity. MV showed some alignment with EM patterns but demonstrated weaker effects. The DP task, despite its widespread use, may be insufficient for capturing cannabis-related attentional differences. Results highlight the importance of task selection in attentional bias research and the potential influence of individual differences in cannabis use severity.

A multimodal MRI radiomics sonata for differentiating small renal masses: a two-center retrospective study.
abstract: BACKGROUND Accurately distinguishing benign from malignant small renal masses (SRMs) is crucial to avoid unnecessary surgeries, yet reliable preoperative diagnostic tools remain limited. METHODS A total of 189 patients with SRMs from two hospitals (2018-2022) were enrolled. Clinical data and MRI features were analyzed by two radiologists. Radiomics features were automatically extracted from manually segmented ROIs using dedicated software. Significant features were selected via univariate analysis, multivariate regression, and Lasso to develop three models: radiomics, clinical, and combined nomogram. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using the Area Under the receiver operating characteristic Curve (AUC). RESULTS The radiomics-clinical nomogram was constructed using T2WI signal intensity (p < 0.001), pseudocapsule (p = 0.001), and radiomics score (Rad-score, p = 0.001) via multivariate logistic regression. In the training set, the nomogram achieved an AUC of 0.962 (95% CI: 0.931-0.993), outperforming both the radiomics model (AUC = 0.918, 95% CI: 0.862-0.974) and the clinical model (AUC = 0.856, 95% CI: 0.780-0.933). Favorable performance was observed in the internal validation set (nomogram: AUC = 0.981, 95% CI: 0.944-1.000; radiomics model: AUC = 0.912, 95% CI: 0.750-1.000; clinical model: AUC = 0.844, 95% CI: 0.578-1.000) and external validation set (nomogram: AUC = 0.971, 95% CI: 0.886-1.000; radiomics model: AUC = 0.928, 95% CI: 0.841-0.989; clinical model: AUC = 0.916,95% CI: 0.760-0.976). CONCLUSION All three models enable effective and non-invasive preoperative differentiation of benign from malignant SRMs, with the radiomics-clinical nomogram exhibiting the highest diagnostic accuracy, supporting its potential as a valuable clinical tool.

title: MPRT-DETR: multi-platform real-time rice panicle detection and counting based on the transformer method and complex field imagery
Dual-state adaptive unrolled network for structure-preserving low-dose CT image restoration.
abstract: Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces radiation exposure but introduces spatially heterogeneous noise and artifacts that can obscure subtle anatomical structures. We address post-reconstruction image-domain LDCT restoration, where degradation suppression and structure preservation impose competing demands on a single restoration trajectory. We propose DSAUNet, a Dual-State Adaptive Unrolled Network that maintains persistent anatomy- and degradation-oriented latent states across unrolled stages. Rather than acting as transient feature branches, the evolving states participate in parameterizing subsequent restoration behavior through a degradation-oriented global policy coordinate for stage-level modulation and state-derived confidence variables for spatially selective regulation. Direction-aware prior modeling and multi-scale state guidance further realize this state-parameterized restoration process. Under the reported protocols, DSAUNet achieves 40.3721 dB PSNR and 0.9642 SSIM on 2DeteCT, exceeding the strongest baseline by 1.6320 dB and 0.0108, and achieves 47.4277 dB PSNR and 0.9846 SSIM under the patient-level five-fold Mayo evaluation, with a 1.0920 dB PSNR gain over the strongest PSNR baseline. On LoDoPaB-CT, it further obtains 38.5501 dB PSNR and 0.9141 SSIM, with the best PSNR, SSIM, and VIF among the compared methods. Controlled raw-state, persistent state-swapping, policy-coordinate, and confidence-map analyses support functionally differentiated state roles and active adaptive regulation. Bidirectional 2DeteCT-Mayo zero-shot experiments reveal direction-dependent transfer behavior, while unified profiling characterizes an accuracy-complexity trade-off. Together, these results support persistent dual-state controlled unrolling as a structured approach to image-domain LDCT restoration within the evaluated settings.
