Genetic transformation patterns along a longitude gradient in Ukrainian populations of Schizophyllum commune fungus.
abstract: The research of fungal biodiversity is important under global climate change and increasing anthropogenic pressure on ecosystems. The most studies focusing on fungal biogeography oriented on species richness. There is a short supply researches on how genetic diversity shifts along a longitudinal gradient within one species. Model fungi with well-characterized genomes and simple cultivation requirements allow detailed research of evolutionary and ecological processes. The aim was to study the genetic profile transformation of the Schizophyllum commune populations by DNA microsatellite loci along a longitude gradient in Ukraine to establish genetic migration relationships and historical features of population development. Our findings reveal that S. commune populations from eastern to western Ukraine, show local genetic differentiation. The separation of populations into three clusters (Don + KrR, Vin + Cher, and I-F) reflects historically independent developmental trajectories. The Mantel test revealed weak but significant isolation by distance (r = 0.1048, p = 0.0016). However, the negative global correlation (Pearson r ≈ -0.56) suggests pure isolation by distance is not the dominant process shaping these populations. The biological significance of the spatial populations pattern suggests that landscape zonation and various ecological barriers restrict local gene flow, whereas long-distance spore dispersal prevents complete isolation. We identified a complex, asymmetric structural network of populations with a core (Don ↔ KrR), pronounced donor populations (Cher and I-F), and a partial peripheral element (Vin). In the absence of pronounced geographic barriers, S. commune populations can maintain local genetic differentiation. Connection density profile fluctuations within populations are shaped by various processes that actively contribute to population disintegration or consolidation and represent signatures of their evolutionary pathways.

title: Exogenous substances promote the formation of Phallus dongsun primordia by remodeling the mycosphere microenvironment.
abstract: Exogenous substance application (ESA) directly influences subterranean processes through the action of macrofungal mycelia, garnering considerable attention for its role in enhancing crop yields and resource utilization. However, the intricate mechanisms of mycosphere metabolite-microbe interactions governing macrofungal development remain unclear. This study employed Phallus dongsun for plate culture and pot experiments, integrating multi-omics analysis to investigate the regulatory mechanisms governing the growth and development of this macrofungus through functional interactions between the macrofungus, metabolites, and microorganisms under ESA. Single-factor plate cultures revealed that 60 mg/L ZnSO4·7H2O exhibited the most pronounced effect on promoting mycelial growth and biomass in all three P. dongsun strains, while 1.5 g/L MgSO4 demonstrated a slightly weaker yet still significant effect. To verify the performance of each ESA under natural conditions, single-factor pot experiments were conducted. Pot experiments showed that 1.5 g/L MgSO4 was optimal for primordia formation and earliness. Furthermore, triacontanol (TRIA, 6 mg/L), vitamin B6 (VB6, 6 mg/L) and ZnSO4·7H2O (60 mg/L) also exhibited promotional effects on primordia formation and earliness, respectively. ESA significantly altered the mycosphere metabolite composition and microbial community structure, enhancing metabolite chemodiversity and keystone taxa diversity (P < 0.05). Moreover, ESA significantly enhanced the accumulation of the keystone taxa Paraburkholderia and major metabolites-such as lipids and organic acids-within the mycosphere. Notably, ESA promoted coupling of carbon (C) and phosphorus (P) cycling, while decoupling nitrogen (N) cycling in the mycosphere. Partial least squares modeling (PLS-PM) further indicated that ESA-induced N cycling constraints significantly stimulated P. dongsun primordia formation and P uptake. Furthermore, ESA indirectly enhanced P. dongsun primordia number by increasing keystone taxa diversity. This finding provided new theoretical insights into understanding the interaction mechanisms between macrofungi and their microenvironments, as well as their microbial ecology.

title: Ethyl cellulose-alginate/poly(vinyl alcohol) dual-layer coating incorporating biochar-immobilized PGPR for controlled urea release, water retention, and plant stress resilience.
abstract: Coated controlled-release fertilizers can synchronize nutrient supply with crop demand, yet single-layer systems are often limited by poor structural integrity and restricted functionality. Here, salt-tolerant plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) were immobilized on biochar and embedded in a dually crosslinked poly(vinyl alcohol)/sodium alginate hydrogel (PSBP). A dual-layer controlled-release urea fertilizer (PSBPEU-CRF) was fabricated using an ethyl cellulose inner diffusion barrier and a PSBP outer hydrogel coating. PSBPEU-CRF enabled sustained viable-cell release and improved bacterial immobilization stability. PSBP hydrogel reached an equilibrium swelling ratio of 424%, improved soil water retention and showed 70.65% mass loss after 28 d. At 2% (w/w), soil water retention remained 20.96% on day 10, compared with 2.35% in unamended soil. PSBPEU-CRF markedly retarded urea release in water and soil; the release profiles fitted the Korsmeyer-Peppas model, indicating anomalous transport governed by diffusion and polymer-network swelling/relaxation. In saline-alkali pakchoi pots, PSBPEU-CRF increased chlorophyll accumulation and antioxidant enzyme activities while reducing lipid peroxidation and the Na+/K+ ratio. Overall, the integration of controlled nutrient release, soil water retention, and rhizosphere functional regulation provided by the PSBP hydrogel layer offers a promising approach for developing multifunctional fertilizers for salt-affected soils. Nevertheless, its long-term field performance, manufacturing scalability, and economic feasibility require further evaluation.

title: Embracing macrophage complexity for research and translation.
abstract: Macrophages are among the most versatile differentiated cell types in the body, serving as key regulators of tissue development, homeostasis, inflammation, repair, and immunity. Their functional diversity cannot be captured by fixed subsets, binary activation states, or single-marker definitions. Macrophage identity emerges instead from the integration of developmental origin, tissue niche, epigenetic history, local environmental cues, and disease-associated signals. Advances in single-cell genomics, spatial profiling, epigenomics, in vivo perturbation, and computational modeling now show that this behavior is organized through modular gene programs, so that any given macrophage state is best described as a weighted combination of program activities rather than a discrete label. We argue that embracing this modular architecture matters not only for annotation but for therapy: macrophage-directed interventions will require defining disease-associated states, identifying surface-accessible entry points into them, and rewiring the underlying programs with spatial and temporal precision.

title: FT-transformer with differentiable feature selection and residual refinement for biodiesel engine performance and emission prediction
Advancing nanomaterials for treatment of eye diseases: a review.
abstract: Ocular diseases involving both the anterior and posterior segments-such as dry eye disease, keratitis, glaucoma, cataracts, diabetic retinopathy, retinal vein occlusion, and ocular tumors-remain major contributors to global visual impairment. Conventional topical and systemic therapies are limited by rapid clearance, restricted penetration across ocular barriers, and poor bioavailability, particularly for posterior-segment targets. Nanotechnology has introduced a transformative therapeutic paradigm by enabling controlled pharmacokinetics, enhanced tissue penetration, and site-specific delivery. A wide range of engineered nanomaterials-including polymeric nanoparticles, lipid-based carriers, dendrimers, metallic and metal-oxide nanoparticles, mesoporous silica systems, cerium oxide nanozymes, carbon quantum dots, nanogels, and electrospun nanofibers-has demonstrated improved drug loading, sustained release, ocular surface retention, and compatibility with biologics and gene-based agents. Emerging minimally invasive platforms, such as 4D printed smart scaffolds, dissolving microneedles and magnetically driven microrobots, further enable precise transscleral or intravitreal delivery, active navigation through the vitreous, and targeted interaction with retinal lesions. Parallel clinical advances, including FDA-approved nanoformulations and ongoing trials, confirm the translational potential of these technologies. Plus, artificial intelligence now accelerates both ophthalmic diagnosis and nanocarrier design, enabling predictive modeling of nano-bio interactions, personalized delivery strategies, and real-time disease assessment. This review integrates current advances in nanomaterial engineering and AI-guided innovation, outlining their convergent roles in shaping next-generation precision therapeutics for vision preservation and restoration.

title: Distinguishing weed patches in Maine wild blueberry fields using drone aerial imagery for targeted weed control
abstract: In the wild blueberry (Vaccinium angustifolium Aiton) system, perennial weeds are a significant challenge. Weeds compete for resources and have a patchy, heterogeneous distribution, often growing among the rhizome of the crop. Producers broadcast spray herbicides to control weeds, but currently seek to lower costs, reduce environmental impact, and mitigate herbicide resistance. Site-specific weed management (SSWM) using weed maps offers a targeted solution, but its adoption is limited by the lack of software compatible with commercial spray equipment and by technological constraints, such as weed patch size thresholds. The objective of this work is to suggest new weed-mapping workflows for ground and drone spraying in wild blueberry fields using RGB drone imagery processed in drone-compatible GIS software: PIX4Dfields. Drone aerial imagery from two commercial wild blueberry fields in Maine was captured in May 2025. To create maps for ground spot spraying, PIX4Dfield’s machine learning-driven “Magic Tool” and five vegetation Index Tool workflows were assessed. For drone zone spraying, maps created with minimum weed patch sizes of 9.3 m2 and 405 m2 were evaluated. All maps were validated using image-based and ground-based accuracy assessments. The “Magic Tool” workflow proved most effective for ground spray maps, achieving ≤98% (image-based) and ≤86% (ground-based) overall accuracy. Among the vegetation indices, the Triangular Greenness Index performed best (≤93% and ≤85% image-based and ground-based accuracies, respectively) at a 20% to 25% pixel exclusion level. For drone zone spraying, the 9.3-m2 minimum weed patch size yielded higher accuracy than the 405-m2 size, although performance was site dependent. Classification accuracy decreased at sites with greater weed species diversity, more uniform weed distribution, and when evaluated against more reliable ground-based reference data. Nevertheless, the resulting maps identified weed coverage ranges of 39% to 52% and 58% to 61% across the two fields, giving growers a practical tool to reduce inputs and implement SSWM.

title: Atmospheric Removal of Nitrous Oxide: Approaches and Feasibility
abstract: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is the third-largest contributor to anthropogenic greenhouse gas forcing and the dominant anthropogenic ozone-depleting emission. While mitigation can flatten emissions, there is no clear pathway to eliminate residual emissions from agriculture and other diffuse sources, a key challenge for climate stabilization. The potential role of atmospheric removal has not been holistically assessed, yet N2O’s high potency and long atmospheric lifetime indicate the potential for a durable climate benefit. This review synthesizes emerging approaches for atmospheric N2O removal, organized by reaction mechanism (thermal destruction and thermocatalysis, photolysis, gas-phase radical reactions, photocatalysis, and biological reduction) and deployment format (closed versus open system). Each is evaluated for technical efficacy, climate viability, environmental and social viability, and economic plausibility using lower-bound cost models. No approach yet satisfies all four: gas-phase radical reactors are precluded by their kinetics, thermocatalytic and photocatalytic reactors require ten- to hundred-fold performance gains, and open-system approaches have the lowest cost floors but face the greatest measurement and governance challenges. These results identify the performance thresholds and broader constraints that govern feasibility across pathways, providing a foundation for a research agenda and for assessing the role of N2O removal alongside emissions mitigation.

title: Integrated stress signaling pathways promote adaptive reprogramming for chondrocyte survival in Metaphyseal Chondrodysplasia Type Schmid
abstract: Collagen X, encoded by the Col10a1 gene, is expressed specifically by hypertrophic chondrocytes (HCs) in the cartilage. Mutations of the Col10a1 gene in humans, which increase the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress in HCs, lead to metaphyseal chondrodysplasia type Schmid (MCDS). However, the mechanism of how HCs respond to ER stress to affect bone development and growth is not entirely understood. In this study, we generated a new mouse model harboring a 13 bp deletion (13del) in the endogenous Col10a1 gene. These 13del-MCDS mice display all the known clinical characteristics of human MCDS, as well as the molecular and cellular changes within the growth plate cartilage. For the first time, we found that triggering ER stress leads to activation of hypoxia and HIFs pathways in vivo, promoting cellular survival in HCs of the 13del-MCDS mice. To test whether the activated hypoxia and HIFs pathways are triggered by ER stress or extrinsic factors, we generated WT/GFP-MCDS chimera mice. Our findings showed that the activation of hypoxia and the hypoxic pathway is an intrinsic response to ER stress, which may partly occur through activation of ATF4 in HCs of mice. In parallel, p53 pathway changes and autophagy-associated protein-quality-control responses were observed in spatial association with altered chondrocyte differentiation and survival. These findings reveal coordinated engagement of multiple stress-response pathways during the adaptive response of hypertrophic chondrocytes to chronic ER stress.

title: CAUSE: a context-aware user security enhancement model for trustworthy consumer immersive applications
abstract: Consumer-focused virtual immersive environments including AR and VR metaverse applications are creating new ways for people to interact, collaborate, and engage in commerce. Simultaneously, user privacy, trust, and security are also at great risk in these environments. This paper proposes the Context-Aware User Security Enhancement (CAUSE) model, which is a policy-based, user-centric, comprehensive, and real-time protection mechanism against such threats. For proactive threat detection and user interaction management, CAUSE incorporates a personalized AI agent. Fine-grained control is exercised by the user through user-defined security policies, interpreted by the policy engine to support context-aware, scenario-based controls. To ensure interoperability across diverse immersive platforms, it envisages user-defined security policy migration and consistent enforcement. The simulation results show that CAUSE effectively addresses threats, caters to complex interaction scenarios and improves user safety in virtual immersive environments. In the simulated evaluation, the Decision Tree risk classifier achieved 94.45% overall accuracy for three-class risk classification and a High-Risk recall of 90.83%. CAUSE addresses some of the key issues with current user-security methods and contributes to the development of safer and more trustworthy consumer immersive environments.

title: Single-step Raman spectroscopy for maple syrup quality control
abstract: Maple syrup quality evaluation involves multiple parameters, including color classification, flavor assessment, and the measurement of sugar concentration, which are influenced by the complex chemical composition of the syrup matrix. Conventional quality assessment relies on separate analytical and sensory approaches, creating a bottleneck in the industrial processing of maple syrup. As such, rapid techniques are needed to assess multiple quality control parameters from a single measurement. In this study, Raman spectroscopy combined with machine learning was evaluated to characterize maple syrup quality attributes using 721 samples representing different color grades (golden, amber, dark, and very dark) and flavor categories. After spectral preprocessing, principal component analysis (PCA) was performed to investigate natural spectral variations among samples. PCA revealed differences associated with syrup color and flavor categories; however, the overlap observed among several groups indicated that the relationship between Raman fingerprints and maple syrup properties involves complex spectral variations that are not fully resolved by linear unsupervised analysis. To improve discrimination, convolutional neural network (CNN) models were developed to extract nonlinear spectral features directly from Raman data. For color classification, the CNN achieved prediction accuracies of 91%, 68%, 73%, and 92% for golden, amber, dark, and very dark syrups, respectively. Flavor classification showed strong discrimination for several defect categories, including OK (83%), √ (76%), VR4 (73%), VR5 (78%), VR13 (100%), and CT (83%), while lower performance for VR1 (55%), VR2 (66%), and VR12 (64%) reflected the challenge of differentiating sensory defects with overlapping chemical characteristics. VR13 showed a high classification rate in the evaluated data; however, the small number of independent VR13 samples prevents a robust estimate of general performance for this class. In addition to Raman fingerprints, fluorescence background variations were evaluated as an indicator of optical properties and were found to correlate with maple syrup light transmittance values used for color grading. The quantitative capability of Raman spectroscopy was further assessed by predicting sucrose concentrations using standard sucrose solutions (45–67%, w/w). Concentration-dependent Raman features were extracted and used to develop a random forest regression (RFR) model, achieving coefficients of determination (R2) of 0.87. Application of the model to real maple syrup samples yielded sucrose predictions with an average bias of 0.35%, indicating that Raman-derived spectral information can be used to evaluate both compositional and quality-related characteristics of maple syrup. Overall, the results reported demonstrate the power of Raman spectroscopy for a multiparametric analysis of maple syrup.

title: How extensive and coordinated is farmers’ participation in agricultural value chains in China? Evidence from contractual–digital chain coupling
The pro-obesity role of G3BP1 through altering adipogenic differentiation in mice via the PI3K/AKT pathway.
abstract: As a growing but non-infectious epidemic, obesity is a common cause of several comorbidities. GTPase-activating protein SH3 domain-binding protein 1 (G3BP1) is a central regulator of stress‑granule assembly that has significant implications in metabolic disorders. This article aims to explore the functional mechanism of G3BP1 in obesity, both in vitro and in vivo. Functional assays were used to detect cellular phenotypes. Reverse transcription quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and western blotting were also used to test metastasis-, phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (AKT) signalling- and Wnt/β-catenin signalling-related genes. Oil‑red‑O staining and haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining were used to estimate lipid deposition. RT-qPCR, western blotting, and immunofluorescence staining were used to determine adipocyte differentiation and lipid metabolism. The TOPFlash/FOPFlash reporter assay was used to identify β-catenin activity. In a murine model fed a high-fat diet (HFD, 60% fat), body weight was measured prior to the detection of adipokine levels by enzyme‑linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), triacylglycerol (TG) concentration using an assay kit, and adipogenic marker genes by western blotting. G3BP1 knockdown inhibited proliferation, migration, invasion, and adipogenesis, and induced cell cycle arrest in 3T3-L1 preadipocytes, and decreased body weight and adipogenesis and fat accumulation in obese mice. G3BP1 activated Wnt/β-catenin and PI3K/AKT pathways. LY294002 (PI3K inhibitor) and SC3036 (PI3K activator) reversed the in vitro effects of G3BP1 or silenced G3BP1 on preadipocyte invasion. G3BP1 may promote preadipocyte proliferation, migration, invasion, and adipogenesis to promote the progression of obesity, which might be relevant to the PI3K/AKT pathway.

title: Research hotspots and evolution trends of human amniotic fluid stem cells: A cite space bibliometric analysis based on WoSCC and PubMed.
abstract: OBJECTIVE To systematically review the research hotspots, knowledge structure, and evolution trends in the field of human amniotic fluid stem cells (hAFSCs). METHODS A bibliometric approach was employed using CiteSpace 6.2.R4 software, with the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC, 2006-2026, including 601 original research papers) and PubMed (1984-2024, including 960 publications) as data sources. Standardized, reproducible search strategies (including synonyms, abbreviations, MeSH terms, and Boolean operators) were developed for each database, and literature screening followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Using the WoSCC dataset as the core, we generated comprehensive visualizations covering author collaboration networks, countries, institutions, keyword co-occurrence, clustering, timelines, time zones, and emerging terms; the PubMed data were used for comparison of long-term publication trends. RESULTS The global publication volume in the field of hAFSCs has shown an overall upward trend, which can be divided into 3 phases: exploratory inception (1984-2006), rapid growth (2007-2013), and stable deepening (2014 to present). The United States (177 articles) and Italy (132 articles) form the dual engines of international collaboration, while China ranks third in publication volume (75 articles) but exhibits relatively weak international collaboration (centrality 0.02). The evolution of research themes is clear: from 2006 to 2009, the focus was on cell isolation, characterization, and in vitro culture; from 2010 to 2015, the scope expanded to multipotent differentiation, animal models, and the treatment of fetal diseases; and since 2018, exosomes/extracellular vesicles have emerged as the most active frontier with the highest emergence intensity (7.37). CONCLUSION Bibliometric analysis indicates that research on hAFSCs has evolved from basic biological characterization into a comprehensive field encompassing multipotent differentiation, tissue engineering, and exosome regulation. Exosomes/extracellular vesicles and targeted repair of organ damage are currently the primary areas of focus. This study is a descriptive analysis; all conclusions are based on publication trend statistics and do not involve validation of clinical translational efficacy.

title: Factors associated with slow employment: evidence from the 2024 undergraduate cohort at Fujian University of Technology, China
abstract: This study estimates slow-employment prevalence at graduation, compares it with the university's full-cohort rate and examines adjusted associations of demographic, GPA, family-context and psychological factors with slow-employment status. A cross-sectional survey yielded 385 valid responses. Work values and career self-efficacy (CSE) were assessed using established measures. SPSSAU analyses comprised descriptive statistics, non-parametric comparisons, Spearman correlations and two nested binary logistic regression models. Slow employment accounted for 14.55% of respondents, close to the full-cohort rate of 15.31%. Relative to GPA <2, GPA 2 to <3 (OR = 4.11), GPA 3 to <4 (OR = 3.52), lower SES (OR = 2.70), and neutral parental stance (OR = 2.81) were associated with higher odds. Work values were not significant after adjustment, overall CSE was not associated with slow employment, and adding both did not significantly improve model fit. Universities may benefit from differentiated support that considers GPA alongside family context. Time-bounded plans can combine examination preparation with continued job search for students pursuing competitive postgraduate or public-sector examinations. Lower-SES graduates may benefit from support for identified financial or mobility constraints, while family-facing guidance may help where timelines or alternatives remain unclear. The study adds multivariable evidence to a literature often based on descriptive or bivariate analysis. It distinguishes slow employment from NEET and gap-year status, identifies factors that remain associated after adjustment, and tests whether work values and career self-efficacy add explanatory value beyond background factors.

title: Interplay between online tertiary education, academic curriculum viability and students’ experiences: the dynamics of digital learning ecosystems
abstract: This study investigates the structural interplay among Digital Learning Ecosystems (DLE), Viability of Online Academic Curriculum (VOAC), Quality of Online Education (QOE) and Students’ Lived Experiences (SLE) within a tertiary education context in Ghana. A quantitative survey design was employed, collecting data from 668 graduate students. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) using AMOS was applied to test four hypothesized relationships linking curriculum viability, perceived quality, digital ecosystems and experiential outcomes. Factor analysis ensured construct reliability, and model fit was evaluated using standard SEM indices. Findings indicate that VOAC significantly associates with QOE, while DLE strongly relates with SLE. Interestingly, QOE does not automatically relate with SLE, suggesting a structural disjunction between institutional quality metrics and students’ lived realities. VOAC minimally associate with SLE, implying indirect pathways mediated by DLE. Overall, the digital ecosystem emerged as dominantly and contextually related to student experience. This study contributes to a more nuanced understanding of online education in sub-Saharan African contexts by differentiating structural quality from lived experience, highlighting the centrality of digital ecosystems and providing actionable guidance for institutions navigating the challenges of digitally mediated learning. For policymakers and educational leaders, these findings imply that investments in digital infrastructure (e.g. reliable connectivity, institutional platforms, device access) should be prioritized alongside curricular reform. The study outcome benefits the society, as recipients of academic knowledge and skills, and will serve as a useful guide by educational institutions for the effective design of online education programs that moves beyond technical implementation to the fostering of genuine societal and human-centric interaction. The study differentiates perceived quality from lived experience, repositions digital learning ecosystems as central to online education and provides a systemic framework for understanding online tertiary education in Sub-Saharan Africa. Implications highlight the need for integrated curriculum reform, ecosystem readiness and experiential design to achieve equitable and sustainable online education transformation.
journal: Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education

title: Immersive Focus+Context Techniques to Assist in Interpretation of High Density Forest Point Clouds
abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) is changing how we interact with complex spatial datasets. VR has the potential within forestry to help analyse remotely sensed spatial data for inventory management. However, challenges of scale and legibility of dense forest point clouds must be addressed. To do so, we present three VR Focus+Context (F+C) techniques: Wedgelight, Remote Lantern, and Ray Lantern. These techniques present point cloud data using a constrained highdetail focus within a broader abstracted context representation, manipulated using egocentric and exocentric interactions. We conducted two user studies. The first informed the design of the F+C techniques. The results from the first study indicate that VR significantly outperforms desktop displays in basic analysis of forestry point clouds, with improvements to both time and accuracy. The second study evaluated the performance of the resulting F+C techniques in a task analogous to real-world forestry operations. Our F+C techniques significantly outperformed current approaches, confirming their viability for facilitating detailed and effective forest assessments. These findings indicate that VR has significant advantages for spatial data analysis tasks in forestry, making a strong argument for its adoption in future analytical frameworks. The F+C visualisation techniques we introduced show considerable promise for analysis of high density point clouds, opening new avenues for development in immersive analytics. Supplemental materials (code, scans, results) are available at https://osf.io/hqc9u.

title: Development of a fabrication-to-benchtop process for SiN-based quantum devices
abstract: Silicon nitride has emerged as a key material for the advancement of future quantum communication and computational devices. However, challenges persist in establishing a comprehensive development process, spanning from fabrication to optical characterization, essential for advancing these devices to their next stage of potential. Maintaining control over the entire process, from start to finish, alongside device modeling, enables more efficient and timely iteration and optimization. Here we introduce a fabrication-to-benchtop process. We employ an in-house stoichiometric recipe for device fabrication and conduct comprehensive characterization of optical losses and material properties. Understanding and controlling the refractive index of the device are vital for predicting device geometries and group indices. Implementing the refractive indices of our fabricated devices, we simulate microring resonators and demonstrate their application in generating optical solitons.

title: DRL-Based Joint Task Processing and Resource Allocation for Remote Sensing in Vehicle-Device-Edge Collaborative Networks
abstract: Remote sensing is a key enabling technology for intelligent vehicle and transportation systems, as it acquires environmental and traffic data beyond the vehicle’s visual range. However, in practical scenarios, the lack of flexible collaboration between sensing nodes and computing facilities leads to low efficiency in the link from remote data sensing to inference, making it difficult to support the effective processing of remote data and meet the requirements of real-time tasks. To address this issue, this paper proposes a vehicle-sensing-edge collaborative model for AI task scheduling and resource management, which integrates multiple vehicles, various sensing devices, and multi-RSU edge servers. This model performs integrated management of remotely collected data and subsequent related AI task scheduling and computing processes, enabling the flexible execution of AI inference tasks on task vehicles, service vehicles, sensing devices, and RSU edge servers. By collaboratively optimizing data collection paths, communication links, and computing resource allocation, the system achieves the joint optimization of task inference accuracy and overall operational cost while balancing load equilibrium and low latency. We design a hybrid algorithm based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL), which decomposes the original problem into sub-problems and combines the Softmax Deep Double Deterministic Policy Gradient (SD3) algorithm with convex optimization calculations. The computational complexity and convergence performance of the proposed algorithm are analyzed in detail. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the algorithm’s inherent advantages of low complexity and fast, stable convergence guarantee the effectiveness of problem-solving. Meanwhile, comparative experiments with 5 comparison schemes under 6 typical scenarios are conducted, which fully verify the superiority of the proposed scheme.

title: Nonuniformity in Multi‑Physical Field Drying of Fruits and Vegetables: Mechanisms, Cascade Amplification, and Artificial Intelligence-Driven Control.
abstract: Nonuniformity is the most critical yet unresolved bottleneck limiting the industrial adoption of multi-physical field drying (microwave, radio frequency, infrared, and ultrasound) for fruits and vegetables. While individual physical field technologies and AI applications have been reviewed separately, a conceptual framework that explains how nonuniformity originates, amplifies, and can be intelligently controlled is currently lacking. This review provides a problem-driven analysis of nonuniformity in physical field drying, proposing a three-stage cascade framework (Initiation → Amplification → Termination) to elucidate the multi-scale coupling between microscopic energy defects and macroscopic quality failure. We further critically evaluate the transition from black-box artificial intelligence (AI) modeling to advanced closed-loop intelligent control strategies involving physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and digital twins, structured along a perception-prediction-control paradigm. The cascade framework reveals that initial minor heterogeneities are self-reinforced through positive feedback loops, necessitating early-warning prediction. AI-driven adaptive control, coupled with synergistic cross-field designs, may provide opportunities to interrupt this amplification process at early stages. We provide a strategic roadmap emphasizing multimodal sensing and physics-based hybrid modeling to achieve precision, uniformity, and sustainability in next-generation industrial drying systems. This review offers a distinctive problem‑oriented perspective that complements prior technology‑centric surveys by placing nonuniformity as the central narrative and offering a conceptual framework for its prediction and control.
journal: Comprehensive reviews in food science and food safety

title: Aero‐VLM: Vision‐Language Guided Oriented Aircraft Detection for Remote Sensing Imagery
abstract: Fine‐grained aircraft detection in remote sensing (RS) imagery is challenged by limited labelled data, domain shifts, high intra‐class similarity and complex environmental conditions. Conventional detectors rely heavily on dense supervision, whereas vision–language models (VLMs) often lack the geometric precision required for accurate localization in aerial scenes. To address these challenges, we propose Aero‐VLM, a hybrid CNN–Transformer framework that combines self‐supervised visual representation learning with pretrained vision–language semantic embeddings for data‐efficient fine‐grained aircraft detection. An oriented detection head with knowledge distillation is integrated with the vision–language representation to improve geometric localization and support efficient inference. We further introduce Aero‐RSI, a 10,000‐image high‐resolution benchmark comprising ten visually similar aircraft categories for fine‐grained detection. Aero‐VLM achieves 64.6% mAP@50 in zero‐shot evaluation on unseen classes, outperforming CLIP, BLIP‐2, Grounding DINO and VisionLLM by up to 44.1 percentage points. With only 10 labelled samples per class, Aero‐VLM improves mAP@50 by 16.1 percentage points, whereas competing models achieve gains of less than 10 percentage points. Cross‐domain evaluation on DOTA, MTARSI and FAIR1M demonstrates strong generalization without additional fine‐tuning, with Aero‐VLM achieving gains of up to 11.0 percentage points over CNN‐based detectors and up to 46.0 percentage points over adapted VLMs. Under full supervision, Aero‐VLM achieves 90.2% mAP@50, exceeding YOLOv11s by 2.5 percentage points and Grounding DINO by 39.7 percentage points. Despite a 33% increase in inference latency relative to YOLOv11s, Aero‐VLM requires approximately 45% less inference time than Grounding DINO, demonstrating a favourable accuracy–efficiency trade‐off.

title: Direct and Trait‐Mediated Effects of Climate on Grassland Productivity Across the Alps
abstract: Understanding how climate shapes ecosystem productivity through energetic constraints and changes in the functional properties expressed by vegetation remains challenging. This is central to trait‐based biodiversity–ecosystem functioning research in mountain grasslands where warming and environmental gradients interact. Here, we distinguish direct climatic controls on productivity from indirect pathways operating through changes in canopy functional composition, physiological state, and within‐plot spectral functional heterogeneity across the European Alps. Using Sentinel‐2 time series (2017–2024), we quantified canopy functional structure from spectral proxies of pigment investment and water status, within‐plot spectral functional heterogeneity using the functional richness (FRic) metric, and vegetation productivity using near‐infrared reflectance of vegetation (NIRv). We combined panel‐data models with piecewise structural equation modeling to partition climate associations into direct and trait‐mediated components operating through canopy functional properties and used varying‐coefficient models to evaluate how these pathways vary along environmental gradients. We identified two pathways linking climate to productivity. Warmer growing seasons increased productivity directly but were associated with a lower chlorophyll‐to‐carotenoid pigment balance, consistent with greater relative carotenoid investment, generating an opposing indirect pathway. Greater winter snow accumulation reduced productivity primarily through a direct pathway, while its canopy‐mediated pathways were uncertain. Climatic water deficit reduced canopy water status and within‐plot spectral functional heterogeneity, but its direct and total associations with productivity were not distinguishable from zero. Environmental context modulated climate–vegetation relationships. Baseline temperature and moisture availability strongly shaped climate effects on canopy traits and productivity, whereas canopy‐property–productivity relationships varied little across space. Positive productivity responses to warming were stronger in wetter and more seasonally variable climatic contexts, but weakened where baseline winter snow accumulation was greater. Together, our findings show that short‐term productivity responses in mountain grasslands reflect a balance between direct energetic constraints and indirect pathways through integrated canopy functional properties, and that this balance varies along macroclimatic gradients.

title: Glycolysis-Dependent Fatty Acid Metabolism Supports Human Tfh Cell Function.
abstract: Follicular helper T (Tfh) cells orchestrate germinal center (GC) derived humoral immunity by providing essential help to B cells. Despite their key role in humoral immunity, the metabolic cues that shape Tfh cell differentiation and functions in humans remain poorly understood. Here, using a human ex vivo Tfh cell differentiation model, we investigated the metabolic requirements of Tfh cell development and function through targeted metabolic perturbation of glycolysis and fatty acid metabolism, transcriptomic analyses, and metabolic rescue experiments. Unexpectedly, early glycolytic inhibition enhanced Tfh cell differentiation but markedly impaired function, including reduced IL-21 production and diminished B-cell help. Transcriptomic and metabolic analyses revealed that glycolytic inhibition was accompanied by suppression of fatty acid metabolism. Consistently, independent inhibition of fatty acid synthesis or oxidation suppressed Tfh cell help functions, including IL-21 and IFN-γ production, as well as B-cell help potential. Interestingly, acetate supplementation partially restored IFN-γ secretion in glycolysis-inhibited conditions, but not IL-21, indicating limited metabolic compensation. Together, these findings reveal distinct metabolic requirements for Tfh cell differentiation and function and identify glycolysis-dependent fatty acid metabolism as an important determinant of human Tfh cell functional competence. This metabolic crosstalk provides new insight into the regulation of Tfh cells and Tfh-driven humoral immunity in vaccination and autoimmunity.

title: Unpacking the origins of among- and within-individual variation in pollen quantity and quality: implications for crop yield and breeding.
abstract: Enhancing crop yields depends on translating fundamental plant biology concepts into practical agricultural solutions - a critical challenge for global food security. Although breeding has historically prioritized yield and stability, the mechanisms underlying variation in key reproductive traits - particularly those determining male fitness - remain largely overlooked. Pollen quantity (grain number) and quality (the ability of a pollen grain to survive, germinate, and sire vigorous offspring) are central to yield and seed quality, yet their biological determinants are rarely integrated into breeding programs. Here, we present a conceptual framework showing how processes such as microspore development, plant aging, and resource allocation - shaped by genetic and environmental factors - generate predictable variation in pollen traits. Rather than reflecting stochastic noise, this variation emerges from coordinated developmental and physiological mechanisms acting across scales, from anther structure to whole-plant resource dynamics and aging. We argue that crop science must shift from a fragmented, gene-centered perspective - which relies on phenomenological statistical models such as quantitative trait loci mapping - toward a systemic approach that integrates genes with development, physiology, and the environment to understand variation in pollen quantity and quality. This shift will enable the implementation of targeted strategies to enhance crop yield through male function.

title: Genome‐Wide Identification of SNP Markers and Favourable Allelic Combinations Associated With Panicle Architecture Traits in a Subset of the 3K Rice Genome Panel ( Oryza sativa L.)
abstract: Rice ( Oryza sativa L.) is one of the most widely consumed cereal crops, serving as a staple food for billions of people worldwide. However, unpredictable climatic fluctuations and the continuous decline in cultivable land pose significant challenges to sustaining stable grain yields. As grain yield is a complex trait with low heritability, indirect selection through highly heritable yield‐component traits, particularly panicle architecture, offers a promising strategy to enhance rice productivity and contribute to global food security. In this study, 300 germplasm accessions selected from the 3K Rice Genome Panel were evaluated during Kharif 2023 for panicle length, panicle weight and number of grains per panicle using an alpha‐lattice design at Mandya and Gangavathi, Karnataka, India. Analysis of variance revealed substantial phenotypic variability for all evaluated traits. Phenotypic data integrated with genotypic information were subjected to genome‐wide association studies to identify genomic regions associated with panicle architecture traits. A total of 41 and 39 marker‐trait associations (MTAs) were identified using the FarmCPU and BLINK models, respectively. Nine MTAs were consistently detected across both models, three of which co‐localised with previously reported genes or QTL regions. Notably, 38 and 36 MTAs identified through FarmCPU and BLINK, respectively, represent potentially novel associations, highlighting key genomic regions for future validation and candidate‐gene discovery. Haplotype analysis of candidate genes revealed favourable allelic combinations associated with increased panicle length ( OsLP1 and OsGRRP ) and higher grain number per panicle ( Gn1a ). Furthermore, the significant SNPs identified in this study can be converted into breeder‐friendly KASP or CAPS markers following validation to facilitate marker‐assisted selection. Among the evaluated accessions, IRGC 647 (6.23 t/ha), IRGC 993 (6.13 t/ha) and IRGC 952 (6.02 t/ha) possessed putative favourable haplotypes across candidate genes for panicle architecture, representing valuable candidate donor lines for future functional validation and climate‐resilient rice breeding programmes.

title: SIK2 antagonizes postinfarction cardiac repair by driving macrophage proinflammatory and impairing efferocytosis
abstract: Macrophages play a key role in cardiac injury and repair after myocardial infarction (MI). Salt-inducible kinase 2 (SIK2), a member of the adenosine monophosphate–activated protein kinase family, is notably up-regulated in monocytes/macrophages of patients with MI and animal models. In this study, we investigated the role of SIK2 in macrophage-mediated inflammation and efferocytosis following MI. Macrophage-specific SIK2 deletion reduces infarct size and improves healing post-MI. Furthermore, SIK2-knockout macrophages decrease proinflammatory factor expression and enhance efferocytosis, thereby increasing repair factors expression. SIK2 associates with tumor necrosis factor receptor–associated factor 2 (TRAF2), promoting its phosphorylation and K63 polyubiquitylation, which exacerbates inflammation and hinders efferocytosis via the P38 and nuclear factor κB pathways. In contrast, the SIK2 T175A mutation exhibits no effect. Macrophage-specific SIK2 overexpression worsens cardiac changes after MI, whereas P38 inhibition reduces this effect. In addition, pharmacological inactivation of SIK2 substantially enhances cardiac repair after MI in mice. These findings highlight the crucial role of macrophage SIK2 in the regulation of inflammation and efferocytosis via TRAF2 polyubiquitination in MI, thereby presenting potential therapeutic targets.

title: Programmable and selective silencing of oncogenic fusion transcripts by CRISPR-Cas13b via breakpoint sequence recognition
abstract: Oncogenic gene fusions are key drivers of cancer, yet most remain undruggable by current therapies. Here, we establish CRISPR- Psp Cas13b as a personalizable platform for systematic silencing of various fusion transcripts. We reveal that recognition and cleavage of the breakpoint sequence by Psp Cas13b disrupt the fusion transcript, resulting in efficient protein depletion. Psp Cas13b cleavage produces aberrant, translation-incompetent target RNA species, a subset of which harbors internal deletions proximal to the cleavage site. We demonstrate that targeting the BCR::ABL1 breakpoint sequence efficiently degrades both wild-type and drug-resistant BCR::ABL1 mutants, which are the primary drivers of tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance and relapse in chronic myeloid leukemia. Molecular profiling revealed that Psp Cas13b impairs BCR::ABL1 tyrosine phosphokinase activity and triggers extensive transcriptomic and proteomic remodeling, leading to erythroid differentiation and apoptosis in drug-resistant cells. Beyond BCR::ABL1, personalized design of Psp Cas13b effectively silences other undruggable oncogenic fusions. Collectively, this study establishes a molecular framework for precise targeting of undruggable or drug-resistant oncogenic transcripts.

title: Cell-intrinsic steroidogenesis regulates mast cell function
abstract: Steroid hormones are well-known regulators of mast cell function, but whether mast cells themselves produce steroids de novo and influences their effector function has remained unknown. Here, we show that mast cells constitutively express the steroidogenic enzyme cytochrome P450 family 11 subfamily A member 1 (Cyp11a1) and produce pregnenolone. Cyp11a1 expression was detected across tissue-resident mast cells from multiple organs, was conserved in human mast cells, and was enhanced by interleukin-3 signaling and after activation. We identified Cyp11a1 as a Gata2-dependent, superenhancer-associated mast cell gene, placing steroidogenesis within the core mast cell transcriptional program. Loss of Cyp11a1 altered transcriptomic and proteomic programs in mast cells, with effects on pathways linked to cell growth, immune signaling, and effector function. Functionally, Cyp11a1-deficient mast cells showed increased degranulation in response to both immunoglobulin E (IgE)–dependent and IgE-independent stimulation. In vivo, loss of Cyp11a1 reduced mast cell abundance in several tissues but exacerbated passive cutaneous anaphylaxis. These findings identify cell-intrinsic steroidogenesis as a regulatory pathway that restrains mast cell activation and anaphylactic responses.

title: Chemogenetic ubiquitin E1 inhibitor TAK-243 CRISPR screen uncovers HAPSTR1/HUWE1 axis in chromatin proteostasis and cell cycle control
abstract: In this study, we sought to comprehensively map ubiquitin signaling networks at the crossroads of cellular proliferation and proteostasis, both crucial in cancer. Genome-wide CRISPR knockout screening in the presence of the ubiquitin E1 inhibitor TAK-243 identified 239 genes whose ablation sensitizes cells to ubiquitination blockade. Follow-up studies reveal a role for the nuclear protein, C16orf72/HECT, UBA, and WWE domain containing E3 ubiquitin protein ligase 1 (HUWE1)–Associated Protein modifying Stress Responses (HAPSTR1), in chromatin proteostasis and DNA replication. We show that HAPSTR1 recruits the E3 ligase HUWE1 to the chromatin, keeping the chromatin-associated proteome in check, and is itself turned over by HUWE1 during cell cycle progression. Structural modeling of the HAPSTR1/HUWE1 complex, supported by mutational analysis, demonstrates that loss of HUWE1 binding renders HAPSTR1 unable to support cellular proliferation when ubiquitin signaling is suppressed. Consequently, HAPSTR1 ablation impairs clearance of chromatin-associated proteins, triggering global transcriptional and proteostatic adaptations. Under diminished ubiquitin signaling, these adaptive mechanisms give way to replication stress and premature S phase entry, culminating in cell cycle collapse and DNA damage. Our findings uncover protein networks exhibiting synthetic lethality with ubiquitin signaling blockade and highlight vulnerabilities of actively proliferating cells to proteostatic imbalance at the chromatin.

title: Muscle stem cells produce a protective Fibrillin-1 matrix to prevent precocious activation
abstract: Diverse biological mechanisms regulate muscle stem cell quiescence, including inhibition of differentiation, adhesion, and translational control. Here, we identify the matrix glycoprotein Fibrillin-1 (FBN1) as a Notch-regulated, cell-autonomous effector, essential for maintaining quiescence. Known for its causal role in Marfan syndrome (MFS), our work positions FBN1 as a critical niche component that protects muscle stem cells from aberrant growth factor signaling. Targeted deletion of Fbn1 in muscle stem cells leads to dose-dependent quiescence defects, characterized by loss of cellular projections, depletion of the stem cell pool, and progressive decline in muscle function. Consistently, human MFS muscle biopsies show abnormally activated satellite cells, implicating stem cell imbalance in the development of MFS-associated myopathy. Mechanistically, the loss of FBN1 up-regulates transforming growth factor–β (TGFβ) signaling, and pharmacological blockade of TGFβ signaling rescues the cellular and physiological defects of FBN1-deficient muscle. These findings reveal a new quiescence-preserving mechanism through extracellular matrix–mediated shielding from mitogenic signals and position stem cell dysfunction as a driver of MFS myopathy.

title: Phosphorylation by CaMKIV regulates the transcriptional repressor activity and half-life of REST/NRSF
abstract: Repressor Element-1 (RE1)–Silencing Transcription Factor (REST) homeostatically regulates neural activity by repressing a large cluster of neural genes. However, whether REST can be regulated by calcium(2+) (Ca 2+ )–activated kinases is unknown. We investigated Ca 2+ /calmodulin-dependent protein kinases (CaMKs) as upstream regulators of REST fate and activity. We show that REST is phosphorylated by CaMKIV at Ser 322 site in the fifth-to-sixth Zn-finger domain linker. A phosphomimic mutant at Ser 322 decreased REST repressor activity and caused its transition to the cytosol, followed by degradation. Molecular dynamics simulations of the phosphomimic REST mutant revealed a sharp decrease in the stability of the REST-RE1 binding interface. Phosphorylation of REST by CaMKIV suppressed the downscaling of excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC) frequency in response to hyperactivity. Moreover, the homeostatic effects of CaMKIV on EPSC amplitude were inhibited in the absence of REST. The results demonstrate that CaMKIV phosphorylation plays a crucial role in regulating REST levels and repressor activity and that an interplay exists between CaMKIV and REST in homeostatic plasticity mechanisms.

title: Fibroblast-like synoviocytes exacerbate autoimmune arthritis upon psychological stress in an IL-6–dependent manner
abstract: Psychological stress affects the immune system and exacerbates autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but the mechanisms underlying tissue inflammation during remission remain unclear. Here, we show that tube restraint stress exacerbates joint inflammation in a murine arthritis model during remission. This exacerbation required interleukin-6 (IL-6) produced by brown adipose tissue (BAT) following sympathetic activation. Fibroblast-like synoviocytes expressing the IL-6 receptor subunit gp130 were critical mediators, as IL-6 stimulated these cells to produce the neutrophil chemoattractant CXCL1. Pharmacological blockade of the β3-adrenergic receptor significantly attenuated stress-induced arthritis flares. In patients with RA, carriers of the hypofunctional Trp64Arg variant of ADRB3 showed no positive correlation between psychological stress and disease activity, whereas noncarriers did. These findings identify a BAT–IL-6–fibroblast axis that reactivates inflammatory memory in arthritis and suggest that targeting stress-responsive pathways may provide a complementary therapeutic strategy alongside current RA treatments without broadly suppressing systemic immunity.

title: CellDiffusion: Enhancing scRNA-seq data integration with accurate inference of cell-cell association
abstract: Integrating single-cell transcriptomic datasets across laboratories, conditions, and technologies remains challenging because of cell type–specific batch effects and heterogeneous biological compositions. Current methods often fail to separate genuine biological variation from technical noise, misaligning distinct cell populations or leaving batch effects uncorrected. To address these challenges, we present CellDiffusion, an unsupervised graph-based model that propagates cellular features through a diffusion process to strengthen meaningful cell-cell associations in data integration. By learning a cell-cell attention network, CellDiffusion adaptively identifies corresponding populations across batches. Our approach applies cell-specific correction in data integration, generating cell embeddings that align cells across batches while preserving intrinsic cell types and developmental trajectories. We validate CellDiffusion across various datasets, including the human endometrium, one of the most dynamic and complex tissues featuring extensive cellular and molecular changes with the menstrual cycle. This framework also improves other essential analyses such as label transfer, clustering, and trajectory inference. CellDiffusion represents a powerful paradigm for accurate single-cell transcriptomic integrative analysis.

title: Practical continuous-variable quantum key distribution with squeezed light
abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) has gathered significant interest for its potential to achieve high secret key rates and seamless integration with existing optical communication infrastructure. State-of-the-art CV-QKD systems primarily use coherent states for simplicity. However, squeezed states of light have been theoretically shown to offer significant advantages, including higher secret key rates, greater resilience to excess noise, and reduced requirements on information reconciliation efficiency. In this work, we experimentally verify these theoretical predictions and propose and demonstrate a practical squeezed-state CV-QKD system based on modern local-local oscillator and digital signal processing techniques. Operating over fiber channels and considering finite-size security against collective attacks, we show the advantages of our system over its coherent-state counterpart. Our work paves the way for squeezed states to become practical resources for quantum key distribution and other quantum information protocols.

title: MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction contributes to neuronal hyperexcitability and depressive-like behaviors
abstract: Astrocyte pathology is increasingly recognized as a key factor in the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD), where disrupted glutamate clearance and impaired neuron-glia interactions contribute to synaptic dysfunction. However, the molecular mechanisms leading to astrocyte loss remain largely undefined. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of MDD, yet most studies have focused on neuronal mitochondria, leaving astrocytic mitochondrial dynamics insufficiently investigated. Here, we identify mitofusin-2 (MFN2)–associated astrocyte dysfunction in depression. SMART-seq profiling of hippocampal astrocytes from chronic social defeat stress (CSDS) mice revealed Mfn2 up-regulation, accompanied by excessive mitochondrial fusion, impaired mitophagy, and astrocyte loss. Elevated MFN2 expression was detected in plasma, postmortem brain tissue, and iPSC-derived astrocytes from patients with MDD. Astrocyte-specific knockdown of Mfn2 restored mitochondrial morphology and mitophagy, thereby preserving astrocyte viability and alleviating depressive-like behaviors. Using mass spectrometry–based label-free proteomics, in vivo calcium imaging, and functional assays, we demonstrated that β-arrestin2 deficiency reduced STAT1 stability, releasing its transcriptional repression on Mfn2 . Normalization of MFN2 expression through astrocytic Mfn2 knockdown or Stat1 overexpression reduced extracellular glutamate accumulation and prevented neuronal hyperexcitability in CSDS mice. Collectively, our findings define astrocytic MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction as a central pathological event in depressive behaviors, with the β-arrestin2–STAT1 pathway acting as an upstream regulatory mechanism. This work reveals an astrocytic pathway in depression and highlights a potential therapeutic target that directly addresses astrocyte pathology, beyond the neuron-centered focus of current antidepressant treatments.

title: Kinetic-driven microphase separation and vitrification of crowded hydrogels with associative bonds
abstract: The thermal response of stimuli-responsive hydrogels is typically viewed through thermodynamic equilibrium. However, in “crowded” networks with dense associative bonds, elasticity and diffusion kinetics dictate distinct nonequilibrium fates. We investigate thermal transitions of a PAAc-CaAc 2 (polyacrylic acid complexed with calcium ions) hydrogel along two trajectories: a quasi-static isobaric pathway (path A) and a rapid quasi-isochoric pathway (path B). Along path A, the gel contracts homogeneously until reaching a hardening temperature via global vitrification ( T hard ). In contrast, path B triggers confined microphase separation into polymer-dense and dilute phases at a critical temperature ( T dem ), followed by a hardening transition via localized vitrification ( T hard PS ). We demonstrate that T dem is governed by a mechanical-thermodynamic competition: The internal pressure ( P c ) to trigger demixing scales linearly with the permanent-network shear modulus ( G x ), maintaining a ratio of P c / G x ≈ 100. We identify T hard and T hard PS as distinct hardening points, with elastically constrained local water content governing T hard PS . This framework provides a strategy for programming nonequilibrium fates and “lockable” properties of responsive soft matter.

title: Observation of a supersolid phase in a spin-orbit coupled exciton-polariton Bose-Einstein condensate
abstract: In Bose-Einstein condensates, spin-orbit coupling (SOC) produces supersolidity. It is a peculiar state of matter, which, in addition to the superfluid behavior, shows periodic density modulation typical for crystals. Here, we report the fabrication of an original type of optical microcavity, allowing the achievement of room-temperature supersolidity for a quantum fluid of light. The microcavity is filled with a nematic liquid crystal (LC) and two layers of the organic polymer methyl-substituted ladder-type poly( p -phenylene) (MeLPPP) hosting exciton resonances. We demonstrate exciton-polariton condensation in the two distinct degenerate minima of the dispersion created by the LC-induced Rashba-Dresselhaus SOC. The condensate real-space distribution shows density stripes located randomly from one condensate realization to another despite the presence of a random disorder potential. This demonstrates the immunity of stripes against disorder and the spontaneous breaking of translational invariance. We also report the random appearance of vortices, another feature of superfluids.

title: Charge-mediated remote epitaxy of Ga 2 O 3 via MoS 2
abstract: Remote epitaxy of the corundum phase α-Ga 2 O 3 is demonstrated through a domain-free, transfer-free monolayer of MoS 2 template synthesized on sapphire. Despite the intrinsic nonidealities of MoS 2 —specifically its thickness and polar bonding characteristics—for remote epitaxy, single-crystalline α-Ga 2 O 3 films are epitaxially grown on polycrystalline MoS 2 with crystallographic fidelity comparable to those grown directly on bare sapphire. This observation substantiates that the substrate lattice potential can still be effectively transmitted through the MoS 2 layer, facilitating epitaxial registry at the growth front. The resulting α-Ga 2 O 3 films exhibit crystal quality and surface morphology on par with those grown directly on bare sapphire. Moreover, a centimeter-scale, crack-free α-Ga 2 O 3 membrane was successfully exfoliated using a Ni stressor, underscoring the mechanical compatibility and scalability of the remote epitaxial process. Structural disordering observed with more-than-bilayer MoS 2 further corroborates the remote epitaxy mechanism. First-principles calculations reveal that interfacial interactions between the bottom S atoms of MoS 2 and the Al atoms of sapphire induce spatially modulated charge distributions on the MoS 2 surface, creating energetically favorable adsorption sites for Ga species. Collectively, these findings establish a mechanistic framework for charge-mediated remote epitaxy across polar interfaces and expand the design space for heterogeneous integration of transferable wide bandgap Ga 2 O 3 membranes in next-generation power electronics and optoelectronic devices.

title: Transcriptional control of meiotic recombination by DREAM complex components
abstract: Meiotic chromosome segregation and recombination, essential for sexual reproduction and evolution, require a specialized gene set. Despite its importance, the transcriptional regulators that directly orchestrate meiotic gene expression remain unidentified in plants. We identify the MuvB core components known from the DREAM complex as key transcriptional regulators of meiotic recombination in Arabidopsis . Loss of DREAM components TCX5/6 and ALY1/2 leads to impaired recombination and fertility defects. Meiocyte-specific transcriptome profiling and genome-wide binding analyses reveal that core recombination genes, including the crossover-promoting helicase MER3, are direct targets. Consistently, MER3 overexpression partially rescues recombination defects in DREAM-compromised plants. These findings establish the DREAM complex components as important regulators of the meiotic program in plants. Given that DREAM dysfunction causes reproductive defects in animals, this regulatory role may be conserved across multicellular eukaryotes.

title: Magneto-mechano-electrochemical fiber for deformation-resilient and smart electronic textiles
abstract: Electronic textiles represent a transformative platform for integrating technology into daily wear, yet their development has been undermined by a fundamental challenge: the conflicting requirements between mechanical deformation for functionality and structural stability for performance. This challenge is particularly acute in cylindrical fiber electrodes, where inherent nonuniform electric field distribution leads to dendrite formation and poor active material utilization—problems that are further exacerbated by mechanical deformation. Here, we present a magneto-mechano-electrochemical architecture that addresses this challenge. Through magnetoelectrochemistry, magneto-mechano-electrochemical fiber promotes uniform electrochemical reactions, extending the battery lifespan by (374 ± 79)% and enhancing the capacity by (61 ± 20)% at a current density of 1.0 ampere per gram in the undeformed state. The magnetic field remains effective in regulating ion transport and stabilizing electrode structure under deformation. This deformation-resilient platform simultaneously enables energy harvesting from body motion and physiological monitoring through electromagnetic induction and magnetoelastic sensing, thereby transforming conventional textiles into deformation-resilient and smart health monitoring systems.

title: Mechanoadaptive nanowire viscoplastic composites with strain-enhanced conductivity for reprocessable bioelectronic interfaces
abstract: Bioelectronic interfaces must mechanically conform and adapt to biological tissues while maintaining stable electrical performance during motion and deformation. Existing soft conductors, however, often couple mechanical strain to electrical resistance, accumulate interfacial stress, and hinder reprocessing. Here, we report nanowire viscoplastic composites that combine silver nanowires with a dynamically crosslinked, short-chain polyborosiloxane matrix to produce emergent electromechanical behavior. The viscoplastic matrix permits deformation-induced nanowire reorganization, yielding high conductivity enhanced with strains. It also imparts fast stress relaxation, controllable yielding, and plastic conformability, enabling stress-free, mechanoadaptive contact with biological tissues. The material is self-healing, reconfigurable, and solvent-processable for recycling. It forms stable adhesion across porcine, rat, and human skin; accommodates hair regrowth; and exhibits excellent cytocompatibility and antibacterial function. As dry electrodes, these composites exhibit low impedance and resolve perilaryngeal muscle fatigue through high-resolution surface electromyography in humans. This work expands the materials design space for bioelectronic interfaces.

title: Suppression of meiotic double-strand break formation in somatic cells by DREAM factors TCX5/6 maintains genome stability
abstract: Meiotic recombination in reproductive cells is initiated by DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) and requires the expression of meiosis-specific genes, yet how the transcription of those genes is regulated in either meiotic or somatic cells remains unclear. Here, using a representative meiosis-specific DMC1 gene promoter as a bait, we identified two DREAM factors TCX5 and TCX6 required for direct repression of DMC1 in somatic cells. Transcriptomic analyses show broad ectopic up-regulation of meiotic genes in tcx5/6 leaves . Consistently, tcx5/6 somatic cells form DSBs and exhibit hypersensitivity to DNA damage compared to wild type. Further genetic analyses reveal that SPO11-1 is dispensable for ectopic meiotic gene activation but essential for the DNA damage response in tcx5/6 somatic cells. Last, we demonstrated that TCX5/6 repress meiotic gene expression through H3K4me3 modification. This finding uncovers an unexpected mechanism for suppressing meiotic recombination in somatic cells, thus preventing genetic diversity and genome instability in organisms.

title: Methyltransferase RsmB chaperones E. coli ribosome assembly by orchestrating the recruitment of ribosomal proteins
abstract: Ribosomal RNA modification enzymes increase cellular fitness, but it’s little known whether this benefit arises from rRNA modification or a chaperone function of the modification enzyme. Here, we show that E. coli methyltransferase RsmB chaperones the initial recruitment of ribosomal proteins to the 16S 3′ domain rRNA, a key step in assembly of the 30S subunit. Real-time single-molecule assembly experiments show that the RsmB product, 16S m 5 C967, has little effect on the rRNA affinity for ribosomal proteins. Instead, RsmB facilitates stable recruitment of primary protein uS7 during transcription while blocking the addition of secondary protein uS19. Completion of the methyltransferase cycle promotes RsmB release, allowing assembly to continue. Dimethyl sulfate footprinting of trapped RsmB-rRNA complexes revealed that RsmB restructures a critical rRNA helix junction. Our results illustrate how an RNA modification enzyme favors the proper sequence of protein addition by temporarily reshaping the energy landscape of co-transcriptional rRNA folding.

title: Substrate-bound structures of yeast ALA synthase reveal protein dynamics initiating heme biosynthesis
abstract: Heme is an essential prosthetic group involved in multiple biological processes in nearly all organisms. Heme biosynthesis is initiated by the pyridoxal 5′-phosphate–dependent enzyme aminolevulinic acid synthase (ALAS). Mutations in ALAS cause multiple hematological diseases. Despite sharing approximately 70% sequence similarity, ALAS homologs exhibit distinct expression and regulatory mechanisms. However, the molecular basis for their functional divergence remains poorly understood. Here, we used x-ray crystallography and molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate the structure and dynamics of Saccharomyces cerevisiae ALAS (scALAS) upon substrate binding. We identified critical conformational changes that occur during catalysis, regulating enzyme activity and protein-protein interactions specific to eukaryotic heme synthesis. Using evolution-guided engineering, we generated scALAS variants with altered catalytic activity and cellular metabolic profiles. Our findings reveal molecular and structural mechanisms underlying heme synthesis regulation and establish a framework for developing targeted therapeutics to treat heme-deficiency disorders and inform a rational design of next-generation therapeutic tools.

title: Breaking the tetrahedral constraint of tetracoordination: Square-planar [ICl 4 ] enables unprecedented birefringence in [C(NH 2 ) 3 ][ICl 4 ]
abstract: Birefringent crystals are indispensable for optoelectronic applications, yet commercially available crystals still suffer from the drawback of insufficient birefringence. Meanwhile, tetracoordination units—traditionally confined to a tetrahedral geometry—have long been sidelined from mainstream high-performance birefringent materials due to their intrinsic nearly negligible polarizability anisotropy. Herein, we break this tetrahedral constraint—demonstrating tetracoordinate square-planar [ICl 4 ] anions as a revolutionary platform for unprecedented birefringence. To achieve this, we report an improved synthesis method that avoids the use of toxic Cl 2 gas, enabling the preparation of [C(NH 2 ) 3 ][ICl 4 ] featuring square-planar [ICl 4 ] units. This compound displays a birefringence of 0.975@550 nm, setting a new record that surpasses all existing compounds containing tetracoordinate structural units. The giant birefringence of this material is attributed to the strong polarization anisotropy induced by the unique square-planar geometry of the [ICl 4 ] tetracoordinate units. This research provides theoretical guidance for designing high-performance polar materials based on tetracoordinate units in giant birefringent materials and promotes applications in related optoelectronic device.

title: PINK1-mediated mitophagy supports lung cancer initiation and limits the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapy
abstract: Mitophagy, the selective degradation of mitochondria by lysosomes, is a major mitochondrial quality-control pathway, yet its role in lung cancer initiation and therapeutic response remains poorly understood. We investigated PINK1-dependent mitophagy in human lung adenocarcinoma and directly monitored mitophagy in vivo using mito-QC reporter mice during lung tumor development. We found that PINK1 activity and mitophagy are increased in human tumors and are activated from the earliest stages of tumorigenesis. Genetic inhibition of PINK1 impaired oncogenic transformation but had little impact once tumor cells were established, identifying mitophagy as a critical early adaptation during lung cancer initiation. PINK1 deficiency markedly enhanced the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapy in vitro and in vivo. Together, our findings identify PINK1-dependent mitophagy as an early vulnerability in KRAS -driven lung cancer and provide a rationale for targeting mitophagy to improve the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapies.

title: Early Neolithic genomes suggest a local origin for millet farmers in East Asia
abstract: Millet cultivation in northern China served as a critical catalyst for Neolithic sedentism and East Asian civilization, yet the demographic origins of the inaugural millet farmers remain contentious. We analyze genome-wide data from seven individuals from the Donghulin (DHL), Dengcaogouliang, and Sitai sites, spanning 11,000 to 7300 years ago, and identify the DHL lineage as the predominant genetic structure in inland northern East Asia following the Last Glacial Maximum. Our results demonstrate profound genetic continuity from the Early Holocene through the intensification of millet agriculture, lending robust support to a model of local development rather than demic diffusion from external territories. Furthermore, we identify the earliest occurrence of the hypoxia-adaptive EGLN1 variant in a 9200-year-old DHL individual, suggesting that the physiological adaptations currently prevalent in Tibeto-Burman populations have deep Neolithic roots. Collectively, these findings necessitate a reevaluation of the early demographic and adaptive landscape of East Asia.

title: Therapeutic-scale CAR-NK microrobots with programmable swarm navigation for targeted solid tumor therapy
abstract: An urgent requirement in chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) immune cell therapy [e.g., CAR–natural killer (NK) cells] for solid tumors is to engineer the cells for precise tumor targeting. Meanwhile, medical microrobots can be navigated toward specific target sites using external magnetic fields. Here, by bridging these approaches, we turn CAR-NK cells into magnetic biohybrid microrobots (CAR-NK microrobots) that achieve controllable long-distance targeted navigation at therapeutic doses (∼10 6 cells) in both murine and nonhuman primate animal models in vivo. CAR-NK microrobots are developed through genetic engineering with CAR structures and loading with magnetic nanoparticles for field-based navigation. Different magnetic field inputs reconfigure their swarms between vortex and ribbon modes, allowing dense aggregation for targeted navigation and further broad dispersion for large-area coverage. Using programmable magnetic fields, in vivo CAR-NK microrobot–based therapy is demonstrated for metastatic leptomeningeal carcinomatosis in brain’s cerebrospinal fluid space. After intrathecal injection, the microrobots are magnetically guided long distance through the spinal canal toward the brain in vortex mode and subsequently spread over the target site in ribbon mode, as visualized by real-time angiographic imaging in a nonhuman primate model, providing a proof-of-feasibility demonstration in a nonhuman primate anatomical setting.

title: Death and chemotaxis: Bacterial chemotaxis enables collective escape from phage predation
abstract: Bacteriophages (“phage”) are viruses that prey on bacteria in diverse environments, from biological tissues to soils. In many of these environments, bacterial hosts are constantly migrating, yet how bacterial migration is influenced by phage predation remains poorly understood. Using transparent granular hydrogels that mimic natural habitats, we directly visualize populations of motile Escherichia coli encountering lytic T4 phage. Unexpectedly, we find that even in phage-rich environments, bacteria successfully form chemotactic fronts that enable them to migrate over large distances without necessarily requiring new phage resistance mutations. At low phage concentrations, the front is indistinguishable from a phage-free control, and the population remains largely susceptible; at higher concentrations, the susceptible population initially collapses, and the front is reestablished by a less susceptible subpopulation enriched under intense predation. Higher phage concentrations delay front formation but not steady-state front speed or shape. By combining our experiments with biophysical modeling, we demonstrate that this phenomenon reflects a competition between collective chemotactic migration and phage predation, quantified by a dimensionless “escape parameter,” in which sufficiently rapid migration allows the population to outpace the spreading infection. This work thus provides mechanistic insight into how cell motility shapes phage-bacteria interactions in spatially extended environments.
