title: Mapping rainfed cereals and olive groves using Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and topographic data in northern Morocco
abstract: Accurate discrimination of agricultural crop categories in heterogeneous, rainfed landscapes remains challenging because crop spectral responses are strongly influenced by environmental variability and complex terrain. This study assessed the contribution of optical (Sentinel-2), radar (Sentinel-1), and topographic variables to the binary discrimination of annual rainfed cereals and perennial olive groves in the Tangier–Tétouan–Al Hoceima region of northern Morocco, a Mediterranean mountain environment characterized by fragmented agricultural systems and rainfed conditions. Using a Random Forest classifier, 38 candidate feature sets were evaluated, representing different combinations of Sentinel-2 spectral bands and vegetation indices, Sentinel-1 radar features, phenological information, and topographic variables to discriminate cereals and olive groves. The results showed that Sentinel-2 variables provided the strongest discriminative power, while Sentinel-1 variables alone yielded comparatively lower performance. The best-performing scenario combined Sentinel-2 spectral bands, Sentinel-1 VV and VH backscatter, Normalized Difference Red Edge Index 2 (NDRE2), Sentinel-1 VV/VH backscatter ratio (RATIO), and topographic variables (elevation, slope, and aspect), reaching an overall accuracy of 0.96 with balanced F1-scores for cereals and olives (0.92 and 0.91, respectively). Sentinel-2-only configurations already achieved high accuracies, particularly when spectral bands were combined with red-edge indices and topographic variables, whereas the addition of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data produced modest but consistent improvements in classification accuracy. SHAP-based interpretation revealed a hierarchical contribution of predictors, with elevation and slope emerging as the most influential variables, followed by NDRE2 and key spectral bands. These findings indicate that the discrimination between rainfed cereals and olive groves in this rainfed landscape is strongly influenced by topographic and environmental gradients, while spectral variables capture vegetation biophysical properties and SAR contributes complementary structural and moisture-related information. Overall, the study demonstrates that accurate mapping of rainfed cereals and olive groves in heterogeneous Mediterranean agro-ecosystems benefits from the integration of spectral, structural, and topographic information. The proposed framework provides a useful foundation for extending crop mapping and agricultural monitoring approaches in data-scarce and climate-sensitive regions.

title: Extreme temperature, digital rural development, and grain production resilience in the Yellow River Basin
abstract: Severe temperature extremes are an increasingly dangerous threat to the resilience of grain production and sustainable food systems, particularly in climate-sensitive river basins and large-scale grain producers. Though previous literature has considered the impact of climate change on crop yield and agricultural efficiency, there has been limited consideration of how extreme temperature events influence the multidimensional resilience of grain production systems and if digital rural development could enhance adaptive capacity. The present study explores the association between extreme temperature events and resilience of the grain production in the Yellow River Basin, an important grain-producing area of strategic significance with high climate sensitivity and ecological vulnerability, in China. On panel data of nine provinces from 2013 to 2022, we develop a grain production resilience index using resistance, recovery capacity, and transformation capacity and implement a two-way fixed-effect model, robustness test, endogeneity test, heterogeneity analysis, and a moderating effect model. As shown by the results, extreme temperature events have a significant negative relationship with grain production resilience, and this result holds even when special samples are excluded and the estimation model is replaced, additional control variables are added, and the variables are transformed. Analysis of heterogeneity shows that the negative correlation is more evident in non-major grain-producing areas and agricultural low-consumption areas, suggesting that infrastructure conditions, economic capacity, and regional support systems may be associated with vulnerability of agricultural production to climate shocks. The results of the moderating effect provide suggestive evidence that digital rural development may play a positive moderating role in the relationship between extreme temperature events and grain production resilience, which suggests that digital infrastructure, information services, and digital finance might be useful in mitigating climate-related production risks. These findings are valuable in the context of research on sustainable food systems as they connect the issues of climate adaptation, agricultural resilience, food security governance, and digital agriculture, and provide evidence that is policy relevant to improving the resilience of grain production in other climate-sensitive river basins and grain-producing regions.

title: Association between digital agricultural technology promotion and farmers’ adoption of extreme climate adaptation technologies: evidence from chili pepper farmers in Guizhou Province, China
abstract: Adaptation technologies are important for reducing the risks associated with extreme climatic events, particularly in mountainous areas where complex topography can increase agricultural vulnerability. Digital Agricultural Technology Promotion (DATP) provides an increasingly important channel through which farmers access information related to climate adaptation technologies. However, empirical evidence on the association between DATP and farmers’ adoption of such technologies in mountainous areas remains limited. Using survey data from 846 chili pepper farmers in Guizhou Province, China, this study employs baseline regression, mediation analysis, moderation analysis, and heterogeneity analysis to examine the association between DATP and farmers’ adoption of extreme climate adaptation technologies. The results show that DATP is significantly and positively associated with both adoption degree and sustained adoption willingness. Mediation analysis identifies three potential pathways consistent with this association: broader information access channels, greater information trust, and stronger information application ability. Moderation analysis further shows that benefit and risk expectation confirmation significantly condition the association between DATP and adaptation behavior. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the positive association is strongest for water resource management and biological control technologies and is relatively stronger among pure farmers, farmers with higher digital literacy, and large-scale chili farmers. These findings highlight the relevance of information access, information credibility, digital capabilities, and farmer heterogeneity in understanding digital approaches to climate adaptation in mountainous agricultural areas. The findings provide empirical evidence for developing differentiated digital strategies to support farmers’ climate adaptation.

title: Crop diversification as a climate-smart agriculture strategy and household welfare in Nigeria: evidence from living standard measurement survey
abstract: Crop diversification is a climate-smart agriculture (CSA) practice with well-documented yield and agroecological benefits, but rigorous, nationally representative evidence on its welfare impacts in Nigeria remains scarce. This study examined the determinants and welfare effects of crop diversification adoption among 3,229 farm households, using the fourth wave of Nigeria’s Living Standard Measurement Study – Integrated Surveys on Agriculture (LSMS-ISA). A probit model identified the determinants of adoption, and an endogenous switching regression (ESR) model, which corrects for selection bias arising from observed and unobserved heterogeneity, estimated the causal impact of adoption on household per capita consumption expenditure and dietary diversity. About 1,846 households (57%) adopted crop diversification. Household size, farm size, age of household head, distance to road, fertilizer use, and temperature exposure significantly increased the probability of adoption, while education, distance to market, access to finance, and rainfall shock significantly reduced it. Adoption increased per capita consumption expenditure by an average treatment effect of 0.72 log points and household dietary diversity scores by 2.03 points among adopters, effects that are large relative to national poverty and dietary diversity benchmarks. These results indicate that limited market access, credit products tied to specialized cropping, and climate shocks jointly suppress adoption. Government agricultural and nutrition agencies should jointly fund a targeted program that redesigns credit products to support diversified cropping, pairs rural road investment with market access, and bundles diversification advice with climate information and weather-index insurance in drought-prone areas.

title: Deep Learning-Assisted Thermography-Derived Crop Water Stress Index for Drought Stress Detection in Potato Plants
abstract: This study investigated the feasibility of using thermography-derived crop water stress index (CWSI) images combined with deep learning for irrigation-level identification in potato plants as a proof of concept. Potato plants (Solanum tuberosum L. cv. Sumi) were cultivated under greenhouse conditions and subjected to six irrigation regimes (i20, i33, i46, i60, i80, and i100) based on soil field capacity. Thermal images were acquired over four imaging weeks from late April to early May 2024. CWSI images were generated from the microclimate conditions and subsequently used for image-based classification. A lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) consisting of four convolutional layers was developed, and a convolutional block attention module (CBAM) was further incorporated as an attention-based comparison model. The classification performance varied across imaging weeks and model architectures. Across repeated runs, the baseline CNN achieved better overall performance than CNN-CBAM, with ACC, PRE, REC, and F1S values ranging from 0.569 to 0.781, 0.534 to 0.828, 0.570 to 0.781, and 0.523 to 0.770, respectively. These results indicate that the incorporation of CBAM did not provide a consistent performance advantage under the current dataset and training conditions. Feature visualisation using t-distributed stochastic neighbour embedding (t-SNE) further showed the distribution of CNN- and CNN-CBAM-extracted features across irrigation levels, while local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME) indicated that model-relevant regions for lower irrigation treatments were frequently located around the canopy margins. Overall, this study provides a proof-of-concept demonstration that thermography-derived CWSI images combined with a lightweight CNN can support rapid, non-contact irrigation-level identification in potato plants, while also highlighting current limitations and future directions for more robust field application. Future studies should validate the method using larger datasets collected across different cultivars, seasons, greenhouse and field environments, and independent plant- or plot-level biological replicates.

title: Pitahaya (Hylocereus spp.) as an Emerging High-Value Crop: Advances in Production, Bioactive Compounds, Postharvest Technologies and Innovation
abstract: Pitahaya (Hylocereus spp.), commonly known as dragon fruit, has attracted increasing attention as a high-value crop because of its nutritional attributes, environmental adaptability, and growing market demand. However, existing reviews typically address individual topics—such as nutrition, cultivation, postharvest management, or sustainability—without integrating these aspects across the production cycle. This fragmentation hinders a comprehensive understanding of how propagation methods, agronomic and reproductive management, and cultivation conditions influence fruit quality and postharvest performance. This review synthesizes scientific and technological evidence on propagation, cultivation systems, agronomic management, nutritional composition, fruit quality, postharvest technologies, by-product valorization, sustainability, and innovation. Scientific publications and patents published between January 2019 and March 2026 were analyzed. An initial search identified approximately 170 scientific records and 2000 patent records; after screening, 105 scientific publications and 96 patents were included in the review. The evidence indicates advances in vegetative propagation, greenhouse and soilless cultivation, nutrient and environmental management, characterization of bioactive compounds, postharvest preservation, and by-product valorization. Patent activity also reflects technological developments in protected cultivation, structural support systems, and digital agriculture. Nevertheless, commercial-scale validation, standardized crop-specific management protocols, quantitative comparisons among production systems, and effective technology transfer remain limited.

title: View-Conditional Representation Concentration in AI-Generated Anime Character Images: A Multi-Encoder Study of Civitai
abstract: Assessments of visual homogenization in generative AI image communities may depend on the image view, visual encoder, and preprocessing procedure. This study develops a view-conditional representation concentration (VCRC) framework and applies it to a frozen Civitai collection comprising 1099 full images and 1096 face-cropped views. DINOv2 embeddings were evaluated using the Vendi ratio, mean pairwise cosine similarity, and average 10-nearest-neighbor similarity, with regional, resolution, and padding sensitivity analyses. Face-cropped views showed a lower Vendi ratio than full images (0.019120 vs. 0.024360) and higher mean pairwise similarity (0.490709 vs. 0.438244). The DINOv2 concentration effect remained positive in the 1088-image audited paired sample under the tested padding and resolution controls and in a 176-image subset whose crops met the primary-face coverage criterion under two independent annotations. In the full audited sample, OpenCLIP and ConvNeXt showed the same effect direction, whereas MAE showed the opposite direction; the magnitude of the MAE contrast was strongly affected by padding. In a separate 205-image annotation audit, the crop contained at least 90% of the primary face in 86.3–87.8% of images, depending on the annotator. Platform tags were not verified against generation prompts, and a matched hand-drawn baseline was unavailable. VCRC therefore provides a reproducible, encoder-aware framework for characterizing view-dependent representation concentration and testing its sensitivity to image processing. Future work should assess its transfer across platforms, generative models, and matched non-generated image collections.

title: A Simple Empirical Method for Estimating Extreme Air Velocities from CFD Mean-Flow Statistics: Validation Using ISS Columbus and CASA Ventilation Data
abstract: Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations based on Reynolds-Averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) models are widely used for spacecraft cabin ventilation design; however, they primarily provide mean-flow quantities and often underestimate velocity extremes relevant to crew comfort, ventilation effectiveness, and stagnation-zone assessment. This study presents a simple empirical post-processing framework for estimating extreme air velocities from CFD mean-flow statistics. The proposed approach expresses the upper velocity envelope as a function of the local mean velocity and standard deviation through a single empirical coefficient, Kc. Throughout this study, the upper velocity envelope is defined consistently as the 99th percentile of the velocity magnitude distribution, denoted p99, and the empirical peak factor is accordingly defined as Kc,p99 = (p99 − μ)/σ. This definition is applied uniformly to the calibration dataset and to all external validation datasets, so that the same target variable is used at every stage of the analysis. The method is calibrated using published velocity-field data from International Space Station (ISS) Crew Quarters studies and subsequently examined against independent ISS ventilation datasets, including the Columbus module and Crew Alternative Sleeping Area (CASA) configurations. Analysis of digitized experimental and CFD-derived velocity distributions yields a robust median coefficient of approximately Kc = 4.5, while external datasets indicate p99-equivalent values generally within the range Kc ≈ 4–6. Independent validation evidence from Columbus ventilation studies demonstrates that accounting for velocity fluctuations substantially improves agreement with experimental observations, reducing distribution mismatch by approximately 83% compared with uncorrected mean-velocity predictions. The external comparison should be understood as a retrospective consistency check rather than a prospective prediction: the peak factors reported for the Columbus and CASA datasets were derived from the same distributions against which they are compared, and they therefore describe the data rather than forecast it. Accordingly, the proposed framework is presented as an exploratory upper-envelope indicator whose transferability is suggested, but not yet demonstrated, by the observed clustering of independently derived peak factors. The results suggest that a simple statistical correction applied to standard CFD outputs can provide practical estimates of extreme ventilation velocities without the computational cost of Large Eddy Simulation (LES). While the proposed framework should be regarded as an exploratory upper-envelope indicator rather than a universal turbulence closure, and while it does not by itself provide a conservative bound or identify stagnation risk, the consistency observed across multiple ISS ventilation datasets indicates that it offers a useful preliminary screening tool for spacecraft cabin ventilation assessment and design.

title: A Controlled Comparison of U-Net Variants for Surgical Instrument Segmentation in Minimally Invasive Surgery
abstract: Background: Surgical instrument segmentation is a relevant computer vision task in minimally invasive surgery, where binary masks can be used to separate surgical instruments from the background. This study compares selected U-Net architectural configurations for binary surgical instrument segmentation on the EndoVis 2020 dataset. Methods: The input images were cropped to 538×701 pixels and paired with binary segmentation masks. To reduce memory usage, the models used an internal resizing step to process images at 256×256 resolution, while predictions were resized back to the original image size for evaluation. Several U-Net variants were implemented and trained under the same conditions, including changes in network depth, filter configuration, kernel size, and pooling strategy. Results: The baseline U-Net achieved an IoU of 0.97 and a Dice score of 0.98. Among the successfully trained configurations, the increased-depth variant achieved the highest numerical Dice score, with an IoU of 0.97 and a Dice score of 0.99. The increased-pooling and reduced-depth variants produced lower IoU and Dice scores within the present experimental setup, while the variable-kernel configuration produced results close to those of the baseline model. The increased-filter and reversed-filter configurations did not produce valid segmentation outputs under the common training protocol. Conclusions: Within the present experimental setting, the extended-depth configuration achieved the highest numerical Dice score among the successfully trained variants. The results are interpreted as a controlled comparison of U-Net configurations for binary surgical instrument segmentation rather than as evidence of general architectural superiority. Because the evaluation used a frame-level split, frames originating from the same surgical recording may occur in different subsets. Although the two-dimensional models process each frame independently without temporal or sequence-level inputs, complete sequence-level statistical independence is not guaranteed. The reported differences should therefore be interpreted within the applied experimental protocol. Future work will include sequence-level evaluation, repeated experiments, and testing on additional datasets.

title: Characteristics of Partial Discharge of Typical Defects in Converter Transformer Under Operation
abstract: Converter transformers, operating in complex electric fields for extended periods, are prone to insulation degradation. To investigate partial discharge (PD) characteristics caused by internal insulation deterioration, this study developed an AC/DC PD simulation platform replicating real-world operating conditions. Four typical insulation defects—turn-to-turn, spacer block, electrostatic ring, and tap changer—were modeled, with experiments conducted in a 35 kV transformer tank using pure AC and composite AC/DC voltages (1:1, 1:3, 1:5, 1:7 ratios). The 48 Phase-Resolved Partial Discharge (PRPD) spectra were processed through image cropping, grayscale conversion, and dimension standardization, with 84% training and 16% testing datasets. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) achieved an overall classification accuracy of 93.7% on the test set. Field validation using ±400 kV real-world converters confirmed the network’s precision in PD pattern recognition, providing technical support for insulation condition diagnosis and fault prediction in converter transformers.

title: Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks for Daily Apparel Retail Demand Forecasting: A Comparative Evaluation Across Forecasting Models
abstract: Operational apparel forecasting requires comparisons that combine strong classical baselines, modern learning architectures, sensitivity analysis, and evaluation across multiple forecast origins. This study benchmarks nine methods for one-step-ahead daily forecasting using 1403 observations of a retailer-defined potential-sales measure from 11 apparel categories in Türkiye. The methods are seasonal naïve (SNaive), exponential smoothing (ETS), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), feedforward neural network (FFNN), standard Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN), long short-term memory (LSTM), Transformer, TimeKAN, and iTransformer, all evaluated under a lag-only information setting. Evaluation combines a 183-day test window, a five-method joint-versus-per-category ablation, fixed-configuration look-back sensitivity, and seven rolling-origin windows. ETS achieved the lowest macro weighted absolute percentage error (WAPE; 12.02%) and mean absolute scaled error (MASE; 0.690) on the test window, while iTransformer and TimeKAN were the strongest learning-based alternatives. Across rolling origins, iTransformer achieved the lowest mean macro WAPE, whereas ETS led five of seven windows and achieved the lowest mean pooled WAPE and macro MASE. Standard KAN showed intermediate performance, while TimeKAN and iTransformer improved with longer look-back windows under fixed configurations. Per-category configurations yielded lower WAPE and MASE values than matched joint configurations in the five-method ablation. Overall, rankings depended on forecast origin, error aggregation, historical context, and information-sharing design.

title: Comparative Pangenomics of the MATE Family Reveals Gene Content Variation and Identifies a Citrate-Transporter-Proximal Candidate Group in Vaccinium
abstract: Plant multidrug and toxic compound extrusion (MATE) transporters participate in citrate transport, aluminium detoxification, and mineral homeostasis, yet their diversity and genomic organisation in Vaccinium remain poorly understood. In this study, we compared the MATE family across 34 blueberry and cranberry genomes and examined a candidate group related to experimentally characterised citrate transporters. The high-confidence family set contained 3479 proteins, and new MATE orthogroups continued to be detected as blueberry genomes were added. Genome searches showed that incomplete or non-standard annotations explained some of the apparent absences: four of the 12 tested orthogroups changed their prevalence category after gene-model reconstruction. In contrast, the candidate group was represented by 66 genome-supported loci, with at least one detected in each crop assembly. These loci were largely dispersed, often retained a similar neighbouring-gene order, and formed eight direct collinear links across six chromosome-scale Vaccinium genomes. A codon model estimated a global dN/dS of 0.876, which did not differ significantly from one. Comparisons of 2 kb upstream regions revealed sequence differences among the assemblies, while two public root transcriptomes showed increased expression assigned to CUFF.34706 at pH 6.5 in ‘Emerald’ and ‘Reka’. Interaction tests did not establish genotype-specific pH responses. Together, these results distinguish variable MATE gene content from a consistently detected candidate group and identify sequences for further studies of transport and regulation.

title: Detection of Eulecanium giganteum Infestation in Jujube Orchards Based on UAV Multispectral Remote Sensing
abstract: The application of remote sensing technology to monitor agricultural pests and diseases provides an effective approach for rapid and non-destructive assessment of crop health. This study evaluated a UAV multispectral remote sensing framework integrating vegetation indices and SPAD information for assessing Eulecanium giganteum infestation in jujube orchards. Initially, 24 vegetation indices were extracted from canopy multispectral imagery, and Pearson correlation analysis was used for feature screening, resulting in a refined subset of 19 vegetation indices. Seven machine learning algorithms were evaluated during model development, with Grid Search combined with tree-level grouped 7-fold cross-validation for hyperparameter selection. Vegetation indices were used as predictor variables, while SPAD value and infestation severity were treated as response variables in the regression and classification tasks, respectively. During internal model development, the CatBoost-19opt model achieved an R2 of 0.81 and an RMSE of 1.84 for SPAD estimation. On the independent test set consisting of 58 jujube trees, the previously selected model achieved an R2 of 0.84 and an RMSE of 1.56. During internal model development, incorporating measured SPAD values improved pest classification performance, with XGBoost-19sopt achieving an OA of 0.89 and a Kappa coefficient of 0.84. On the independent test set, the measured-SPAD configuration achieved an OA of 0.88, whereas both the VI-only and VI combined with predicted-SPAD configurations achieved an OA of 0.71. Thus, incorporating predicted SPAD did not improve overall classification accuracy relative to using vegetation indices alone. Further model optimization and additional validation across different orchards, growing seasons, and phenological stages are required before the approach can be considered for operational large-scale monitoring.

title: Enhancing Lettuce Seed by Pelleting and Packaging Techniques
abstract: This study developed a seed pelleting method using natural and bio-based materials and an effective post-pelleting storage strategy to improve the performance of small-sized seeds with limited internal nutrient reserves. Lettuce (Lactuca sativa L.) was used as a model crop. Organic filler materials consisting of diatomaceous earth (DE) combined with bat granular (DE+BG) and DE combined with solid vermicompost (DE+SVC) were evaluated. Furthermore, binding solutions were prepared from gum arabic supplemented with Streptomyces sp. crude extract at 0, 5, 50, and 500 ppm. Non-pelleted seeds were the control. The optimal natural- and bio-based pelleting formulation was subsequently stored with activated clay as a moisture-adsorbing material under ambient and cold conditions for 6 months. Results found that the DE+BG contained higher macronutrient levels (N 2.7%, P2O5 1.4%, K2O 1.0%) than DE+SVC and significantly improved shoot growth under both laboratory and greenhouse conditions without affecting germination. The binders combined with the 500 ppm crude extract significantly enhanced seedling vigor, photosynthetic performance, phytochemicals, and increased biomass accumulation (p < 0.05) in the plant. Importantly, packaging the seed pelleted with activated clay and storing it under cold conditions effectively maintains seed germination and seedling performance during storage. These findings demonstrate a novel integrated natural- and bio-based pelleting and storage approach that enhances early seedling growth and preserves seed quality during storage.

title: Temporal Shifts in Fish Landing Composition, Stock Status, and Diversity in Lake Volvi, Greece: A Six-Decade Analysis (1961–2024)
abstract: Long-term fishery records are essential for detecting ecological change in data-limited freshwater systems. We analyzed 64 years (1961–2024) of commercial landings for ten fish categories from Lake Volvi, Greece, combining temporal, multivariate, forecasting and catch-only approaches. Total landings fell 89.8%, from 620 t in 1962 to 63.3 t in 2024. Six categories declined significantly after autocorrelation correction, whereas Gibel carp increased; excluding a documented reporting discontinuity left the decline and all diversity trends unchanged. Changepoints in landings (~1971, ~1978, ~2002) did not coincide with a compositional boundary at 1990/1991, so production decline and reorganization were not synchronous. Composition differed strongly among three a priori periods (PERMANOVA R2 = 0.656, p = 0.001), reflecting a shift from native dominants to a low-production assemblage increasingly influenced by non-native Gibel carp; diversity increased while recorded richness showed no trend. Eight series yielded viable catch-only fits. Estimated terminal biomass lay below one-fifth of BMSY for six, irrespective of terminal year, whereas exploitation ratios were strongly terminal-year dependent: five of eight changed Kobe quadrant between 2022 and 2024, owing to carried-forward values in the final two years. Severe depletion of the native taxa is therefore the robust stock-status finding; single-year exploitation classifications remain conditional on terminal year.

title: Plastic Energy Density-Based Time-Dependent Seismic Performance Evaluation for Underground Structures
abstract: Large underground structures such as subway stations are critical components of urban lifeline systems, but their seismic deformation and damage mechanisms remain not fully understood. This paper investigates the seismic response and damage mechanism of a typical two-story three-span underground frame structure in soft soil using three-dimensional nonlinear finite element analysis. The deformation transmission between the structure and surrounding soil is examined, the frequency response characteristics of the soil-structure system are revealed, and the energy dissipation and damage evolution are systematically analyzed. The results show that the predominant frequency of structural relative displacement is governed by both the free-field site and the structure itself. Soil deformation imposes forced displacement on the structure and suppresses its natural vibration. Seismic input energy is mainly dissipated by damping and plastic strain energy, with central columns and slabs as the primary plastic energy-dissipating components. The most severe damage occurs at the base of the lower columns. A plastic energy density-based damage index is proposed, which offers a supplementary perspective for time-dependent cumulative damage assessment of underground structures.

title: Assessment of Cropland Abandonment and Vegetation Recovery on the Chinese Loess Plateau
abstract: Cropland abandonment alters agricultural land use and may enable improvements in vegetation cover. On the Chinese Loess Plateau, the extent and spatial variation of these changes remain critical questions for land management. This study used annual land-cover trajectories to identify persistent cropland withdrawal from 2000 to 2020 and Landsat-derived fractional vegetation cover (FVC) to assess vegetation change. The total first-abandonment area was 80,700.64 km2, and the annual area of first abandonment peaked in 2004 at 7176.16 km2 and subsequently declined amid interannual fluctuations, with abandoned cropland concentrated on gentle slopes. Across five representative years, the mean FVC of land classified as abandoned each year rose from 0.273 in 2000 to 0.381 in 2020. These values reflect changes in pixel populations rather than the trajectory of a fixed set of fields. Among pixels mapped as abandoned in 2020, 86.07% showed increasing FVC over the entire study period, including 60.12% with significant increases. Extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) analysis with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) identified precipitation as the strongest predictor of spatial variation in the FVC change rate, accounting for 39.6% of the model’s relative importance. SHAP dependence patterns showed model-based transition points at approximately 395 mm of precipitation and 10 °C of temperature. These findings characterize vegetation-cover change associated with abandoned land and its environmental variation, whereas the full-period trends cannot isolate vegetation change caused by abandonment.

title: Classification and Remote Sensing Characterization of Large Catastrophic Landslides in the Southeastern Tibetan Plateau, China
abstract: Large catastrophic landslides in the southeastern Tibetan Plateau are characterized by huge volumes and complex chains that frequently cause river damming and casualties. Based on field surveys, multi-temporal satellite imagery, Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV), Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) deformation measurements, and meteorological and seismic records, this study classifies these landslides into three types by their initiation and disaster-chain processes: (1) rock–ice avalanche → debris flow → landslide dam; (2) debris flow → landslide dam; (3) rock avalanche → landslide dam. Representative cases illustrate the material sources, initiation settings, and downstream impacts of each type. The occurrence of such landslides is influenced by the interplay of four groups of factors: fractured rock masses and abundant loose deposits provide the material basis; high mountains and narrow river valleys provide the spatial framework for landslide evolution and promote river blockage; pronounced climatic changes provide the background conditions and may affect slope stability in glaciated areas through glacier retreat; and frequent strong earthquakes can both instantaneously trigger failure and cause cumulative damage that predisposes slopes to subsequent failures. Ongoing climate warming and repeated seismic activity are expected to increase landslide susceptibility, highlighting the urgency of multi-hazard early warning and proactive mitigation. This study supports early warning prioritization and risk governance in high-mountain valleys across the Tibetan Plateau.

title: CAP-DBNet: A Class-Adaptive Prototype-Guided Dual-Branch Collaborative Network for Remote Sensing Image Semantic Segmentation
abstract: High-resolution remote sensing image semantic segmentation faces challenges from large-scale variation, fine boundary preservation, and class imbalance. This paper proposes CAP-DBNet, a compact framework that combines a RepViT M2.3 backbone with a global–local collaborative decoder (GLCD), a class-adaptive hybrid loss (CAHL), and a class-adaptive prototype-guided calibration module (CAPC). CAP-DBNet integrates class-center global and window-local modeling through bidirectional feature exchange, mini-batch class-frequency-aware supervision, and prototype-based residual calibration. Rather than introducing an isolated new attention or prototype mechanism, this work focuses on the coordinated design of these components within an efficient segmentation framework. In five repeated experiments with different random seeds, CAP-DBNet achieves average mIoUs of 85.16%, 88.32%, and 55.75% on Vaihingen, Potsdam, and LoveDA, respectively, improving over the same-backbone LOGCAN++ baseline by 1.43, 1.24, and 1.44 percentage points. Compared with D2LS under our evaluation protocol, CAP-DBNet uses 3.55× fewer parameters and requires 8.35× fewer floating-point operations (FLOPs). These results demonstrate an accuracy-efficiency-oriented global–local and class-adaptive framework for remote sensing semantic segmentation across three public benchmarks.

title: Adaptive LiDAR–Inertial–GNSS SLAM Framework for Georeferenced Mapping in Challenging Urban Environments
abstract: Maintaining accurate, georeferenced dense maps requires reliable global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) observations to constrain global drift. Degraded observations must be prevented from distorting trajectories and local maps as reception transitions from open sky to urban obstruction and complete signal denial indoors. This study develops and evaluates Dense LiDAR–Inertial–GNSS simultaneous localization and mapping (DLIG-SLAM) to adapt GNSS integration and local mapping as reception conditions change. Built on Dense Multi-Scan Adjustment, the framework estimates the local trajectory and dense map separately from the transformation that connects them to a global coordinate frame. GNSS observations are assessed separately for updating this transformation and correcting the estimator. An online switcher selects among integration strategies according to measurement reliability, estimator readiness, and trajectory consistency. Outdoor–indoor state changes reconfigure local mapping, while voxel size adapts to the observed scan point population. Evaluation was performed on four KITTI driving sequences and an urban canyon outdoor–indoor mission in Toronto, recorded with standalone single-point positioning GNSS. GNSS coupling through an inertial navigation estimate achieved the lowest three-dimensional trajectory root mean square error on three of the four KITTI sequences. Online switching did not consistently outperform fixed integration strategies in the KITTI trajectory evaluation. In the Toronto dataset, inertial navigation-mediated coupling achieved the lowest horizontal georeferencing root mean square error of 1.29 m, while full-navigation factor graph smoothing achieved the lowest three-dimensional georeferencing root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.71 m. Online switching achieved the lowest cloud-to-cloud root mean square distance of 6.1 cm against a terrestrial laser scanning reference within the evaluated facade and ground floor region. Controlled experiments also evaluated the effect of separate GNSS admission paths and global transformation policies. The results support adapting GNSS integration to changing reception conditions and mapping objectives, as stronger coupling did not uniformly improve trajectory accuracy, global placement, and local geometric agreement.

title: Long-Term Mangrove Dynamics and Environmental Associations in the Sundarbans, Bangladesh: Integrating Remote Sensing, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI
abstract: Mangrove ecosystems are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic disturbances and climate change, despite providing ecological services, including biodiversity conservation, coastal protection, and blue carbon storage. Long-term evaluations of mangrove dynamics and associated environmental conditions remain limited, particularly in the Sundarbans, the largest mangrove forest in the world. This study examined the spatiotemporal dynamics of the Sundarbans mangrove ecosystem, Bangladesh, using multi-temporal Landsat imagery (1990–2025), Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Model performance was evaluated using the Global Mangrove Watch (GMW) dataset and spatially blocked holdout validation. Classification accuracy was high (94.56–100%) under internal and spatially blocked validation (93.5–99.8%), whereas comparison with GMW yielded lower accuracies (66.4–95.7%). Change detection showed that mangrove area expanded from 2096.66 km2 in 1990 to 3875.95 km2 in 2025, a net gain of almost 1779.29 km2, with substantial inter-period variability and a pronounced mapped decline between 2000 and 2005. SHAP analysis indicated that the relative contributions of model predictors changed over time, with NDVI contributing more strongly to model predictions in recent years than NDWI and NDMI. Mangrove gain, loss, and net change were statistically associated with cyclone exposure and elevation, while precipitation and river discharge showed less consistent relationships. This study highlights a practical method for monitoring spectral dynamics in vulnerable coastal ecosystems and supports mangrove conservation.

title: A Comparative Study of Client-Level Stabilization Techniques in Federated Learning for Robust Plant Disease Recognition
abstract: The successful integration of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms in precision agriculture provided farmers with the means to identify potential issues, such as early disease detection or pest infestations, by making crop-related predictions. The new technological developments in this field improve the functioning of traditional agriculture by reducing the dependence on specialized human expertise and facilitating greater access to diagnostic procedures. However, most studies conducted in this area rely on centralized training of AI models, which leads to increased costs and raised privacy-related concerns. Federated learning (FL) offers a compelling framework for collaboratively training machine learning (ML) models on distributed datasets without centralizing the data owned by each participant. FL offers significant advantages in the preservation of data privacy, facilitates the collaborative exploitation of geographically distributed data sources, and reduces the risks associated with centralized collection. In this paper, we investigate the current limitations and performance boundaries of existing Federated and privacy-preserving learning in distributed sensing systems for plant disease detection, in scenarios that closely resemble real-world conditions. Our analysis specifically examined how FL aggregation algorithms, such as FedAvg, FedAvgM and FedProx, work in a custom multi-client experimental setup where data is partitioned so that each participant observes only those symptom patterns associated with specific environmental and climatic conditions. We propose further partial aggregation of the local model, an approach where we send only the model backbone to the central server, while the classification head of each participant remains strictly on the client side. The construction of environmentally heterogeneity is combined with a globally representative stabilizer node designed to preserve knowledge across disease classes that may be absent from certain clients.

title: Identifying the Achilles’ Heel: Using Complex Network Analysis to Pinpoint Systemic Vulnerabilities in the Global Food Supply Network
abstract: Systemic risk in the global staple food trade network has become a critical threat to global food security amid escalating geopolitical frictions and frequent extreme weather events. This study constructs directed weighted trade networks for wheat, rice, maize and soybean covering 196 economies, and applies a cascading failure model to compare cross-crop structural vulnerability. Simulation results reveal stark heterogeneous risk profiles: a shock originating from a top rice exporter in India spreads across two cascading rounds and impacts 25.5% of total network nodes, while a parallel shock from a top soybean exporter in Brazil triggers nine propagation rounds affecting 86.2% of nodes; by comparison, equivalent shocks to wheat and maize networks only affect 22.4% and 24.5% of nodes respectively. Under identical targeted attack conditions, rice and soybean networks suffer sharp connectivity deterioration after removing a small number of core exporter nodes, while wheat and maize networks retain relatively higher residual connectivity under the same attack intensity, reflecting that crop trade systems with higher supply concentration exhibit greater systemic vulnerability. This work adopts a single-year static network framework; future research will extend to multi-year dynamic network tracking and incorporate adaptive supply-chain feedback mechanisms. Despite this boundary, the study fills the research gap in cross-crop systemic risk comparison, providing robust empirical evidence for differentiated global food supply-chain resilience governance.

title: Foundation models in reverse engineering, CAD reconstruction and additive manufacturing: A systematic review
abstract: Reverse engineering is undergoing a profound transformation driven by the emergence of foundation models. These models, together with their applications, are progressively extending the limits of artificial intelligence (AI) from geometrical reconstruction to a more sophisticated level engineering reasoning. In contrast to traditional methods, which usually use sequences of algorithms for specific 3D retrieval and reconstruction tasks, current foundation models train geometrical representations that are able to support semantic reasoning, computer-aided design (CAD) reconstruction, and intelligent manufacturing in a unified way. This work provides an overview of foundation models within the context of reverse engineering and their combination with CAD reconstruction and additive manufacturing. Starting from a systematic bibliometric analysis of the recent literature, the present review is mainly focused on the development of representation learning and reviews the key geometric forms that are being used by the current foundation models. The paper also explores the engineering abilities facilitated by such models in the reverse engineering process. Furthermore, current challenges, research obstacles, and future directions are critically explored, emphasizing the recent transition toward intelligent engineering systems. The analysis shows that foundation models are gradually making reverse engineering move from being an assortment of discrete computational activities to becoming an engineering process workflow that is made possible by means of geometry representations and multimodal reasoning as well as engineering AI. Finally, considerations on the importance of developing engineering conceptual frameworks to interpret the emerging role of foundation models in future intelligent engineering systems are drafted.

title: Controlled Evaluation for Numeric-Field Forgery Detection in SROIE Receipts using Fine-Tuned EfficientNetV2-S
abstract: Altered amounts, dates, and identifiers on retail receipts represent a practical source of expense and tax fraud. However, public receipt datasets such as Scanned Receipts OCR and Information Extraction (SROIE) contain authentic receipts but do not provide forged counterparts, limiting controlled evaluation of receipt-forgery detection methods. Chakraborty (2025) reported 97.1% accuracy using a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based receipt-forgery detection framework. Building on this research context, the present study investigates forgery detection at the numeric-field level, focusing on receipt components that directly carry financial information. Using SROIE, a receipt-grouped benchmark of paired authentic and synthetically forged numeric-field crops is constructed. Two controlled forgery mechanisms are considered: splicing a donor numeric field from the same receipt and erasing and re-rendering a field with a specified proportion of its digits changed. Authentic and forged crops undergo the same Joint Photographic Experts Group (JPEG) compression procedure, and receipt-level grouping is used for training, validation, and test partitioning at approximately 70/15/15. An ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNetV2-S is fine-tuned end-to-end using linear warm-up, cosine learning-rate decay, and exponential moving average (EMA) weights, with model selection based exclusively on validation accuracy. On the held-out test set of 4,602 crops, comprising 2,301 authentic and 2,301 forged samples, the reference detector achieves 98.09% accuracy, 99.42% precision, 96.74% recall, an F1-score of 0.9806, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) of 0.9971 at a fixed decision threshold of 0.5 in a single run with seed 42. Most remaining errors correspond to missed forgeries. The reported accuracy is numerically higher than the 97.1% reported by Chakraborty (2025), but direct comparison is limited by differences in datasets, sample construction, and evaluation protocols. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) analysis indicates attention to numeric text regions but also, in some cases, to crop boundaries and background regions, suggesting that synthetic generation artifacts may contribute to the observed performance. As the study relies on synthetic forgeries without multiple baseline architectures, ablation experiments, multiple random seeds, or real-world forged-receipt evaluation, the findings are limited to the defined synthetic tampering processes rather than general real-world forgery-detection performance.

title: Supply Chain Redundancy Strategy and Food Security in Kenya’s Arid and Semi-Arid Lands
abstract: Food insecurity remains a chronic development challenge in Kenya’s Arid and Semi-Arid Lands (ASALs), where structural deficits in distribution infrastructure magnify climatic and market shocks. This paper examines the empirical influence of a supply chain redundancy strategy on food security across Kenya’s 29 ASAL counties. Grounded in the Resilience Model, Theory of Constraints (TOC), and Resource Dependence Theory (RDT), the study operationalises redundancy through three primary indicators: physical buffer stock management, strategic storage capacity (warehouses, silos, and cold chains), and multi-modal distribution channel capacity. A pragmatic research philosophy utilising an explanatory cross-sectional survey design was executed. Primary data were gathered through structured questionnaires administered to County Directors of Agriculture and Crop Production Officers across all 29 ASAL counties (N=29; 100% response rate). Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was employed for data reduction, extracting a single dominant factor for Redundancy explaining 78.4% of total variance. Binary logistic regression and marginal effects estimations were conducted. The empirical results reveal that supply chain redundancy has a statistically significant positive effect on food security (β=1.842, p=0.014). Marginal effects estimation indicates that a unit increase in supply chain redundancy increases the probability of an ASAL county achieving food security by 28.6 percentage points (dy/dx=0.286, p=0.018). Diagnostic evaluations confirmed the absence of severe multicollinearity (VIF 0.05). The study concludes that maintaining deliberate operational slacks and safety buffers transforms fragile agricultural supply chains into resilient, shock-absorbent distribution networks. It recommends that devolved county administrations institutionalise inter-county strategic food reserves, incentivise private warehouse hub construction, and implement hermetic storage technologies to insulate vulnerable pastoral and agro-pastoral populations from extreme food price volatility and supply disruptions.
journal: East African Journal of Agriculture and Biotechnology

title: Supply Chain Collaboration Strategy and Food Security: Evaluating the Moderating Role of Political Governance
abstract: Cross-sectoral partnership and multi-stakeholder coordination are critical mechanisms for managing food distribution networks operating in vulnerable dryland environments. This paper investigates the empirical effect of a Supply Chain Collaboration Strategy on food security across Kenya's 29 Arid and Semi-Arid Land (ASAL) counties, while specifically assessing the moderating role of Political Governance. Grounded in Resource Dependence Theory (RDT), Complex Adaptive Systems (CAS) Theory, and institutional theory, collaboration was operationalised through inter-county food-sharing agreements, public-private-humanitarian partnerships, joint logistics coordination, and real-time information sharing. Political Governance was operationalised as a composite metric measuring policy consistency, political stability, procurement transparency, and intergovernmental institutional alignment. Utilising an explanatory cross-sectional survey design within a pragmatic research paradigm, primary data were collected via structured questionnaires administered to County Directors of Agriculture and Crop Production Officers across all 29 ASAL counties (N = 29; 100% response rate). Data reduction was conducted using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), extracting robust single factors for Collaboration (79.2% variance explained) and Political Governance (77.8% variance explained). Binary logistic regression, interaction-term modelling (SCC × PG), and marginal effects estimations were computed. In the direct logistic model, supply chain collaboration exhibited a statistically significant positive effect on food security (β = 1.712, p = 0.018; marginal effect = 0.264, p = 0.021). Moderation analysis revealed that the interaction term between collaboration and political governance was positive and statistically significant (β interaction = 1.482, p = 0.038). This confirms that political governance positively moderates the relationship between supply chain collaboration and food security. Marginal effects interaction plots demonstrate that in ASAL counties characterised by high political stability, policy consistency, and institutional alignment, the probability of supply chain collaboration successfully delivering food security increases to 84.2%, compared to only 28.1% in low-governance contexts. The study concludes that collaborative supply networks require supportive political governance frameworks to achieve optimal food distribution resilience. It recommends that national and county governments institutionalise inter-county regional food security blocs, streamline public-private partnership procurement regulations, and insulate food logistics from local political interference.
journal: East African Journal of Interdisciplinary Studies

title: Cloud-Assisted Smart Agriculture System Using IoT Sensors and Python-Driven Machine Learning for Crop Yield Optimization and Soil Health Prediction
abstract: This chapter presents a cloud-assisted smart agriculture system that integrates Internet of Things (IoT) sensors with Python-driven machine learning models for crop yield optimization and soil health prediction. Real-time data on soil moisture, temperature, humidity, pH, and nutrient levels are collected through distributed sensors and transmitted to a cloud platform for storage, preprocessing, and analysis. Machine learning algorithms, including Linear Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Neural Networks, are applied to both historical and real-time datasets to generate accurate predictions and decision support. The results indicate that ensemble models, particularly Random Forest, achieve superior performance in handling complex agricultural data. The proposed framework enables efficient resource utilization, improved productivity, and data-driven decision-making, contributing to sustainable and precision farming practices.

title: SOCIO-ECONOMIC AND EXTENSION DETERMINANTS OF INTEGRATED PEST AND DISEASE MANAGEMENT ADOPTION IN LABLAB (LABLAB PURPUREUS) AND RELATED GRAIN LEGUMES: A SYSTEMATIC SCOPING REVIEW
abstract: Lablab (Lablab purpureus (L.) Sweet) is a multipurpose legume whose productivity is limited by pod borers, aphids, storage bruchids and viral and fungal diseases. Integrated pest and disease management (IPDM) packages exist, but little is known about why smallholders do or do not adopt them. This review asks which socio-economic, extension and institutional factors shape IPDM adoption in lablab and analogous smallholder grain-legume systems. A systematic scoping review was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidance. We de-duplicated and screened records from Google Scholar (semantic and full-text search) and PubMed (n = 400) against population concept–context criteria; we retained 12 studies from database searching and 8 from citation and targeted searching. We charted data on setting, crop, design, sample, analytical model, and reported determinants, and synthesised them narratively with an evidence matrix. Only three included studies concern lablab, and none estimates an adoption model; the evidence base is dominated by common bean and cowpea in East and West Africa, with two Indian studies. Across systems, extension contact, training frequency, access to crop information and membership of farmer groups were the most consistent positive correlates of adoption. Education and off farm income were generally positive; age was negative or inconsistent; land size was mixed. In Lablab, farmers rank economic returns as both the main motivation and the main constraint, with poor prices, weak market channels and lack of improved varieties prominent. Labour, cost and yield risk, insecticide promotion and subsidies, and weak seed systems constrain adoption, and gender shapes both preferences and access. IPDM adoption in lablab is best understood as an investment decision conditioned on market incentives and knowledge access rather than a purely technical choice. Priorities are household-level adoption studies in lablab (particularly in India, the crop's centre of diversity), measurement of adoption intensity and dis-adoption, and gender disaggregated analysis.

title: RECENT ADVANCES IN DIRECT SEEDED RICE: PHYSIOLOGICAL ADAPTATION, CROP MANAGEMENT, AND GENETIC IMPROVEMENT
abstract: Owing to insufficient water, labour shortages and accelerating climate change, direct seeded rice (DSR) has emerged as a feasible and resource-efficient alternative to conventional transplanted puddled rice (TPR) systems, conserving water and reducing methane emissions. However, the initial growth phases are frequently impeded by inadequate seedling emergence, intensive weed competition, nutritional deficiencies and exposure to variable soil moisture and aeration conditions in some DSR systems, including low nitrogen use efficiency, which can impair the establishment of a healthy crop stand and stability of its yield under DSR. Identifying and phenotyping rice germplasm for critical physiological traits is essential for developing cultivars that thrive in DSR environments. The physiological basis of genotypes adaption to DSR conditions need to be integrated with phenotyping and breeding strategies. This review synthesizes the knowledge of the physiological traits that facilitate DSR adaptation evaluates both conventional and high-throughput phenotyping (HTP) techniques — digital imaging, canopy temperature measurement, chlorophyll fluorescence analysis, and remote sensing technologies to precisely evaluate these traits in field and controlled environment and examines how quantitative trait loci (QTL) mapping, genome-wide association studies (GWAS), and marker-assisted selection (MAS), significantly facilitates the development of rice varieties suitable for DSR. The review highlights the importance of multi-trait phenotyping frameworks and multi-environment testing in accelerating genetic improvement and ensuring sustainable rice production in direct seeded agricultural systems.

title: WOMEN FARMERS, AGRICULTURAL EXTENSION AND ACCESS TO IMPROVED CROP GENETIC TECHNOLOGIES: A REVIEW
abstract: Women play a vital role in agriculture through crop production, seed selection, livestock management, post harvest activities, household nutrition and conservation of plant genetic resources. However, women farmers often face gender-based constraints in accessing land, credit, markets, agricultural extension, information, quality seed and improved crop technologies. Improved crop genetic technologies, including high-yielding, disease- and pest resistant, drought- and heat-tolerant, early-maturing and nutritionally enhanced varieties, can contribute significantly to productivity, food security, income generation and climate resilience. Nevertheless, technological availability alone does not guarantee adoption or benefits among women farmers. Access to information, financial resources, inputs, markets and household decision-making strongly influences technology uptake. Gender responsive agricultural extension can help overcome these barriers by linking women farmers with researchers, breeders, seed producers, input suppliers and markets. Approaches such as participatory varietal selection, farmer field schools, women extension workers, self-help groups, community seed systems, farmer-to-farmer learning and digital advisory services can strengthen women's participation in agricultural innovation. This review highlights the need to recognize women as active partners in crop breeding, varietal evaluation, seed production, technology dissemination and agricultural decision-making. Integrating gender-responsive extension, marketing and seed systems with improved crop genetic technologies can promote more inclusive, productive, resilient and sustainable agricultural development.

title: White Ocean Mixed Strategy and Performance of Manufacturing Firms in South-East, Nigeria
abstract: Manufacturing firms in South-East Nigeria continue to contend with an unstable operating environment characterized by infrastructural deficits, intense rivalry, and eroding market share, prompting renewed scholarly interest in strategic typologies capable of restoring competitiveness. To this effect, this study examined white-ocean mixed strategy and performance of manufacturing firms in South-East Nigeria. Specifically, the study ascertained the extent to which red ocean/competitive strategy boost market share, determined the degree to which blue ocean/monopoly strategy enhance value innovation and evaluate the effect of green ocean/sustainability strategy on the survival of selected manufacturing firms in South East, Nigeria. A survey research design was adopted. Primary data was used to gather information from the respondentsand this was also supported by reviews from secondary sources for validation. The target population of 781 consists of staff of the five selectedmanufacturing firms in South East, Nigeria. The sample size of 265 was derived from Taro Yamane formula. The study utilized Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) and Simple Linear Regression Model of SPSS Version 22.0 to test the hypotheses. The result of the findings revealed that red-ocean/competitive strategy boost market share of selected manufacturing firms in South East, Nigeria, blue ocean/monopoly strategy enhance value innovation of selected manufacturing firms in South East, Nigeria, green ocean/sustainability strategy had a significant effect on the survival of selected manufacturing firms in South East, Nigeria. The study concluded that white ocean mixed strategy positively and significantly enhanced manufacturing firms’ performance in South East, Nigeria. The study recommended that management of manufacturing firms should improve on differentiation strategy, cost leadership strategy, market focus strategy and corporate growth strategy to remain relevant and compete favorably in the market, they should review their policy to provide new and innovative ideas and services that align with society's needs and desires and they should improve on green practices in energy and water consumption, waste management and awareness creation among employees.

title: Pedicel-Targeted Strawberry Harvesting via Imitation Learning on a Low-Cost Teleoperated Robotic Arm
abstract: Precise pedicel-targeted grasping in strawberry harvesting remains a critical bottleneck due to the pedicel's small diameter (1.3-3 mm), color similarity with surrounding foliage, and precise force control required for clean abscission zone detachment. As a market-grade crop, strawberry aesthetic value makes bruise-free pedicel detachment essential over direct fruit grasping. Classical approaches struggle to unify vision models, motion planning, and contact manipulation into a robust framework, particularly in occluded canopy environments. Therefore, this work presents a visuomotor imitation learning pipeline for pedicel-targeted strawberry harvesting that unifies perception, motion planning, and contact manipulation from collecting human teleoperation demonstrations, training an Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) policy with a ResNet-50 visual backbone, and deploying the learned policy autonomously on a Jetson AGX Orin edge platform at 15 Hz. The trained policy achieved consistent loss convergence from 2.84 to 0.091 over 100K gradient steps on 130 demonstrations. We have also established a reproducible open-source pipeline with publicly released dataset and model weights for the agricultural robotics community. Full dataset is available at, https://huggingface.co/datasets/nitindominicrai/strawberry_pedicel_grasp_teleoperation and trained policy at, https://huggingface.co/nitindominicrai/act_strawberry_pedicel. To replicate this work, all code, configurations, and deployment instructions are publicly available at, https://github.com/nitin-dominic/autonomous_strawberry_pedicel_harvesting.

title: Anytime Contracts for AI Services
abstract: AI services are prone to moral hazard, as model providers can silently route requests to cheaper, lower-quality models, and the inherent stochasticity of model outputs makes this degradation hard to detect. Contract theory addresses moral hazard by designing payment rules that reward high-quality outputs and prevent strategic overcharging. However, existing frameworks assume interactions of fixed duration, whereas AI services are typically consumed through subscriptions and pay-as-you-go APIs that users can terminate at any time based on observed performance. We show that this flexibility can break standard contracts, opening them up to abuse by either the providers or users. To address this, we extend contract theory to account for unknown exit rules. We formalize the problem as a Principal-Agent game, and show that budget-optimal contracts in this setting are proportional to anytime-valid hypothesis tests based on likelihood-ratio e-values. We give an efficient algorithm for computing anytime contracts and show how betting e-processes can be used to approximate them when the models are unknown. Finally, we evaluate our findings on synthetic data and data from deployed LLMs.

title: Prune the Leaky Neurons: Mitigating Private Data Leakage in Fine-Tuned LLMs via Joint-Embedding-Guided Pruning
abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on proprietary records enables domain adaptation but introduces two challenges: (i) privacy leakage of memorized private data, such as personally identifiable information (PII), and (ii) balancing private data removal with utility preservation. Existing defenses, including data sanitization and differential privacy, often degrade performance, while privacy-neuron editing lacks a PII-free reference to distinguish identity-specific neurons from those supporting useful text. We propose JEPA-Prune, a post-hoc neuron pruning framework guided by a model trained exclusively on PII-free views. Alongside the fine-tuned private model, JEPA-Prune, trains a public model on surrogate and masked views of the same records using a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA), capturing domain knowledge without identifiers. A cross-model representation probe quantifies deviations between private representations of leaked records and this PII-free reference. Integrated gradients and a scale-invariant specificity score then identify PII-responsive neurons, which are pruned without retraining. Experiments show that pruning just 1.6% of neurons reduces PII inference accuracy by up to 7.4x and PII extraction recall by up to 13.9x, while keeping unseen-text perplexity within 16% of that of the unpruned model for most LLMs. In contrast, privacy-neuron editing increases perplexity by at least 26x.

title: Replay Pruning and Few-Bit Integer Inference for Hardware-Efficient Speed-Sign Recognition
abstract: Speed-limit sign recognition on an automotive camera system-on-chip (SoC) must fit a detector and a classifier (the reader) into the memory, arithmetic, and energy budgets of the device. In our two-stage recognizer, the detector, a YOLO-family network with ReLU and hard-sigmoid operators, is compressed by channel replay: an iterative pruning cascade identifies the channels to remove, the recorded deletions are replayed on the original task-trained network, the parent, and one continuous knowledge-distillation recovery follows. On a YOLOv5n, replay removes 60.3% of the parameters at the accuracy of the parent and, in validation mAP50-95 over five matched seeds, outperforms iterative pruning and training from scratch, and its per-step variant (per-step replay) is the most accurate pruning method. On a YOLOv8n, replay and per-step replay outperform every other method and the unpruned parent. The reader, a five-layer CNN with 18k parameters, and the post-processing of the YOLOv5n and YOLOv8n heads use integer arithmetic only. With 4-bit weights and 8-bit activations (W4A8), the reader matches FP32 accuracy in 12.1 KB of on-chip memory, and an executable streaming model reproduces the INT8 class predictions of its runtime on all 9,850 test crops. On a Jetson AGX Orin, INT8 is faster than FP16 only in the implicit formulation of TensorRT, and the replay detector runs fastest on the deep-learning accelerator (DLA). Trained on public data only, the combined system of 0.72 M parameters recognizes 95.2% of the signs of a held-out automotive camera at 90% precision and 94 frames per second.

title: A Unified Solution to the Low-Mass X-ray Binary Diversity Puzzle: Saturated Magnetic Braking Coupled with Irradiation-Driven Winds
abstract: The standard magnetic braking (MB) model has long failed to explain key properties of low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs)---including their accretion rates, the formation of ultracompact binaries, and orbital expansion---casting doubt on binary evolution and gravitational-wave progenitor predictions. Phenomenological modifications exist, but a unified, physically grounded mechanism has been missing. Here we show that the overlooked coupling between magnetic saturation and irradiation-driven winds (IDW) provides this missing framework. Accretion-powered irradiation enhances the donor wind, which in turn amplifies MB exactly where needed. Our Saturated MB + IDW (SMB+IDW) model simultaneously resolves three outstanding discrepancies with no fine-tuning: (1) it reproduces the full observed distribution of accretion rates across persistent and transient LMXBs; (2) it naturally explains ultracompact X-ray binary formation; and (3) it quantitatively matches the orbital period distribution of descendant millisecond pulsar (MSP) binaries---a critical independent test failed by all previous models. Critically, the SMB+IDW model transforms MB from an externally imposed condition into a self-consistently regulated process tied to the accretion history. By unifying LMXB evolution to MSPs in a single physical picture, our work resolves the long-standing diversity puzzle and establishes a physics-based foundation for next-generation population synthesis, gravitational-wave progenitor predictions, and compact binary interpretation across cosmic time.

title: The Source of Data Value: Consumer Disclosure, Access Design, and Platform Monetization
abstract: Digital marketplaces increasingly earn revenue from transaction commissions and seller-facing data services. Sellers may purchase data to increase revenue or avoid competing with an informed rival. We examine how consumer disclosure rights shape these motives and the platform's incentive to provide data. We develop a game-theoretic model of a commissioned platform, two differentiated sellers, and privacy-sensitive consumers. Data generates value through bilateral sales-revenue gains and competition threats arising from asymmetric access. Under mandatory collection, the platform can monetize defensive adoption, even when bilateral personalization reduces seller revenue. Under voluntary disclosure, anonymous purchasing and strictly positive privacy costs make unilateral disclosure unattractive in the baseline. Exclusive access thus yields no usable information, restores sellers' no-data rejection payoffs, and eliminates defensive fees. Profitable provision therefore requires nonnegative bilateral revenue gains. Under full fee extraction, sellers retain their no-data net profits. This revenue alignment does not guarantee welfare gains: additional transactions may benefit consumers, whereas segmentation in an already covered market can raise anonymous prices and reduce welfare. Capping anonymous offers at their no-data benchmark protects individual consumers and limits positive-mass provision to the transaction-creation region. Extensions consider access choice, heterogeneous privacy costs, imperfect identification, and limited contractual credibility. Platforms should evaluate data services based on both bilateral-use and seller-rejection outcomes, and sellers should distinguish revenue-enhancing from defensive investments. Regulators should distinguish equal-access rules from effective consumer control and monitor pricing in anonymous channels.

title: Federated Multiagent Soft Actor Critic for IRS Assisted Cognitive Radio Networks under Partial Observability
abstract: Intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs) can improve spectrum efficiency and interference control in cognitive radio networks (CRNs) by reconfiguring the propagation environment. This paper presents FMASAC, a federated multi-agent soft actor-critic framework for IRS-assisted CRNs under partial observability, in which distributed secondary users (SUs) jointly select their transmit power and the phase shifts of an assigned subset of IRS elements using only local observations. Primary user (PU) protection is incorporated through an interference-penalized reward, and SUs coordinate by periodically averaging model parameters at a federated server, without exchanging raw observations, channel state information, or replay data. We formulate the problem as a partially observable Markov decision process, specify the local learning and aggregation procedure, and characterize its per-round communication cost. Illustrative performance trends contrast FMASAC with centralized SAC, independent SAC, IRS-fixed multi-agent reinforcement learning, and a heuristic CRN strategy. We also outline the simulation-based evaluation and the open challenges, namely constraint handling, agent heterogeneity, and scalability, that are needed to validate the framework.

title: MailRail: Mitigating Incast Congestion with User-Space, Node-Based Flow Control
abstract: Irregular workloads, such as those stemming from Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, frequently induce severe incast congestion in large-scale parallel environments. Existing fabric-level congestion control mechanisms rely on reactive, link-level rate limiting that degrades overall throughput. While receiver-driven, credit-based flow control offers a proactive alternative, as process counts scale memory slots per rank fall below usable thresholds, rendering traditional rank-based accounting untenable. To address this challenge, we introduce MailRail, an out-of-order, asynchronous messaging framework, along with a novel user-space, node-based credit flow control system. By shifting credit accounting from individual processes to shared per-node pools, our proactive, fabric-agnostic approach maintains sufficient credit availability even as process density grows, enabling processes to dynamically utilize freed credits without waiting for receiver-side redistribution. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that node-based flow control achieves up to a 1132x speedup over unconstrained execution at an adversarial incast ratio of 4096:1 while adding minimal overhead on uniform workloads.

title: Provable Authority: A Protocol for Verifiable Authority Resolution and Control Across Human, Organizational, and Agentic Transactions
abstract: Payment systems authenticate users, devices, accounts, and cryptographic credentials, but a relying party, such as a counterparty, payment rail, marketplace, or autonomous agent runtime, generally cannot obtain compact, independently verifiable evidence that the party presenting one exact transaction holds current organizational authority to execute it under the applicable evidence, policy, budget, and approval state. Agentic commerce makes this gap operationally urgent: a software agent can produce a valid signature while acting outside its delegated purpose, after its sponsor's authority has changed, or on transaction details that differ from those a human approved. We describe the ChainIT Authority Protocol, a subject-neutral and rail-neutral pre-execution authority and evidence control plane. The protocol separates durable identity, a versioned organizational authority record (the Authority Resolution Pactvera), sourced evidence assertions, deterministic reason-coded policy predicates, and organization-configured dispositions; binds each decision and human approval to a canonical transaction digest; reserves capacity atomically so that limits hold under concurrency; and authorizes commit only through a single-use, sender-constrained Execution Authorization Credential consumed at the rail adapter, with append-only lifecycle evidence sealed after the terminal outcome. An Agent Subject Profile adds the workload registration, attested key hierarchy, and sovereignty boundary required when the acting subject is an AI agent, without introducing a separate authority concept. We specify the commit-time execution predicate and bounded-freshness status rules, give enforcement profiles for fiat (ACH, wire, card, instant payment) and stablecoin rails, and state residual risks and non-goals.

title: Designing an AI Agent That Does Not Tutor: Design Rules for Socratic Probing in Introductory Physics
abstract: Instructors need to know whether a student understands a concept, not only whether the student can produce a correct answer, and the two have come apart: a student can paste a physics question into a chatbot and submit a fluent, correct answer without understanding it. We built a conversational AI agent for introductory mechanics that only probes. It is designed as an instrument that a correct answer alone should not pass.
