title: From Model Accuracy toWorkflow Reliability: A Practical Framework for Enterprise AI Systems
abstract: The predictive or generative capacity of a model isn’t enough for enterprise AI applications. Several factors can affect whether a user’s task succeeds: retrieval, enterprise data, orchestration, external tools, human approvals, and infrastructure. While a number of these dependencies are acknowledged in current standards and research, there is a practical approach to communicating what specific functionality an AI system needs to reliably do to be considered a product team. Objective: This article compiles and reviews existing literature on AI quality, generation with a machine learning production system, retrievalaugmented generation, agent failure, and service reliability from a workflow perspective to define and explore enterprise AI reliability. Approach: This is provided by a targeted narrative review of relevant standards, research publications and a first-party production incident. The contract details what job it is supposed to perform, what results the user expects, the conditions under which it can
journal: International Journal of Computer Studies and Advancement in Current Research

title: Supporting the Adoption of Digital Technology On-Farm: Ten Tips for Extension
abstract: We held a symposium to exchange lessons from U.S. and European experts on how Extension can be best designed to support adoption of digital agricultural innovation. We highlight 10 tips for an Extension audience in the United States: (a) ensure connectivity between all actors involved in agricultural innovation, (b) utilize the private sector, (c) advocate for adoption costs, (d) shape an enabling digital ecosystem, (e) create a service, not just a technology, (f) update Extension agents' digital skills, (g) support farmer-led innovation, (h) capture everyday farmer practices, (i) monitor and evaluate progress, and (j) offer long-term support.

title: Community-Based Crop-Residue Management for Open-Burning Prevention, Soil Restoration, and Climate Resilience: The BIO-NO BURN™ Case Study in Thailand
abstract: Background Open burning remains a low-cost but environmentally damaging method of managing crop residues in Thailand. Community enterprises may provide a locally governed alternative when residue collection, processing, quality control, and evidence systems are designed together. Objective: This case study describes the BIO-NO BURN™ model, its implementation context and management architecture, and the evidence chain used to distinguish documented organizational activity from modelled estimates and future targets. Methods A retrospective descriptive review was conducted using the enterprise’s official performance report, registration and governance records, summarized operational records, and a 2026 project-design package. The case was examined through five evidence domains: organizational setting and geographic scope, implementation process, operational records, investigation/data checks, and documented versus prospective outcomes. Claims were classified as documented activity, modelled estimate, or planned target. No proprietary microbial formula, inoculum ratio, cultivation method, or propagation procedure was examined or disclosed. Results The enterprise reports a 2,500-rai pilot area in fiscal year 2025/2026, adoption of a 100% no-burn policy for that pilot, initiation of GPS/polygon data collection, and a reported 92% per-rai reduction in 46-0-0 fertilizer use relative to its internal project baseline. These results remain self-reported and require reconciliation with plot, purchase, issue, weighbridge, production, and inspection records. The case architecture specifies a six-function operating chain from participant enrolment and residue-source identification through processing, quality control, field application, and review/corrective action. A separate 12-month demonstration is designed for 100 households, approximately 220 rai (35.2 ha), four community compost hubs, 20 demonstration plots, at least 300 tonnes of residue diversion, and at least 180 tonnes of quality-controlled compost; these are prospective targets, not achieved results. Conclusion BIO-NO BURN™ offers a replicable governance and traceability architecture rather than a single technology. Its main contribution is the integration of community no-burn agreements, distributed processing, batch records, field application records, safeguards, and adaptive review. Environmental and greenhouse-gas claims should remain provisional until baselines, activity data, emission factors, leakage assumptions, and independent verification are completed.
journal: Journal of Climate Change and Pollution

title: Soil and Root-Associated Microbial Responses to Abiotic Stress under Climate Change: Implications for Carbon Cycling, Plant Resilience, and Microbial Bioinoculants
abstract: Soil and root-associated microbial communities are pivotal to terrestrial biogeochemical cycling; however, compounding global change stressors increasingly compromise their structural and functional resilience. This review synthesizes microbial responses to key abiotic perturbations, including elevated atmospheric CO2 (eCO2), thermal anomalies, hydrological extremes (drought and flooding), and nutrient imbalances (N and P). We critically evaluate how these factors regulate microbial carbon use efficiency (CUE), greenhouse gas emissions, and the distribution of metabolic traits, specifically the balance between fast-growing (r-strategists) and slow-growing (K-strategists) populations. We also explore mechanisms of plant-microbe interactions under stress, focusing on root exudation patterns and phytohormone signaling (e.g., ethylene modulation via ACC deaminase). By bridging microbial physiology, metagenomics, and trait-based ecology, this study underscores the critical need to parameterize soil microbial mechanisms into climate feedback models to advance ecosystem management, ensure crop resilience, and improve the efficacy of soil bioinoculants.

title: The Trust Paradox of AI-Generated Content Transparency: Impulse Buying from the Perspective of Generative Agents
abstract: As generative artificial intelligence becomes increasingly embedded in digital e-commerce environments, the transparency labeling of AI-generated content has emerged as a crucial institutional variable in modern platform governance. Drawing upon the established information–trust–behavior theoretical logic, this study conducted a large-scale AI-agent simulation, comprising 900 distinct purchase decisions executed by large language model agents, to systematically test how disclosure labeling affects simulated consumer trust and simulated impulse buying intention. Furthermore, the research investigated whether trust acts as a mediating mechanism and whether consumer involvement moderates these relationships. Rigorous model-rationality validation confirmed that the agent decisions consistently conformed to their assigned behavioral personalities and rational economic logic. The empirical results demonstrated that disclosure labeling significantly suppressed both simulated trust and impulse buying intention. Additionally, simulated trust positively predicted impulse intention, revealing a negative indirect association within the disclosure–impulse behavioral link. Notably, consumer involvement moderated the trust–impulse path during the primary simulation phase, although this moderating effect was not replicated in the cross-model robustness check. Ultimately, these comprehensive findings reveal the critical boundary conditions of the institutional logic surrounding the exchange of transparency for trust. The study provides robust, simulation-based empirical evidence for the development of AI-content labeling policies and offers valuable insights for optimizing platform information governance strategies in the digital economy.

title: Adoption, Impacts and Barriers to Decentralised Solar Energy in a Tribal Region: Evidence from Dungarpur and Banswara Districts of Southern Rajasthan, India
abstract: This study examines the extent and pattern of decentralised solar energy adoption in the predominantly tribal districts of Dungarpur and Banswara in southern Rajasthan, India (twenty villages across ten tehsils), measures its economic and social effects, identifies barriers constraining wider uptake, and assesses whether adoption follows geographical suitability. A cross-sectional household survey was combined with stakeholder interviews and spatial correlation against an independently constructed suitability index. Four hundred respondents were selected using multi-stage stratified random sampling, with tehsils chosen to represent all three classes of a previously constructed Solar Potential Index and villages paired as well-connected and remote. A 42-item schedule covered energy use, awareness, adoption, impacts and barriers, and 24 stakeholders were interviewed. The analysis used percentages, chi-square tests, t-tests, before-and-after comparisons for adopters, and Pearson's correlation between the tehsil-level suitability index and observed diffusion. Only 16.0% of households used any solar system while 44.5% intended to adopt within two years. Solar irrigation pumps accounted for 52.3% of installations, indicating that adoption in this region is predominantly for productive rather than domestic use. Among pump adopters, irrigated area rose 45.8%, cropping intensity 24.6% and net farm income 46.7%, while irrigation expenditure fell 86.6% and weekly night-time irrigation labour fell from 9.4 to 1.2 hours. Awareness declined steeply from general familiarity (56.0%) to knowledge of the application procedure (14.0%). Education, income, gender and holding size were all significantly associated with adoption (P < .01), and the suitability index correlated with observed diffusion at r = 0.70 (P < .01). Affordability emerged as the binding constraint: 59% of willing respondents could contribute no more than Rs. 25,000 against a required farmer share of Rs. 1.0–1.2 lakh. Adoption is therefore limited not by the resource or willingness but by finance, procedural information, maintenance services and grid capacity; in a Fifth Schedule area where land transfer is restricted, community-owned and service-based models are more appropriate than the land-acquisition model used in western Rajasthan.
journal: Asian Journal of Advanced Research and Reports

title: Multi-Omics Integration for Crop Improvement: Connecting Genomes, Transcriptomes, Proteomes and Metabolomes
abstract: Crop improvement increasingly depends on resolving how inherited sequence variation is converted into context-dependent molecular states and, ultimately, agronomic phenotypes. Genomics supplies stable information on allelic and structural variation, whereas transcriptomics, proteomics and metabolomics progressively capture regulatory activity, functional molecular abundance and biochemical state. Their integration is therefore attractive, but the central breeding question is not whether more data can be combined; it is when added molecular layers improve causal inference, trait prediction or selection decisions beyond a strong genomic baseline. This critical narrative review evaluates evidence linking the four core omics layers in crop research, with emphasis on pangenome-aware genomics, expression and association mapping, proteome and post-translational regulation, metabolic endophenotypes, multi-block statistical integration, network models and machine-learning approaches. The literature indicates strong value for cross-omics integration in candidate-gene prioritisation, pathway reconstruction and mechanistic interpretation, particularly when genomic associations are anchored to expression, protein or metabolite variation measured in relevant tissues and environments. Evidence for routine prediction gains is less uniform. Metabolomic and transcriptomic profiles can be highly predictive in some populations, yet comparative studies show that combined multi-omics models may fail to outperform genomic prediction when molecular measurements are noisy, environmentally contingent, redundant with genetic relationships or evaluated without stringent out-of-environment validation. Proteomic integration adds biologically important information that is not reliably inferred from messenger RNA, but coverage, cost and post-translational complexity remain substantial constraints. The field is moving towards graph pangenomes, matched longitudinal sampling, interpretable multimodal models and integration with deep phenotyping and environmental covariates. The most defensible near-term strategy is consequently selective rather than maximal integration: deploy the molecular layer whose biological position and measurement reliability match the breeding question, validate improvements against genomic baselines, and prioritise designs that can demonstrate transfer across environments and breeding cycles.
journal: International Journal of Plant & Soil Science

title: Securing Enterprise AI Supply Chains: A Framework for Model Provenance, Third-Party Risk, and Compromised AI Components
abstract: Enterprises assemble AI systems from externally sourced models, datasets, libraries, agents and serving components whose origin and integrity they cannot directly observe. This study asks how provenance assurance, third-party dependency exposure and supply-chain governance relate to the disclosed-vulnerability record of such components, and argues that this record measures security observability as much as security risk. Drawing on resource dependence, information asymmetry and signalling theory, we assemble a cross-sectional secondary dataset of 1,321 widely used open-source AI/ML components (GitHub, deps.dev, OpenSSF Scorecard, OSV, PyPI statistics, CISA KEV) and the 1,000 most-downloaded Hugging Face models, and estimate negative binomial, logistic, hurdle and zero-inflated models with robust standard errors and influence and selection diagnostics. Disclosed advisories are rare but concentrated: 8.9% of components carry one yet attract 39.4% of monthly downloads, and advisory publication rose from 54 in 2023 to 486 in the first nine months of 2026. Advisory counts rise with ecosystem reach (incidence rate ratio 2.49 per log unit of stars), release activity and, in the Scorecard subsample, detection and disclosure practices (IRR 1.48 per index point), whereas hardening and provenance controls show no negative association. Disclosure therefore tracks scrutiny and transparency rather than the absence of defects, motivating a six-pillar framework in which continuous observability, not silence, is the basis for trusting AI components. We recommend that enterprises assess AI suppliers on verifiable provenance, safe serialisation and disclosure capacity rather than on advisory counts and embed AI bills of materials and exploitation-aware monitoring in continuous engineering controls, and that standards bodies distinguish disclosure capacity from vulnerability prevalence in AI risk frameworks.
journal: Journal of Engineering Research and Reports

title: Harnessing the Bacterial Membrane-Derived Oral Vaccine to Potentiate Antitumor Immunity and Metabolic Control of T Cells.
abstract: The fluctuating gastrointestinal milieu and its restrictive epithelial barrier represent critical challenges for the design of oral cancer vaccines. Nevertheless, leveraging the gut microbiome as an interventional strategy has recently gained traction, especially in patients on immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Here, microbial-derived double-layered membrane vesicles are developed as adjuvants and cell-free carriers, fused with cell-penetrating peptide-modified antigens, and encapsulated in an alginate/chitosan-microsystem to engineer oral vaccines. This design strategically harnesses the crosstalk between the gut microbiome and gut-associated lymphoid tissues, driving dendritic cell maturation, plasma cell activation, and production of immune-stimulatory cytokines within the mesenteric lymph nodes and lamina propria. In mouse prophylactic and therapeutic tumor models, the select Bifidobacterium bifidum-derived oral vaccine combined with anti-PD1 treatment enhances cytotoxic antitumor responses, along with Th1-, Th17-immunity, leading to potent tumor suppression, prolonged survival, and long-term protection against tumor rechallenge. Mechanistically, the vaccine promotes interferon-γ-producing T cells and antitumor efficacy with ICI therapy via the improved microbiota diversity and signaling metabolites, with an indole-3-acetic-acid (3IAA) enriched diet profoundly shaping T-cell recruitment and differentiation. Our findings uncover a tryptophan metabolite-driven immune axis that amplifies the specific antitumor immune response, redefining oral vaccines as a powerful tool for cancer immunotherapy.

title: A Biomanufacturing Digital Twin for Consistent N-1 Seed Bioreactor Transfers for Commercial Monoclonal Antibody Production.
abstract: Process consistency in biomanufacturing, particularly for commercial products, is critical for achieving consistent yield and product quality. The N-1 seed bioreactor stage, where cells grow before the transfer to a production bioreactor, often faces variability in final viable cell density (VCD), which leads to variable seeding densities in the production bioreactor and subsequent variability in total protein output per batch. In this study, we address the challenge of precise batch transfer by developing an upstream, stage-specific, level-2 digital twin (digital shadow). Here we show that a cell growth process model predicts growth accurately and updates forecasts using off-line and in-line measurements, enabling precise determination of the final sample time. Deployment of this seed transfer digital twin led to all N-1 to production transfers falling within acceptable limits and resulted in statistically significant increases in harvest yield relative to historical batches. This improvement is attributed to significantly higher on-target accuracy of final N-1 VCDs and significantly higher working volumes in the production bioreactors. Our findings demonstrate that such digital twins ensure consistent cell density during transfer, improve overall upstream process consistency, and lay a foundation for more advanced process control strategies.

title: Tourism Demand Prediction With Tourist‐Generated Images and Text: An Ensemble Sparse ELM Approach
abstract: This study examines the predictive value of tourist‐generated images and text for daily tourism demand forecasting. Building on established L 0 ‐regularized extreme learning machine (ELM) formulations and ADMM‐based sparse optimization, we construct an ensemble forecasting framework, termed ES‐ L 0 ‐ELM, that combines image‐derived and textual predictors with numerical variables. The framework integrates sparse output‐weight estimation with model selection and weighted aggregation. Experiments on Jiuzhaigou and Mount Siguniang show that ES‐ L 0 ‐ELM achieves lower forecasting errors than the evaluated benchmarks. On the Jiuzhaigou dataset, it reduces MAPE by 18.66% and 14.33% relative to recent tourism forecasting models BERT‐ELM and TFIDF‐Tran‐ELM, respectively. Image features provide greater predictive gains than text features, whereas their combination yields the best performance. This study provides a sparse ensemble forecasting framework and empirical evidence of the complementary value of tourist‐generated images and text.

title: MRI-Based 2.5D Multi-Instance Deep Learning for Differentiating Pathological Subtypes of Brain Metastases From Lung Cancer.
abstract: BACKGROUND Distinct treatment strategies for small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) and non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) brain metastases require accurate noninvasive subtyping. PURPOSE To develop and externally validate a biparametric MRI-based 2.5D multi-instance learning (MIL) deep learning (DL) model for discriminating SCLC from NSCLC brain metastases, with performance compared against clinical, radiomics, and 3D-DL models. STUDY TYPE Retrospective. POPULATION This study included 366 patients from four institutions. Center 1 provided the training set (n = 199; mean age, 63.88 ± 10.79 years; 72.36% male) and an internal tuning set (n = 85; mean age, 64.73 ± 9.53 years; 67.06% male). Centers 2-4 were pooled into a single external test set (n = 82; mean age, 62.26 ± 10.60 years; 63.41% male). FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE 1.5 T and 3.0 T; contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging and fluid-attenuated inversion-recovery imaging. ASSESSMENT The 2.5D-MIL model was benchmarked against clinical, radiomics, and 3D-DL models and evaluated on internal tuning and pooled external test sets. STATISTICAL TESTS Shapiro-Wilk, Student's t-test, Mann-Whitney U, chi-square, univariable and multivariable logistic regression, and DeLong tests were used. Performance measures included the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) with 95% confidence intervals and classification and calibration metrics. Statistical significance was defined as two-sided p < 0.05. RESULTS In the internal tuning set, AUCs were 0.842 (2.5D-MIL), 0.740 (clinical), 0.710 (radiomics), and 0.747 (3D-DL). In the external test set, AUCs were 0.826 (2.5D-MIL), 0.826 (clinical), 0.696 (radiomics), and 0.664 (3D-DL). Differences between 2.5D-MIL and the clinical (p = 1.000), radiomics (p = 0.139), and 3D-DL (p = 0.119) models were not significant. DATA CONCLUSION The MRI-based 2.5D-MIL model showed potential for noninvasive differentiation of SCLC from NSCLC brain metastases. Larger prospective studies are needed before clinical use. EVIDENCE LEVEL 3. TECHNICAL EFFICACY Stage 2.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI

title: The assembly pathway for human papillomavirus L1 capsid protein is encoded in electrostatic interactions.
abstract: Human papillomavirus L1 protein spontaneously folds and assembles into 60 nm virus-like particles (VLP), with T = 7d icosahedral symmetry at high salt concentrations but not in low salt. Rapid increase from low to high salt during the assembly process gives poor-quality VLPs, while slowly increasing salt, over as many as 48 h, gives rise to high-quality VLPs. Insight into this behavior is drawn from a computational model based on the cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structure of the human papillomavirus Type 16 VLP. Electrostatic potential energy barriers were calculated using the linearized Poisson-Boltzmann equation. After initial, rapid oligomerization of monomers into symmetrical pentamers (capsomeres), these units form pairwise interactions in energetic order, lowest barrier first. But at high salt concentrations, the energetic barriers are more or less equal and irregular particles form, both in simulation and in experiments. The interaction interfaces were modified by mutation to favor the smaller, 30 nm T = 1 icosahedral symmetry and disfavor T = 7d symmetry. The results were smaller particles. By carefully controlling ionic strength, and/or by mutating interface residues by design, it is possible to make high quality, highly immunogenic VLPs directly from unpurified bacterial lysate, without requiring the use of a disassembly/reassembly step.
journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society

title: Ultrasound-Responsive Hydrogels Empowered by Two-Dimensional Sonosensitizers Enable Spatiotemporally Controlled Fracture Fixation and Bone Regeneration.
abstract: Precise adhesion of bone fragments and robust bone regeneration are both essential for successful fracture healing, yet existing hydrogel adhesives rarely achieve controllable fixation and sustained osteogenesis simultaneously. Herein, we report a polyphenol-engineered ultrasound-responsive injectable hydrogel for fracture fixation and bone regeneration. The hydrogel is composed of dihydrocaffeic acid-modified chitosan, gelatin methacryloyl, a 2D sonosensitizer (PGO-Fe) constructed from polydopamine-mediated ferroferric oxide-decorated reduced graphene oxide, and polydopamine-modified hydroxyapatite (PHA). The hydrogel initially forms reversible, shape-adaptable adhesion to bone via catechol-mediated noncovalent interactions. Upon high-intensity ultrasound (HUS), PGO-Fe enhances sonodynamic activity through Fe(III)/Fe(II) redox conversion, triggering secondary covalent crosslinking and enabling a controllable transition from compliant adhesion to rigid fixation. Polyphenolic components confer reactive oxygen species-scavenging capacity and promote macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype, creating a favorable regenerative microenvironment. Under low-intensity ultrasound (LUS), the hydrogel activates Piezo1-mediated calcium influx, thereby enhancing osteogenic differentiation. In vivo, this system achieves nearly complete defect bridging and mechanical performance comparable to wire fixation in rat calvarial and rabbit ulna models. This work provides a minimally invasive strategy that integrates controlled fixation, immunomodulation, and mechanically enhanced osteogenesis for complex fracture treatment.

title: Genomic prediction of single cross families of perennial ryegrass under two nitrogen managements.
abstract: The performance of a single cross is determined by the additive effects of the parents and their interactions, which can be estimated through general combining ability (GCA) and specific combining ability (SCA). With genome-wide marker information, it is possible to predict GCA for new parents and the genetic value of unrealized crosses. Several studies in crops such as maize (Zea mays L.) and rice (Oryza sativa L.) have demonstrated the potential of genomic prediction for single-cross performance. However, no study to date has explored its relevance in perennial ryegrass (Lolium perenne L.), an obligate allogamous species bred in genetically heterogeneous families. In this study, we estimated genetic parameters and evaluated genomic prediction models for dry matter yield and nutritive quality traits in F2 family bulk. Data were obtained from a large partial diallel involving 104 parents from two genetically distinct subpopulations identified by admixture analysis. Families were evaluated across multiple environments under two nitrogen conditions. Genotyping-by-sequencing generated 42,145 high-quality variants used to estimate genomic relationships. Variance component analyses revealed limited GCA and SCA interactions with environment and nitrogen management. Predictive abilities of parental models exceeded 0.60 and often 0.70 for most traits, whereas including nonadditive effects did not improve predictive ability. Genome-wide association analyses identified six quantitative trait locus regions and 45 candidate genes within linkage disequilibrium intervals averaging 92 kb. Our results demonstrate that genomic prediction of single crosses in perennial ryegrass can achieve high accuracy, particularly when both parents are represented in the training population.

title: Wild boar collision data and satellite computer vision refine habitat suitability mapping across France
abstract: Wild boar (Sus scrofa) populations have expanded rapidly across Europe, leading to escalating human-wildlife conflicts (HWCs), notably wildlife-vehicle collisions (WVCs), increased agricultural damage and disease transmission. In continental France these issues are compounded by the species’ ecological adaptability exhibiting increasing overlaps with urbanization and transportation networks. In this study, we leverage time-series environmental data, computer vision and Species Distribution Modeling (SDM) to predict wild boar habitat suitability and investigate its spatiotemporal drivers. We use presence-only data from WVC reports on the national railway and road networks, along with publicly available GBIF observation collections, as complementary occurrence streams in our SDMs, while addressing inherent sampling biases of these datasets with tailored corrections. A key innovation of this study is the integration of national scale, annually updated high-resolution land cover predictors explicitly focused on wild boar resource preference. By fine-tuning a multitemporal Vision Transformer foundational AI model on multispectral satellite remote sensing imagery we capture subtle seasonal phenological differences. Our results highlight clear spatial, seasonal and annual variations in wild boar habitat suitability. The multitemporal SDM pipeline yields meaningful predictions when extrapolating to novel environmental scenarios such as climate extremes. Adding rail and road WVC records to GBIF-based SDMs retained high performance metrics while altering predicted spatial patterns and feature importance distribution. The methodological and ecological insights gained through this study provide additional knowledge for French transportation planning, agriculture and wildlife management. Identifying regions with high seasonal habitat suitability can inform targeted interventions. More broadly, our results demonstrate that advanced, data-driven methods are becoming indispensable for proactively and sustainably addressing HWCs in an increasingly anthropogenic world.

title: A novel approach for reliable differentiation of lymphatic endothelial precursor cells in vitro
abstract: The lymphatic system plays critical roles in fluid homeostasis, immune regulation, and lipid transport, making its dysfunction a contributor to numerous pathological conditions. Lymphatic tissue engineering aims to develop therapeutic strategies for lymphatic regeneration and repair, depending on the availability of suitable cell sources for lymphatic endothelial cell generation. Key cell sources explored for lymphatic tissue engineering include the dermis, bone marrow (BM) and stromal vascular fraction (SVF). To our knowledge, no existing differentiation protocols can accurately generate lymphatic endothelial precursor cells (LEPCs). This study presents a novel in vitro differentiation protocol for generating murine LEPCs from stromal SVF, dermis and BM-derived mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). The feasibility of using them as tissue sources was first evaluated leading to dermal cells exclusion due to low yield post-isolation, and highlighting the limited differentiation efficiency of BM-MSCs. SVF-derived LEPCs showed the most prominent results, exhibiting robust LEPCs differentiation and superior scalability. In vitro characterization confirmed that LEPCs maintain a distinct lymphatic endothelial phenotype, exhibiting high migratory capacity, robust capillary-like network formation, and consistent expression of key lymphatic markers across 2D and 3D cultures, supported by strong transcriptomic alignment as validated by RNA-Seq. Furthermore, in vivo modelling demonstrated their preclinical efficacy, as transplanted LEPCs integrated seamlessly into pre-existing lymphatic vessels within a wound-healing model. The protocol provides a consistent platform for studying lymphatic endothelial biology and potential applications in regenerative medicine and therapeutic angiogenesis.

title: Urban construction archive policy in China: historical evolution, instrument configuration, and contemporary challenges
Performance evaluation and interpretability of a Qwen LangGraph agent for AI written and AI rewritten text detection
abstract: The widespread adoption of large language models has increased the need to distinguish human-authored text from AI-generated content, including cases in which generated text is subsequently rewritten or paraphrased. In practice, many detectors output only a single AI-likelihood score or percentage, offering limited transparency and little indication of whether a passage appears directly AI-written (AIW) or AI-rewritten (AIR). This study presents an agentic detection framework for two connected tasks: binary provenance detection (Human versus AI) and conditional subtype detection (AIW versus AIR). The dataset combined the Human-ChatGPT Comparison Corpus (HC3) and the ai-text-detection-pile with 4,348 pre-generated AIR records produced by a single GPT-based rewriting workflow. The proposed Qwen–LangGraph AI agent was compared to a HashingVectorizer–TF-IDF–SGD classifier, DeBERTa-v3-xsmall, and ELECTRA-small. On the binary test set, DeBERTa-v3-xsmall achieved the best discrimination (99.4995% accuracy and 99.9911% AUROC), whereas the agent achieved 98.8816% accuracy and 99.9187% AUROC. On the AI-only test set (10,769 AIW; 1,274 AIR), the agent obtained the highest threshold-based accuracy (96.7367%), macro-F1 (90.0357%), and AIR F1 (81.8643%), but its AUROC (83.2507%) and AUPR (79.7336%) were lower than those of the DeBERTa-v3-xsmall and ELECTRA-small transformers. Paired DeLong and McNemar analyses with Holm correction showed that the agent improved threshold-based AIR performance over the lexical baseline. Interpretability was operationalised through lexical weights, linguistic and out-of-distribution diagnostics, sentence-level indicators, and route traces. The findings support the use of AI as decision support, not as automated proof of plagiarism or misconduct.

title: A comprehensive review and bibliometric analysis of deep learning applications in plant disease detection
abstract: Agriculture is a major component of many countries’ economies worldwide, especially in developing nations. The major challenge farmers face is the rapid spread of plant diseases, which often goes unnoticed and causes major yield and economic losses. Traditional methods such as human inspection and laboratory testing are often time-consuming, inaccurate, labor-intensive, and unsuitable for large-scale farming. To overcome these challenges, advanced technologies like Machine learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) have emerged in recent times, providing early and accurate detection of plant diseases. This paper focuses on recent advances in applying deep learning techniques, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), to detect plant diseases. Across 1081 publications from 2014 to 2024, studies show that CNNs are well suited to extracting and analyzing features from plant images and clearly distinguishing healthy from diseased specimens. The models discussed in the surveyed literature generally report performance in terms of key parameters such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, which this review compiles and discusses rather than benchmarking through new experiments. The results show high accuracy and strong potential for real-world agricultural applications. The bibliometric analysis reveals growing interest and collaborative efforts in the research domain, especially among institutions specializing in artificial intelligence and agriculture. Moreover, the results support the practical application of deep learning in agriculture for plant health monitoring and highlight the importance of comprehensive studies in solving agricultural problems. The study provides a foundation for further innovations in automated plant disease detection and supports the transition to smart farming solutions.

title: An opinion evolution prediction model based on graph attention and ordinary differential equations
abstract: Accurately predicting the dynamic evolution of user opinions on social media is important for understanding opinion diffusion mechanisms, identifying patterns of collective behavior, and supporting public decision-making. Existing opinion dynamics models provide interpretable descriptions of opinion evolution but rely on idealized assumptions and may not adequately capture the structural complexity of real-world social networks. In contrast, purely data-driven methods have strong approximation capabilities but lack explicit modeling of underlying social interaction processes. To address these limitations, we propose GA-ODE, an opinion evolution prediction model that integrates a graph attention mechanism with neural ordinary differential equation (ODE) constraints. GA-ODE adaptively learns differentiated aggregation weights for neighboring nodes through a graph attention mechanism and employs a gated evolution unit to balance individual opinion persistence and neighborhood assimilation effects. We further introduce a structure-aware ODE consistency regularizer based on probabilistic bounded confidence and incorporate the adjacency matrix into the dynamical residual as a topology-aware mask. Experimental results show that the topology-aware mask provides limited benefits on clean graphs but improves prediction performance under structural perturbations and helps maintain dynamical consistency in degraded network conditions. Evaluations under non-idealized dynamical settings further show that GA-ODE maintains prediction performance in the presence of opinion repulsion effects and external event shocks. Experiments on multiple synthetic datasets and one real-world dataset validate the effectiveness and robustness of GA-ODE. However, the model assumes that social interactions remain static within the observation window and is sensitive to sparsely represented classes.

title: Large language model multiagent systems for industrial problem discovery and prioritization
abstract: A persistent gap separates academic research priorities from the operational challenges faced by manufacturing firms. Established identification methods, among them Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) workshops, Lean audits and consultant engagements, are episodic, bounded by participant expertise and organised along departmental lines, which makes cross-departmental issues hard to surface. Multi-agent systems built on large language models (LLMs) have meanwhile shown collaborative problem-solving ability in software engineering and, more recently, in shopfloor scheduling and supply chain coordination. This article is a Perspective. It develops a framework and a research agenda; implementation and empirical evaluation fall outside its scope and are set out as its first research priorities. Three contributions are offered. The first is a synthesis of literature from industrial problem identification, LLM-based autonomous agents and manufacturing AI, which positions the proposal against existing industrial LLM agent work. The second is a framework in which six domain-specialised agents (production, quality, maintenance, supply chain, safety, energy) would collaborate through a five-phase protocol: worker-driven discovery, cross-departmental analysis, candidate-relationship detection, consensus-based financial assessment and debate-driven prioritisation. The prioritisation procedure is fully specified, including the normalisation of financial estimates, a measure of estimate dispersion, the derivation of criteria weights, a non-compensatory gate for safety-critical items and a mandatory human verification step. The third is a worked calculation on a hypothetical steel manufacturing vignette, included so that the procedure can be reproduced and scrutinised rather than as evidence of effectiveness. A preliminary qualitative readiness assessment and a three-horizon agenda of fourteen research questions complete the paper. The benefits identified are presented as hypotheses for that agenda to test rather than as demonstrated outcomes.

title: A lightweight explainable hybrid convolutional neural network for potato leaf blight detection
abstract: Potato (Solanum tuberosum), the fourth most abundant food crop in the world, is subjected to significant challenges due to diseases such as late blight, causing global annual yield loss exceeding $6.7 billion. Current methods of detection are time-consuming and frequently fail to identify early-stage infections. Deep learning, and particularly the Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) provide fast and scalable automation of disease classification compared to traditional methods. In this work, potato leaf diseases were classified by many CNNs such as XceptionNet, DenseNet121, a 5-layer CNN, a 6-layer CNN, and a custom hybrid CNN model (SpudNet5-R3). The datasets we used are as follows: (1) PlantVillage dataset was used and (2) PLD dataset which contains healthy, early blight, and late blight potato leaves. A full preprocessing pipeline was carried out which includes resizing, colour normalization, and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE). Targeted data augmentation strategies were applied to tackle the class imbalance. The models were trained, validated, and tested individually on three datasets and the input images were resized to 224 × 224. We analysed performance measures such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and inference time for finding the best model. In addition, Grad-CAM visualization was used to provide interpretable insights into the model predictions, showing the leaf regions that contributed to the classification. Experimental results show the strong competitiveness of our custom SpudNet5-R3 architecture, obtaining testing accuracy of 99.07% and macro F1-score of 99% on the PlantVillage (D1) potato dataset. It achieved also the testing accuracy of 95.56% and a macro f1-score of 96% on PLD (D2) dataset, demonstrating the successfulness of CNN architectures customized for robust and accurate recognition of the potato diseases.

title: AI literacy for AI natives? A four-country comparison
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly mainstream in children's homes and everyday lives. Using neo-ecological theory as a conceptual framework and Yang et al.'s (2026) five-component AI literacy progression model as an analytical lens, this document analysis examined core ECEC curricula and related guiding documents currently in use in Australia, China, Japan, and South Korea to determine whether early childhood education and care (ECEC) guiding documents are keeping pace with the rapid development. The analysis reveals that the curricula of Japan and South Korea contain no explicit reference to AI literacy, prioritising human-to-human relationships and offline safety. China's national ECEC guidelines similarly contain no AI references. However, Shanghai's strategic action plan explicitly positions kindergartens within broader AI education initiatives, though without specifying pedagogical progressions for young learners. Australia demonstrates limited and uneven alignment across AI literacy components, with the strongest alignment in “Interacting with AI Agents” and no alignment in “Understanding Human-AI Relationships”. Young children’s development of AI literacy is thus likely to remain contingent on the home environment, where they may be interacting with AI agents and creating artefacts more than developing awareness of ethical considerations and risks. Wide differences in children's foundational AI literacy capabilities may entrench educational disadvantage along the lines of AI literacy as it becomes increasingly mainstream in society. We argue that curriculum-guiding documents should be strengthened by articulating explicit AI literacy learning priorities and developmental expectations for young children, accompanied by culturally responsive resources to equip educators to facilitate equitable learning.

Some generalizations of the tornado model
abstract: A possible mechanism of tornado generation is associated with the Schwarzschild criterion for convective instability. The supercooled cloud-air mixture near the axis starts to descend and, due to the super adiabatic temperature gradient, the overheated near-surface air mass rises. The complete system of equations for full model includes equations for the stream function, for the azimuthal velocity component, and for the change in density. The refined model considers rotating convection within the framework of ideal hydrodynamics. The simplest model uses a separate equation for the stream function and can be applied to the initial stage of vortex generation. Within the framework of the simplest model, an analytical solution is combined from 8 linear dependencies by height. Rotation increases due to the conservation of angular momentum. Within the framework of the refined model, some unidirectional differential rotation arises, but it depends on boundary conditions (can be local). The full model studies the tornado development as rotating convection from the very beginning to the quasi-stationary stage. Velocity components increase in a coordinated manner. Two cases are considered: a single whirlwind and a two-eyed tornado. Radial flows converge towards the central part of the tornado near the earth surface, and there is an outflow from the "wall" to the axis and to the periphery near the top of the tornado. The maximum vertical velocity component is achieved at a certain radial distance at a certain height. The maximum azimuthal velocity component is achieved in the tornado "wall". Tornado generation criteria are discussed.

title: Review of AI agents in engineering design workflows
Stage-specific exposure to an activity-permissive medium enhances neuronal activity in oligodendrocyte-enriched cortical organoids.
abstract: Oligodendrocyte-enriched cortical organoids (OCOs) are a powerful platform for modeling oligodendrogenesis in a human cellular context. However, neuronal activity is impaired in conventional culture media, limiting assessment of neuronal function in conjunction with oligodendrocyte biology. To address this, we used a modified BrainPhys medium termed neuronal activity medium (NAM) and defined the optimal developmental window for NAM exposure to generate OCOs with robust neuronal activity (NAM-OCOs). Stage-specific exposure to NAM, prior to oligodendrocyte expansion, leads to enhanced structural complexity, as evidenced by increased organoid size, heightened synaptogenesis, and upregulation of transcripts associated with neuronal morphology. Further, NAM-OCOs display increased cellular heterogeneity, with GABAergic interneurons exhibiting enhanced inhibitory synaptic features and a more advanced developmental transcriptional state, while preserving oligodendrocyte development and oligodendrocyte-axon associations. Altogether, our studies demonstrate that stage-specific exposure to an activity-permissive environment enhances neuronal activity, establishing an OCO model which integrates neuronal activity with oligodendrocyte development and differentiation.

title: ED-71 ameliorates oxeiptosis-associated signaling in BMSCs under diabetic osteoporosis by alleviating PKM2-associated metabolic dysregulation and mitochondrial dysfunction.
abstract: Diabetic osteoporosis (DOP) poses a significant clinical challenge, characterized by elevated fracture risk linked to bone quality deterioration. The pathogenesis involves reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and metabolic dysfunction in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). This study investigates the role of oxeiptosis, a novel ROS-triggered, caspase-independent cell death pathway, in DOP and explores the therapeutic potential of Eldecalcitol (ED-71). In a type 2 diabetes mouse model, ED-71 treatment significantly ameliorated bone loss and suppressed the upregulation of oxeiptosis-associated molecular changes in BMSCs. In vitro, high glucose (HG) conditions induced oxeiptosis-associated signaling, mitochondrial dysfunction, a glycolytic shift, and impaired osteogenic differentiation in BMSCs. ED-71 intervention partially counteract these effects. Mechanistic studies predicted a potential molecular interaction between ED-71 and PKM2, a key regulator of glycolysis, which reduced its abundance and reversed metabolic imbalance. These effects were accompanied by improved mitochondrial function and enhanced Nrf2/GPX4-mediated antioxidant defense, ultimately suppressing the KEAP1/PGAM5/AIFM1 oxeiptosis-associated signaling. Pharmacological activation of PKM2 by TEPP-46 partially reversed ED-71's protective effects, supporting a functional involvement of PKM2 in the observed mechanism, although genetic validation is required to establish causality. In conclusion, ED-71 may alleviate mouse DOP by reducing PKM2 expression to correct metabolic reprogramming and mitochondrial dysfunction, thereby suppressing oxeiptosis and restoring HG-treated BMSCs' osteogenic potential, offering a novel mechanistic foundation for its therapeutic application.

title: Small phytopeptides: rising stars in broad-spectrum plant defense and sustainable crop protection
Evaluation of six generative large language models answering pre-analytical questions in medical microbiology.
abstract: OBJECTIVES Large language models (LLMs) have the potential to be integrated into diagnostics workflows, yet their reliability in pre-analytical diagnostic stewardship remains uncertain. We aimed to evaluate the performance of six LLMs answering common pre-analytical questions in the domain of medical microbiology. Next, we propose a blueprint to evaluate LLMs in medical microbiology. METHODS We compared general-purpose models from OpenAI (GPT-3.5, GPT-4) and Meta AI (Llama2-7B, Llama2-13B), alongside two domain-enhanced versions (customised GPT-4 agent and Llama2-7B Medical) in a hybrid evaluation framework. First, we quantified the response length (word count), then assessed the similarity between LLM-generated responses and expert-reviewed reference answers (BLEU/ROUGE scores, BERTScore). Finally, thirty-three medical professionals rated the accuracy and completeness of the LLM-generated responses on a 1-7-point scale. RESULTS Responses of OpenAI models showed greater similarity to the reference set and significantly outperformed Meta AI-based models in accuracy and completeness. The customized generative pre-trained transformer (GPT) matched performance of OpenAI's general-purpose models, while generating significantly shorter responses (p<0.001). Quality ratings varied markedly between professionals, as medical microbiologists and experienced infectious disease specialists assigned significantly lower scores compared to infectious disease trainees and medical students (p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS We observed considerable variation in LLM performance and highlight differences in perceived response quality across professional groups, emphasizing the need for critical appraisal when consulting LLMs for pre-analytical guidance.

Dock2 deficiency compromises erythroid differentiation of hematopoietic stem cells.
abstract: Anemia is a prevalent pathological characteristic observed in a variety of hematologic disorders, predominantly resulting from impaired red blood cell production or increased erythrocyte degradation. DOCK2, a pivotal guanine nucleotide exchange factor within the DOCK protein family, is uniquely expressed within the hematopoietic system. Previous research has established that the absence of Dock2 significantly disrupts the development and function of several immune cell subsets, including T cells, B cells, NK cells, and granulocytes. However, the role of DOCK2 in erythroid development and associated biological processes remains undefined. This study aimed to investigate the biological function and molecular mechanism of DOCK2 in erythropoiesis. We generated both global and hematopoietic-specific Dock2 knockout mouse models. Results from routine blood analyses and flow cytometry consistently revealed pronounced anemic characteristics in Dock2-deficient mice. Subsequent phenotypic evaluations preliminarily ruled out excessive erythrocyte apoptosis and exacerbated hemolysis as primary contributors to the observed anemia. The developmental defect was attributed to the aberrant differentiation of bone marrow hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs, Lin-Sca-1+c-Kit+). Subsequent bone marrow transplantation and in vitro colony formation assays demonstrated that the deletion of Dock2 led to a compensatory increase in the number of hematopoietic stem cells, while significantly impairing their intrinsic capacity for erythroid differentiation. Integrative transcriptomic and proteomic analyses further demonstrated significant downregulation of Pepd and Prkcd in Dock2-deficient mice, yet it remains unclear whether reduced Pepd and Prkcd expression regulates erythropoiesis. Further functional experiments are necessary to validate this hypothesis in future research. In conclusion, our study identifies DOCK2 as a critical regulator for maintaining normal erythroid differentiation in hematopoietic stem cells. The absence of Dock2 disrupts hematopoietic lineage commitment, resulting in a developmental arrest of the erythroid lineage and the onset of anemia. This research advances our understanding of the regulatory mechanisms underlying erythropoiesis and the pathogenesis of anemia. Additionally, it underscores the potential of DOCK2 as a promising therapeutic target for clinical anemic conditions.

title: Ginsenoside Rg1/Rb1 relieves periodontitis via inhibiting IKBKG -mediated NF-κB pathway to enhance COL1A1 expression.
abstract: BACKGROUND Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease driven by microbial dysbiosis, and effective pharmacological strategies remain limited. This study evaluated whether combined ginsenoside Rg1/Rb1 protects against periodontitis and whether this protection involves IKBKG-dependent NF-κB regulation with restoration of COL1A1. METHODS Periodontitis was induced in rats by steel-wire ligation plus Porphyromonas gingivalis lipopolysaccharide (Pg-LPS) challenge, followed by local gingival administration of Rg1/Rb1. In parallel, Pg-LPS-stimulated human periodontal ligament stem cells (hPDLSCs) were used to model inflammation-impaired periodontal ligament stem cells, and IKBKG was knocked down to test causality. RESULTS In vivo, Rg1/Rb1 dose-dependently attenuated periodontal inflammation and alveolar bone resorption, accompanied by reduced IL-6 and TNF-α levels, preservation of bone volume, up-regulation of IKBKG and COL1A1, and suppression of NF-κB activation. In vitro, Rg1/Rb1 preserved hPDLSC viability, restored osteogenic differentiation-related proteins (ALP, OCN, RUNX2, and COL1A1), and reduced inflammatory cytokine production. IKBKG knockdown abolished these protective effects, indicating that Rg1/Rb1 acts through IKBKG-dependent control of NF-κB signaling. CONCLUSION Combined ginsenoside Rg1/Rb1 alleviates periodontitis by coupling anti-inflammatory activity to restoration of COL1A1 and osteogenic differentiation-related programs through IKBKG-dependent NF-κB regulation, supporting its potential as a therapeutic strategy for periodontitis.

title: Effects of polysaccharides from the rhizome of Menispermum dauricum DC on alleviating chemotherapy-induced immune damage and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment associated with PD-1/PD-L1 regulation.
abstract: In this study, we established a metastatic tumor model by tail vein injection of fluorescent-labeled Lewis lung cancer cells. We systematically evaluated the in vivo antitumor effects of the rhizome of Menispermum dauricum polysaccharides (MDP), a homogeneous polysaccharide obtained through sequential chromatographic purification, its efficacy in alleviating cyclophosphamide (CTX)-induced chemotherapy damage, and its ability to improve the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). We also investigated whether its mechanism is associated with the PD-1/PD-L1 pathway. Concurrently, an in vitro tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) model was established to validate the regulatory effects of MDP on macrophage polarization. The results indicated that MDP effectively inhibits tumor growth and prevents metastasis in the metastatic tumor model. Combined with CTX, MDP alleviated CTX-induced weight loss and damage to the spleen and thymus while exhibiting synergistic antitumor effects by reducing the lung index and increasing the lung index suppression rate. In terms of immune regulation, MDP promotes Th1 differentiation, suppresses Th2 differentiation, reduces the proportion of Treg cells, and activates Th17 and CD8+ cytotoxic T cells, thereby improving the TME. It also promotes TAM polarization toward the M1 phenotype while inhibiting M2 polarization, significantly elevating the levels of M1 macrophage activators (LPS and IFN-γ) while decreasing those of M2 macrophage immunosuppressive factors (TGF-β and IL-10). This effect may be associated with the downregulation of PD-1/PD-L1 protein expression. In vitro experiments further validated the ability of MDP to induce TAMs to reverse from the M2 to the M1 phenotype. In summary, MDP shows significant immunomodulatory and antitumor potential, supporting its development as a polysaccharide drug for tumor treatment or adjuvant therapy.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Semi-Supervised Framework with Supervised Contrastive Learning for Sugarcane Leaf Disease Detection
abstract: Sugarcane leaf diseases severely impact crop yield and quality, making accurate and timely detection critical for sustainable agriculture. Conventional deep learning models for plant disease detection depend on large annotated datasets, which are expensive to obtain and challenging to prepare due to challenges commonly observed across crop disease detection tasks, including (i) high intra-class variation caused by diverse symptom expressions across growth stages, (ii) subtle inter-class similarities between diseased and healthy tissues, and (iii) the risk of noisy labels degrading model reliability. To handle these challenges, we presented an Uncertainty-aware Mean-Teacher based Semi-Supervised Learning Disease Detection Network (U-SSDNet) that leverages unlabeled data while maintaining robustness. First, discrete wavelet transform preprocessing is applied to enhance lesion visibility and reduce intra- class variation. Subsequently, the KL divergence is employed to refine the pseudo-labels and reduce the impact of confirmation bias. At the same time, supervised contrastive learning is applied to make the features more distin- guishable and improve the separation among different classes. Experimental evaluations on sugarcane leaf disease datasets, considered a representative case study, demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves performance close to that of fully supervised models while requiring far fewer annotated samples and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art supervised and semi-supervised approaches.

title: DynamicVis: Dynamic visual perception for efficient remote sensing foundation models
journal: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: The advancement of RS technology has enabled high-resolution Earth observation; however, interpreting these images using modern VFMs remains a significant challenge. Unlike object-centric natural images, RS imagery is fundamentally characterized by extreme target sparsity and massive spatial redundancy. Key objects of interest (e.g., ships, vehicles) often occupy less than 1% of the spatial extent, surrounded by vast, target-free backgrounds. Existing VFMs predominantly rely on uniform dense processing (e.g., ViTs) and pixel-reconstruction pre-training paradigms (e.g., MAE). These approaches inherently waste substantial computational capacity on modeling redundant backgrounds and inadvertently dilute the feature representations of small, sparse targets. To bridge this structural misalignment, we propose DynamicVis, a visual foundation model explicitly tailored to the sparse nature of RS imagery. Architecturally, DynamicVis introduces a Dynamic Region-Aware SSM that bypasses uniform computation. It adaptively routes and incrementally models only task-relevant, high-salience tokens while employing a parameter-free integration for background context, drastically reducing the complexity of processing ultra-long 2D token sequences ($\sim$100,000). Crucially, to equip the network with robust spatial-selection capabilities, we propose a novel Region-Level Meta-Embedding Multi-Instance Learning (MIL) pre-training paradigm. Trained on a million-scale dataset, this paradigm explicitly disentangles sparse foreground instances from dense backgrounds in the latent semantic space, overcoming the semantic ambiguity of conventional pixel-reconstruction methods. Extensive evaluations across nine diverse downstream tasks reveal that DynamicVis exhibits exceptional efficacy, particularly dominating in sparse-target and instance-level perception tasks (e.g., small object detection, and change detection).

title: Cultivation interruptions reduce fitness without consistently increasing phenotypic plasticity in an evolutionary reaction-norm model.
abstract: Phenotypic plasticity can buffer environmental change, but its evolution depends on cue reliability, fitness costs, genetic variation, and the duration of selection. We developed an individual-based Trait-Environment Fitness Interaction (TEFI) model to examine how cultivation interruptions affect absolute fitness and reaction-norm evolution. During interruptions, selection, reproduction, and mutation ceased, while damage accumulated and decayed after cultivation resumed. Across 100 replicate populations per scenario, long interruptions produced substantially lower final fitness than continuous cultivation. Seed-matched analyses showed lower mean fitness after intermediate and long interruptions, whereas 95% paired intervals for short and recurrent interruptions included zero. None of the baseline interruption scenarios clearly increased mean or final plasticity. Duration experiments, mechanism ablation, genetic-correlation tests, environmental controls, and global sensitivity analysis showed that the fitness response was robust, whereas the plasticity response was conditional. Damage and incomplete recovery contributed to the long-interruption fitness decline, whereas the direct cost of evolved plasticity contributed little. A clear plasticity increase occurred only when long interruptions were combined with strong directional environmental change. Across seven crop datasets, normalized plasticity was lower in rice and wheat than in the other five crops (difference = 0.102, hierarchical-bootstrap 95% interval: 0.072-0.177; exact one-sided permutation P = 0.0476), with the direction robust to alternative metrics and leave-one-dataset-out analyses. This provides a quantitative consistency test, not crop-specific validation of TEFI. Our results identify interruption duration, environmental direction, and recovery opportunity as determinants of post-interruption fitness and caution against assuming that cultivation interruption universally promotes greater plasticity.

title: β-Hydroxybutyrate alleviates intestinal aGVHD via remodeling gut microbiota-bile acid axis and inhibiting TLR4-NF-κB-driven Th1/Th17 differentiation.
abstract: The intestine is a major target organ in acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD), and its microbial homeostasis critically influences disease pathogenesis and progression. Emerging evidence indicates that beta-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) can remodel the gut microbiota and dampen pro-inflammatory immune activity. To investigate the therapeutic potential of BHB in aGVHD, we first reanalyzed publicly available transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing data from patients with aGVHD, which revealed that genes involved in ketone body metabolism and transport were significantly decreased in intestinal tissues. We then used a murine model of aGVHD to evaluate the therapeutic effects of BHB by clinical scoring and intestinal histopathological examination. To define the immunological and microbial mechanisms, we integrated flow cytometry and ELISA for Th1/Th17, intestinal tissue-resident T and circulating T cells assessment, and with multi-omics analyses, including fecal 16S rRNA sequencing, fecal metabolomics, and intestinal transcriptomics. We further explored whether BHB directly regulates T-cell migration and differentiation and therefore assessed its effects on Th1 and Th17 differentiation in vitro. BHB treatment reduced the clinical score of aGVHD, alleviated intestinal injury in mice, and showed effects similar to those of methotrexate (MTX). BHB also corrected gut microbial dysbiosis, enriched Akkermansia muciniphila, and ameliorated bile acid metabolism dysregulation. Moreover, BHB inhibited intestinal T cell migration and Th1/Th17 differentiation both in vivo and in vitro. Mechanistically, transcriptome sequencing suggested that suppression of the TLR4-NF-κB pathway may underlie these anti-inflammatory effects. In summary, BHB effectively alleviates intestinal damage in aGVHD mice, likely through coordinated microbial, metabolic, and immunological regulation, and may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for aGVHD.

title: SentiAgent: An agentic LLM framework for context-aware and explainable sentiment analysis.
abstract: Sentiment analysis has become a fundamental task in Natural Language Processing (NLP) due to the rapid growth of user-generated content across social media, e-commerce, healthcare, education, and customer feedback platforms. Despite the success of transformer-based models and Large Language Models (LLMs), existing approaches often struggle with contextual ambiguity, implicit sentiment, sarcasm, commonsense reasoning, and limited explainability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes SentiAgent, a novel Agentic LLM framework for context-aware and explainable sentiment analysis. The framework employs multiple autonomous agents that collaboratively perform contextual understanding, external knowledge integration, sentiment reasoning, and explanation generation. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets-SST-2, IMDB Reviews, Sentiment140, and Amazon Product Reviews-demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. SentiAgent achieved 97.43% accuracy, 97.18% precision, 96.95% recall, 97.06% F1-score, and 0.99 AUC, consistently outperforming conventional machine learning, deep learning, transformer-based, and standalone LLM models. Ablation studies further validate the contribution of each autonomous agent, while qualitative analyses highlight the framework's ability to produce transparent and interpretable sentiment predictions. The proposed framework provides a scalable and trustworthy solution for next-generation explainable sentiment analysis.•Introduces SentiAgent, a collaborative Agentic LLM framework for context-aware and explainable sentiment analysis.•Combines contextual understanding, external commonsense knowledge, and autonomous reasoning to improve sentiment prediction and interpretability.•Achieves state-of-the-art performance on four benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior accuracy, robustness, and transparency over existing approaches.

title: Maternal delivery of a MuSK agonist antibody reveals a novel strategy for understanding and treating early-onset neuromuscular diseases.
abstract: Congenital myasthenia (CM) comprises a group of neuromuscular diseases caused by mutations in genes responsible for the formation and function of neuromuscular synapses, including genes encoding neuronal Agrin, low-density receptor-related protein 4 (Lrp4), muscle-specific kinase (MuSK), downstream of kinase 7 (Dok7), and receptor-associated protein (Rapsyn). Although mouse models have been invaluable for studying neuromuscular diseases, including CM, early neonatal lethality, due to respiratory failure, has made it difficult to study disease progression or assess potential treatments. Previously, we demonstrated that postnatal delivery of a MuSK agonist antibody rescued neuromuscular synapses and prevented disease in a mouse model of Dok7 CM. To determine whether a MuSK agonist antibody could benefit other forms of CM, we delivered a MuSK agonist antibody to pregnant mice and thereby their progeny. Maternal delivery of a MuSK agonist antibody prevented neonatal lethality of Dok7 mutant mice, allowing the mice to survive for at least two months. Maternal delivery of a MuSK agonist antibody also rescued neuronal agrin mutant mice from neonatal lethality, but the mice failed to survive for two months, even after additional postnatal treatment with the agonist antibody. Partial and full denervation were prominent in rescued neuronal agrin mutant mice, suggesting that poor attachment and withdrawal of nerve terminals are responsible for their postnatal lethality. These findings indicate that neuronal Agrin has functions in synaptic differentiation and maintenance that are independent of MuSK activation. Classifications: Biological Sciences / Neuroscience.
