title: Lightweight frequency-aware hybrid vision transformer for fine-grained plant disease recognition
abstract: Plant diseases can substantially reduce crop yield and quality, while accurate disease recognition on edge devices remains challenging because images often contain subtle lesion textures and complex backgrounds. This study proposes a lightweight frequency-aware Dual-Embedding Hybrid Vision Transformer, termed DE-HVT, for fine-grained plant disease recognition. Here, “frequency-aware” does not denote an explicit or orthogonal separation into independent frequency bands. Instead, it refers to complementary frequency-biased processing by two spatially aligned embedding branches: OBPE preserves slowly varying structural cues, whereas the CDC-based TexPE branch has a zero response at zero spatial frequency under the linearised θ = 1 analysis and therefore exhibits difference-sensitive, high-pass-like responses to lesion boundaries and textures. Their outputs are fused by element-wise addition before MHSA, while ConvFFN introduces local spatial filtering after global token interaction. Experiments were conducted on the Plant Pathology and PlantVillage datasets using the same training and evaluation protocols for all compared models. Across three independent runs, DE-HVT achieved a mean Top-1 accuracy of 93.51 ± 0.44 % and a mean macro-averaged F1 score of 93.64 ± 0.40 % on the more challenging Plant Pathology dataset. On the controlled-background PlantVillage dataset, all evaluated models achieved near-ceiling recognition performance. The model contains 4.10 million parameters and requires 0.85 GFLOPs. On a Snapdragon 865-based mobile platform, it used 46.86 MB of memory and recorded a maximum observed inference latency of 111.96 ms per image. These results indicate that DE-HVT provides a favourable balance between recognition performance and computational efficiency within the evaluated datasets and under the tested mobile-device conditions.

title: Systematic vegetation index discovery for phenology-based crop mapping
abstract: The Systematic Vegetation Index Discovery (SVID) framework generates and evaluates large numbers of vegetation indices (VIs) by combining spectral bands with basic arithmetic operations. We evaluated whether systematically discovered indices could improve agricultural land-cover classification compared with conventional indices such as NDVI while reducing the dimensionality of multitemporal spectral data. We applied SVID to a 323.9 ha agricultural landscape in Andong, South Korea, containing rice paddies, pepper fields, and plastic-covered greenhouses, using 32 cloud‐free Sentinel‐2A images acquired during 2022. Of 1,328 candidate expressions, 1,144 produced numerically valid rasters. A separate Random Forest model was trained for each index using its 32‐date temporal profile and evaluated against 500 independent reference points withheld from training. Before ranking, 388 expressions were identified as algebraically identical to another expression, and a further 355 were strictly monotone transformations and therefore indistinguishable to a rank‐based classifier. The 1,144 indices consequently represented 401 distinct features. Several near‐infrared‐to‐visible ratio families outperformed NDVI. The best‐performing index, (NIR – Red)/(Green × Blue), achieved 97.0% overall accuracy and a Kappa coefficient of 0.873, compared with 94.4% and 0.734 for NDVI; this difference was significant by McNemar's test (p = 0.002). The improvement was concentrated in the greenhouse class, whose producer's accuracy increased from 58.6% to 84.5%. A model using all four raw bands across all dates (128 features) achieved 96.0% accuracy and was statistically indistinguishable from the best single index, demonstrating a four‐fold reduction in dimensionality without a detectable loss in accuracy. Rank positions were nevertheless unstable: ten of the 401 features were statistically tied with the best, and mathematically identical formulations differed by up to 3.4 percentage points because of finite‐precision effects. SVID can identify compact spectral representations that perform as well as or better than conventional indices and full multiband temporal models. However, the instability among top‐ranked indices suggests that results should be reported as index families with confidence intervals rather than as a single winner. Limitations include the use of one site, one year, and four spectral bands; broader testing across sites, years, and spectral configurations is needed.

title: Farmers market as public quick commerce infrastructure: a conceptual policy framework for digital transformation
abstract: The rapid digitalization of food retail through private quick commerce platforms has transformed urban food consumption patterns in India. Despite the investments in digital infrastructure, Uzhavar Sandhai (Farmers Market), a farmer-to-consumer direct marketing system in Tamil Nadu, is still limited to traditional physical markets. This study suggests a strategic rethinking of Farmers Market as a public quick commerce infrastructure layer, incorporating digital marketplaces, hyperlocal logistics and cooperative governance to boost farmer market competitiveness and promote public value, food system resilience and equitable digital market access. In this study, the Farmers Market Digital Platform model is developed by applying the conceptual policy design approach to convert the Farmers Market platform into a decentralized public quick commerce network. This study identifies the institutional, technological and governance reforms necessary to support the digital transformation of farmer markets using publicly governed digital infrastructure. This reorientation of Farmers Market to public digital infrastructure could form the policy roadmap for platformization of agriculture in Tamil Nadu, which would benefit small farmers, urban consumers, and municipalities and help alleviate inefficiencies in supply chains. As a conceptual policy framework, the proposed model has not been empirically tested and requires future pilot implementation and validation before adoption. The study contributes to the evolving literature on agricultural digitalization by offering a vision for the potential redesign of existing public agricultural markets as digitally enabled public service infrastructure, which can enhance farmer welfare and urban food system resilience.

title: Digital tax governance and resilient agricultural machinery investment: a lifecycle analysis of an upstream pathway to sustainable food systems in China
abstract: Tax incentives can support agricultural-machinery investment, but their value depends on taxable capacity, documentary evidence, and timing. We use a policy-calibrated single-case simulation of Company A to evaluate 432 prespecified lifecycle rules across ten demand-policy stress paths for 2026–2033. The model integrates value-added tax, corporate income tax, R&D incentives, tax-loss and credit vintages, investment timing, and model-implied adjustment exposure. Scenario weights are judgmental rather than estimated frequencies. The constrained rule combines 7% R&D, equipment and retrofit in 2026, straight-line tax depreciation, and no exemption-based separate accounting. Its expected NPV is CNY 16.82 million and its 20% lower-tail CVaR is CNY 12.61 million. Expected NPV is 5.40% higher than under Company A’s static plan but only 1.51% higher than under baseline compliance. Relative to baseline, CVaR is 5.82% lower and risk-adjusted NPV is essentially unchanged. These results are conditional on the stated parameters. The proposed food-system pathway is theoretical because machinery adoption, farm output, prices, diets, and nutrition are not observed.

title: PEAS-DeiT: Multi-Scale Spatial Attention Enhanced DeiT for Pea Leaf Disease Classification
abstract: Early and accurate detection of pea diseases is essential for reducing crop losses and supporting precision agriculture. Although deep learning methods have shown good performance in plant disease classification, CNN-based models may have limitations in learning long-range relationships and detailed disease features. In this study, an explainable transformer-based framework, named PEAS-DeiT, is proposed for automated pea leaf disease classification. The proposed approach integrates a multi-scale spatial attention mechanism into the Data-efficient Image Transformer (DeiT) architecture to enhance the representation of disease-related visual features. A unified pea leaf disease dataset (UPLDD) was constructed by combining multiple publicly available datasets, covering six classes, including five disease categories and healthy samples. The proposed model was evaluated against CNN-based and transformer-based architectures using five-fold cross-validation. Furthermore, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) analysis was performed to investigate the regions contributing to model predictions. Experimental results demonstrate that PEAS-DeiT achieved an accuracy of 93.11%, showing competitive performance compared with the evaluated CNN and transformer-based models. The gradient-based saliency analysis also revealed localized response patterns in several evaluated samples, providing qualitative insight into the image regions contributing to model predictions. Statistical analyses were conducted to evaluate the performance differences among the compared models. These findings indicate that PEAS-DeiT provides a competitive approach for pea leaf disease classification within the evaluated experimental setting.

title: Spatiotemporal Conditional Diffusion with a Vision-Language Model: Spatial Quality Modeling for Adaptive Fusion of Radar Forecasts
abstract: Combining diffusion forecasts requires decisions about which candidates to retain and how to preserve strong echoes. We propose STCD-VLM, which learns candidate subset quality for adaptive fusion of radar nowcasts. Six observations condition spatiotemporal conditional diffusion (STCD) to generate five candidate sequences covering 120 min. Radar descriptors and representations from a frozen Gemma 4 31B vision-language model (VLM) condition a shared quality network. The network evaluates all 31 nonempty subsets and selects one for the complete sequence, combining its mean and pixelwise maximum. Evaluation on 256 event groups from eight Chinese S-band radar collections yields critical success indices of 0.25871 and 0.12712 at 30 and 40 dBZ. Relative to five-candidate maximum aggregation, these scores increase by 0.04108 and 0.02185, while false alarm ratios decrease by 0.08070 and 0.08203; 15 km fractions skill scores improve by 0.08433 and 0.07822. Fixed five-candidate fusion accounts for most of the mean CSI improvement over maximum aggregation. Adaptive selection adds 0.00170 to this mean under the same fusion rule, with higher CSI30, lower false alarm ratios and slightly lower CSI40. A matched zero-VLM control has similar principal score estimates, leaving the independent benefit of VLM inputs to be established. These comparisons support a quality-guided fusion framework that improves strong-echo overlap and neighborhood coverage agreement relative to maximum aggregation, while producing an event-specific forecast through one sequence-wide subset decision.

title: A BOQ-Driven BIM-to-Python Workflow for Time-Dependent Construction Unit-Price Forecasting Under Inflationary Conditions
abstract: Cost estimation remains challenging under volatile market conditions and rapidly changing material prices. This study develops a BOQ-driven BIM-to-Python workflow for time-dependent construction unit-price forecasting by linking BIM-generated Bills of Quantities (BOQs) with a Python-based forecasting layer. The workflow is demonstrated using six structurally similar villas in Esentepe, Northern Cyprus, covering 33 construction-element price targets and historical price records from 1997 to 2023. For the principal recent-market case, seven observations from 2020 to 2023 were used to predict an external March 2024 holdout. Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression was compared with Random Forest, support vector regression, quadratic regression, and a last-observed-price persistence benchmark. Random Forest achieved the lowest external-holdout mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 5.45%, compared with 6.37% for persistence and 9.38% for OLS. Expanding-window validation across 99 historical predictions yielded MAPEs of 20.23% for persistence and 20.98% for OLS, indicating performance variation across market periods. Training-window sensitivity showed that the 2020–2023 OLS window produced the lowest March 2024 error among the historical windows examined. The 2024–2029 outputs are therefore presented as long-horizon trend scenarios rather than externally validated forecasts. The findings support a data-linked, BOQ-driven workflow that combines BIM project information with a model-agnostic forecasting layer while explicitly acknowledging uncertainty in long-term extrapolation from sparse price data.

title: YOLO-Based Leaf Disease Detection in Smart Agriculture: Evolution, Task Adaptation, and Deployment Challenges
abstract: Computer vision-based leaf disease detection has become an important technical approach in smart agriculture and agricultural inspection services. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning have provided effective solutions for automated leaf disease monitoring, and You Only Look Once (YOLO)-based detectors have attracted increasing attention for balancing detection accuracy and inference speed. However, leaf disease detection remains challenging because lesions often occupy small regions, exhibit subtle visual features, have blurred boundaries, and appear against complex backgrounds, with considerable variation under field conditions. To address these challenges, numerous studies have improved lightweight backbones, feature fusion mechanisms, attention modules, detection heads, loss functions, and training strategies. This critical narrative review examines YOLO-based leaf disease detection, organizing reported adaptations by task characteristics and interpreting their outcomes in relation to datasets, annotations, and evaluation conditions. Representative studies report gains in detection performance, model compactness, or measured inference speed, together with trade-offs that depend on the task and configuration. Nevertheless, several challenges remain, including limited dataset diversity, insufficient cross-crop and cross-environment generalization, inadequate consideration of annotation uncertainty, biased evaluation of lightweight models based only on parameter reduction, and the gap between benchmark performance and real-world deployment. Future research should focus on task-oriented optimization, robust visual perception, improved model generalization, and efficient deployment toward intelligent agricultural monitoring systems.

title: Evaluating the Robustness of Zero-Shot Time Series Models Against Data Degradation in Industrial Sensor Streams
abstract: Zero-shot time series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast unseen series without target-specific training, offering a way to significantly reduce the deployment overhead in enterprise pipelines and industrial sensor streams. However, their performance is documented almost exclusively on pristine benchmarks, whereas industrial data streams feature missing values, sensor outages, and amplitude spikes. Whether these models absorb such faults natively, and thus whether costly imputation stages can be removed, remains unquantified. In this study, we evaluate the robustness of three TSFMs from distinct architectural families, Chronos (tokenization), TimesFM (patching), and TiRex (xLSTM), subjecting their context windows to random missing data, contiguous block missingness, and injection of point anomalies at escalating severities and assessing point accuracy (relative RMSE) and 80% interval reliability (PICP) against a clean baseline. The results show that random dropout and transient spikes are natively absorbed by all three models (accuracy loss below 3%), while sustained contiguous outages are the dominant failure mode, with patch-based TimesFM most exposed (up to 59%). TiRex stays well calibrated throughout, while tokenization-based Chronos yields persistently overconfident intervals. These patterns persist and the contiguous outage vulnerability is amplified on data with genuine operational anomalies. For the evaluated models, sensor streams, and tested corruption severities, the results indicate that direct inference remains close to the clean-context baseline under independent random loss and sparse positive spikes, whereas prolonged outages warrant additional missing-data handling.

title: Geomaterials and GPR Characterisation of the Castellina Fortress (Norcia, Umbria, Italy): Construction and Reconstruction from the 1500s to the Present
abstract: An integrated petrographic–geophysical workflow is applied to the Castellina Fortress (16th century AD) to investigate: the masonry texture, construction techniques and lithological provenance. The field activities focused on several architectural structures of the Castellina, including the main façade that was embedded inside the fortress out of a previous building, named Podestà Palace (13th century AD). The petrographic analyses document the use of lithoid limestones from the Maiolica, Scaglia Bianca and Scaglia Rossa Formations (Umbria–Marche Stratigraphic Succession) in the Podestà Palace, while limestone breccias can be mainly found in the cloister columns. The Ground-Penetrating Radar (GPR) data, supported by advanced numerical modelling, show a heterogeneous internal texture in the Castellina Fortress related to the use of both lithoid materials and earthquake-derived debris for the columns. The provenance analysis points out that the limestones were quarried from Monte di Colle, Monte Belvedere and Monte Poggio Vallaccone (southeast of Norcia), whereas the breccias largely derived from debris cones composed of breccia, gravel, and conglomerate deposits that still crop out today in the mountainous area surrounding the plains of Norcia and Santa Scolastica. This study demonstrates the potential of combining two different geoscience disciplines to reconstruct material supply zones and building characteristics in the field of cultural heritage.

title: Financial Resilience Under a Major Gold-Price Regime Shift: A Benchmark-Based Assessment of Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Econometric Models
abstract: Machine-learning and deep-learning models are increasingly applied to financial-market forecasting, yet their reported accuracy is often measured in price levels and rarely tested against a stringent benchmark under changing market conditions. It therefore remains unclear whether added model complexity delivers genuine, resilient predictive value or merely reflects the persistence of the underlying price series. This study addresses that gap by evaluating one-day-ahead gold-price forecasts within a transparent, leakage-resistant, benchmark-centred framework during a major structural regime shift. Using daily COMEX gold futures (2014–2026), we compare Ridge Regression, SVR-RBF, Random Forest, GARCH(1,1), and a bidirectional LSTM against a naïve random walk, with ARIMA and exponential-smoothing benchmarks, using strictly chronological splitting, training-only preprocessing, a return-space target, and two-sided and one-sided Diebold–Mariano tests. Structural-break analysis confirms a pronounced regime shift, with the gold price rising from roughly USD 1051 to USD 5318/oz and volatility breaks falling inside the out-of-sample period. All models attain near-unity price-level R2 but non-positive return-space R2, and none of the flexible models significantly outperforms the naïve benchmark; only a heavily regularised linear model shows a marginal one-sided edge attributable to gold’s upward drift rather than to learned structure, while GARCH’s contribution lies in calibrated uncertainty rather than point accuracy. Increasing model complexity did not yield resilient incremental predictive value, and the study offers a reproducible template for benchmark-based evaluation of forecasting systems.

title: Comparative Time-Series Modeling and Short-Term Forecasting of Electric Arc Furnace Voltage Using Hybrid and Deep Learning Approaches
abstract: Accurate modeling and short-term forecasting of electric arc furnace (EAF) voltage are important for power quality analysis, process monitoring, and the development of data-driven compensation and control strategies. The strongly nonlinear and time-varying behavior of the electric arc makes its voltage difficult to represent using simplified analytical or low-order parametric models. This study compares several modeling approaches using industrial voltage and current measurements acquired on the secondary side of a three-phase furnace transformer. The investigated methods include a hybrid Fourier–polynomial model optimized by a genetic algorithm, a CNN–GRU model, LSTM and BiLSTM networks, and a Dilated CNN–BiLSTM architecture. The models are first evaluated for same-interval voltage estimation over a common measurement interval using RMSE, MAE, R2, and a current-interval V–I RMSE. A separate direct multi-horizon forecasting experiment is then performed using a 40 ms historical voltage–current window and prediction horizons of 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 40, and 60 ms. Persistence and one-period predictors are used as reference baselines. For same-interval estimation, the Dilated CNN–BiLSTM achieves the lowest mean errors across three independent runs, with an RMSE of 5.33 ± 0.59 V, an MAE of 4.13 ± 0.44 V, an R2 of 0.99986 ± 0.00003, and a current-interval V–I RMSE of 1.70 ± 0.41 V. The BiLSTM obtains the next-lowest mean RMSE, 9.26 ± 4.25 V. In the forecasting task, no single neural architecture achieves the lowest RMSE at all prediction horizons. The BiLSTM provides the lowest neural model RMSE at 5 and 20 ms, the LSTM at 2, 10, and 60 ms, while the BiLSTM and Dilated CNN–BiLSTM yield nearly identical RMSE values at 1 ms. At 40 ms, the one-period baseline produces a lower RMSE than the neural models. The results show that forecasting performance is strongly horizon-dependent and that increased architectural complexity does not necessarily guarantee lower forecasting error. This study also demonstrates the importance of distinguishing same-interval voltage estimation from true future forecasting when evaluating EAF voltage models.

title: PySkyLumos: A Python-Based Polarized Skylight Simulator
abstract: This paper presents PySkyLumos, an open-source Python framework for simulating skylight polarization measurements and metadata. It implements the Rayleigh, Berry, and Pan models, covering single scattering, the splitting of the neutral points caused by multiple scattering, and the elevation-dependent motion of these points. Benchmarks show a fivefold overall speed-up and up to two orders of magnitude faster Stokes-parameter image formation than a recent open-source simulator. Validation against real polarization-camera images shows close agreement between the simulated and measured polarization patterns, supporting its use in algorithm development for bio-inspired computer vision, navigation, robotics, and sensing.

title: Dual-Domain Fusion for Small-Object SAR Ship Detection in Complex Scenes
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) ship detection is essential for maritime surveillance, yet coherent speckle can obscure tiny offshore vessels, while high-response coastal structures can produce target-like responses. Repeated downsampling further weakens sparse vessel signatures, whereas a separate high-resolution prediction head increases dense prediction costs. We propose a dual-domain detector that embeds spatial–frequency encoding, multiscale refinement, and high-resolution feature transfer within the backbone–neck–pyramid representation. Scharr-derived boundary cues are coupled with learned frequency context and remain discriminative as features are fused across scales, while sample-preserving space-to-depth transformation and global–local receptive-field modeling integrate shallow detail into semantically stronger P3 features without introducing a separate P2 prediction head. Coordinated FSEM, MSFE, and SOEP modules preserve fine vessel structure and reduce clutter-induced ambiguity throughout the detection hierarchy. Experiments on SSDD, HRSID, and RSDD-SAR evaluate detection accuracy, cross-dataset transfer, limited-data behavior, sensitivity to controlled perturbations, and edge deployment. Across 30 seed-matched SSDD runs, the method improves mAP50:95 over the baseline by 2.70±0.34 percentage points. It achieves 69.3% and 71.5% mAP50:95 on HRSID and RSDD. On the Atlas 200I platform, the compiled FP16 model retains 69.3% mAP50:95 while running at 101.8 frames/s.

title: MTC-TCN-Attn: A TCN-Attention-Based Multi-Task Collaborative Prediction Method for Wheat Soil Moisture
abstract: Wheat is one of the most important staple crops worldwide, and soil moisture plays a critical role in regulating crop growth, irrigation management, and agricultural water-use efficiency. Accurate soil moisture prediction is therefore essential for precision agriculture and intelligent irrigation scheduling. However, soil moisture variations are driven by complex interactions among meteorological conditions, soil layers, and temporal dynamics, resulting in strong nonlinear characteristics and long-term dependencies that remain challenging for conventional prediction approaches. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Multi-Task Collaborative Temporal Convolutional Network with Attention (MTC-TCN-Attn) model for multi-variable wheat soil moisture prediction. The proposed framework integrates a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) with a multi-head self-attention mechanism, where causal and dilated convolutions are employed to capture multi-scale temporal dependencies, while the attention module adaptively identifies informative time steps and enhances global temporal feature representation. Furthermore, a multi-task collaborative learning strategy based on shared feature representations is developed to exploit the intrinsic correlations among multiple soil-moisture-related variables and improve model generalization. Experiments conducted on wheat field data demonstrate that the proposed MTC-TCN-Attn model outperforms representative benchmark models, including SVR, LSTM, Transformer, and Multi-Task Long Short-Term Memory (MT-LSTM), across all five prediction targets in terms of R2, RMSE, and MAE. For the three principal soil-moisture-state variables, the proposed model achieved R2 values of 0.9147, 0.9651, and 0.9622 for surface soil moisture (SSM), subsurface soil moisture (SUSM), and soil moisture profile (SMP), respectively. Compared with single-task and multi-task TCN baselines, the proposed MTC-TCN-Attn model consistently reduces prediction errors and improves robustness by effectively integrating temporal dependency modeling and cross-task information sharing. The results indicate that the proposed framework provides an effective approach for multi-variable soil moisture forecasting and has promising potential for intelligent irrigation management and precision agricultural applications.

title: Environmental Sensing and Borrower Feature Interaction for Uncertainty-Aware Loan Risk Prediction Under Extreme Climatic Conditions
abstract: Extreme climatic events, including severe heatwaves, prolonged droughts, and anomalous flooding, can substantially disrupt agricultural production stability and further increase the risk of agricultural loan default. To address the limitations of conventional credit assessment in fully exploiting environmental sensing information, the scarcity of extreme-disaster samples, and fluctuations in sensing quality, a robust default risk prediction framework integrating agricultural environmental sensing observations, borrower-feature interactions, and uncertainty-aware learning is proposed. First, environmental exposure features and borrower-specific attributes are separately extracted through a dual-branch encoding network, and bidirectional cross-attention is employed to capture nonlinear interactions between climatic conditions and borrower risk. Subsequently, a climate-constrained disaster scenario augmentation mechanism is introduced to expand extreme-environment samples under regional, seasonal, crop-growth-stage, and inter-variable relationship constraints. A stabilized weighting strategy is further constructed by combining stochastic prediction with uncertainty estimation, thereby reducing the influence of highly noisy samples and anomalous observations on model training. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a PR-AUC of 0.791, a ROC-AUC of 0.909, and an F1-score of 0.781 under the combined evaluation of normal and extreme climatic conditions, while attaining a Brier Score of 0.098 and an ECE of 0.027. Under degraded sensing conditions involving missingness, noise, and bias, the model maintains high discriminative capability (PR-AUC of 0.758, ROC-AUC of 0.891, and F1-score of 0.756) and well-calibrated risk estimates (Brier Score of 0.112 and ECE of 0.031). Disaggregated evaluations across perturbation types, sensitivity analyses regarding spatial matching and synthetic labeling, external temporal holdout and cross-regional validations, and post-hoc feature attribution analyses further confirm the robustness and practical interpretability of the framework. Overall, the proposed framework consistently outperforms Logistic Regression, SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, DNN, LSTM, Deep Ensemble, and the previous model.

title: Toward Resilient Rural Resource Governance: A Cost-Effective, Data-Driven IoT System for Sustainable Beehive Monitoring and Management
abstract: Beekeeping occupies a challenging intersection: it is economically vital across vast, under-served rural areas, yet the tools available to manage it rarely match that scale. This paper presents a low-cost, solar-powered IoT system designed to address this gap. Rather than treating beehive management as a narrow agricultural concern, the system frames it as a case study in distributed, data-driven resource governance. Each hive is fitted with an ESP32-based sensor node that tracks temperature, humidity, and equivalent CO2 (eCO2), while solar-powered base stations provide GPS positioning and intrusion detection. All components are connected through a tiered wireless architecture: a 100 m 2.4 GHz RF sensor link connects individual hive nodes to solar-powered base stations, which forward aggregated telemetry to the cloud over a 120 m Wi-Fi or cellular uplink. The system was evaluated in an active apiary across five hives and two solar-powered base stations, which operated continuously for two weeks without failure, including during periods of darkness. The sensors are supported by a four-layer backend architecture that converts raw readings into real-time alerts and monitoring dashboards, providing a decision-support layer designed to assist beekeeping associations and agricultural authorities. The modular backend enables these organizations to coordinate operations, such as pesticide-spraying schedules and hive density across branches, while establishing a practical software foundation for future integration of AI-based analytics and additional sensing modalities. Taken together, the results present a practical, low-cost model for extending resilient, sustainable resource monitoring into rural and agricultural settings, with direct relevance to Saudi Arabia’s beekeeping sector and potential applications in similar deployments elsewhere.

title: Cyclospora cayetanensis at a crossroads: A critical re-evaluation of foundational assumptions in research and public health
abstract: Cyclospora cayetanensis remains a poorly controlled foodborne pathogen despite decades of research and major advances in molecular detection and genomic characterization. This review critically re-evaluates three foundational assumptions that continue to shape research, diagnostics, and public health practice. First, the widespread use of Eimeria and Cryptosporidium as surrogate organisms is examined in light of the limited direct validation of their ability to reproduce key biological characteristics of C. cayetanensis, particularly with respect to sporulation, environmental persistence, and intervention efficacy. Second, emerging phylogenetic and genomic evidence indicates that human-infecting Cyclospora comprises multiple genetically distinct lineages with reproductive isolation, raising important questions regarding taxonomy, epidemiology, transmission, and virulence. Third, the host-parasite-immune axis remains incompletely understood, particularly the mechanisms underlying the greater severity, persistence, and recurrence of infection in immunocompromised individuals. Across these three areas, the evidence reveals a persistent gap between what can be detected and what can be effectively prevented or controlled. The review therefore proposes a translational research framework that links foundational biological investigation to intervention development, implementation, and public health practice. Key priorities include direct validation of surrogate models, improved genomic resolution, standardized methods for assessing oocyst viability and infectivity, stronger agricultural water and on-farm controls, real-time molecular surveillance and traceback, and improved therapeutic and preventive strategies for vulnerable populations. Progress in controlling cyclosporiasis will require a shift from predominantly descriptive research toward evidence-based, actionable approaches that translate biological and technological advances into measurable reductions in transmission and disease.

title: Regional Competitiveness and Agricultural FDI Intention: Evidence from Vietnam’s Red River Delta
abstract: This study investigates the determinants of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) intention in the agricultural sector of Vietnam’s Red River Delta. Drawing on regional competitiveness theory, it develops a conceptual model in which agricultural infrastructure, FDI attraction policies, and human capital influence FDI intention indirectly through the mediating role of regional FDI attractiveness. Data were collected from 307 senior managers and board members of foreign agribusiness firms operating in the region. Structural equation modeling results indicate that agricultural infrastructure, supportive FDI attraction policies, and human capital significantly enhance regional FDI attractiveness, which in turn exerts a strong positive effect on FDI intention. Bootstrapped mediation analysis confirmed the significant indirect effects of these factors via FDI attractiveness. Multi-group analysis further revealed sectoral differences, with human capital playing a particularly important role in animal husbandry compared to crop production. This study extends regional competitiveness theory to the context of agricultural FDI at the subnational level in a developing economy. It establishes FDI attractiveness as a key mediating mechanism linking physical, institutional, and human resources to investors’ intentions, moving beyond static locational advantages to emphasize dynamic regional capabilities. For provinces in the Red River Delta seeking to attract high-quality, technology-oriented foreign capital into agriculture, the study underscores the value of integrated strategies and subsector-specific approaches to foster sustainable agricultural development and value-chain integration.

title: A comparative review of machine learning models and deep learning architectures for pregnancy progression prediction
abstract: Monitoring the course of pregnancy is of paramount importance, enabling the identification of negative outcomes and clinically significant changes. Although parity status may contribute to information needs, status as first-time mothers is not considered as a causal determinant. This paper presents a structured scoping review comparing conventional and deep learning approaches to pregnancy-related prediction tasks. The reviewed machine learning models include logistic regression; random forest; Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost); Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and their gated variants, long short-term memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs); Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs); transformers; and hybrid architectures. The analysis employs six dimensions: performance; ability to encode temporal data; model interpretability; data requirements for training; computational costs; and clinical relevance. As primary studies report outcome-specific performance results, the findings are presented across outcome domains rather than aggregated rankings of model architectures. In a study on predicting preterm-birth outcomes, a transformer achieved a test-set Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUROC) of 0.792, compared to 0.78 for logistic regression, 0.751 for random forest, and 0.717 for a Support Vector Machine (SVM). In predicting preeclampsia, a CNN achieved an AUC of 0.85 on holdout validation and 0.81 on an external test set, with an AUC of 0.98 for early-onset preeclampsia. CTGFusionNet, which employs a hybrid architecture of convolutional, recurrent, and attention layers applied to Cardiotocography (CTG) and clinical records, reported 97.85% accuracy for the task of fetal-distress classification. The findings highlight the complementary strengths and weaknesses of conventional and deep learning models for the analyzed tasks. The choice of an architecture should be informed by the target outcome, data type, volume, and quality, calibration and validation strategies, requirements for interpretability and fairness, and computational costs rather than a singular emphasis on performance.

title: Evaluation of grain sorghum accessions for the breeding of multipurpose varieties in the Lower Volga Region
abstract: Introduction. Due to climate aridization, interest in grain sorghum is increasing in arid regions of the country, including the Lower Volga region of the Russian Federation. The potential of grain sorghum as a multipurpose crop is being realized in various areas of the agro-industrial complex, such as forage production, food production, and the starch and syrup processing industry. The development of new productive grain sorghum varieties adapted to biotic and abiotic stressors is impossible without utilizing the rich diversity of genetic resources in the global plant material collection at VIR, which forms the foundation for developing new varieties. The research object and methods. The research was conducted in 2023-2025s on the experimental field of the Rossorgo. The study analyzed 38 collection accessions of grain sorghum of various ecological and geographical origins, assessed for morphometric parameters and grain productivity indicators. Statistical analysis of the data was performed in Agros 2.09 program using the “statistical analysis of a sample” method. The goal of the research was to analyze grain sorghum accessions from the VIR nursery collection for the purpose of developing productive varieties and hybrids for various applications. The results and discussion. High variability of grain sorghum accessions in morphometric parameters and productivity elements was established. The following samples were noted by the weight of 1000 seeds, distinguished by large grain size: k-4075, k-2058, O-k-8803/1 with 31.83-36.22 g, as well as valuable constant samples, characterized by increased grain yield – 06-2037, k-9115, k-2058, O-k-8803 (1) (4.72-5.11 t/ha) and biomass – k-9115, k-10112, B-03-3003 (17.69-19.85 t/ha). Conclusion. Among the studied collection of grain sorghum, three accessions – K-2058, O-K-8803/1, and K-4075-are particularly valuable. They possess a combination of valuable traits: large grain size, high grain yield, significant starch content (71.0-75.0%), light white-blue seeds, and stable annual seed maturation. All these characteristics correspond to those of a model variety optimal for processing into starch and starch products.

title: Smart Plant Disease Detection Using Deep Learning
abstract: Plant diseases can damage crops and reduce both the quality and quantity of agricultural production. Finding a disease early is important because farmers can take action before it spreads. However, checking plant leaves by looking at them manually is not always easy, especially when different diseases have similar symptoms. This research presents a Smart Plant Disease Detection system that uses deep learning and image classification. The system is designed to identify tomato leaf conditions from images and classify them into three categories: Healthy, Early Blight, and Late Blight. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) was trained using a plant disease image dataset. The images were prepared and used to teach the model the visual patterns of different leaf conditions. The trained model was tested with a new image and successfully identified the condition of the leaf. In the project test, a healthy tomato leaf was predicted with 99.99% confidence. A simple Gradio interface was also created, allowing a user to upload a leaf image and get a prediction. The system can make plant disease identification quicker and easier and may help farmers and other agriculture-related users take early action..

title: An Agricultural Skid-Steering Robot for Tomato Leaf Disease Detection and Targeted Pesticide Spraying: An Updated Prototype and Current Technology
abstract: Agricultural workers may be exposed to pesticides during conventional crop-protection operations, while timely identification of leaf diseases remains important for effective crop management. This paper presents an updated discussion of an agricultural skid-steering robot originally developed for tomato-leaf disease identification and targeted pesticide spraying. The prototype combines a four-wheel skid-steering platform, ultrasonic sensing, an MPU6050 inertial sensor, Arduino Nano control, ZigBee communication, MATLAB-based image processing, K-means clustering and an artificial neural network (ANN) classifier. Tomato-leaf images representing healthy leaves, bacterial spot, early blight, late blight and leaf mold are processed through image acquisition, preprocessing, colour-space transformation, clustering, segmentation, feature extraction and classification. The detected disease condition is then communicated to the robot controller, which activates the pump for the corresponding programmed spraying interval. The original prototype demonstrated the feasibility of integrating image-based disease recognition with a mobile agricultural platform. The present manuscript retains the original prototype observations while adding a current technology perspective. Recent studies show a transition toward YOLO-family detectors, lightweight deep-learning models, edge AI, autonomous navigation, multi-sensor perception and variable-rate robotic spraying. These developments identify practical pathways for extending the prototype toward real-time field deployment without claiming that such newer technologies were implemented in the original system.

title: Non-contact lens metrology from optical flow and differentiable ray tracing
abstract: Accurate lens surface metrology is essential to determine the manufactured geometry of refractive optical elements and their deviation from the specified design. We demonstrate a transmission metrology method that reconstructs refractive lens surfaces from the displacement of a wavelet-noise-patterned mask. Lens-induced distortion is represented by a dense displacement field. A differentiable ray tracer fits the lens geometry using a calibrated near-telecentric camera model with an effective finite ray origin. We validate the method on commercial lenses. The recovered geometries agree with nominal specifications, and the plano-aspheric reconstruction is compared with chromatic confocal profilometry.

title: Discovery or Memorization? A Faithful Benchmark for Real-World Business-Logic Vulnerability Discovery
abstract: The rapid advancement of cybersecurity agents in vulnerability discovery has increased the need for benchmarks that evaluate their capabilities accurately. However, synthetic benchmarks lack realism, real-life benchmarks are prone to contamination, and many existing benchmarks have already been saturated by current models. We therefore set out to develop a benchmark that is realistic, reproducible, resistant to contamination, and challenging. Our key insight is that real-life business-logic vulnerabilities are subtle and exercise complex application interactions, making them naturally demanding. The difficulty lies in specifying evaluation criteria precise enough to faithfully measure model capabilities while keeping the tasks free of data-leakage. We introduce AnonVul, a cross-language benchmark of 132 application-level business-logic vulnerabilities, built by a semi-automated pipeline that anonymizes each task, injects oracles from expert-written specifications, and differentially verifies proof-of-concept exploits. The benchmark spans nine languages, with two evaluation tracks on black-box and grey-box settings, where each task runs in a sandbox with specialized oracles embedded in key exploitation steps. We evaluate six state-of-the-art vulnerability-discovery agents on the AnonVul benchmark, measuring discovery success, cost-effectiveness, anonymization sensitivity, oracle validity, and failure modes. Our results show that AnonVul remains challenging, with the best agent succeeding in only 23.11% of attempts. On a matched cohort of 20 vulnerabilities, restoring software identity increases discovery from 21.25% to 40.83%, highlighting the importance of controlling recognizable software knowledge when evaluating vulnerability discovery.

title: Sulphur-bearing molecule survey towards prestellar and starless cores in the Perseus molecular cloud
abstract: Sulphur is drastically depleted from the gas phase in dense starless and prestellar cores, creating the long-standing "missing sulphur problem". Observations of sulphur-bearing molecules are crucial to understanding sulphur chemistry, core-environment relationships, and the physical evolution of star-forming regions. We present a survey of four sulphur-bearing molecules, HCS+, OCS, H2CS, and SO, towards 15 starless and prestellar cores in the Perseus molecular cloud using the Yebes 40m telescope. The HCS+ 1-0, OCS 3-2 and 4-3, H2CS 1_{0,1}-0_{0,0}, and SO 3_2-2_2 transitions were observed, fitted with Gaussian profiles, and column densities were calculated assuming local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE). We also compare these with observations of CS, CCS, and CCCS from a previous study. HCS+, OCS, H2CS, and SO are detected in 100%, 93%, 100%, and 73% of the sample, respectively. Derived column densities are (2.2-17.0)x10^11 cm^-2 for HCS+, (1.9-25.0)x10^12 cm^-2 for OCS, (1.0-15.0)x10^12 cm^-2 for H2CS, and (0.3-17.0)x10^13 cm^-2 for SO, spanning over an order of magnitude. HCS+ and SO abundances strongly correlate (inversely and directly, respectively) with core volume density, reinforcing their early- and late-type status. Correlations indicate a differentiation between carbon and oxygen chemistry for sulphur-bearing molecules, with CS showing the strongest correlations as expected. Cores in protostellar outflow paths do not show consistently higher abundances. The chemical age (SO/CS) correlates with physical age (volume density), except for Per752, an outlier likely linked to an enhanced cosmic ray ionization rate. These results provide a robust observational baseline constraining chemical models of sulphur chemistry in early star formation.

title: Boundary Control of a Modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest Beam via Reduced-Order Reinforcement Learning
abstract: In this paper, we study the active vibration control of an elastic beam using reinforcement learning (RL). The physical system is modeled by a modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest type linear partial differential equation with simply supported boundary conditions. The dynamics are approximated by a reduced-order model (ROM) obtained through eigenvalue expansion and truncated Galerkin projection. Control is applied through boundary actuation. The resulting finite-dimensional system is formulated as a continuous-time Markov decision process and solved numerically using the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm. All modeling steps, from physical formulation to temporal discretization and control design, are explicitly described. A systematic comparison is performed between the controller learned via PPO and the classical linear quadratic (LQR) regulator. The analysis highlights the strengths and limitations of each approach, both from a theoretical and practical point of view, with particular emphasis on energy dissipation mechanisms and actuator constraints.

title: Smartphone-Based, Field-Deployed AI Inspection System for Power Distribution Infrastructure
abstract: Routine inspection of power distribution infrastructure remains challenging for utilities operating geographically dispersed networks, where conventional manual inspection can be difficult to perform consistently and at scale. This work presents a smartphone-based AI inspection system for assessing targeted distribution-infrastructure conditions from images captured by field personnel. The proposed workflow integrates image-quality and viewing-perspective validation with AI-assisted assessment of pole lean, crossarm and top-cleat tilt, voltage level, vegetation-clearance risk, and distribution-transformer (DTR)-ground clearance. The system integrates deep-learning models with monocular depth estimation, geometric analysis, and rule-based processing within a common multi-stage inspection workflow designed for practical field operation. The system was pilot deployed across five selected distribution feeders within the Eastern Power Distribution Company of Andhra Pradesh Ltd. (APEPDCL), where 1,222 defect instances were identified across the assessed categories and subsequently tracked through a rectification and verification workflow, with 84 defect instances recorded as rectified during the study period. Feeder-level interruption records were also examined over the study period; however, the available observations do not provide sufficient evidence to establish a reliability improvement attributable to the proposed system. A curated multi-module field-captured dataset, PD-Defect, is also publicly released to support reproducible research in distribution-infrastructure inspection. The field deployment demonstrates the practical integration of smartphone-based AI-assisted inspection into field inspection and maintenance activities, providing a mechanism for systematic identification, documentation, rectification tracking, and verification of targeted distribution-infrastructure defects.
