Structure-grouped QSAR validation reveals modest ranking performance for ToxRefDB-recorded lung neoplastic findings.
abstract: Organ-specific quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling is constrained by sparse, heterogeneous animal pathology data. We evaluated molecular structure and bioactivity data from the Toxicity Forecaster (ToxCast) program for a database-derived lung neoplastic pathology endpoint using a dataset of 560 standardized parent representations (53 positive and 507 database-supported otherwise-negative) in 328 structure-validation groups. Of 2189 contributing studies, 95.7% used oral administration and 1.6% inhalation; the inhalation-specific neoplastic subset contained one positive representation. Nested group-aware validation, whole-group bootstrap, full-pipeline label permutation and a design-qualified otherwise-negative sensitivity analysis were applied. Morgan ExtraTrees yielded a pooled out-of-fold area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.643 (95% confidence interval, 0.566-0.719) and average precision (AP) of 0.175 (0.119-0.282). Penalized Morgan logistic regression yielded ROC-AUC of 0.669 and AP of 0.202; paired confidence intervals did not establish ExtraTrees superiority. Restricting the otherwise-negative class to 427 representations meeting stricter evidence criteria yielded ExtraTrees ROC-AUC of 0.620 and AP of 0.198. ToxCast integration did not establish incremental discrimination. Screening 7216 non-training structures produced model-dependent rankings: ExtraTrees and logistic regression shared nine Top-25 entries, whereas only 4-methylbenzophenone from the nine-structure targeted review set appeared in both lists. The results support modest structure-associated ranking information for this heterogeneous database endpoint, but not pulmonary or inhalation carcinogenicity classification or validated prioritization utility. This study provides a structure-grouped benchmark for organ-specific computational toxicology and informs future comparisons of biological descriptors and the design of independent validation studies.

Molecular mechanism of S100A11 inhibiting anti-HCC immune function of NK cells.
abstract: OBJECTIVE To explore the regulatory role and underlying molecular mechanism of S100A11 in the anti-hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) function of natural killer (NK) cells, and to provide a novel target and theoretical basis for optimizing immunotherapy for HCC. METHODS The expression of S100A11 was validated in clinical specimens. A stable S100A11-knockdown NK92 cell line was established via lentiviral transfection. CCK-8 assay, cell cytotoxicity assay, flow cytometry, Western blot and other experiments were performed to detect changes in NK cell biological functions and related signaling pathways. An HCC xenograft mouse model was established to verify the antitumor effect in vivo. RESULTS S100A11 was highly expressed in HCC tissues, and its expression level was positively correlated with pathological differentiation grade. Knockdown of S100A11 significantly enhanced the proliferation, degranulation, cytokine secretion and cytotoxic activity of NK92 cells against HCC cells. Moreover, S100A11 knockdown upregulated the expression of activating receptors and downregulated inhibitory receptors on the surface of NK cells. Mechanistically, S100A11 regulated NK cell functions by suppressing the phosphorylation of key molecules in the MAPK signaling pathway and the endoplasmic reticulum stress pathway. In vivo experiments demonstrated that S100A11-knockdown NK92 cells markedly restrained tumor growth, increased NK cell infiltration in tumor tissues, and caused no obvious hepatic injury. CONCLUSION S100A11 inhibits the anti-HCC immune function of NK cells by negatively regulating the MAPK and endoplasmic reticulum stress signaling pathways. Targeting S100A11 can restore the cytotoxic activity of NK cells, which is expected to serve as a novel potential target for precise immunotherapy of HCC.

title: Incremental adverse impact of pathological factors in head and neck cancer with extranodal extension.
abstract: PURPOSE Pathological extranodal extension (pENE) is a well-established adverse prognostic factor in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). This study aimed to investigate multiple adverse pathological features and to demonstrate their cumulative impacts on prognosis among patients with pENE-positive HNSCC. METHODS A cohort of 281 patients with pENE-positive HNSCC that underwent upfront surgery followed by adjuvant chemoradiotherapy between 2008 and 2016 was retrospectively analyzed with Cox proportional hazards models being employed to identify factors associated with overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS). RESULTS The 5-year OS and DFS rates in this cohort were 45.7% and 41.5% respectively. Positive surgical margins, poor tumor differentiation and positive metastatic lymph nodes over 3 (>3) were all independently associated with inferior OS and DFS. Patients were stratified into groups based on the number of these adverse pathological "P" factors (0, 1 or 2). When stratified by the number of these "P" factors, the 5-year OS rates were 55% for patients with none, 37.5% for one, and 6.7% for two factors (p < 0.001). A similar trend was observed for 5-year DFS (50.5%, 34.5% and 0.0% respectively; p < 0.001). The 2-factor group was small (n = 15), resulting in substantial statistical uncertainty. CONCLUSION Among patients with pENE-positive HNSCC, the accumulation of adverse pathological "P" factors was associated with incrementally poorer survival outcomes despite standard adjuvant chemoradiotherapy. These findings suggest that cumulative pathological risk factors might help identify patients at particularly high risk, although validation in larger independent cohorts is warranted.

A Holistic Approach to Potato Suberin Analysis: A Time Travel from Breakdown Products to Suberin Deposition to Metabolite Profiling of Wound Periderm.
abstract: The outer skins of potato tubers undergo healing after the wounding that occurs during cultivation and processing of this major food crop, but the macromolecular structure of the suberized cell wall barriers that mitigate drought and infection has remained elusive. Because many prior models have drawn upon top-down analyses of depolymerization treatments that are known to be incomplete, we devised a comprehensive strategy of bottom-up monitoring of wound-healing metabolites at several time points, solid-state NMR (ssNMR) compositional analysis of the suberized cell wall, and top-down chemical analysis of soluble chemical depolymerization products. Liquid and gas chromatography - mass spectrometry (LC-MS and GC-MS) metabolite profiling were conducted for extracts from wound tissues in four potato cultivars with differing skin morphologies at 0, 1, 2, 3, and 7 days post wounding. In parallel, 13C ssNMR was used to characterize the suberin-enriched polymeric material. Finally, the biopolymer composite was subjected to mild chemical breakdown followed by LC-MS and GC-MS analyses. By coordinating these phytochemical analyses, we found new glycoalkaloid, sterol, and phenolic amine compounds that are incorporated within the biopolymer composite. These findings enrich our picture of the suberin macromolecular structure that develops after wounding or in native skins to protect potato tubers from environmental threats.

Genome-Wide Analysis of Iron and Zinc Transporter Genes Identifies Putative Candidates for Sorghum Biofortification
abstract: Sorghum bicolor (L.) Moench is a valuable cereal crop for tackling micronutrient malnutrition globally through biofortification of essential nutrients, iron (Fe) and zinc (Zn). Sorghum seeds exhibit significant variability in Fe and Zn content, yet only two biofortified varieties have been released so far. In this study, a comprehensive in silico identification, characterization, and expression analysis of Fe and Zn transporters was conducted to shortlist putative candidates for sorghum seed biofortification. A total of 61 transporters belonging to YSL, ZIP, HMA, NRAMP, NAS, FER, and VIT gene families were shortlisted. Their gene models, unique motifs, chromosomal locations, phylogenetic relationships, protein–protein interactions, and cis-elements were determined. Expression profiling of developing S. bicolor M35-1 seeds, and other tissues including leaf, stem, root, panicle, and mature seeds revealed putative candidates regulating Fe and Zn accumulation in seeds. These candidates will leverage future breeding and genome editing efforts for sorghum seed biofortification.

title: Differentiable End-to-End Sensor Array Optimization for Electronic Nose via Local Self-Attention
abstract: Electronic noses (e-noses) based on cross-selective gas sensors often suffer from severe redundancy, which degrades odor analysis accuracy and impedes practical deployment. Here, we introduce a fully deep-learning-based sensor array optimization (SAO) framework that learns an optimal subset of sensor array through an end-to-end differentiable manner. Unlike conventional step-by-step workflows, which separate feature extraction, feature selection, sensor selection, and model training, our method jointly optimizes the sensor selection strategy, feature extractor, and task-specific network, enabling global collaborative optimization. Core to the framework is a local self-attention mechanism that infers sensor-wise importance while preserving the temporal structure of individual sensor responses, together with a tanhshrink-based gating function that drives redundant channels exactly to zero without requiring explicit sparsity regularization. Experiments on a 13-channel polyaniline sensor array exposed to six volatile organic compounds show that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 91.18 ± 0.55% using only four sensors, reducing the number of sensors by nearly 70% while outperforming conventional approaches. These results demonstrate that the differentiable SAO can improve both efficiency and accuracy in practical e-nose applications.

title: Priming of human iPSCs with doxorubicin causes genome-wide transcriptional reprogramming and functional impairments in iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes
abstract: How Doxorubicin (Dox) mediated damage to stem cells or cardiomyocytes contributes to cardiotoxicity and cardiac regeneration is unclear. Using a human iPSC-based model together with corresponding iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes (iCMs) revealed that iPSCs are much more sensitive against single short pulse-treatments with Dox than iCMs. Major mitochondrial impairments such as increased mitochondrial fragmentation, loss of mitochondrial membrane potential, reduced ATP levels, and altered mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) organization, yet neither increased ROS formation, nuclear DNA damage response, nor apoptosis were detected in Dox-treated iPSCs. Whole genome transcriptome profiling revealed major differences in the transcriptional response to Dox including downregulation of genes regulating cellular homeostasis and energy metabolism. Dox exposure at the iPSC stage, termed priming here, shifts the global transcriptional landscape of iCMs towards reduced cardiac muscle regeneration, energy metabolism, muscle contraction, and increased fibrosis. Functionally, priming caused iCMs to ‘memorize’ this early Dox treatment resulting in reduced ATP levels, altered mtDNA organization, and in impaired contractility and oscillating Ca2+ handling. We propose that Dox-induced mitochondrial dysfunction and transcriptional priming in stem cells alters durably cardiac and bioenergetic properties of its progeny which may impair the regenerative capacity after differentiation. This may be of particular relevance for children and teenagers undergoing chemotherapy.

title: Pilot intraindividual secretome profiling of adipose-derived stem cells in multiple symmetric lipomatosis
abstract: Multiple symmetric lipomatosis (MSL) is a rare adipose tissue disease characterized by progressive, non-encapsulated, symmetrical fat accumulation. Its pathophysiology is still not completely understood. Here, we performed the first intraindividual comparison of secretomes of human adipose-derived stem cells (hASCs) isolated from affected and unaffected regions of n = 15 patients (proteomic discovery cohort n = 5). Affected MSL-hASCs tend to show accelerated metabolic signals and higher cell densities with preserved adipogenic differentiation capacity. Secretome transfer of affected MSL-hASCs significantly increased metabolic activity of wt-hASCs after 24 h in 4/7 samples (all explorative Benjamini-Hochberg corrected p = 0.040). Bottom-up proteomic analysis identified 811 proteins, of which 220 were classified as secreted. Thirteen proteins exhibited nominally significant dysregulation of expression, including CALR (p = 0.0061), LAMC1 (p = 0.0241), S100A7 (p = 0.0281) and HDGF (p = 0.0474), but none remained significant after application of the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction to control the False Discovery Rate (FDR) at 0.05. Transcriptional validation by rt-qPCR revealed a trend toward downregulation of hLAMA4 and hCFB (both p = 0.0625). In conclusion, convergent patterns are consistent with extracellular matrix remodeling and PI3K/AKT-ERK-associated proliferative signaling. This model supports a hypothesis of progenitor-level dysregulation rather than a single clonal driver in MSL, which will require further mechanistic validation in larger cohorts.

title: Honokiol, a structurally defined natural product, promotes SIRT3-linked bone formation in osteoporotic bone remodeling and fracture repair.
abstract: CONTEXT Honokiol is a structurally defined biphenolic natural product with reported mitochondrial and cytoprotective activities. Whether honokiol modifies pathological skeletal remodeling through sirtuin 3 (SIRT3)-linked mechanisms remains unclear. OBJECTIVE This study investigated whether honokiol regulates bone cell lineage responses and improves osteoporotic bone remodeling and fracture repair through SIRT3-associated bone formation. MATERIALS AND METHODS Mouse bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells and RAW264.7 cells were used to assess osteogenesis, adipogenesis, and osteoclastogenesis after recombinant SIRT3, honokiol, or SIRT3 siRNA transfection. In vivo effects were examined in ovariectomized mice and stabilized femoral fracture models. Local AAV-shSIRT3 delivery was used to evaluate target dependence. Outcomes included micro-computed tomography, histology, osteocalcin immunohistochemistry, calcein double labeling, and three-point bending analysis. RESULTS Recombinant SIRT3 enhanced osteogenic mineralization and suppressed adipogenic differentiation and osteoclastogenesis. Honokiol increased SIRT3 expression and produced a similar lineage-shifting profile. SIRT3 knockdown markedly attenuated honokiol-induced osteogenesis, whereas its anti-adipogenic and anti-osteoclastogenic effects were only partly reduced. In ovariectomized mice, honokiol improved trabecular microarchitecture, mineral apposition, osteoblast activity, and femoral strength while reducing marrow adiposity and osteoclast burden. In fractured femora, honokiol increased mineralized callus formation, osteoblast activity, and biomechanical recovery. Local AAV-shSIRT3 intervention weakened these benefits, particularly for bone-forming and structural endpoints. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION Honokiol demonstrates a preclinical skeletal pharmacological profile characterized by predominantly SIRT3-linked bone formation. Its broader effects on adipogenic and osteoclast-associated responses appear only partly SIRT3-dependent.

title: Comparative analysis of select 3D human mesenchymal stromal cell-derived spheroid models for adipogenic differentiation.
abstract: In vitro modelling of adipose tissue (AT) commonly employs 2D systems, which do not fully capture the complexity of AT, lacking cell-cell interactions and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling. Despite the innovations in 3D culture systems offering physiologically relevant AT platforms, the field lacks consensus and cross-protocol method comparison. We performed a comparative analysis of three scaffold-free spheroid-generation techniques: Ultra Low Attachment plates (ULA), Hanging Drops (HD), and Microwell Culture Plates (MCP), utilizing human AT-derived mesenchymal stromal cells. Each method produced viable spheroids of similar size and morphology within 48 hours. However, MCP demonstrated greater uniformity and a significant increase in mass density when compared to ULA and HD. Adipogenic media increased spheroid size in ULA and MCP, but not in HD spheroids. Notably, the diameter of ULA spheroids was 2- and 6-times larger compared to HD and MCP ones, respectively, regardless of adipogenic induction. Gene expression analysis indicated that all techniques led to PPARγ and ADIPOQ expression during adipogenesis. All methods supported adipocyte differentiation, as evidenced by lipid droplet accumulation, PLIN1, CD36, and HSL expression, and ECM rearrangement. These findings suggest that all the described techniques constitute a robust platform for producing adipogenesis-competent spheroids, while method-specific differences suggest an application-dependent choice.

title: Review for "yancc: A GPU-accelerated, differentiable solver for neoclassical transport in tokamaks and stellarators"
Decoding common and complex genotypes of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy using methylation profiling and long-read sequencing
abstract: Due to the complexity of the genomic region, the relationship between genotype, phenotype, and epigenetics in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy remains incompletely understood, and diagnostics limited in precision. In this study, we applied Oxford Nanopore Technology long-read sequencing to characterize FSHD1 and FSHD2 patients with common and previously confirmed genotypes (n = 14). This approach enabled the simultaneous determination of allele-specific methylation profiles, haplotype, and repeat length. Our results confirm the presence of an asymmetric methylation gradient increasing from the proximal to distal end of 4q35 repeat arrays with a steeper slope in FSHD1 (2.5–8.1%/repeat unit) compared to the two FSHD2 patients (0.3 and 1.2%/repeat unit) studied. The slope is therefore a potential marker to differentiate both types of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy, being less biased by repeat length compared to parameters determined in current bisulfite sequencing-based methylation assays. By determining distal methylation allele-specifically long-read sequencing overcomes a major limitation of such assays. Distal methylation of pathogenic (range 22–45%) and non-pathogenic repeat arrays (range 77–87%) (P < 0.0001) is clearly separated and shows a stronger correlation with age-corrected clinical severity (r = -0.81, 95%-CI: -0.48–-0.94) compared to studies based on bisulfite sequencing. Overall, this strengthens distal methylation as a superior diagnostic marker of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy disease status. Detailed clinical and genetic characterization of a second cohort (n = 20) comprising patients with complex genotypes (n = 11) and FSHD2 (n = 9) was performed using our bisulfite sequencing-based methylation profile analysis, complementary methods, and in three cases, long-read sequencing. Based on these results we highlight underrecognized patient groups at risk of misdiagnosis when methylation analysis is not part of the diagnostic workup: i) patients carrying a 4qA166 repeat array, ii) patients with underrepresented population backgrounds, iii) facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy patients carrying 11 repeat units in the absence of global hypomethylation, and iv) FSHD2 patients without a detectable causative variant in known epigenetic suppressor genes (SMCHD1, DNMT3B, and LRIF1). We hypothesize that unknown epigenetic modifiers explain the penetrance of repeat arrays with 8–10 repeat units in the European and North American population, the pathogenicity of some repeat arrays with 11 repeat units, and the hypomethylation of the entire 4q35 repeat array in some FSHD2 patients without a detected variant in known epigenetic suppressor genes. From our results recommendations for standard diagnostics are derived. Finally, we hypothesize a preliminary model linking DNA methylation, known genetic parameters and disease severity.

title: Single-Cell and Spatial Perspectives on Source-Sink Dynamics in Plants.
abstract: Source-sink relationships describe how plants coordinate carbon production, transport, and utilization to support growth, reproduction, and stress responses. Classical physiological studies established a robust organ-level framework for carbon allocation, but these approaches largely treat tissues as homogeneous units. Recent advances in single-cell and spatial omics technologies now reveal that both sources and sinks consist of diverse cell populations with specialized metabolic and transport functions. In this review, we synthesize emerging insights from single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, and integrative multi-omics to show how cellular heterogeneity shapes photosynthetic source strength, vascular transport interfaces, and sink development. We further discuss how stress responses, signaling molecules, and plant-associated microbiomes dynamically reprogram source-sink relationships in a spatially structured manner. Finally, we highlight opportunities to integrate high-resolution molecular atlases with physiological modeling and machine learning approaches to develop predictive frameworks for carbon allocation. These advances suggest that future crop improvement strategies will increasingly rely on cell-type-specific engineering of transport processes and metabolic sinks rather than simply enhancing photosynthesis.

title: Male cone development in Ginkgo biloba uncovers recurrent reproductive modules partially shared with Cycas circinalis.
abstract: The origin of seed plants transformed land plant reproduction by protecting the embryo and enabling dispersal across diverse ecosystems. Yet many reproductive mechanisms remain poorly resolved, as research has focused predominantly on angiosperm models. Because phylogenomic analyses recover Ginkgoales and Cycadales as a clade sister to the remaining living gymnosperms, Ginkgo biloba provides an informative system for investigating reproductive traits in early-diverging spermatophytes. Here, we integrated phenology, histology, RNA-seq, arabinogalactan-protein candidate profiling, and JIM8 immunolocalization to investigate male cone and pollen development. Male ontogeny was divided into three main developmental macro-stages, each characterized by a distinct transcriptional program: primordial maintenance in M1; microsporogenesis, tapetum activity, callose dynamics, and pollen wall formation in M2; and pollen maturation, endothecium reinforcement, and dehiscence in M3. A targeted candidate-gene workflow further identified structural and regulatory modules linked to tapetum differentiation, meiosis, sporopollenin biosynthesis, pollen maturation, microsporangial opening, and sex-determining-region-associated expression. JIM8-reactive epitopes showed stage- and tissue-specific redistribution across microsporocytes, tetrads, the tapetum, developing pollen, and the endothecium. A targeted comparison with a newly generated Cycas circinalis transcriptomic dataset recovered comparable reproductive modules, although with differences in their temporal deployment. These findings establish a comprehensive comparative framework for investigating shared and lineage-specific features of male reproduction in early-diverging gymnosperms.

title: Valproic Acid Inhibits Glioma Cell Proliferation by Inducing Neuronal-Like Differentiation Partly Through HDAC1/REST Suppression.
abstract: Inducing differentiation of glioma cells, including glioma stem cells (GSCs), into neuron-like cells represents a promising therapeutic strategy. Our previous drug repositioning study revealed that histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitors are potential inducers of glioma cell differentiation. In this study, the antiepileptic drug valproic acid (VPA), a known HDAC inhibitor with blood-brain barrier permeability, was investigated for its ability to induce neuronal differentiation in glioma. The results showed that VPA treatment induced pronounced neuronal-like morphological changes and upregulated expression of neuronal markers in glioma cell lines U87 and LN229 and their derived GSCs, while concurrently inhibiting proliferation and attenuating stemness. Proteomic sequencing and bioinformatics analyses confirmed the enrichment of neuronal differentiation-associated proteins and downregulation of cell cycle-related proteins following VPA exposure. Mechanistically, VPA reduced the thermal stability of HDAC1 and RE-1 silencing transcription factor (REST) and downregulated their protein levels. Pharmacological inhibition of HDAC1 or REST phenocopied VPA-induced differentiation, whereas REST overexpression attenuated this effect. In vivo, VPA administration significantly delayed subcutaneous U87 xenograft tumor growth, prolonged survival in an orthotopic GSC xenograft model, and reduced HDAC1/REST expression while inducing neuronal marker expression in tumor tissues. Furthermore, Connectivity Map analysis identified mTOR inhibitors as potential synergistic agents, and the combination of VPA with rapamycin exhibited synergistic anti-proliferative effects. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that VPA suppresses glioma growth by inducing neuronal-like differentiation partly through HDAC1/REST inhibition, which uncovers a distinct differentiation-based anti-glioma mechanism of VPA, supporting its potential clinical utility and providing a rationale for combination strategies in glioma differentiation therapy.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

title: Metric-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Object Hallucination Reduction in LVLM-Based Image Captioning
abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have excelled in joint visual and language understanding, particularly in image captioning. However, LVLMs remain prone to object hallucination, describing non-existent entities in the given image. Previous remedies, including dataset-enhanced supervised training and reinforcement learning from human feedback, show promise but rely heavily on costly human involvement, limiting scalability. To address this, we propose a reinforcement learning framework to mitigate object hallucination in LVLM-based image captioning, driven entirely by natural language processing (NLP) metrics. While optimizing reinforcement learning solely on NLP metrics offers scalability, it also introduces pitfalls: reward hacking, sparse feedback, and costly training. Our framework sidesteps these by introducing an Object Consistency Score (OCS) capturing both correctness and coverage of objects, incorporating KL-regularization for denser token-level guidance, and designing a lightweight PPO variant that fine-tunes adapters atop a frozen LVLM backbone, achieving efficiency and stability. Extensive experiments on the InstructBLIP baseline demonstrate the effectiveness and generalizability of our framework, achieving a substantial hallucination reduction of up to 41\% on the COCO dataset and 29\% on the Visual Genome. Furthermore, the framework can enhance caption quality by incorporating complementary evaluation metrics such as BERTScore and METEOR. These results reveal a broader insight in multimodal learning: LVLMs can effectively self-correct hallucinations using metric feedback, motivating deeper exploration into scalable reinforcement frameworks that significantly reduce human effort.

title: Stackelberg Game with Multi-Agent Transformer for ISRS-Aware Resource Re-optimization in Multi-Band Optical Networks
abstract: The rapid expansion of generative AI is driving computing infrastructures toward interconnected AI data centers. Multi-band optical networks have become the backbone of such connectivity. To accommodate increasingly dynamic traffic demands, these networks require continual resource re-optimization to improve resource utilization and reduce service blocking. However, multi-band transmission amplifies inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering(ISRS), inducing nonlinear coupling among services. This coupling complicates re-optimization, as local adjustments perturb the global power profile, creating interdependent optimization decisions across services. Moreover, the nonlinear interactions vary with the subset of services selected for re-optimization, and inappropriate selection may reduce re-optimization effectiveness or diminish achievable benefits. To address these challenges, we propose a Stackelberg Game with Multi-Agent Transformer (SG-MAT) approach for ISRS-aware resource re-optimization. SG-MAT employs a leader-follower structure, in which the MAT-based follower models nonlinear coupling and generates coordinated channel reallocations, feeding the utilization improvements to the leader. Using this feedback, the leader identifies critical service subsets, approximating a Stackelberg equilibrium to guide global decisions and enabling consistent and efficient re-optimization. Simulation results show that SG-MAT achieves the highest utilization improvement and reduces the blocking ratio by approximately 30% under moderate traffic loads, with computational complexity comparable to benchmarks.

title: Comparative accuracy of imaging modalities for differentiating malignant small testicular masses.
abstract: OBJECTIVES To synthesise evidence comparing the diagnostic performance of imaging modalities in differentiating malignant from benign small testicular masses. PATIENTS AND METHODS A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-compliant search of PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane and Web of Science databases up to 6 May 2026 identified 11 studies comprising 707 patients with small testicular masses (predominantly <2 cm) who underwent imaging prior to a histopathological or, where unavailable, a mixed clinical/radiological follow-up reference standard. Diagnostic accuracy measures for six modalities (brightness-mode [B-Mode] ultrasonography [US], colour doppler US [CDUS], contrast-enhanced US [CEUS], magnetic resonance imaging [MRI], strain elastography [SE] and strain ratio [SR]) were synthesised using a Bayesian bivariate hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic model. RESULTS The CEUS demonstrated the most reliable discriminatory ability with a pooled sensitivity of 91% and pooled specificity of 81%, yielding the highest diagnostic odds ratio of 46. B-Mode US remains a valid screening test with the highest sensitivity of 96% but a specificity of only 39%. CDUS showed a pooled sensitivity of 69% and a specificity of 81%. MRI had a pooled sensitivity of 91% and a specificity of 38%. SE demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 87% and a specificity of 56%. Finally, SR reported the lowest sensitivity at 74% and a specificity of 50%. CEUS demonstrated significantly higher specificity than B-Mode US (ratio 1.9, 95% posterior interval [PI] 1.2-4.4) and MRI (ratio 1.8, 95% PI 1.0-5.2). CONCLUSION The CEUS demonstrates the highest combined sensitivity and specificity for differentiating benign from malignant testicular masses, significantly outperforming conventional B-Mode US and MRI in specificity. CEUS represents a compelling decision-making tool to support testis-sparing strategies and reduce unnecessary orchidectomies for indeterminate small testicular masses.

title: Beyond Productivity: AI, Community, and Sustainability in Open Source Software
abstract: Open source software (OSS) development communities have long provided digital infrastructure worldwide and been a central subject of CSCW research on online communities and peer production. However, the ongoing emergence of generative AI and agentic coding is disrupting OSS collaboration and project organizations. Recent literature indicates that some productivity gains have been observed by contributors, but these benefits have not been evenly distributed across OSS projects and communities. Moreover, generative AI has disrupted socialization norms in these communities with slop produced by bots, agents, and bad-faith AI-assisted contributions. The resulting technical debt and invisible labor faced by maintainers in handling the influx of AI-generated code critically threaten the sustainability of OSS projects. In this one-day workshop, we will bring together researchers and OSS stakeholders to explore the risks these communities face and discuss interventions for sustaining OSS collaboration. In addition to supporting the long-term viability of open-source software, we seek to understand how AI influences coordination, trust, and equity within large-scale collaborative work environments.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 Companion of the Computer-Supported Cooperative Work and Social Computing

title: Designing Relationship-Aware Technologies for Remote Intergenerational Support
abstract: Communication between older adults and their remote younger family members is often constrained by differences in technical skill, communication styles, and daily routines. My research explores how technology can support these relationships without replacing human interaction. I design and study three systems: (1) HelpCall, a video-conferencing add-on providing synchronous, step-by-step guidance for remote tech support; (2) FamilyDitto, a mimetic AI agent enabling socially rich, semi-synchronous intergenerational interactions; and (3) ExtraEyes, mimetic voice agents providing technical and decision-making support during online browsing. Together, these projects will advance the design of technologies that not only bridge technical and social gaps but also cultivate meaningful, emotionally rich connections between generations.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 Companion of the Computer-Supported Cooperative Work and Social Computing

title: HIROBA: A Configurable Open-Source Platform for Studying the Social Dynamics of AI-mediated Video Communication in Mixed Human-AI Groups
abstract: AI agents are increasingly embedded in group video communication, yet researchers lack experimental platforms for controlled study of mixed human-AI group dynamics. Current tools require researchers to compromise their methodologies. Commercial video products lack experimental control over agent configuration, and research video systems are one-off prototypes built for a single study. We present HIROBA1, a self-hostable open-source video conferencing platform for studying mixed human-AI group dynamics with multiple AI agents. HIROBA enables four researcher-controlled configuration dimensions of a video session, including human-AI group composition, embodied agent characteristics (e.g., social roles, behaviors, and appearance), Wizard-of-Oz operation, and controlled experiment setup. Our demo lets attendees configure HIROBA for representative communication or collaboration tasks, run pilot sessions, or join meetings as participants, while collecting feedback to inform the platform’s roadmap. Together, these dimensions give researchers a shared experimental platform to navigate the realism, control, and scalability trade-offs of AI-MC research in video settings.

title: SpatialTutorX: Exploring Shared AI Facilitation for Collaborative Procedural Learning in Mixed Reality
abstract: Professional procedural training often requires learners to coordinate attention, communication, and action around shared physical artifacts, while expert facilitation remains limited, inconsistent, and difficult to scale. In real-world medical training and practice, clinicians frequently collaborate with peers, negotiate procedural decisions, and coordinate around shared physical tasks. We propose SpatialTutorX, a mixed-reality procedural training system that explores shared AI-MR facilitation embedded within immersive collaborative procedural work. Building on our prior single-user system for lumbar puncture training, this new version enables two learners wearing mixed-reality headsets to participate in the same training session around a shared physical manikin. Learners view synchronized mixed-reality procedural guidance, coordinate actions around the manikin, discuss procedural decisions with one another, and jointly interact with the same AI facilitator during the task. Through this demo, we invite CSCW attendees to examine how AI agents can function as shared instructional actors within collaborative, embodied, and socially organized professional learning practices.

title: A Field Study of Mimetic Agents for Relationship-building in Workplace Mentorship
abstract: A Ditto is an AI agent that emulates a person’s voice, appearance, personality, and knowledge, enabling interaction even when the person is unavailable. While advances in generative AI have made such systems increasingly feasible, little is known about how they function within real-world social relationships. We examine this question in a workplace mentorship context, where interns often face barriers to building rapport with mentors due to power differentials and limited availability. In a two-week deployment with 14 interns and two non-supervisory mentors, interns had on-demand access to their mentors’ Dittos, while mentors reviewed interactions and updated their agents. Through logs, self-reported measures, and interviews, we found that Dittos can lower the barriers to initiating contact and sharing information, enabling low-stakes exchanges that carry over into more frequent human-to-human interaction. These exchanges can, in turn, foster familiarity and comfort over time, illustrating how mimetic agents can scaffold social connection when designed to remain embedded within human relationships.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 Companion of the Computer-Supported Cooperative Work and Social Computing

title: JENNIE: Joint Expression of Narrative, Nurturing, Inquiry, and Engagement
abstract: A joint book-reading activity between caregivers and children has been proven to benefit children’s literacy skill development. Systems supporting joint reading have been explored to reduce parents’ burden and increase children’s engagement by facilitating question-and-answer interactions, with the introduction of AI systems enabling dynamic, contextually appropriate question generation and, in some cases, story generation. However, current work often focuses on reducing the burden of joint reading by giving the system greater control, positioning it as a replacement for human guides. This research introduces JENNIE, a multimodal joint-reading companion that participates in reading with the caregiver by responding to the caregiver’s and the child’s interactions. JENNIE can process users’ utterances and visual information, such as the book’s illustrations, perform the book’s characters and narrator with theatrical voicing, and participate in conversations between caregiver and child. The system utilizes voice-based conversational agents (CAs) to support children’s learning by generating contextually appropriate educational questions aligned with the book’s learning goals. In this paper, we share our current progress and ongoing efforts in designing parent–child–AI joint learning.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 Companion of the Computer-Supported Cooperative Work and Social Computing

title: Hidden Profile Decision Making in Multi-Agent LLM Groups
abstract: The hidden profile paradigm is a foundational tool of CSCW research on computer-mediated group decision making: a group can identify the collectively optimal option only if its members surface their uniquely held information, and asynchronous communication is known to improve that pooling in human groups. As multi-agent LLM systems take on group decision-support roles, it is unclear whether the same channel-level interventions improve their performance. We replicate the hidden profile paradigm with groups of three LLM agents from four families (Kimi K2, GPT-OSS 120B, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Llama 4 Scout 17B) in a two-by-two design crossing communication mode (synchronous, asynchronous) with information distribution (shared, hidden). Across 219 valid sessions, only one model-by-mode cell exceeds the three-candidate chance baseline of 33 percent: Kimi K2 under asynchronous communication, at 87 percent correct (Fisher’s exact, two-sided p equals 0.002), an early-stage result from 15 sessions that awaits larger-n replication; two other models share private information at rates above 75 percent but never aggregate it into the correct decision. In this task and these model families, information sharing and information integration appear to be dissociated capabilities, and we develop the implications for CSCW systems that scaffold AI-mediated distributed decision making.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 Companion of the Computer-Supported Cooperative Work and Social Computing

title: CollabPEAS: A Collaborative VR System for Learning AI Agent Design Through the PEAS Framework
abstract: We present CollabPEAS, a collaborative system for artificial intelligence (AI) literacy in which pairs of learners come to understand how an AI agent’s behavior is produced by human specification. Working in shared virtual reality (VR), learners jointly specify a virtual cleaning robot using the PEAS framework (Performance measure, Environment, Actuators, Sensors), developing competencies for reasoning about how AI agents sense, decide, and act. The system integrates three coordinated design elements: (1) a five-step PEAS-guided design flow, implemented in VR, that makes agent specification choices spatially grounded and observable, (2) a block-based coding interface that preserves the perceive, decide, act reasoning cycle, and (3) collaboration supports designed to structure negotiation and shared ownership between partners. We situate CollabPEAS within AI literacy and collaborative learning research and discuss directions for future evaluation.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 Companion of the Computer-Supported Cooperative Work and Social Computing

title: AI-Mediated Ecological Participation: Connecting Public Feedback, Institutional Response, and Wetland Data through Generative AI
abstract: Wetland conservation involves ecological changes that are often slow, complex, and difficult for the public to perceive or act upon. Existing environmental communication mainly relies on reports, videos, and one-way information delivery, which limits public understanding, feedback, and sustained participation. Based on a formative questionnaire and interview study with 25 participants, this poster identifies three challenges in wetland communication: limited understanding of ecological processes, weak public – institution feedback channels, and unclear links between individual actions and ecological outcomes. In response, we present an early-stage design exploration of a generative AI-mediated participatory platform for wetland conservation. The proposed system uses a black-necked crane as an ecological agent to translate wetland monitoring data into dynamic visual scenes, supports public environmental observations through a shared feedback map, and connects institutional responses back to public-facing scene updates. Rather than treating generative AI only as a content generation tool, this work frames it as sociotechnical infrastructure for connecting ecological data, public feedback, and institutional response. We further discuss design considerations around data provenance, AI-generated ecological visualization, uncertainty communication, and institutional accountability.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 Companion of the Computer-Supported Cooperative Work and Social Computing

title: PersuaBridge: Real-Time Coaching for Negotiating with Value-Embedded AI Agents
abstract: Human–AI negotiation is an emerging phenomenon where goal-driven, value-embedded AI agents engage in transactional discussions to persuade people and counteract human persuasion. As such agents become culturally attuned negotiators, little is known about how people adapt and react, whether coaching can support them, or how cultural profile differences and reasoning effort affect the social dynamics of persuasion. We present PersuaBridge, an AI training framework that combines culturally profiled AI role-playing with real-time coaching involving multiple agents. To endow novices with realistic experiences of such social interactions, the framework enables users to negotiate with LLM counterparts that are either culturally aligned or misaligned, with or without turn-by-turn coaching. Our study shows that coaching significantly improves negotiation outcomes. Cultural misalignment with the agent yielded higher donations than alignment in baseline models, but this gap attenuated after controlling for the AI’s initial offer, suggesting an anchor-sensitive pattern rather than a clear sign of cultural congruence. Deeper AI cultural reasoning elicited longer participant replies without raising donations. Our framework informs the design of AI systems that support human users in building agency in value-diverse, global, agent-involved negotiation. Moving from human-human negotiation to human-AI negotiation also implies the need for comparative CSCW research, concerning how CSCW knowledge and principles that model and support social collectives apply to emergent human-AI collectives.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 Companion of the Computer-Supported Cooperative Work and Social Computing

title: Permissive Intimacy, Opaque Governance: A Qualitative Analysis of Policies Across Prominent Companion AI Applications
abstract: Companion AI platforms increasingly promote emotionally intimate, romantic, and sexual relationships with artificial conversational agents. Yet little is known about how these platforms publicly frame and govern the intimate interactions they make possible. Through a qualitative platform-level analysis of public-facing materials from 14 high-traffic CompAI platforms, we find that platforms regularly present AI companions as emotionally responsive, customizable relationship partners, while governing sexual or romantic interaction through uneven and often opaque policies. Although platforms frequently restrict explicitly violent or minor-endangering content, they rarely acknowledge emotional or sexual risks and often provide limited transparency around moderation enforcement and model memory affordances. We argue that CompAI intimacy is selectively governed: platforms make some content boundaries visible while leaving the relational risks of sustained intimate interaction largely underdefined.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 Companion of the Computer-Supported Cooperative Work and Social Computing

title: From Individual Guidance to Team Support: AI in XR Professional Training
abstract: This SIG will provide CSCW, HCI, XR, AI, and learning sciences researchers and practitioners with an opportunity to discuss how AI can support collaboration in XR-based professional training. Prior work has explored XR for simulation-based training and AI for tutoring, feedback, assessment, and adaptive learning. However, while AI is often discussed as an interactive partner or agent, less attention has been paid to how AI can support collaboration among human trainees in XR-based team training. In professional training contexts such as healthcare, emergency response, education, manufacturing, and workplace learning, AI agents may act as tutors, patients, victims, clients, coaches, evaluators, or facilitators, shaping how trainees communicate, coordinate, make decisions, and reflect on their performance. This SIG will create a space to discuss how these AI roles should be designed, how learners and instructors interact with AI-supported XR training systems, what methods are needed to study collaborative learning and teamwork in these settings, and what ethical, pedagogical, and deployment challenges should guide future CSCW research on AI-supported immersive team training.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 Companion of the Computer-Supported Cooperative Work and Social Computing

title: "I Will Be Right Here Whenever You Need Me": Designing AI-Mediated Collaborative Support for Adolescent Mental Health in Border Regions
abstract: Adolescents in border communities often face emotional challenges and avoid formal psychological support because of stigma, privacy concerns, and fragmented trust across families and schools. Existing conversational agents for youth mental health mainly support one-on-one interaction, with limited attention to collaborative support relationships. We conducted formative interviews with 19 adolescents from China–Myanmar border regions and propose an AI-Mediated Collaborative Support Framework that reconceptualizes conversational AI as a sociotechnical mediator for emotional disclosure, trust-sensitive communication, and support coordination across adolescent–home–school relationships. Based on this framework, we developed Moodie, an AI-mediated mental health prototype, and conducted a three-week pilot deployment with 10 adolescents. Preliminary findings indicate that participants perceived Moodie as a low-pressure space for emotional expression and preparation for communication with trusted adults, highlighting the potential of conversational AI for collaborative youth mental health support in resource-constrained contexts.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 Companion of the Computer-Supported Cooperative Work and Social Computing

title: Agricultural productivity and local economic resilience to heat stress: Evidence from rural India
abstract: Rising temperatures pose significant risks to rural livelihoods in India, yet limited empirical evidence explains how local economies sustain consumption during extreme-temperature events. This study examines whether agricultural productivity, measured through district-level rice yields, functions as a locally embedded resilience mechanism that moderates the welfare effects of extreme-temperature exposure. Using nationally representative household survey data aggregated into a district-level panel, the study applies fixed-effects, gender-disaggregated, and quantile regression approaches. The analysis shows that higher rice productivity is positively associated with rural consumption under both normal and extreme-temperature conditions, with comparatively larger coefficients during periods of heat stress. This relationship remains robust across alternative heat measures, model specifications, and time periods. Gender-disaggregated estimates indicate distinct consumption-buffering patterns, consistent with income-stabilization mechanisms among male-headed households and food-security-based mechanisms among female-headed households. Quantile estimates further show that the positive association extends across the consumption distribution, although its magnitude varies. By situating agricultural productivity within local economic systems, the study highlights its contribution to place-based resilience. The evidence supports investments in irrigation, heat-tolerant crop varieties, accessible extension services, and stronger local agricultural markets, alongside targeted support for vulnerable households, to promote rural development.
journal: Local Economy: The Journal of the Local Economy Policy Unit

title: Exploring Human Coach Distinctiveness in an Age of AI: An Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis of the Roles of Values
abstract: Objective: This study examined how professional coaches understand the role of values in their practice and why they see these as central to what human coaches offer compared with AI coaching agents. Method: Interpretative phenomenological analysis was used with semi-structured interviews with 13 experienced professional coaches. Results: Four group experiential themes were identified: values as the ethical and professional foundation of coaching practice, values as a purposive tool for client development, the reflexive and regulated coach and values as a distinctly human relational practice. Participants described values as central to coaching practice rather than one tool among many. They also linked embodied self-regulation, multimodal alignment and relational trust more strongly with human coaches than with AI coaching. Conclusions: The findings deepen understanding of values in coaching and of what coaches see as distinctively human, with implications for coach training, professional supervision and the responsible use of AI in professional coaching.

title: Deep learning-based prediction of seismic response histories of base-isolated structures
abstract: Conventional machine learning approaches in earthquake engineering have primarily focused on predicting peak structural response quantities, often neglecting the time-dependent nature of seismic behavior. This study applies a sequence-learning framework to directly map ground-motion time series to the full dynamic response history of base-isolated structures. A numerical dataset is generated using a MATLAB/Simulink simulation environment, where a multi-degree-of-freedom base-isolated system is subjected to recorded earthquake motions through linear time-history analysis. Both seismic input and structural response are represented as time series, allowing the model to learn temporal relationships without relying on predefined intensity measures or simplified response descriptors. A sequence-based Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model is employed to reconstruct response histories, including displacement and acceleration. The predicted responses show strong agreement with numerical simulation results, demonstrating the ability of the model to capture both amplitude variation and temporal evolution of structural behavior. By combining physics-based simulation with deep learning, the proposed methodology provides an efficient alternative for time-dependent seismic response estimation and offers potential for rapid structural assessment under earthquake loading.

title: Proteomic landscape of IGF-I gene transfer in osteoarthritis-derived human bone marrow stromal cells undergoing chondrogenesis
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a progressive joint disease marked by the breakdown of cartilage and impaired repair capacity. Gene therapy applied to human bone marrow-derived adherent stromal cells (BM-MSCs) with recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) vectors represents a promising strategy for cartilage regeneration. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its effects remain largely unexplored. In this study, we investigated the proteomic changes induced by rAAV-mediated insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-I) gene transfer during the chondrogenic differentiation of BM-MSCs derived from OA patients. BM-MSCs from OA donors were transduced with recombinant rAAV vectors encoding either IGF-I or the lacZ gene (β-galactosidase) as a control and cultured in three-dimensional micromass systems under chondrogenic conditions for 21 days. Histological, immunohistochemical (IHC) and immunofluorescence (IF) analyses were performed to characterize the chondrogenic phenotype of the model and to provide orthogonal validation of selected proteomic findings. Mass spectrometry-based proteomic profiling identified protein detection patterns and quantitative changes associated with IGF-I overexpression. Pathway and protein-protein interaction (PPI) analyses were carried out to explore the functional implications of differentially expressed proteins. A total of 4,284 proteins were identified, of which 112 showed notable changes in detection patterns or abundance associated with IGF-I. Functional enrichment analyses showed involvement of pathways related to metabolism, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) homeostasis, apoptosis regulation, cell proliferation, glycosylation, and the endosomal sorting complex required for transport (ESCRT) machinery. Histological and IHC analyses provided supportive evidence of cartilage-related matrix deposition. Orthogonal validation by IHC and IF confirmed the IGF-I-mediated upregulation of β-catenin and exportin-1 (XPO1). Further analyses provided exploratory evidence of increased active β-catenin and predominantly extranuclear distribution of sirtuin-1, a known XPO1 substrate, in IGF-I-transduced micromasses. This study provides the first proteomic characterization of rAAV-mediated IGF-I gene therapy in OA-derived BM-MSCs undergoing chondrogenesis. The IGF-I gene transfer was associated with broad proteomic changes involving metabolic and protein processing pathways, and enhanced cartilage-specific matrix deposition, highlighting molecular mechanisms of potential relevance to cartilage repair in OA.

title: Smart farms, virtual mirrors: AI-powered digital twins reshaping modern agriculture
Modelling the Structural Determinants of Households’ Indebtedness among Agricultural Households: An ISM-MICMAC Approach
abstract: Background: Agricultural households’ indebtedness is influenced by interconnected farm, financial and household conditions, making it important to understand relationships among its structural elements rather than examining them independently. This study develops a systemic representation of these interrelationships using literature-derived structural elements. Methods: Seven structural elements were assessed through expert judgement using interpretive structural modelling (ISM) and MICMAC analysis. 40 experts were contacted, 38 responded and 37 responses were considered valid. Three senior experts subsequently reviewed and consolidated the pairwise judgements. Twenty-one unique pairwise relationships were assessed and used to construct the Structured Self-Interaction Matrix, reachability structure and hierarchical model. Result: The final structure comprised two levels. Landholding Size occupied Level 2 and had driving and dependence powers of 7 and 1, respectively. Production capacity, cost burden, access to formal credit, farm income, borrowing level and household indebtedness occupied Level 1, each with driving and dependence powers of 6 and 7. The findings indicate an interconnected structure in which Landholding Size forms the foundational element.
journal: Agricultural Science Digest - A Research Journal

title: Nutritional Status of Soils Under Cassava Cultivation Using the Diagnosis and Recommendation System (DRIS) in the Savanna Zone of the Central African Republic
abstract: Cassava is an important crop that ensures food security for the population in the Central African Republic (CAR). It also significantly contributes to improving farmers' incomes. Unfortunately, there is no specific data on soil nutrient status that would allow for informed management of the crop’s nutritional condition and yield improvement, despite existing potential. The Diagnosis and Recommendation Integrated System (DRIS) is an approach used to interpret plant tissue analysis results and helps assess the nutritional status of crops. It focuses on comparing paired nutrient ratios and concentrations of nutrients in leaf tissues with norms developed from high-yielding crop populations. The objective of this study is to apply the DRIS model to determine the nutritional status of cassava cropping systems in the savanna forest zone of CAR. In total, 126 leaf samples were collected from cassava fields in the region. Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), Potassium (K), Calcium (Ca), Magnesium (Mg), and Zinc (Zn) contents were analyzed. Root yields were also recorded. Significant differences (p = 0.001) were observed between the root yields of the low and high-yielding sub-populations. Based on the Nutritional Balance Index, nutrient requirements for cassava in this savanna zone were ranked as: Ca > Mg > N > K > P > Zn. The study recommends the implementation of Integrated Soil Fertility Management (ISFM) technologies in cassava cultivation systems in each zone, with emphasis on Nitrogen and Calcium supplementation.

title: From Detection to Investigation: A Survey of Foundation Models and Agents for Financial Fraud and Financial Crime
abstract: Foundation models are extending research on financial fraud and financial crime from isolated risk detection to document understanding, relational analysis, and investigative workflows. A gap nevertheless separates model outputs from candidate evidence and actionable conclusions. This survey examines advances in six families of foundation models: language, vision, speech, temporal, graph, and tabular models. It compares their roles and limitations along two dimensions: the risk-control lifecycle and the directness of the supporting evidence. Existing studies show that pretraining can support representation reuse and the processing of unstructured information, with direct validation in some financial tasks. Cross-modal identity binding, information availability over time, report faithfulness, and case-level benefits require separate evaluation. Evidence on investigative agents spans prototypes, controlled tasks, expert assessments, and industry disclosures, which establish different aspects of workflow feasibility, task performance, and user assessment. Establishing gains in investigative efficiency and reductions in financial losses requires case-level comparative evidence. We examine entity and temporal alignment, the organization of candidate evidence, constrained tool execution, and investigative benchmark design, together with the implications of adversarial threats, privacy, fairness, and model risk governance. Research priorities should shift from expanding system functionality toward factual traceability, sufficient evidence for decisions, and reviewable actions.

title: Interpretable Reinforcement Learning for Fixed Wing Aerial Pursuit with Differentiable Decision Trees and Curriculum Learning
abstract: Neural policy networks can achieve effective control in dynamic pursuit tasks, but their decisions are difficult to audit. This study replaces the actor in proximal policy optimization with a full binary differentiable decision tree and uses a two-stage curriculum to stabilize learning. The policy was trained in a JSBSim six degree of freedom fixed wing simulation with a 15-dimensional observation, eight discrete maneuvers, a 0.2 s simulation step, and 100 million interaction steps. The learned tree has five decision levels and 32 leaves, and it is discretized after training into feature-threshold rules and deterministic leaf actions. Across 1,000 evaluation episodes covering ten initial pursuit geometries, the combined tree policy and curriculum achieved a 98.8 percent success rate, compared with 96.2 percent for neural PPO, 90.0 percent for soft actor-critic, 50.7 percent for deep Q-learning, and 0 percent for decision tree policy optimization under the reported configurations. Mean inference time was 0.26 ms per decision for the tree policy and 0.63 ms for neural PPO. In 100 direct matches against neural PPO, the tree policy won 57. The final policy can be inspected as 32 rules, although the present results are limited to one simulator, one discrete action design, and evaluations without reported variability across independent training seeds.

title: Phenology-driven multisensor unsupervised crop mapping in data-scarce irrigated agriculture: a case of Adea District in Ethiopia
abstract: Accurate irrigation planning, water allocation, and agricultural productivity assessment are frequently constrained in data-scare regions where reliable ground-based crop information and spatial coverage data are limited. This study addresses these gaps using a phenology-driven, multisensor unsupervised crop-mapping framework implemented within Google Earth Engine (GEE). The approach integrates monthly normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) profiles from Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1VV backscatter, and digital elevation model–derived terrain slope into unsupervised K-means clustering algorithm. Adea District, Ethiopia, served as a demonstration site to evaluate and interpret the phenological signatures of key irrigated crops. The identified crop types were mapped to estimate spatial coverage and compared with the ground truth observations of irrigated wheat and tomato fields. The approach successfully distinguished irrigated wheat and tomato fields with an overall classification accuracy of 91%, a Kappa coefficient of 0.82, and estimated cultivated areas of 666.93 and 812.35 ha, respectively. Combining phenological profiles with multisensor satellite observations significantly enhance unsupervised classification performance in heterogeneous, smallholder-dominated agricultural landscapes. The cloud-based framework offers a computationally scalable and cost-effective solution for crop mapping, and water productivity monitoring in data-scarce agricultural regions.

title: AI-Enabled Sustainable Precision Farming Using Raspberry Pi and Coral Edge TPU with Cloud-Based Model Training
abstract: Precision Agriculture requires intelligent, adaptable and efficient technology that is capable of making decisions in agriculture at the right time, based on the condition of the plants and the environment. This paper proposes the development of an AI-based sustainable precision farming system based on computer vision, cloud based model training, Raspberry Pi, Coral Edge TPU and the Internet of Things (IoT) sensing. The proposed architecture's sensing layer, edge processing layer, cloud intelligence layer, and application layer enables a complete data processing pipeline from the field to real time decision support. Crop photos are collected for AI condition classification and agricultural conditions such as soil moisture, temperature, humidity and light intensity are collected by built-in sensors. After the above preprocessing, normalisation, image resizing and augmentation, the dataset is divided into training, validation and test sets. The trained deep learning models in a cloud environment are then quantized and converted to be optimized for the edge, following this step. Following this step, the trained deep learning models are quantized and converted for optimization on edge. The optimized model achieves an exemplary accuracy of 94.82%, precision of 94.47%, recall of 94.05% and F1-score of 94.26%. Deploying with the Coral Edge TPU reduces inference latency to approximately 38ms compared to Raspberry Pi-only processing, increases processing throughput to 26.3 pictures per second and reduces CPU usage. The edge-assisted architecture reduces the need for constant connection to the cloud, giving local decision making a leg up. Illustrative sustainability study estimates that condition based monitoring can save 22% of the irrigation water used every day. The findings indicated that the introduction of the edge AI and cloud intelligence in precision agricultural systems that are responsive, scalable, and resource-efficient is technically possible.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: Energy-Efficient Smart Agriculture Management Framework Using IoT and Ensemble Machine Learning for Intelligent Crop Health Monitoring and Resource Optimization
abstract: Context: Smart agriculture plays an important role in addressing the challenges of food security, environmental sustainability, and sustainable farming through IoT. Farmers are facing many issues in traditional farming, such as inefficient monitoring and poor crop health detection. Traditional farming has a negative impact on crop production and sustainability. In this regard, the development of intelligent and energy-efficient agricultural monitoring systems has become crucial for contemporary precision farming applications. Objective: This study aims to monitor crop health and optimize resource use using machine learning techniques. Our proposed system intends to monitor crop conditions in real time, enhance agricultural management, and minimize unnecessary sensor utilization and communication overhead. Material/methods : In this paper, we used five machine learning classifiers to monitor crop health using sensor data. The agricultural sensor data (soil moisture, soil temperature, soil pH, humidity, air temperature, solar radiation, wind speed, NDVI index, and 5G latency) were used for crop health monitoring. The models, such as RF, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost, and soft voting were used for crop health classification into the Healthy, High_Stress, and Moderate_Stress categories. The experimental observation revealed that soft voting achieved the highest accuracy of 94.5%, macro-F1 score of 0.945, weighted F1 score of 0.945, and AUC-ROC score of 0.988 compared to the other models. The cross-validation results further validated the robustness and stability of the proposed framework. The IoT-enabled intelligent agriculture management system offers an efficient, scalable solution for real-time crop health monitoring
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Engineering a multifunctional bioactive coordination polymer nanoplatform for inflammation-responsive bone regeneration
abstract: Inflammatory bone diseases are closely associated with impaired osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and excessive inflammatory signaling. Sinomenine (SIN) exhibits anti-inflammatory activity; however, its therapeutic application is limited by poor bioavailability. In this work, a multifunctional nanoplatform (CS-1@CP1@SIN) was constructed for SIN delivery and electrochemical sensing applications. The nanocomposite exhibited a mesoporous structure, structural stability, and improved electrochemical response characteristics. In a TNF-α-induced inflammatory MSC model, CS-1@CP1@SIN improved cell viability, reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β and IL-6), and enhanced the expression of osteogenic markers (Runx2, ALP, and OCN). In addition, the CS-1@CP1@SIN-modified electrode exhibited enhanced electrocatalytic activity toward tert-butylhydroquinone (TBHQ), enabling sensitive and reliable electrochemical detection. These results demonstrate that the proposed nanoplatform integrates anti-inflammatory therapy and electrochemical sensing functions, providing a multifunctional strategy for inflammatory bone disease treatment and food antioxidant monitoring.

title: Women at the Helm: Female Top Managers and Business Process Innovation in Ecuadorian Firms
abstract: Women’s participation in senior management has increased, yet evidence regarding its relationship with different forms of business innovation remains inconclusive, particularly in emerging economies. This study examines whether formal Ecuadorian firms with a woman as their top manager are more likely to report business process innovation than firms led by men. A quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional design was applied to firm-level data from 345 enterprises included in the World Bank Enterprise Survey Ecuador; 66 firms (19.1%) reported a female top manager. Process innovation was measured from WBES item H5, which asks whether the establishment introduced a new or improved process during the preceding three years, including production or service methods, logistics/delivery/distribution, or supporting activities. Weighted logit models with firm controls and sector and region fixed effects were estimated. In the main specification (n = 327), female top management was associated with higher odds of process innovation (OR = 3.475; 95% CI [1.570, 7.688]; p = 0.002), and the direction remained positive across robustness checks. No statistically significant association was found with product innovation, R&D expenditure, or green-practice adoption. The findings therefore support a differentiated interpretation: female top management is associated with internal process change, but not uniformly with every innovation outcome. Because the data are cross-sectional and the female-manager group is comparatively small, the estimates are associational, their precision and heterogeneity are limited, and generalization is restricted to the formal non-agricultural private-sector population represented by the WBES sampling frame.

title: Predicting Lentil Seed Yield from Agronomic Traits Using a Foundation-Augmented Machine Learning Ensemble
abstract: Accurate agricultural yield prediction is crucial for crop management and data-driven decision-making. This study proposes a machine learning framework for predicting total lentil seed yield using 264 observations collected during a single growing season at one location in Sivas, Türkiye. Seven regression models and the tabular foundation model TabPFN were evaluated through nested cross-validation. The fixed post hoc Foundation-Augmented Averaging Ensemble (FAAE) combined TabPFN, Extra Trees, CatBoost, and XGBoost using equal weights, while the primary fully nested evaluation selected the four ensemble members within each outer training fold. The fully nested FAAE achieved R2 = 0.891 ± 0.045, comparable to the strongest individual models, while the fixed post hoc FAAE yielded R2 = 0.897 ± 0.038. Split conformal prediction produced well-calibrated uncertainty intervals at 80%, 90%, and 95% coverage. SHAP and LOCO identified pods per plant and biological yield as the dominant predictors of lentil yield. Overall, these findings indicate that FAAE can provide competitive predictive performance within a leakage-controlled framework while also supporting uncertainty quantification and biologically meaningful interpretation. Because the dominant predictors, pods per plant and biological yield, are measured at or near physiological maturity, the proposed framework is more suitable for end-of-season yield estimation than for early-season forecasting. The framework therefore shows potential for within-trial yield assessment, although validation using replicated material across additional years and locations is required before broader generalization.

title: Reliability-Aware Evaluation of TabPFN for Small-Sample Crop Classification in Mountainous Agricultural Regions Using Multi-Temporal Sentinel-2-Derived Features
abstract: Crop classification in mountainous agricultural regions is challenged by fragmented fields, limited reference samples, class imbalance, and strong spatial heterogeneity. We evaluated the Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) for reliability-aware small-sample crop classification using 2857 reference samples from Yuxi City, China, and 66 multi-temporal Sentinel-2-derived spectral, vegetation-index, and texture features, excluding longitude and latitude from model inputs. Under five fixed stratified 70/30 splits, TabPFN achieved an overall accuracy of 0.8944 ± 0.0127 and a Macro-F1 of 0.8798 ± 0.0173, outperforming five conventional baseline classifiers. Probability reliability analysis and selective classification further showed that confidence scores were informative of prediction risk and could support the prioritization of low-confidence samples for expert review. Calibration analysis also indicated agreement between confidence and empirical correctness. In matched five-fold validation, pooled Macro-F1 decreased from 0.8632 under stratified random folds to 0.6559 under projected-coordinate spatial folds, a 24.0% relative reduction, although TabPFN remained the highest-ranked classifier among eight tabular models. Excluding four EVI-derived predictors reduced Macro-F1 from 0.8806 to 0.8573, indicating a useful but non-exclusive dependence on these predictors. Overall, the results show that random validation can be optimistic under spatial dependence and that broader cross-region and cross-year generalization requires independent evaluation.

title: Prototype Matching Guided by Temporal–Phenological Quantitative Features for Crop Classification
abstract: Accurate crop classification requires effective representation of crop-growth dynamics and traceable classification decisions. This study proposes a prototype-matching framework guided by quantitative temporal and phenological features to establish explicit relationships between crop-growth representations and class-level references. Using multi-temporal Sentinel-2 imagery from an oasis agricultural region in Manas County, Xinjiang, China, four major crops were investigated: cotton, maize, spring wheat, and winter wheat. The framework integrates explicit temporal statistics, quantitative phenological descriptors, and their corresponding deep representations into a unified feature space. Class prototypes are constructed from the resulting representations, and final crop labels are assigned through explicit sample–prototype similarity or distance comparisons. Prototype-space relationships are further analysed to quantify class separability and examine potential classification ambiguity. The results demonstrate that temporal representations provide stronger class separation than phenological representations, while their integration enables continuous temporal dynamics and structured phenological characteristics to be examined within a unified prototype space. Prototype-space analysis reveals clearer separation for cotton and maize, whereas spring wheat exhibits the smallest similarity and distance margins. In the primary field-level classification experiment, the framework achieves an overall accuracy of 96.03%, a Kappa coefficient of 0.9356, a Balanced Accuracy of 86.05%, and a Macro-F1 of 86.26%. In a separate experiment under common training conditions, prototype matching achieves a Balanced Accuracy of 91.36% and a Macro-F1 of 89.53%, exceeding Transformer and random forest by 7.36 and 12.78 percentage points in Balanced Accuracy, respectively. The improvements are particularly evident for spring wheat. These findings demonstrate that the framework connects quantitative crop-growth representation with explicit prototype-based classification while providing measurable evidence for interpreting class-specific discrimination and classification ambiguity.
