title: MindVLM: Neural-Grounded Visual Captioning via Subject-Aware Semantic Evidence Selection
abstract: Translating visual brain activity into natural language offers a powerful window into human cognition and neural semantic representation. Most prior brain-captioning approaches project fMRI signals into language space using paired supervision. However, the widely used Natural Scenes Dataset (NSD) was built based only on image-fMRI pairs, while existing methods rely on MS-COCO captions as indirect textual supervision. Critically, during fMRI acquisition, participants observe only cropped image regions, whereas the associated MS-COCO captions describe full scenes. This mismatch creates a fundamental gap between neural representations and textual supervision, introducing an inherent semantic loss in NSD-based brain captioning. To mitigate this limitation, we reformulate brain captioning as Neural-Grounded Visual Captioning, where language is generated directly from visually grounded neural evidence rather than text supervision. We propose MindVLM, a framework that maps fMRI signals into subject-aware visual tokens and leverages a frozen vision language model (VLM) to produce interpretable and personalized descriptions. Instead of point-wise regression, MindVLM focuses on extracting semantically relevant visual cues from neural activity, naturally accommodating partial observability and inter-subject variability. Extensive experiments on NSD show that MindVLM consistently improves caption quality across multiple VLM backbones, including LLaVA-v1.5, Qwen2.5-VL, and Gemma3, beyond intrinsic model priors. Despite requiring neither text supervision nor an LLM during training and operating under an image-grounded inference paradigm distinct from conventional captioning methods, MindVLM remains competitive with supervised approaches, suggesting that subject-specific neural grounding provides an efficient, scalable, and interpretable path toward faithful brain-to-language generation.

title: Byzantine-Resilient Federated Large Language Model via Hypergraph Message Passing
abstract: Federated Large Language Models (FedLLMs) are promising to deliver privacy-preserving, collaborative intelligence. The decentralized training process is vulnerable to Byzantine attacks that corrupt semantic consistency and factual resilience through malicious model updates. This paper presents a new resilience strategy that prevents semantically corrupted knowledge from propagating during federated aggregation. A defense problem is formulated to jointly maximize global accuracy and suppress manipulated model updates, enabling trustworthy knowledge aggregation without accessing private local data. To strengthen the resilience of FedLLMs, we develop a novel Hypergraph Message Passing Graph Autoencoder (HMP-GAE) framework, where low-rank model updates are represented as nodes in a hypergraph and high-order semantic relationships among multiple agents are exploited through iterative message passing. By leveraging historical checkpoints and cross-agent relational reasoning, HMP-GAE identifies and suppresses semantically inconsistent updates while preserving knowledge alignment among agents throughout federated training. HMP-GAE is implemented using Qwen-2.5 and Llama-3.2 as pretrained FedLLM backbones and evaluated on AG News and Yahoo! Answers datasets. Compared to existing defenses, HMP-GAE improves global accuracy by $1.21$\%, reduces final-model classification semantic entropy by $44.08$\%, and lowers perplexity by $13.34$\%. HMP-GAE outperforms the GAE-based defense by improving the accuracy $1.39$\%, reducing the semantic entropy by $54.5$\%, and lowering perplexity by $35.5$\%.

title: Neural expectation-maximization and meta-models
abstract: We interpret Transformer networks as learned approximations to a hybrid probabilistic-inference procedure that combines max-product Loopy Belief Propagation (LBP) with Expectation--Maximization (EM). In this view, a Transformer performs inference in partially observed Markov Random Fields (MRFs) whose structure and parameters are not given a priori but are inferred from data. We show that self-attention implements a differentiable approximation to max-product LBP on an input-conditioned, dynamically structured MRF, with attention weights encoding learned structural affinities. We further establish an EM correspondence at the level of depth: each layer updates latent representations in an E-step-like forward pass, while the transition $θ^{(l)} \to θ^{(l+1)}$ across layers acts as an implicit M-step. Building on this interpretation, we introduce \emph{meta-models}, a design paradigm in which inputs generate instance-specific parameters, unifying mechanisms such as self-attention, mixture-of-experts, and gated units within a single framework. Empirical results support the proposed perspective.

title: Faithful and Complete LLM-Assisted Automated Construction of Hierarchical Hardware Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Hardware datasheets contain engineering specifications essential for component selection, system integration, and hardware compatibility verification. However, manual inspection is tedious and error-prone because datasheets are lengthy and heterogeneous, with dense information fragmented across tables, figures, and text. Although large language models (LLMs) can automate this process, naïve one-shot processing omits relevant specifications even when the document fits within the model's context window. We present an automated LLM-driven pipeline that transforms hardware datasheets into general-purpose hierarchical hardware knowledge graphs through chunk-based property extraction, hierarchical routing, and iterative refinement. The framework uses LLMs for information extraction and semantic reasoning while preserving source provenance and applying graph updates through validated instructions and deterministic local execution. This staged design reduces per-query context and maintains traceable intermediate representations. The resulting knowledge graphs provide semantically organized, source-grounded hardware properties for downstream retrieval and reasoning. We evaluate the framework on 20 hardware datasheets spanning diverse component types and document lengths. We assess property faithfulness and introduce inter-graph completeness to measure relative semantic coverage without exhaustive ground truth. Our framework achieves 98.8% property faithfulness compared with 76.1% for the one-shot baseline, while fully covering 83.6% of faithful baseline properties; in the reverse direction, the baseline fully covers only 10.5% of ours. These improvements provide more reliable and comprehensive engineering information for downstream hardware design and verification, reducing the risk of overlooked constraints and incorrect decisions.

title: Credit Attribution in Timestamped Soccer Networks Using Multivariate Hawkes Processes
abstract: The two main traditional player statistics used in soccer are goals scored and assists, with an assist credited when a player's pass immediately leads to a teammate scoring. Attributing credit solely to the player who makes the final pass before a goal fails to account for the contributions of multiple players in the buildup to the goal. Consequently, traditional statistics provide only a limited view of player involvement. In this paper, we use multivariate Hawkes processes (MHPs) to model timestamped sequences of passes and shots, which form continuous-time networks. MHPs provide a branching mechanism where an event (a pass or shot) can be generated as a child of a previous event, which allows us to quantify each pass's contribution to a subsequent pass or shot. This approach distributes credit across multiple passes within an attacking sequence, making it applicable across a wide range of situations. Building on this framework, we propose expected goal involvements (xGI), a metric that measures a player's involvement in creating goal scoring opportunities based on their passes. This metric identifies players who play key roles in creating goal scoring opportunities even if they do not make the final pass, offering a more comprehensive measure of attacking involvement and player performance.

title: Game Petri Nets: Compositional Modeling and Analysis of Large-Scale Strategic Systems
abstract: Large-scale strategic systems, such as maintenance workflows, cyber campaigns, and multi-agent AI pipelines, consist of many interactions whose outcomes determine which later interactions become possible, who takes part, and with what resources. We introduce game Petri nets, formalized as outcome-driven compositional game Petri nets (OCGPNs), to model and analyze such systems. Local games are attached to places of a colored Petri net, and a game-to-token interface converts each resolved game into typed tokens that enable, synchronize, or block subsequent games. For general, concurrent nets, we give an operational semantics and a structural theory based on invariants and Farkas certificates, which shows that guards can certify unreachability whereas incentive instruments can only change values. For sequential nets, the net induces a stochastic game on its game places. We prove that global equilibria are exactly collections of equilibria of local games augmented by continuation values, characterize through successor-level pivotality when downstream games change upstream behavior, and compute values place by place via a decomposition into strongly connected components, at a cost additive in local game sizes. A composition calculus based on place fusion glues certificates across subnets and summarizes downstream subnets by their entry values. Two running examples, a maintenance workflow and an intrusion campaign derived from multi-resolution cyber-defense games, illustrate the theory, including the composition of a newly discovered attack scenario with an existing campaign.

title: Tactile Sensing-based Secure and Gentle Grasping of Unknown Objects
abstract: Reliable robotic manipulation requires maintaining a firm grasp while strictly avoiding both contact slip and structural damage to the object. Satisfying these inherent \textit{secure-and-gentle} grasping constraints is challenging for unknown objects. We present a novel online data-driven predictive control framework for safe dynamic robotic grasping of unknown objects. The proposed system features a pair of compact, single-channel tactile-sensing modules that characterize the gripper-object dynamic interaction in real time, entirely bypassing the need for prior knowledge or offline training. A finite-state-machine-based grasping force probing mechanism is developed to establish the initial grasping force and explicitly identify grasping force constraints. Through online dynamics learning, a Gaussian Process (GP) model captures gripper-object interaction dynamics. The model uncertainties are further used to form robust grasping constraints, which are embedded into a model predictive control scheme. We demonstrate error convergence in a probabilistic sense. The proposed control framework runs at 100~Hz in real time to dynamically manipulate and handle objects rather than static holding. Extensive experimental evaluations across diverse contact surface topologies and various types of objects validate superior performance and efficiency compared to baseline strategies. The proposed method is able to manipulate objects ranging from delicate items, such as raw tofu and marshmallows, to rough objects, such as rocks.

title: Meta-Reflective Evolution Effectively Improves Production AI Systems
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-guided evolutionary optimization has successfully improved prompts, programs, and even entire AI systems. Most optimization methods select a candidate from the search frontier, then mutate it in one LLM pass based only on its failures. This focus on the frontier can stall on production AI systems, where isolated failures reveal little about complex, hidden interactions. We introduce CoCoEvolve (Cortex Code Evolve), an evolutionary optimizer built around what we call meta-reflection, wherein an agentic mutator (Cortex Code) selectively retrieves evidence from the entire evolutionary history and probes the live system before verifying and proposing mutations. We apply CoCoEvolve to optimize three classes of production AI systems: data agents, LLM-powered data pipelines, and data engineering workflows. On DABStep, CoCoEvolve tops the public leaderboard, reaching 92.8% held-out hard accuracy compared to 78.4% for Meta-Harness and 30.4% for GEPA under matched conditions. Across six LLM data pipeline workloads, it outperforms every evaluated baseline. On data-eng-bench, CoCoEvolve lifts test-set solve rate from 59.1% to 77.4%, past the best baseline of 73.6%. It also has 11 percentage points higher accuracy than GEPA on HotpotQA while remaining competitive with specialized optimizers on established mathematical and systems benchmarks. Matched ablations confirm that each component of CoCoEvolve contributes to these gains, demonstrating the value of meta-reflection for optimizing production AI systems.

title: Drude, Where's My Charge? End-to-End Learning of Polarizable Drude Force Fields for Polymer Electrolytes
abstract: Molecular dynamics simulations of solid polymer electrolytes require force fields that are fast enough to converge ion transport over hundreds of nanoseconds, yet accurately describe the ion-polymer interactions that govern it. Fixed-charge force fields meet the first requirement but neglect electronic polarization, an effect often approximated by scaling ionic charges using empirically chosen factors. Here we present AutoDrude, a differentiable framework that parametrizes polarizable Drude force fields directly from DFT energies, forces, and dipoles, with no empirical tuning and at only 1.20 times the cost of a fixed-charge simulation. For PEO-LiTFSI, the dipole-constrained (hard-constraint) AutoDrude model reproduces the experimental ionic conductivity as accurately as the best charge-scaled model (17% versus 16% mean absolute percentage error). We compare the polarizable forcefield to fixed charge ones models by fitting a fixed charge model. Unlike the charge-scaled models tested here, however, AutoDrude also reproduces the dilute-limit cation transference number, its increase with salt concentration, and the absence of Li-TFSI contact ion pairs at low concentration. A penalty-based (soft-constraint) variant yields a closer fit to the DFT reference yet underestimates the conductivity by up to an order of magnitude, demonstrating that closer agreement with DFT training data alone does not guarantee accurate ion transport. These results indicate that although charge scaling can reproduce ionic conductivity the explicit inclusion of polarization is necessary to capture the concentration dependence of cation transport in PEO-LiTFSI.

title: Phantom Zernike Wavefront Sensor: Phase Contrast with Engineered Focal Plane Reference Speckles
abstract: We introduce the Phantom Zernike Wavefront Sensor (phantom ZWFS), an engineered reference extension of phase-contrast wavefront sensing in which controlled pupil plane modulation generates off-axis coherent speckle structures that undergo localized focal plane phase shifts. These references may replace the central ZWFS reference when the on-axis PSF core is required for another optical function, such as photonic science coupling, or may augment a conventional central ZWFS response to provide additional wavefront information. Using a monochromatic scalar model, we derive the resulting carrier structure and show how the engineered references can be recovered through spatial demodulation and incorporated into calibrated reconstruction. A simple four-reference realization demonstrates that the reference geometry redistributes photon sensitivity across spatial frequency magnitude and orientation, producing mode dependent changes in linearity and cross-talk rather than a uniform improvement over a classical ZWFS. We then consider differential piston on a seven segment aperture as an application specific example. A hybrid sensor retaining the central ZWFS phase region and adding six engineered references that match the segment geometry gives similar precision near the phased state but substantially improved performance at larger piston excursions. Under the adopted photon-noise-limited benchmark, the hybrid reduces the nonlinear reconstruction error and provides better conditioned optical encoding of the piston state than an idealized vector ZWFS, allowing more precise piston estimation from the same detected photon flux at larger piston excursions.

title: Synergistic Use of Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, & EnMAP Data towards Advancing Agricultural Monitoring in Greece
abstract: Accurate and frequently updated land cover and crop type maps are essential for environmental monitoring, agricultural management, and informed decision-making. While multi-temporal SAR and multispectral data from various satellite sensors have been widely assessed towards this end, the potential of spaceborne hyperspectral Environmental Mapping and Analysis Program (EnMAP) data for such applications, remains largely unexplored. This study evaluates the added value of multi-temporal EnMAP observations combined with Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 time series for joint land cover and crop type mapping in a complex landscape of Western Greece. A detailed reference dataset comprising 32 classes (14 non-crop and 18 crop categories) was developed, and progressively richer sensor configurations were evaluated using a Random Forest classifier. Different representations of the high-dimensional EnMAP feature space were assessed, including original bands, spectral indices, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and Minimum Noise Fraction (MNF) transformations. All experimental configurations achieved Overall Accuracy (OA) rates above 88% and average F1-score above 78%. Incorporating Sentinel-1 temporal metrics increased OA from 88.13%, using Sentinel-2 spectro-temporal metrics alone, to 89.40%, while the addition of EnMAP features further improved performance across all feature representations. The highest OA (90.27%) and average F1-score (83.45%) were achieved by combining Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 metrics with the MNF-transformed EnMAP features. Overall, multi-temporal EnMAP information enhanced notably the discrimination of spectrally complex and overlapping classes, particularly those with lower baseline performance, while dimensionality reduction techniques provided the greatest classification benefits. These results encourage further research on hyperspectral time series over broader spatial extents and their integration into operational land cover and crop type mapping frameworks.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things in Smart Agriculture: A Bibliometric and Thematic Review of Data Infrastructures and Sustainability Implications
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping smart agriculture through prediction, automation, resource optimization, and data-driven decision-making. However, its effective and sustainable deployment depends on reliable Internet of Things (IoT) data infrastructures supporting sensing, connectivity, data acquisition, transmission, and distributed processing. This review maps research at the intersection of AI, IoT, and smart agriculture and examines its data-infrastructure requirements and sustainability implications. Drawing on 441 Scopus-indexed, peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2017 and 2025, the study combines bibliometric performance analysis, science mapping, and content-based thematic interpretation to identify publication trends, intellectual foundations, influential research fronts, emerging themes, and deployment challenges. The bibliometric analyses characterize AI–IoT research in smart agriculture, while IoT data infrastructure provides the principal analytical lens, and sustainability and responsible deployment are examined through interpretive synthesis. The findings reveal rapid publication growth and prominent themes involving connected sensing, predictive analytics, edge intelligence, remote sensing, smart irrigation, cybersecurity, blockchain, and edge–cloud processing. Persistent barriers include limited interoperability, inconsistent data quality, energy requirements, scalability constraints, cybersecurity and governance risks, affordability, and unequal adoption in resource-constrained contexts. The review concludes that sustainable AI-enabled agriculture requires reliable, secure, interoperable, energy-efficient, inclusive, and context-appropriate digital infrastructures.

title: SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT FOR ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION IN BANGLADESH: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES
abstract: Bangladesh exemplifies a central paradox of sustainable development: how to maintain rapid economic and social progress without undermining the ecological systems upon which development depends. This paper critically examines Bangladesh's environmental governance architecture, the major barriers to its effective implementation, and opportunities for achieving a just green transition. It adopts a qualitative, desk-based methodology combining doctrinal legal analysis with critical examination of national policies and plans, international commitments, judicial decisions, and institutional reports. The analysis demonstrates that Bangladesh has an extensive environmental legal and policy framework, including constitutional obligations, pollution-control legislation, environmental courts, climate strategies, and long-term delta planning. However, its implementation remains constrained by fragmented institutional authority, inconsistent enforcement, inadequate monitoring capacity, weaknesses in environmental assessment procedures, limited local government capacity, and continuing incentives for environmentally harmful investments. Climate vulnerability further intensifies these governance challenges, disproportionately affecting low-income and climate-vulnerable communities. Nevertheless, significant opportunities exist for a just green transition through renewable energy, resource-efficient industries, circular production systems, nature-based adaptation, sustainable agriculture, green finance, and digitally enabled environmental accountability. The paper proposes a reform agenda centred on enforceable environmental standards, strategic environmental assessment, open environmental data, stronger institutional coordination, enhanced local capacity, effective application of the polluter-pays principle, and meaningful public participation. Sustainable development in Bangladesh will become credible only when environmental protection becomes a binding condition of development decision-making rather than a remedial response after environmental damage has occurred.
journal: Journal of Asian and African Social Science and Humanities

title: Disentangling Climate and Non-Climate Determinants of Cereal Productivity: Evidence from India’s Arid and Semi-Arid Regions
abstract: Assessing the impact of annual climate variability on cereal crop yields is crucial for addressing food security challenges in countries with arid and semi-arid regions. Using district/state panel data for India (1998-2021), this study estimates fixed-effects, fully modified OLS (FMOLS), and dynamic OLS (DOLS) models and applies Pedroni and Kao tests to establish long-run relationships between climate, agricultural inputs, and yields of wheat, rice, and millets (bajra, jowar, and other small millets). Cointegration results indicate a stable long-run association among variables. Across crops, cultivated area is a strong, positive correlate of productivity. For wheat, higher mean maximum temperature and greater rainfall (when excessive) reduce yields, while agricultural credit supports productivity; mean minimum temperature shows limited effects. For rice, area remains strongly positive, temperature effects are generally negative but imprecisely estimated, and aridity substantially depresses yields. For millets, maximum (and in some models minimum) temperature lowers yields, whereas rainfall, fertiliser, and agricultural credit are yield-enhancing. Taken together, the results show that models omitting input and financial controls risk overstating climate impacts; including credit and fertiliser management meaningfully attenuates climate-only effects. Policy implications include targeting heat-risk management and stress-tolerant varieties where temperature pressures are acute, improving water management in rainfall-sensitive systems, strengthening access to well-structured agricultural credit, and promoting fertiliser stewardship and place-specific crop strategies to bolster resilience and sustain cereal production under a changing climate.

title: Forecasting Pakistan’s Food Crop Trade: ARIMA-Based Evidence on Export and Import Dynamics
abstract: International trade in major food crops plays an important role in Pakistan’s food security, agricultural economy, export earnings, and dependence on imported supplies. Although previous forecasting studies in Pakistan have mainly focused on crop production, area, and yield, relatively less attention has been given to the future behaviour of food-crop exports and imports. This study examines the historical trade patterns and future prospects of wheat, rice, and maize in Pakistan using annual time-series data for 1961–2024. The Augmented Dickey–Fuller (ADF) test was used to examine the stationarity of the selected trade series, followed by automatic Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) models to forecast future export and import trends. The results show considerable differences in the trade behaviour of the three crops. Wheat trade has experienced substantial fluctuations, including periods of increased import dependence and varying levels of exports. Rice has maintained a stronger export-oriented position, although its trade has also changed considerably over time. Maize, which historically had a relatively limited role in international trade, has shown a notable increase in both exports and imports in recent years. The forecasts for 2025–2034 suggest different future patterns across the three commodities. Rice imports are expected to increase, while rice exports show a gradual upward movement. Maize trade is also projected to remain active, whereas wheat trade is expected to follow a comparatively gradual path after its historical fluctuations. These findings highlight the different trade dynamics of Pakistan’s major food crops and demonstrate the usefulness of commodity-specific forecasting for agricultural trade planning. The study provides useful forward-looking information for anticipating import requirements, planning exports, and addressing potential food-security concerns. However, the forecasts should be interpreted with caution because future trade conditions may also be affected by climate, domestic production, international prices, exchange-rate movements, and government trade policies that are not explicitly included in the univariate ARIMA models.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Fine-Tuned Transfer Learning CNN Architectures for Automated Citrus Fruit Disease Classification
abstract: Early and accurate detection of citrus diseases is essential for maintaining fruit quality, minimising crop losses, and supporting sustainable agricultural production. Automated image-based diagnostic systems offer a scalable alternative to conventional manual inspection, which is often time-intensive, subjective, and susceptible to diagnostic variability. This study presents a transfer-learning-based deep learning framework for automated classification of citrus fruit diseases using a curated image collection derived from Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) resources. The dataset was organised into two classification groups: lemon and orange. The lemon dataset initially comprised 208 images across four classes: Healthy, Canker, Mold, and Scab, while the orange dataset contained 2,240 images across two classes. To address data scarcity and improve model generalisation, targeted data augmentation involving zooming (0.8–1.2), rotation (35°), and horizontal flipping was employed, increasing the datasets to 1,600 and 4,000 images for lemon and orange, respectively. Five ImageNet-pretrained convolutional neural network architectures—VGG16, ResNet50, InceptionV3, DenseNet121, and EfficientNetB0—were fine-tuned and evaluated using a stratified 70:30 training–testing protocol with five-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score under a standardized experimental configuration. The results demonstrate that InceptionV3 achieved the highest classification accuracy of 90.0% on the four-class lemon dataset, while DenseNet121 obtained the best accuracy of 93.0% on the binary orange dataset. These findings indicate that appropriate transfer learning and targeted augmentation can substantially improve classification performance and model generalisation, particularly in limited-data agricultural imaging scenarios. The proposed benchmarking framework enables systematic, controlled comparisons of fine-tuned CNN architectures under consistent preprocessing, augmentation, training, and evaluation conditions. The resulting models can be integrated into real-time citrus disease diagnostic systems and deployed on resource-constrained platforms, including mobile and edge-computing devices, supporting scalable precision-agriculture applications.

title: Maize genetic diversity is largely unstructured by human ethnolinguistic diversity in its center of origin
abstract: Population structure and environmental features often capture major axes of genetic variation in many species. Yet the impacts of human activity often remain unquantified. For domesticated species that rely on human activity for survival and dispersal, human movements and cultural differences may play key roles patterning genetic diversity. Maize is a staple crop of enormous cultural importance to indigenous peoples of the Americas, but cannot survive or disperse without farmers. Using publicly available genotyping and passport data from approximately 2,000 traditional maize varieties, more than 500 whole genome sequences of humans from Mexico, and indigenous linguistic maps, we quantify anthropogenic effects on maize genetic diversity in the Americas. Maize shows very little overall structure, highlighting the effectiveness of indigenous farmers in moving and mixing maize populations. While principal components of maize diversity show meaningful correlations to human genetic diversity, our linear modeling suggests little additional impact of human population structure beyond shared geography. Though differences in maize diversity are often patterned by language locally, we find only weak genome-wide effects at larger spatial scales. Despite the relatively weak global signal of anthropogenic effects, linguistic GWAS, outlier FSTanalyses, and selection scans identified loci associated with specific languages. Leveraging landscape-level sequencing data, we highlight how anthropogenic factors have shaped patterns of maize genetic diversity across Mesoamerica.

title: SIMORGH: Ensemble-Aware Geometric Deep Learning for Apo-State and Cryptic Ligand Binding Site Prediction
abstract: Most computational methods identify protein–ligand binding sites from ligand-bound (holo) protein structures, where the binding pocket is already preorganized. Although convenient for benchmarking, this setting differs from the practical drug discovery scenario, in which binding sites must be inferred from ligand-free (apo) proteins. In fact, binding-competent conformations may represent only a subset of the accessible structural ensemble, while transient and cryptic pockets can emerge through conformational fluctuations. Consequently, prediction from a single static structure is often insufficient. Here we present SIMORGH, an ensemble-aware SE(3)-equivariant geometric learning framework that predicts ligand binding sites by integrating information across protein conformational ensembles. SIMORGH employs a two-stage architecture consisting of a structure-level equivariant encoder that learns geometric representations from individual conformations and a lightweight ensemble-level aggregation module that combines them into residue-level binding predictions while scaling near-linearly with both protein and ensemble size. We evaluate SIMORGH across multiple complementary settings, including the PLINDER apo benchmark, molecular dynamics trajectories spanning more than 200 cryptic-pocket proteins, and established community benchmarks. SIMORGH consistently outperforms existing static and dynamics-aware methods under the challenging ligand-free setting, while identifying cryptic binding pockets, maintaining strong prediction consistency between paired apo and holo structures, and scaling efficiently to large multi-chain complexes. To facilitate reproducible, transparent, and accessible use, Simorgh is available through the Galaxy Europe server ( https://usegalaxy.eu ).

title: AI agent supervision of structural model building and refinement
abstract: Structural model building and refinement need many decisions between different programs. These decisions often depend on an experienced researcher who knows how the programs work together and how to read experimental data. We used Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 to supervise this work for 24 cryo-EM and X-ray cases. The work finished in about 36 hours on one workstation. The agent prepared the inputs, ran established programs, read the validation results, compared candidate models and chose the next step. For 15 deposited cryo-EM models with weak starting geometry, the median MolProbity score improved from 2.62 to 1.76. For three crystal structures, the agent models came close to the published Rfree values. Chemical information such as ligands, ions and modifications must be provided by the researcher, in the same way as the sequence. With this information, the agent can place and check these components. These results show that agent supervision is acceptable when every decision can be inspected. The researcher makes the final scientific judgment. We suggest practical requirements for this kind of use. Future AI agents may help researchers obtain high quality and reliable structures of biological macromolecules.

title: Defining a subgroup within autism leads to potential enrichment criteria in investigational therapeutic development: Comparing resting state gamma band power to a fragile X syndrome reference sample
Trust in AI-mediated electronic commerce: a systematic review and integrative framework
abstract: Artificial intelligence now stands between merchants and consumers across digital exchange, in chatbots, recommenders, virtual influencers, generative content, service robots and robo-advisors. Consumer reliance on that intermediary is shaped in part by trust. This review synthesises 166 studies in which trust or calibrated reliance is explicitly measured, manipulated or theorised, screened from 7,606 records under PRISMA 2020, with 45 trust-adjacent studies reported separately. Coding what is trusted shows three referents, the AI agent, the deploying merchant and the platform-institutional system, distributed non-randomly across applications. Formal testing finds no detectable association between the direction of the anthropomorphism effect and either stakes or referent, a provisional association between disclosure direction and stakes, and a strong association between reporting any boundary condition and experimental design. The resulting framework links referent, mechanism, boundary condition, trust and reliance state, outcome and repair, and reframes electronic commerce design around calibrated reliance rather than maximal trust.

title: AI Agent Platform Engineering
A Unified System for Intelligent Financial Fraud Detection
abstract: Modern financial ecosystems require real-time, transparent, and trustworthy fraud detection systems capable of processing massive transaction volumes while meeting regulatory and auditing requirements. This paper presents a unified, modular system integrating four layers: (a) a blockchain-based transaction logging mechanism, (b) an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) fraud detection engine, (c) a Mistral large language model (LLM) client for natural-language reasoning, and (d) an AI agent for orchestration. A Python-based prototype demonstrates the complete pipeline—from transaction ingestion to fraud scoring, explanation generation, and immutable blockchain storage. The system serves as an educational and experimental platform for research and development, offering flexibility and extensibility for future enhancements.
journal: Proceedings of the 7th National HBCU Blockchain, Fintech & AI Conference

title: Ensemble LLM Consensus Architectures for Deterministic Trade Signal Generation: An Empirical Study of Multi-Persona AI Panels in Retail FinTech Applications
abstract: This paper presents an empirical study of a multi-persona large language model (LLM) consensus architecture deployed in a live retail FinTech platform for equity and options trade signal generation. Grounded in a prior quantitative trading framework (Anton, 2025) and building upon academic antecedents in multi-agent LLM systems (Xiao et al., 2024), the Edge Stack Trading platform deploys a six-persona AI analyst panel producing structured, constrained verdicts across a real-time multi-signal scoring architecture. Analysis of nine live trade reports generated between April and May 2026 reports a preliminary 87.5% directional accuracy rate across eight assessable signals in an exploratory proof-of-concept evaluation, with unanimous panel consensus strongly correlated with system confidence extremes. Inter-model disagreement functions as an auditable risk signal, and model API failures produce identifiable, recoverable degradation patterns consistent with graceful degradation requirements for financial AI systems. The architecture addresses the 2026 conference theme of Reliable and Deterministic AI for Financial Systems through structured verdict formats, role-constrained persona prompting, and explicit multi-signal deterministic scoring as mechanisms for AI governance in retail financial decision support. One incorrect signal (Palantir) reveals a boundary condition in which extreme valuation risk overrides technical alignment, informing a specific architectural recommendation. Implications for HBCU financial technology education, democratized institutional-grade AI analysis, and regulatory auditability are discussed.
journal: Proceedings of the 7th National HBCU Blockchain, Fintech & AI Conference

title: Engineering Trust in Algorithmic Lending: Explainable, Fairness-Aware Credit Risk Modeling for Financial Inclusion
abstract: Consumer credit decisions are increasingly influenced by machine learning, but its use creates a major conflict for financial inclusion because models that are geared for predictive accuracy may encode and magnify inequalities against the very groups that inclusion-oriented lending aims to assist. This study asks whether predictive performance alone is a sufficient basis for trust in algorithmic lending. Using the UCI Default of Credit Card Clients dataset (30,000 borrowers in Taiwan), we train and compare logistic regression, random forest and gradient-boosted decision tree (XGBoost) classifiers and subject the strongest model to SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) interpretation, a demographic fairness audit across sex, education and age, a feature-ablation test and a post-processing mitigation. XGBoost attains a ROC-AUC of 0.775, on par with established benchmarks, confirming that raw accuracy is not the differentiating contribution. The audit reveals moderate but real disparities in false-positive rates, with the youngest and least-educated applicants most often wrongly flagged; we also show that naively including a very small subgroup substantially overstates apparent disparity. The assigned credit limit is strongly stratified by education and age, yet removing it does not reduce the disparity, illustrating that “fairness through unawareness” is insufficient because the signal is redundantly encoded in correlated features. Group-aware decision thresholds, a straightforward post-processing solution, lower the education false-positive gap from 0.082 to 0.005 at the expense of 0.4 percentage points of accuracy. We suggest a layered evaluation approach and contend that explainability, meticulous fairness auditing and mitigation are necessary conditions for reliable, inclusion-focused credit AI.

title: ECOSYSTEM MAPPING OF STARTUPS, ENTREPRENEURS, AND SMEs IN BAUCHI STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: This study presents an ecosystem mapping of startups, entrepreneurs, and small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Bauchi State, Nigeria, using a survey research design. The population comprised entrepreneurs, startup founders, and SME owners across multiple sectors in Bauchi State, while 1,000 valid responses were obtained from 1,200 distributed questionnaires through stratified random sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered online and offline and analyzed using descriptive statistics, specifically frequencies and percentages, supported by charts. The study examined demographic profiles, business sectors, challenges, technical skills, income levels, and support needs of entrepreneurs. The findings revealed that the majority of respondents are aged 26–35 years (56.8%), with females representing 71% of respondents. Over 93% currently run a business, concentrated in food processing and catering, agriculture, textiles/fashion, ICT, and related activities. Major challenges include limited funding (72%), restricted market access (18%), and technical capacity gaps, while more than 92% expressed interest in acquiring new skills such as digital marketing, financial management, and ICT. Although 51% earn below NGN 50,000 monthly, respondents identified opportunities for locally produced goods in wider markets. The study concludes that Bauchi hosts a vibrant but resource-constrained entrepreneurial ecosystem, requiring targeted interventions in financing, skill development, shared infrastructure, and market linkages to enhance productivity and economic inclusion.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN AFRICA: NIGERIA'S ROLE IN THE GLOBAL DIGITAL ORDER
abstract: The rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies presents transformative opportunities and significant challenges for Africa's sustainable development aspirations. This paper examines the intersection of AI, international cooperation, and sustainable development in Africa, with particular focus on Nigeria's evolving role in shaping the emerging global digital order. Drawing on Nigeria's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2025–2029), the African Union Continental AI Strategy (2024), and the United Nations Global Digital Compact (2024), the analysis situates Nigeria within a multi-scalar governance architecture spanning national, regional, and global levels. The paper contends that Nigeria occupies a strategically significant position as both a beneficiary of and contributor to global AI governance frameworks, yet confronts structural constraints including infrastructure deficits, human capital gaps, and data sovereignty challenges that condition its capacity to translate policy ambition into tangible developmental outcomes. Through examination of Nigeria's five-pillar AI strategy, emerging AI applications in agriculture and healthcare, and its participation in international AI governance forums, the paper identifies pathways through which Nigeria can leverage international cooperation to advance sustainable development while contributing to a more inclusive global digital order. The findings suggest that Nigeria's trajectory offers valuable lessons for other African nations navigating the complex interplay between technological catch-up, sustainable development, and global governance participation.
journal: International Journal of African Research Sustainability Studies

title: Studies on the Effect of Elevated Temperature and CO2 on Yield of Maize Crop under Raipur Condition
abstract: Climate-driven changes in temperature and atmospheric CO2 may alter maize productivity, and their combined effects can differ among cultivars and sowing environments. This study used the CERES-Maize model within DSSAT to assess yield responses of NK-30, NK-7328 and NK-6110 under Raipur conditions. The model was calibrated with 2022–23 crop, weather, soil and management data and validated with 2023–24 data. Grain yield was simulated for three sowing environments (D1, D2 and D3) under the current condition, elevated CO2 concentrations of 450, 500 and 550 ppm, temperature increases of 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5°C, and corresponding combined CO2-temperature scenarios. Root mean square error and percentage error were used to characterise differences between the present and scenario simulations. In the CO2-only simulations, grain yield increased across cultivar–environment combinations, with tabulated changes ranging from about 2.1% to 10.2%. In contrast, temperature-only simulations showed yield reductions ranging from 2.19% to 10.61%. Under combined elevated CO2 and temperature scenarios, yield remained below the present simulated values, with reductions ranging from 1.17% to 7.62%, indicating that the positive CO2 response only partly offset the simulated temperature penalty. Responses varied among cultivars and sowing environments. The findings demonstrate the value of locally calibrated crop simulation for examining cultivar-specific maize yield responses to incremental climatic changes under Raipur conditions.
journal: International Journal of Environment and Climate Change

title: Constraints Faced by Farmers in Using Social Media for Agricultural Information in Kanpur
abstract: Aims: This study identified the major constraints experienced by farmers in using social media for agricultural information and to document their suggestions for improving digital agricultural extension services. Study Design: An ex post facto research design was adopted. Place and Duration of Study: The study was conducted in Bilhaur block of Kanpur Nagar district, Uttar Pradesh, India, during 2023–2024. Methodology: A total of 120 smartphone-owning farmers were selected through simple random sampling from six villages of Bilhaur block. Primary data were collected through personal interviews using a structured and pre-tested interview schedule. The data were analysed using frequency, percentage, and rank-order techniques to identify the major constraints faced by farmers and their suggestions for improving the utilisation of social media for agricultural information. Results: The major constraints reported by farmers were lack of training on the use of social media (92.50%), language and cultural barriers (87.50%), low educational level (84.16%), lack of technical knowledge (81.66%), lack of trust in adopting social media (79.16%), and poor network connectivity (75.83%). Among the suggestions, ensuring a reliable and uninterrupted electricity supply (92.50%), improving village-level network connectivity (82.50%), providing financial support (80.00%), providing agricultural information in Hindi and other regional languages (75.83%), and providing training to improve farmers’ understanding of social media (75.83%) were the most frequently suggested measures. Conclusion: The findings indicate that farmers’ effective utilisation of social media for agricultural information is influenced by educational, technical, infrastructural, economic, language-related, and institutional constraints. Improving rural digital infrastructure, providing practical training, ensuring reliable electricity and network connectivity, providing agricultural information in Hindi and other regional languages, and strengthening linkages with agricultural extension services may help improve the effectiveness of social media as a complementary agricultural extension channel.

title: Dynamic modelling of phase‐change solvent carbon capture process based on AT ‐ BiGRU ‐ MHA
abstract: While it is crucial to address the pronounced nonlinearity, substantial time delays, and complex dynamics of post‐combustion carbon capture (PCC) systems using phase‐change solvents, most existing studies rely on idealized simulation data and thus have difficulty representing real industrial noise and long‐range temporal dependencies. To overcome these limitations, this study develops a high‐fidelity dynamic prediction model. Using operational data from the China Huaneng Group phase‐change CO 2 capture platform, we propose an improved AT‐BiGRU‐MHA neural network. The model utilizes a bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU) to extract temporal features and integrates an adaptive multi‐head attention mechanism—with positional encoding and a learnable temperature coefficient—to emphasize critical historical states. A global–local feature fusion strategy is introduced to enhance responsiveness to recent trends. Experimental results demonstrate high accuracy for 2 key variables. For the CO 2 capture rate, the model achieves an RMSE of 0.0158, a MAPE of 1.0460%, and an of 0.9753. For the stripper bottom temperature, it yields an RMSE of 1.9796, a MAPE of 0.3359%, and an of 0.9846, consistently outperforming baseline models. Attention‐weight visualization enhances the transparency of the model and offers insights into the underlying process dynamics, showing that different heads capture distinct long‐range and short‐term dynamics. This model offers a continuously differentiable foundation for nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC), facilitating CO 2 capture rate tracking and energy management under variable operating conditions.

title: Short‐Term Agricultural Drought Prediction Using Explainable Data‐Driven Models and Quantified Uncertainty
abstract: Accurate short‐term prediction of agricultural drought is critical for sustainable crop management and climate risk mitigation in drought‐prone regions. This study evaluates the effectiveness of the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) as a key lagged predictor of agricultural drought in the Palakkad district of Kerala, India. Multiple machine learning and deep learning models were evaluated using lagged values of SPEI and the Standardized Soil Moisture Index (SSI) to predict SSI at 1–3‐month lead times. An additional model configuration incorporated global climatic indices to assess their potential influence on regional drought dynamics. Predictive uncertainty was quantified using Quantile Regression (QR), and model interpretability was evaluated through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to identify the primary drivers of drought evolution. Unlike most short‐term drought studies, this work jointly integrates predictive uncertainty and explainable artificial intelligence to enhance operational reliability. Results indicate that the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) consistently achieved the highest predictive accuracy, with R 2 values reaching 0.84 at 1‐month lead time, decreasing to 0.53 at 2‐month and 0.26 at 3‐month. Root mean Square Error (RMSE) ranged between 0.50 and 0.59 at 1‐month lead time, but increased progressively at longer lead times. The Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) demonstrated comparable performance, with R 2 values ranging from 0.77 to 0.82 across different grid points at the 1‐month lead time. Uncertainty analysis demonstrated high coverage reliability (PICP ≈ 0.88–0.89) across ANN models, with increasing interval width at longer lead times. SHAP analysis confirms that local lagged hydroclimatic variables dominate near‐term drought prediction, while climatic indices provide only marginal improvements. The integration of uncertainty quantification and interpretability enhances the operational utility of these models, offering a transparent and scientifically robust framework for short‐term drought prediction, early warning applications and climate‐resilient agricultural management.

title: MRpro: Open Framework for Model-Based, Learned, and Quantitative MR Imaging-Application to Low-Field MRI.
abstract: MRpro is an open-source framework for MR image reconstruction and quantitative parameter estimation, with particular relevance to low-field MRI. Built on PyTorch, it supports modern deep-learning reconstructions and standardized data exchange through ISMRMRD for raw k-space data and DICOM and NIfTI for reconstructed images and parameter maps. This facilitates integration into existing pipelines and the use of data from different devices. MRpro provides unified data structures for the consistent manipulation of MR datasets and associated metadata, together with a library of composable operators, proximable functionals, and optimization algorithms. The operator library includes a unified Fourier operator for all common trajectories and operators specifically developed for low-field applications, such as a B 0 -correction operator. Together, these components underpin ready-to-use implementations of key reconstruction algorithms. For deep learning, MRpro includes data-consistency layers, differentiable optimization layers, state-of-the-art backbone networks, and access to public datasets to facilitate reproducibility. Automated quality control supports collaborative development. We demonstrate MRpro for automatic reconstruction, iterative SENSE, deep-learning-based reconstruction, and quantitative parameter estimation. For selected Cartesian and non-Cartesian tasks, iterative SENSE reconstructions from MRpro differed from those obtained with BART, SigPy, and MRIReco by less than 3% relative RMSE. Further applications use public and simulated datasets and measured low-field data acquired at 0.3 T, 0.6 T, and 47 mT. MRpro provides a reproducible and maintainable foundation for future MR imaging research.

title: Impact of Neighborhood Socioeconomic Status on Presentation and Treatment of Thyroid Cancer.
abstract: OBJECTIVE We examined associations between multilevel sociodemographic factors and extent of disease at presentation and time to treatment in patients with differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC). STUDY DESIGN Population-based study. SETTING California Cancer Registry (CCR). METHODS All adults diagnosed with DTC in California from January 1, 1988 to December 31, 2020 were included. Main independent variables were neighborhood socioeconomic status (nSES) and race/ethnicity. Covariates included individual sex, marital status, insurance type, and year and age at diagnosis. Primary outcomes were tumor histology, size, and stage at diagnosis. Secondary outcome was time from diagnosis to treatment. RESULTS Among 88,894 individuals diagnosed with DTC, 77% were female, more were residents of higher SES neighborhoods (24% Q5 vs 13% Q1), and nearly half (48%) were non-Hispanic (NH) White, followed by 27% Hispanic and 7% of another NH Asian American ethnicity. In multivariable models, the odds of presenting with distant metastases were higher with lower nSES (OR Q1 vs Q5 = 1.33; 95% CI = 1.17, 1.50), male sex (OR female vs male = 0.43; 95% CI = 0.40, 0.47), and Black (OR = 1.24; 95% CI = 1.04, 1.49), Hispanic (OR = 2.02; 95% CI = 1.84, 2.21), Chinese American (OR = 1.80; 95% CI = 1.50, 2.16), Filipino American (OR = 2.07; 95% CI = 1.81, 2.36), or another Asian American (OR = 1.78; 95% CI = 1.56, 2.04) race/ethnicity. Lower nSES was associated with longer time from diagnosis to treatment (OR = 1.24; 95% CI 1.12, 1.38). CONCLUSIONS People of lower nSES, male sex, and certain racial/ethnic groups were diagnosed with more advanced disease and had longer times to receipt of definitive treatment. Multilevel sociodemographic factors impact DTC presentation and treatment access.
journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery

title: The potential global distribution of Drosophila suzukii, including consideration of irrigation and Australian host cropping areas.
abstract: BACKGROUND Spotted wing drosophila, Drosophila suzukii (Matsumura), is a major fruit fly pest of cherries and berries across Eurasia and North America, with a restricted distribution in the southern hemisphere. It is currently ranked the third greatest threat to Australia on the National Priority Plant Pest (NPPP) list (2024). Various CLIMEX, MaxEnt and mechanistic models of the potential global distribution of D. suzukii have not included irrigation effects. Here, we model the potential global distribution of D. suzukii using CLIMEX, mapped as a composite of natural rainfall and irrigation. For Australia, we overlay the composite potential distribution with host crops to identify commercial areas at risk. RESULTS The potential distribution of D. suzukii includes all Australian commercial host growing regions. The global projected range extent changes by 6% when irrigation is included, and mean within-range global cell suitability increases by 5 Ecoclimatic Index points. Globally, the CLIMEX results indicate potential range expansion in South America, sub-Saharan Africa, South East Asia and Oceania. CONCLUSION We have demonstrated a straightforward assessment of the overlap between host production and the potential distribution of a priority pest. This method can be applied to other NPPPs in Australia as part of a broader modelling framework, or to similar cases in other regions. © 2026 The Author(s). Pest Management Science published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd on behalf of Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Impacts of stochastic parameterizations on forecast error growth and predictability in convection‐permitting simulations over the Maritime Continent
abstract: This study investigates how different stochastic parameterizations influence forecast error growth in convection‐permitting simulations over the tropical Maritime Continent. First, we introduce perturbations to boundary layer, microphysics, and convective schemes to identify the dominant sources of uncertainty in high‐resolution tropical forecasts. A clear hierarchy in error growth is found: boundary‐layer perturbations produce the strongest and fastest growth, microphysical perturbations yield intermediate growth, and convective perturbations the weakest. Independent of perturbation source, the regions of largest forecast uncertainty align with areas of active convection, highlighting the strong coupling between diabatic processes and error amplification. Second, we examine sensitivity to perturbation amplitude, temporal decorrelation time‐scale, spatial correlation length scale, and tendency versus parameter‐based formulations. Results show that perturbation amplitude is the dominant control on forecast error growth for both formulations, while temporal decorrelation time‐scale plays a secondary role. Notably, this sensitivity is particularly pronounced for tendency perturbations, which directly project onto dynamically growing modes, and weaker for parameter perturbations, whose impacts are mediated indirectly through the physical processes. Overall, this study provides guidance for the design and tuning of stochastic parameterizations in tropical ensemble forecasting systems, with boundary‐layer processes identified as the dominant source of subgrid‐scale model uncertainty. While physical consistency considerations remain important, this study indicates that this uncertainty is most effectively represented by applying perturbations to tendencies rather than model parameters, except at early lead times when weak turbulent activity limits subgrid tendencies.
journal: Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society

title: PhyDiCT: Plug-and-Play CT Reconstruction from Sparse X-Rays via Differentiable Rendering and Strong Priors
abstract: Reconstructing 3D Computed Tomography (CT) images from a few X-ray projections is a highly ill-posed inverse problem due to the loss of volumetric information. We propose PhyDiCT, a training-free framework that integrates a differentiable Physics-based forward model, grounded in the Beer-Lambert law, with a text-conditioned Diffusion as a strong prior to reconstruct 3D lung CT images. We refer to our approach as training-free since the prior model is used without fine-tuning, and our goal is to steer the denoising procedure to generate samples consistent with X-ray observations. We guide the diffusion generation using Split Gibbs sampling to jointly optimize for projection fidelity (reward) and consistency with prior knowledge. Also, we introduce a test-time refinement step that enhances image realism and anatomical coherence. We extensively evaluate our method on publicly available 3D CT datasets using both perceptual and semantic metrics, demonstrating that it surpasses existing plug-and-play diffusion and fully trained reconstruction approaches. Our findings highlight that combining a strong generative prior with the underlying physics of image formation substantially improves reconstruction quality, e.g., 7.5\% improvement on SSIM compared to full training methods. Code will be released at https://github.com/batmanlab/PhyDiCT.

title: Head-to-head comparison of quantitative perfusion parameters derived from DECT, IVIM, and DCE-MRI for renal mass characterization: a within-patient, prospective study.
PathScaleBench: A Multidimensional Benchmark of Cross-Scale Representation Behavior and Magnification-Shift Robustness in Pathology Foundation Models
abstract: Pathology foundation models (PFMs) are widely used as frozen encoders, but their behavior under changes in histologic magnification remains poorly characterized. We developed PathScaleBench to quantify cross-scale representation behavior and determine whether it is associated with downstream magnification-shift robustness. Seventy-one audited native-40 × The Cancer Genome Atlas whole-slide images from eight cancer types were sampled at the same tissue centers at 40 × , 10 × , and 2.5 × using a native-field-of-view (native-FOV) protocol. Eight PFMs were evaluated using centered kernel alignment (CKA), relative retention, bidirectional cross-scale retrieval, cancer retrieval, and neighborhood preservation. Eight-class linear probes were trained at one magnification and tested at all three using ten repetitions of five-fold patient-grouped cross-validation. Model rankings varied by metric. Phikon achieved the highest mean CKA (0.714), relative retention (0.774), and neighborhood preservation (0.248); Virchow2 achieved the highest cross-scale retrieval similarity (0.643); and Midnight achieved the highest cancer Recall@1 (0.845). No representation metric was significantly associated with Recall@1 at the model level after multiplicity correction. Midnight showed the lowest magnification generalization gap (0.082), followed by Virchow2 (0.181) and UNI2 (0.224). Across 1704 case-model-scale-pair observations, pair-matched retrieval similarity was associated with corresponding shift robustness (Spearman ρ = 0.159, 95% confidence interval 0.059–0.264; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0021). Cross-scale PFM behavior is multidimensional; global alignment, local correspondence, biological identity, neighborhood topology, and downstream robustness are not interchangeable. No model dominated all dimensions. Representation profiles can support model selection, but magnification robustness should be tested directly.
journal: Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Physics-informed vessel trajectory prediction via finite difference kinematic losses
abstract: Accurate and physically consistent vessel trajectory prediction is crucial for navigational safety, route optimization, traffic management, and autonomous navigation. Traditional data-driven models often lack physical constraints, leading to forecasts that violate vessel motion dynamics, particularly in scenarios with sparse or noisy data or during sudden changes in course or speed due to environmental factors. To address this limitation, we present a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) framework for trajectory prediction that integrates an established kinematic model of vessel motion directly into the neural network training process via first- and second-order, physics-based finite-difference loss functions, leveraging standard numerical techniques, forward Euler method, Heun’s second-order approximation, and a midpoint approximation based on Taylor series expansion, to enforce fidelity to fundamental physical principles by penalizing deviations from expected kinematic behavior. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of this PINN approach across state-of-the-art deep learning architectures using real-world AIS datasets spanning diverse maritime conditions. Results show that the proposed approach yields a statistically significant reduction in average displacement errors—demonstrating representative improvements of 14% with the ConvLSTM model and up to 32% with the complex TCN model on the Arctic dataset—while maintaining physical consistency. These findings enhance model reliability for mission-critical maritime operations, where accurate forecasting improves situational awareness at sea.

title: Impacts of needle-leaved forests landscape pattern and environmental factors on the spatial differentiation of pine wilt disease in China
abstract: Following its emergence in China, pine wilt disease (PWD) has continuously expanded, creating substantial risks to regional forest ecosystems. However, most existing research emphasizes climate and other macro-scale associated factors, and lacks long-term and systematic analysis approached through the lens of forest landscape patterns. The research focuses on describing the spatiotemporal dynamics of PWD in China across the period 1982–2020 and identifying the dominant factors influencing its distribution. We specifically examined how needle-leaved forest landscape patterns interact with environmental conditions to shape the spread of PWD across regions. We applied the optimal parameters-based geographical detector (OPGD) model to analyze the spatial differentiation of PWD outbreaks. Needle-leaved forest landscape metrics and environmental variables were integrated to evaluate their individual and combined effects on disease spread. PWD has progressively expanded over the past four decades. The epidemic was primarily distributed along the southeastern coastal zones and subsequently extended toward the northwestern interior. Landscape factors such as patch density, patch number, landscape shape index, mean patch size and connectivity index, and environmental factors such as temperature, roads and population had high explanatory power on PWD spatial patterns, and the interaction of the two factors considerably improved the interpretive capacity for epidemic differentiation. Our findings enhance ecological understanding of disease spread and provide a scientific basis for risk assessment, early warning, and landscape-based management strategies in forest ecosystems.
